notes_for_editor.note: Standing is not confirmed: the Register describes the tower as decommissioned and privately owned, but no statement of current condition or recent photo was found, so facts.status is 'unknown'. Owner names appear in the Register description and are left out of the story and evidence quotes. The brief's 'George & Rebecca Taylor' is the Register's administrator field and was kept. The Forest Lookouts page has only a county and agency line. The Jackson's Ramblings post and the 1819 News column add nothing new on this tower. Used 1 WebSearch and about 7 page reads, over the per-tower budget, because the sources are thin.

Thin record. NHLR is the only tower-specific source. The Forest Lookouts Aimwell page has a header only (Marengo County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. Kaufmann's 1819 News column is general, cited only for the MC-39 and climbing context, not for Aimwell's condition. NHLR gives a 100' Aermotor without naming a model, so the MC-39 point is not applied to Aimwell. Brief record matched: 1951 built and 2010 registration. height_m 30.5 converts 100 ft. Staffing, fires, access and current condition are left out because no source supports them. The only evidence that the tower still stands is NHLR's 'only one remaining' wording; no visit date is given. No photos added.

The 1941 history comes from newspaper passages quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (Daily Mountain Eagle), not from the original paper. The Weebly passage spells it 'Alridge Tower'; the tablet and NHLR use Aldridge. NHLR lists the build year as unknown, so the 1941 event rests on the May 29, 1941 'now completed' line and the June 1941 dedication. Brief gap closed: no built event was in the record. Access upgraded from unknown to private from NHLR's 'located on private property' line; no owner or permission information was found. Not verified: condition after the July 2022 site visit, staffing and fires. Kaufmann's column is general and does not name this tower. No photos added.

Thin record. NHLR is the main source. The Weebly Allison page has a header only (Choctaw County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. Jackson's Ramblings repeats the Register's description and gives AL 45 where the Register gives AL 44. The UWA archive listing includes an August 9, 1926 letter from Mr. Allison to Major Bunker about a lookout tower; no tower is named, so it is not linked to Rudder Hill. Brief record matched on the 1954 built field and 2010 registration. The 1953 date comes from the Register description and is added as a replacement event. No photos added. Not verified: current condition, access, staffing and fires. The drone video and any other video or social posts were not read and are not cited.

Thin record. Read: the FFLOS register page, the Forest Lookouts Alabama stub (name, county, agency only), the OpenStreetMap node (name and tags only) and the 2019 Alabama report by the nominator, which is general and does not name Aquilla. Nothing found on build date, staffing, fires, removal or condition, and no access statement. The brief's 'gone' status rests on the register's former-site category; no removal record was found. OpenStreetMap gives the point an elevation of 142 m against the register's 146 m; the difference is small and unexplained, so it is not in the story. Worth trying: Choctaw County newspapers, Alabama Forestry Commission records (the AFC has a public records policy), and a message to the nominator, who wrote in 2019 that he was seeking photos and stories of former lookouts from local history societies. The Flickr set of Choctaw County towers was not read. No corrections proposed.

Thin record. The register entry and a stub page are the only Asbury-specific sources. Two searches and the reads found no build date, design, height, staffing or fate history. The 1819 News feature is state context, not site evidence. Story kept short per the guide. Nothing read says whether the land is open to visitors.

Only the NHLR detail page and the Talladega National Forest Wikipedia article were read. An Anniston Star article ('Grant allows restoration of fire tower', annistonstar.com) appeared in a search snippet describing a Friends of the Talladega National Forest effort to restore a Bankhead tower north of Heflin. Both fetch_text and WebFetch returned HTTP 429, so it is neither read nor cited. Retry it: it is the likeliest source for current condition and access. The maker claim is the register writer's hedged belief and is kept hedged. Brief elevation (419.1 m) and USFS agency match the register; no corrections. The name 'Bankhead' points to a different national forest, so the register's Talladega placement should be double-checked against the Forest Service. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story's no-condition-change line was narrowed to 'in the sources we could read', because the unread Anniston Star snippet may describe restoration work on a tower north of Heflin (Cleburne County).

Built year, design, elevation, registration and the Salem note all come from the NHLR register entry alone; no second source for the build. The register's 'only surviving' wording implies standing when written, but the date is unknown, so the record's 'standing' status is not independently confirmed. No staffing, fire, access or current-condition source found. Wikipedia's Beauregard article does not mention the tower. The Forestry Commission homepage and the FFLOS Alabama page gave nothing useful. The 1819 column does not name this tower; it is used only for statewide context and the climbing warning. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 7 page reads.

Thin record. The 1948 build year is in the Register and matches the 1948 dedication notice quoted by Forest Lookouts; the Anniston Star page itself was not checked. No design, height, staffing, fire, condition or access information was found. The record's 'standing' status is unconfirmed by any dated source, so it is not in facts. Web searches returned only an Oklahoma tower also named Beaver Mountain, which was excluded. The Register gives the build year only, so no design or height facts were added.

Story body is about 128 words, at the low end of the range, because the evidence is thin. The register gives name, county, agency, registration date, coordinates and 'No trace of tower remains'; I found nothing on build date, staffing, fires or use. Alabama Forest Fire Lookout Association 2018 report text and the easternuslookouts.weebly.com Alabama list mention the site only by name and agency; the weebly detail page 404s. The register point and the map-listing point differ by two degrees of longitude, so the story leaves the exact spot open. Recommend the editor keep this as a stub or hold it until a local history source turns up. Fact-check 2026-10-10: story no longer treats the MountainZone Becks Mountain as the same site; the position is stated as conditional.

Build year (1942) and the CCC Camp P-76 attribution agree across the NHLR entry and Jackson's Ramblings. Registry number conflict: NHLR says US 862, AL 40; Jackson's Ramblings says US 862, Al 41. The story reports both and does not pick one; NHLR is the register of record, so check it before any correction. Jackson's spells the town Bellville, while the register and record use Belleville. Facebook and YouTube posts seen in search were not used (one calls the county Connecticut County). The drone videos are the only sign of a recent visit or sighting, and they carry no condition or access statement. No staffing or fire source found. The Forest Lookouts Alabama list in the local cache (eastern_us_lookouts/lee.html navigation) does not include Belleville, Beauregard or Blackjack; treat that as a snapshot, not a verdict. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads.

Thin record: NHLR is the only substantive source. The Forest Lookouts Bibb page has a header only (Bibb County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. The Alabama Forestry Commission Facebook post on fire towers was not readable beyond its title. The 1819 News column is by Thomas Kaufmann, who also nominated Bibb to the Register; it is general about Alabama towers and is cited only for the MC-39 model context, not for Bibb's condition or climbing status. A Jackson's Ramblings entry for Brooks Lookout Tower (Conecuh County) is a different tower and was not linked to Bibb. height_m 30.5 converts NHLR's 100 ft. Access, staffing and current condition are left out of facts because no source supports them. No photos added. Not verified: whether any closure or restoration has happened since 2009.

One detailed Register entry (nominated by Andrew Zerb; photo credit Andrew Zerbe) and a thin Forest Lookouts page. No staffing, fire, restoration-date or current-status sources were found. A Forest Service Bankhead page read had no tower content. The 30.5 m height is the 100-foot tower height converted, not a cab-floor height. The record's built year of 1936 may be widened to the Register's circa 1936-1938 range.

Lowest confidence of the three: only the NHLR register entry describes this tower. No source found for condition, current status, public access, staffing, fires, or who built it (the register lists the Forestry Commission only as administrator and cooperator). The record's 'standing' status is not confirmed by any source read. Searches returned mapping and topo-map pages (anyplaceamerica, mapcarta, itouchmap) that add nothing on the tower's history, and were not cited. The 1819 column is general statewide context and does not name this tower. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 4 page reads.

NHLR is the only tower-specific source. The 1941 build year and 2009 registration in the brief match the Register. Height_m 36.6 is converted from the Register's 120-foot wording in its description, not from a separate height field, so check it if strict. The Forest Lookouts Blacksher page returns 404. Two WebSearch queries found no history beyond the Register. Status standing is taken from the Register's 'still standing' wording. No photos added: the NHLR photo us853_blacksher.jpg is already in the photo manifest and its license is not stated on the page.

Unresolved agency conflict: the Register's 'Administered by' field names Charles Daniel Mullins, its description says the tower was built for the Alabama Forestry Commission, and Forest Lookouts names the Forestry Commission. Left out of facts.agency pending a human look; the record's agency field is unchanged. The Register gives only 'late 1940s' for the build, so no built event was added. The condition description is undated. Web searches found no other source on this tower or its owner. The ownership correction is for human review.

Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the only substantive source. Its 2016 description is the latest word on condition, so current status, access and climbing rules are unverified. No build date, designer or staffing history in any source read; the easternuslookouts.weebly.com page guessed at as boar-tush.html returned 404 and was not used. A Facebook video titled 'Boar Tush Lookout Tower in Haleyville, Alabama' appeared in search; it is unread and unused, and Haleyville is the nearest town to the NHLR coordinates. Grokipedia and Wikipedia's Boar Tush community article were checked and do not add tower history. Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the main source, and the Forest Lookouts page for Bridge Creek is a header only (Lawrence County, Alabama Forestry Commission) with no body text. NHLR is the only tower-specific history. TopoQuest confirms the name, county and approximate location (its coordinates agree with the Register's to about 0.001 degree) but nothing about the history. Four independent sources agree on location, the 1934 completion and the CCC build; the 1934-35 and 1936 dates differ by source and are both given. Current access is supported by the Encyclopedia of Alabama and the 2026 America's State Parks guide, not by an official park page; the official alapark.com Cheaha page has no Bunker Tower text. No corrections to the brief's record; events and agency match.

Build year 1948 agrees across the register, the 1948 newspaper dedication and the blog. Unresolved: the state number is AL 42 in NHLR (and in the record) but AL 43 on Jackson's Ramblings. The 1948 dedication is known only from a newspaper quote on Forest Lookouts; no original newspaper page was read. Verification 2026-10-08: the 428 ft figure is the register's elevation, not a hill height; OpenStreetMap's tag is tower:construction=lattice, not a tower type.

Thin record. The NHLR disagrees with itself: build field 1936, description 1935. No source read gives staffing, closure, fate or current public access, so the story says so. The NHLR links an article, Exploring the Forgotten Fire Towers of Alabama (rootsrated.com), which returned no text from fetch_text; it was not read. Access status should be checked with the Talladega National Forest before any visit advice is published.

Thin record: no build year, designer, builder, staffing or access information found. The Alabama state forestry history PDF has no Cains Ridge mention, so it is not cited. Single source: the FFLOS register page. No staffing, notable fire or access sources found. The make of the tower and the removal date conflict across sources and the story reports both. Brief's status 'standing' is wrong: both NHLR and FFLOS say removed.

Only two sources, and neither describes the tower's condition after the 2011 registration, so the record's 'standing' status and 'unknown' access are unconfirmed. No staffing, fire or fate information was found; one web search added nothing new. NHLR elevation 402 ft (123 m) matches the record.

Single source: the NHLR page. It gives no build year, design, height or builder. Two WebSearch queries found nothing about this tower; the results were other Cedar Grove places and fire departments. Brief elevation_m 48.5 agrees with the Register's 159 ft (48 m) to rounding. Direct conflict on build date: NHLR says 1935 (CCC, 1930s); the Anniston Star items reprinted by Forest Lookouts describe construction in 1947-49. Hoover Historical Society page (hooverhistoricalsociety.org/historical-sites/crawford-bluff-park-fire-tower-cab/) returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text. Record status 'standing' is wrong per both registers; the 11-27-21 update gives no removal date or cause. Record kind 'tower' may need review now that FFLOS lists it as a former site. Single source: the FFLOS register page. Two sources only. Build year conflicts: NHLR 1960 vs Anniston Star item (quoted by Forest Lookouts) 1961. Only the two register pages describe this tower, and they repeat one description, so the history is thin. Both give 1952 for the reconstruction and removal around 2010. The original construction date and earlier site are unknown. The 100 ft figure is the register's tower height, not confirmed as height to the cab floor, so height_m is omitted. The NHLR page gives the state number as AL 36, but the FFLOS cross-reference says AL 37; the record keeps AL 36, the NHLR page's own number. Access is set to closed because no tower remains; the park itself is public. The state forestry PDF is a manuscript submitted in March 1961, reproduced by the Department of Conservation; its author is not named in the text read, and its 157-tower count is general, not specific to this site. No new photos. Two web searches added nothing specific to this tower.

Single source: the Former Fire Lookout Sites register. Two web searches found no other record of a tower at this site. The register gives only a decade for the build (1930s), so no built event is recorded. The register describes a tower with a 12x12-foot cab; the record's kind 'unknown' could be updated to tower, but that is a gap, not a clear error, so no correction is proposed. A Forest Lookouts page for this site was not found in the cache or on the guessed URL (404). The Open Pond Fire Tower in Conecuh National Forest is a different tower (US tower #97, CCC 1938-39) and is not used. No photo URL was extracted.

Build date conflict: the register says the CCC completed the wooden tower in 1939, but a Piedmont Journal item dated April 1, 1938 (quoted on Forest Lookouts) already describes a 30-foot wooden structure in use. Removal of the steel tower is not dated in any source read; the 2013 hike notice calls the site removed. Burgess Point origin of the steel tower rests on the register alone. A Komoot listing (user-contributed, not used) describes a Burgess Fire Tower at Bluegrass Point, Clay County, dated 1936, which may be related. Spelling: Duggar in the register, the 2013 notice and the 1938 items; Dugger on the Forest Lookouts page title. No photos added: the register credits Al Pelham for a 1939-1959 photo, but no image URL was extracted.

Single source: the Former Fire Lookout Sites register. Two web searches found no record of an Eldridge fire tower, and no other record of the remains. The agency is 'State of Alabama' per the register; the Alabama Forestry Commission was not confirmed. The status is changed from the record's 'gone' to 'ruins' because the register says the bottom section remains on the ground.

Single substantive source: the NHLR detail page has no visit report, condition note or staffing answer. The brief's status standing is not confirmed by any source read, so status is left out of facts. Thomas Kaufmann's 1819 News column is general about Alabama towers and is not used for this tower's condition. Not verified: build details beyond 1949, fire history, staffing, current condition, access, fate.

One source for the build year, design, agency and registration: the NHLR entry, read in full (it names Alabama Forestry Commission as administrator). The 1819 News article is general background and does not name Fabius. Not found: staffing, fire history, condition today, access, and any dated source for the record's 'standing' status (the Register does not state it). A search surfaced the Joe B. Shirley tower near Huntsville in Madison County, a different tower, excluded. The 120 ft height (36.6 m) is the Register's figure and may not be cab-floor height. One register source (read in full) for the 1941 build, the CCC camp and the 2021 registration. The camp name 'Vrendeburgh' matched no source found. Only two sources: the FFLOS entry and a TopoQuest map-name listing. The TopoQuest 'Tower' label is a map feature name, not a check on what stands. Register (read in full) and one WAFF news report from August 2024. Build year conflict: Register 1936 vs Forest Lookouts 1938. The Forest Lookouts page is short, with one dated line. Thin record. The NHLR detail page is the only substantive source and it gives no build year and no status, access or staffing details. The source 2 title matches the page title, 'Climbing New Heights'.

No photos added; none were checked for license.

Thin record. The NHLR detail page is the main source. Its description says the tower was built in 1935 by the CCC, but its Built field says 1938; the story reports the conflict. The brief's coordinates and elevation (81 m, 265 ft) match NHLR; the brief's '1938 built' is the NHLR Built field, so no correction is proposed. Only one source has substance: the NHLR page. The 1949 date is from its Built field and names no builder. Two web searches and the cached FFLOS and Wikidata pages gave nothing about this tower. The record's status 'standing' is not stated by the register; no current status or visit report was found. The record's material 'steel' is not stated for this tower. Height 30.5 m is converted from the 100 ft overall height; cab floor height is not given. Suggested check: Alabama Forestry Commission records or Perry County historical sources.

Nearly every fact comes from the NHLR page, including the 2019 condition and staffing answers and the early-2020 sale. Only one register page gives facts about this tower. Single source: the FFLOS entry. The register's name 'Kingsville' matched no place I could confirm. Only the Former Fire Lookout Sites page describes this tower; its design and reclamation statements are attributed to Alabama Forestry Commission records. No staffing, fire or access sources found.
