A Historical Marker Database snippet calls it the oldest lookout still in use on the Forest; not used because the page was not read. Record kind 'ground' is consistent with the NRHP building record but no source read states it in those words. Record access 'unknown' should now read closed (2015 notice), not confirmed for today.

Height is the register's 123 ft; not converted because the register does not say whether that is to the cab floor. 'Tallest fire tower in Arizona' is the register's own claim, unverified. The 'still active' statement is from the register page, which gives no date for it, so staffing is left out of facts. Access 'restricted' is an editorial call for tribal land, not a source term. The register's 'Fort Apache-White Mountain' spelling is in its Location field. Record coordinates match the register exactly; the FFLA list is about 0.0003 degrees away.

Thin record. The Forest Lookouts page gives only the name and agency. The FFLA list gives county, type (tower) and status (gone). Peakbagging Table 1 gives the LO site elevation (6647 ft, benchmark) and the key. No build date, design, staffing or fire history appears in any readable source, so none is written. A search snippet from it describes remains of a 40-foot wooden tower, but it is not quoted here because it cannot be checked against a readable page. Worth a re-read by someone who can open it. Record access was 'unknown'; now 'permission' based only on a travel site (RoadScout), not an official source. Confirm the permit rule with the White Mountain Apache Tribe before relying on it. Staffing and fire history were not found in any source read. The register's 'continues in active service' is undated. Height conflict: register gives 80 ft for the 1934 tower, RoadScout gives 60 ft. RoadScout says 'Climb to the top' and that access to the tower varies; the story advises against climbing because no official source gives a climbing rule. Current staffing/access status is only as current as these pages (dates on them unclear), so the tower record's staffing/access fields are left 'unknown' rather than overwritten; story says staffed 'each fire season' per source wording. No photos beyond the one already in the tower record were found within budget.

Every history fact rests on one register entry. The 1932 date and wooden cab were not corroborated: a WebSearch found no McKay-specific source, and the MC-24 towers it surfaced nearby were 1933. The 'still active' claim is from the register page, which gives no date for it, so staffing is left out. Access 'restricted' is an editorial call for tribal land. Suggest a tribal or BIA records check, or the West Lookouts McKay page if it exists (not cached, not read).

Conflict on structure: FFLA lists a ground lookout; SummitPost says the summit once held a lookout tower. The story reports both. Height conflict: Wikipedia 9,470 ft, SummitPost 9,466 ft; the story gives both. No build date, design or staffing record in readable sources. Peakbagging Table 1 row Miller Peak (LO site) carries status code C (badly damaged), which sits oddly with the LO site label (building removed); not used. The 2011 Monument Fire burned the mountain's pines (Wikipedia), but no source ties it to the lookout, so it is left out. No photos recorded. The SummitPost page is a hiker's overview rather than a dated trip report, and its 'short' remark describes the hike as a whole, not the spur.

Brief height 213.4 m is wrong; the tower is 60 ft (about 18.3 m). Current access, staffing and rental status could not be found. Agency is left out of facts: the pages read confirm Prescott National Forest but not the current administering unit. The NRHP nomination PDF (S3) returned 403, the NPGallery asset pages carry no readable text, the Living New Deal page returned 403, and the Facebook pages were unreadable. A 1944 'Twenty years ago' column on Forest Lookouts repeats a 1924 notice and is not counted as a separate event. Page reads for this tower went over the per-tower cap because of failed nomination fetches. Used two web searches.

The 1956 claim about a forest fire is cited to Wikipedia only; the reference Wikipedia cites was not opened. The newest staffing evidence is the 2013 GVRHC summary; check the current season status before trusting it. Access 'public' means trail access on foot, not a cab tour; no source states a cab-entry rule. The NHLR and GVRHC agree on the 1916, 1922 and 1966 towers.

Status is unconfirmed. The record says standing and the 2014 register visit form says good condition, but Wikipedia's short description says 'Destroyed fire lookout house' with no supporting text. The NRHP listing (Moqui Lookout Cabin, 1988) has a 1925-1949 period and 1932 significant year, which do not match the 1952 tower; the nomination PDF (NARA s3 link returned 403) and the NPGallery GetAsset link could not be read, so it is not known whether the listing covers the 1952 structure or an earlier cabin. The Wikipedia body describes a groundhouse with a 14x14 ft footprint, while the register describes a cab on a metal tower. A surgent.net excerpt about a 1954 inspection was in search results only (the site's certificate had expired) and is not used. Access is unknown; no access key set. Height 83 ft converted to 25.3 m. The 2014 comment about the author's parents is a visitor's personal note, not an official staffing record; the commenter is not named in the story. Story wording was changed from 'stands' to 'is in' and from 'at this site' to 'in the Blue Ridge area' because the link between the 1988 listing and the 1952 tower is unconfirmed.

Tower is gone and the cabin collapsed in December 2018 (federal review). Removal date conflicts (2019 in West Lookouts, by 2024 in NHLR and FFLOS) and height conflicts (48 ft vs 50 ft) are both left visible in the story. No source read describes what remains of the cabin, or current public access, beyond FFLOS saying only rubble remains of the tower. Staffing is set to unstaffed as of 2024 by inference from the demolition; change to unknown if you prefer a sourced-only status. The NPGallery PDF is OCR text, so only clean lines were quoted. The 2021 AZ Central hike article was blocked (HTTP 403) and is not used. The West Lookouts page is a hobbyist history and its 2019 removal date is single-sourced.

The Forest Lookouts Mount Baldy page mixes two mountains. The 1925 and 1928 items, and the 1922 Patagonia fire report, describe a Mount Baldy in the Santa Rita Mountains in Coronado NF; they are left out. The 1914 and 1918 items are tied to St. Johns and Eager, both in Apache County; the attribution to this lookout is by place, since the item names only Mt. Baldy or Old Baldy. The 1918 item's 12,000 ft figure conflicts with survey figures. An Arizona Highways article in search results says three-quarters of the mountain, including the summit, is on the reservation; it was not read in full, so it is not used. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the tribal wilderness rule; no permit process was found. Ownership is mixed (reservation with some national forest on the eastern slope), so the record's 'federal' ownership is not corrected here. No photos recorded; the Peakbagging photo page has no image URL in the cache.

Record height_m is 15.2 (about 50 ft); the register and the 2013 summary both give a 53-ft tower, so facts.height_m is set to 16.2. Not a record correction, but worth checking. The record's status_note cites FFLA; FFLA was not read, and the cab-removal claim rests on the GVRHC summary. The GVRHC summary is dated 2013 but has a photo captioned 2014, so the story now says the platform photo is from 2014 and says no later source gives the current state; it no longer says the tower still stands. Register says the cab is metal; the 2013 summary says wood R-6. The newspaper items come through a fan site (westlookouts) and were not checked against originals. No public-access source was found, so no access key is set. The early structures (1926 station, 1929 bid, 1937 50-ft tower) are not tied to the 1958 tower in any source read.

The gone record is a crow's nest at the summit. Sources describe a 1913 summit tower replaced in 1928, but none explicitly ties the FFLA crow's-nest row to that tower, so the link is inferred from location and the replacement. The standing Lemmon Rock lookout (us-az-lemmon-rock) is a separate record and is covered here as the replacement. The photo year is the Commons upload date (2012), not the date the photo was taken. Access to the summit site is not established. Worth trying: Tucson newspapers from 1913 and 1928 on the summit tower and its removal; Coronado National Forest history files.

The build dates (1936 original, 1983 replacement) and the 2002 registration come from the NHLR detail page only. Standing status comes from the firelookout.org listing. The date the 1936 tower reached the museum is unknown, so no relocation event is set (events need a year). The NHLR museum page URL the record links as '../us-az-mount-ord-at-rim-country-museum/' returned 404, and the Go-Arizona and Payson Roundup pages returned 403 and 429, so the museum's account (whole tower or only the top section) is unresolved. Search snippets (not used) mention a 2013 forum thread about decommissioning and a rotating camera; they were not verified on a fetched page. Access and staffing are unknown. Suggest checking with the Rim Country Museum (Payson) or the Tonto National Forest Mesa Ranger District before publishing a 'today' section.

The move date is not in any source read; the register gives none, and no museum page was found. The City-Data listing is undated. A search snippet (not read, not used) gives the original tower as 60 feet tall, and a museum video is described as showing the original lookout cab; whether the whole tower or only the cab is at the museum needs checking. Original-tower facts come from the register and Mountain Field Guide. The record's 'public' access level rests on the museum listing, not a current hours check.

History from 1911 to 1976 comes from newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; those items were not checked against the original papers. The NHLR page is the only source for current status ('remains in active service', undated). Access level is not stated in any source read, so access is omitted; the record's access 'unknown' stays. No trail or visit information found. The Forest Lookouts page has a 1996 'National Register' entry whose text was cut short in the page output, so it is not used. Height 30 ft converted to 9.1 m. Search results and listing sites about current access were not read, so nothing from them is used. The Forest Service Bradshaw Ranger District page was not read.

Height 22.9 m is converted from the register's 75 ft; the brief had no height. The April 25, 2009 registration date and the July 4, 2009 ceremony are both recorded; they are not in conflict. Staffing is not stated in the fetched pages. Public access status is not confirmed; the only road detail comes from a travel guide. The Abbey claim rests on the travel guide alone. The Forest Lookouts North Rim page gave no tower detail in the text fetched. The 'summit' location comes from the travel guide only.

Brief access 'permission' is not supported by any source read, so no access level is set. Brief agency matches the NHLR administered-by line. NHLR 'in active service' is undated. Two WebSearch queries found no history of the tower. An undated KTAR article about an Oak Ridge wildfire was not linked to the tower and is not used. Staffing, fires and visitor status are unknown.

History rests on the NHLR detail page alone; the FFLA list gives status only. Two web searches found no independent history, staffing, fire record or access rule. Search snippets gave other elevations (2,590 m; 8,525 ft) that I did not confirm from a fetched page, so they are not used. The record had no build year; 1934 is added from the NHLR. A hiker trip report in search results (hikearizona.com) says a locked chain-link fence blocks the tower. Current staffing and climbing status are not established by any source read; the story says so. Thin record. The only history found is one 1917 newspaper account, quoted second-hand by Forest Lookouts. No build year, no removal date and no photo. Two conflicts. First, the FFLA list says ground level, but the NGS 1947 description says steel tower; the proposed correction is medium confidence. Only two sources, and the history is from a 2002 register entry. Two web searches found no builder, date, staffing or fire history beyond the register. Thin record. The NRHP nomination PDF on NPGallery is marked not yet digitized, so the 1939 significant year and any staffing, use or closure history could not be checked. No build year is given beyond the Forest Service's early 1980s, so no built event is recorded. The 1913 plan is a newspaper report of a plan, not confirmation that a tower was built. The access level 'restricted' is our judgment from the trail being open and the lookout being an active staffed lookout; no source says whether the cab is open to visitors, so change it if the Tusayan Ranger District says otherwise. Record name, coordinates and elevation match the register. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the earlier draft's sentence that an earlier structure may have stood on the butte but the sources describe none is removed, because a 1972 item on the Forest Lookouts page calls a 'Forest Service fire lookout shack on Red Butte', which predates the early-1980s tower. The story now says only that the sources do not say when a tower first went up. The 1972 item is not used in the story, and its crime report is not used at all; an editor may add the shack, without that detail, if wanted. The directions now name Forest Roads 320, 340 and 340A, as the Forest Service trail page gives them from Tusayan; the earlier draft named only 340A.

Status rests on the Forest Service project page (removal decision signed March 5, 2020; listed 'Completed') and the FFLA list ('Gone'). No source gives a demolition date or describes what remains on the summit. The register text (2006) describes the cab in use. The record's kind 'two_story' matches the FFLA label '2-Story Cab'; the register does not use that term and describes a cab on a 10-foot concrete block base. The register's Built field says 1958, but the same entry says a wooden tower was used there in the 1920s, so 1958 is the cab date. The Kaibab project documents (on Box and Pinyon Public) were linked but not readable here. No access, trail, or visit information in any source read.

Four sources, but the 2020 summary says it was compiled from the FFLA and NHLR websites, so it is not fully independent of them. Access: no source says whether visitors may enter the cab; the summary says the forest road ends at the lookout, and the 2010 hiker walked it. hikearizona.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Search snippets gave other hike distances (about 9 miles round trip) from pages I did not open, so they are not used. NHLR and FFLA coordinates differ by under 1 km. The NHLR line about listing until 2023 is not used. Access level is left out of facts because the sources do not state one.

Two web searches and the FFLA rentals check found no current visiting or rental listing, so the story says the sources do not say. The 1931 original comes only from the register's description. The 2011 fire fact rests on posts quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; no independent fire report was read. The FFLA list is undated, so standing status is as of an unknown date. The record's built 1965 is the replacement, so an editor may want to keep the 1931 and 1965 events as added here.

Thin record. The 1960 date appears only in parentheses in the register description, so it is kept as a probable build year. The record's material 'steel' is not in the register text read, which describes a wooden cab on a metal platform; verify before keeping it. The register's 12-foot tower height looks low for a lookout at this elevation and may be a height above the platform; verify before using. Two web searches found no operator, fire history or visiting information. A search snippet attributed a 1960 date to an FFLA row, but the FFLA pages read do not show it, so it is not used. The Navajo Parks rules page was read; the permit page surfaced by search returned 404 and is not used.

Record height 91.4 m (300 ft) matches no source; see corrections. Build year: the register and a 1929 USFS photo say 1929, but a 1928 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts calls the steel tower recently completed. Left at 1929, unresolved. Staffing and cab access are unconfirmed: the register's active-service line is undated, and the rangeoflight.net trip note is undated. The photo url is the Flickr page, not the direct image file, which I did not extract. Forest Service picnic-site page read: no lookout content. HikeArizona returned 403, so the trail distance is unverified and not used. Access level set to unknown: no source gives a restriction, so the earlier restricted value was unsupported.

Status gone rests on the Fire Lookout Association list and a Forest Service removal project marked completed. No source says when or whether the tower was physically taken down, and none describes the site now. Staffing and access come from an undated album and an undated travel account, so they show only what those pages said when written. The Kaibab project documents on Pinyon Public were not read and may record the demolition. Search budget used: 2 searches; 6 page reads succeeded plus one 404 (Wikipedia has no Round Mountain article).

Rim conflict is unresolved by coordinates: the record's lat/lon come from the register. The 1926 'fire lookout established at Signal Hill' is second-hand, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page from a Park Service Director's report; the original was not read, and it may be the same site as the 1929 tower or an earlier one. The record's material 'steel' is inferred from the LS-40 model name; no source read says steel. Access and current condition are not verified beyond the 2009 'inactive' statement and the undated FFLA 'Standing' list. One web search was used and found no visiting information.

Almost all history and design detail rests on the NHLR detail page; the FFLA indexes add only standing status and register number. No staffing, access, visit or fire sources were found: hikearizona.com (trail page on Signal Peak) returned 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, and no Wikipedia article exists for this lookout. Facts omit access and staffing because no source supports them; NHLR's 'active station' wording is not read as staffed. height_m converts NHLR's 59 ft. The FFLA index coordinates (33.29317, -110.83597) differ from NHLR's (33.29312, -110.83595) by under 10 m; no correction proposed. A search hit for a Washington Signal Peak lookout (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/wa/) is a different tower and was not used. No photos added. Peakbagging's Arizona table (revised 2024-10-02) codes the structure A, meaning good condition and capable of being staffed; that is a building condition, not a staffing record.

The NRHP nomination PDF (NARA copy) and the Living New Deal page both returned 403 and were not read. The 1938 CCC build date and the c.1996 fire rest on Ominous, a user-run listing site; check both against the nomination before publishing. No staffing, fire history or public-access information was found, so no access fact is recorded. The brief's county (Cochise) is correct. The OpenStreetMap entry tags the site as ruins, which fits the fate.

The Skinner Ridge build year is 1929 or 1933 per the 2020 report; the brief's 1929 is kept as the first-listed date. Height 59 feet (about 18 m) is the figure for the tower as it now stands at Encino. No staffing, fire or access information for the ridge site was found, so none is recorded. The 2016 Tusayan East decision covers a tower on the ridge, but no source read confirms it was built; check the project documents or recent imagery before saying anything stands there. The 1941 standing and Barbara Zinn's document are known only through the 2020 report. Encino's current status rests on a 2020 source; newer confirmation is worth finding before publishing.

Only one primary-type item was found: a June 1921 newspaper report (Tombstone Weekly Epitaph, reprinted by Forest Lookouts). No build date, tower type, staffing history or removal date was found. The Wikipedia article and the Forest Service trail page describe the place and an abandoned prison camp, but neither says the camp is the lookout site; do not connect them without a source. The brief's county 'Coronado' is a forest name and is corrected to Pima. Access is not recorded.

Build, cab remodel and registration come from the NHLR page alone. The 'staffed' status rests on one July 2005 magazine mention and is not current. The article's climb rule is general Forest Service practice, not stated for this tower. The lookout named in the article is left out of the story. Search snippets citing an Instagram repost, a Georgia tower and a separate Arizona list were not used. Access and current condition are unknown beyond the FFLA standing label, which carries no date.

The azrock.org 2022 post was read but not used: it calls the tower wood and stone and no longer in use and gives a 7,255 ft peak, both at odds with the other sources. Current staffing rests on an undated blog and an undated Forest Service page, so a dated source would strengthen it. Flickr photos (alanenglish) turned up in search but were not read or added. The CCC attribution comes only from the blog.

The 1920 staffing comes from newspaper notices transcribed on the westlookouts page, not from the original scans; no build or removal date was found. The trip report's title names Mica Mountain but the foundation sentence does not name the peak, so the link to the FFLA Mica Mountain tower record is an inference. Whether the 1920 station sat on the Spud Rock summit or on Mica Mountain is not settled by these sources. The FFLA type 'Unknown' is kept as recorded. Nothing describes the summit today; no photo was found.

Brief's record (1935 built, NHLR 2004 registration, NPS agency, unknown access) checks out. Access can move from unknown to public for the hiking trail, but whether visitors may enter the cabin is not documented. Sources disagree on build details (stone base in the register vs frame on masonry in the narrative) and the narrative also has a 'by 1937' summary that is compatible with the 1935 finish but less precise. Summit elevation (NPS 7,310 ft) differs from the register's lookout elevation (7,238 ft). No specific fire at the lookout was found. The 2008 NRHP date is Wikidata-only. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows coordinates 32.01414, -109.32508, slightly off the register's 32.01111, -109.32639.

Nearly all of the history rests on one register entry, plus Wikidata for the county. No newspaper, Forest Service or tribal source was found, and the latest staffing date is 2011. Access is listed as unknown: the story says no public visitor information was found, and it does not infer permission rules. Photo candidates not added: a 2008 Panoramio photo on Wikidata (license not checked) and the register's 2008 photo credited to Chris English (license not stated). Three web searches were run for this lookout, one over the two-search budget.

Current access and staffing are unverified. 'In active service' comes from the 2003 register entry. I set access to restricted on that reading, so please check with the Bradshaw Ranger District. The Waymarking page did not render. Name variants: Tower Mountain (register, West Lookouts) and Towers Mountain (trail guide). The 1924 tower and 1933 tower are not clearly the same structure. No notable fires found in these sources.

Build year (1937), height (32 ft) and standing status agree across the Register, Peakbagging and the FFLA county list. Staffing rests on Peakbagging's code table (AS), not a staffing roster; as_of is the table's revision date. No source names a specific fire, a staffing history or a visitor rule. The access and visit notes rely on the onX trail page, which is commercial, and do not say whether the cab can be entered or climbed. A 1936 benchmark disk under the tower is mentioned on the Peakbagging photo page; not used, since no source ties it to the 1937 build. A Wikipedia Turkey_Butte URL returned 404. The Peakbagging table gives Turkey Butte a usually-staffed code; no recent staffing confirmation was found. FFLA index coordinates (35.03206, -111.90419) differ from the Register's (35.032000, -111.903300) by roughly 80 m; no correction proposed. No photos added.

Closed status rests on the register's wording ('closed to public access'); the register page carries no date, so current status should be confirmed with the Kaibab National Forest Williams Ranger District or the Army before the access note is trusted. The NRHP listing 87002481 is titled 'Volunteer Lookout Cabin' and is a building with significant year 1939; whether it refers to the tower, the earlier wooden lookout or another structure is not stated in the sources read. The record does not show the NRHP listing; a human should decide whether to add it. The 1921 newspaper items name the trail builder H.S. Perry; no further detail was pursued. Record height 9.1 m matches the register's 30 ft; coordinates and elevation match the register. Flickr and tripbucket search snippets repeat the register's closed-access wording; they were not read and are not cited. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: 'contractor' is replaced with 'successful bidder' (the Williams News wording). The Volunteer Mountain location now cites the Forest Lookouts page too, and the 1930s start-date sentence cites both sources. The 1988 listing is confirmed by NPGallery's date-published field (1/28/1988).

Tower fate is disputed. The Weebly page says it was destroyed; the 2020 NHLR visit and the GVRHC hiking-club report both describe a standing steel frame. The story reports the dispute. Height: the record gives 13.7 m, but both the register and the hiking club give 46 feet (about 14.0 m); a correction is proposed. Model (MC-40 vs CL 100-106) and elevation (9,984 vs 10,029 ft) are unresolved and both are reported. The Living New Deal page and the NARA nomination PDF returned 403, so the NRHP nomination text itself was not read; the CCC architect claim comes from the NPGallery record. Staffing and the trail note are from the May 2020 register visit only, not checked since. The GVRHC PDF publisher name is taken from the domain and was not confirmed from the document. Read budget: seven read attempts, one over the six-read cap (two of the attempts were 403 errors).

Thin record. No visit report, staffing record or fire history was available: the register page has no visit section, and the FFLA list gives only the status 'Standing'. The NRHP nomination text could not be read (NARA PDF returned 403). Search snippets of the nomination, which I could not quote, give conflicting figures: about 45 ft Aermotor HC-40 with a 7 ft cab in one, and 99 ft Aermotor nC-40 with a 7 ft cab in another. Both differ from the register's 46 ft LX-25; this is unresolved and the story uses the register's figure. The proposed height correction (13.7 m to 14.0 m) assumes the register's 46 feet is the right figure. Leads not read: a Western News article of 2025-09-05 about volunteer restoration of historic Arizona lookouts (may cover this tower); a 1964 newspaper item describing a three-person fire-watch crew (historic staffing, snippet only). The Living New Deal page returned 403 and the weebly page for West Peak returned 404. Read budget: six reads, all used.

Only the NHLR detail page gives history: 1962 build, 2022 registration, nominator, site description. The FFLA index gives standing status and the longitude conflict; the Peakbagging table gives the A condition code (good condition, capable of being staffed), which describes the building, not staffing. No staffing, fire, rental or visitor-rule source was found. Searches for Wade Luther and BLM Arizona Strip returned nothing specific to the lookout. A Whitney Pass Road near Whitney Pockets (aravada.com) is a road name, not linked to the lookout. The wchsutah.org Aravada Farm page failed with an SSL error and was not read. NHLR's cabin photos (courtesy of Wade Luther) are not added: their license is not stated. Facts omit height and visit fields because no source gives them.

No build date, builder or staffing years were found in any page read. HikeArizona search snippets give 1930 construction and a 1984 Dry Lake replacement, but HikeArizona returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The NHLR Dry Lake page describes a different, earlier 54-foot tower, not Willow. The FFLA asterisk key (read 2026-10-09) means the structure stands with the cab no longer in place; the earlier wording "marked as standing" ignored the asterisk and was corrected in the story. Access needs a San Carlos Apache Tribe permit; the story does not give a contact.

Brief record checks out: 1936 build, 2001 NHLR registration, USFS agency, 46 ft (14.0 m) height. The NRHP nomination PDF itself was unavailable (HTTP 403 on the NARA S3 copy), so the design and NRHP details rest on the NPGallery metadata, Wikidata and the NHLR page. Staffing status is not given by any source read; the only staffing evidence is the 1912 timeline entry. A Facebook group post says the tower has not been regularly staffed for some time, but it is undated and was not used. Living New Deal also credits the CCC with the 1936 build; not fetched. Access is unknown; the brief's unknown stands. Sources differ on the tree-stand start (register 1910, timeline 1912 stationing) but they are not contradictory. Photos on Wikidata (Woody Mountain Lookout Tower (full).jpg) have no fetched URL and were not added. The 1936 current-tower date is inferred from the register's wood-tower span ending 1936 'when the current tower was built', not from a stated build field. The timeline has no entries after 1936.

The register page is detailed: built 1934, burned after 1968, nothing remains. The Forest Lookouts page supplies the only staffing name (Leo Chatfield, 1936, via a California Ranger item). That page also prints a November 2, 1959 Appeal-Democrat item about a Tahoe fire that burned 'several buildings and a lookout station'. The item does not name Alaska Peak, so it is left out of the story; an editor should check whether it refers to this site. The record's 'removed 1968' event is a simplification: the register says 'removed after 1968' in its field and 'burned in a wildfire after 1968' in its description, so the event type should be 'burned'. This is noted, not proposed as a correction. Public access is not stated in any source; the story says so. The register's 1939 and 1968 photos are credited (Mark Swift Collection; Michael Szyhowski) but their image URLs were not captured, so none are listed under photos. No other source was read; one search returned only Calpine Lookout pages, which are a different site.

Brief height_m 24.4 is 80 feet; corrected to 18.3 m (60 feet) per NHLR and HistoriCorps. Elevation differs: NHLR 6,192 ft, HistoriCorps and Campflare 6,225 ft; not in facts or story. The closed-to-public status rests on an undated third-party Campflare listing that cites no Forest Service page; check the Eldorado National Forest before relying on it. The Eldorado cabins page grep found no Alder Ridge mention. A 2000 news item on the Forest Lookouts page reports a death at the lookout; it is left out of the story as not needed for the history. No source read gives staffing or fire history, and no source confirms a rental has opened. No photos added.

Brief's record checks out on 1966 build, NHLR US 1147 / CA 112, San Mateo County, and standing status (FLA). Brief's 'They share a register number' conflict: Wood Butte, Oregon is listed in the FFLOS register as US 1147 (OR 495) in data/towers/or/us-or-wood-butte.json, while Allen is NHLR US 1147 (CA 112). These are different registers, so the numbers may just coincide; I did not verify this against a single register. Brief's coordinates (37.38709, -122.29501) match the FFLA list, not the NHLR point. Register text gives the tower height as '51" 6" high', which is probably 51 ft 6 in; I did not add height_m because the reading is uncertain. Register says it was closed in 1981, which I recorded as staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1981; the register does not use the word 'staffed'. Access is unknown; the register is silent on visiting. Register photos are credited to Scott McClintock; no image URL was captured, so no photos were added. The register's Salinas origin is not confirmed by the other sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'dry spell' wording was replaced with the source's 'unseasonably dry weather', and the 1956 item is now footnoted in the story.

Correction proposed for height_m (15.2 to 18.3). Access and visiting status were not found in any source, so no access key is set. The Stanislaus album dated 2022 is the most recent source. The 1932 Kling item is the only staffing name found. No notable fires found.

Both pages draw on Lookouts of the Los Padres Forest (Reaves, 1988), so they are not independent sources. The brief's kind 'unknown' is a cabin on a post, not a tower. Two searches found nothing on what remains today, so the story says so. No access or visit facts were added because no source gives them. No photo added: the register's 1988 photo credit has no image URL in the cache.

Build date conflicts: NHLR says 1914 (first service); the plaque says the original lookout was built in 1924 and the current structure by the CCC in 1935. The story reports both. Registry conflict, not in the story: the firelookout.org California list (https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/) gives NHLR US 1180, CA 115 at 38.88230, -120.05465, while NHLR's own page gives US 518, CA 56. The brief's number matches NHLR and was kept. No source read describes the buildings after the June 2010 photo captions, so the current condition is unknown; closed/standing rests on NHLR's undated description. Access is inferred from the Forest Service road page, which does not say whether the buildings are open. No photos added: the Weebly captions cite a July 1941 National Archives photo and June 2010 photos by Ron Kemnow, but give no image URLs. OpenStreetMap way 905267264 (Angora Fire Lookout, tower:type observation) was checked but not used. Budget: 9 distinct pages read against a 6-page budget (the CEQAnet and Forest Service pages were needed for the fire date and access), plus 2 web searches.

Brief status_note ('cab is gone', FFLA) is not verified: the cached FFLA California index shows Standing* and 3-Story Cab with no note text, and the register says only that the roof blew off. The Kern County Fire Department Facebook post could not be read. The 1940 lease is the only ownership history, and the current owner is unknown. The 1954 fire items are the only staffing evidence.

Access level and climbability are not stated by any source read, so the access and visit keys are left out. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ codes the lookout as a 2-Story Cab, Standing, NHLR US 182, CA 7, which matches the record's kind and the register. The record's $500 figure comes from cr-rest-2020.pdf, not the cr-ca-north-2020 report, which gives no amount. The 2021 staffed mark is five years old. A WebSearch turned up a trail-guide snippet saying the modern lookout is manned during fire season, but that page was not read, so it is not cited.

Two substantive sources agree on the 1993 restoration, 1994 registration and the 1990 condemnation; they disagree on build year (1932 vs 1934). The 2026 staffing claim comes from a single article (kymkemp.com) that appears to repost a Forest Service item; treat as seasonal staffing as reported. Sources read do not say whether the public may visit or climb the tower; rental status not found. The Register visit report from 2007 records staffed yes but was not cited. Elevation in a peakbagging entry (6,960 ft) differs from the Register's 6,891 ft; the Register figure is used. Height 8.8 m in our record is unsupported; see corrections. No photos added.

Distance from Quincy is disputed: the register's 2005 visit says 6 miles east, a 1937 Plumas Independent item says about 12 miles east. Not resolved; the story reports both. The record's 'built 1934' is the register's construction-start date; the newspapers show the permanent station completed in November 1937. A human should decide whether the built field needs a correction. The register's 11' figure is not labelled (cab, tower or height), so no height_m is given. The record's event 2025 'restored' overstates the FFLA report, which lists the work as ongoing; it is recorded here as 'other'. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ agrees with the register: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 601, CA 72.Access level is not stated by any source read, and the last register visit is from 2005, so access and climbability are left out. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the 2005 register visit, which is old. The 1994 notice names the Quincy/Greenville Ranger District; the register now names the Mt. Hough Ranger District.

Two sources only: the NHLR entry (a 1939-43 recollection in a January 2003 visit comment, a September 2004 comment on closure and dismantling, and a June 2020 visit report) and one June 1938 Mountain Democrat item quoted on Forest Lookouts. The 1937 build year is the register's; the 1938 item shows the site in use by then but does not date construction. The 1939 and 1943 staffing dates come from the recollection and are approximate. The lineman's-steps tree is reported as the writer's memory and appears in the story only as that memory. Current closure and dismantling status were not checked; two web searches found nothing further. Record height was blank and is filled from the register (80 ft = 24.4 m). Staffing as_of is now the 2020 visit report, not undated.

Brief's built 1966 is the replacement year, not the first structure. The 1929 newspaper dates and the register's 1934 start disagree; both are kept. No source describes what remains on the site today, and the register does not say whether the summit is open to visitors. The brief's status 'gone' is not supported: the register lists removal as Unknown, so status is set to unknown. A 1966 National Park Service photo of the Ash Peak lookout structures exists in the NPS NPGallery (public domain, photographer Richard McLaren) but no direct image URL was confirmed, so it is not added to photos.

Only one site-specific source: the Former Fire Lookout Sites register. The Forest Service and Army roles come from it alone. Removal date and current condition are unknown; the register says Removed Unknown. The Wikipedia article gives the national service's deactivation date only; it does not say this post closed then. A San Luis Obispo Tribune article on wildfire lookouts came up in search but timed out twice and was not read. Search budget used: 2 searches; page reads: 5 successful, one of them an OCR PDF that gave nothing usable; 2 timeouts on a newspaper article.

The name in the record, Babbit Peak Lookout, matches the register, so no name correction is proposed; the 1929 and 1965 items use Babbit and the 1930 to 1960 items use Babbitt. The record has no built year; the 1929 newspapers support 1929 as the build year (construction was announced for July 1929 and the building was in use by late August). That is recorded as an event, not a correction. The 1928 and 1929 papers place the station on Bald Mountain. Identity with the register's Babbit Peak is inferred, not stated, and should get a human look. The newest staffing record is the 2011 register visit; the 2007 and 2009 FFLA reports describe staffed use but not current status. A web search turned up a 2025 Sierraville Ranger District page that does not mention Babbitt Peak; search snippets were not read, so nothing from them is cited. The FFLA list agrees with the record: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 515, CA 53. Access level is not stated in any source read; left out. No new photos were added.

Only three sources; no build date, staffing record beyond a 1938 residence, or removal date was found. The Peakbagging table also has a Shasta County entry named Jacks Backbone / Backbone Ridge (LO site); it is probably a different site and was not used. The 1961 NGS benchmark ID is LU2121 on the Forest Lookouts page but LU2122 on Peakbagging; both are dated 1961. The FFLA type Ground does not clearly match the 1961 wood house with chimney, so the type may be stale. No photo was found.

Construction dates conflict for the first structure (1942 vs about 1943) and the current tower is 1950 in most sources. Status data is thin: the fire-lookouts.org page was last updated in 2013 and Peakbagging.com's closure date (1986) has no other source. No source read gives a current visitor policy for the cab. Elevations differ by about 260 ft depending on whether the lookout or the summit is meant. Fire-lookouts.org credits its cost and historic-eligibility points to a 1988 report that was not read directly. Trail length conflicts: CalWild gives 2-3 miles round trip; fire-lookouts.org gives two miles from the parking area to the lookout (about four miles round trip). The story gives both.

Thinnest of the three: no build date, staffing record, or removal date was found. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook post, seen only as a search snippet, describes a 1963 Bald Eagle lookout on Plumas NF with tripod legs and a crank cab; the page returned only a login wall to fetch_text, so nothing from it is used or quoted. It is the best lead for build and staffing history. The Forest Lookouts page calls the site Bald Eagle Butte while FFLA calls it Bald Eagle Mountain; the two names are treated as one site on the basis of the matching Plumas County location, which should be confirmed. The 1974 notice's 'the dam' is not named. No photo found.

Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the only substantive source. Its build, cab, transfer, administration, staffing and registration facts all come from that one page. The Forest Lookouts Butte County listing has only a February 23, 1929 quote about a planned 60-foot steel tower on Baldy Peak, east of Stirling City; it does not name Bald Mountain. The tower record data/towers/ca/us-ca-bald-mountain-cal-fire-butte-county.json has height_m 18.3, which equals 60 feet and so may have come from the Baldy Peak quote. No source read gives this lookout's height, so height_m is left out of facts and story. Please confirm or remove height_m in that tower record. Checked 2026-10-08: the register footer (raw crawl cache) reads "Last updated on July 31, 2020", which dates the page, not the staffing note. Not in facts or story: a search snippet for the Butte County Battalion 1 page (buttecounty.ca.gov/553/Battalion-1) says the lookout is no longer staffed by lookout personnel and has two ALERTCalifornia cameras. That page returns HTTP 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so it is not footnoted, and the snippet is not quoted. A human should check it, because it would change the staffing and today sections. The transfer to CDF is dated only to the late 1950s, so no event year is given. Staffing has no as_of date: the register footer says the page was last updated July 31, 2020, but our reader drops that footer, so it is not cited. Access, climbability and current condition are unknown and left out. No fire history was found in the sources read. Searches returned other Bald Mountains (Maine, Idaho, Inyo, Mono, Sierra, Sequoia and El Dorado National Forests), which were excluded. No photos added; the record's three NHLR photos are all-rights-reserved.

Record height of 15.2 m (50 feet) is not supported; the register gives a 30-foot steel tower and a 1982 item says 32 feet. Nearly all history comes from dated newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not checked against the original papers. The 1911 to 1983 items were re-read in full on the page, including the 1931-1983 entries; the 1982 item names its subject as Delma and the fire specialist as Dwain Schrader. Current staffing, rental and access are unknown. Two web searches found no Eldorado source on this lookout, and the Forest Service page turned up was about Big Hill. The 1958 bid may have covered the 1912 tower; whether a tower stood on the site before 1965 is not stated. The 1982 staffing is recorded as staffed, with no current information.

Do not confuse with us-ca-bald-mountain-sierra-nf (a different lookout in Sierra NF). The record's '2024 assessed' event (site visit on 24 May) is not in any page read, so it is left out. The record's access value 'unknown' is replaced with public, based on the Forest Service road page and the FFLA visitor count. The 1956 and 1969 items come from newspaper quotes reproduced on the weebly page, not from the newspapers themselves. The FFLA testimonials on the host page are dated September 2026, which hints at 2026 staffing, but no 2026 report was read, so staffing is dated 2025. The 1980s end of full-time service has no exact year in the sources, so it has no dated event. The PDF calls the lookout '61-year-old'; that is not used.

Only one site-specific source: the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, so the Forest Service and Army roles rest on it alone. The brief's 1942 is kept as the event year; the register says circa 1942/43. Removal date and current condition are unknown. The Forest Fire Lookout Association California list has several other Bald Mountain entries in other counties (Butte, El Dorado, Fresno, Mono, Tulare), so keep this one tied to San Luis Obispo County and the US 2043 / CA 149 registry number. The Wikipedia article gives the national service's deactivation date only. Search budget used: 2 searches; page reads: 5 successful, one of them an OCR PDF that gave nothing usable; 2 timeouts on a newspaper article.

Do NOT use the 2025 'Visiting Volunteers' end-of-season report (firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/cr-cal-s-bm-2025.pdf), the 2026 Record-Courier article, or firelookouthost.org/bald-mountain: they concern a different Bald Mountain lookout on the Inyo NF (Mono County, built 1963). Build year is unresolved: register 1954, fire-lookouts.org and a 1955 Region 5 memo point to 1955; the story says so. Road date is unresolved (register: about a decade after 1954; fire-lookouts.org: 1967). The record's 2004 'restored' event (propane lighting, lightning protection repair, potable water, benches) was not found in any page read and is left out of the story; please verify or drop. The record's 1999 and 2001 registration events are both kept; the event notes explain the difference. height_m 12.2 converts the register's 40-foot tower; it is not stated whether that height runs to the cab floor. The cr-az-2009.pdf file is a multi-chapter FFLA compilation (first section is Arizona); the Bald Mountain passages are in its California sections, and one of them says Sierra National Forest where every other source says Sequoia. Staffing is 'seasonal' from the Forest Service page (manned, summer hours). The same PDF's 2009 Sequoia status list says Bald Mt was 'Staffed 5 days with USFS GS employee', which conflicts with the volunteer 'not staffed' entries; the story reports both and does not resolve it. The fire-lookouts.org page was last updated in 2013 and its staffing line is dated. No new photos added. Budget used: 6 distinct pages and 1 web search.

Built year conflicts: the register gives 1934 for a 20 ft tower, California Lookouts gives 1936 for a CCC-built 18 ft 6 in tower; both kept in the story, not resolved. Record height_m 10.0 looks wrong. Nothing after the 2008 photos describes the cab, and no current access notice was found; status 'standing' rests only on the FFLA list. Newspaper quotes come through a hobbyist transcription page, not the originals. Do not confuse with the Inyo NF Bald Mountain Lookout in Mono County (1963 tower), which search results return first.

The 1916-1923 staffing/construction detail comes from an enthusiast compilation site (californialookouts.weebly.com) that cites period Siskiyou County newspapers and a 1952 USC&GS data sheet; I could not verify those primary sources directly, only the compiler's summary of them, so treat names/dates in events for 1916-1923 as secondhand. The NHLR-dated 1938 tower and the 1919 lookout house are almost certainly two different structures on the same peak (record's 'built: 1938' event refers only to the surviving tower) - worth a note on the tower page if the editor wants to preserve both construction dates. Several undated NHLR photos (a 'California Plan 4A Cabin' and a 'Tree Platform') suggest yet other structures/eras on this site that no source dates; not added as events since no year is given. Kathy Shoopman's start-year lookout is called 'Bald Mountain Lookout' in the Action News Now piece but multiple other outlets (ABC10, Yahoo/AP, KTVL) place her first post at 'Baldy Mountain Lookout... west of Happy Camp', matching this record; I treated it as the same site given the matching location description, but flagging the name discrepancy. No source found addresses current public access, trail, or drive-up status, so visit/access facts were left out rather than guessed.

Gone status is well supported (1977 USGS note, FFLA list, 2020 trip report). No source gives a build year, so no built event was added; the 1941 survey description is the earliest dated reference to the house. Elevation is not in the facts schema: Peakbagging lists 5775 ft (about 1760 m) as spot elevation, so the record's elevation_m could take 1760. The FFLA list gives no NHLR or FFLOS registration for Baldy Peak. Do not confuse with Baldy Mountain (Happy Camp) or Deadwood Baldy. The valhikes post is a personal trip report, so it is used only for the present-day burn and the square of rocks and scattered debris at the site. The trail page gives no current closure.

Record height 4.3 m is most likely the 14-foot width of the lookout house (1952 station description: 14 ft square), not the height; the register and 1940 report say 30 feet and a 1960 recollection says about 60. The 2024 Forest Service project concerns a communications tower at Ball Mountain in the same section; the sources do not confirm that it is the historic lookout or whether the historic cabin stands. The Forest Lookouts page gives the township as 46N in its header but T45N in an author's note; the Forest Service project says T46N. The 1922 item names Goose Nest mountain. A separate Ball Mtn lookout sign (Mendocino NF, about 1940) was not used. The register's June 2025 photo was not added as a new find.

Do not merge with us-ca-ball-mountain (Siskiyou County, Klamath NF, US 1383). Search results for Ball Mountain mostly describe that Siskiyou tower and must not be used for this one. No staffing or access facts found, so none are recorded. The register's photo credit (Upper Lake Ranger District Collection) has no image URL, so no photo was added. Only two sources, so confidence is medium.

One register entry plus one hobby site. The hobby page's 1933 bulletin quote names a 'Bald Rock Lookout Station' and a lookout, Fred Whitlock; it does not name Ball Rock, so it is not used. A separate NHLR entry, Ball Mountain Lookout, is a different site and should not be merged with this record. No new photos with image URLs were read.

The Mountain Democrat article shows no year; it says the tower was gifted '10 years ago' and gives a Thursday, Feb. 23 proposal deadline, which matches the 2017 sale notice, so it is probably from February 2017. The story calls it an undated Mountain Democrat article. No source read gives the outcome of the February 2017 sale; the City resolution declaring the tower surplus (evogov 40043.pdf) appeared only in search snippets and was not read. The brief's elevation is kept from NHLR, and FFLOS gives a different figure. The brief record is consistent with 80 ft (24.4 m). Access is left out because no source read gives access to the peak or to Gold Bug Park. Two WebSearch calls and five distinct page reads were used; the Mountain Democrat homepage fetch returned HTTP 429 and a later attempt at the old URL returned 404.

No source read gives current access or visiting rules, so access is omitted and the story gives no directions. Heights (60 ft in 1926 and 1971, 65 ft in 1948) and the 1911 versus 1926 build dates are unresolved and the story says so. The brief's 1926 build date matches the register field; the 1911 wooden tower is added as an event. The 1926 Livermore and Woodland items and the 1931 Timberman item are read only through the weebly compilation. The register has photo credits (Ron Kemnow, Mark Swift Collection) with no direct image URLs captured, so no photos entry was added. The 2008 CEQA item is a project description, not proof of completion. Confidence is medium because the dates and heights conflict.

Gone status rests on one FFLA list entry, with no date or cause in any source read, so the fate is thin. The Forest Lookouts page has nothing after 1983. Record ownership is unknown; the 1975 report calls it the only county-owned station with a fire lookout tower, so local ownership could be proposed for human review. Access level is left out of facts because no source read describes access today. A 2024 Merced County story about closing or merging fire stations names Ballico Station 92, but no source ties that station to this site, so it is not used. The FFLA list gives no NHLR registration for Barfield.

Built, staffing and removal are each sourced by at least one dated item. The CCC attribution comes only from Peakbagging; Forest Lookouts says men from the Vista Grande camp. Peakbagging's Barker Peak page says the cab stood from 1935 to the late 1960s, while the same page says the lookout was removed by 1970. Elevation 4360 ft (about 1329 m) appears on the Peakbagging Barker Peak page, not in the facts schema. No source describes trail access or current condition beyond the 2013 foundation photo, so access is left out of facts. The Forest Service Black Mountain page covers the Black Mountain lookout only as a 1926 build and a 1935 move.

Build date is disputed. NHLR Built field says 1947 but its description says built in the 1950s; Wikipedia says 1947 or 1945; an Aug 1945 clipping reports a station in operation on the hill; a Jan 1948 clipping says the new tower was still being built. The 1947 record is kept, not corrected. The sources suggest an earlier station existed and the current tower was finished around 1947-48, which is an inference from the clippings. Footprint disagrees: the 1948 clipping says the tower is 16 ft square, Wikipedia gives the tower as 20 by 20 ft, and the NHLR gives a 20 ft enclosed tower. height_m 6.1 uses the clipping's 20 ft platform height. Access level 'restricted' is an inference from Cal Fire administration and the radio-tower summit; no source states the cab's visitor status. Bay Area Peaks lists 'Agency: California State Parks' for the hike area, probably the reservoir SRA rather than the lookout; not used. No current staffing or condition source found; staffing is left out of facts. Wikipedia's references include a 1992 lease notice with personal contact details; not used. No photos added. One WebSearch used.

Brief height_m 18.3 matches 60 feet (NHLR). Brief built 1927 is stated as circa 1927 in NHLR; no correction proposed. Elevation 1,035 m (NHLR) matches the brief. Access moved from unknown to restricted per NHLR (undated quote from a 1991 visit, MVT 10/91, and the 2019 register text). No source read gives current staffing, current fire-detection use, or a 2020s visit. A June 2024 lightning fire that damaged transmitters on Bear Mountain appears in search results (KMPH, Fresno Bee, Newscast Studio) but the Fresno Bee page timed out and was not read, so it is left out; worth checking. Forest Lookouts and the 2007 report disagree on the house's fate only through the Register. The area is 'Squaw Valley' in these sources; a later name change was seen only in an unreliable mirror and was not verified. No photos added; the Register's 1955 Cal Fire photos have no image URLs in the text read.

Register is the only detailed source. Its Built field is 1980 for the current steel tower; the description places a 1933 CCC-era lookout on the same site, so both dates are kept and no correction is proposed. The brief says standing; no source dated after the 2008 list confirms the cab's current condition, so status is left at the record's value. The Cal Fire list is a 2008 document and says only that the lookout may be staffed that season; it is not evidence of current staffing. Access 'restricted' follows the Register's wording about locked gates. Not used: an ALERTCalifornia Facebook post on the lookout (fetch_text and WebFetch both returned only 'Facebook'), and a search snippet saying the lookout is no longer in service, which I could not confirm from a readable page. The Forest Lookouts Bear Mountain page had no article text beyond its index and header. No photos added; the Register lists a 1953 National Archives photo but I did not read its file. Page reads: 6 total, 1 WebSearch.

Only three sources were read. The most recent staffing and condition evidence is the 2019 register entry and a 2006 photo note, so current staffing and access are not confirmed. Access level is omitted; the only access fact is the register's 'some 6 miles from paved road'. Several Bear Mountain lookouts exist (Fresno County, Shasta-Bear with ALERTCalifornia cameras, Fowler, Siskiyou). This record was matched to the Siskiyou station by county, coordinates and the PeakBagging Siskiyou County entry; the 1939 Dry creek fire item on the weebly bear-mountain1.html page was not used because it is not confirmed to be this station. The register credits photos (Ron Kemnow 2008, Fred Johnson 2006) with no direct image URLs captured, so no photos entry was added.

History comes from one page (Forest Lookouts) that quotes 1936-1944 newspapers; I could not open the newspapers themselves. No removal date or site description found, so the story says only that FFLA lists it gone and that no source describes the site today. Staffing fact is historical (1944), not current. The FFLA row has no register number; numbers printed just above the row in the text belong to Bear Mountain (Fresno County). Brief record has no register entries, so nothing to correct.

The history sheet is undated and unsigned, and I fetched it over http because its https certificate has expired; its 'debris remains' statement may be old, so the story says only that the sheet says so. The sheet's section and township (T25N R6E sec 21) agree with Forest Lookouts (25N-6E-21). Do not confuse with Ben Lomond in Santa Cruz County (1954 fire photo) or Ben Lomond, Arkansas. The 1915 and 1930 staffing dates come from the sheet and the Abby diary it quotes; the 1920-1924 dates come from newspapers reprinted on Forest Lookouts.

Brief height_m 17.4 conflicts with the register's 30 ft tower; corrected to 9.1. Agency is disputed across sources (USFS per register; CDF/CAL FIRE per West Lookouts and Wikipedia) and the story says so. The Rumsey Fire citation is Wikipedia, used as a lead; its dates and arson finding are from its own text, which cites CAL FIRE reports that were not read. A Record Net 2004 article was blocked (HTTP 403). The Internet Archive record is public domain; no image URL was retrieved, so no photos entry. No staffing information found. Nothing read describes the site today. A non-primary summary says the tower was built in 1949; not used, the register and the 1948 photo record agree on 1948.

Thin record. The only dated claim (1968) comes from a personal GitHub note that cites nothing. The Forest Lookouts page gives only name and county. The FFLA row's register cell is blank; the FFLOS number printed above the Bidwell text in the cached page belongs to Berryessa Peak, so no register is claimed. The peakbagging table lists no national forest for this site. The same note is tagged 'destroyed' with no date; not used in the story. Worth a second look in Glenn County or Mendocino NF records if someone can reach them.

Destruction in the 2018 Camp Fire is well supported by three sources. The 1949 build date and the 1925 steel station may describe different towers; sources do not say whether the 1949 tower replaced the 1925 one. Staffing after 1928 is unresolved (Peakbagging contradicts itself). Access not recorded because no tower remains. Brief's height (19.8 m) and standing status corrected. The 1924 and 1925 newspaper items are quoted from a hobby site transcription, not the original papers.

Access is marked restricted, not unknown as in the brief, because the sources describe a working fire site with no public visiting arrangement; treat that as an inference. Staffing as_of is undated (USFS brochure). The 1916 and 1994 items are Mountain Democrat notices as reproduced on the californialookouts page, not the newspaper itself. Brief's 'events' correction: the 1935 original build was missing. The USFS PDF has interleaved columns and ligatures; quotes were copied from extracted text and need the ligature in 'staﬀed' to match. Lead not used: californialookouts also quotes a Sacramento Union item of September 15, 1911 that calls it the Big Hill lookout, so staffing may go back before 1916; the story's 'at least to 1916' remains true.

Very thin record. The NHLR detail page is the only substantive source and says very little is known. Build date: the record's 1930 is more precise than the Register's 1930's, so a correction is proposed rather than applied. The brief's kind 'two_story' is not supported by any source read; the Register gives no storey count, only the design resemblance to Green Mountain Lookout. Please check it. Brief's 'standing' is not stated by any source read; no current condition is recorded. Access 'restricted' is an inference from tribal land and Bureau of Indian Affairs administration; no source states visitor rules, so the story now says not to assume public access and to ask the tribe or BIA first. The Forest Lookouts page has no body text beyond its heading and one line. Not read: Thornton's 1986 survey. No photos added; the Register shows a Fred Johnson photo but I did not read its file. Page reads: 4 total (NHLR, Forest Lookouts twice, Hupa Wikipedia). WebSearch: 1.

The register is firm on the 1980 removal and on nothing remaining, but the build date and tower height conflict with the 1952 and 1954 items. Those two items were read only as quoted on the hobby site; originals were not checked. The register's photo caption 'Billy's Peak Lookout - 1953' has no image URL in what we read, so no photo was added. Peakbagging lists 'Billys Peak (LO site)', which agrees with removal.

Status is unknown, and the lookouts' names differ across newspaper items. Do not use the 2001 'Black Butte lookout tower collapses' article or the 2021 'On the lookout' article from The Nugget (Sisters, Oregon): both concern a different Black Butte near Sisters, Oregon. The brief's 'ground' kind is not confirmed by any source read; the register calls it a 'structure' with a narrow window set. No photos with image URLs were read; the register lists a 2009 'Lookout Site' photo credited to Ron Kemnow, but no image was fetched.

Brief records to check: height_m 4.0 is not supported by any page read here, so it is left out. The fflos_registered date (April 15, 2020) is not visible in the cached FFLOS text, so it is left out. The brief's coordinates (41.366537, -122.348119) differ from the west_us_lookouts point (41.39348, -122.36486); not resolved. Sources disagree on the 1975 vs 1977 move and on which 1962 structure was lost. The 1931 start comes from newspaper clippings only; no structure type is given for 1931. The FS sheet says the building was moved, so the 'today' paragraph describes only the foundation the sheet names.

Single source (FFLOS register entry). Two searches and the FFLOS sister pages added no second source. The brief's fflos_registered date (January 22, 2020) is not visible in the cached FFLOS text, so it is left out. The 30-foot tower height is converted to 9.1 m for height_m. No access or visit information was found, so those keys are left out. The brief's coordinates were not checked against another source.

Record height_m 152.4 is wrong; 30 ft is 9.1 m (see corrections). The record's 1939 built year is the current BC-301 cab. A July 1922 glass house on a thirty-foot tower is an earlier structure on the same peak; the Register does not say whether the 4AR cab was that house, so the two are not matched. 'Siskiyou Bear Lookout' and the 2008 closure appear only on Forest Lookouts; two searches found nothing on either. Current status and access are not found in any source read, so the story says so and gives no access rule. Only two sources were read. The FFLA California list was grepped, but its layout did not allow reliable registry numbers, so none were taken from it.

Built year, design size and 1975 last staffing come from the register; the FFLA-SDRC page supports the 1979 sighting and the 1986 window. Removal date is disputed (1983 vs by 1986), and the story reports both. Elevation disagrees: the register's 3,168 ft (966 m) vs about 4,048-4,051 ft at nearly the same coordinates, so the correction is only proposed. The cab code differs (BC-301 vs C3), so the story gives only the 14x14-ft size. No source says whether the public can reach the repeater site, so access is omitted rather than guessed. Do not confuse with the San Bernardino NF Black Mountain Lookout on Barton Peak, a different tower.

No current status, staffing or access found. Two searches returned only other Black Mountain lookouts (Plumas NF near Milford, Wyoming, Idaho) and a 2013 CAL FIRE incident on Black Mountain Road near Auberry; none of those is this tower and none is used. Record ownership 'federal' is not checked: the Register names CDF as administrator and Sierra NF as cooperator, so the editor may want to review it. The undated 'two story' note on Forest Lookouts conflicts with the Register on when the room beneath the cab was added. Height 6.1 m comes from the 20-foot tower on Forest Lookouts; the Register gives no height. The description's '(MVT 10/91)' credit suggests the 'recently replaced' stairway may date from the early 1990s.

No staffing history (first/last staffed, notable fires) found in the sources checked; story says so plainly rather than guessing. Minor built-year (1934 vs 1935) and tower-height (10' vs 11') discrepancies between NHLR's narrative and structured fields/Recreation.gov are noted but not fully resolved.

The sbnfa.com page in the brief returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The current-conditions 'Closed for the season' line on the Forest Service page was read on 2026-10-08 and may not reflect a later reopening. NHLR's undated 'seven days a week' staffing claim conflicts with the Forest Service's fire-season hours. The NHLR description says the cab was restored after the 1980s but gives no year, so no restoration event is recorded. A photo log (peakbagging.com, May 2022) gives a 14 ft cab on a 20 ft steel tower; that was not used because it is a single hobbyist source that conflicts with the NHLR cab dimensions, which were not quoted in the story. The 1928 and 1929 Rita Morris items are secondhand quotations on a lookout history site; the originals were not checked. No notable fires were found in the sources.

The brief's kind (two_story) is left as recorded; FFLOS describes a CL-100 cab on an 11-foot block tower. The brief's fflos_registered date (December 22, 2019) is not visible in the cached FFLOS text, so it is left out. The 11-foot tower is converted to 3.4 m for height_m. No access information was found for the peak. A Los Padres trail page for Black Mountain Trail was found but does not name the lookout, so it was not used. The Smith Mountain page is a different site and its registration date (June 19, 2010) is not used for this lookout. A Los Padres lookout list (Black Mountain 1964, 11 ft) was seen only as a search snippet and not fetched, so it is not cited.

Status is standing per the 2017 register text and the May 2025 hike report, which describes it as dilapidated and not safe to climb. No source found a fire at the lookout. Last staffing year not found; newspaper items run to 1946. Elevation differs across sources (7,765 / 7,769 / 7,792 ft); register figure matches the record. The 1933 newspaper item also reports a personal arrest of the previous lookout; left out of the story. Built year 1935 comes from the register alone; no construction record found. Access is hike-only in wilderness; no current closure notice found. Do not encourage climbing.

Coordinates conflict: the Register gives 40.840149, -121.175983, while the record's West US Lookouts point is 40.82361, -121.16222, about 2.2 km apart. Neither is corrected here, and the story gives only the county and forest. The height of 13.7 m is the 45-foot tower; the Register gives no cab height. Only two sources exist, and the Forest Lookouts page has only a location code. Status, staffing and access were not found in two searches. Search results mixed in the Black Mountain lookout near Milford in Plumas NF, a different tower, which is not used.

Record is ground and gone with no build date, staffing or site description. The 1931, 1933 and 1934 items come only through the Forest Lookouts page that quotes them; the original newspapers were not checked. The 1934 notice names South Fork Mountain. Whether that is the same site as FFLA's Blake Mountain point (40.61424, -123.56070) is not confirmed. Two web searches found nothing specific to this lookout. Access and staffing are left out as unknown. PeakVisor's summit coordinates (40.614024, -123.561281) match FFLA's Blake Mountain point. The 1931 clipping spells the river 'Mad Rover'; the story uses Mad River. FFLA also lists a South Fork Mountain tower in Shasta County (40.65408, -122.52501), so the name alone does not link the 1934 notice to this site.

History is well sourced (NHLR plus 1924-1939 newspaper transcriptions, which are secondary and were not checked against the original papers). Current access and rental status were not found in the sources read, so there is no access or visit block. Camera feeds named Bloomer Lookout appear online (ALERTCalifornia, opencctv) but I could not confirm they sit on this tower, so they are left out. Staffing names come from the transcriptions only. The dedication date was corrected from early July to June 1925: the June 24, 1925 Gridley Herald reports a Saturday dedication with Pratt giving the speech, and the July 5 article describes the same event later.

Agency conflict: the record and the register name the U.S. Forest Service as administrator, while the register text and ALERTCalifornia say CAL FIRE operates the lookout. Both are stated in the story. The ALERTCalifornia post's 1966 CCC era wording conflicts with the register's 1934 CCC date; the register is followed. The CAL FIRE fact sheet is undated (CDN link). The access note is dated 1991. No staffing record or fire history for this lookout beyond the 1920s newspaper items. Living New Deal (CCC context) returned 403 and was not used. The NHLR photos are all rights reserved, so none were added.

The FFLA California list has three Blue Mountain entries (Calaveras, Kern, Modoc); this story covers only the Kern one at 35.75994, -118.75949, and the record's enclosed_tower kind matches FFLA's Encl. Tower. The newspaper items come through the Forest Lookouts page that quotes them; originals were not checked. A web search snippet describing a 1935 Forest Service tower near Woody was traced to a geocache (GCQBEX) for a Blue Mountain in Montana, so it is disregarded. No construction date, removal date or site description was found. Staffing is known only for 1953.

Record height_m 7.6 (25 ft) is supported only by the 1931 report; NHLR says 20 ft and the October 1929 papers say 22 ft. I left height out of facts for your choice. The 1962 house is a rebuild on the existing tower and was not in the brief's events, so I added it as 'replaced'. The NHLR staffing line is undated; as_of is the date I read it. The NHLR's 1929 date and the 1963 newspaper's 1931 date conflict; the story says so. FLO also lists a separate tree lookout, Blue Mountain Tree (East Peak), that this record does not cover. No rental or access notice was found, so there is no access or visit block.

Status: both FFLA lists read Standing for the tree (statewide list: Blue Mountain Tree (East Peak); county list: Modoc, Tree Standing). An earlier reading that the statewide list said Gone was wrong; the Gone rows nearby belong to other lookouts. No dated source after 1948 for the tree itself. Record height_m 6.1 (20 ft) matches the 1945 proposed tower, not the 1948 NGS description of a tree about 40 ft; not corrected, needs a human look. The NGS text is quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not read from NGS. Two web searches found nothing usable about this tree (results were other Blue Mountains and an unrelated Modoc tower). No staffing or fire history found. No photos. Do not encourage climbing.

The Register's 'still staffed each year' wording is repeated by dangerousroads.org, so it is not independent confirmation; the Register's own visit reports point the other way. No 2025 or 2026 source on current staffing or access was found. The summit road description comes from a road-trip site, not a land manager. A Scott Valley News Facebook post about the tower was not readable (login wall). A SummitPost entry for a Blue Ridge in Tulare County (1930, 60 ft) is a different tower and was not used. Our record's height 33.5 m matches the 1952 survey, not the Register's 80 ft. No photos added; the Register page carries captions only, with no image URLs.

Unresolved: (1) the 1933 radio item says 'the tower or the stone cabin' at Blue Ridge, which sits badly with the 1930 move; (2) the register gives 60 feet for the original tower, Angeles Adventures gives 50 feet for the moved tower; (3) Forest Lookouts spells it Bodel Peak, the register and Angeles Adventures Bodle Peak. No source read describes public access to the site today. The firelookout.org index also lists a different Blue Ridge (Tulare County, relocated to the Tulare County Fairgrounds); it is not this lookout. Record status 'gone' is consistent with the sources if read as tower only; the stone cabin is the surviving structure.

The record's name, 2010 removal, 2011 restoration and fairgrounds location check out. The open question is what is displayed: FFLOS says only the cabin is on ground-level display, while the 2011 FFLA report and the 2017 Sun-Gazette describe the tower or lookout building being displayed, and the 2024 Buck Rock post describes the decommissioned lookout on display; the record's kind 'ground' may reflect this, so it was left unchanged. Height 18.3 m is converted from the register's 60 feet for the tower; the original-site record (us-ca-blue-ridge-tulare-county) lists 22.9 m and was not checked here. No current opening hours found; access is 'public' only in the sense of fair-time display. No photos added.

Two records describe this lookout: this one (the mountain site, coordinates match FFLOS) and us-ca-blue-ridge-lookout-site-at-tulare-county-fairgrounds (the display). Story covers both, as the brief asks. Unresolved: (1) height: FFLOS and the December 1930 report say 60 feet, the April 1931 report says 70 feet above the base; the record's 22.9 m matches neither, so the correction above is for a human to confirm. (2) Display: the 2017 Sun-Gazette says the building is on permanent display; FFLOS says only the cabin is on ground-level display. The FFLOS entry is undated apart from its assessment mark, so its date is unknown. (3) Location: 'east of Exeter' (1930) and '15 miles east of Springville' (2017). (4) FFLOS says the facilities are under the State Department of Fish and Game, while CAL FIRE is listed as administrator; not resolved. Newspaper details are from the Forest Lookouts transcriptions of the Fresno Bee, not from the papers. The fairgrounds record's claim of visitor days in 2011 and 2024 is supported by sources [4] and [5]. No current status found for the mountain house and garage, and no new photos added. Other Blue Ridge records (us-ca-blue-ridge, us-ca-blue-ridge-2) were not checked.

Two web searches found no page about this tower. The Weebly file name says broad-camp but the page heading reads BOARD CAMP; the story uses the page heading. The 1934 and 1953 items come through the Forest Lookouts page that quotes them, and the originals were not checked. No construction date, removal date or site description was found. The 1931 Blake Mountain clipping mentions Board Camp mountain only as a place on a telephone route, so it is not used as evidence of a lookout.

Height is disputed (60 ft register vs 50 ft Angeles Adventures). Access level is not stated by any source read, so facts.access is omitted. The Woolsey Fire claim rests on the register alone. The register spells Mulholland as 'Muholland' (kept as written in the quote). The register's Halloween 1930 sentence about an earlier timber lookout is left out because it does not say that lookout stood at Bodle. The Triunfo register also says a tower on that summit was built in May 1930 and burned in the November 1930 Potrero fire, which does not square with a Bodle tower arriving in 1934; check before relying on the Triunfo dates. A search summary gave a 50-foot height and a Woolsey claim it could not verify; neither was used.

History is well sourced and consistent: FFLOS (built 1946, removed 1989), the LA Times (March 16, 1989, Wednesday demolition) and Forest Lookouts (March 15, 1989) agree. No source describes the site today, so no access level is recorded. The OC Parks listing title suggests a hike route to the lookout, but the listing text we fetched carries no description, so verify before adding access. Elevation disagrees: the Times gives Bolero Peak as 1,600 feet, the FFLOS record gives the site as 1,756 ft (535 m), and the record's 535.2 m is kept. Agency: FFLOS and the Times say Orange County or its Fire Department; Forest Lookouts places the site in Cleveland National Forest, which may describe the land rather than the owner. The LA Times line that the structures were built by state prison work crews refers to the lookouts generally; Bolero is not named in that sentence. The staffing 'unstaffed' value rests on 'not used for over a decade' (Forest Lookouts, 1989).

Brief status standing holds (NHLR 2019; staffed 2021). Brief access 'unknown' set to restricted. No height_m: NHLR gives only the 9-foot block tower, not total height. Peakbagging photo is dated July 2012. A 2021 River Complex (Haypress) fire link to this lookout appears only in social posts I could not open, so it is not in the story. Built 1934 from the register; a 1924 newspaper item already refers to a Bonanza King lookout station, so an earlier structure may have existed; not resolved. Built year (1912), Ed Bish as ranger and the 29-ft ladder are consistent across the register and FFLA-SDRC.
