Core history (1948 tower, 1983 end of service, 2011-12 restoration, 2012 reopening, FFLA staffing from 2012) is supported by two or more sources. The 1921/1934 earlier towers rest on NHLR, FFLA, SDUT 2012 and Friends. The brief's events not verified here and left out of the story: the 2010 agreement with State Parks, the 2016 'opens' item (the NHLR link title only), the 2017 mast and leak work, the 2019 FFLA $300 grant, and the 2023 $300 door-frame grant. Gone status is from the FFLA California list only; no source gives the removal date or how it ended. Register NHLR US 394 CA 58 appears on the FFLA list but the record's registers field is empty and no NHLR page is cached; not checked. Staffing after 1957 unknown. No build date in any source read; the record has none either. Almost all history comes from one page (Kemnow), which quotes 1937-1977 notices and Forest Service documents. Access is private land per the Register; the story does not describe any route and advises staying off private land. History is newspaper-only (1922-1932, via the Kemnow page). No build date, design, staffing after 1932, or removal date in any source. Standing lookout; the record's 1942 build date matches the NHLR and fire-lookouts.org for the present cab, so no correction is proposed. Only two sources: a 1932 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and one county-list row. Elevations disagree and no source explains why: the register gives 9,127 ft (2,782 m) for the site, which is the record value; a 1933 newspaper gives 9,232 ft; a 1935 newspaper gives 9,400 ft; the NPS trail listing runs up to 9,235 ft. Thin record. Left unresolved, so not in resolved_conflicts. No source states that the tower was completed or when it was removed; the story therefore says 'Removed' and 'gone' without a date and does not claim a build year. Elevation figures disagree slightly between sources (8,408 ft brief/NHLR vs 8,502 ft fire-lookouts.org); story avoids stating a number. Brief build year 1933 confirmed by NHLR and Forest Lookouts. Brief access 'unknown' set to restricted; I did not check the Forest Service rental page. County is contested (NHLR Shasta versus FLO and survey record Trinity); the proposed correction needs your check. The record has no height and the NHLR gives only elevation, so no height_m. Rental status unconfirmed: Campflare shows the site as Closed and says a 2025 rental was anticipated but not on Recreation.gov; a Roamze listing repeats the 2025 expectation. Build history is disputed: the Chamber of Commerce says built 1934 and rebuilt 1960, the Register and the 1965 article point to 1966. Build year 1935 is supported by the Register Built field and the 1935 newspaper reports; the Register's 1933 CCC claim is the only dissent and is reported in the story. All history comes from newspaper items that Forest Lookouts transcribes; the original papers were not opened. Record height_m 152.4 is wrong; the register describes a 20 ft tower. Elevation differs across sources (9,000 / 9,200 / 10,500 ft in clippings vs 9,288 ft in the register). Tower status conflicts. Peakbagging says the 30 ft tower came down about 2004 and only a 1949 benchmark remains. Built date 1932 is well supported by 1932 clippings. Removal is only 'the 1980s' per the register, likely late 1980s; the record's 1980 is a decade start, not a sourced year. Build year is disputed: NHLR says 1942, Peakbagging's June 2010 note says 1944. Built 1943 rests on the register alone (plus its 1943 photo caption); the 1935 proposal is a single newspaper report quoted by Forest Lookouts. Brief build year 1935 confirmed. Brief access 'unknown' set to closed on the Register's locked-gate note, with the land-control conflict stated. No fire history found. Elevation differs slightly between the brief (1778.8 m / 5,836 ft) and Recreation.gov (5,980 ft) — not flagged as a correction since it's a minor discrepancy in secondary description text, but worth a glance if precision matters. Two distinct prior structures are easy to conflate: (1) a 1924 lookout on Bear Basin Butte itself, burned 1936, unrelated to the current building; (2) the Camp Six/Upper Coon Mountain cabin (built 1934 per NHLR, or first built 1923 per FFLOS with an undated later replacement cabin) that was moved to Bear Basin Butte in 1996 (recreation.gov) or 1997 (FFLOS) and is the structure standing today. The tower record's own 'built: 1934' event matches NHLR but not FFLOS; left as-is since it's directly sourced. No corrections proposed to the tower record itself -- its fields (name, location, status 'relocated', agency) all check out against these sources. The FFLA CA list entry confirms 'Relocated' status and the NHLR US 288/CA 21 numbers; an adjacent table row for a different lookout (Basalt Hill, NHLR US 880/CA 90) sits right next to this one in the cached HTML and could be misread as a conflicting register number for Bear Basin Butte -- it is not, it belongs to the preceding row.

Build date and location are disputed across four sources (1923 Camp Six Mountain; 1934 Upper Coon Mountain per NHLR; 1935 French Hill per FS; 1939 per NGS). The NHLR and FS pages describe the relocated structure at Bear Basin Butte, not the original site. The Bear Basin Butte record (NHLR US 288, CA 21) should carry its own history: the NHLR says an earlier Bear Basin lookout was built in 1924 and burned in 1936 after a lightning strike; that record was not checked here. The name Camp Six may come from a CCC camp on French Hill Road; a search snippet suggested this but no page was read to confirm it, so it is not used. No source describes access to the piers today. The Bear Basin rental is bookable, but the access key is omitted here because it describes the relocated cab, not the Camp Six site.

Brief's 2020 registration date (Dec 12, 2020) is not in the cached register page (Date Registered value is blank), so it is left out. Register and Peakbagging disagree on whether anything remains; the USGS datasheet cited by Peakbagging was not read. The 1936 item is secondhand via a volunteer site. Only two sources, one of them a register entry with little detail. No staffing, fire, or access records found. The register page does not describe current conditions beyond the six piers. Identity unconfirmed. The only record is an OSM way with name, man_made=tower, tower:type=observation and a condition note; no register (NHLR or FFLOS), staffing, or news record found. Removal date unknown per the register. The foundation statement is undated on the register page. No source read gives a build year; the Rocky Butte record says only that the cab replaced a CCC-era lookout on Cerro Alto, so the story says CCC-era with no year. No source read gives a build date, a builder, a staffing history, or the date the lookout tower came down. The weebly Chalk Mountain page has only its heading, so it was not cited. Well sourced on history (newspaper run in the Forest Lookouts page, register visit report, 2025 chapter report, park guide). Single source: the FFLOS register page. The Forest Lookouts Cherry Hill page has the name and section heading but no entries, so no staffing or fire records were used. Sources are thin. The NHLR is the main source; the Forest Lookouts page supplies the 1990 budget-cut note; Peakbagging.com has a 2006 photo caption; the Bay Area Peaks trip report is undated. The Forest Lookouts page also lists 1931-1938 items about Signal Ridge and a Greenwood lookout, and a 1956 Ground Observer Corps entry that does not clearly name this site; none of these were used. The ffla-ccwr.org page in the brief could not be fetched (name resolution failed), so it was not read. No current owner or access policy was found. No source read places the station on the summit, so the story does not say so.

Brief status gone holds: the 2021 blog found only remnants, and the FFLA California index row for Cold Springs (Trinity) reads Tower, Gone, with no registry number. No agency or current access source was found, so no access level is recorded. The Forest Lookouts index also lists a Cold Springs under Humboldt County; this record follows the Trinity County heading and the FFLA coordinates. CAL FIRE's Lookouts list has a different Cold Springs Lookout in its Mendocino column (not this site). The 1934 facts rest on newspaper excerpts as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the original newspaper was not read. Today's condition rests on one blog visit.

Brief had no build event; 1934 added from NHLR and the weebly page. height_m 6.1 is converted from the NHLR 20-foot tower height. Brief's record (elevation 1674.6 m, agency, registration 2020) matches NHLR; no corrections. Staffing, access, and current condition beyond the 2024 Forest Service project were not found in the pages read; the 1942 and 1953 Klamath County items seen in a search snippet were not attributed because the page was not read. Whether the camera and solar work was installed is unconfirmed.

Two sources. The first structure's exact year is not given, so no build event is dated before 1936 (the 1911 staffing event is a separate fact). Staffing rests on one October 1911 Morning Union item quoted by Forest Lookouts. One WebSearch returned a Columbia Hill schoolhouse in North Columbia and nearby lookouts, nothing on this lookout. Brief record checked: kind, county, agency, coordinates and built year (1936 register field) match. No access facts written: no source read describes public access.

The Forest Service page (updated August 31, 2026) lists the site as closed after the Timber and Plaskett Fires and says it is reachable only on foot; the story says so and does not encourage a visit. The record's 'all-metal tower' design conflicts with the register and Forest Lookouts descriptions of a wooden ground cab later sided in metal; it is kept in facts.design and the record's design field is not on the corrections list, so please decide whether to change it. status stays 'standing' in the record; the status_note is a judgement call (standing, but full of radio gear and not in use as a lookout) and can be dropped. Staffing 'unstaffed as of 2023' rests on the 2023 year-end report and the 1990 last-staffed date. The 2024 and 2025 Cal-South annual reports (cr-cal-south-2024.pdf, cr-cal-south-2025.pdf) show the same repeater-gear wording in search snippets but were not read, because of the page budget. A 2025 report snippet (cr-cal-s-m-2025.pdf) says there is no current direction to move the repeater equipment out of the lookout; also unread. The FFLA Monterey page gives its location as '60 miles southeast of Monterey', which looks wrong, so it is not used. Historical cab and roof facts are from the register and Forest Lookouts page; the 1923 build year is consistent across both. No new photos. Budget used: 6 distinct pages and 2 web searches.

The build history rests on the register alone: 1931 for the first lookout on a water tank, 1938 for the present K-brace tower. No second source explains the sequence. The record's Wikidata value (1938) is noted only. Access and the hiking-only route come from SummitPost, a climbing guide, so treat them as secondary; the register does not describe public access. No NRHP listing, staffing record or visit report was found, so the staffing status is unknown. The FFLA list gives only 'Standing'. The 2020 SCU Lightning Complex coverage found in search concerns Lick Observatory and is not about this lookout, so it is left out. Access level 'permission' is my reading of the SummitPost advice; the register does not state a permit rule. Read budget: three page reads; the cached FFLA and Wikipedia-list pages were checked locally.

The 1980 closure and 1985 fire agree across KVPR and Fresno County Fire. The 1935 build date comes from KVPR alone; Forest Lookouts gives no build date. The Fresno County Fire line about a station opened in the early 1930s refers to McKenzie Fire Camp, not this lookout, and was not used. The Internet Archive Black Cards items are public domain per their rights notes, but no direct image URL was verified, so no photos were added. Whether the summit is public is not stated in any source; access key omitted.

The register files it with former fire lookouts but describes a WWII Aircraft Warning Service tower, so the story does not call it a fire lookout or a non-lookout (the brief's kind 'ground' fits). Only two sources were read: the register and Wikipedia. Two web searches found nothing on the post beyond the register, and the Corona Heritage museum page turned up in search without any AWS content. The 2018 exhibit reference is quoted from the register and was not checked directly. The NPS aircraft-warning PDF covers Joshua Tree, not Corona, and was not used. Suggest asking Corona Heritage Park & Museum about the post's location and any AWS records.

Both staffing items are newspaper notices quoted secondhand by Forest Lookouts (Siskiyou Daily News); the originals were not checked. The October 1929 notice may mean Friday was a fire guard at the Trumble ranch rather than at the lookout; the story now gives the notice's own wording (of the Cory lookout) and also reports the Trumble ranch post, so check it. No build date, design, access or removal detail was found in any source. The Siskiyou County page on Forest Lookouts lists Cory Peak under Klamath National Forest with a legal description only (40N-7W-18); not used. The brief record (kind unknown, gone, agency, county, coordinates) matches the sources; no corrections.

Build date is the main dispute (Register 1953; unit history early 1940s; archive caption December 1952). The 1935-1941 lookout at the pass may be a predecessor station rather than the same building. The 1976 and 1985 items rest on former firefighters' recollections printed on the Register page. A Facebook group comment (not used, social media) says the land was sold in the 2000s; ownership is unverified. The 'closed' access level reflects abandonment and the 1986 closure, not a posted notice. Kings County per Register. The Fresno-Kings unit history says the site overlooked Sun Valley, while the 1935 item says it overlooked the Kettleman Plains; the story keeps the 1935 wording, which is footnoted to that item.

The 1915 to 1921 staffing and the 1915 fire come from newspaper items and a forest chronology that the Forest Lookouts page quotes; the originals were not checked. No source found describes the site today or gives access, so there is no access key and the story says so. Paradise Craggy is a separate lookout and was not used. Brief record matches the register (ground, gone, US 2020, CA 137); no correction needed.

Four sources agree on the 1934 build, the 1989 burn and the concrete slab. The 2023 Stanislaus post refers to 1938 and the 2024 post dates its photo to August 1953; neither changes the story. No staffing, fire or access source for this site was found, so those keys are omitted. The Weebly Crandall page holds only a title and a removal field, so it is not cited. No photo URL was captured, so no photos are added.

The brief's 1931 build and 1998 NHLR registration are confirmed. NRHP listing (1996) and the 1995 nomination were not in the brief's events and are added. The Wikipedia 'still in use in the 1980s' is a decade, not a year, so no year-specific event was created. The 1995 nomination's planned restoration and helitack use are from the nomination text itself; I found no source confirming the restoration was done. Access is marked public because the trip report and the NRHP nomination describe visitor access to the lookout, but the sources do not confirm whether the cab interior is open to visitors; check before treating that as settled. Staffing as_of is the 1995 nomination date, the only staffing detail found. The Atlas Obscura and Parkwolf listings were seen only in search results and are not cited.

Build year: register 1914 vs East Bay Times around 1916; both kept. Staffing span: EBT says the Mendenhall family held the job 1926-1940, but a May 1942 clipping shows Henrietta back on duty; the register says 1942. End of service: register 1973 vs a family recollection of 1969. Demise: register says removed (date unknown, before 1986); EBT says vandals burned it in the 1970s; no date given for either. Location conflict in the record (FFLOS 37.606031, -121.620286 vs west_us_lookouts 37.60083, -121.61639) is about 0.7 km apart and was not resolved. Elevation: register gives 2,962 ft (903 m); EBT gives 2,675 ft for the ridge; the record's 902.8 m was left alone. Name variants: the register uses both 'Cattlemen's' and 'Stockmen's' Protective Association; the EBT and clippings use 'Stockmens'. The story treats them as naming variants of the same Livermore group, which the sources do not state outright. The register photo is already in the record; no new photos. Current ownership and public access are not documented beyond the register's 'Private Ranch' label. The Livermore Heritage Guild PDF in the search results did not fetch.

Status gone rests on the FFA California list, which shows Crystal Peak as Gone next to the FFLOS number; the FFLOS detail page gives only an unknown removal date. No source describes what remains today or whether the site is open. The FFA list gives coordinates 39.59928, -120.07070, about 5 km from the FFLOS coordinates used in the record; Wikipedia's peak coordinates (39 33 28 N, 120 05 18 W) agree with FFLOS, so the record is unchanged. The brief's conflict note says the lookouts share a register number; the three US numbers differ, and the state number CA 126 also appears on an NHLR entry, which may be what was meant. The 1938 smoke sighting is not tied to a confirmed fire at the lookout. The 1939 and 1940 road closures are recorded as other events, not closures of the lookout.

County disagrees: the NHLR page says Ventura County, while the California Lookouts page and the FFLA county list say Santa Barbara County; the record says Ventura, so a human should check the county line before changing it (not proposed as a correction here). The 1970 staffing rests only on a reader comment. The asterisk on 'Standing*' in the FFLA list is not explained in the source text read. The AWS cabin's WWII-era date is not given beyond 'World War II'. Road conditions come from undated or older web pages and may have changed.

Register and chapter agree on the 1918 timber tower, the 1930s steel tower, the 1933 park incorporation and the mid-1980s loss, but disagree on the cab code (BC-301 vs C3) and the cause of loss. Brief's '1930 built' was rounded from the register's 'Circa 1930's'. Access set to public from Wikipedia's hike description, a secondary source; the brief had unknown. Staffing items for 1939 and 1944 come from a lookout history site quoting old newspapers; the newspapers themselves were not checked. No photo added: no image URL with a verified licence.

Thin record: the register entry is the only substantive source for the 1914 date, the photo, the removal status and the private-housing note; the Weebly list adds only the word Removed. Not used: a 1986 TDAR record (core.tdar.org document 47246) for a BLM land parcel called Darby Knob, which does not describe the lookout in its catalogue entry; and a 2013 blog that repeats the 1914 photo with a doubtful place name. The 1914 photo is credited by the register to the Stanislaus National Forest Archive; no image URL was extracted, so no photo entry. Brief kind 'platform' is doubtful. Register says 'circa 1914' where the brief says 1914.

Current access is not established: the register does not say whether the site is open, and the PeakVisor trail note is a third-party listing. The brief's kind enclosed_tower matches the register's enclosed timber tower; no brief fields were found wrong. Register photos not extracted to photo entries (1933 tent photo courtesy Mark Swift Collection; 2008 foundation photo courtesy Ron Kemnow), no image URLs found in the text.

Build year conflicts (1932 steel tower per fire-lookouts.org vs 1934 CCC tower per NHLR); both are reported. The brief's L-4 design is only the 1932 cab; current cab is C-3(L). The brief's NHLR registration date (2019-12-23) does not appear in the cached register text, so no nhlr_registered event was added. A Deadwood Lookout Rec Cabin in Idaho (destinationwild.com) is a different tower and was excluded. The EverybodyWiki article is flagged as AI-generated and was not used. No notable fires and no recreation.gov listing found for the California tower. Access level set to restricted based on the register text; no rental program found.

Brief matches the sources (Trinity County, ground, Gone). The 1933-34 construction, staffing plan and road details come only from newspaper excerpts quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers themselves were not read. The 1933 staffing item is a plan, so it is not logged as staffed. No removal date or method found anywhere. The Trinity County list page gives the location as 35N-10W-36. No FFLOS or NHLR register entry found (firetower.org California index has no match). No photos found.

Significant three-way disagreement on the current tower's height/origin/install year across all three sources used; flagged in both the story and resolved_conflicts rather than silently picking one. Brief's access was 'public'; narrowed to 'restricted' with a note since sources say it's only open to the public when staffed (intermittently, via volunteers). Did not independently verify the Buck Rock Foundation's current program status beyond what fire-lookouts.org states. The 1930 two-room house and 1943 telephone-line rebuild sentences were confirmed live on californialookouts.weebly.com but had no evidence entry in this file; added 1930/1943 events and folded their quotes into the existing cite-3 evidence entry.

Brief matches the sources (Shasta County, enclosed tower, Gone). Only one dated item was found (June 1945 staffing, quoted secondhand from The Dunsmuir News). Forest naming differs within the Forest Lookouts county list (Shasta NF for Delta Point, Shasta-Trinity NF for Girard Ridge); the story reports this rather than resolving it. Unlinked lead, not used: a 2018 Delta Fire near Lakehead (CAL FIRE incident page, seen only in a search snippet, roughly 3 km from these coordinates) shares the name. No source ties it to the lookout, so it is left out. No FFLOS or NHLR entry found; no photos found.

Brief matches the sources (Siskiyou County, ground, Gone, Klamath NF). The only dated history is the 1958 Chronological History entry, quoted secondhand; the set-up date is not given, so the story says described in 1958. The 'Removed' evidence is a one-word status line on the Forest Lookouts page. No FFLOS or NHLR entry found; no photos found; mindat.com returned 403 and was not used.

Thin record: two lists and no dated events. Two searches returned nothing about this site (results were other Devil's Peak and Devil's Head towers, plus a 1993 notice for Valley Springs Peak, which is a different site). The story body is about 60 words, below the 120-word floor, because nothing more is sourced; it was not padded. Record fields agree with both sources (lat/lon, county, agency, gone status). Fact-check 2026-10-10: removed the unsourced 'ground-level structure' gloss from the story, because the FFLA page has no legend for the Ground type, and added the second source to the first sentence. Worth trying: Stanislaus National Forest records for former lookouts and Calaveras County historical society files.

Two WebSearch queries found only New York's Dickinson Hill Fire Tower (us-ny-dickinson-hill), a different tower; do not merge them. Source spells the town Montpeliter once and Montpellier elsewhere; the story uses Montpellier. The 30-ft height is converted to 9.1 m. The Forest Lookouts excerpts are transcriptions of newspapers and were not checked against the papers. The June 1941 and May 1942 board orders have near-identical wording and are presented as two dated orders. Not found: contractor, removal date, current condition, public access. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story now says the supervisors set aside money for communications (not that they paid for them), the station was providing fire protection (not meant to protect), and the board committed $200 on condition of a Merced match (not offered); the lookout-station and supervisors sentences were reworded away from the excerpt's phrasing. Merced County placement is now quoted from the page heading. The June 1941 order's Stanislaus attribution is an inference from its wording, kept.

The build date is the main open question: NHLR says 1935, and newspapers describe 1938-40 construction. The record's height_m of 23.0 is not supported by any source read, so it was left out of facts. The record's kind three_story conflicts with the NHLR's two-story tower. A 1950 Daily Independent Journal item in the Forest Lookouts list reports a dedication on June 8, 1950, probably a retrospective column; unresolved and not used. The rental listing is cited only for its repeat of the 1935 and 1975 dates; the story does not say the lookout is rented out. The NextDoor post shows only '28 Sep' with no year. The 1961 death is reported without the name. The ffla-ccwr and firelookout.org pages were not read.

Built date, 1936 staffing and the 2009 removal are well sourced. Fate after 2012 is not: no source read says whether the tower was rebuilt at Davis, and none describes the site now. The 2014 excess-property entry is from the weebly page and is a listing, not a sale. Two web searches used; no later update found. Brief's agency (U.S. Forest Service) matches the Register; the CEQA notice shows CAL FIRE as the 2009 public agency. Photo leads, not recorded because licenses were not checked: archive.org Knedler 1952 photos of Digger Butte (casbcfm_000226, casbcfm_000228). FFLOS 2018 registration (April 3, 2018) verified on firetower.org but not used in the story.

Brief's height_m 7.6 conflicts with the Register's 10-foot tower; proposed 3.05 with correction. Elevation in the brief matches the Register; the 8,327 ft figure in the 2017 report and Peakbagging is a documented disagreement. The 1940 item spells the relief lookout's name Maynerd in one place and Maynard in another. Staffing is documented through 1940 only in newspapers; the Register's present-tense staffing claim is undated. Access and climbing status are not in the sources read.

The record's 1974 build date and elevation (NHLR 7,145 ft = 2,178 m; record 2177.8 m) match the NHLR, so no correction is proposed. Sources disagree on the history between 1948 and 1974 (1949 opening vs 1948 erection vs 1952 dedication vs a 1979 replacement of a WWII airport control tower), and the story says so. Current staffing and access are not confirmed: the staffing line rests on a Peakbagging page with a 2002 photo, and the access level 'restricted' is my reading of the NHLR's not-readily-accessible note, not a stated rule. The CAL FIRE PDF is an undated copy hosted on a personal site. The Lassen Historical Society item on susanvillestuff.com returned 403 and was not read. Story is about 380 words including footnotes.

Current location is supported by three sources. The 1994 move date comes from a secondary quote of a newspaper item, which we did not see directly. The brief has two coordinate sets for the summit (NHLR 40.740525, -120.826906 and west_us_lookouts 40.74795, -120.83024); we used the NHLR set and did not verify the other. A search result mentioned a closed lookout tower on the Forest Service site; this is unconfirmed and not used. Check with the Eagle Lake Ranger District before any visit.

Core facts (1939 build, staffing to 1982, 1994 move, 1997 registration) agree across sources. The record's coordinates (40.55811, -120.78245) sit about 170 m from the Forest Service point (40.557561, -120.780547); the Forest Service point is official and was not changed. Peakbagging gives 6,749 ft for the old butte site while the NHLR gives 6,705 ft; that belongs on the sibling us-ca-dow-butte record, not this one. The 1971-72 staffing recollection is a single account and is dated only to that engine-crew period. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1994 relocation year that the earlier corrections entry proposed is already in events, so the corrections list was cleared. The Forest Service office hours (Tuesday to Friday) are not used in the story; the story points to the office address only.

Height conflict unresolved: brief height_m 4.3 (about 14 ft) against the register's 6 foot enclosed timber tower, which may be a height or a sizing figure; the story avoids giving a height. Current access is not documented in these sources; the 1960 Weebly entry ('Lookout opened by Nancy Hood. Could not get car all the way.') describes access at that time only and was not used in the story. The register credits its photos to the National Archives and the Nancy Hood Collection; no image URLs were found in the text, so no photo entries.

Record kind 'ground' agrees with FFLA and with the NGS wood lookout house description; no correction. The 1921 name W.C. Duncan and the 1932 name W. Duncan are assumed to be one lookout; sources do not say so, so the story uses both names as written. No build date found in the sources read. The 1921, 1931 and 1932 items are newspaper excerpts transcribed on Forest Lookouts, not checked against the papers. One WebSearch lead (a 2021 fire map labelling a Post Creek Lookout nearby) is unconfirmed and not used. No current condition or access source found. Story omits the fined hunter's name. Fact-check 2026-10-10: added the James Farley and 'intending to hunt' evidence quotes, which the story's claims rest on; the story now cites the NGS survey as well as Forest Lookouts for the former-site claim. Two sentences that followed the excerpt's or survey's wording (the 1931 telephone line and the 1961 survey description) were reworded. No other corrections.

The newest dated source is the January 2019 NHLR visit report, so today's condition is unknown. Peakbagging.com is undated apart from a 2011 photo credit; its 'in good condition' statement conflicts with the 2019 visit and is reported with that caveat. The FFLA standing listing is also undated. Waymarking pages returned no readable text and were not used. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with 'closed' (gated). The brief's 'standing' status holds, with a status note about the 2019 condition.

Dates and design come from the register alone; the record's 1943 build year matches it. Staffing is from a 2023 Forest Service feature and may be out of date; no later staffing record was found. Access is thin: no rental listing and no Forest Service visiting page was read. The access level is unknown, not public: the only access evidence is a 2020 hiking trip report, and no source read says whether the cab is open to visitors. The fire camera project page: search snippets reported two versions, one showing the project in progress and one completed; I read only the version with the May 16, 2025 decision date and could not confirm installation. The blog's account of the earlier station is unverified. The register's photos are all rights reserved, so none were added.

Brief's record (elevation 1841.3 m, agency, NHLR US 1152 registration on Nov 27, 2016) matches the Register; no corrections. Brief had no build event; the sources show 1931 plans only, so no built event is asserted. The 1953 Knedler photograph (archive.org/details/casbcfm_000249, public domain per the archive record) is a new find but its image file URL was not fetched, so no photos entry is included; the editor can pull the JPG from that item. The April 2020 blog is a personal account; only the access fact was used and the author is not named. Staffing and current condition beyond the 2020 blog and 2019 fire are not in the sources read. The fire page shows no damage to the lookout.

Height left out: the register's '15 foot enclosed timber tower' may mean the tower or the cab, so the record's height_m stays null. Access was 'closed' and is now 'unknown': the register's 'unsafe for use' wording is not a closure notice, and no current Forest Service or CAL FIRE notice was found, so check with Lassen National Forest before stating access. The register text is from the 2011-2012 plan, and the newest source is the 2020 project page, so the current condition is unverified. The dyermtn.com resort site describes a separate resort proposal on the mountain and is not used. No new photos. Build year 1934 agrees across both sources.

The newest staffing record is the June 2008 CAL FIRE list, and the newest registry event is 2019; current condition, staffing and public access are unverified. The 1982 lower-room date is derived from 'ten years later'. The 1971 fire item is a reprint of a Red Bluff Daily News story. The CAL FIRE PDF is a copy on a personal site (citlink.net), not a CAL FIRE URL. The brief's 1963 build date is the current tower; a lookout has stood here since at least 1933.

Brief height_m 152.4 (500 ft) is not supported by any source read, so it is not in facts; please check before keeping it. The 1934 build and 2018 burn are well supported. No current access or ownership source was found; the road and trail details come from a guide page of unknown date and a local wiki, and the Little Basin ownership point is from a local wiki. The FFLA index row for the Santa Cruz Eagle Rock reads Gone with no registry number, which fits the burn. Brief events are otherwise consistent with the sources.

Name in the record carries the wrong forest (Arapaho-Roosevelt, from the register); the Forest Lookouts page says Trinity National Forest. See corrections. Build year is unclear: the lookout was in use by August 1933, and the building was being completed in August 1934. The 'lookout house' design comes only from the 1975 survey description. Staffing is limited to the 1933 fire guard; the 1940 mule story is about supply, not staffing. No source on current access or ownership beyond the forest, and no source describing the site now beyond the register's remnants note. Record coordinates (40.743083, -123.326017) were not checked against the sources. The register's foundation photo (Mark Nelson) is already in the record, so no new photos were added.

Thin record: the 1928 entry is the only dated detail; no completion date, staffing record or removal date was found. FFLA California list row confirms Platform and Gone (Siskiyou row, not the Santa Cruz or Trinity Eagle Rock rows). The Forest Lookouts page only repeats the 1928 quote. The FFLOS page has a June 2025 photo but no image URL in the cached text, so none added to photos. Public access is not stated anywhere; facts.access omitted. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads for this tower.

History is well sourced from four pages. Current status is not: the latest staffing source is 2010 and no access rules were found, so no access or visit facts are recorded. The register gives elevation 6,483 ft while the Jenner blog gives 6,444 ft; neither is recorded in facts. The brief's conflict note says the record shares a register number with another entry; I did not check that other entry, and US 104 is what the register page shows. The 1925 vs 1926 cab date is flagged in the story, not corrected.

Only one dated source places a lookout here: a 1925 newspaper line quoted on Forest Lookouts. No build date, design, height or fate beyond the FFLA 'Gone' entry was found. The mountain is not on the FFLOS California index in our cache, so there is no register entry. Record kind 'unknown' and FFLA type 'Unknown' are both left unchanged. Nothing here changes the record.

Staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1973 is inferred from SummitPost's last staffing year; no later staffing source was found. Whether the house is open to visitors is not stated in any source read. The Klamath NF Facebook post returned a login wall and was not used; the 2024 details come from the FFLA Instagram reshare. The Redding and Bluewater articles were blocked (403) and not used. The brief's 'access unknown' is replaced with 'public' (hike-in).

Two detailed pages plus an FFA list row. The Oregonian story is only available second-hand, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; no original was found. The register text has the typo 'at lease'; the evidence quote keeps the source spelling and the story says 'at least'. The staffing row uses the Wilsons' departure (November 1959) as the last known staffing, not a formal end date. No photo with a URL found. No access statement in any source, so facts.access is omitted. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads for this tower.

The Peakbagging slab and wood-pole observations come from undated photo captions, so the story says the slab and pole are what the photos show. The 1936 items are quoted from a newsletter on the Forest Lookouts site and spell the peak Estella in one item. The public access picture for both the air base and the original preserve is undescribed. The current tower is covered by us-ca-estelle-mountain-at-hemet-ryan. No new photos added (no verified image URLs).

Built, design, move and registration are well supported. The move year varies by source: about 1958, 1958, or before 1960. The 1936 items are newsletter excerpts quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. The 1935 construction credit differs slightly (California Division of Forestry plus CCC on NHLR, CCC alone on FFLA). The brief's 'None relocated' event is contradicted by its own note, hence the correction. Height_m is the 30 ft tower height, not overall height. No current access policy was found. Photos were not added.

Unresolved conflict: FFLA lists the lookout as gone (no date); an undated SummitPost climbing guide says an abandoned tower still stands. The guide names two landowners at gates on the route (N3 Cattle Company; Biel Property, Inc.) but does not say who owns the summit. The guide's route crosses a fence, so the story gives no route directions, only a warning about the fence. Record kind 'unknown' and FFLA type 'Unknown' are both left unchanged. The 1926 fire comes from a Tribune report quoted on Forest Lookouts; the original paper was not read.

The record's 1934 build date, 1999 registration and 1594.4 m elevation match the NHLR, so no correction is proposed. The record's coordinates match fire-lookouts.org. Sources disagree on the L-4 cab count (20 vs 18) and on elevation (5,231 ft vs 5,256 ft). The CCC attribution rests only on Peakbagging. Staffing and active-service claims come from pages last updated in 2013; no 2026 confirmation was found, and the access level 'restricted' is a judgment. The fire-lookouts.org/cali/fence_meadow/ variant returned the same text, so it was not counted as a separate source. Story is about 330 words including footnotes.

The record's height_m 152.4 (500 ft) is not supported by any source read: the register gives no height, and the history page gives none. It looks wrong for a cab on a 12-foot base. Left out of facts. Not added to corrections because no sourced proposed value exists; a human should check and remove or correct it. Record kind two_story was not checked against a source. Unresolved conflicts: (a) cab model, the register description says CL-100 while a photo caption says CL-30; the story uses CL-100. (b) Access: the 2020 register visit found a locked gate on the approach road, while the Forest Service day-use page lists the site as open daily and year-round. The FFLA project page linked in search returned 404, so it was not used. (c) Completion of the 1922 station is not confirmed in sources read. (d) The end of staffing, presumably the 1970s, is the register's estimate, not a dated record. The 2025 report's account of the federal workforce cuts is the chapter's own explanation; the story attributes it to the report. Fact check 2026-10-08: the 2025 report dates the meeting 1/21/25 but also calls it Inauguration Day, which was January 20, 2025; the story says only January 2025 and attributes the day to the report. The summit wording comes from a 1922 trail item, not the register. The Ontiveros name is printed as Zolla, Tollo, Zollo and Z. A.; the story uses Zollo Ontiveros and names the Z. A. form. The day-use page does not describe the tower as open to visitors, so the story says only that. No new photos. Budget: register, Forest Lookouts page, 2022 and 2025 chapter reports, and the Forest Service day-use page; one search.

Register spells the county 'Calavares' (corrected in the brief). Height conflict between register (10 ft) and 1948 survey sheet (15 ft); height_m follows the survey figure. Removal date unknown in every source read, so no removal event. Build date is contested and the story says so; the record's built 1934 is the register's Built field, but its own description dates the current structure to 1943, and other pages say 1936 build with 1952 move. Build date is unresolved: the 1973 register date may refer to a later tower, since the register's design note cites a 1991 test period (MVT 10/91), but no source read confirms that. The 1952 Knedler photo is a public archive item, but its licence was not checked, so it is not added to photos. The 2011-2012 plan note ties Fredonyer's preservation status to Dyer Mountain, see the Dyer story.

Whether the 1930s lookout was built is not confirmed in the sources read; the record kind 'tower' conflicts with the 1931 plan for a rock lookout house and the 1934 fire outlook building. A 1931 brush-fire report from the King City Rustler could not be read (cdnc.ucr.edu returned 403).

The 1935-1940 history comes from newspaper clippings compiled by the Forest Lookouts site, cited as secondary. The 1950 'Ten Years Ago' weather-reading item is a 1940 retrospective and was left out. Thin record: two pages only. The 1941 item is quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and was not checked against the Bakersfield Californian. Two sources only: the FFLOS register and a Forest Lookouts compilation of 1925-1933 newspaper items. Two sources, both with history text. Built-date conflict (1911 vs circa 1913) and the 1934/1937 rebuild question are in resolved_conflicts. No build year found in the sources read; the earliest dated staffing (1911) starts the story. Record coordinates 35.74278, -119.14389 have no source in the pages read. firelookout.org shows latitude as Undetermined with no longitude, so the coordinates need checking before use. Do not confuse with the Black Mountain lookout on the Sierra National Forest in Fresno County (NHLR; CCC-built 1934, still standing per NHLR snippet), a different site. Brief checked: 1939 build date and 2019 NHLR registration confirmed on the NHLR page; elevation 310.9 m matches the NHLR's 1,020 ft for the Fairplex site. Coordinates and elevation in the record are for the Fairplex display site; the original summit is a separate site (NHLR gives 34.160096, -117.799767 for the original location, not read in this pass beyond the NHLR snippet) and the sibling record us-ca-johnstone-peak-san-dimas covers it. Not verified: any separate Southern California Mountains Foundation post (search snippet only, not read) or the Forest Lookout Association list.

Five sources read. The 1992 Fairplex move date and the 2019 NHLR registration of the Fairplex record (Nov 2, 2019) are in the sibling record us-ca-johnstone-peak-at-la-county-fairplex and are not repeated here. Only the FFLOS register page has content. The Forest Lookouts page for Jones Point (californialookouts.weebly.com/jones-point.html) shows a header and 'Removed' with no history text, so it is not cited. Two WebSearch calls found nothing on this site. Current status rests on two sources (the design-build firm's post, dated about one month before this run by its own label, and the FFLA list entry New 2026); no Forest Service page or news report on the completed tower was read, so the completion date is not confirmed beyond 2026. The 2013 staffing and access claims are from a page last updated March 1, 2013 and are not current. The brief's 'New 2026' came from the FFLA row for Jordan Peak and is verified. Yore Sequoia, abc30, and the Forest Service trail page appeared only as search snippets and were not quoted. A YouTube video of the new tower exists (search snippet only, not read). Elevation conflicts: 9,038 ft per NHLR and FFLOS, 9,122 ft per fire-lookouts.org. The brief's 'burned' event is supported by FFLOS (2020 SQF Complex Fire) and NHLR (destroyed September 14, 2020). No photos added.

Three sources agree the lookout burned in 1975, but disagree on the build year (1935 register vs 1936 move from Mount Lukens) and the 1960 fire size. Angeles Adventures is a local history site without a named author; it is the only source for the 1936 move and the staffing names after 1939. The 2019 detection use comes from the register's description. No Forest Service record was found. A search snippet that gave 1976 for the fire was not fetched and is not used.

No staffing or notable fire found in the pages read. Brief's access was unknown; now closed per the Forest Service page dated Aug 2026, so recheck. Peakbagging.com (search snippet only, not read) reports the cab gone in 2001 photos; a lead for dating the cab removal. The 1979 date rests on one blog. Brief's 'fflos=gone' conflict is the cabin, not the tower.

Destruction in the September 2024 Line Fire is stated by NHLR and Hundred Peaks, but I could not open the Mountain News article (HTTP 429 on every attempt), so the fire's exact date and the 'steel framework only' detail rest on Hundred Peaks alone. Rebuilding status is unverified, and the register's statement carries no date. The 1954 tower-versus-cab question is unresolved. The brief's 'standing' status was corrected. Access was set to restricted because nothing remains to enter; the brief had 'unknown'. Staffing as_of is the 2024 destruction year. The californialookouts page is a compilation of newspaper clippings with its own dating; the story's 1929 and 1954 dates are the report dates July 18, 1929 and June 16, 1954. Fact-check 2026-10-08: 'San Bernardino Mountains' was replaced by the register's San Bernardino National Forest, and 'no tower left to climb' by 'no cab to visit', because the sources say the lookout was destroyed but do not say the steel framework is unclimbable.

The register and the 2008 trip report disagree on what remains, so the story reports both. The trip report is a personal account, not an official survey, and it is dated October 6, 2008. The 1917 storm report comes from a weebly transcription of a Bakersfield Californian item, not the original paper. A search snippet that named Sequoia National Forest for Kern Peak was not fetched and is not used; the register and the weebly page both say Inyo. No Forest Service record was found.

Destruction in the August Complex fires is supported by two independent sources (FFLA chapter report and peakbagging.com). Brief status gone is more specific as destroyed; facts.status uses destroyed, no correction filed. Height is the open question: the Register's 17 feet, the 1942 survey's 30 feet and the 1935 steel frame of 20 feet disagree, and height_m 9.1 follows the survey. The Register and the weebly header use different forest names (Six Rivers now; Trinity National Forest in the older header); the story uses Six Rivers. No staffing source was found, so none is recorded. No photos recorded: the peakbagging page's photos have no license or URL in the cached text. One web search used; it surfaced the peakbagging destruction note and no description of the site after the fire.

No source describes public access, so access is omitted. The FFLOS page cites NHLR US 1338, CA 161 for this site, while the firelookout.org list shows NHLR US 1367, CA 190 for a Kettle Rock in Plumas; unresolved. The NHLR page for this site was not in the cache (404). The OpenStreetMap way 864276937 tags a lookout tower but gives no current status, so it was not used. Staffing events are a selection from the 1922-1959 notices (1926 Frank Bare, 1927 Robert Thompson and 1944 Gene Leichter omitted). Ready for review; the 1952/1953 and 1920/1923 disagreements are stated in the story.

The brief's 1934 build date and 2019 registration are confirmed. Not used: a Shasta County Fire Safe Council Facebook snippet gives 1932 (page would not load, so unverified), and a geocache listing (GC1HP35) calls the lookout abandoned (page would not render). Access to the cab interior, staffing and climbability are not in any source read. Source 4 is a single hiker's track of unknown date. The 13-foot figure is the register's own wording and may describe the tower or the cab.

No correction to the brief record: the 1945 built year and the 2010 NHLR registration hold up, though the Register description says 1946. The FFLA list shows status 'RF Hazard' with no explanation; the Forest Service calls the tower closed to the public. Sources describe a 1923 glass house and a 1945/46 cab but do not say whether the cab replaced the glass house or the 1920s cabin in the Register photo caption. Staffing end date and closure date not found; a later Forest Service or FFLA page might give them.

Build year conflict: the November 9, 1932 letter plans construction for the next spring; the site note says built 1932. Removal date not found. The FFLA list also gives this gone site NHLR US 882, but that register page is not in cache. Access rests only on a hiking-app trail listing.

Brief's 1912 build date and 1996 registration confirmed on the NHLR page. Brief's 2070.2 m elevation matches the NHLR's 6,792 ft (2,070 m). Brief's height_m 9.1 is not supported by any page read in this pass, so it is left out of facts; the editor should check it against the NHLR or the flyer. The 'two_story' kind is supported by the NHLR photo caption about the 1912 house forming the first floor. Access 'restricted' is a judgment: the 2025 release calls it an active part of the detection network and the 2012 event used limited parking. The 2014 and 2025 fire items come from a Forest Lookouts page and a republished Forest Service release. Current staffing is not confirmed beyond the release's wording. The flyer PDF was read directly. Not verified: the NHLR's 'Oak Knoll' cooperator versus the Scott River and Salmon/Scott district names. No photos added: the NHLR photo credits (Ron Kemnow, Nancy Hood Collection) have no licence stated in what was read.

Only two sources, and they disagree on what was built. Searches returned nothing else about this lookout: hits for Lakeview Point were Lake Mead-area photos, and Lake Mountain is a different Klamath lookout. A 1958 Klamath forest eligibility report may cover this site but was not fetched. The brief's 1937 build year is contested by the register's own description.

Unresolved: build year 1912 (register) vs 1913 (1913 newspapers, local history); loss date June (1914 newspapers) vs summer (register) vs September 13 (local history); cabin size 12 ft 8 in (register) vs planned 10 by 10 ft (1913 newspapers) vs 10 ft by 6 ft (local history); occupant W.H. Packard (local history) vs Marshall M.F. Packer (1920 obituary), not known to be the same man. The record's 1912 is proposed for correction to 1913. The Lassen Historical Society post on susanvillestuff.com returned HTTP 403 and the NPS Facebook post returned no text, so neither was used. The trail record is a 1981 NRT application. No photos added. Confidence medium: no source describes the summit site today.

Almost every lookout fact rests on one source, the NHLR register page; the Wikipedia citation supports only the 1946 state forest date. The Cal FIRE page for the forest returned HTTP 403 when read, so staffing and current condition are unknown. A search snippet attributed to Cal FIRE said the lookout is staffed periodically in fire season and dated it to 1935; that claim was not readable and is not used. The 1978 date and the reason for the rebuild are unexplained in the register. The register lists the summit elevation as 6,738 ft (2,054 m), and the record matches. The register does not say whether the tower can be climbed, so climbable is null. The access note is dated 10/91 and may be out of date. No new photos were added because the register photos are all rights reserved.

Only the register entry and the FFLA county list had Lava Peak history. The californialookouts.weebly.com Lava Peak page holds only township data. No staffing or fire history was found, so none is written. The register mentions a trailer residence noted on the Thornton survey; not used. The status correction (gone to ruins) and the built-year precision are for editor review. Low confidence: only the register and one FFA list entry cover this site, so the history is thin.

Confirmed: the 1961 build year and the January 3, 2015 registration. The brief's 18.3 m height matches the 1915 first tower (60 ft), not the 1961 cab (30 ft per the register), so the correction is proposed. Staffing rests on a 2004 visit note and an undated road guide, and no recent staffing source was found. A Facebook post from the Forest Fire Lookout Association (search snippet only, not read) calls the first tower 60 feet, and it is not cited. The 1915 papers quoted on the weebly page are reprinted newspaper extracts, not checked against the original papers.

Thin record: the register entry, a one-line Klamath National Forest chronology entry quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, and general Aircraft Warning Service context from Wikipedia. No staffing, fire, or current-site information was found. The 'built' event is a temporary cabin, not a permanent lookout, and the register says the replacement question is unknown. Wikipedia was used only for service-wide dates (May 1941 organization, May 29, 1944 deactivation); it does not mention this peak. The chronology is cited as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the original Klamath National Forest history was not read. Possible follow-up: the Klamath National Forest history volume and the Siskiyou County Museum photo credited on the register. The lat/lon in the record matches the register.

Brief said the 2024 evaluation was done and a report submitted; the source is a volunteer schedule (Evaluate ... Submit report), so the story says it is listed, not done. Build year conflict (1957 register vs Oct 1958 article) is reported, not corrected. Staffing comes from an undated photo site. Access and winter closure come from a third-party 4WD guide, not a Forest Service source; confirm with the Carson Ranger District or the Humboldt-Toiyabe MVUM before relying on it. The brief's registration date and NHLR record matched the page read. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the guide says 4WD is recommended, not required, and the story now says so; the photo page's staffing statement is undated and the story now says the page gives no date for it. Pages read: 6 (2 of them the same FFLA PDF with different greps) plus 2 web searches.

Record says gone; the cab and tower were moved to Pike County Peak (us-ca-pike-county-peak, researched separately), so relocated fits. Replacement year: register 1961, June 1962 newspaper announced construction; both kept. Move year: 1983 (register, NHLR, local history) vs 1984 (Peakbagging). Size: 1949 survey gives 14 ft square and 26 ft high; the register's 1933 wording is a 10 enclosed timber tower; not reconciled. The Peakbagging text is a 2006 photo caption page. No source describes the Lexington Hill summit today. Confidence medium.

Thin record: no construction date, design detail or staffing found. The FFLOS register page for US 1988 is not in cache, and firetower slug guesses returned 404. The tower kind comes only from the FFLA list. The peakbagging table gives elevation 7,540 ft, which the brief lacks; the table key defines EL as elevation in feet, so it is now in facts.

Brief record matches the Register (built 1966, NHLR registered 2019). Staffing 'seasonal' is an approximation of 'intermittently during predicted lightning events'. No build date found in the sources read, so none is recorded. The 1938 woodpecker item is quoted over several lines on the Forest Lookouts page, and the 2005 burn date conflicts with the 2008 report. The 2008 report does not name the fire.

Build-year conflict (1940 NHLR vs 1920s Recreation.gov) is unresolved; a primary USFS historic-structures record would help settle it. The californialookouts.weebly.com source did not return page-specific content for this lookout (returned only a sitewide county directory) so it wasn't used.

Ownership disagrees: the register says state land, while a 1926 clipping says the county received a deed from a land company. No source describes the lookout footprint today. History comes from newspaper clippings reprinted on californialookouts.weebly.com; originals were not checked.

Thin record. The Forest Lookouts page carries only a header (county and forest); two web searches found no build, staffing or removal history. The index gives coordinates 39.68863, -122.70863. The trip report is undated and is the only source on the site today. Access level public is an inference from the road and trail described there; verify with the Mendocino National Forest before publishing.

Identity unknown. The record name is the bare word 'lookout'; OSM tags are only man_made=tower and tower:type=observation, with no ownership, height or date. Two Mountain Democrat excerpts (as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page) and the index are the only sources. Two web searches found no Eldorado-specific hit. Next step if wanted: the Mountain Democrat archive (CDNC) for 1913 to 1930s, or Eldorado NF records. Index coordinates 38.88348, -120.56112.

Date and fate conflict across sources (see resolved_conflicts). The 1915, 1918 and 1927 newspaper items are reprints quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; I did not see the originals. Page title on Forest Lookouts is Mount San Antonio (Old Baldy), so the identity question is for the editor.

The 1930 newspaper text comes secondhand, transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page (Ukiah Republican Press and Ukiah Dispatch Democrat); the originals were not checked. The index gives no removal date. Two web searches found no other Lookout Peak history. The trail article is the only source about the peak today and does not mention the station. Index coordinates 39.13617, -123.24596.

Nearly all lookout-specific detail rests on one source, Angeles Adventures, whose own dates, cab size and 1958 staffing conflict; all three are kept as disputed. The 1937 crash comes from that source alone. The Nike site is a separate installation about four miles away and appears only for context. Brief status gone matches all sources. The brief's agency line is consistent with the Forest Lookouts header.

The brief's record says this entry shares a register number with another lookout; I did not identify the other entry, and NHLR gives US 742, CA 81 for this one. The FFLA San Diego-Riverside page says the staffed tower is the only one on the Cleveland National Forest still staffed by Forest Service employees; that is a claim by the chapter, not a Forest Service source. The socalfirelookouts.org page in the brief could not be reached (DNS failure). AllTrails returned HTTP 403. The Facebook ALERTCalifornia snippet (1925 original, 1964 replacement) was not opened. Public climbing rules and current staffing are unverified.

Only one substantive item describes this place: a 1938 newspaper quote on the Forest Lookouts page. Its type is unknown, the Forest Fire Lookout Association gives no location, and the brief's coordinates have no source in the cached pages. No source describes the site today. The FFLA line reads 'Undetermined' in the coordinate position; that is read here as no coordinates.

The 1940 build date and the removed status come from the Forest Lookouts page, which cites A History of the Siskyou National Forest; that book was not opened. The remains and 4x4 access come from a user-comment section on an amateur-radio site and should be checked before publishing. No staffing data in the sources read. The 'Siskyou' spelling is the source's own. The brief's name is Low Divide (Stone Corral); the Forest Lookouts page calls it Stone Corral.

Two sources only: Kemnow's page (quoting the Klamath NF chronology and a 1934 John Buck account, plus a 1947 newspaper and 1951 chronology line) and one undated trip report. The cab move to Ukonom Mountain has no date and I found no source saying whether that cab still stands. A search snippet mentioned a 'Ukonom Lookout Tower' on 2017 fire maps; I did not open those PDFs, so it is not cited. The trip report's 'empty cinder block structure' may or may not be the lookout site; the story says so. The Ukonom Ranger District is administered by Six Rivers NF per a search snippet, unverified; a district office contact in Orleans could confirm the move date and the cinder-block structure. Record kind two_story is consistent with the FFLA index listing.

Brief's 2018 events (a $300 FFLA stabilization grant and emergency stabilization materials) are not in events: the cited 2018 chapter report URL returned HTTP 404 and no other source read covers them. Brief's 2021 'restored' is corrected to 'modified' because the chapter describes protective plywood shutters and a suspended project.
