Cab model conflict (CL-160 vs CL-30) is unresolved at source level; CL-30 is recorded. No source read is dated after 2021 for staffing, so 'unstaffed as of 2021' is the latest supported status. Weebly page (californialookouts.weebly.com/lyons-peak.html) not used beyond its header.

Two sources: Kemnow's page with 1934 and 1935 newspaper quotes, and a trip report. The 1935 Oakland Tribune article names a superintendent, Kaufmann; no other source found for him. No removal date found. A concrete block on a summit in the same trip report belongs to a different peak in the Lassic area, so it is excluded. The trip report also appears at peak_5,640ft_n3_1.html with identical text; signal_n3_1 is cited. A 1936 Humboldt Times clipping about a 'fire lookout at Mad River' appeared only in a search snippet and is unverified; not cited. The article's '1934 road' and '1935 built' dates come from one feature and are not corroborated. Record agency was null; the trip report's Six Rivers NF statement is used for facts.agency.

PeakVisor says the lookout burned in the 1970s; the register says a 1972 windstorm destroyed it. The register's account is more detailed and is used, but the disagreement is unresolved. The register's claim of an earlier lookout destroyed in September 1932 is contradicted by the next day's newspaper. Today's condition rests on one 2018 trip report describing foundations; no survey, photo or later source was found. The record's 'removed 1972' is proposed as 'destroyed 1972' in corrections.

Two sources: Kemnow's page (about a dozen newspaper items, 1915-1932) and a SummitPost climbing guide. Status conflict: removed (no date) vs burned long ago; not resolved. Name variants: Magee/McGee; Williams spelled Todd, Tod and Ted; Goodman's 'about 17 years' (1932) does not square with the 1918-1919 Williams items. Web searches turned up no corroboration for Goodman or the Williams names, and a Wikipedia lead says there was once a watchtower but gives no dates (not cited). Next places to check: Lassen National Forest history or archives, the Lassen Historical Society, and the 1918 and 1930s Lassen forest reports. Record agency matches the Kemnow header.

Built date, design beyond the 13 steps, and the date and cause of the loss are all unknown. History rests on newspaper quotes reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the original newspapers were not read. Do not confuse with the Manzanita Mountain lookout in Modoc County (FFLA NHLR US 1332, CA 155), which is a different, standing site. The 1936 and 1937 pages quote staff by name; those names are historical and from the newspapers only.

Correction proposed for the 1934 built event: the Register's Built field reads 1934/1974. The 1974 date is not explained in the sources read; the 1952 fire and 1935 item indicate the 1934 building existed then, so the replacement date is not clear. The 2008 CAL FIRE table lists it as Manzanita Peak Lookout, Modoc County. The 2008 staffed status is a 'may be staffed' list, not a record of actual staffing. The Forest Lookouts page for Manzanita is a 1935-1956 record set; nothing after 1956 was in the cached text. Staffing and access today are unknown.

The record's kind 'ground' (from FFLA) is not confirmed by any source read; the 1940 newspapers say only 'lookout building' and do not mention a tower or a ground cabin. The 'only the foundation remains' line is undated and no later source was found. The 1940 paper places the lookout about four miles east of Markleeville; the register places it atop Mogul Peak, and the trail guide reaches Mogul Peak, so the two are treated as the same site. The trail guide shows a route, not whether the foundation is visible from it. No photo of the site today was found.

NHLR is the main source. The Forest Lookouts page is a set of press clippings read as data. Build year is unresolved (1914 NHLR vs a 1912 clipping). No read source dates the deactivation, vandalism or restoration beyond the NHLR sentence; a search summary claimed a 1997 restoration from one source, which was not verified and is not used. A 1939 clipping names 'Waddles Maher', probably a typo, so it is not used. The 1935 clipping places Maher among rangers from the station, not as lookout, so the story says he was placed at the station. Public access to the cab is not established. Record fields match NHLR: Placer County, elevation 2,626 m, registered 1998 (US 277, CA 12 confirmed on the register page). No photos added.

County conflict: the record and the FFLA list say Siskiyou/Trinity; the Forest Lookouts page places it under Trinity County and quotes a 1926 paper saying the station is in Trinity county. Not resolved here; a human should check the county. Agency is Trinity NF per the Forest Lookouts header, but the 1926-1931 quotes say the lookout also served the Klamath Forest. The 1924 (Adler) and 1926 (Addler) names may or may not be the same person. The 1931 abandonment is a reported plan, not a confirmed closure. FFLA type is Ground; the 1931 diary calls it a lookout building. Record kind 'ground' is consistent. Built date and the date of loss are unknown; the original newspapers and Klamath NF chronology were not read.

The fate is corroborated by three independent sources (NHLR, Forest Service notice, SFGate). No staffing history appears in the sources read, so none is recorded; the WWII monitoring role and the rental are the operating history. The NHLR page carries a March 2025 photo credited to Darin McQuoid, but no image URL was available, so no photo is recorded. Campflare and the Forest Service listing were seen only in search results and are not cited. The Forest Service listing shows 'Site Closed'.

Thinnest of the three. The Forest Lookouts page gives a county heading only, with no history text. Beyond the FFLA row, the only source is a tDAR citation record (the report itself is not held there and was not read), so the link between the 1998 report and the lookout is by catalogue keyword only. Agency left unset: the Stanislaus NF link comes from the report title, not from a statement about who runs the site. Built date, type detail, staffing, and fate are all unknown. Possible next leads: the Stanislaus NF heritage records for the Hungry burn project (report #05-16-2133) and local newspaper archives for Tuolumne County.

Access is unknown: no source says whether the summit is open to visitors. Removal has three accounts (after 1984 per FFLOS; late 1980s per Carey; burned April 7, 1987 per one trail guide), and the burned date rests on a single source whose 'facility' is ambiguous (communication site or lookout). No corrections to the brief: slug, ground-cabin kind, 1934 build and 2019 registration all check out. Staffing dates come from 1935-39 newspaper excerpts, not an official roster. No photos added: the FFLOS and peakbagging pages carry captions only, and no image URLs were retrieved.

Built year is disputed: the register gives 1934 and a June 1934 paper says building was about to start, while the Klamath chronology quoted on Forest Lookouts gives 1935 for CCC construction. The story gives both. The record's height of 4.6 m matches the 1952 survey's 'about 15 feet'; the survey describes the house, not the cab floor, so it is treated as overall house height. Status rests on one register line; no later source was found. The 1964 staffing date is the publication date of the paper, not the years worked.

Build year is 1937 per FFLOS but 1936 per Angeles Adventures; story says so. Fire name differs (Big Tujunga vs Mill Fire) but both match Nov 1975. The present-day foundation, tank and shack remnants rest on one climbing-site page (SummitPost) with no date visible in the text we read; treat as recent-ish but unverified. Angeles Adventures shows a lookout photo credited to Paul H. Rippens and LA Times photos, but no image URLs or licences were captured, so no photos added. The record's coordinates (34.349622, -118.312309) and Angeles Adventures' (34.348462, -118.313603) differ by about 175 m; not corrected. Access is recorded as public because it is National Forest land reached on foot, not because a source states a public-access rule. Route corrected 2026-10-09: the walk is about four miles of dirt road to Mendenhall Saddle, then about a mile of abandoned road; the first draft left out the dirt-road leg.

Both sources are dated or undated: the volunteer page was last updated February 2017 and the register page is undated. Current staffing and condition are unconfirmed. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'restricted' based on the locked-gate note; check with the Sierra National Forest before changing it. The record's values for county, year built and registration all check out; no corrections proposed.

Fate rests on one undated peakbagging photo page ('completely gone except for a concrete slab'); no source describes the site today or its access. Brief status 'gone' is supported by that page; access left unset. Build date: register circa 1945 conflicts with 1939-40 newspapers via Forest Lookouts; correction proposed to 1940, editor to decide. Brief height_m 182.9 (600 ft) has no source; correction proposes removal. Forest Lookouts and peakbagging list the site under San Luis Obispo County, which conflicts with the register's Kern County; the 1940 text places it near Fellows and Taft, so the record stays Kern. Photos: the FFLOS page credits a circa 1945 image to peakbagging.com and peakbagging credits a 6 Sept 1940 newspaper photo, but no image URLs or licences were captured, so none added. Two search calls and four page reads used.

Brief kind 'ground' follows the FFLOS Type column (Ground). The 1939 and 1943 items call it a fire lookout but do not describe a structure, so its form is unknown. Staffing 'staffed' as_of 1943 records the agreement for a June-September spotter, not confirmed operation. Peakbagging's key says LO site means the building was removed and there may be no evidence remaining, or status is unknown; that is not a confirmed removal date. Two searches found no post-1943 account and no photo. Access and present condition are not described by any source read. Peakbagging gives 2620 ft elevation (not used).

The brief's 'standing' status is not supported: the register accounts and Peakbagging conflict on the fire damage, and none describes it as unharmed. Sources disagree on whether the main building survived; a USFS or NPS statement from the October 2021 access would settle it. The Sequoia NF Facebook post returned no text when read, so it is not cited. No source after 2021 on rebuild, access or rental. The Peakbagging page is undated. Used 6 page reads and 1 search. Staffing as_of is the 2021 fire year, since the 1996 date is the last staffing and the Peakbagging 'not currently staffed' note is undated.

Record built year 1933 matches NHLR, so no correction was made. Record kind 'enclosed_tower' could not be confirmed or refuted: the visitor guide describes stairs, a platform and a cab, and NHLR describes the first lookout as a ground house. Staffing comes from the NHLR form field and comment; the Calexplornia staffing claims were not verified and are not used. The NHLR entry dates 2004 yet mentions 2005 restoration; this is not explained in any read source. Calexplornia is a visitor blog; used only for the brochure date and visit conditions. The early-1930s date is the visitor guide's conclusion from the three disagreeing sources, and the story now attributes it that way. No photos added.

Thin sourcing: the register, one hiking-guide elevation and Wikipedia for the AWS program. The brief's gone status is not supported by the register (see corrections). No staffing, fire history or site-today description found. The AllTrails listing returned 403 and was not used.

Only two sources. The California Lookouts (Forest Lookouts) page has a Mitchell Peak heading with no text. The removal decade and today's condition rest on a single 2006 column; no source after 2006 describes the site, so treat the 'today' section as dated. The column (by Susan Spano, Los Angeles Times, September 18, 2006) is republished on FireRescue1. The register's build year and the 1962 slab are both from the register. Photos: the register credits NPS photos (Under construction 1962) and a peakbagging.com photo of the remaining slab, but no image URLs were captured. A public-domain NPS image (NPGallery asset fc21e68b-ae14-4c1d-8d80-2f1fa195cb1f, 'Construction, Mitchell Peak Lookout', credit Scottie Steenburgh per the asset comment) is a candidate once its direct image URL is confirmed; no photo added. Search calls used: 2. Page reads: 4 (FFLOS, Forest Lookouts, FireRescue1, NPGallery asset page).

Height is unresolved: 1940 history 10 ft, 1942 station about 20 ft high, 1952 recovery top about 30 ft. The brief's 3.0 m was left out of facts; the editor should decide whether to keep it. Peakbagging's table lists Monkey Creek Ridge without the '(LO site)' tag it gives Mike's Peak and Mosquito Ridge, so it may record the site differently; check before relying on it. A search result for a Ride with GPS route titled Monkey Creek Ridge Lookout Site did not load its page text, so it is not used. No source describes the site today or public access. No photos found.

Brief height_m 152.4 is unsupported; no source gives a tower height, so it is proposed for removal. Brief's 1961 rebuild date is corrected to 1960 on NHLR and newspaper evidence, with the Mountains Foundation's 1961 noted. Current status conflicts: the Mountains Foundation (2025) says closed under a Line Fire closure order, while the Forest Service page (updated May 11, 2026) gives drive-up and cab-visit rules when staffed and mentions no closure. A search snippet described the Forest Service page as closed and last updated March 2025; the fetched page says May 11, 2026, so the story uses the fetched text. The 2014 report's planned 2015 rental system is not confirmed by any later source read. Staffing as of 2026 is from the Forest Service page and NHLR, not a dated roster.

Thin record: one 1937 newspaper item plus FFLOS and Peakbagging listings. No build date, description, photo or post-1937 account found. The 1937 item announces an assignment, so staffed as_of 1937 is an assignment, not confirmed service. Mapcarta gives 3,510 ft and Peakbagging 3509 ft elevation (not used). The 2022 Mosquito Fire (Placer and El Dorado counties) is a separate topic; no source ties it to this lookout, so it is left out. Natural Atlas calls it a lookout tower, but its page text did not load, so it is not used. Today's condition and access are not described by any source read.

Height corrected from 22.9 m to 18.3 m (60 ft) on the basis of two press items, since no source read supports 75 ft. Access is not established: no source says whether the public may visit, and a search summary claiming the summit is private property was not in any page read, so it is not used. A Cal Fire 1989 CEQA notice for a generator building was found in search only and not read. Wikipedia is used for the name, the Santa Cruz Mountains range and summit facts only. Land terms follow the 1922 dedication item, which calls the arrangement a rental; the story now says so. A 1923 press item names Mrs. Serena C. Smead as owner of land near the station in a suit against state foresters, which the land-donor account does not address and which needs a deed check before any ownership claim. No photos added. Current status rests on the 2019 NHLR entry, which describes the station in the present tense.

Access and rental status are not established: the NHLR page says only that the structure is maintained and faces a proposed tramway. Search snippets (not fetched, not cited) mention a road from Dunsmuir and a hike to the tower; check before publishing any access claim. The Mount Shasta News article returned HTTP 403. The Forest Lookouts newspaper items end in June 1963. The lookout's name appears as Cown (1956, 1959), Cowen (1960, 1962) and Cowan (1963) across the items, and the story uses Cowen. The brief's record (built 1933, standing, NHLR registration 2020) is consistent with the NHLR page; no corrections proposed.

Built year disagrees within the register (Built 1942 field vs 1943 description); the Forest Lookouts page gives 1942 with an unseen 1988 book as its source. The 1944 'closed' event uses the first year of the register's 'sometime in 1944 or 45' range, so treat the year as approximate. The 1954 date and fire name agree across both sources (spelled Devils Peak on the register, Devil's Peak on Forest Lookouts). Record status 'gone' and elevation 1,350 m match the register (4,428 ft). No source found describes what remains on site today or public access. The register's Ron Kemnow link was not read. The Caliente and Mount Carmel stories share the AWS background, so the volunteer sentence is kept short.

Early history is unresolved: the 1933 80-foot tower, the 1946 lookout photograph and the 1949 100-foot tower are all in the record, and the story says so. Access is restricted per the register's 'secure facility' wording; no visiting information was found and none is given. The 1933, 1938 and 1955 items are read only through the californialookouts compilation. Waymarking and academia.edu pages could not be read. The archive.org photo (public domain, Aug 1946, W. Fairbank) is a candidate image, but only its details page was captured, so no photos entry was added. The 30.5 m height is converted from the register's 100 ft.

The brief's note about conflicting materials is not borne out in the sources read: the register and state parks both say sandstone, and no source named another material. The brief's 1938 build date is the CCC start year; completion was 1941-42 per state parks, which is a substantive difference for the record. The 1931 lookout station comes from a newspaper excerpt reprinted on a fan site (californialookouts.weebly.com), not checked against the original paper. A mdia.org search snippet mentions Company 2932-V starting in 1938; the page was read only in part and that detail is not cited. No source read gives current hours for the summit museum, so the visit note is general.

Brief's 1920 built date comes from the register's Built field; its description gives a cupola completed in 1912, so the record should be corrected. Removal date is unknown in every source read. The hiker's remains and the register's foundation may or may not be the same ruin. The Oregon Hikers post is an undated personal trip report, used only for what remains. The Forest Lookouts page is a compilation of newspaper clippings; staffing after 1931 is not documented in these sources, so the story stops there.

Design history (three successive structures, 1925/1931/1961) is well documented by NHLR, but no source gives named keepers, specific fires spotted, or a current staffing/access status beyond NHLR's general 'staffed daily during fire season' line, which is undated and may be stale. NHLR's descriptive paragraph also mentions 'Mi-Wok Ranger District, 4,939' elevation' separately from the page's stated lookout elevation of 4,931 ft; this reads like boilerplate district text rather than a conflicting lookout elevation, so no correction is proposed.

Brief's 1918 built date conflicts with the register's own description (circa 1915) and with a 1916 newspaper; the story gives circa 1915 and states the disagreement. The Lakes Basin page is a commercial lodge's guide (the lodge operates under a Forest Service permit); it is used only for the 1910 and 1932 dates and for what remains at the summit. The Hake PDF is a two-column scan; the quote 'the last to serve on Mt. Elwell and the' is a single line from the cached text. Staffing after 1936 is not documented here, so the story stops at the 1930s. Morehead's June 1923 start and the May 1924 'third year' notice do not form one run of seasons, so the story gives them separately. The Hake sentence is split across two evidence entries because the PDF columns interleave.

Brief lacked a built event; 1926 is supported by a dedication date and multiple newspaper items, against the register's 1927. The register's 60-foot figure matches the brief's height_m of 18.3; Angeles Adventures gives 68 ft 4 in overall, unresolved. The summit is on Forest Service land reached by Road 3N17, which passes the lower Nike site, a correctional camp and county fire station; do not direct visitors into those grounds. The Angeles Adventures page carries photo captions with credits (USFS, USC, National Archives) but no license terms, so no photos are recorded. Tower staffing after 1940 is not documented here.

Build year is disputed: the register and Wikipedia say 1931; 1930 items quoted on Forest Lookouts describe construction and a station that year. Not settled. The 2019 and 2020 FFLA reports list the lookout as 'Harkness LO (Lava Beds Nat. Mon.) #516', which conflicts with the register's Lassen location. The Dixie Fire loss rests on the register and Wikipedia; Wikipedia cites a Redding Record Searchlight article (Chapman, 2021) that we did not locate. No source describes the site after the fire, so what remains and whether the site is open are unknown. The Forest Lookouts page was read in full during the 2026-10-09 verification pass; its Sept 10, 1930 completion item is now in the story and the events list. The NRHP nomination (NPGallery 100001211) was not read. Wikipedia's staffing line is undated. No WebSearch was available in this run.

No current access rule, visit report or rental listing was in the two pages read (NHLR detail page and the weebly compilation). The NHLR staffing statement is undated, so as_of is 'undated'. The StoryMaps Lost Sierra Route page returned no text. The 1913 weebly item describes starting work on a station, which may be a precursor of the 1915 building; not used in the story. Attribute the dated newspaper items to the weebly compilation, not to the original papers, which were not read. Budget: about six page reads were used on this tower; no further reads were attempted.

Four sources read. The 'foundation only' claim and the Portola museum claim come from SummitPost, a user-written hiking guide, and nothing else read confirms either; the Portola claim conflicts with the Quincy record. The sources do not say whether the 1936 tower replaced the 1922 station. A 1995 Feather River Bulletin item seen only as a search snippet says the tower was removed in 1986; the CDNC page returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. Record elevation 1057 m is the fairgrounds (register 3,468 ft), not the 8,372-ft summit. Fairgrounds hours and current condition are not in the sources read.

Three sources only, and they disagree on the build date: the register says 1936; the Quincy marker credits CCC Company 989 with building it in 1935; the Forest Lookouts page shows a lookout station on the mountain by 1922, so the 1936 tower may have replaced an earlier station. Not resolved. A 1995 Feather River Bulletin item, seen only as a search snippet (cdnc.ucr.edu), says the tower was removed in 1986, against 1984 in the register and the Forest Lookouts page. The CDNC page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Worth checking if CDNC can be reached. The record's kind 'two_story' is not supported by anything read: the register describes a '10 foot enclosed timber tower', so the kind is left unchanged for an editor to check against firelookout.org. The record's elevation (1057 m) is the fairgrounds site (the register gives 3,468 ft there), not the summit's 8,372 ft. The record's 'relocated' entry had no year; 1984 is added. A Plumas National Forest Facebook post seen only as a search snippet mentions the lookout at fair weekends; it was not read. Current hours and condition are unverified. No photos added: the register photos have no URLs in the sources read.

History rests on the register and Angeles Adventures, with newspaper transcripts for 1927-1938. The brief's 30.5 m height is not supported by anything read; the 22-foot tower figure is proposed as a correction, so check it. The register and Angeles Adventures disagree on the agency. The register text does not place the later 2002 structure, so the story does not say where it stood. The trailheads differ (Islip Saddle per Modern Hiker, Windy Gap per the Forest Service); both routes are public trails. The firelookout.org California index also has an 'Islip, Mount' row with FFLOS US 2083 and NHLR US 1057 marked Gone; I did not open it, so a possible duplicate record is unchecked.

Two sources only. Today's condition rests on the register's 1991 site note (MVT 10/91); nothing later was found, and the Sonoma County Library record has no text. The Water Boards PDF on the Mount Jackson mercury mine was not used for the lookout: it concerns the mine site off Sweetwater Springs Road. Staffing evidence runs from 1929 to 1939 in the newspaper transcripts; no later staffing was found. The register's built field (1948) disagrees with its own description (1928 first lookout, 1947 oldest construction); the story follows the description and mentions the field.

Height conflicts (45, 50, 75 feet) are reported in the story. Reopening year: the Record-Bee 2019 article says 2015; a Lake County News article dated May 14, 2017, reportedly says June 2016. That page returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text, and a WebFetch summary was used only to learn of the conflict, so no quote from it is used and the story does not cite it. The brief's 2017 solar panel and window repairs, 2018 rotten-wood repair and FFLA grants, 2019 $500 grant, and the August 2015 Cal Fire agreement were not found in any page read, so they are omitted. The Weebly Konocti page has only a header, no history. No source read after 2021 describes the tower's condition or whether repairs or reopening have happened; search snippets from a petition, Facebook posts and a TikTok video were not read and are not used. Photos: the NHLR page has a credit (Photo courtesy of Bill Ulmer) but no image URL, so none added. Budget: 5 distinct pages read (NHLR, Weebly, 2019 and 2021 FFLA reports, two Record-Bee articles) plus one 403 article, against a 6-page budget; 2 web searches used, and one WebFetch used after the 403.

No build date, builder, staffing history or removal date appears in any source I could read, so the story has no built or staffing section and no removal date. Only two blog posts describe the site itself, and both are 2023 visits. The record's name and coordinates (40.2964, -123.5515) fit a Goat Hill site, but no Goat Hill coordinate was checked. The 2023 blog refers to 'the lookouts' in the plural when describing a water source, so the number of lookout structures is unverified. A Moments in Dirt and Ink Facebook post about a removed lookout on Goat Hill returned only its title in the crawl, so it is not cited. Research budget exceeded: four searches and about 16 page reads, against a budget of two and six per tower.

Sources disagree on the 1922 versus 1923 start, the 1935 versus 1936 move, and whether the Josephine Peak tower is the Lukens tower; the story gives both accounts. No source describes what remains of the 1922 lookout on the summit. No access rule for the summit was found; Komoot describes a route to the top but not an access rule, so the access key is omitted. The brief's 2019 registration was not re-checked.

Brief said access 'unknown'; recorded as private from the NHLR description (dated October 1991) and Bay Area Peaks (undated). Brief's 1979 date for the existing tower confirmed; first lookout (1921) and 1942 tower added. thedirtymule.com (search snippet calls it an active lookout) returned 403 and was not used. Photo lead not added: archive.org item casbcfm_001080 (July 1953 construction photo) seen in search results; licence not checked.

Thin: the 1932 Los Angeles Times story is known only as quoted by Angeles Adventures and the register; I did not see the original article. The summit metal posts and drill holes are one visitor's observations and are not confirmed as lookout remains. The register's elevation (7,114 ft) and Wikipedia's (7,129 ft) differ. The brief's gone status is not supported (see corrections).

Only the register detail page, the register list and one PeakBagging page were read; no Forest Service record was found. The Wikipedia article for Mount Pinos does not mention the post. The PeakBagging page credits a photo to Fred Johnson dated May 15, 1943, but it gives no image URL, so no photo entry was added. Grokipedia was not used.

Only one register page carries the lookout's history (built 1967, mobile R1M trailer, removal 'Mid-1970's'). Searches and reads found no staffing, fire record, or current-site description. Elevation conflict on the register page: the header gives 8,849 ft (2,697 m), which matches the record's 2697.2 m, while the description gives 8,420 ft; the record's figure was kept. The Forest Lookouts page reproduces a 1972 Caltrans survey description with driving directions through a wire gate; directions are deliberately left out of the story. The 1975 removal year is a midpoint placeholder for 'Mid-1970's', not a dated record. No photo was added: the 1969 image URL was not in the cached text.

Good newspaper detail (1934-46, via the Forest Lookouts transcriptions, not checked against the original papers). The removal date is unknown: the record says 'After 1992' and the register says 'some time after that', so no removal event is dated. Current condition and public access are from two hiking guides and a 1991 register note; no source describes what remains of the lookout. The Lundell first-name conflict is unresolved. The register's 1946 and 1950 photo credits (Sonoma County Library; rntl.net) were not verified as new finds, so no photos entry was added. Elevation: the register gives 4,340 ft (1,323 m), matching the record's 1322.8 m.

Clippings (via Kemnow) give the 1934-1948 history; FFLA gives gone status; the Santa Maria Times feature (undated) gives the antenna-crowned summit. Unresolved: builder (federal vs state) and station height (about 2,000 ft in 1934 vs 1,336/1,344 ft later). No removal date, no removal record and no current access statement found. The FFLA entry 'Solomon' (Tehama/Trinity, no coordinates) is a different record and was not used. Staffing 'unstaffed' is inferred from the gone status. Two WebSearch calls used; no further reads of other sites. Fact-check 2026-10-10: staffing changed from 'unstaffed' (an inference from the gone status, no source states it) to 'unknown'. Dated evidence anchors added from the dated clippings on the Kemnow page; the 1,344 ft lookout elevation is confirmed in the peak table row.

Core facts (USFS administration, CCC origin, C-3 cab, 1999 NHLR registration, still in service per NHLR) are solid across the NHLR page and fire-lookouts.org. Build year (1934 vs 1935), height (30-32 ft vs 34 ft), elevation and coordinates disagree between sources; the record's 18.3 m height is not supported by either and is proposed for correction. Not verified: the brief's 2010 'Fresno County RAC grant' and 2011 RAC grant (about $18,000), and the 2018 FFLA restoration grant. The FFLA 2018 PDF (firelookout.org cr-ca-sierra-2018.pdf) returned no readable text, and no readable source mentions the RAC grants, so these are left out of events. 'BRF' in the 2010 report is not expanded in any source read. Staffing, notable fires and rental status were not found. A WebSearch snippet from fs.usda.gov (media/135997) says Mount Tom is the only Sierra NF lookout eligible for NRHP listing, but that PDF returned no text in fetch and is not cited. Also unread: onX and peakbagging.com pages (snippets give 30-34 ft and 9,030 ft). Current access should be checked with the Sierra National Forest before trusting the seasonal access note.

Very thin record. Kemnow's page has only a heading; FFLA gives coordinates, AWS type and gone status; peakbagging gives the 3,564 ft elevation, Chualar map and LO-site label. Peakbagging also lists the park/other land column as 'Private Land'; not verified and not used in the story. No build date, staffing or fire record found. The story is shorter than the usual 120-word floor because the sources have nothing more. The WebSearch calls for this site returned nothing useful; the AWS definition came from one extra Wikipedia read beyond the page budget. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 3,564 ft figure is the lookout elevation (EL column), not the summit.

The register supplies the 1919 fire duty and the July 1924 fire, but no build date; the build date comes from Wikipedia, which gives first completion in 1910 and completion in 1912 after an optics delay. Angeles Adventures is a hobby site that relays Thornton's book and 1920s newspapers; its 1924 Forest Service start date is not confirmed by a primary source. The 1924 year for the Los Angeles Times item comes from the '1924:' heading on the Angeles Adventures page, not from the item text. Access: the PBS SoCal sentence is the only source that places visitors inside the 150-foot tower, and it says usually, not always, and it is undated; the observatory's own site confirms the grounds and tours but does not mention the tower. Tour prices and hours were not checked and change. The record's agency is Mount Wilson Observatory; the observatory's site says the Mount Wilson Institute manages it, which may be worth noting in the record. Photos: the register images are all rights reserved, so none were added.

Register's own text conflicts on the build year (1936 description vs 1948 Built field), the loss of a tower (1967 caption vs 1986 standing lookout) and removal (1990s, by 1991, 1980s per hiking guide). Brief's '1948 built' and '1990 removed' are corrected. Access set to restricted from the hiking guide's note about the gate closing at sunset; secondary source, and the summit is a communications site, so check before publishing. The 1967 fire comes from a Union-Tribune article; the excerpt read describes the fire but does not mention the lookout. No photo added: captions cited, but no image URL or licence verified.

Current staffing and access are only confirmed to May 14, 2020 (visit report). The planned June 1, 2020 start is a plan, not a confirmed fact; the staffing status says so. No rental source was read and no later visit report appears on the NHLR page. The weebly newspaper items end in 1931. The tower's height is a 1929 plan (70 ft) and a 1930 comparison (50 ft taller than the old station), not a measured figure, so no height_m is recorded. No corrections to the brief's record were found. Budget: about three page reads and no web searches used.

Brief coordinates (36.0161, -118.6143) match NHLR; fire-lookouts.org gives 36.0057 N, 118.3655 W, about 22 km away in longitude, so the brief coordinates were left unchanged. The brief elevation is corrected in corrections because two sources say 8,142 ft. The InciWeb citation uses the inciweb-dev.fs2c.usda.gov host the search returned; the canonical InciWeb address was not checked. NHLR is undated in the text read. The Forest Service trail page is undated in the text read. The 1947 and 1948 condor items come from a Forest Lookouts page that quotes Fresno Bee items. No source read describes the site after the 2021 fire beyond the rubble photos; access and any remains today are unverified. Two WebSearch calls and six distinct page reads were used.

The two sources are near-duplicates (NHLR cites fire-lookouts.org as its source), so this is effectively a single-source history. No information found on current public access, a rental program, or precise staffing end date. The brief's event list matched these two sources exactly; no corrections needed. Worth a follow-up check with Sierra National Forest or Forest Fire Lookout Association for current access/condition details.

Not verified: the record's 2007 rehab event (189 steps, Buck Rock Foundation) and the $13,000 rebuild figure. The buckrock.org and ponderosaca.com pages returned HTTP 404, and the December 2012 update gives no dollar amount. Recorder article (HTTP 429 on two tries) not read. California 2017 PDF yielded no Needles text. The record's kind two_story is not confirmed by these sources and is left unchanged. WebSearch budget was used up before this lookout, so no further searches were run.

Current condition rests on a 2012 blog and a 2017 hiking write-up; no 2020s source was read. The Ojai Valley News article returned HTTP 429 twice and firelookouthost.org returned 404, so ffla_groups 'ruins' (brief) is unchecked. Height 152.4 m removed as unsupported. The replacement's loss is recorded only as 'the 1970s' in the sources, so no year event is listed for it. 1935 is the start of construction per a newspaper; completion year not found. Staffing after 1956 not found.

Thin record. Kemnow's page has one dated item, a 1923 Blue Lake Advocate clipping about a lookout station at the head of Squaw Creek, a tributary of the Pit River. It does not name North Fork Mountain, so it is not used as build or staffing history. FFLA: Ground type, Gone, no register number. Peakbagging: LO site, elevation 5,358 ft; the Shasta-Trinity forest value was checked against the table's Forest column on 2026-10-10. Do not confuse with the West Virginia North Fork Mountain (Pendleton County, Smoke Hole); a Wikipedia article under that name was read and is about the wrong mountain. No staffing, fire or removal record found. Two WebSearch calls returned nothing usable for this site.

No current access rule, visit report or rental listing was in any of the four pages read. The NHLR page has no visit reports for this tower. The HABS PDF is an OCR text and some digits are garbled (for example the wooden tower year and the 54-foot height), so quotes were chosen from clean text on the history page or the Register. The historic-structures page asks readers for a status update, which is why access stays unconfirmed. The staffing as_of 1971 is the last fire-season year, not a current status. Budget: about six page reads; one web search for rentals returned no direct listing.
No source consulted gave a tower height in meters, so height_m was omitted from facts rather than filled with the elevation figure.

Dates conflict: 1934 plan, 1939 CCC wood tower (register), 1942 wood tower (1974 article), 1958 vs 1959 steel tower, and a 1932-33 road vs 1934 road crews. Current staffing and access are unknown; the latest staffing note is a 2012 photo caption. The county agenda item is dated June 9, 2015 (Board Agenda Date), and the story gives that date. No public access info found, so no access key. The register's 2018 photos were not captured as image URLs, so no photos added.

Status correction is the main finding: the record says gone, but the cab stands on a relay tower with a weather radar dome (Angeles Adventures and register photo caption; not seen first-hand). Height and replacement dimensions conflict across sources (30 vs 36 ft; 30 ft vs ten feet taller). The 1973 closure date comes from the Angeles guide alone; the register says in use through at least 1968. Staff names are from the Angeles guide and the 1924 newspaper quote; the guide's names are not checked against the Los Angeles Times or The Signal. The 1923 'Oak Hill' name needs a look. Access level is restricted because the summit is an equipment site; no source describes public access to the cab. Photos on the register page (1926 Los Angeles Times, 1963 The Signal) are credited but no image URLs were verified, so none were added. Two web searches and about six reads were used.

Staffing conflict: the register says staffed in fire season as of 2015, while Peakbagging (photo dated November 2007) says abandoned for some years. Undated, so the newer source is unknown. Elevation conflict: the register gives 7,970 ft (2,429 m), Peakbagging 7968 ft, and the tipurdy page 7964 ft; the story gives all three. No access, visit or structure height data found, so those keys are omitted. A Wikimapia page returned no text when fetched and is not used. The record's built year 1960 is only the 1960s decade.

Today's status rests on one 2020 bike route guide, not a survey or site visit. Access level is omitted: no source states whether the site is open to visitors, and the 1971 access note is historical. The 1919 date is hedged in FFLOS ('may have been'). The 1921 station may or may not be the same structure as FFLOS's original; the brief's 1933 build date is correct for the enclosed tower. No photos added: captions only (a 1981 photo credited to the Siskiyou County Historical Society via FFLOS; 1981 and 2009 photo credits on the Siskiyou County page), and no image URLs were retrieved. The 1971 'Ida Lake' staffing is the last keeper found; later staffing is unknown.

Brief record confirmed: 1935 build, standing, Cal Fire NEU agency. Current staffing is not confirmed past the 2021 volunteer call. The YouTube link in the brief was not read. Access restricted to the public per NHLR; the brief's access 'unknown' is replaced accordingly.

The Forest Lookouts page quotes Chronological History of the Klamath National Forest volumes and Blue Lake Advocate and Siskiyou items; I did not check the original volumes. Source 3's title and publisher now match the PDF's own header (Forest Fire Lookout Association, California-Northern Chapter, 2025 Year-End Report). The 2025 report also has an Orleans entry marked 'Project Status: PENDING' that mentions tribal consultation; the project's scope was not confirmed, so the story does not use it. The 2013 item dates the wrap as 'August (7?), 2013', so the year is the only firm date. Access and rental status are not established; the brief lists access as unknown. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook post in search results returned only its title, so it is not used. No photos added. Brief corrections: the built event needs the 1914 house and the 1933 replacement.

Current status is contested. The register says both staffed each fire season and Sometimes, and lists the lookout as available for rental; a 2010 photo page says it has been converted to a rental lookout. The rental claim is not confirmed by a booking source, and the register's rentals page I checked does not name Orr Mountain. The register's staffing entry is undated; as_of 2019 comes from the October 2, 2019 visit report. The register gives elevation 5,823 ft and Peakbagging gives 5,830 ft; not recorded. The forest service 2013 article linked from the register (fs.fed.us) could not be fetched. Search budget: three web searches were run for this record, one over the two-search limit.

The 1988 negative declaration is garbled ('AT THE SAN BENITO COUNTY VENTION DISPLAY'). CEQAnet says the attachments are not online and must be requested from CAL FIRE, so the destination is not confirmed. The 1988 filings name Pacheco Peak and a lookout tower but not the register's cabin or tower directly; the link to the register's record rests on the same summit and the same era, and a reviewer could confirm it with CAL FIRE. The register's removal window (1986 to 1991) fits the 1988 filing. The brief's 1980 removal year has no source and is proposed for correction. Staffing, public access and current site condition were not found in any source read. Photos: none new; the register's 1977 and 2013 photos are already in the record. Searches: one WebSearch on the history and removal of the lookout, one on the 1988 and 1994 CEQAnet records.

Thin sourcing: four listings and one table key. The Forest Lookouts page has only the site name and agency, with no history. Two searches found no build date, builder, staffing, fire or current-site description, so the story is short and says nothing about those topics. The peakbagging key suggests no remains may exist, but that is a general definition, not a site report. Record kind 'ground', status 'gone', agency and coordinates match the listings; no corrections. Ownership 'federal' is not stated by a source read here; it is consistent with Mendocino NF. Worth a fresh search for a Mendocino NF lookout history before publishing.

Built year conflicts: the register says 1914, the July 1913 newspaper expected occupancy by August 1, 1913, and the telephone line was finished October 1914. The 1926 chronology entry says the cabin was actually at Big Bend Meadow, but the register says a nearby cabin was used early on; the story does not reconcile these. The Forest Lookouts chronology stops in 1931, so the register's 'served into the 1960s' is not confirmed by the sources read. Staffing names are from newspaper items only. Access and current condition not found; the register says nothing remains. One WebSearch returned hiking and peak-listing pages plus a lead to a 1958 Klamath National Forest lookout eligibility study, which was not read. No new photos; the record's Nancy Hood photo is already in the record.

Ownership is 'unknown' in the record, but Forest Lookouts quotes the 1931 county annual report calling the peak county-owned property; consider setting ownership to county. No staff names were found, so staffing is left out. No photo with a usable URL was found; Angeles Adventures credits LA Public Library photos but links none. Angeles Adventures spells the airport 'Whitman' where the usual name is Whiteman; the story avoids the name. The demolition date is not given by any source read, so the story says only that the tower is listed as demolished. Record kind 'tower', agency and coordinates match the sources.

Current staffing and public access are not established; the brief lists access as unknown and the NHLR page does not address it. The NHLR says Location: Siskiyou National Forest, while the Forest Lookouts page files the lookout under Siskiyou County and CDF; the story uses the NHLR's administrator. The 1932 chronology entry is internally inconsistent: it is dated February 23, 1932 but refers to a Saturday, September 27th; the story now flags that the year is uncertain. The NHLR page does not expand 'ECW', so the story keeps the abbreviation. The brief's event list has no construction event; the 1935 build and the 1932 house are added. A search snippet for an ALERTCalifornia Facebook post says the lookout was built in 1935 and that ALERTCalifornia installed cameras there in 2023; Facebook returned only the post title on fetch, so it is not cited. A reviewer who can open it could confirm current use. The Forest Lookouts page also lists a 1934 panorama photo session and a 1948 season; not used beyond the events. No photos added. The brief's kind (ground), status (standing) and NHLR registration (October 27, 2019) match the sources; no corrections proposed.

Only two pages with substance were available: the register entry and the Forest Lookouts page. The construction date is 'circa 1931' per the Thornton Survey, and the May 1931 newspaper item shows the lookout in use by then. The land manager is disputed: National Park Service and Sequoia National Park on the register, Sequoia National Forest on the Forest Lookouts page. The brief's access 'unknown' stands. The status 'gone' rests only on the FFLA list; no source describes removal or the site today. A WebSearch surfaced a Sequoia and Kings Canyon historic photo record (calisphere.org, item 190e4fcea67a2073300486ec4dd7b2db) tagged 1930 for pack materials to the Paradise Peak lookout site; the page returned no readable text, so it is not cited. A reviewer who can open it could confirm a 1930 construction start and the NPS attribution. Photos: none new.

Unresolved: the two-story wooden lookout is dated 1929 by the register and 1934 by the NPS article. The cab is 13 by 13 feet per the register, while Buck Rock and the NPS give the steel tower as 14 by 14 feet. The firewatcher's surname is spelled Simms by Buck Rock and Sims by the NPS. Elevation is 7,471 ft in the register and 7,520 ft on Buck Rock. Current hours come from a 2026 Buck Rock page and should be rechecked before publication. The French Wikipedia stub was read but not used.

Ownership is 'unknown' in the record; no source read names the owner of the tower site, and Angeles Adventures calls most of the mountain BLM public land. The access level 'public' rests on that land-status line; the roads at the base are private, and no rule on entry to the old site was found. The Sage Menu page is a user-review hiking listing and is used only to corroborate the concrete base that Angeles Adventures also describes. Record kind 'enclosed_tower', status 'gone', coordinates and agency match the sources. Two searches turned up no demolition date and no staff beyond 1938 and 1949.

Elevation conflict: the register gives 3,975 ft (1,212 m), Peakbagging gives 4024 ft; the record uses the register value. No source gives access level, so no access key. Current status after the 2016 photo note is unknown. Photo: a public-domain 1952 outhouse photo is on Internet Archive (casbcfm_000230); the direct image file URL was not captured, so no photos entry was added.

No source after 2016 on the mountain tower, so its current condition is unverified. The brief's source_pages entry '../us-ca-pegleg-mountain-at-susanville-fairgrounds/' is a broken relative link (the NHLR address returns 404), so it was not used. A CAL FIRE LMU Facebook post, seen only as a search snippet and not read, gives 1985 for the dismantling; that date is not cited, so the move is recorded as 1984 from Lassen News. The 1913 versus 1920s question about which building went to the fairgrounds is unresolved. Access to the mountain tower is not covered by any source, so no access key is given. Used 5 page reads (one returned 404) and 1 search.

Sources conflict on whether the fairgrounds structure is the original 1913-era lookout or a replica. Lassen News says the old lookout went there; the register says the 1920s lookout went there and a replica was on display by 2008; the 1984 and 1985 county notices speak of a replica and then a reassembled exhibit. A CAL FIRE Facebook post (dates the move to 1985 and says replica) could not be read and is not used. The parent record dates the move to 1984. The Sierra Daily News original returned 403; the same text was read via NewsBreak. No report after July 2023 on current hours; the status note and access note say so.

Only two readable sources. The register has no status field, so the story no longer says the tower is standing; firelookout.org's California list (NHLR US 1323, CA 146) marks the site Standing, which an editor could cite with a quoted line if wanted. The brief's 2019 assessment (9 Dec 2019, Buck Rock Foundation support) is not in the story: its source, firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/cr-ca-sierranv-2019.pdf, returned no text from fetch_text, so it is unverified. Coordinates: register gives 37.731953, -120.261390; the brief's west_us_lookouts record gives -120.2506 longitude (about 1 km east); register used. Registry number: register detail page says US 1327, CA 150; firelookout.org list says US 1323, CA 146; the list may be stale. No staffing history, notable fires or current access arrangement found. One search snippet mentioned a Coulterville bed-and-breakfast named Penon Blanco Lookout; it is not linked to this tower in any source read, so it is left out.

Today's status is the weakest part: the only 2023 source is a hiking blog, which describes climbing the tower; the story does not encourage that, and the record should not treat the blog as an official status. No official access rule or closure notice was found. Peakbagging's staffing line is undated. Build-date conflict (1965 Register vs 1972 footing) is reported, not resolved. A 2018 Trinity Journal snippet says the lookout dates to 1972; that article returned HTTP 429 to fetch_text and was not read or cited. The Forest Service project summary for fire-detection cameras on Shasta-Trinity (search snippet only) was not read and may or may not involve this site. Photos: the NHLR page has a photo credit (2009, courtesy of Ron Kemnow; 1972 anchor pier, courtesy of peakbagging.com) but no image URLs were read, so none added. Budget: 6 distinct pages read (NHLR, Weebly, 2013 FFLA report, Peakbagging, valhikes blog, FS trail page) against 6, plus 2 web searches. The brief's 1965 build and 2013 staffing events are confirmed; the brief's 2019 registration is confirmed.

Brief errors: built 1983 is the relocation year, and height_m 24.4 m is the 1913 tree platform (see corrections). No source read gives visitor access or climbing rules, so the story says so and no access key is set. Staffing evidence is a 2006 photo caption plus 1920s-40s newspaper items; no current staffing data was found. One WebSearch was used.

Build year conflict (1958 Register vs 1985 Peakbagging) is unresolved; the story says so. The Pilot Peak name is linked to this tower by matching descriptions (CAL FIRE list, CBS report, Peakbagging page), not by a source that states it outright. CBS report has no date on the cached copy. mtdemocrat.com article on CAL FIRE bringing four towers back into use returned HTTP 429 twice and is not used; it may be worth a retry. A CAL FIRE Amador-El Dorado post in search results mentions the Pilot Hill lookout spotting a fire; not fetched, so not used. Access is recorded as restricted from a 10/91 note in the NHLR and may be out of date.

The Tahoe Quarterly piece carries '26 Sep' and is filed under 'Fall 2025', so its season matches the register's fall 2025 repair start; it is not dated more precisely. The NHLR 2007 visit report is the only detailed condition report. The brief's note about a different NHLR number is explained by the separate Stanislaus lookout (US 1394), which is excluded. No 2026 status was found, so 'standing, inactive' rests on the register and Tahoe Quarterly. No closure notice was found; access is recorded from the 2007 visit report and the Tahoe article. Used 5 page reads and 1 search.

Newest staffing and condition evidence is the 2012 chapter report; current staffing, condition and public access are unconfirmed. The brief's access 'unknown' is omitted rather than filled in, because no access route was readable: the trailforks Pilot Peak Road listing returned HTTP 403. The brief's 2012 'modified' event is supported, but the report calls the work in progress, so the story says so. The 2012 report also has a separate 'Pilot - Not staffed' entry in another district's list; the text read does not tie it to this lookout, so it is not used. The 1962 build is recorded as 1962, the start of the NHLR's 1962-63 range. The height of 20 feet is converted to 6.1 m. No photos were added: the NHLR page's 2010 photo credit is to Ron Kemnow and the license is not stated.

No access key is set: the BLM open-access statement covers BLM parcels in the Preserve, and no source read describes the lookout compound or says whether the public may climb or enter it. The lookout shares the summit with repeater towers, which may restrict entry. No notable fire is recorded in the sources read. Staffing evidence is a December 2004 photo caption and 1937-38 newspaper items. One WebSearch was run for this tower; the Wikipedia reserve article and CNPS tour pages were seen in results but not fetched.

Brief's 2009 NHLR registration date and firelookout.org county label ('Los Angeles') for NHLR US 773 appear to be a rendering glitch on the firelookout.org list page; NHLR's own detail page confirms Mendocino NF, so I did not use firelookout.org as a cited source. Did not independently verify the 2009 registration date against a primary NHLR page excerpt (the live NHLR page I fetched didn't show the registration date field in the text returned), so it's carried from the brief rather than newly confirmed. Verification pass 2026-10-04: re-fetched californialookouts.weebly.com directly and confirmed via the Aug 7, 1944 Redwood Journal item that Mersinger's injury happened 'on Pine mountain while fire fighting' and that he is 'forestry lookout at Pine Mountain, near Upper Lake' -- the separate Aug 9, 1944 Ukiah Republican Press item calls the site the 'Pine Hill Lookout,' which is an inconsistency in the original press clippings, not a different site; both articles are about the same lookout and both are now cited.

Register and newspaper sources agree on the 1935 build and the 1968 burning, and the brief record matches them, so no corrections are proposed. Staffing ends 'by the late 1940s' per the register and is consistent with a 1968 item saying the tower had been abandoned for 20 years; no staffed_last event is written because the source gives no exact year. The cloud seeding use is recorded as an 'other' event dated 1960 (decade start only). The register's 'hippies' attribution is repeated with attribution and not endorsed; the Pasadena excerpt does not name a cause. Public access and current site condition are not described in any source read, so no access or visit facts are written. The Angeles Adventures lookouts page lists Pine Mountain, but its text was not read for site details. The brief id ends in '-2', which suggests a sibling record for another Pine Mountain. A rental listing says a Lake County Pine Mountain near Potter Valley was built in 1933 and used for fire detection until 1942; that is a different site and is not used here. No photos are listed: the register's newspaper images (dated March 29, 1934 and July 19, 1964) are credited but their image URLs were not captured.

Built, staffing and fate rest mainly on the register, which quotes a Stanislaus National Forest note; the 1934 construction is supported by two 1934 newspaper items as quoted on Forest Lookouts. The brief's note that another record shares register number US 1883, CA 78 was not resolved: the register page itself confirms that number for this site, and the other holder was not identified. The brief's 'ground' kind matches the register's 'ground cabin' wording. Access is recorded as public only because a hiking guide describes a trail to the site on national forest land; no closure or permit rule was read, so an editor may want a Stanislaus National Forest check before relying on the access level. The trail guide's account that the structure stood on the mountainside, and the glass-windowed station it recalls, were left out of the story because they come from a visitor's recollection on that page. Photos: the register lists a 1935 photo and a 2011 photo with credits, but no image URLs were captured, so none are listed.

Low confidence because the build year 1923 rests on one register field, and no source read gives a removal date. The register's status is 'Former' with removal unknown; SummitPost's 'once had a fire lookout' supports the present-day 'gone' status but is an undated climbing guide. The Forest Lookouts (weebly) page for this site has no descriptive text beyond the header and was not cited. A search snippet from a video titled for Pinnacle Rock described a metal anchor left at the summit; the video page did not load as text, so the claim is unverified and left out of the story. Editor should check it before any note about remains is added. The 1945 photo's image URL was not captured, and the license of the USFS Flickr page was not visible in the text read, so no photos entry is written. The register's own 1945 photo is credited to the Upper Lake Ranger District collection; its image URL was also not captured.

Height disagrees: 30 feet (register) against 36 feet (Los Padres history via Forest Lookouts). The trip report is undated in the text we read; find its date before publishing the remains line with more weight. The register's 'Nothing remains at the site' conflicts with the trip report's four pillars. The Marble Cone Fire facts come from Wikipedia; its cited sources were not read. The Santa Maria Daily Times quote is secondhand through the Forest Lookouts page. Access rules today are not in any source read. Sid Ormsbee lookout is a different site; it is mentioned only as a warning.

Location conflict not resolved: FFLOS gives 35.47994, -118.35937 (used in the brief); the west_us_lookouts record gives 35.45107, -118.39175. No build date or design found in the sources read. The 1931 and 1936 items spell the lookout's first name Theo and Ted; I did not assume they are the same man in the story. A trailforks listing (seen only in search results; fetch returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited) says the old Piute Lookout tower no longer exists; worth checking by hand. An undated Sequoia NF post mentions a Peak Fire near Piute Peak; not used. Budget: 2 searches, 5 page reads.

Thin record: one register detail page, one Forest Lookouts page that credits Irma Oksen Reaves's 1988 book, and the register list. The register credits its photo to that book but gives no image URL, so no photo entry was added. Search snippets mention a 2026 Plaskett Fire in Monterey County, but none of the pages read tie it to this site, so the story does not mention it. No source says whether the public can reach the area.

No source read says whether the public may visit or climb the tower, so no access level is recorded. The CCC build year is not in any source read. Sources disagree on the 1955/1956 move and the Lone Pine start date (1920 vs 1924). The Weebly page for Platte is only a county index and is not cited. The 2008 CAL FIRE list is the only staffing source besides the 2017 photo page. The first record's 1956 build date is a relocation date.

Registry numbers disagree: register detail page says US 1368, CA 191; firelookout.org California list says NHLR US 1309, CA 132. Register used. The register does not use the word cab for this tower, so the story describes it as a BC-301 plan on a steel tower. Status 'standing' from the brief is not confirmed by any source read here, and the story does not claim it; the firelookout.org status column did not extract. Access and visiting arrangements not found. The November 1941 item says Duncan had been on Plummer for 32 years, which predates the 1937 tower; unresolved, and the story says so. A search snippet described a roughly 5-mile East Tule Trail hike from FR 2N10/3N08; the Forest Service handout URL returned 404 and the claim is not cited. The 1940 quote is attributed to Trinity Forest News on the source page, dated June 28, 1940.

Coordinates disagree: the brief point (38.6122946, -120.4477204, from OpenStreetMap) and FFLOS (38.62991, -120.38012) are about six km apart. The story says so and does not pick one. Status disagrees too: the brief says gone, FFLOS says Abandoned; the story keeps gone because the OSM tag and the peak-list LO site point the same way. Only one dated item was on the Forest Lookouts page (1929). A 2019 Eldorado NF lookout booklet on docslib names Plummer Lookout only in a garbled line, so it is not cited. Newspaper archives (The Mountain Democrat, via CDNC) were not searched; they could add construction and removal dates. Budget: 2 searches, 4 page reads.

No build date or design found in the sources read. The 1935-37 notices come from newspapers quoted on Forest Lookouts; the 1937 notice says the station 'will open' May 5, so the opening is not confirmed. The brief's coordinates (36.00395, -120.0571) match FFLOS; the Wikipedia Kettleman Hills infobox gives a close point. FFLOS type is Unknown and the brief kind agrees, so no correction. Not tried: Hanford Sentinel or Fresno Bee archives after 1937, which might show when the station closed. Budget: 2 searches, 4 page reads.

Thin record: two 1937-38 Ukiah newspaper items, one Peakbagging photo page and two listing pages. firelookout.org row for Poison Rock: type Encl. Tower, status Gone, no register number. The NHLR US 1368, CA 191 first drafted here belongs to Plummer Peak (Trinity County) and was removed. The kind correction to tower was withdrawn because firelookout.org lists Encl. Tower. Access and ownership unverified; no visit facts recorded.

Record elevation_m 652 uses the register's 2,139 ft; the land trust and 2019 Press Democrat say 2,204 ft (about 672 m), so the record may want updating. The 1967 built year is for the Red Oat Mountain tower; the 1981 move was missing from the record and is added to events. Could not confirm from pages read whether the new steel building has opened, so status is left as the record has it (standing). Staffing as_of is undated because the group's pages carry no dates. Staffing and closure dates conflict between the 2018 volunteer report and the 2019 Press Democrat. Not used: a Cazadero CSD update that said the lookout was open, seen only in a search snippet and not read on the page.

Only the foundation is described today; no source states access or whether the peak is open to visitors. The 1951 Pony Peak Fire (about 4,900 acres near Cottage Grove, per a wildfire lessons-learned page) shares the peak's name, but no source ties it to the lookout, so it is left out. The 1924 and 1928 references to a Pony Peak Lookout predate the 1934 cabin FFLOS calls the first structure; the story says so without resolving it. Staffing dates come from the register, not an official roster. No photos added: captions only (a 1925 temporary-site photo on FFLOS; a 1925 photo credit on the Siskiyou County page), and no image URLs were retrieved.

Design, 1934 build date and 2019 NHLR registration are well supported. Staffing and fire history were not found in the two searches and page reads, so the story says nothing about staffing; the record's staffing stays unknown. The record's access 'unknown' is set to public because the cabin is a reservable rental; a human may want to confirm the access wording. Name differs by source (NHLR 'Fireman-Lookout House', Forest Service and Recreation.gov 'Guard Station'). The record's built=1934 and nhlr_registered=2019 are correct; no corrections proposed. Capacity and plumbing conflicts are reported in the story, not resolved.

Single source: the FFLOS register entry. The californialookouts page for Potato Hill carries only an index line, so it is not cited. Two WebSearch calls found nothing about this lookout; the Potato Hill trail listings (try-ranger, trailforks) are not tied to this site and were left out. The register gives the tower height as '20 enclosed' with no unit, so no height is recorded. No photo URLs were captured, only the caption and credit. The story has no staffing, fire or access detail because no source gives any.

Single source: the FFLOS register entry. The californialookouts Poverty Hill page is an index line only, so it is not cited. The mindat page for the Poverty Hill mining district returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Two WebSearch calls found no other account of this lookout. No photo URLs were captured, only the caption and credit. Height converted from 25 ft to 7.6 m. The story has no staffing, fire or access detail because no source gives any.

Three sources. Register (1934 build, 45-ft tower) conflicts with a 1931 newspaper (planned 30-ft tower, spring 1931); the story uses the register. The 2006 CAL FIRE notice planned removal for restoration and possible display; no source read says the display happened, and the register says the cab and 14 ft remain on site, so the plan and the register do not match. Corrected the brief's removed year: 2011 is the visit that found the tower already dismantled. The 1931, 1935 and 1985 items come from the californialookouts clippings, which quote newspapers; the originals were not read. The 1985 KERG item is cited to the clipping only. No photo URLs captured (captions and credits only). Staffing 1982 is the photo caption; no later staffing found. Two WebSearch calls used: the second found no record of the planned display.

The brief's built 1912 and removed 1981 both check out against the register and the 1981 article. Open conflicts: (1) Wikipedia says the lookout is on the peak and otherwise intact, citing a 1977 NRHP nomination form by Gordon Chappell. The NPS nomination URL we tried (npgallery 78000295_text) returned a PNG image, not text, so the form itself was not read. (2) Mule route start: Blue Lake (register) vs Butte Lake (1981 article); both are quoted in the story. (3) The register's transfer to the San Bernardino NF is dated only to 'the early 2000's', so no event with a year is recorded for it. (4) The register says the Forest dismantled the Cajon Mountain tower. A search snippet from SummitPost describes a tower on Cajon summit 'missing its cabin and platform'. That page was not read, so it is not used; check it before relying on either account. Staffing and notable fires: none in the sources read, so none recorded. Access: the register gives no visiting information, so no access key. Do not confuse with West Prospect Peak, a separate lookout in Lassen National Forest; a search snippet says it is still in service, which is unverified and not used. No photos added.

Thin record. The register has no Built field and no other source read gives a build date or builder. The July 1947 item names Ray Arnold as a lookout on Quartz Hill for the Forest Service and quotes a Klamath National Forest official; it does not name the forest Arnold worked for, so the story does not say so. The register names CDF as administrator. Status 'standing' from the brief is unverified: the firelookout.org list tags the site FFLOS and its status column did not extract. Access comes from one undated trip report, so gates may have changed. A search snippet listed a 1958 Klamath National Forest lookout inventory held at Southern Oregon University (sou.libraryhost.com); not read, not used. Suggest checking the Quartz Hill row in the firelookout.org California list before publication.

Record says gone; firelookout.org says gone (type ground); visitor accounts describe a communications site and no lookout cab. The firelookout.org row for Radio Hill has no register number. An earlier draft's NHLR US 1153, CA 114 and Encl. Tower belong to Quartz Hill and were removed. The kind correction to enclosed_tower was withdrawn because firelookout.org lists Ground, which matches the current value. The 1948 call was a May 1948 plan, not a confirmed event. Ownership unverified: Peakbagging lists private land, and the 1973 county purchase was authorized but not confirmed as completed. Access level not recorded because no source states it. The 2024 Daily Kos post and the undated Idaho Alpine Zone page are personal accounts, not official records.

Brief note says this record 'shares a register number' with another site. The firelookout.org index table is hard to read from the crawl text, so the match could not be checked; the register's own page gives US 687, CA 10 for Ranger Peak and this record keeps that. Check the other site's record. Unresolved: (1) Cab fate. The register says the cab was enlarged and kept in use until June 2010; Wildfire Today (June 25, 2010) says the crew built a 560-square-foot office from the dismantled remains, moved uphill in 1974. The story reports both. (2) Elevation: the register gives 5,035 ft; SummitPost says 5082 feet (not in the story). (3) Build year: 1926 (register) vs 1935 (SummitPost). The SummitPost page is a climbers' log and its date is not shown in the lines we read; it is the only source for what remains today, so the story presents it as a climber's account. Access: no official source read; the fire road and firebreak details come from the log only. Check San Bernardino NF for closures before relying on the visit note. No staffing or fire history found, so none recorded. Register photos are credited to others and their URLs were not captured; no photos added.

Gone status is well supported by the 1977 USGS recovery note and the firelookout.org row (type Tower, status Gone, no register number). Thin on everything else: the 1935 build date comes from a 1939 history quoted second-hand on Forest Lookouts. The forest name differs across sources. An earlier draft gave FFLOS US 687, CA 10, which belongs to Ranger Peak (Riverside County), so it was removed. 'Only' was dropped from the Six Rivers claim because the full Peakbagging table was not checked. No source describes the site today or its access.

Height conflict: 1934 item says 60-foot steel tower (matches record 18.3 m); 1951 item says 50-foot tower. Not resolved. Status: both FFLA lists read Standing* (cab no longer in place, per legend). An earlier note that the statewide list read Gone was wrong. No source after 1964 for the tower; two web searches found only other Red Hill towers and nothing for Plumas. Staffing history is well sourced from several newspaper clippings transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page (Feather River Bulletin, Indian Valley Record, Plumas Independent, Nevada State Journal, Portola Reporter). No photos found. Do not encourage climbing.

The owner's name is left out of the story and the record; the CBS article names a private resident. The NHLR 'three-story' kind in the brief is not stated in any source read, so it is not recorded. No height is recorded. The 1928 vs 1937 build-year conflict and the 1966 vs 1975 occupancy conflict are not reconciled. CBS page carries no date. No access route for visitors exists: the site is a private residence. The Calisphere item returned no text and is not cited.

Two sources, both agreeing the tower is gone. Two web searches found no build date, builder, staffing or fire history for this Trinity County tower; the Wildwood and Peanut hits were 2025 fire news, not lookouts. The 1961 station description is the only physical description. Shasta-Trinity ranger district files or the Trinity County Historical Society are the likely next checks.
