Thin record. The Forest Lookouts Red Mountain entry for Glenn County is a heading with no body text, the FFLA index gives only a type and status, and the OSM node has tags only (no history, no date). The story is below the 120-word floor because the sources do not support more; expand it once a dated source turns up (NHLR, a newspaper, or Forest Service records). Two web searches found nothing on this site. CAL FIRE's Lookouts list places a Red Mountain Lookout in its Humboldt-Del Norte column, not Glenn County, so it should not be used for this record.

The register's staffing line is undated; as_of is the date it was read. The register registration date and build year are consistent with the 1951 newspaper item. Nothing in the sources says whether the cab survives the communications relocation; the NPS release (dated December 29, 2017, archived) is not an updated source, and its 2022 permit expiry is not confirmed as carried out. The story first said 2018 for that release; the release date is December 2017. Access is recorded as public from the register; climbing is not confirmed, so the story does not encourage it. Photos not recorded: the register lists three photo credits (Osborne Fire-Finder, Sunset View, 2009 by Ron Kemnow) but I found no image URLs. The YouTube link in the record returned no page content.

The fire and the loss are well documented (FFLA report, CAL FIRE, two FFLA pages). No source describes the site after the fire, so access is left unset rather than guessed. The brief lists both burned and destroyed for 2022; they are the same event, so merge them. The name spelling San Bernadino comes from the NHLR title and slug; the forest is the San Bernardino National Forest. Social-media and chamber-of-commerce snippets about the fire were not cited because they were not read as pages.

Two sources only; both describe the site from the outside and neither reports a recent visit, so the 'no public access' point rests on the absence of any visit information. The Register gives elevation 1,608 ft (490 m). The Register's 1973 and FFLA's 1977 replacement dates for the present cab conflict and are both reported. Access was 'unknown' in the brief and is now 'restricted' (active communications site). The brief's 1935 event is attributed to FFLA, not the Register. Not checked: whether any public trail or viewing exists on the Fallbrook communications site. Checked 2026-10-08: the Register's 'near the Mexican border' location is now reported beside FFLA's Fallbrook location. The 1973 vs. 1977 disagreement now cites both sources.

History is well sourced across the register, the CPRR museum page and the forest lookouts page. Current condition rests on one 2023 blog sketch seen from the highway; no source gives current access, ownership details or a physical inspection, so no access or visit facts are recorded. The AllTrails trail page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The record's county (Nevada) matches the forest lookouts page header. The 1920 and 1931 items are newspaper reports quoted on the forest lookouts page; the 1931 item names the man who died, which the story leaves out.

Brief status gone should read relocated: the structure stands at Pole Mountain (see us-ca-pole-mountain). Nothing in the sources describes the Red Oat Mountain site now. Access and staffing today are for the Pole Mountain record: the 2009 visit report predates the 2018 public hiking opening. Move year conflicts across sources (1967 build is consistent). Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Ron Kemnow name was dropped from the citation, because the page does not name him as author.

No source found on current staffing, public access, or whether the cab is open to visitors, so those keys are omitted. The newspaper staffing items end in 1962. Sources spell the lookout staffer both Hansen and Hanson. The register's earlier 1933/34 lookout is not confirmed by the newspaper items I read. The register's photo credit (2008, Ron Kemnow) has no image URL, so no photos are recorded. The GovTribe copies of the RFQ attachments returned HTTP 403; the story relies on the FBO Daily notice. The FBO notice's Amendment 05 (October 1, 2026) changed the quote due date; the story uses the response date shown on the notice. No corrections to the record: the 1941 build year, agency and elevation match the register.

Status is disputed: the register (2018) and fire-lookouts.org (2010 demolition, page updated 2013) conflict, and no newer source was found. A field check would settle whether the cab still stands. The design is disputed (two stories per the register, three per fire-lookouts.org). The June 1928 newspaper items describe construction as planned and under way; none records completion, so the story says the county set about building the station rather than that it was finished. Not used: a kavelookout.com page titled Red Top Lookout (built 1924, replaced 1928, restored 1996-97, Mount Stuart Range), which appears to be a different lookout. A December 1955 photograph of this lookout is catalogued on archive.org (casbcfm_000714, Cal Fire Museum), but I did not check its image URL or licence, so no photo is recorded. The register lists the lookout as Built 1934; the correction is proposed for human review.

All historical detail comes from one page quoting 1931-32 newspapers; two web searches found no second source naming Thomas Boswell or the station. Next checks: Shasta Historical Society archive or Redding Record Searchlight files. Whether the building or station survives is unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Ron Kemnow name was dropped from the citation (the page does not name him as author), and the 1931 fire date now follows the July 9, 1931 report.

Most detail rests on one register page. Its account of the earlier station's fire and crew is a reminiscence (Jack Rimmer, paraphrased by John Damann, quoting a Harrison Irving Scott book), so it is secondhand and gives no year for the fire. The Ridge Route gallery describes the area above the road, not the lookout. The register credits photos and images to Jack Rimmer and Mike Guerin, but gives no image URLs, so no photo entries were added. No source says whether the site is public.

Built 1927 and destroyed 1932 agree across four sources. Height differs (20 ft register vs 14 ft Carey). No new photos with direct URLs captured; firetower.org photos (Ranger and Mrs. Green, 1928; site today, Carey) were not downloaded. Access level 'public' is inferred from the trail walk Carey describes; no closure notice was found. The 2011 visit is the latest description, so the current site condition is unverified.

Nothing in the sources gives a build date, design or history for the Rincon Mountain site itself; the Weebly page has only a county heading. The FFLOS and Carey sources agree that the Nordhoff Peak structure came from Rincon Mountain around 1950. The FFLOS page gives no county, so identity rests on the name and the FFLA county listing. The kind correction is unverified. Carey's 2012 post is a blog; its steel-frame remark is the only source on the current state at Nordhoff Peak.

Brief checks: elevation (2,037.9 m), coordinates and agency match the NHLR page. height_m 209.1 has no source; proposed removal above. The brief's 2017 event (FFLA 500-dollar restoration grant, from cr-ca-sierra-nevada-2017.pdf) is left out: that PDF returned no text through fetch_text and is unverified. Open conflicts: (a) the Forest Service's 1934 staffing start against the 1915 and 1936 notices; (b) the 1987 notice describes a former lookout station becoming the hut, while the FS describes the hut as sharing the summit, so which building is rented is unclear; (c) NHLR marks the site available for rental, while the FS guide says lookout use is not part of the hut rental. The Mountain Democrat article has no year in the fetched text, so the restoration is undated in the story. The FS rental guide is undated, so staffing status is as of an unknown date. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer says a lookout has been on the summit 'since at least 1915'; the 1915 item is a notice that a man would go on duty. The Forest Service rental guide is undated, so its status is reported as of that guide, not today.

The register is the only detailed source. The Cerro Alto page supports only the 1973 end of the Cerro Alto tower; the register does not date the cab's move, so the story does not link the two dates. The 1933 build year is the register's Built field, and 1977 is treated as the cab replacement. The water tank, vault and microwave tower come from notes marked MVT 10/91 and may no longer stand; no newer source was read. The 'restricted' access level is our reading of 'not open to the public'; the register does not use that word. No staffing names or fires were found, so none are recorded. Search results (archive.org and californiarevealed) show photographs of the lookout dated August 1953, August 1956 and May 1958 in a California forestry collection; not used because reuse terms were not checked. A 1968 county board item mentions a Bureau of Land Management letter about the Rocky Butte lookout; not used because it does not say what the letter concerned.

Forest conflict: the register says Modoc National Forest, while the July 1930 Klamath News item says the point lies in the Shasta forest but is run by Modoc officers; both are reported in the story. Brief checks: elevation_m 1578.9 matches the register's 5,180 ft (1,579 m);the peakbagging page gives 5,256 ft, which is not reconciled, so the story gives both. The 1930 Klamath News item (construction to start) does not match the register's 1937 build date; the sources do not say whether the 1930 work happened or was delayed. The register says rebuilt in 1956, the peakbagging page says rework or repairs in 1956. Present public access is not in any source read (a Forest Service directions note linked from the peakbagging page was not located), so no access fact is recorded. Staffing is from the register (undated) and a peakbagging note (photo captions from 2006 and 2012). No photos added: the register and peakbagging photos were not fetched as image URLs. The 1930 road description is quoted as a historic account only. The brief's kind two_story was not changed; the register's cab-on-block-tower description is not clear enough to correct it. Fact-check 2026-10-08: footnotes added to the county-line sentence and the 1930 road sentence; 'living out of a tent' follows the peakbagging wording; 'design' removed from the BC-301 description, which the register does not use; the story now says 'current lookout' where it had said 'current cab'.

The brief's 1986 removal date is an outer limit: the register gives 'After 1973, prior to 1986', so the story says the removal happened in that window. Access 'public' is inferred from the site lying in an EBRPD regional park; no source read gives summit hours or rules, so confirm with EBRPD before publishing. No source read names who staffed the tower, so the staffing section is omitted. No photos added: a 1927 Fritz-Metcalf photo (digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu/record/15455) and a calisphere copy (calisphere.org/item/013ec25fb096d8f3b7b08500eee6ddd3) appeared in search results but were not opened, so license is unchecked. The May versus June 1927 opening conflict is unresolved; a Berkeley Daily Gazette copy or a dedication notice would settle it.

The brief's record is correct on the 1931 build year and the NHLR elevation. Access was 'unknown' but NHLR says the site is not open to the public. Heights disagree across sources (30, 35, 40 ft), so none is recorded. Staffing is from a 2007-era photo page and undated text; no current staffing source was read. The 1970 rental and enlargement are hedged in NHLR. Peakbagging calls this lookout 'Big Hill', but the Eldorado National Forest has a separate Big Hill Lookout; do not conflate the two. Newspaper quotes come through Forest Lookouts; the original newspaper pages were not read.

Height 30.5 m is converted from the register's 100 ft tower figure; the register's 97 ft (30 m) is the site elevation and is not the tower height. Access rests on one 2024 trip report, so it is marked restricted at medium confidence. No fire staffing data were found. A Living New Deal page (403 when fetched) says the tower 'still stands today' per a search snippet; it was not read or cited. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now says the register places the tower in Glenn County and gives Wikipedia's Glenn and Colusa Counties separately; the 2024 blog post is dated September 2024, and the visit date is not stated in the post.

Built date 1934 agrees between the register and the Truckee-Donner article (plaque photo). Visit reports disagree on staffing (2009 staffed, 2010 not, 2015 staffed) and on road needs (2009 two-wheel-drive possible; 2015 4x4 recommended). The 2009 visit report says 10 miles north of Downieville, while the Truckee-Donner article says northwest; the story reports both. The access level public rests on one 2015 visitor comment. No current (2020s) staffing or access source was found; the ArcGIS StoryMaps Lost Sierra Route page returned no text. The brief's kind enclosed_tower was left unchanged: the register describes a live-in cab on a short tower, which does not clearly contradict it. The asbestos mention comes only from the register's description and was not checked elsewhere. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the staffed comment, the early-morning account and the two-wheel-drive comment all come from the one 2009 visit report (Oct 17, 2009), not from two separate 2009 visitors. The 2010 and 2015 reports are separate. The register says the last mile is a bit steep, not steep.

The relocation rests on the register (which gives no move date) and on Carey's 2011 reasoning: a 1950 map showing a building above Salisbury Potrero and none at Black Willow Spring, a 1984 history counting two surviving cabins of that design, one of them there, and one owner's reply. Carey's identification is an inference, so confidence is medium. Open conflict, not resolved: Hike Los Padres (camp survey dated 02-23-2022) describes 'the rustic cabin on Salisbury Potrero' that hikers pass on the Bull Ridge Trail. That may be a different building, or the AWS post may not have been wholly moved. A field check or a Los Padres National Forest source would settle it. The relocated event is omitted because no move date is known and the event schema needs a year. The record's kind 'unknown' is left for an editor; the sources call it a cabin or AWS post. Name: the record's 'Portero' matches neither the register ('Portrero') nor Carey and Hike Los Padres ('Potrero'); a correction is proposed. Access: Carey says a ranching family owns the cabin and leases the land under it, so it is treated as private. The register's photo (credited to the USFS and Craig R. Carey collection) has no URL in the sources read, so no photos were added. The Jackson Cabin name comes from Carey and is not in the register.

Build date is disputed: the register's Built field says 1935 but its description says the cabin was constructed as early as 1922; the 1922 LA Times item was a plan, and Angeles Adventures says 1927-28 with operation to 1935. The 1937 move to Vetter Mountain rests on Angeles Adventures quoting D. Von Schmausen's Vetter Mountain paper, which we did not read. The 2009 loss and 2019-2020 rebuild come from ANFFLA and match the existing us-ca-vetter-mountain record, which also notes a 1935 vs 1937 build-year conflict; both records point to the same lookout but do not show it is the San Gabriel cab. The footings line in Angeles Adventures may refer to Vetter Mountain rather than the summit, so today's remains on San Gabriel Peak are unconfirmed. Both Vetter cabs are 14 by 14 feet, which fits the move but is not proof. Staffing names disagree (Mathys for the 1929 season in the 1930 paper; Glenn Moore in 1929 per Angeles Adventures). No access rule was found for the summit, so no access key is set. Worth a look: whether the 1937 relocation belongs in the Vetter Mountain record.

Only two sources, both register-style pages that share their text. Build year conflicts (1922 register vs circa 1930 chapter); the register's Built field is used. Neither source states access, so facts.access is omitted rather than guessed (brief had unknown). The californialookouts.weebly.com San Juan page was read: its header lists 'California Department of Forestry' and 'Removed' with no narrative, which conflicts with the USFS agency; it is not cited. No staffing dates or fires found in the sources read; the emergency-staffing line is kept as 'thought to have been used'. No photos.

No fire history and no staffing details appear in either source read, so the record has no staffed or fire events. Access 'unknown' is replaced with closed, based on the Register's 'not open to the public'; that note is undated, so the present-tense access claim rests on it alone. Search snippets from AllTrails, Komoot, Yelp, Tripadvisor and Facebook describe visiting the area; they were not read and are not used. The 1945 fence and 1960 handover are added beyond the brief's two events. The 1934 build date in the brief matches the Register. The Register's 1934 photo (Pasadena Post) and 2017 photo (Brad Eells) have no license stated, so none are listed. The 30-foot height is from the Register, converted to 9.1 m. The Register lists the site under the second URL form (nhlr.org/nhlr.org/...) in the brief; it was not read separately.

History rests on the register and newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts site; the 1936 fire date is the October 2, 1936 newspaper date, not a confirmed fire date. Today's remains and the access picture come from a 2025 hiker's trip report and a summit page, not an official source. Access is marked restricted: the 2025 trip report describes a seasonal gate on Forest Road 1N34 and a summer closure, and no site-level rule was found; a Forest Service check before any visit would settle the current status. Record height_m 3.0 is consistent with the 10-foot tower. The summit page's 1935 timber-tower claim is noted but not adopted.

No source read gives a build date for the city lookout or says what became of it. The record's gone status rests on the FFLA list alone, which we did not quote. The 1924 item describes a plan. The LAFD Mountain Patrol history (lafra.org) says the department built three lookout stations and does not name San Vicente, so it is not used. An Angeles Adventures lookouts blog appeared in search and may cover this lookout; it was not read because the page budget was spent. The Nike site is at San Vicente Mountain Park; whether it sits on the old lookout's summit is not stated.

Remains on the summit are confirmed by two sources (a 2005 photo page and the Forest Service); neither says which lookout generation they are. A search snippet for a 360Cities panorama describes foundations of the 1926 and 1957 towers, but that page returned 403 and is not cited. The 1939 forest history and the 1919 diary are quoted through the Weebly page, not read directly. Agency and kind are the two points for a human to check; the kind correction is unverified.

Built year: the record's 1923 is taken from the register's 'Circa 1923/1933/1961' field; the register text dates the current structure to 1961, so a correction is proposed, not applied. 1987 fire: the September 3 'destroyed' and September 13 'spared' items are quoted second-hand on the Forest Lookouts page; the original Ukiah Daily Journal items were not read, so the disagreement is reported, not resolved. Current status: no official 2020s source was read. The 2019 trip report is one visitor's account of a decommissioned cab with antennae. The FFLA California list row was not legible enough to confirm status. A search result mentioned a fire on private land near Little Signal Peak; its date and any effect on the lookout were not confirmed, so it is left out. Staffing: the 1992 note is the last staffing reference found. Access: the Forest Service page is the authority for public access. No climbing is encouraged. No new photos added; the record's register photos carry 'All rights reserved'.

Not proposed as a correction, because two sources agree on the record's point. A firelookout.org California list has a Santa Margarita entry with NHLR US 1328, CA 151 and the record's coordinates. Grep context near it shows 'Standing' and '3-Story Cab' lines, but we could not confirm those belong to this entry, and we did not read its register page. This conflicts with the removal reported elsewhere and needs a human check. The 1988 loss rests on the Forest Lookouts and San Diego chapter pages; no source gives current site access or remains, and the register's site video links were not viewed. No WebSearch was available in this run. Fetch budget for this lookout was used up.

Brief status gone is confirmed by the index. Build year conflicts: work under way in September 1929 (Lompoc Review), 1930 (Carey citing Brown), 1931 (some sources). Design rests on an unnamed reader comment on Carey's post, not on a primary record. Fate is unconfirmed: Carey and a 2019 blog both point to the 1948 Wheeler fire without confirming it. Access set to permission because the route crosses private gated land; the story gives no directions. Staffing covers only 1932 (Kennison). No corrections proposed.

Built year conflicts (1934 register and Carey vs 1935 Peakbagging). Removal date is unknown in all sources read. No source read says whether the site is open to the public now, so access is omitted rather than guessed; the brief's 'unknown' stays. Carey's 2013 post describes a visit made about the winter of 2011-12, not a 2013 visit. Photos on firetower.org ('Location of removed tower', Carey) were not downloaded. The register's 'Santa Ynez Lookout' photo caption and the blog comment about a lookout named Gus Grimm (1965) were not used, since comments are not sourced evidence.

Read: the FFLOS detail page (firetower.org), the FFLA-SDRC page, the weebly page (newspaper excerpts 1912-1930, read through targeted grep windows; the page is long and only part of it was seen), Wikipedia (excerpt), and the firelookout.org California list (the Santiago line was not readable; the grep window was cut). The brief's 'fflos=gone' is not supported by the FFLOS detail page, which says the tower and catwalk still stand; the firelookout.org list line should be checked. The CCC 1935 removal is unclear against the 1930 75-ft tower reference. Access is set to restricted from the communications-site description; no public-access rule was found. The 1964 relay-building tower may not be the 1951 tower; the sources do not say. No photos were added. No source found detailing what fires Sardine Peak watched for or who staffed it historically beyond the current unstaffed status. Height_m in the brief (2479.5, an elevation not structure height) was left unchanged since no source gave a differing figure (nhlr.org lists elevation as 8,135 ft / 2,480 m).

Build year conflicts: 1928 (1934 report) vs under construction March 1929 (The Signal); the event uses 1929. Elevation conflicts: The Signal gives 5,390 ft, Angeles Adventures 5517 ft; elevation not used in the story. Angeles Adventures calls it a Forest Service lookout; the story uses the county department named in the 1929 report. Tejon relocation is disputed: the county's 1936-37 report describes a Tejon tower erected in December 1936, and a Tejon site record dates piers to 1936; the story says it is unclear whether the Sawmill tower went there. Access rated public from a hiking site, not checked on the ground. Brief height 9.1 m and status gone are consistent with sources; no corrections proposed.

Administration conflict: the register says Cal Fire administers the site; the Forest Service project page says the site is administered by Plumas National Forest and sits in the proclaimed Lassen National Forest. The record's agency is Cal Fire and its ownership is 'federal'; neither was changed. Build date and timeline: the 1937 obituary has Dave Reese at the peak for six years and in Forest Service employ nine years before 1937, which would predate the register's 1931 date. Either an earlier structure stood there or a date is off; unresolved. Cab history: the original wood cab was destroyed by fire, but no year is given, and the replacement cab is undated. Current status: the register has no status field. Its description, marked MVT 10/91, refers to the existing cab, and the Forest Service project summary uses the present tense for the lookout. Nothing dated after 2019 confirms the lookout is standing today, so status 'standing' rests on those two sources. The Butte County Battalion 1 page returned HTTP 403 to both our fetch and WebFetch, so current staffing and camera coverage are unconfirmed. A search summary said staffing has ended and two ALERTCalifornia cameras cover the site; not verified, not used. Register number: a California lookout directory row seemed to show NHLR US 1358, CA 181; the register page says US 1310, CA 133, and the register's own number is used. A 1967 item about a seismograph theft names 'Saw Mill Peak Lookout Station in Shasta County'; it is a different county and is not used. Access: no source read says whether the public may visit. No new photos added.

A search result (not a fetched page) mentioned a closure after winter wind damage and a later reopening of the road and trail. I could not verify it in a fetched page, so the story omits it. Check Lava Beds alerts before publishing. The kind correction is a judgement call based on the nomination's wording. The staffing as_of date is the NPS page's last-updated date, not a staffing confirmation.

Dates disagree: the register gives 1940 (CCC erected the L-601 tower); the North Coast Journal says constructed 1941; the 1942 survey says the lookout was being completed when a 1941 station was occupied. Not resolved. The register's 1976 build date is unexplained; no source read says what happened in 1976. The 1942 'wooden structure' and the register's 'L-601 tower' are reconciled only loosely by the 2020 account of modifications. Current status and access: the register calls it an interpretive site for park visitors, and the 2020 account describes a staffed season, but no source read gives current hours or says whether the cab is open. A search summary described a later trip report calling the lookout closed and gated, and another search summary said the land is Yurok Tribal land; neither was read in a page we could quote, so both are left out and should be checked before publication. The 1965 item is a burglary report, included for history only. No new photos added; the record's register photos are credited to Ron Kemnow, Mark Swift and Fred Johnson, all marked 'All rights reserved'.

Staffing, fire history and public access were not found in any source read; the access level is left out of facts for that reason. The record's line that FFLA began coordinating with the forest is only partly supported: the FFLA report describes SHPO coordination and an interest in an MOU with the FFLA. The record's 'FFLA began coordinating' wording may be worth tightening. The FFLA report's year is taken from its filename (2025) and its text says only 'this summer'. The design text keeps the Register's wording '10 foot enclosed timber tower', which may describe the cab rather than total height, so no height_m is given. A Klamath NF Facebook post mentions ALERTCalifornia cameras at the historic lookout; the post was not readable, so it is not used. The Register's photos (credited to the Nancy Hood Collection and the Siskiyou County Historical Society) have no URLs captured, so no photos are added.

Thin record. The index gives only type, county, coordinates and status; the Forest Lookouts page has no text beyond its title. The index types it AWS, so it may not be a fire lookout; the editor should decide whether it belongs in this set. Elevation is from Mapcarta. A peak datasheet snippet gives 1,219 ft, but that page returned 403 and was not read. The story uses no staffing, build or fate claims because no source gives them.

Status: the Forest Lookouts page labels it Removed with no date or source; both FFLA lists say Standing, Ground type, no register. The 1971 item is a warning about budget cuts, not a closure. An earlier note that the statewide list showed an enclosed tower with NHLR US 1382, CA 205 was wrong: that number belongs to Scott Bar Mountain (Siskiyou). One web search found nothing about a removal or this lookout. No staffing after 1956 found. No photos. Do not encourage climbing.

The brief's Boucher Hill duplicate claim and 2017 refurbishment both come from cr-ca-sierra-2018.pdf, which returned only 5 characters of text, so they are unverified and left out of events; the Boucher Hill claim does not appear in any page read. Not checked on the ground. Spelling varies: Shaffer, Schaffer (the 1940 item says Schaffer Peak). Elevation differs: Peakbagging lists 6739 ft, a blog post says 6375 ft; elevation is not used. Landon Lookout near Eagle Lake may be the Greens Peak lookout (us-ca-don-landon-greens-peak); not confirmed.

Only the register describes the site today, and that line is undated. No source read says whether the site is open to the public or how to reach it, so no access key is set; a Mendocino National Forest check would settle it. The height_m of 21.3 is the 70-foot tower converted to metres, taken as the structure height. The 1941 water-system item is quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not read on the original newspaper. Leads not used: a UC Berkeley Library photo record for 'Lookout tower. Sheetiron Moutain, Lake County' (digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu/record/17033), which gave no date or text we could read, and a 2017 Mendocino NF social-media post with an unverified reader comment about a later use of the lookout; neither is cited. No source after the 2008 blog describes the site, and none says whether the public may visit. The brief's height_m of 213.4 matches the 700-foot plunge figure in the 1962 report, so it is proposed for correction. FFLOS credits a USFS/Siskiyou County Museum photo, but no image URL was found, so no photo entry was added.

Not checked on the ground. Trail length differs: Wilderness Portal gives 5.2 miles round trip with close to 1,000 ft of gain (used in the story); SummitPost gives 5 miles round trip and about 700 ft. The brief's agency field was generic; see corrections.

Current access and visitor status were not found in any source read, so no access level is given. The 2008 FFLA report's trailer date (1973) and the Register's 1960s date are both kept. The 'moved to Oregon' claim in the record's 2007 event is not in any page read and is proposed for removal. The Register's photos (credited to Ron Kemnow and Fred Johnson) have no URLs captured, so no photos are added. The 1914 staffing entry relies on a single 1914 newspaper item as quoted by Forest Lookouts, not on the newspaper itself.

Thin record: two 1943 and 1947 newspaper items on one page, the FFLA list, and a Peakbagging row. No build date, removal date or current-site description found; the story leaves those out. A Facebook group post (not cited) says the lookout was built to a 1934 C3-type design per a California lookout report; that claim is unverified and not used. The Peakbagging row lacks the (LO site) label that other removed lookouts carry, so its status there is unclear. The NHLR and FFLOS pages were not reached. Not checked on the ground.

Record kind two_story is not confirmed by these sources; they describe a 14 by 14 foot steel cab on a 10 by 10 foot concrete block base. Staffing as_of uses Wilderness Portal's 2026-06-19 verification date. Fire-lookouts.org's access and staffing details are reported alongside Wilderness Portal's rather than overriding them. No specific fire at the tower is named in the sources read. No photos added: the NHLR photo captions have no image URLs in the pages read.

Record access 'unknown' can now read 'permission' (NHLR and Monterey County Now agree). The source_pages entry for a 2017 NYT article returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The OpenStreetMap way only tags the tower as an observation tower, so it is not cited.
