The Rex's Fire Lookout Page that the register cites was not located. The brief's gone status, Boundary County and Kaniksu agency all check out. Verified 2026-10-10: story wording changed from regional to Idaho register; cite 2 year quotes added for 1935 and 1955.

Two pages plus the FFLA list; both pages agree on 1938 and 1958. The 1939 footing date is a disagreement the story reports as is. The two CCC-era names are left out on purpose: they are private individuals whom the source could not identify. Access is not stated (the page says hike-in); no access level is recorded. The existing photo on the record is from idahofirelookouts.com and is not new. A second search for Bussel timed out and returned nothing.

Camp, cabin, tower and destruction years agree across firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Unresolved: the 1931 death. The Idaho page dates it 6/17/31; newspaper reprints (dated June 23 and 24, 1931) say a Sunday evening. The victim's first name (James, Ben, Glen) and age (about 19 or 23) differ between reprints; the story says so. Idaho Fire Lookouts is unsure whether the Butler Mountain footings belong to the 1936 tower. Coordinates need a human check: the brief's record uses 48.13047, -116.52547 (idaho_fl), while the firelookout.org list and firelookout.com give 48.11893, -116.51886. No access or photo licence information found. Not a death to be sensationalised: the story keeps it to the sources. Verified 2026-10-10: the mine sentence now says located to match the quote.

NHLR lists the tower as available for rental despite the extremely difficult approach (boat + 6-mile/5000ft hike); worth confirming current rental arrangements with the Salmon-Challis National Forest before publishing that as an active booking option. Build year (1933 vs 1934) unresolved across sources.

Only two lookout pages and the FFLA list; the 1935 cab and 1954 destruction both appear on the two lookout pages (Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com); no independent corroboration beyond those pages was found. Searches did not find a Mulligan Hump lookout elsewhere. Unverified lead, not used in the story: a search summary described a UIdaho aerial photo captioned 'Buzzard Roost lookout', St. Joe NF, dated 1961; the link I tried returned 404 and I could not open the item, so it may conflict with the 1954 date and should be checked. A Clearwater NF list (https://www.fs.usda.gov/media/259185) has a Mulligan Hump cabin (1930s, ruins, 3930 ft, Sec13 T42N R6E), probably a different peak; not linked. The elevation (4871 ft) is in the source but not recorded in facts. Drive-up is the Idaho FL label and describes road access only.

Thin record: short listings only, with no year for the crow's nest's abandonment and no staffing, access or photo found. The county list's 'Calusa Point' may be this lookout; not merged and not confirmed. Two web searches found nothing new. The status correction (gone to abandoned) is for human review.

Two lookout histories agree on the 1931 camp, 1934 tower and 1962 loss, and on the Kaniksu agency. The Idaho register says Removed with no year. Staff entries come from photo captions and give no dates of tenure beyond the year shown. Elevation 5850 ft per firelookout.com; a search snippet gave about 5,859 ft, which was not read and is not used. No present-day site description or access information found. The brief's gone status and Boundary County check out. Verified 2026-10-10: staff years now described as photo captions, not tenure.

Four pages agree on the 1932 crow's nest, the west-butte patrol point and the 1947 abandonment. Today's account rests on one undated personal hiking page (WillhiteWeb), which is the only source for the trails and the towers; no agency statement on access was found. The same page says the route crosses city land and an LLC-labelled area, so check land status before any visit advice. The Idaho FFLA state list (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/id) has no Canfield Butte entry. The record's 47.7314, -116.73172 point was not checked against a map. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says no staffing history is documented, so no staffing facts are given. In the verification pass the access level was set back to 'unknown' from 'public': the hiker's account gives driving directions and calls the trails popular, but does not say who may enter, and no agency statement was found. The first sentence of the story now carries footnote 1, and two sentences were reworded so they no longer copy a source's wording. The editor should check land status before any visit advice.

Thin record. The 1936 date and the L-4 design appear on two pages (firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com); the sources do not show whether these are independent, so treat them as one report until checked. The staff list (1934 to 1950) is 'known' personnel, not a full roster. The 1934 Howard Green item is cited on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page to a Bonners Ferry Herald item that was not read. No source describes the site today, and none gives an access statement; the only access note is the 'Hike-In' tag. The FFLA list gives the same point as the record (48.99719, -116.64592). The record has no events; 1936 is added as built, which the editor may want to check. Verification pass: the 1936 entry, the Howard Green item (dated 06/07/1934 on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page) and the 'Removed' status on the Forest Lookouts page were confirmed in context. A footnote was added to the first sentence. No facts changed.

Two coordinate sets disagree by about 1.9 km: the FFLA list gives 47.99567, -116.52182 (used in the record) and the idaho_fl source gives 47.99153, -116.49637. None of the pages read here gives coordinates in its text, so the point is unresolved; a map check is needed before the pin is trusted. No source read describes the site today. A search snippet from hikearizona.com mentions remnants at the summit, but the page returned HTTP 403 to our reader, so this is unverified and worth a human look. AllTrails also returned 403. Do not merge with us-id-cape-horn-peak-2 (Custer/Valley, Challis National Forest), which is a different lookout with the same name. No staffing record was found; Idaho Fire Lookouts says none is documented. Verification pass: the 1930 crow's nest, the 1935 30-ft L-4 tower and the 1952 destruction were confirmed on the firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts and Idaho Fire Lookouts pages. The FFLA list says 'Tower Gone', not 'destroyed', so it now supports only the gone sentence, which carries footnote 4. A footnote was added to the first sentence. No facts changed.

Record facts checked and not changed (story wording and evidence quotes were tightened 2026-10-10): name, county (Shoshone), kind (tower), gone status and coordinates (FFLA list) agree with the sources read. The Idaho Fire Lookouts category listing gives an address of Dago Peak, which is not used here. Jay Murray (1937) appears only on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page. The 2024 post is the latest description found; no visit report after it. No photographs found.

Height and elevation figures differ slightly between NHLR/idahofirelookouts (7,667-7,681 ft; 72 ft tower) and Wikipedia/NRHP nomination (85 ft ground-to-cab). Did not independently pull the NRHP PDF itself (John F. Elliott, 1992) for primary confirmation; Wikipedia's summary of it was used instead.

Record kind 'ground' matches the FFLA 'Ground' label and the cupola cabin. Elevation 6,210 ft is from Idaho Fire Lookouts; elevation is not a facts key so it is only in the story. No new photos: the image URLs on these pages are not in the text we read. Forest Lookouts quotes the 1927 report as the 'Caribou Peak lookout' and places the cabin in NW 1/4 of section 30, T59N R2W; not used. The 'staffing as_of 1952' date is the abandonment year, not an end-of-staffing date from a source.

Destruction in 1971 and the 1933 build date agree across all three lookout sites. Elevation 4,592 ft (two sites) is only in the story because it is not a facts key. The 'Pend Oreille TPA' label appears on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; it is recorded as agency as the source names it, and it may be a timber protective association rather than a land agency. No source describes the site today. The existing record photo is credited to Idaho Fire Lookouts; no new photos were found.

Thin record: a 1933 cabin entry, a 1934 name, and an abandonment tag with no date. The 1934 name is cited second-hand through Idaho Fire Lookouts; the Bonners Ferry Herald itself was not read. Idaho Fire Lookouts spells the forest 'Kanisku'; the correct spelling is used. Forest Lookouts gives the legal location as 61N-1W-9; the story spells it out as township 61 north, range 1 west, section 9. No photos found.

1936 and 1947 agree across the pages; the Kemnow list marks both with c. (circa). Record elevation_m is null; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 4,098 ft (about 1,249 m), added as a note, not a correction. Access level left unset: the page says drive-up but not whether the ground is open. No staffing, fire or site-condition sources found.

Height disputed: 30-foot pole on firelookout.com and the Idaho site, 20-foot on the county list; the story reports both. No staffing, access or new photos found. Record location (47.05742, -115.1768) is the FFLA list point and was not checked against a map.

The tower record's 'conflicts' entry lists firelookout_com as giving a built year of 1928, but that page's actual text matches nhlr exactly (1916/1928/1950 sequence) — likely a mis-extraction when the record was built. Recommend the conflict be cleared rather than left open; no new correction filed since the record's 'built: 1950' field is already right. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed a sentence claiming secondary listings 'collapse' the three build dates and citing recreation.gov for the full 1916/1928/1950 sequence — no evidence quote supported that framing (recreation.gov's page does independently state the same three dates, confirmed by spot-check, but the sentence as written made an unsupported claim about other listings). Also rewrote the 1950-cab sentence, which copied the nhlr.org description almost verbatim.

Cabin vs camp is unresolved: firelookout.com and the Kemnow list say cabin; Idaho Fire Lookouts says camp. Only the 1940s decade is given, so no dated events were written. Record kind 'ground' matches the FFLA listing. Elevation 3,950 ft is in the story only, since facts has no elevation key. No site description, staffing or fire sources found; a 2026 'Castleford Butte' fire map was not used because nothing ties it to this site.

Unresolved location conflict: the record uses the FFLA list point (47.9521, -116.10983); the record's idaho_fl source gives 47.9441, -116.1418. Elevation disputed (4,090 ft on firelookout.com, 4,291 ft on the Idaho site); the story gives both. The 'cement footings remain' line on the Idaho Coeur d'Alene category page belongs to Divide Peak, not Cathedral, so it is not used. No staffing, access or new photos found.

Three independent listings agree on 1931 and 1960. The Clearwater list is a table, so its quotes are short fragments. Record design and height_m were null; the 30-foot figure is added from the sources, not a correction. No staffing, fire or site-condition sources found.

Kootenai County, Coeur d'Alene NF, the crow's nest c.1929, the 20-foot L-4 tower c.1934 and the 1959 destruction agree across three pages. The Forest Lookouts page attributes its dates to Kresek, and the other two appear to draw on the same older record, so this is one underlying source rather than three independent ones. Brief coordinates 47.88222, -116.6381 match the firelookout.org list (Cedar Mountain, Kootenai, Tower Gone), which we read as the index page at https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/id; that page is not cited in the story. Do not confuse this site with us-id-cedar-mountain-2, the St. Joe National Forest peak in Shoshone County (47.33006, -115.83358). The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1940 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description for the tower, which may help place the site but was not checked on the ground. The sources give no date for any 'Removed' event, and none describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to the public, so the access object is omitted from facts. The brief's events list had only 1959 destroyed; the 1929 and 1934 builds and the 1950 radio item are added.

The 1915 cabin, the 1930s 30-foot tower and the 1922 injury agree across the sources that describe them. No source dates the removal, so the status is removed with no year. The register's foundation and remains are the only description of the site as it is now, and the willhite hiking write-up is undated and personal. The brief's conflict on coordinates (register 47.330102, -115.833571 against a 47.3502, -115.84238 Idaho record) was not checked: the Idaho Fire Lookouts page we read gives no coordinates. Do not conflate this site with a Potlatch Lumber photo titled Cedar Mountain Lookout tower (University of Idaho, plcphotos65, dated 1917, Bonner County at 47.0138, -116.5787), which is a different peak. The Idaho Fire Lookouts Cedar Mountain page under the Coeur d'Alene region (1929 crow's nest, 1934 20-foot tower, destroyed 1959) also appears to be a different peak. The Clearwater Forest list does not include this site.

Four thin pages, with no independent corroboration of dates. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says it has no documented staffing history for this lookout; staffing is left out of the story and facts. The Forest Lookouts page gives only the county, the Kaniksu National Forest and the code 64N-5W-12. Elevation is 5,295 feet on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts, but the facts schema has no elevation key, so it appears only in the story. Coordinates 48.90755, -116.929 match the firelookout.org list. The brief's kind 'platform' is not contradicted, but the sources call it a crow's nest. Search turned up a second Idaho Fire Lookouts URL (north-idaho-panhandle-region/cedar-ridge) that was not read; it probably repeats the same page. A 2011 Boundary County lookouts article (naturallynorthidaho.com) was checked and does not name Cedar Ridge. Do not confuse with Cedar Knob (Idaho County) or Cedar Mountain (Kootenai).

The three pages agree on the 1928 camp, the 1930 10-foot L-4 tower, the Cameron Hill patrol point, the 5,591-foot elevation and the 1964 destruction. Weebly's dates are attributed to Kresek and firelookout.com's to the same record, so these may not be independent. The name story, the 1936 Halm quote and the 1953 Boy Scout item come only from the Forest Lookouts page, which reprints 1936 and 1953 newspaper items; they were not checked against the newspapers. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history and shows an undated photo from the Bert Russel Collection; the photo has no image URL in our read, so no photo record is added. A web search found no account of what remains on the summit. The brief's 'gone' status is consistent with 'Destroyed 1964'. Do not confuse with us-or-cemetery-ridge, the Oregon site.

Three lookout pages agree on the 1952 destruction and the c.1934 log cabin, but Forest Lookouts attributes both dates to Kresek, so they may share one origin. The climbing guide says the lookout was soon abandoned but gives no date; the story flags this disagreement and keeps the 1952 date. The 1922 photo is a single source for the shelter and Fred Gardner; it is the only named lookout found. Its rights statement was not read, so it is not added to photos; check the item page for a licence. A search snippet warned that a 1952 University of Idaho photo is of Root Knob Lookout, not this site; that record was not read and is not cited. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history. No record corrections proposed; the record's 1952 event matches all three pages.
Consider updating the record's 'built' field or adding a note that 1980 is the current tower's build year, with the site's lookout history going back to 1931.

Two record coordinates disagree (ffla 46.7025, -116.3937 vs idaho_fl 46.71295, -116.3851), and Idaho Fire Lookouts says the exact location is unknown, so the record's point is unconfirmed. Proposed correction is precision only; no coordinate is proposed. Sources say abandoned in the 1940s; the record's 1940 is approximate. Only Forest Lookouts gives the full agency name; the other two give CTPA. The Forest Lookouts date is attributed to Kresek, and the 1934 crow's nest is the only design described. One WebSearch found nothing on this lookout. Access, condition and staffing are unknown and omitted from facts.

Location: the record point (47.60944, -116.05861) matches the Idaho site pin for the nest. firelookout.com and the Forest Association index give a camp point at 47.62906, -116.05026, about 2.3 km away; not changed. Kind is 'unknown'; a tree-built nest may fit 'tree', editor's call. No staffing record. Kresek's book was not read directly; its 2010 claim is second-hand via the Idaho site.

The three pages agree on the 1940 build and 1955 abandonment; Forest Lookouts attributes its dates to Kresek, so they may share one origin. The record's height_m 9.1 matches the 30-foot figure on Forest Lookouts (30 ft is about 9.14 m). The record kind 'tower' is kept; the sources call it a pole platform. The record status 'gone' understates the cabin ruins firelookout.com says remain; consider a status that reflects ruins if the schema allows it. The one WebSearch returned mostly Castle Butte, a different lookout on the Nez Perce-Clearwater, and was not used. Idaho Fire Lookouts photos are credited to the Fire Lookout Museum and Luke Channer with no licence stated; no new photos added. The record's existing photo is from idahofirelookouts.com.

The 1931 build and the ruins-from-1961 date agree across four sources. The 1943 smokechaser names come from one Idaho Fire Lookouts page and are not confirmed elsewhere. The brief's kind 'ground' is proposed as 'tower' in corrections; check the vocabulary. The Forest Service list places the site at Sec 31 T39N R8E, which matches the brief's township. No source describes what stands on the rock today. Idaho lists it as hike-in ruins only. Two Facebook leads (6C Idaho History, 1954 Chateau Rock lookout photo exhibit, and a Kelly Frazier post dated November 10, 2021) were found, but only their titles were readable, so no photos were added. Access is recorded as public with a caution about the rock scramble, not as an invitation to climb.

Thin record: no builder, purpose, staff, fire history or abandonment year in any source read. The three cabin listings agree on 1915. The brief's kind 'ground' matches the FFLA type column. Coordinates come from the FFLA index row (46.99960, -115.73880). No photo found. No source describes what remains or whether the site is public; the story says so. Elevation is unrecorded on both lookout pages, so none is given.

Build year is 1930 in four sources and 1933 on firelookout.com, which may be a copy of the Burton Peak cabin's date (also 14x14 and 1933); this is not confirmed. Elevation differs: 8,608 ft in the register, 8657 feet on the two other sites. No staffing names were found; Idaho Fire Lookouts says none are documented. The 2021 Dixie Jumbo Fire material is in Keeping Watch's collection; no source read says the fire reached the cabin, so the story does not say so. The hike-in is inside the wilderness and no trail distance was found; check with the Payette National Forest before publishing visit advice. Keeping Watch pages carry images with no direct image URLs, so no photo entries were added.

Build year: 1939 in four sources (firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, climbing guide, and the 1940 USGS note supporting a tower by then); the 1996 Spokesman-Review guide gives 1948 for the cabin and tower and says it was dismantled in late 1950s. Unresolved; the story says so. Location: the record point (47.89165, -116.5299) and idaho_fl (47.91717, -116.53062) are about 2.8 km apart; the sources here do not settle it. Height 12.2 m is from the 40-foot pole height; the sources do not give the cab height. No staffing history found in these sources, so none is recorded. Access is public hike-in per the climbing guide; the trail was not checked against 2026 Forest Service status. No new photos; the existing idahofirelookouts photo in the record still applies.

The 1915 build and 1939 abandonment appear on all four pages, but they trace to firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts page and a 1996 newspaper hike guide; no Forest Service record was found. The 1929 staffer comes from a book named by Idaho Fire Lookouts and was not checked. The 1922 ranger item names Chilco but not the peak, so it is an 'other' event and not a staffing fact for this summit. The 1996 guide gives 1948 for the North Chilco tower, which conflicts with 1939 in the North record. No source describes what remains today; the 1996 guide describes only a former site. The record kind 'ground' is not stated in any fetched source. Location: record (47.86641, -116.55427) and idaho_fl (47.87129, -116.54964) are about 640 m apart; not resolved here.

Build year: 1933 in three sources (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, climbing guide) and 1934 for an R-1 cabin on the Forest Lookouts page, which also gives 1935 as the first staffed season; no source reconciles 1933 and 1934. The cause of the 1969 destruction is not given anywhere. Boise National Forest comes only from firelookout.com. Foundations rest on one 2016 climb report quoted by the climbing guide. The R-1 design is from the Forest Lookouts page alone; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say ground cabin. Access is public hike-in in wilderness per the sources; wilderness rules and current trail status were not checked for 2026.

The brief's height_m 3.7 is not supported by any of the five sources read, so it is left out of facts; check before publishing. The 2003 fate is disputed (destroyed vs removed) and no source gives detail. Access 'public' rests on the climbing guide's road description and Wikipedia's road/bike trail line; no closure notice was found. Staffing dates from newspapers quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, which the staff lists omit. A 2020 wildfire on the peak appeared in search results (eastidahonews.com); it was not read or used because nothing ties it to the lookout. No new photos were found. Search budget: one WebSearch.

Location conflict not resolved: idaho_fl gives 48.02738, -116.7817 and firelookout.com and the FFLA list give 48.02515, -116.76994, roughly 0.9 km apart. No source checked says which is the site. The 1940s destruction has no exact year; a 1940 'destroyed' placeholder event was removed because a dated 1940 loss would contradict the July 1949 staffing. The 1936 tower may or may not replace the 1926 platform. The 20-foot figure is taken as height_m; it is the tower height as stated. Pend Oreille TPA is a label on firelookout.com and is not expanded here. Nothing about fires or access was found.

Current condition rests on a 2003 register visit and a 2016 Forest Service list. No newer visit report was found, so check the site before any public claim about its state today. The 1920s cupola has no exact year. The Jimmy Clarke death comes from a hobbyist site citing a book and is included with attribution only.

The 1936 build and 1962 destruction dates match across all three lookout listings. The firelookout.com page gives elevation 3500 ft; height 30 ft converted to 9.1 m. No staff, fire history or cause of destruction in any source read, so none is stated. Photo credit noted but no image URL was found, so no photo entry. The willhiteweb.com Grassy Mountain page describes a 1936 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab destroyed 1962 (or late 1950s); it was not used for this record, but check that the two are not confused.

Dates and township match across firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts county list, and the USFS Nez Perce list (compiled April 2010 from Kresek). Location conflict in our record: the FFLA index gives 45.98085, -115.73092 (verified in this run); the brief lists 45.98818, -115.72873 from Idaho Fire Lookouts, which the page text I read did not show, so it is unverified. The story gives no coordinates. Our record's county 'Idaho' is 'Idaho County' in the sources. No photo, staff or fire history found.

Thinnest of the three. Two site pages, a county list and the FFLA list all agree on 1935 and 1953 and on the L-4 cab. No staffing, fire or present-day site evidence was found, so the story is short on purpose. The brief's county (Shoshone) is confirmed by the FFLA list. No Idaho register (NHLR or FFLOS) entry for this site was in the cache.

Original-site description rests on the 1996 HABS report; no source describes the site after 1996 apart from the NHLR cabin fire in 2000. The NHLR gives Borlaug's Nobel year as 1974; the story does not repeat the year. Outside the sources read, the Nobel Peace Prize he won was in 1970, so the NHLR year looks wrong and should be checked before any year is added. The moved-tower record us-id-cold-mountain-at-payette-lake-holm covers the same tower, so this story leads with the original site and carries the move.

Build year conflict: HABS gives privy 1934, tower 1935, cabin 1936-37; NHLR gives 1935; Idaho Fire Lookouts and Keeping Watch give 1934. The story says so. Restoration vs acquisition: NHLR says a private party restored the top 20 feet in 2007; Keeping Watch says removed and acquired by a private party in 2008. Both are reported, not reconciled. Borlaug's Nobel year: NHLR says 1974. From memory, his Nobel Peace Prize was 1970. That is not supported by a fetched source here, so the story omits the year. A human should check the register's wording before it is reused. The HABS report is dated April 1996 (its cabin-extant finding predates NHLR's 2000 burn date; not a true conflict). Record 'ownership' is 'unknown'; NHLR names Richard Holm, Jr. as owner, which could be a correction, but it is a gap rather than an error, so not proposed. The record's coordinates and elevation (1556 m) are for the current Payette Lake site, not the original Cold Mountain site (about 8,084 ft per HABS). A separate record us-id-cold-mountain exists for the original site, which FFLA lists as Gone; the two may need linking. Access level 'private' comes from NHLR owner and Keeping Watch's 'home of a private party'. No photos added; NHLR photo in the record is all rights reserved.

The 40-foot figure is converted to 12.2 m; the sources do not say whether it is overall height or to the cab floor. The 'still there' note on firelookout.com is undated, so the cabin's current state rests on that page plus the rental listing on idahofirelookouts.com. The Forest Service camping and cabins page checked does not list this cabin, so the rental booking route is unconfirmed. Record status 'gone' describes the tower, not the surviving cabin; the editor may want a status that covers a standing cabin. The access level 'restricted' is our reading of a rental program. No staffing or fire history found.

Three sources agree on 1930, 1958 and the 1979 removal. The FFLA Facebook post on this site was seen only as a search snippet and could not be read; that snippet says the cabin was also torn down in 1979, which conflicts with firelookout.com's header (1930-1958 for the cabin era). Not used. A geocache listing (GC6MB2D) mentions remains in a search snippet; the page would not load, so it is not used. Do not confuse this with the separate Cold Spring lookout in the St. Joe-Clearwater region on idahofirelookouts.com (46.786, -115.304), which is a different site.

The record's L-4 design and 6.1 m height match the 20-foot L-4 tower on firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page. No source names a builder or any staff. The record photo links to idahofirelookouts.com; its 1946 date comes from the file name, not the page, so please check it. Firelookout.com says 'gone' and Idaho Fire Lookouts says 'destroyed or removed'; no source says which. No site description found.

Dates for the build (about 1933) and the 1963 loss agree across three sources, apart from the 1965 in the firelookout.com header. The Idaho page's Selway label is a regional grouping; the agency (Nez Perce National Forest) comes from firelookout.com and the Forest Service list. No present-day site description was found in these sources. The record had no events, so the 1933 and 1963 events are new.

The cupola date (1924 vs 1931) and tower height (50 vs 53 ft) conflict across sources. The brief's 1924 built event refers to the cupola and is corrected to 1955 for the standing tower. Restoration status is unverified since the 2020 reporting. Check on site before any public claim that restoration is under way.

Thin record: four sources, all agreeing the tower is gone with no removal date. No source describes the site today, so no remains or public-access facts are set; access stays unknown. The 1938 date is 'about 1938' on firelookout.com and '1938' on Idaho Fire Lookouts; the story keeps 'about'. No new photos found; the existing idahofirelookouts.com photo in the record is unchanged. The record coordinates are the FFLA point and were not checked against a map.

History is consistent across four sources: platform 1917, 25 ft 1919, L-4 cab 1941, abandoned 1963. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is public, so access and remains are not set. Kind correction is a proposal for the editor to confirm (tree vs tower). Elevation 6,534 ft is in the story, not a facts key. No new photos found.

Location conflict not resolved here: FFLA gives 48.70696, -116.5349 and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 48.70854, -116.55715 (about 1.6 km apart). The record keeps the FFLA point. The NaughtyHiker write-up is undated on the page and its comments run to August 2017, so the footings claim may be out of date. Staffing as_of 1961 is the last named staff member, not an abandonment date. No new photos found.

NHLR's own description is internally a little inconsistent (mentions a 1936 gable-roof L-4 being moved in 1953 after earlier saying the log cabin replaced the frame cabin in 1931, without saying when the L-4 itself was built relative to the log cabin). idahofirelookouts.com's staff list is informal/crowd-sourced (note the comment thread correcting the Anderson staffing dates) but is the richest source for named observers.

Built and destroyed years agree across all four lookout pages and lists; the Forest Service PDF text is scrambled in extraction, so its Cooperation row was read by hand. The link to the Lolo Forest rests on a place-name note that calls the peak Cooperation Mountain: probably this site, not proven. The record's coordinates (46.42684, -114.8209) were not checked against Sec 27 T36N R13E, 8 miles SW of Powell RS; a person should check the pin. No staffing or fire history was found in the sources, so none is written.

Status is unresolved: the statewide index says Tower Standing, while two detailed pages say abandoned in the 1940s and do not confirm the pole remains. The abandonment is dated only to the decade, so no event was entered. No staffing history or fire found. Neither detailed page gives a visit date. The Idaho Panhandle roll-call PDF (ppolinks.com/forestservicemuseum/2022_1_11.pdf) lists Smith Creek district as Copeland in 1927; not cited, worth checking if the station's name history matters.

Thin record: four short pages, consistent with each other. The Weebly page only lists the site under Kaniksu National Forest with a link to another lookout page, which was not read. A guessed NHLR URL returned 404, so no NHLR entry was found. The staff names are quoted in evidence only and are left out of the story. The removal year is not in any source, so the event list does not record one. The record's access 'unknown' is set to public by inference from the hike-in note.

Four pages with a clear build sequence, but they disagree on the steel tower year (1940 vs 1942), and firelookout.com's R.I.P. span does not match its own later entries. The record's height_m 12.2 (40 ft) matches the 1923 pole tower, not the later 50-foot steel tower (about 15.2 m), so it was left as is. The design correction is in corrections. Staffing is one named lookout (1944), and the name is not used in the story. The story says footings remain at the summit only as Willhite describes them. The access 'public' level is inferred. The index lists the Boundary and Kootenai Copper Mountains separately, which the story notes so readers do not confuse them.

Current record's 1953 build year is confirmed as the current-structure date; the 1929 first-tower date is additional context not currently in the brief. No photos found beyond those already credited to the Fire Lookout Museum on existing source pages (not newly sourced here, so omitted from photos).

Thin and not independent: the design, 1934 date and 1974 gone date come from the two lookout pages (same site family) and the county list; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list only confirms gone. Two web searches found no other record of this tower. Caution: a firelookout.com page for Arctic Point (Payette NF, Big Creek) uses nearly the same wording (72' steel tower with a log cabin, built 1934), so the Cottontail design line may have been copied from it. Check against a Payette NF source before publishing. Record coordinates (45.3822, -115.74643) were not checked against 9 miles NNW of Warren or T24N R6E, 32. The record has no events; the 1934 and 1974 events are added from these pages.

All four sources are lookout-site lists; the two Idaho pages and the county list agree on 1929 and 1965, but they are not independent of each other and no primary record was found. Two web searches did not confirm the site. Confusion risk: Cottonwood Butte is a different lookout, and its Idaho Fire Lookouts page (Payette/Salmon NF, 9349 ft) also gives a 1920s log cabin and 1965 destroyed; the 1965 date should not be carried over without a source for this site. Record kind 'ground' fits the FFLA 'Ground Gone' entry. The coordinates (45.91852, -116.6617) fit '24 miles west of Grangeville', but were not checked against 30N-3W-23. The 'Private' access level is from the listings only; no visit rules were found.

Four pages with a consistent 1952 build and 1989 staffing. Two issues to note. First, the end of the lookout: firelookout.com says gone and Idaho Fire Lookouts says destroyed, so the story avoids naming a cause. Second, the 1955 Air Force installation: the Weebly page quotes a newspaper saying construction would begin in August, and Willhite says it was put in that year. The Weebly page also carries a bare 'Removed' tag with no context, so it is not used as evidence. The Lewiston Morning Tribune article about the lookout being unstaffed returned 403 and was not read, so nothing from it is used. A search snippet about the lookout being unmanned after 31 years is unverified and is left out. The record's county 'Idaho' is Idaho County. No record field was in error.

Dates conflict. firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 1965 and may not be independent. Bing Young (1982, via the climbing guide) doubts the cabin lasted long after the 1935 map. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Don Clark for 1987-1989, which is after its own 1965 date. WillhiteWeb says the Idaho County Cottonwood Butte was still staffed in 1989, so that entry may be a mix-up; not confirmed. Do not merge with the Idaho County Cottonwood Butte near Craigmont (1952 cabin, gone by 1994). A search snippet also mentions a 1965 radar station dismantling on a Cottonwood Butte (St Gertrude's Museum Facebook post, not fetched); it appears to concern the Idaho County peak. Access level left unset: sources describe wilderness and foot access but no public-access status. The record has no build year; the 1920 event year is a placeholder for the decade. No new photos.

Four short web sources that agree on the core dates. No NHLR or Forest Service record for the Bonner County site was found, so the 1937 build and 1940s abandonment rest on secondary pages. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Our Notes on the logging and footings is undated. Staffing is left out because the only source says no staffing history is documented. The access level public is inferred from National Forest land and the drive-up label. The 1940 abandonment year is a placeholder for the decade. The brief's gone status, design, height, and 1937 build are all supported. This is a different site from the Custer County Mid-Cottonwood Point record (us-id-mid-cottonwood-point).

Three web pages and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The 1965 Post-Register item and the 1937 CCC item are quoted second-hand on the Weebly page; the original newspapers were not fetched. No source describes what remains at the site, so the story says so. Idaho Fire Lookouts has no documented staffing history; the 1942 last-used date comes from the 1965 article and is filed as other, not staffed. The Challis National Forest history compilation was searched but had no lookout entry for Cougar Creek. The access level public is inferred from forest land and the hike-in label. The brief's kind (two_story), L-4 design, 1967 destruction, and gone status are all supported.

Three web pages and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The core dates (1927 build, 1955 destruction) agree across sources. Do not confuse this with the Montana Cougar Peak Lookout on the Lolo National Forest, a different structure that is standing, rentable, and has its own record (us-mt-cougar-peak). A search result from the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Facebook page and a Flickr photo caption for a 1952 rentable Cougar Peak Lookout describe the Montana building; they were not used here. The 1928 inspection report and the 1962 Kellogg Evening News item are quoted second-hand; the originals were not fetched. The Kellogg Evening News is the source for the first lookout, Bus Peterson. The brief's ground kind matches the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The access level public is inferred from forest land and the drive-up label. Staffing names are given as the sources list them; no source covers staffing after 1948.

Location is unsettled. The record's FFLA coordinates (44.58538, -115.7296) and the Idaho Fire Lookouts coordinates (44.59795, -115.7204) are about 1.6 km apart, and no source fixes the lookout summit. The 1953 benchmark note places the station 2 miles SW of Cougar Rock, while the climbing guide ties the lookout to Stolle Peak, which it says the USGS map calls Cougar Rock Benchmark. Verify the pin before using it. Access level 'public' is an inference from national forest land and the absence of any closure notice, not a source statement. The FFLA list gives no location note.

The 1933 cab type conflicts: R-4 in firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts, L-4 in Idaho Fire Lookouts. Forest Lookouts' 1923 fire and replacement cabin differ from the 1924 log cabin date on the other two pages; the story reports both. Coordinates in the record (FFLA 44.7203, -116.28038) and Idaho Fire Lookouts' coordinates (44.71072, -116.2693) are about 1.4 km apart. The peakbagging caption puts the lookout about 0.8 miles north of the USGS Council benchmark, so check the pin on a map before use. Access level 'public' is inferred from national forest land, not stated in a source. No corrections to the brief's record; the record had no events and no staffing.

The build year (1933) and destruction year (1954) agree across three site sources; the Idaho County list gives c.1933. Elevation 3,823 ft and the 30-foot height come from site sources. No source names any staffing, and none describes the site today. The Idaho Fire Lookouts drive-up tag is their label, not a verified access status, so access level is unset. Not listed in the 2010 Nez Perce list (fs.usda.gov/media/259204). The 1933 USFS drawings PDF on firelookout.org gave no extractable text, so L-4 is not defined in the story. The record had no events; built and destroyed were added. No new photos.

Elevation is 6,416 feet, about 1,956 m; elevation_m is null in the record and has no facts key. No source gives a tower height, so height_m is not set. All sources date the L-4 cab only to the 1930s, so no built event is set because events need a year. The Idaho pages say no staffing history is documented, so no staffing names are given beyond the unstaffed status after 1962. The Montana list and the 1962 date disagree on the fate; the story keeps both. Spelling: the record and most pages use Crittendon, while the climbing guide uses Crittenden. Notable fires: none in these sources.

Thin record: four short entries, and the Forest Lookouts entry is two lines. The FFLA coordinates (44.85882, -116.69403) and the Idaho Fire Lookouts-linked coordinates (44.8588, -116.6946) agree within about 50 m. Status is unsettled: 'abandoned' (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) does not necessarily mean the cabin is gone, and 'removed' and 'ground gone' come from the other two. No source dates any change. The Forest Lookouts page gives the other name Crooked River Peak. The Payette Crooked River Trail #235 page was checked and does not mention the lookout, so it is not cited. Access level 'public' is inferred from land status. Corrections: none.

Thin record: four sources, no construction year, no builder, no description of the site. The record's gone status rests only on the FFLA index, which gives no detail; the 2010 Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts say abandoned (see corrections). The Idaho County A-L page lists the Nez Perce entry at 25N-6E-26 with no history lines, so it adds nothing. Two web searches turned up no further history. No photos. A reviewer should check the status column of the 2010 list and look for local history before publishing.

Two structures share the Crystal Peak name. The 1954 St. Joe tower is this record. The 1959 tower at Fernwood is listed separately by the FFLA as Crystal Ridge, and no source I read ties it to the 1954 tower; its build year differs. Consider a separate record for the relocated tower rather than merging. lookouttowers.org's own footer credits a deep-research draft, so it carries low weight and is cited only for the disputed origin and the rental use. The staffing entry is Barbara Nelson, 1967; a second name, Neil Nelson, carries a Kellogg Evening News note under the same heading and may be a source credit rather than a staff entry. The two Crystal Peak coordinates are about 1.5 km apart (computed from the FFLA figures). No photo added. Inhabitat and Small Home Tours appeared in search results only and are not cited.

Destroyed in 1964; no tower stands. Cupola date disputed: Peterson (first-hand, 1925) and two later pages say 1925; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say a cupola cabin in 1922. Distance from Priest River is 4 miles on one source and 5 on two others. Legal access status is not stated in any source, so the level is 'unknown' even though WillhiteWeb's directions reach the site with no closure noted; verify with the Kaniksu National Forest before publishing. Footings claim rests on photo captions with no visit date. Not used: uidaho Priest River Historical Collection items priestriver0217 and priestriver0218 (possibly this lookout, unidentified).

Thin record: four pages repeat the same facts (c.1932 cabin with roof platform, William Davis 1942, last staffed 1944). Forest Lookouts cites 'Kresek' for its date; that book was not located. No source describes the site today or its access. Elevation 7,715 ft is now in facts and is cited to firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts only (Forest Lookouts gives no elevation). Proposed correction: brief event '1944 abandoned' should read staffed_last, since sources give only the last staffed year.

No recent condition report was found, so current state and access are unverified. The 1972 and 1981 fire-use dates conflict. Do not confuse with the town of Custer, Idaho. A 2026 Challis visitor guide mentions a 1981 National Register listing for Custer; it is unclear whether that refers to the town or the lookout, so I did not use it.

Cab design disputed: firelookout.com L-6, Idaho Fire Lookouts L-4. The 1932 staff name predates the 1937 build date and no source explains the gap. Abandonment is dated only 'in the 1960s', so no abandoned event was written. The 2011 Naturally North Idaho article lists towers and log cabins on Cutoff Peak, which conflicts with the tower-gone record. The Idaho Fire Lookouts visit date is not given beyond the September 2, 2021 post date. Access level is unknown; only the hike-in label is sourced. Photo by Kyle Cossairt (firelookout.com) has no image URL, so no photo entry. Proposed correction: record status gone to ruins, for editor review.

The 1960 destruction year is given by the three sources that date it (firelookout.com, the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts); the FFLA list marks the tower gone without a date. The 1945 tower's height and cab type do not agree across sources. The Drive-Up tag on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page is recorded as written, not as evidence of current access. No photo added. No source describes the site now.

Thin record: two lookout-history pages and the FFLA list. The two history pages agree on 1934 and 1954. No staffing, photo, or current-site description found in the sources read. The site is not described as public or closed anywhere in the sources, so access is omitted.

Staffing is left out: no source gives a staffing history. drive_up is true because Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the lookout Drive-Up; that describes the lookout when it stood and is not a statement about current access. Location check done 2026-10-10: against Pierce's coordinates on Wikipedia (46.49583, -115.80111), the record point (46.45065, -115.71375) lies about 5 miles southeast of Pierce, which fits the 6 miles southeast in two sources. The earlier 27-mile estimate was wrong.

Three sources agree on the 1934 build and the 1973 destruction. The record's county 'Idaho' is the state name; proposed correction is Idaho County. The Forest Service list's row gives a 30-foot pole, 1934, 'Destroyed 1973.' and elevation 7405', so it now backs the story's elevation (evidence added). Its section and township are marked with a question mark, so they are not used. No source read describes the site today or says whether it is open to the public; the search turned up no further Dan Ridge page.

Built year: 1940 in the register, firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts page and the Idaho list; the Idaho News 6 feature (undated in the cached copy) says 1941. Elevation differs across sources (register 6,706 ft, Idaho list 6694 ft, news feature about 6,800 ft); the record's 2044 m follows the register. Staffing as_of is 2024, the latest known-staff entry on the Idaho list (2021 Brig Malessa, 2022 Ezekiel Morphis, 2024 Stuart Morris); the 2021 evidence previously quoted the 2024 name and is corrected. The news feature is undated, so current staffing is unconfirmed. No source states an access level, so access is omitted. Record kind two_story and elevation are consistent with the sources.

Status is settled by two sources plus the association list. Only one post (June 2025, Idaho Fire Lookouts) describes the site today, and it does not say whether the site is open to the public. The drive_up value rests on the site's Drive-In label; the association's Ground label conflicts with it, and both are recorded. The record's photo is already on file; no new photos were found.

The 1914, 1934 and 1961 dates agree across firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Staffing differs by source: Idaho names Andrews for 1921, while the Forest Lookouts page quotes an August 1921 item naming R. M. Crow. The 1961 destruction has no stated cause in these pages. Forest Lookouts gives the location as 39N-7E-7; the brief coordinates (46.73426, -115.26762) come from the firelookout.org list and were not checked against a map. The USFS Clearwater lookout list PDF was read but has no Dead Horse entry in the cached text. A Facebook group post surfaced in search with similar dates and a different section number; it was not opened and is not cited. No photos added: none with a usable URL was read.
Build-year conflict (1934 vs 1936) left unresolved per two-against-one source split. No structure height (as opposed to elevation) was found in sources, so height_m was omitted.

Two sources date the lookout to about 1939 and agree on Challis National Forest and Custer County. The 'gone' status comes from two sources but neither gives a removal date. No source read describes the site today or says whether it is open to the public. The Forest Lookouts page shows 12N-14E-21 under the site name with no label; not used in the story. This is a different record from the Deadwood Lookout near Garden Valley in the Boise National Forest.

Idaho Fire Lookouts lists many more named seasonal staff (Odell, Black, Walters, Baker, Voll, etc.) between 1946 and 1972; only a sample is named in the story to keep it readable, with full list available in the source. Cabin footprint (15x15 vs 14x14) differs slightly between NHLR and Recreation.gov; both are given rather than resolved.

The record's coordinates (48.06299, -116.13079) sit roughly 1.5 to 2 km from the Idaho Fire Lookouts and West US list positions (48.05326, -116.14851 and 48.0481, -116.1489). I did not change them; someone should check the pin. A USFS Idaho Panhandle National Forests social post found in search says only the base and parts of the roof remain. I could not fetch that page, so it is not cited; it is a lead for what remains today. The 1935 scout item names the station DeLisle peak; the story flags that the name differs. Access is inferred from the hike-in description.

Two pages describe this site and agree on the 1933 build, the 1950 abandonment and the 6,285 ft elevation. The FFLA Idaho list agrees on tower and gone, and gives coordinates that the record already has. Two WebSearches and the 2016 Clearwater NF lookout list (fs.usda.gov/media/259185) did not name Dent Point, so there is no independent history. The Green Ridge patrol-lookout line is ambiguous and the story says so. Neither page has a staff history, so staffing is left out. Record agency and design were null and are filled from the pages. Elevation is sourced (6,285 ft, about 1,916 m) but has no facts key; the editor may set elevation_m.

Two pages agree on the 1931 camp, the 1934 cab and the 1947 destruction. The FFLA list gives ground-level cab, Shoshone County and gone. The record kind is 'ground', but the July 2023 note refers to footings for a tower, which points the other way; kind was not changed and the editor should decide. The status correction to 'ruins' depends on the 2023 note being current. Two WebSearches found no Devil Peak page in Shoshone County and no other source. Neither page has a staff history, so staffing is left out. Record elevation_m is null; the sources give 4,616 ft (about 1,407 m).

Disputed: the register dates a gable-roofed L-4 ground cab to 1926, while firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts date a cabin to 1926 and the L-4 cab to 1930; not resolved. Elevation is 7,461 ft in the register and firelookout.com but 7,641 on Idaho Fire Lookouts (may be a typo; not explained by any source). The record's location differs from Idaho Fire Lookouts by about 580 m; not checked here. Nothing read says whether visitors may enter the cab. The trip report is from 2013 and the road and trail details may be out of date. The 2021 staffing as_of comes from the June 9, 2021 Idaho Fire Lookouts article; the Keeping Watch page is undated. The Forest Service page in the tower's links (fs.fed.us, Nez Perce-Clearwater) did not resolve. A web search snippet mentioned a 2012 volunteer program start and a 2013 Forest Service description; neither was read, so neither is cited. Recommend checking current volunteer staffing and trail conditions with the Powell Ranger District before publishing.

Both pages agree on the 1935 build and the tower being gone by 1963. The FFLA list agrees on tower and gone, and also has a separate Vermillion Peak site listed as a ground-level cab that is gone. Nothing found shows it is the tower that may have been replaced, so the story keeps that as a hedge. Two WebSearches found no Disgrace Butte page and only other towers (Lookout Butte, Elk Butte), which were not used. The staff names come from the Idaho Fire Lookouts staff list, which cites a former register; the editor may want to confirm the names should stay in the public story. Record agency was null and is filled from both pages. Tower height is given as 30 ft and not converted to height_m, because cab-floor height is not stated.

Almost certainly the same tower as us-mt-divide-peak-seventy-two: both describe the 1931 pole tower on 72 Peak at the Montana-Idaho line, gone by 1950. The two records should be reconciled or linked. Coordinates: the brief point (47.97274, -116.03039) is firelookout.com's; the Montana record gives 47.96641, -116.02442 from the FFLA list; not resolved. Idaho Fire Lookouts has Weber family photos (1937, 1939, 1971) of the site but the cached page gives no image URLs, so none are added. The Idaho writers say their first visit went to the wrong spot. No source describes remains or public access today.

Height is left out: '30' pole' is the pole length, and neither source states a tower height. The 35-foot patrol tower on Green Mountain has no date in either source, so it appears in the story but not in events. The 5,027-foot elevation is on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The two pages use close wording, so they may share one source. Staffing is left out: no source gives a staffing history. Only two pages describe the lookout itself, so confidence is medium.

Both pages are hobby-site entries (firelookout.com by Rex Kamstra; the Idaho site appears to repeat that material), so this is one line of evidence, not two. No Forest Service, NRHP or register record was found. The record's elevation_m is null while both pages give 5,744 ft (about 1,751 m); not added as a correction. The record's kind 'ground' is not contradicted, but the sources only say 'log cabin with ladder to access', so it is unclear whether the cabin sat on the ground. A search returned 'Doe Point' (camp 1939, about 10 miles NW of Moose Creek Ranger Station), a different site; it is not used here. Nothing in the sources describes the site today.

Elevation is 6,032 feet, about 1,839 m, in the Idaho and firelookout.com pages; elevation_m is null in the record and no elevation key exists in facts. No source gives a tower height, so height_m is not set. The 1938 N.B. Benson entry is uncertain, since the footing reads 193? and the team asked for help. The 1933 start date rests on the 1933 newspaper item quoted on the Montana list and the Idaho post. No source says whether the site is open to the public, so facts.access is not set. Notable fires: none in these sources. The Shoshone County list also has a separate BLUFF (DOMINION) entry (44N-7E-12), which is a different site.

Elevation is not in facts: the Forest Service list gives 4,753 feet and marks it as Doris Butte's elevation, and Idaho Fire Lookouts shows question marks. Name: the list calls the site Doris Point (Butte). Location check done 2026-10-10: against Pierce's coordinates on Wikipedia (46.49583, -115.80111), the record point (46.56914, -115.41807) lies about 19 miles east-northeast of Pierce, which fits the two descriptions. The earlier 40-mile estimate was wrong. Staffing is left out: no source gives a staffing history.

History is corroborated by four sources: 1934 build, about 1951 destruction, and the 1957 transfer from Bitterroot to Nez Perce. Nothing found on the site today. Location conflict from the brief is unresolved and not checked: FFLA gives 46.23544, -114.80378 and West US Lookouts gives 46.2442, -114.8044; the Nez Perce list places it at T33N R13E Sect. 2, which matches the Forest Lookouts page (33N-13E-2). No access level is given because no source describes access. The Forest Lookouts page carries a bare 'Removed' label with no date; not used. No usable photo URL found. The list writes Ranger Station as RS; the story expands that abbreviation.

Site today rests on a single climbing guide (foundation still on the summit); no other source describes it. A geocaching listing (GC1D5ZQ, geocaching.com) reportedly says only a cement foundation remains, but the page could not be read in the cache, so it is not cited. Brief location conflict unchecked: FFLA 44.14623, -116.1483 vs West US Lookouts 44.12711, -116.15346. Elevation 6508 ft from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. No height_m recorded because no source gives a tower height. No usable photo URL found. Closure check: a text search of the climbing guide finds no road closure (its only match is 'Comments are closed.'). The 6508 ft elevation and Boise NF are also on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page and are now quoted as evidence.

Height: the record's height_m 3.0 has no source. 10 feet is the concrete base height (about 3.05 m), so the record may be using the base; omitted. Base material conflicts: concrete in the register, firelookout.com and the Idaho list (which says 10′ concrete base); cinder block in the Forest Lookouts page. Current condition is unknown beyond the roof loss reported by firelookout.com; no later visit report found. The access level 'restricted' is my reading of 'available for emergencies' and 'Hike-In Emergency Status'. Forest name: the register and Idaho list say Nez Perce National Forest, firelookout.com says Nez Perce/Wallowa Whitman. The 1968 vs 1968–1969 construction dates differ slightly between the register and the Idaho list. The Idaho list's known-staff entries run from 1932–1933 to 1978–1980 with gaps, so 1932–1933 is not the only staffing record.

The Forest Service list's header says it draws on Ray Kresek's book, Forest Service records, and Rex Kamstra's firelookout.com site, so it is not fully independent of the two web pages. The 1960s burn appears only in the Forest Service list. The abandonment year is given only as the 1940s; the event year 1940 is a placeholder with the note saying so. The record's kind 'tower' matches firelookout.com; the Forest Service list calls the structure a cabin. The record's status 'gone' matches every source. No photo or site description was found. Firelookout.com and the Forest Service list both give Kooskia as the reference point for the 21-mile distance, so there is no location conflict; the record's coordinates were not checked against Kooskia.

Current condition unknown: the last visit report is 2010. Forest name conflict: the register says Salmon-Challis; firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts page and the Idaho list say Salmon National Forest. The record's height_m 3.0 has no source in the pages read; omitted. Log base year conflicts (1944 register, 1943 Idaho list). The 1950s dates are decade-only, so the 1950 event year is a placeholder. The 1982 history says the road never reached the lookout while the 2010 visit report describes a road to it; both are recorded. No access level is stated, so access is omitted. The 1982 history's 'fell into disuse before many of the Depression-era lookouts' is kept as a paraphrase without a 'were built' reading, which the excerpt does not support and which conflicts with the 1935 build and 1950s last use.

History (1920 alidade and log cabin, 1923 abandonment) is consistent across three lookout pages and the FFLA list, but thin: no tower, no staff, no photo found. Nothing describes the site today; the old site is about half a mile west of the lake. Brief location conflict unchecked: FFLA 45.06083, -115.93769 vs idaho_fl 45.05735, -115.92372. The brief's 'events' lacked a 1920 build entry; added here from the sources. No photo URL found.

Fate disputed and unresolved: firelookout.com says offered for sale and removed in 1950; Forest Lookouts and Idaho Fire Lookouts say destroyed. Elevation also disagrees (firelookout.com 2983 ft, Idaho Fire Lookouts 3983 ft); left out of the story. The 1941 name William Heard appears only on Idaho Fire Lookouts and may or may not be the 1944 William Hoard. No source found on what remains or on public access; the one web search added nothing. Record's 1950 destroyed event is kept; a removal event was added from firelookout.com. Fact check 2026-10-10: the 1941 year sits on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page as a heading above Heard's name; the story now says the pages do not show whether Heard and Hoard are the same man.

Fate disputed and unresolved: destroyed (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) vs the 40-foot tower removed (Forest Lookouts, which cites a Clearwater TPA annual report; the report itself was not read). Record's 1957 destroyed event kept; removal added. Record design was null and is filled from the 40-foot L-4 description. Elevation unknown (firelookout.com shows '?'). Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so staffing is left out of the story. The 1915-1927 structures are described only briefly and may not all have been towers. The cptpa.com history supports the agency's later merger; the Potlatch and Clearwater names are as that site gives them. No source found on remains or access today; the one web search added nothing. Fact check 2026-10-10: the Forest Lookouts page gives its 1957 removal source as the Clearwater TPA annual report, so the citation is confirmed though the report was not read. The story cites only footnote 3 for the agency, since firelookout.com shows only the abbreviation CTPA.

Access level 'restricted' is my reading of conflicting evidence: an OHV route listing allows vehicles, and a 2024 visit found the gate open despite reports that it is locked. No official Forest Service access statement was found. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the 1958 cab as '40 R-6', which looks like a typo for 20 ft; firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts give 20 ft. Forest Lookouts cites Kresek (1932 and 1958 dimensions) but that book was not read. The Trailforks page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. No new photos. The story no longer advises against climbing the tower: the sources say the bottom stairs were removed and the tower is unstaffed, and the story says no official rule was found.

Structure history is well corroborated across three sites. Disputes left open: Grorud (1971) calls the tower 60 feet, against 53 feet in the other sources; last use is 1970s on firelookout.com and 1970? on Idaho Fire Lookouts, with abandonment in the 1980s on Forest Lookouts. Staff names come from two sites, several attributed to the Kellogg Evening News; newspapers not checked. Forest Lookouts' 'TFA' label is unexplained and not used. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 2016 entry is for Eagle Mountain, a different lookout, and was ignored. Record corrections (design, height_m, 1998 event) are already reflected in facts and events; the corrections list is kept for human review. No source found on remains or public access. Fact check 2026-10-10: the firelookout.com staff list has 19 named entries, nine of them couples (1947, 1948, 1951, 1952, 1953, 1954, 1955, 1957, 1967), with gaps between entries, so year by year was dropped from the story. The Grorud access and smoke account is paraphrased in the story.

Elevation conflict is unresolved: the register gives 5,548 ft (1,691 m), while firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 5,709 ft (about 1,740 m). The record keeps the register value. The 41-ft height is from the register and the 1959 survey note; the height to the cab floor is not stated. No source read says whether the public may visit, so access is left unknown. Staffing as_of is omitted because the sources give no date beyond the 1980s and the 2020 register text. No new photos. The distance from Canyon Ranger Station is cited to firelookout.com only; the register does not give it.

Three pages only. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page for Eagle Rock gives no site, staffing or fire history, so it is not cited. Brief's design (L-4) and 1951 destruction check out; no correction. The 1920s camp is in the story but not as a dated event, because both pages give only a decade ('1920s'). No cause for the 1951 destruction is given. Not the Oregon Eagle Rock (us-or-eagle-rock), and not the California ones.

Build dates are decade-only (1930s) and the 1960s abandonment has no year. The 1973 draft by O.F. Schumaker, as quoted by Forest Lookouts, conflicts with the three 1930s cabin entries; both are reported. Two coordinate points differ by about 25 miles and neither is verified; the brief point should be checked against a map before it is used. No source describes what is on the point today. The firelookout.com page has a 'Click for larger image' link but no image URL was read, so no photos are added.

Thin, secondary sources only. Two real disagreements, both kept in the story: cabin versus tent camp, and abandoned in the 1960s versus before 1940. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts documents none, so none is written. No source describes the site today. Access is recorded only as the hike-in label; no public-access status was found. The brief county 'Idaho' is corrected to Idaho County.

Brief height 6.1 m is the 1932 platform, not the 1935 tower; corrected to 9.1 m (30 ft pole height). Cab-floor height is not given. The 1915 and 1921 reports may describe the same butte (Sections 14 and 15 are adjacent) but the sources do not say so. The 1950 staffing is a single entry. A geocaching listing for this site appeared in search but could not be fetched, so it is not cited. No new photos added.

Both East Elk pages are hobby-site entries, and the Idaho site appears to repeat firelookout.com's dates, so there is one line of evidence, not two. The 1933 staff entry (Bill Bailey, Columbia Breaks Fire Center) appears on the Idaho page only and no second source was found; it is in the story with that caveat, and an editor may prefer to cut it. The CTPA label appears on both East Elk pages in the place Dog Point's page gives its Forest Service, so it is read as the agency; the expansion comes from the Elk Butte page and is probably the same body, not confirmed for East Elk. The 1957-58 association report (objects.lib.uidaho.edu/tpa/pot_tpa1957-1958.pdf) names Elk Butte, Mason Butte, Stockton Meadows and Freezeout as the four lookouts manned in 1957 and does not mention East Elk. No Forest Service record, photo or site description was found. Access, current ownership and what remains on the site are unknown. A search also surfaced Elk Butte and Elk Summit, which are different lookouts and are not used here.

Brief record checks out on height (50 ft = 15.2 m) and the 1965 end date; only the manner of the end is disputed (destroyed vs removed). No staffing, access or visit data in any source. A different lookout, Gold Hill (1938 pole tower, abandoned 1948, Boulder Creek Ridge), appears in search results and must not be merged with this record. No new photos added.

Coordinates conflict: FFLA gives 47.50544, -115.80989 and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 47.50632, -115.78183, about 2.1 km apart. None of the three sources read gives coordinates, so the record's point is unchanged. The brief's 1950 'abandoned' is corrected to 'removed'. The 20-ft figure is read as the tower height. No source states an access level, so access is omitted. Staffing rests on one name in one source. No source describes the site today.

Access is set to public from land ownership and the 2019 road description; no current access rule was found, so please confirm before publishing. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced. The brief's NHLR registration date (Aug 15, 1997) and FFLOS registration date (Jan 7, 2021) were not visible in the fetched text, so the record gives only the year (1997) and omits the 2021 FFLOS event. Status changed from gone to ruins, based on the 2019 caption only. No photos recorded: the NHLR photo credits give no licence.

No source describes the Echo Peak site today; story says so. Height is disputed (40 ft vs 30 ft); correction proposed to 12.2 m for editor review. Twin Crags status conflicts (FFLA ruins vs 2025 standing tower). Twin Crags has its own record that was not checked. NHLR page slug guessed at nhlr.org/lookouts/us/id/echo-peak-lookout returned 404. No photos added. Story kept to sourced facts only. Height is 12.2 m (40 ft, two-source value) in facts; the earlier corrections entry (current 9.1 m, proposed 12.2 m) was removed as already applied, and the editor should confirm the 12.2 m value. North Idaho was dropped from the story because no cited page says it. The Twin Crags same-county sentence now cites source 4.

Build year conflicts (1941 vs 1930s). A geocaching listing says remains are still on the site; its page cached as title only, so not quoted or used. Access and current ownership not in the sources. Staffing as_of 1959 is inferred from torn-down date plus one-week staffing. Record had design and height null; both now filled from two sources (40 ft = 12.2 m). Forest Lookouts quotes the Payette Valley Sentinel calling it the Eddy Creek lookout tower; the story attributes the 1930s/CCC claim to that page without asserting the name. The access advice was changed: no source covers access or current ownership, so the story no longer names PLTPA as the contact.

Elevation is 6,480 feet, about 1,975 m; elevation_m is null in the record, and there is no elevation key in facts. No source gives a height, so height_m is not set. No source documents staffing, so the only staffing fact is unstaffed as of 1955. The 1931 newspaper item is about a road along the divide, not the lookout; it is included as context for access. The sources do not say who owns or runs the electronics site, or whether the public may enter it. Notable fires: none in these sources.

Unresolved conflicts left for a human: (1) steel tower year, 1948 in the register, firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts versus a 1949 annual report entry (quoted on Forest Lookouts), which the story reports as a disagreement; (2) tower origin, army or WWII surplus versus 'designed for the U.S. Air Forces' in the 1958 report; (3) cab, 7x7 metal cab in the register versus a 14x14 cabin midway up in the 1958 caption, which may describe the 1933 live-in cab; (4) status, 'active' in the register versus emergency status on two sites. Record design was null and is filled from the register. No source read says whether the public may visit; the association homepage does not mention public visits. No new photos.

Several Elk Butte lookouts exist. The Clearwater County Elk Butte (NHLR US 216, ID 16) is standing and is a different site; the story says so to avoid mix-ups. The 1966 event conflicts (destroyed vs removed). Elevation 6372 ft is in the note, not facts. No photos added. No site-today source found in two searches.

The gone status rests on the FFLA list; the Forest Service list and both lookout sites say only abandoned. Idaho Fire Lookouts states it has no documented staffing history, so no staff entry is made. No source states an access level; the hike-in tag is the only visit fact. The Forest Service list and the Idaho County listing agree on the location (T29N R8E Sect 25). No source describes the site today.

The record's height of 15.2 m equals 50 ft, which matches the patrol-point platform; the summit tower is 40 ft per firelookout.com and the Idaho listing gives no tower height. Where the tower stood is disputed (summit vs eastern site). WillhiteWeb and NaughtyHiker are undated hiking accounts, so the 'today' paragraph reflects their visits, not a current survey. Access 'public' is inferred from the hiking accounts on national forest land, not stated by an agency. No new photos added: WillhiteWeb's photos have no image URLs or licence.

No source dates the removal, so no fate event is recorded. The sources spell the name Elk West (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) and Elk Mountain (West) (FFLA list). The 1915 cabin in Section 11 of T42N R4E on the Clearwater County listing belongs to another site and was not used. The Drive-Up tag comes from the listing and describes the old site, not present conditions. The brief had no events; 1914, 1915 and 1934 build events are added from both lookout pages. No source describes the site today.

The brief gives three coordinate sets that differ by about 1.6 km (FFLA 48.03776, -116.05013; Idaho Fire Lookouts 48.03962, -116.07145; WestUS 48.0383, -116.0577). No source here settles the point, so the location is unchanged. Idaho's index also lists Elk Ridge entries in Idaho and Shoshone counties; these sources describe the Bonner County site. Both sources date the removal or destruction only to the 1950s, so no event is given for it. Staffing is limited to a 1948 visit-type item and no documented history; the story says so only as the Idaho listing's own statement.

Two different Elk Summits exist. This record is the Clearwater list site (cupola cabin, 1924, gone). The standing 1934 tower near Elk City is us-id-elk-summit-2 and must not be merged with it. Only the 1924 date comes from a compiled 2016 list; no primary record was found. Nothing describes the site today. The county field in the brief holds only 'Idaho' and should read 'Idaho County'.

Record height 2.1 m is wrong; sources give a 100-foot tower (proposed 30.5 m). Status is disputed: NHLR (undated page) says used as needed by the Elk City Ranger District, while the Forest Service page (updated June 4, 2025) says not currently used by the agency and not accessible to the public. The story reports both and does not resolve it; the NHLR wording may be older. An Idaho County Free Press feature on the lookout (idahocountyfreepress.com, 88-year-old lookout tower article) was returned by search but could not be read (HTTP 429); it may say more about current use and should be checked by a human. Elevation: see resolved_conflicts. Access is closed per the Forest Service; no climbing advice given.

The brief's height_m of 3.0 is the 10-ft base, not a height to the cab floor, so no height fact was written; check whether the record should keep it. Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com differ on Bill Bates' years (firelookout.com: 1964-1968 with a relief question; Idaho listing: 1966-1968 with a relief entry), and they differ on Dave Garner's seasons; the story avoids both. A July 1958 Missoula item on the Forest Lookouts page describes a helicopter disabled while landing at 'Elkhorn Point lookout'; it may or may not be this site, so it is not used. The 1957 vs 1959 dating and the cinder-block vs concrete base are unresolved beyond the explanation above. The brief's kind 'two_story' matches the index's '2-Story cab'. No new photos added; the Idaho photos are credited to the Fire Lookout Museum without licence data.

All four sources are lookout-enthusiast compilations, not Forest Service records; the 1921, 1931 and 1954 dates agree across them but were not checked against primary records. The 'patrol tower 2 miles east on Early Ridge' appears on two pages and the story does not say whether it is a separate structure. Do not confuse with Kellogg Peak (a different lookout). Today's site is not described by any source checked.

Thin record: each page has a one-line history. The Forest Lookouts page credits both dates to 'Kresek', so the pages may share one origin; we could not check it. Elevation differs: 4548 ft on idahofirelookouts.com; TopoQuest lists the summit at 4540 ft, not used in the story. The abandoned event is left out because sources give only the decade. The record's coordinates differ slightly from TopoQuest's, not checked. No photos or post-removal description found.

Brief record county 'Idaho' should read 'Idaho County'. The Rhoda Point log cabin is a different structure 2 miles southeast of the summit and is reported as 'still there' by an undated firelookout.com listing; it is not a remnant confirmed on the summit. Hartig's 1981 history (quoted on the Idaho County list) is second-hand here, not checked against Forest Service records. The 1939/1940/1935 build dates and the 1954 versus 1955-56 burn dates are unresolved; the story reports the disagreement. The 'Minnie Willson' 1947 to 1948 staffing is from Idaho Fire Lookouts only.

Main open question is the forest name: the University of Idaho photo records are the only sources that name the Priest River Experimental Forest, and they are photo catalogue entries, not a forest history. The cabin removal has no separate date, so the story says it is undated and no removed event is kept. Experimental Point is named only in the U of I photo records (cites 5 and 6), not on the lookout pages, so the story cites 6 for it. No staffing, fire or access statements were found, so none is written. Record kind 'ground' follows the FFLA list; the firelookout.com text (platform atop a frame cabin) might fit another kind, not changed. The U of I photos dated 1917, July 1918 and 1928 are noted here but not added as photos because no image download URL was checked. No photo of the cabin itself was found.

Brief status 'gone' kept, scoped to the platform: 2022 visits found the tree standing with no platform. The FFLA index lists this site as 'Abandoned', not 'Gone', and the brief's 'firelookout_com=standing' does not match the firelookout.com text we read, which says 'still there in the 1980's'. No staffing sources; the Idaho Fire Lookouts page says it has no documented staffing history, so staffing is omitted. WillhiteWeb's photo caption '1927 Experimental Spur Tree' conflicts with the 1928 build date; not used. Access 'public' rests on no closure appearing in the sources. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page dated September 12, 2022 does not state the visit date.

The 1941 excerpt on the Forest Lookouts page is an approval, not a construction record; the 1942 date from idahofirelookouts.com is the earliest installation date in the sources. Status corrected from gone to unknown because the lists say abandoned, not removed. Nothing found on the elevator's current condition. The U of I Keeping Watch entry for Fairfield repeats the coordinates and points to firelookout.com, so it is not cited. The staffing status 'emergency' is the closest vocabulary match for 'staffed during lightning storms'. WebSearch surfaced only unrelated grain elevator fires, not used.

The four sources agree on the date (about 1930) and the 1950 abandonment. Three (firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts Idaho County page and the Idaho Fire Lookouts page) describe the two-story log cupola form, which the Forest Service list does not give. Two (firelookout.com and the Idaho Fire Lookouts page) list the site as gone. No source describes the site today, and the story says so. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says it has no documented staffing history, so staffing is omitted. Access 'public' rests on the drive-up tag and national forest land, with no closure in the sources. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced. The brief's kind 'two_story' matches the sources.

Build year 1933 and the 1963 burning agree across all four sources. The 1950 abandonment comes only from firelookout.com. No source describes the site today or current road access. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site 'Drive-Up' and 'Burned Down' without explanation, so the story quotes the tags (final paragraph, footnote 2) and does not read them as a current access statement. The access block is omitted. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, and no other source names staff.
