No photos added: the Forest Service Facebook post carries three photo captions (1939, 1950s, September 1963), but I did not have their image URLs. The brief's events list had no entries for this lookout; these are new. The brief's kind 'two_story' is not checked here.

The brief's height 14.6 m matches the 48-foot 1931 pole tower, not the R-6 tower; see the correction. The move year differs (1975 vs 1976). The cabin burned in the 2010s; sources give only that decade, so no event year is set for the fire. Staffing is a partial list of known personnel (1948 to 1972), not a roster. Access 'public' is our inference from the riding description. The Idaho Fire Lookouts Black Mountain page says 'Drive-Up Moved' and gives a 2019 move; its current status and whether the rental program opened are not confirmed by any source read. A reader comment on the Faset page is not used. No photos added.

Build year 1933 and the 1967 end date agree across sources; removed versus destroyed is the only disagreement. No source names staff or notable fires. Remnants rest on one climbing-guide photo caption (2019). Access level public is inferred from the drive-up tag and the forest-road route; no source states an access rule. Elevation in the record (2742 m) matches the register. Fact-check 2026-10-09: no factual errors; reworded three sentences that copied quote wording; added evidence for the 2019 date and the forest-road route.

Three sources disagree on the 1930 or 1931 build and on the base height (6 or 8 feet). The 1934 burning and the cabin manned through 1953 conflict on the same Weebly page. The brief's 'abandoned 1985' is not supported as an abandonment date; the 1981 history quoted on the Weebly page gives the late 1960s or early 1970s for last use. No source read describes the site today, the road's condition or current public access, so the access block is omitted. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site 'Drive-Up' and 'Removed / Destroyed' without explanation; the story quotes the tags (final paragraph, footnote 2) and does not read them as an access statement. The 1934 point is also an absence claim: none of the three sources explains how a building burned in 1934 came to be manned through 1953, so the story cites all three footnotes for it. Staffing is a partial list of named personnel (1917 to 1934), not a roster. The Weebly page's long quotes are from The Clearwater Story and a 1981 Lochsa history; I cited the Weebly page for them, not the originals. No photos added.

Three sources, no staffing or fire records found. Height and cabin-move year conflict; both are reported. A LandmarkHunter search result says the cabin went to Grangeville Lions Park in the 1970s, but that page timed out and is not cited. The cabin's current condition is unverified.

Two lookout pages disagree on the build year (1930 vs 1937). The Bonners Ferry Herald items the Idaho page cites were not read directly. Access is listed as public because Trail #27 is a listed Forest Service trail; re-check the trail page before relying on it. The Forest Service trail page is the only current-day source.

The three sources agree on the 1922, 1925 and 1931 structures and the 1969 destruction. The footings and beam are the Idaho Fire Lookouts team's belief ('what we believe'), so the story presents them that way. Elevation 6531 ft appears on firelookout.com and the Idaho Fire Lookouts page; the schema has no elevation key. A USFS Idaho Panhandle NF Facebook post appeared only as a search snippet (not read) and is not used. Route and closure details were not found, so access rests on the Hike-In tag and the St. Joe National Forest listing. The brief's kind 'tower' fits the sources.

Both sources give the same three dates and probably share an origin, so they are not independent confirmation. No source describes the site today or gives access or height; access and visit are left out. Elevation 4490 ft is on both firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com (the second in the page header), so it is now a facts key (elevation_ft) and the story cites both sources for it. Record coordinates are consistent with '14 miles ENE of St. Maries'. Record status 'gone' and event 1952 are supported. Story is short because the evidence is thin.

The three lookout pages agree on the 1932 tower and the 1956 loss, but none gives a cause, a day, or site conditions. The 1934 fire is not named in the quoted account. The L-4 description comes from a Nez Perce NF style guide and is general, not specific to this site. The index's (Kresek) attributions were not traced. Brief height 6.1 m matches the 20 ft figure.

No record corrections needed. The 1993 cause is disputed: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say a vandal set it over the winter; Forest Lookouts says a stranded camper accidentally burned the building and garage later in 1993. The story reports both without choosing. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site Drive-Up Burned, so the story reports that label as a suggestion of road access and says no source confirms current access. The 1959 telephone relay rests on one hobby-site page quoting the Idaho State Journal. No Forest Service record was found.

Thin sourcing: four lookout sites plus one forest study whose online copy stops after the introduction and omits the lookout list. Not used: the Forest Lookouts Idaho page lists an October 1920 Kendrick Gazette item (Fly camp, seven miles south of Chamberlain Basin) under the Fly Hill heading; it does not name the peak, so it is not tied to this site. The 1931 staff entry predates the 1934 build; a reviewer may want the Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry entry. Record kind two_story left as is; sources describe an L-4 cab atop a log crib. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the Forest Lookouts page lists Fly Hill under Clearwater National Forest and an item dated October 8, 1920; the online study copy stops after its introduction and omits the lookout list; no factual errors found, and three sentences that copied quote wording were reworded.

Record status gone is not supported by the firelookout.org list, which says Abandoned; the proposed correction is ruins. The 1928 Daily Panidan item also includes an unrelated anecdote about a rescued man, which the story leaves out. The abandonment year is only a decade in every source. The site-today description rests on one 2022 hobby-site post. No photos added. Searches did not turn up a Forest Service record. Revised 2026-10-10: the story now dates the 2022 visit and no longer says no source describes the remains (the 2022 post does); 'first structure' is now 'earliest structure listed'.

Record facts hold up: gone per the firelookout.org list, Nez Perce NF, Idaho County. Staffing 1939 to 1941 rests on one source (Idaho Fire Lookouts citing a former registry). The L-4 dimensions come from a general Nez Perce NF publication, not a site-specific record. The trailhead page is cited only for the road and trail; it does not describe the lookout site. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site Drive-Up Abandoned / Destroyed, which the story reports as a label only; the trailhead page does not describe the lookout site. No new photos added. Revised 2026-10-10: 'first lookout' is now 'earliest lookout on record'; the L-4 sentence is reworded so it no longer copies the Forest Service quote.

Build year conflict unresolved: firelookout.com says the 20-foot pole L-4 tower was built in 1931; idahofirelookouts.com lists an L-4 cab on a 20-foot pole tower in 1934. Both give 1953 as destroyed. Height 6.1 m is converted from '20' pole' and may not be height to the cab floor; flagged, not verified. Forest name: firelookout.com says Nez Perce National Forest; Komoot uses Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. Komoot is a recreation listing, used only to say the point is a rest area with no tower mentioned. Photo already on record (credit idahofirelookouts.com) is not a new find. Elevation 5003 ft is on both firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com and is now a facts key (elevation_ft). Story wording was changed so it does not copy the Idaho Fire Lookouts timeline line. No source describes the site today.

Five sources, three of them lookout-history sites that overlap. Build and destruction dates conflict and the story gives both. Staffing has only the 1916 newspaper item and a 1919 name. The undated University of Idaho document is the only one that treats the remaining lookouts as a group. No source describes the site today or whether it is open to visitors.

Sources agree on the 1912, 1937 and 1971 dates. The record's two coordinate datasets disagree (46.99856, -116.02818 vs 47.01639, -116.02472); none of the pages read gives coordinates, so the record was not corrected. The sources give 11 miles east of Clarkia and township 42N, range 3E, section 12 (weebly page). The August 2025 visit report is the only current-condition source and is a visitor's account, not a survey. Staffing from 1915 onward comes from newspaper items quoted on two lookout sites.

Status correction is proposed, not applied. Coordinates were checked: Wikipedia gives Pierce, Idaho at 46.4958 N, 115.8011 W, so the record point (46.50337, -115.71711) is about 4 miles east of Pierce, consistent with the sources. Height 12.2 m is converted from '40' pole' and may not be height to the cab floor; flagged. Komoot summit listing is used only to say no structure is mentioned. Its page gives elevation 1,610 m (about 5,282 ft), about 45 ft under the 5,327 ft in firelookout.com and the Forest Service list, so it may be a different point; the story says only 'a French Mountain summit' in Clearwater County and does not claim it is the same point. Forest Service list is a 2016 compilation whose French entry gives Sec33 T37N R6E, 40' pole L-4, 1932, abandoned 1948, 5327 ft. No source describes the site today. Elevation 5327 ft is on firelookout.com and the Forest Service list and is now a facts key (elevation_ft). A second citation was added for the crow's nest platforms.

Built year and height disagree: 1934 and 40 ft (sources 1, 2, 3) vs 1933 and 50 ft (source 4, Louis Hartig's 1981 Lochsa history as quoted on the weebly page; the book itself was not read). Demolition: destroyed 1960 (3, 4) vs gone by 1963 (1, 2); both are stated. No source describes the site today, and no source states public access beyond the drive-up label. The record had no events; built and destroyed events were added. Source 3 lists one USFS photo but none was fetched, so no new photo is recorded.

Idaho Fire Lookouts and Forest Lookouts both draw on Ray Kresek's book, so they are not independent confirmation of each other. Elevation differs: FFLOS 2,074 m (6,806 ft); firelookout.com 7,003 and 6,820 ft; Idaho Fire Lookouts 7,003 ft. The record's 2074.5 m matches FFLOS and was not changed. The Forest Service Nez Perce list has an abandoned 1950 entry on the Blacktail row whose column alignment is unclear, so it is not used. Access today unknown; only the hike-in label is recorded. No photo URL found.

The record lists only the L-4 design; the site had a treated-timber replacement in 1961-62 and an interim cupola trailer, so the design field was widened rather than corrected. The record's agency (Coeur d'Alene NF) is correct but partial; Idaho Department of Lands took over operations in 1966. The 2025 visit found scraps and two believed outhouse pits; no source describes any structure remaining. Visit access is drive-up per Idaho Fire Lookouts, with no access rules given.

Brief record checked: status gone, kind two_story, agency Salmon National Forest all agree with the sources; access stays unknown, so no access key. Elevation 8,276 ft appears in sources 1 and 2 but the schema has no elevation key, so it appears only in the story. The 1951 notice concerns a telephone line, not the cabin; do not read it as a demolition order. The sources do not say how the cabin came down, so the event is 'removed' and not 'destroyed'. Two WebSearch calls and six distinct pages read (the Forest Lookouts page was re-grepped, not re-read); the Salmon-Challis fire lookouts page and the Salmon forest history did not mention Gant. No site-today description found.

Brief's elevation (2010.8 m / 6597 ft) matches both NHLR and Wikipedia exactly. Brief's access field was 'unknown'; proposed 'restricted' based on hike-in, staffed, wilderness-area status. Idahofirelookouts staff list had some garbled text (e.g. 'AbaStaffed') from page formatting; used only the clean names/years. Al Koenigs is recorded in 1925 and 1927 (not 'late 1920s'); Tommy Reed is recorded only in 1956, not 'much of the 1950s' -- story corrected to match the source's actual staff-year entries.

Four sources agree on the 1934 cabin and the same-year fire, and none conflicts with the record (kind ground, status gone). No source describes the site today. The Forest Service list places it 17 miles W of Moose Creek RS. A Facebook group post from the Clearwater Trekkers about clearing Gedney Creek trail #708 appeared in search results only; it is undated and was not used.

Thin but consistent: four sources agree on the 1939 pole tower with a tent and on abandonment in the 1940s. The record's 1940 abandonment year is more precise than any source (see corrections). The record is right that the tower is gone (source 4). No source describes the site today. Access rests only on the 'Drive-Up' label on source 2.

Both lookout pages carry the same Fire Lookout Museum photo credit, so they are probably not independent. The brief's record was right on status and kind but had no 1933 build event; added. Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented, so staffing is left out of the story. Two searches found no description of the site today, and the story says so. Access level is not stated by any source, so access is omitted.

Record height 12.2 m matches the 1932 40-ft pole tower; the standing 1958 tower is 41 ft (proposed 12.5 m). Build year: 1932 per NHLR, Idaho and Forest Lookouts; a Priest River Experimental Forest storymap appeared in search with 1933 and a 1951 rename, but its page returned no text and it was not used. Current staffing rests on a Jan 2022 Idaho Fire Lookouts post and an undated firelookout.com line (staffed in summer); no current Forest Service source was read, and a 2020 IPNF post about access limited to staffed lookout towers appeared in search but was not readable. Access level left unset because no source states public visiting rules; the record's access 'unknown' stands. Elevation and forest-name conflicts are in resolved_conflicts. Staff names come from newspaper items quoted by the Forest Lookouts and Idaho sites; no new photos were recorded.

Both pages give only decades for the build and the abandonment, so no events are recorded; the story uses the decades. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the agency as Clearwater-Potlatch TPA and does not expand TPA, so the field keeps the label as printed. Neither page describes what remains today. A Clearwater National Forest lookout list PDF (fs.usda.gov/media/259185) was checked and has no Goat or Grassy entry, so it is not cited.

Brief has two coordinate sets (ffla 48.7778,-116.05948 and idaho_fl 48.77311,-116.05292), about 0.7 km apart. No source read gives coordinates, so the conflict is unresolved and the brief's coordinates are left unchanged. Do not merge with a different lookout also called Goat Mtn: idahofirelookouts.com/st-joe-clearwater-region/goat-mtn/ describes a St. Joe NF tower (elevation 6155, 1916 crow's nest, 1934 pole tower with L-4 cab, destroyed 1961, patrol point on Blackdome). A guessed NHLR URL for this lookout returned 404. Brief access 'unknown' kept, so no access key. Six distinct pages read and one WebSearch. The only site-today description is the single 2011/2024 article, which does not name this lookout.

Do not merge with us-id-goat-mountain: that record is the Boundary County Goat Mountain (Kaniksu National Forest, cupola cabin 1924, destroyed 1965), a different lookout. The record's location conflict is open: the FFLA list gives 46.99262, -115.84718 and the Idaho Fire Lookouts map point is about 1.9 km away (47.00885, -115.83934). The story gives no coordinates. Two searches found no description of the site today; the story says so. Staffing is not documented by Idaho Fire Lookouts, so it is left out.

Three listings agree on 1931, 1972 and the agency name; brief event '1972 destroyed' matches. No source read describes the remains or public access. A YouTube page titled 'Goblin Knob at Priest Lake' returned no text, so it is not used. The source spells the second staff name 'Lawerence'; check the spelling before publishing. The Priest River Community Foundation page was searched for mentions of this lookout and has none, so the story does not link the 1972 loss or the 1931 build to the 1931 Freeman Lake fire. Photo credits to the Fire Lookout Museum appear without a license, so no photos are added. Two WebSearch calls; five distinct pages read.

Destruction year disagrees (1956 Idaho Fire Lookouts, 1966 firelookout.com); the 1966 record date is credited to idaho_fl but that page says 1956. The 1919 Ben Thomas staffing is doubtful: the quoted newspaper names Gold Hill Lookout and Kemnow flags the location as possibly wrong. height_m 22.6 is converted from the 1933 74-ft tower. Kemnow's header gives legal description 40N-3E-35, but the 1915 report quote says Sec. 36. Potlatch TPA annual reports were not opened directly; the 1915 quotes are as printed on Kemnow's page. No source describes the site today or gives access.

Elevation conflict left open: 4,889 ft (1,490 m) on NHLR vs 7,790 ft on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The brief's location conflict is unresolved: firelookout.org list coordinates 44.67137, -115.83580 (matches brief ffla) vs 44.65839, -115.83738 (Idaho list, per brief). Story uses no coordinates. The record us-id-gold-fork-at-crawford-work-center covers the same cabin; this record leads with the original site. Idaho Fire Lookouts carries National Archives photos from August 1955 (Greenlee, Sprague, Muir) but no image URLs were captured, so no photo entries were added. The 1955 staffing comes from photo captions, not a staff list.

Four pages plus the firelookout.org list agree on the 1918-20 platform, the 1933 cabin and the 1988 move, but disagree on the 1988 destination and on elevation. Both are reported in the story. The brief's 'None relocated' event is wrong and is corrected. A firelookout.org listing also has a separate 'Gold Fork Valley' entry at 44.67137, -115.83580 marked Ground Gone; it is not clearly the 1918-20 site, so it is not used. Staffing is documented only by two 1935 and 1945 newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, and the originals were not read. Access is left unknown; only the 'Drive-Up' label is recorded. No notable fires were found. Height is not recorded.

Only four sources, all short. None describes staffing, fires, or the site today. Coordinates differ: the firelookout.org index gives 47.43280, -115.83290 (matches the record's ffla point), while the brief's idaho_fl point 47.43076, -115.82516 is about 0.6 km away; not settled here. idaholookouts.weebly.com/gold-hill.html covers a different Gold Hill (Latah County, 42N-4W-23); its 1915 Harvard telephone item is not this lookout and was not used.

Four independent sources agree on the 1931 build and the 1954 end date, but the wording conflicts (destroyed vs removed). The 2018 USFS Facebook post also carries a 1938 interior photo of Wayne Tautfest (Doland Broker photograph, USFS collection); no image URL was captured, so no photos entry. No staffing beyond that photo and no fire records were found. The NFSL Fixed Fire Detection PDF and the Clearwater Story book were cached but had no Gold Hill line.

Height correction: the record's 6.1 m is the 20-ft 1920s platform, not the 1934 L-4 tower (40 ft = 12.2 m). The 1920s camp is decade-only, so it is left out of events. Kemnow's 1934 entry also lists a 40-ft platform patrol tower 3/4 mile NE, which is not in the record. No staffing sources. No source describes the site today or gives access. Elevation 4534 ft is in the story but has no facts key.

All four sources agree on the core facts (1933, 40-foot pole L-4 tower, abandoned 1955, now gone), so the confidence is high, but the story is short because there is little else. Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented, so staffing is omitted. Access today is unknown beyond the drive-up label. The Forest Service list credits a photo to Harold Coffman; no photo URL was found, so no photo was added.

Thin record: three web pages, no staffing, no fire history, no site description. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history (page dated 2025-10-02); not used in the story. Access key omitted because no source states access. The NFSL Clearwater lookout study download (nfsl.contentdm.oclc.org item 28879) returned only its introduction, and its text does not name Gospel Hill, so it is not cited. The brief's status 'gone' rests on 'probably removed', so treat as gone with a hedge on the date. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now calls it the Gospel Hill site, since no source describes its terrain.

Destruction in 1955 is agreed by all three lookout listings. The Forest Lookouts page has a '1969: Destroyed' line directly above the NIRA POINT entry; that line belongs to Nira Point, not Graham, and is not used. The June 1930 lightning and fire item and the July 1931 completion report are quoted on the Forest Lookouts page from the Spokane Daily Chronicle; the original newspaper was not checked. The 'open to hikers' claim rests on one 2016 hiking blog, not an agency source. The 'Granham Peak' spelling in the 1930 item is the newspaper's, not ours.

Destruction is decade-only (1950s) in all three pages, so the record's 1950 is proposed as a correction and no destroyed event is dated. The record location (idaho_fl) differs from the FFLA/firelookout.com point by about 0.76 km. Do not confuse with the NHLR Granite Mountain entries for Salmon NF or Payette NF, which are different towers. No staffing sources and no site-today source.

Built date conflicts (1929 vs 1934); story uses 1934. Rental status unconfirmed: firelookout.com says planned; forest camping page lists one unnamed lookout. Access is unknown in the record and no visit info was found, so no access block. Search results also showed a different Granite Mountain Lookout on the Payette NF (NHLR, 1955 L-4 tower) and one on Mount Baker-Snoqualmie; neither is this record and neither was read.

Record height 3.7 m is wrong; the present tower is 20 ft (proposed 6.1 m). Name collision risk: two other Idaho lookouts are called Granite Mountain (Idaho Fire Lookouts southern-idaho page: 1923 camp, 2003 NHLR, North Fork Ranger District; north-idaho-panhandle-region page: 1932 cabin and 1934 L-4 tower, destroyed in the 1950s). Neither is this Payette tower and their facts were not merged. Current staffing is unverified for 2026: the staff list shows a 2026 entry and the 2025 visit confirmed a staffed season, but the FS guide (undated in the copy read) says unmanned. Staff names were deliberately left out of the research file; the staff list includes current seasonal staff. Access: the trail is public and non-motorized; no source describes rules for entering the tower. The NHLR page shows photos (1953 USFS, 2017 courtesy Keith Lanom) but no image URLs were retrieved, so no photos are recorded.

The two Idaho-facing sites repeat the same wording and dates, so they are not two independent confirmations. The 1933 and 1935 staff entries rest on Bonners Ferry Herald items that are cited second-hand; I did not read them. No Forest Service or NRHP text was found for this site. The Idaho page gives an elevation of 6,205 ft; the record's elevation_m is null and could be filled (about 1,891 m). Records us-id-grass-mountain-2 and -3 are other sites (coordinates 45.39 N and 45.15 N) and were not touched. Story is about 180 words; evidence supports the built, staffing and destroyed statements, and nothing in the sources describes the site today.

Two different lookouts share this name. This record is the Payette NF tower in Idaho County (6,262 ft). The Kaniksu NF Grass Mountain in Boundary County (6,205 ft; platform tower and cabin in the 1930s, L-4 tower 1936, destroyed 1955) appears on the Idaho Fire Lookouts northern-idaho page (grass-mountain-lookout-2) and firelookout.com grassmtn234; those were read and deliberately not used. Three sources agree on the 1934 cab and the 1978 destruction; little else exists. No staffing source found, so none is written. The brief county 'Idaho' is corrected to Idaho County.

Brief checked: Shoshone County, Coeur d'Alene NF, L-4, 30 ft (9.1 m) and gone all match the sources. Construction date conflicts (1924 vs 1925-28) are unresolved; no Forest Service primary record was found. Staffing is only the two 1927 names, each tagged (Diary); the diaries themselves were not read. The 1927-28 packer recollection is Ken Maryott's, per the Idaho Fire Lookouts page. No photos added. Access level 'public' rests on the drive-up description and WillhiteWeb.com's 'should be open' remark; no closure reported.

Brief checked: Idaho County, Clearwater NF, 6,190 ft, ground type and gone all match. The brief had no design; L-3 comes from Hartig (1981) via Forest Lookouts. The access level is omitted because sources say hike-in but describe no permissions. Nothing in the sources describes the site today. Hartig's 'torch job' is quoted without detail; the story says only that Bill O'Brien went in to do it, and Hartig is the only source for the fate of the buildings.

Build year conflict (1923 vs 1924) noted in the story. No documented staffing list beyond Maclean. Access level set to public/hike-in since it sits in designated wilderness with no restriction mentioned, but it's a serious approach, not a casual visit.

The brief listed status as plain 'standing'; sources indicate it's specifically on emergency-use status rather than seasonally staffed, so I added status_note and staffing accordingly. Idaho Fire Lookouts visit post includes several Fire Lookout Museum photos already credited there; not treated as new finds here since they're attributed to that site rather than a fresh source.

Thin record. The 1935 date rests on one underlying source (Kresek) repeated across three sites. No staffing, fire, or current-site information found. Brief checked: Valley County, lat/long, ground type and gone all match. Name variants: Grays (North) Peak and Gray's Peak (North). Story is short because the evidence is short.

Build year and design come from two register sites (firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts) that may share a source; no agency record was read. Height 12.2 m is the 40-foot pole converted; the brief had no height. The Trapper Peak Fire is confirmed by the Boundary County Museum, but no source places the lookout inside the burn or names its exact spot. The Forest Lookouts page gives the legal location 64N-4W-19, not checked against the coordinates. One search for an independent Green Bonnet record found nothing. The Kaniksu National Forest or the Boundary County Museum may hold a file. Today's site condition is not in any source read.

The 1931 build date and the 100-foot height appear in three sources, but the two Idaho-facing pages share wording and the weebly list is a compiled history, so this is not a primary-record check. The weebly list names the Nez Perce National Forest with a township code; I did not verify the forest name against a Forest Service record for 1931, so the agency fact is only as good as that list. Idaho Fire Lookouts states that no staffing history is documented; the story leaves staffing out. Height of 30.5 m is 100 ft converted. Wall Peak is named as the patrol point but not located. The existing record photo is credited to idahofirelookouts.com; I did not change it. Story is about 130 words; the thin evidence is why.

The 1914 annual report and the June 1915 Elk River Sentinel item are quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; they were not checked against the original paper or report. A search for an independent Green Mountain record in Clearwater County found nothing and returned other Clearwater lookouts instead. The Idaho list's Crowsnest Abandoned status is the basis for the proposed status correction. Today's site condition is not in any source read. Drive-Up is an Idaho Fire Lookouts tag, not a road description.

Built history is consistent across sources. Access and rental status are not established: the only access signal is the Idaho Fire Lookouts Drive-Up tag, so no access block was written. That page also shows a Staffed tag next to Drive-Up, but its text ties the staffing to a 2020 fire. The Nez Perce National Forest may now be Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest; the sources use the older name, so check before publishing. Forest Service list PDF fs.usda.gov/media/259202 (as of 2010) was read but not cited. It lists Green Mountain for emergency use, but the table text was too garbled to quote.

Three sources agree on the 1934 L-6 cab, the 5,872-foot elevation, the Clearwater National Forest and the gone status. The distance from Kelly Creek ranger station also agrees across firelookout.com and the Forest Service list. The Forest Service list's Chateau Rock row says its patrol camp was 3 miles east atop Green Point; that describes another lookout's patrol camp, so I did not use it. No staffing history is documented in these sources, so the story leaves staffing out. The record's ground classification matches the statewide list. No photo or site description was found. Access is unknown; the site is on national forest land, but no source says whether the public may visit it. Story is about 125 words; the record is thin, so it stays short.

Build date and design conflict across three sites: 1934 L-4 cabin on two register sites against a 1933 R-1 gable roof house on the Forest Lookouts page. Not reconciled. The brief's height_m 6.1 is the 20-foot footprint from the 1959 survey description, so removal is proposed. One search for an independent record found nothing. The 1959 description is quoted from the Forest Lookouts page; the NGS datasheet itself was not checked. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Hike-In tag is the only access detail. Today's site condition is not in any source read.

Brief lists only the 1953 destruction. Sources show a lookout burned in July 1926, so the 1934 tower was not the first; no source says whether it replaced the earlier one. Elevation conflicts (4,589 vs 5,800 ft). No source describes the site today. Lakeview is given without a state by Firelookout.com. The web search found no further source.

Brief kind is ground and status gone; sources agree on the 1914 cabin, 1929 cupola cabin and 1955 abandonment. Staff list runs 1930 to 1946 per Idaho Fire Lookouts. Conflicts: crow's nests (Firelookout.com says four remain; 2022 post says none) and the 1946 Miller first name. The 2022 visit is a single hobbyist account, not a survey. The web search gave a geocaching listing that was not fetched or used.

Thin record: three pages agree on 1935 build and 1970 destruction; no staffing or cause is given. Elevation 9,454 ft is from Idaho Fire Lookouts only. The firelookout.org index lists a different Grouse Creek Point at 45.68257, -115.10234 (camp, abandoned); that is a separate place, not this site. The web search found no further source.

Dates conflict. A 1914 newspaper item (via Forest Lookouts) already places a lookout here, while firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts date a 10x10 frame cabin to 1921; the story does not link the two. The end is unresolved: removed (Forest Lookouts), destroyed (Idaho Fire Lookouts), R.I.P. with unknown end (firelookout.com). The brief's location conflict is unresolved: the record uses the Idaho Fire Lookouts point (48.50793, -116.2555) while the FFLA point is 48.49728, -116.26597; no page read gives coordinates. Staffing facts are left out of facts because the tower is gone; the staffing events carry the dated names. No new photos: the record already has the Idaho Fire Lookouts 1921 image.

Thin sources. Two sites say L-4 cab (1930s); Forest Lookouts says camp (Kresek). No removal date. The FFLA Facebook post (search snippet only; the page could not be read in the cache) says built 1935 and taken down; it is not used because no quotable text was cached. The 2017 communication site Grouse Peak South is 8 miles ENE of Challis; the lookout is 8 miles northeast, and the two may be on the same summit, but no source confirms it, so the event is marked other and is not used as a status for the lookout. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history, so staffing is left out. Access and the present state of the summit are not described by any page read. Record coordinates (44.56532, -114.09483) match the FFLA point and are close to a third-party peak listing; not checked against a source that gives coordinates. No new photos.

Two Grouse Points sit on the Clearwater. This record (FFLA 46.41048, -114.69014) matches the Forest Service row six miles south of Powell RS (built 1934, burned 1934). The 1933 tower three miles north of Lochsa RS is the subject of us-id-grouse-point-2 and -3. The dedupe review kept -2 and -3 apart at 3.0 km; the sources (FS row, firelookout grousepoint269 at -115.33464, Idaho St. Joe page at -115.3426) suggest they are one tower, which the owner should confirm. Coordinates differ: FFLA 46.41048,-114.69014 vs Idaho Selway 46.41076,-114.67777 (949 m). Idaho's Selway page gives elevation as ????, as the FS list does. The brief's 'destroyed' event is corrected to 'burned'. The owner's brief shows a 1934 event only; this research adds the 1934 built event. No staffing or fire history beyond the Pete King burn was found. Page reads ran one over the per-tower budget (seven) because two of them were needed to separate the two Grouse Points.

Core facts (30-foot tower, burned in the August 1934 Pete King Fire, gone) agree across five sources. Dates (1933 versus 1934) and tower material (pole, log, round timber) disagree; both are in the story. Staffing dates come from Hartig's 1981 account alone. Other Grouse Points are in the same sources and were not used: a Clearwater NF entry 6 miles south of Powell RS (L-4 tower, 1934, burned 1934) on the Forest Service list and the Forest Lookouts list, and an FFLA index entry at 46.41048, -114.69014. The Lessons Learned page covers the fire, not the lookout. The brief county 'Idaho' is corrected to Idaho County.

Sources agree on the 1926 crow's nest, the 1928 log cabin with cupola and the destruction around 1950. Location conflict in the brief is unresolved: the record uses the FFLA point (45.88644, -114.92982), while the Idaho Fire Lookouts point is 45.89129, -114.93546; no page read gives coordinates. Harry Farris is listed with no year, so no staffing date is taken from him. The far-right '1920s' entry on the Forest Service row sits in a column whose heading is unclear in the text, so it is not used; the 1926 crow's nest is in the build-date column of the Grouse Ridge row. Photo: the Forest Service history PDF has a caption 'Grouse Ridge LO, no date' credited to a Sid Poppe photo in the Dick Walker Collection, but it has no image URL, so it was not added; the record already has an Idaho Fire Lookouts photo.

The history agrees across both lookout sites, and the site notes describe almost nothing left. Coordinates disagree by 762 m: FFLA 47.75567,-116.14272 vs Idaho 47.76131,-116.14851; the record uses the FFLA point. Neither source gives a staffing history or a fire. The existing photo in the record is from the Idaho site and needed no new find. Page reads: two lookout pages plus the FFLA list; one Shoshone County page added nothing.

Brief status gone and kind tower hold up. Brief lists two coordinate sets (FFLA 48.96206,-116.36136; Idaho Fire Lookouts 48.97384,-116.37159) that are not resolved here; the story gives no coordinates. Access level is omitted because no source says whether the land is open to the public today; visit.drive_up is true from the 'Drive-Up' label and the easy-ride note on the 2023 post. Staffing lists come from two fan sites that differ: Idaho Fire Lookouts adds 1938 (Roy Meeker), 1940 (Lester Spurgeon) and 1970 (Deborah Schleef) names that firelookout.com does not list. No fire history or rental information found.

Brief status gone and ground kind hold up. Four sources only, and none documents staffing, so no staffing sentence is written. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it cannot fully read the carvings in the cement, so the 1926 platform date is its own reading. Cause of the 1950 destruction is not stated in any source read. A Facebook group post (1936 photo, grandparents at the lookout) appeared in search only and is not used. Access level is omitted because no source says whether the land is open to the public.

Sources disagree on the end: 'Abandoned' with no date (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus 'burned in 1960s' (Forest Service list). The FS list calls the building a crow's nest smokechaser cabin; the record's kind 'ground' fits 'smokechaser cabin' but should be checked against photos before the story calls it a ground cabin. Built 1931 is added as an event because the record had none. Record coordinates 45.54821,-115.94230 match FFLA; Idaho's point is about 0.001 degree away. No staffing history or fire was found, and no photo was found.

Brief status ruins, ground kind and L-4 design hold up. The present state of the ruins rests on one climbing guide with no date (its photo caption is labeled 1990 but not used) and on 'Ruins' labels from two lookout sites. The Forest Service trail page, last updated March 10, 2026, describes the trail to the lookout but says nothing about the ruin. The 1917 entry is a camp, not a cab. Access level public comes from the trail page. No fire history, abandonment date or rental information found.

Conflicts not resolved: base height 8 ft (register, Idaho Fire Lookouts) vs 10 ft (firelookout.com); design R1/L-4 (register) vs L-4 (others); the 1963 two-story house with an R4-80 cab (Forest Lookouts only) is not reconciled with the 1935 L-4. The 1959 survey wording on Forest Lookouts (14 ft square, wooden, concrete base) fits either account. Current status is thin: Idaho Fire Lookouts says 'Drive-Up Emergency Status' with no date shown; the Idaho Climbing Guide says 'no longer in use' with no date shown. Whether the cab is open to visitors is not stated anywhere read. A web search snippet mentioned an onX listing saying the lookout is no longer manned and an Idaho Statesman item on the road loop; neither was read, so neither is cited. The record's height_m of 3.0 is near a 10-foot base but the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 8 feet; not changed. Recommend a Boise National Forest check on current status, road access and the 1963 house before publishing.

Four short pages agree on a 1932 crow's nest and a 1947 abandonment, and two of them give a second crow's nest about 1.25 miles north. The record says gone, but no source says the structure was removed or destroyed, so a correction to abandoned is proposed for review. The record kind 'platform' is left alone; sources say crow's nest. A different Haystack Mountain in Lemhi County (firelookout.com haystackmtn319, Salmon National Forest) is a separate lookout and was not merged. No staffing, fire or present-day site evidence was found; no photos were found.

Thin and conflicting. The 1924 newspaper items (via the Forest Lookouts page) describe a tower and cottage under construction; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe a 1930s crow's nest. The story states both and does not reconcile them. Record status 'gone' is not supported: FFLA says Abandoned. The FFLA list also has a separate Haystack Mountain in Shoshone County (47.76125, -115.94824), which is not this lookout. Firelookout.com gives elevation 8800 ft; no facts key for elevation, so omitted. The 'drive-in' label is not checked on the ground. No new photos.

Full staffing history is thin in these sources (only one named staffer, Kris Anderson 1983, found clearly). The brief's flagged build-year conflict did not materialize across the three sources checked; could not reach the dead Nez Perce NF link listed in source_pages to check further. No evidence of a rental program; it reads as an actively staffed lookout.

Disputed: the L-4 date (1934 on firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts; 1940 on the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts), the base date (1959 base build vs 1960 completion), and the wilderness name (register: Frank Church neighbour; Keeping Watch: Selway-Bitterroot). Elevation: the register's 8,116 ft (2,474 m) matches the record; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6727′, not used. Access level omitted: drive-up is supported, but no source states public or closed status, so a visitor check is advised. The 2025 staffing rests on one source. The Keeping Watch page says 'Built: 1930', which is the first platform, not the current cab. No source read describes the lookout as burned, moved or abandoned. Record height_m 3.0 is not confirmed; sources give a 10-foot base only. No new photos recorded.

One source gives the full chronology for this tower, and it is a short record. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page for the gone tower returned a 404 in the cache, so it is not cited. Do not merge this record with the standing Hemlock Butte (46.47352, -115.62924, US 767 ID 57). That lookout has a 1921 cupola, a 1934 50-foot pole L-4 and a 1954 tower, and the NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts histories describe it, not this one. No photos or present-day site evidence were found.

The Forest Service page (fs.fed.us, Nez Perce-Clearwater) failed to resolve, so the agency fact rests on the register alone. Height and first-structure dates conflict across sources. The 1948 known staff entry predates the 1954 tower. The register and firelookout.com give an L-4 cab for the 1954 tower; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a flat cab. No current public access rules were found. Keeping Watch (UIdaho) gives only a coordinate and a link, so it is not cited.

The 1934 and 1955 dates agree across firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page (which cites Kresek). The 1934 built event is new; the 1955 destroyed event was already in the record. No source says what remains, who staffed it or how it was destroyed. The 'hike-in' tag is from Idaho Fire Lookouts and the trail was not checked. The L-6 size comes from a Nez Perce National Forest style note, not a Coeur d'Alene source. The story is short because the record is thin.

The record's design L-4 applies only to the 1932 cabin; the current cab is R-6 (correction proposed). The record's kind two_story with height_m 3.0 is left as is: sources describe a 10-foot base under a flat-top cab, so the kind label may need a look. Access level is not set: the only signals are the Hike-In tag and the McCall Life hike description, with no closure or permit information found. The McCall Life feature centers on one staff member's personal experience; the story uses only lookout facts and names no one. Known-staff names on Idaho Fire Lookouts are omitted on purpose.

History is consistent across four sources, and the 1961 date is backed by a Forest Service statement quoted in the climbing guide. Access is upgraded to public from the register's 'Open to public use'. The record's county 'Idaho' is left alone, since it follows the convention used for the other records. Current condition and staffing are not reported after 2012; the climbing guide and firelookout.com pages are undated. Forest: the register says Lolo/Clearwater National Forests and Idaho Fire Lookouts says Lolo / Clearwater National Forest, so they agree. No wilderness designation year is stated in any source, so the story gives only the 'three years' relation. No new photos recorded.

Record kind is platform; the FFLA list types it Crowsnest and the Clearwater list Crow's Nest. Left unchanged because the kind vocabulary is not in view here. Status gone is not supported: the sources say abandoned in 1941 and say nothing about removal. No staffing history on either site page, so staffing is left out. Elevation 4,475 ft is in the Clearwater list and the Idaho page; the record has none.

Construction (1922 tower, 1934 frame cabin) and 1966 destruction agree across the register, firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Open issues: the 1937 Post-Register item (quoted on Forest Lookouts Idaho) says a new station was established, which does not fit the 1922 date; staffing rests on that single 1937 item. Elevation differs by 33 ft between the register and the other two sites. The 2021 register photos are not added to photos because no image URLs were extracted. Forest name spelled Caribou-Targee on the register, Caribou-Targhee on firelookout.com and Carabou-Targhee (typo) on Idaho Fire Lookouts; the record's current spelling follows the register, so no correction proposed. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story's Idaho Fire Lookouts spelling claim was corrected to the Targhee spelling; the 1937 item's date, station and fire details match the Forest Lookouts page, which does not say which station spotted the fires; the footings credit to Samsara Duffey matches the register.

Built 1935 and abandoned 1939 agree across sources. The 1957 dynamite demolition rests on one page (Forest Lookouts). That page also has a 1921 entry 'Replaced Big Rock 62' that is unclear, so it is left out of the story. The record had only the 1939 event; the 1935 built event is new. A Nez Perce National Forest lookout table (fs.usda.gov/media/259204) gives the same 1935 and 1939 dates but was not cited. The hike-in tag is from Idaho Fire Lookouts; the site was not checked. No new photos.

Brief county 'Idaho' matches the Idaho lookout list, so no correction. Elevation 7,260 ft from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The removal date and cause are not stated in any source, so no removal event is recorded. One WebSearch found nothing about this lookout. Site today not described by any source. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 'hike-in' is the only access statement; access level left unset. No photo URL was found, so no photos are listed.

Three sources only; the 1930s crow's nest date is decade-only. The record matches the sources on county, kind, status and the 1958 destruction, so no corrections. Record elevation is null; firelookout.com gives 4,715 ft. Searches for Hill 36 and Ally Point found no other source, and the Clearwater list does not cover St. Joe sites.

Brief record matches the sources: Boundary County, Kaniksu NF, 1937 build, 1958 destruction. The Forest Lookouts Removed status conflicts with destroyed 1958 and is reported as a conflict. One WebSearch found no cause or date beyond the listings, so no cause is written. Staffing names come from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The Idaho Fire Lookouts hike-in note is the only access statement. Confidence medium.

Thin: two site pages and the FFLA list, and two searches found nothing else. No source gives an abandonment year, so the only event is the 1930s crow's nest, recorded with a decade-only year. Record kind is platform; the FFLA list types it Crowsnest. Left unchanged. Record status gone is not supported; the sources say Abandoned.

Brief said destroyed for 1961; sources say destroyed or removed, so the event is recorded as removed with the conflict noted. Brief agency typo corrected. Bonner County and 4,580 ft elevation come from firelookout.com. No staffing is documented by any source, so none is recorded. One WebSearch found no independent source. Only the November 9, 2024 Idaho Fire Lookouts post describes the site today. No photo URLs found.

The dates agree on all four pages, but Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb credit them to Kresek and the other two give no source, so the agreement is less independent than it looks. Only Idaho Fire Lookouts describes the site today (an electronics site); no second source found. No staffing or fire history is sourced; the 1930 event year stands for 'the 1930s'. Gate status is seasonal and undated. Brief record has no errors found.

Story is about 123 words, near the floor of the range, because the sources give only a location, a 1934 pole L-4 tower and a destroyed outcome. No source dates the destruction, so there is no destroyed event. The brief record matches the sources; no corrections. The brief lists access as unknown; I left access out because no source states a public-access level, only the Drive-Up tag. Nothing is said about remains; the Forest Service list has no photo for this site.

Two different Horse Heaven lookouts exist. Idaho County (Nez Perce/Payette NF, this record) and Lemhi County (ground site, Salmon NF, 45.26295, -114.54673). Source 5 and the Lemhi firelookout.com page are about the Lemhi one. The 1934 Ivan Decker staff entry is unresolved: Idaho Fire Lookouts attributes it to the Recorder Herald, but the only Recorder Herald quote we found is on the Salmon NF page. Now in events as an unresolved entry, attributed in the story to Idaho Fire Lookouts; the story says the 1934 name is not settled. The 1932 Biba entry is single-sourced. Location: the brief's Idaho Fire Lookouts coordinates (45.26993, -116.5482) do not appear in the page text we read; the FFLOS point (45.26955, -116.57609) matches firetower.org, about 2 km apart. Not resolved. Photos on firetower.org (cabin, 1930 and 2009) were not captured; no image URLs were extracted.

The brief record (Lemhi County, Salmon National Forest, cabin) is supported by firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts Salmon listing. The brief's coordinates appear in no source we read; by rough arithmetic they fit '32 miles WNW of Salmon', so treat them as unverified. Elevation 8,086 ft appears on this Lemhi listing and on the Idaho County tower alike, so it is not used. The 1934 Decker item is credited by name to a Horse Heaven without a county: Forest Lookouts places it with the Salmon listing, while Idaho Fire Lookouts' West Central page (Payette NF listing, 1929 cabin, 1931 tower, 1950 destroyed) matches the Idaho County register entry but does not name the county. us-id-horse-heaven.md (Idaho County) cites the same item and should be reconciled with this one. No staffing is attributed to this tower. No photos checked.

Construction (1934) and destruction (1978) agree across the three Valley County pages. The 10-foot figure may describe the pole or crib rather than the whole tower, so height_m 3.0 is approximate. Staffing rests on one Krause entry (1956). Sister page us-id-horse-mountain-2.md covers the Adams County tower (US 1434, built 1935) and should not be merged with this one; its staffing names (1939, 1981) do not overlap the Valley County entries. No photos checked. Brief record has no errors found.

Staffing history is thin — only two documented years (1939, 1981) across both sources checked, with a large undocumented gap in between. firelookout.com (not cited, consistent with others) also lists it as built 1935, 30-foot timber tower, staffed every summer, confirming the other two sources without adding new facts.

Story is about 123 words. Three sources agree on the 1938 build and the 1950 abandonment; the Forest Service list gives the 1950s. Height 9.1 m is converted from the 30-foot figure. The brief lists the county as Idaho; the sources give Idaho County. Access is left out because no source gives a public-access level, only the Hike-In tag. No source describes what remains at the site.

Fate date (1983 vs 1985) is unresolved; a newspaper or Forest Service record would settle it. The access note relies on a climbing site (SummitPost) and no Forest Service closure check was made. The site's location is uncertain: two coordinate pairs about 1 km apart, and SummitPost puts the lookout on a summit two miles from the lake. The brief's name has a typo ('SIte'). No new photo with a usable URL was found; the register credits Roger Lord for its photo.

Story is about 133 words. The 1939 entry places the crow's nest on Murray Peak, 1.25 miles northwest; the FFLOS coordinates may mark Murray Peak rather than Horseshoe Peak. Not resolved, so the story does not say which spot the coordinates mark. The brief status gone conflicts with the index's Abandoned; the correction is proposed for editor review. Idaho Historical Aerial Photographs item A1152 (1935) lists Murray Peak as a feature; its rights notice restricts reproduction and its record does not mention a lookout, so no photo is added.

Built year (1938) and L-4 design agree across three sites. The 1939 newspaper item calls the lookout newly constructed, which fits 1938 but reaches us only through the weebly page. Status (standing, abandoned) and access rest on a 2004 NHLR visit report and undated summary pages; no 2025 or 2026 visit was found, so re-check before publication. Staffing as_of is the read date because Discover Sawtooth is undated. No staffing history after 1960 was found beyond 'into the 1970s'. The brief's access value 'unknown' is replaced with restricted. No corrections to the brief's record.

Four sources agree on the 1932 cabin, 1934 tower, 1970 cabin move and 1977 removal. The 6,091 ft elevation appears on Idaho Fire Lookouts (6091') and Willhite (6,091 feet). The Idaho Fire Lookouts tag 'Drive-Up Removed' may mean the lookout is removed rather than the road being closed, so drive_up true rests on Willhite's 'Hiking Distance: Drive-up' line; please check. The footing and parking area come from Willhite's photo captions, which are undated. Access level 'public' is an inference from the trailhead description, not a stated rule. The brief's gone status and tower kind hold; design was null in the record and is filled from firelookout.com. Staffing is not documented by any source and is left out. Used 2 searches and about 5 page reads. Checked 2026-10-10: Willhite's page has no closure wording, so the Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Drive-Up Removed' tag is still unexplained.

Dates, design and agency agree across all four sources. No source describes remains or public access; Idaho Fire Lookouts says hike-in only. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented, so no staffing facts were recorded. Location: the FFLA list coordinates (46.10152, -115.6) match the Idaho Fire Lookouts map pin, so no location conflict.

Three sources agree on the 1930s cabin, 1940 L-4 cab, 1950 abandonment and 2000 burning. The record's 2000 event reads 'destroyed'; all three sources say burned, so the research file uses 'burned'. This is a label choice, so no correction is written. The 'abandoned' staffing status and 'hike-in' (drive_up false) rest on one line each. No source describes the site today. A search snippet from the Lewiston Tribune (page returned 403, not readable here) names the Hot Springs Lookout among structures lost in the Clear Creek fire; it is not cited because the page could not be read, and the fire is not named in the story. Worth checking. Used 2 searches and about 4 page reads. Checked 2026-10-10: the wind sentence now paraphrases the Recorder Herald item without implying a cause. The Lewiston Tribune snippet is still unverified and is not in the story.

Location conflict is unresolved: the FFLA list gives 46.47004, -114.83953, while the Idaho Fire Lookouts map pin (from its category page data) is about 760 m away at 46.4768643, -114.839558. The story gives no coordinates; check before publishing a map pin. Elevation: the Forest Service list gives 5,535 ft (cite 3, the only source with a figure); firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts leave it blank or unknown. The story attributes it to the Forest Service list, and facts.elevation_ft records it. Staffing: no staffing source found.

The sources disagree on the base of the 1968 cab; the story reports all three versions and does not choose one. The 1990 removal date comes from two sources; Forest Lookouts says only Removed. The 1932 and 1938 staff names come from a single Idaho Fire Lookouts page citing The Idaho Statesman; the Statesman itself was not read. The 1932 entry also names a child, which the story and research file leave out. Staffing status is not given as a fact because no source says whether the site is staffed today. No source describes the summit today. Used 1 search and about 5 page reads. Checked 2026-10-10: the cabin is now placed at the lookout site, since no source says it was on the summit; the cab base is reported as the sources differ on construction. The Idaho Statesman itself was not read.

Build and destruction dates agree across all three pages, but the Forest Lookouts Idaho page credits its dates to Kresek and the other two pages do not name a source, so they may not be independent. Only one item, the 1937 Northern Idaho News mention, names a person connected to the lookout, and it is quoted second-hand. No source describes the site today. A search result suggested a possible mix-up with a 1934 L-4 tower at Diamond Peak (Kaniksu NF, Washington); that was not checked. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page shows a photo credit to the Bonner County Historical Society (Chuck Peterson collection) but no image URL was captured, so no photo is added. Brief record: no correction needed.

Built and destroyed dates agree across the three pages. Staffing rests on one page (Idaho Fire Lookouts, 1940 to 1943, George Terrien). The Forest Lookouts Idaho inventory credits its dates to Kresek; the cached page shows only the attribution '(Kresek)'. A search summary said the inventory credits Kresek's book, which the page itself does not spell out, so it is not repeated in the story. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page carries a 'Courtesy: The Fire Lookout Museum' photo credit and firelookout.com a 'Photo courtesy the Fire Lookout Museum' note, but no image URL was captured, so no photo is added. No source describes the site or patrol point today. Brief record: no correction needed.

The 1923, 1930, 1934 and 1964 dates come only from the two lookout-history pages, which list identical dates; the county inventory confirms only the agency and township-range-section code. No staffing history is published, so none is in the story. No source describes the site today. A search result described the agency's later name, Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association (C-PTPA); that page was not read, so the story uses the older name the inventory gives. The 1930 entry is a log cabin, and no source says whether it replaced the 1923 platform. The brief record needs no correction.

Thin record: two history pages, a 1925 newspaper item and a 1927 fire wardens report, both as quoted on the weebly page (the newspaper and report themselves were not read). Nothing describes the site today and no source gives an access level, so facts.access is omitted. The weebly entry shows a 'Removed' label with no date; not used. Location: the brief's three coordinate sets differ by roughly 2 km (FFLA 48.07312/-116.67517 as in the brief; Idaho 48.06249/-116.6959; West US 48.0842/-116.6863); not checked on a map. Do not confuse with two other Huckleberry Mountain lookouts: the Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Huckleberry Mountain Lookout' page without the -2 suffix (Coeur d'Alene NF, 4,865 ft, tower removed 1950) and a Pend Oreille County, Washington Huckleberry Mountain that appeared in search with its own 1925 records. Neither was used.

County Kootenai and status gone confirmed; no corrections to the brief. Removal wording differs across sources (removed vs removed or destroyed). Today's condition rests on one visitor account (willhiteweb.com) that describes tree cover and no remains; no source describes footings or ruins, and public status is not stated. The FFLA 'Relocated' table lists a Summerfield tower as 'Relocated Huckleberry Mtn' (Clearwater County, private). That is a different Huckleberry Mountain, a 1933 L-4 and 1975 R-6 tower per the firelookout.com Calder page in search results, so it does not change this record, but check that the relocation row is not linked here.

Four sources agree on the core story (L-4 pole tower, R-6 replacement, 2013 GSA auction, 2014 removal, ruins on site) and the disagreements are small (1933 vs 1936 first lookout, 1974 vs 1975 R-6 tower, 2013 vs 2014 sale), all reported in the story. Re-erection is unverified: the Idaho Fire Lookouts page points to the owners' Facebook page for the removal and rebuild, which returned only its title when fetched. A Gazette Record article ('Huckleberry makes a move', gazetterecord.com) was returned by search but was HTTP 429 twice and is unread; it may say where the tower stands now. Access: no source gives an access level; only the Drive-Up tag, so facts.access is omitted. Staffing 'as_of 1995' is the end of staffing per FireLookout.com; the Idaho known-staff list runs to 1980 but is not labelled complete. Height 6.1 m is the 20-foot figure converted. No photos added.

Thin record: three list-style history pages with the same facts, plus one land-trust sentence that is the only evidence of what stands today. The sentence does not say what the remains are. The 1946 staffing comes from a Kellogg Evening News item cited by Idaho Fire Lookouts; not read. Access: no source says whether the summit is open to visitors, so facts.access is omitted. A willhiteweb.com Hudlow Mountain hiking page (idaho_lookouts/hudlow_mountain/hayden_lake_055.htm) turned up in search and may describe the summit today; it was not read because of the budget. The brief's 1952 'abandoned' is proposed as 'gone' in corrections; the sources do not say abandoned. Kind 'ground' in the brief is consistent with the FFLA index ('Ground Gone').

Elevation conflict: the register gives 4,189 ft (1,277 m), which matches the record's elevation_m 1276.8, while Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 4248′ (about 1,295 m). Record left as is. height_m is not filled: the register gives a 41-foot wooden tower but not whether that is to the cab floor. Unreconciled: the 1932 newspaper (60-foot poles, under construction) against the about-1933 L-4 date. Staffing as_of 2021 comes from an Idaho Fire Lookouts page dated December 30, 2021; firelookout.com is undated. Access level omitted: 'Hike-In' is supported, but no source states public or closed status. The 1977 newspaper item calls the peak a granite peak, which does not fit a timber tower; the story does not repeat that. No new photos recorded.

All three sources are lookout-history listings, not Forest Service records. The destruction year is 1964 in two sources and 1963 in one; left unresolved in the story. The staff names come from the Idaho Fire Lookouts list, whose 1934 and 1935 entries cite Wallace Press-Times reports we did not read. Nothing describes the site now; a Coeur d'Alene National Forest record or a recent site report would settle what remains.

Thin record: three sources (firelookout.com, the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts) agree on the 1934 build and 1945 abandonment. The Forest Lookouts Idaho County list and the FFLA entry give no build or abandonment date, and none of the sources describes the site today or gives a height. FFLA lists the kind as 2-Story cab; the sources describe an L-4 cab on a log crib without a story count, so two_story is unconfirmed. No staffing is documented (Idaho Fire Lookouts says so). No new photos found.

Camp, cab and abandonment dates agree across three sites. No source says when the cabin came down or what is on the summit now. A YouTube video (watch?v=Hhv1I5VFG0o) turned up in search with a description claiming remains (melted glass, nails, concrete supports) and a later forest-fire burn. The page could not be read here, so that claim is not used. Worth checking against a site report or Kaniksu National Forest records. The CCC photo is marked 'In Copyright - Educational Use Permitted', so it is cited but not added to photos.

Three sources agree on 1934 build and 1971 destruction and on the 20-foot L-4 tower. Location and elevation match the record's coordinates and county. The 1959 staffing rests on one name in two pages that cite the same source. The only account of remains is a single visit post dated November 14, 2024, and no source gives an owner or access level beyond the drive-up tag.

Four sources agree the 1930 platform tower, 1932 L-4 cab and 1934 burning. The FFLA list gives the kind as 2-Story cab. These sources describe a 35-foot platform tower with a living-quarters cab on a log crib, so the record's two_story may fit the cab rather than the observation structure; left for the editor. The name-origin sentence comes from a place-name list in the Clearwater history; the entry does not give a location, so the link to this lookout is inferred from the name, and the story now says so. The Coeur d'Alene record (us-id-idaho-point) is a different tower with the same name: another forest, 6,505 feet, 14 miles ENE of Magee. No new photos found.

Thin record. Three sites agree on a 1930s crow's nest and a 1942 abandonment, and none describes the site after that. No staffing, fire or access-closure sources were found. The brief's two coordinate pairs are about 670 m apart (FFLA 48.57299, -116.06616; Idaho Fire Lookouts 48.56794, -116.07118). The record's 'gone' status is not supported and is proposed as 'unknown'.

Three short listings agree on all dates. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history for this lookout, so no staff are named. No source describes the site today or its condition, and the drive-up tag comes from one listing only. Worth checking against St. Joe National Forest records or a site visit report.

Three sources agree on the c.1927 camp, the 1931 cab and the 1957 destruction. No source gives a cause of destruction, staff names or the site's condition today. The 'Ruins' label on firelookout.com sits next to the Brush Hill patrol tower, so it is not applied to the summit site. Brush Hill may have its own record (us-id-brush-hill, status ruins) to cross-check. The sources do not say whether the 1931 cab stood at ground level, so the 'ground' kind is left as recorded.

The move to Horseshoe Lake is backed by four sites. Hartig's 1981 report is the only dissent. No source describes the original Indian Grave site today, so the 'today' paragraph says so. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the entry 'Drive-Up Moved' without saying which site it means. The Horseshoe Lake end of this history is also covered by us-id-horseshoe-lake, which has its own unresolved 1983 vs 1985 date. The brief's 'gone' status is proposed as 'relocated'.

Fact-check pass 2026-10-04: the original research omitted John Crawford's 1976-2008 staffing stint, which idahofirelookouts.com's known-staff list actually gives in full (1976-2008 Crawford, 2009-2010 Zimmerman, 2011-2013 Gilley, 2014-2015 Anderson, 2022-2024 Crawford again); the story previously implied Crawford's 2022 return was his only tenure. Corrected in both files. The 1929 log-cabin build year on NHLR versus the 1928 cabin/pole-tower date on idahofirelookouts.com may refer to the same construction episode.

Staffing status conflicts across sources; the 2015 end date rests on the NRHP nomination alone. The nomination PDF was read by grep excerpts, not in full. Access 'restricted' is a judgement from drive-up plus an active Forest Service detection site; no visitor policy was found. Do not confuse with the Washington Indian Mountain Lookout (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/wa/indian-mountain-lookout/), a separate tower with a 1953 replacement. Idaho Fire Lookouts' known-staff list is partial and was not used beyond 1942. No photos with a verified URL and licence were found. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the West Mountains line now describes the view from the lookout, not its location; the 2021 staffing post is dated in the story; the off-limits advice was replaced with a sourced statement.

Only 1934 build date is given, by two listings that appear to share a source lineage (firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts both cite a 1934 cabin). No staffing, fire or removal detail found in the sources read. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says it has no documented staffing history, which is not used. Do not merge with the 1934 lookout on Oreana Ridge (dangerousroads.org): that one is at 8,103 ft on FR-067 and is a different site. Record coordinates match the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. No photo found.

Construction year 1922 agrees across firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, the Clearwater NF post and the Montana photo caption. Destruction date and cause are not given anywhere read. Record county 'Idaho' matches the source's 'Idaho County, Idaho'; no correction. Two 1922 photo leads were found but not fetched for image URLs, so no photos entry: Montana History Portal (Bud Moore collection, under construction 1922) and University of Idaho Selway-Bitterroot item sbw106 (Howard R. Flint, 1922, public domain). The Clearwater NF post also speculates about a 1932 ranger trip; that is not used because it is not documented.

Four sources agree on the 1934 tower and the 1950 destruction, and the brief record's 1950 event matches. Added the 1934 build event. Today: an undated WillhiteWeb photo caption (footing almost covered), an undated 'for now' remark on the same page about views and access, and the Idaho Fire Lookouts drive-up tag; no source states public access, so no access key. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 4060 ft; not stored as a fact key. No staffing or fire sources found, so none written. Verification 2026-10-10: the story previously said no source described the site as it is now, which contradicted the caption and 'for now' remark; reworded. All 13 quotes were found on the first run.

Build date of c.1939 agrees across three listings, but structure type conflicts (cabin vs framed tent). Forest Lookouts attributes its 1950s abandonment to a source it names only as Kresek. The 1940 and 1942 station listings come from a silo.tips copy of a Challis NF history compilation; the table layout is hard to read, so it is cited only for the station name appearing in early-1940s tables, not for who staffed it. Idaho Fire Lookouts reports no documented staffing history, which is not contradicted, just not filled in. No photo found.

Verification 2026-10-10: the story had said Idaho has other lookouts called Iron Mountain, which its single footnote does not support; reworded to at least one other. All 11 quotes were found on the first run. Thin record: two site pages and a county list agree on the 1934 build and 1955 loss. Two web searches found nothing further about this site. Do not use these other Iron Mountain sites for this record: firelookout.com/id/ironmtn.html (Camas County, Sawtooth NF, cabin 1961), the NHLR entry above, and the UIdaho Keeping Watch item at 43.538, -115.045. Roman Nose (Boundary County, 1955 L-4 cab, lost 1999) is also a different site. Added the 1934 build event; the brief record's 1955 destroyed matches.

Build year disputed (1919 vs 1923). Do not confuse with the standing Camas County Iron Mountain at 43.53827, -115.04492 (NHLR US 1439, ID 131), or the Curry County, Oregon, site on firetower.org. Brief record matches the listing row (45.96814, -115.54188, Ground, Gone). No source found describes the site today. Access level not set: only the drive-up label is documented.

idahofirelookouts.com has no documented staffing history for this lookout; the Weebly site supplied strong newspaper-sourced staffing detail instead. No current rental or regular staffing was found; status_note reflects firelookout.com's 'available for emergencies' description, which may be dated.

Verification 2026-10-10: the story now says the UIdaho photo was matched to this lookout by its title. The UIdaho photo's own coordinates (45.80014, -115.430217) are about 20 km north of the brief's 45.627, -115.382, so the photo-to-lookout link is unconfirmed by location. All 16 quotes were found on the first run. Conflicts left open in the story: the 1931 tower (60-foot wooden with 7x7 cab per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; 90-foot steel per Forest Lookouts) and the timeline (UIdaho photo dated approximately 1951 showing the tower down, against a 1953 replacement and 1972 removal). Brief coordinates 45.627, -115.382 were not checked against Elk City; the UIdaho photo says 14 miles SSE. Brief record had no events; added from these sources. The existing brief photo (idahofirelookouts jackmtn1) is not repeated. Staffer name is as printed by Idaho Fire Lookouts and not verified further.

Idaho Fire Lookouts spells the name Jacknife; the record and the other sources use Jackknife. Do not confuse with the Lakeview Lookout, a separate page on idahofirelookouts.com (1931 L-4 on a 40-ft pole tower, destroyed 1956). A USFS Idaho Panhandle NF social post (facebook.com/USFSIPNF) shows a circa-1932 photo of this tower; not cited because it is a social post, but it is a photo lead. Brief record matches the listing row. No source found describes the site today.

Dates (1928 patrol point, 1932 cab, 1948 last staffed, 1949 abandoned, 2020 NHLR) agree across sources. Thin points: the Forest Lookouts page is an unsigned compilation, and the 2019 condition report is one visitor's report. Access 'public' is a judgement: no closure or permission found, but the site is hike-in with no trail. No notable fires were found in the sources read. Do not confuse with a Facebook post for a 1932 L-4 cab 27 miles north of Weiser, Washington County, elevation 7589 ft, which is a different tower. firelookout.com credits photos to Shawn Ogden and Luke Channer, but no URL or licence was found, so no photos are listed. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the condition findings now have evidence quotes from the NHLR form fields; the distance and the advice not to climb are sourced or marked as our judgement.

Two detailed pages plus the FFLA list; the dates agree across them. No source describes the site today. Neither page names the managing forest, so agency is left out. A web search returned a Jackson Mountain lookout in Pend Oreille County, Washington (willhiteweb.com, lookout 189); it is a different site and is not used. The header reads R.I.P. 1929-?, which is not a conflict with the 1935 abandonment.

The 1927 quote comes from the Forest Lookouts transcription of the Idaho Statesman, not the paper itself. Staffing as of 2020 is from the register, and Idaho Fire Lookouts names a 2025 staffer. The register and firelookout.com disagree on whether the current structure is one or two stories. The record height of 3.0 m is the 10-foot concrete base, not a tower height.

Separate from us-id-jackson-peak (standing 1927 cabin at 44.07793, -115.41386, about 30 km northeast); do not merge. Brief record matches the ground/gone listing row at 44.00975, -115.77652. No source gives a date for abandonment or removal, and no source describes the site today. Staffing is undocumented per Idaho Fire Lookouts.

The 1932 build date is 'about' or 'c.1932' on three sites; Rex's page attributes the date to Kresek, a source not checked. The L-6 vs L4 design disagrees and is flagged in the story. The 1936 road item is dated August 20, 1936 on Rex's page (a Newport Miner item as quoted there); the newspaper itself was not seen. The 1960s destruction has no year in any source, so no destroyed or removed event is dated. No staffing or fire history was found, so none is written. The idahofirelookouts photo (jaspermtn1933, credit Fire Lookout Museum) has no stated licence and is not added. Access 'restricted' rests on the gated road in one 2022 trip report. Brief record matches: status gone, height 15.2 m (50 ft), design L-6, agency Kaniksu National Forest.

Two detailed pages agree on the 1930 build and the 1950 destruction; the FFLA list agrees on Tower Gone. No independent source was found, and a second web search turned up nothing on Jay Peak. A Sand Mountain lookout in Oregon in the results is a different site and is not used. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no documented staffing history, so no staffing is recorded. Neither source gives a cause for the 1950 destruction.

Fate is solid: four sources say it burned in 2015, and the FFLA list says Tower Gone. Construction is less certain. Two sites give 1929 for the cabin and crow's nest, and a 1928 newspaper item quoted on Forest Lookouts names 'Jay peak' among new Lolo forest structures without naming this site; the story uses 1929 and flags the item. The 1955 tower date is from three sources. Nothing found on what remains at the site or whether it is open to visitors, so access is omitted. Staff names are left out on purpose. Brief record checked: status gone, design L-4, 12.5 m (41 ft) and Clearwater NF all agree with sources. The brief's county 'Idaho' was not checked against a source and was left alone.

Three sources only. Sources 1 and 2 agree on 1920, 1932 and 1965 but are short; source 3 is a compiled set of quotes from Potlatch annual reports, The Timberman and the Elk River Sentinel, which I read only as quoted on that page. The 1915 reference to 'the Jericho lookout' may describe an earlier structure, and the record does not say what it was. Land ownership and current access rules were not found; the site is not described as public or private anywhere I read. The brief record's kind 'tower' is accurate for the 1932-1965 structure but the site began as a tree platform. A web search turned up a Jericho Tower climbing page, which is a different feature and was not used. No photographs with direct image URLs were found.

Core dates (built 1934, destroyed 1972) and the 40-foot L-4 design agree across three sources. The distance from Powell and the 30-foot caption in source 5 conflict and are reported, not resolved. The photo caption in source 5 is hedged; I did not treat it as firm evidence of this lookout's location or of current drive access. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so no staffing fact is recorded. A Montana History Portal audio record (node 65775) describes fires of 1929 and 1934 near the Jerry Johnson trail; it does not describe the lookout, so it is not used. The Montana photo may be a candidate for a photo entry, but I did not have a direct image URL and its copyright status is 'In Copyright', so none is recorded. Land ownership and current access rules were not found.

Two detailed pages plus three University of Idaho photo records. No source names the 1992 fire, and the search turned up no name. The 1992 event is recorded as burned, matching both pages. The 1930 and 1933 dates come from catalogue metadata. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists drive-up for a site where the structures burned; a human may want to check current access with the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests before any visit is suggested.

Thin sources: the two lookout-history pages repeat the same dates, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association table only confirms the tower is gone. County conflict left unresolved: firelookout.com says Boundary County, while the FFLA table and our record say Bonner. Elevation 6,371 ft (about 1,942 m) is in firelookout.com but elevation_m is empty in the record. Staffing is one name for 1933 and is not dated as first or last. The L-4 design background comes from the University of Idaho Keeping Watch page, not from a Jeru-specific source. Two searches found no other source, and no photo. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 'Hike-in' tag is historical access only; no visit facts were written. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 1934 and 1955 dates are now also quoted from Idaho Fire Lookouts (cite 2). The story's L-4 sentence paraphrases Keeping Watch instead of repeating its wording.
