The abandonment year is the main open question: 1967 (firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts citing Kresek) against 1942 in the Nez Perce NF list. The table layout puts '1942' twice in that row, once beside 'abandoned' and once in what looks like the photo column, so I could not be sure which is the abandonment date. The 1914 station and the 1939 platform may or may not be the same structure; the sources do not say, so the story presents them as separate entries. Forest Lookouts' Idaho County (M-W) page mentions a 1939 100-foot steel tower built by the Nezperce NF on a mountain I could not identify; it is not this site and is not used. No staffing history, access rules, or current description of the site was found. No photographs with direct image URLs were found.

The CTPA expansion in the story is inferred, not stated by either lookout page: it is most likely the Clearwater Timber Protective Association, one of two predecessors that merged in 1966. Cited the cptpa.com home page because its About text is there; a more specific About URL was not located. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no documented staffing, so none is written. 'Drive-Up' tag on a destroyed site is included but flagged in the story. 'Patrol point 2 miles northwest' meaning is unclear and is stated as listed. Elevation 4,218 ft is in both pages but elevation_m is empty in the record. The record had no events before this run. No photo with a usable licence was found. Fact-check 2026-10-10: predecessor and merged-body names now match cptpa.com (Potlatch Timber Protective Association; Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association). The 1923 sentence now carries its cite. The story now flags the drive-up tag as possibly out of date for a destroyed site. The CTPA expansion is stated as an unconfirmed inference.

Thin sources: three pages agree on 1934 and 1947, but none says why the cab was built or abandoned, and neither lookout page documents any staffing, so none is written. Distance: firelookout.com and the Forest Service list both give 20 miles east of Pierce (the list's 'SE of Pierce' rows belong to other lookouts). The Forest Service list was compiled June 2016 and its header cites firelookout.com among its sources, so it is not independent of firelookout.com. Record coordinates were not checked against the legal description. The record's kind 'ground' is not contradicted; the sources say only 'L-4 cab' and 'cabin'. No photo was found. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 1934 and 1947 dates are now also quoted from Idaho Fire Lookouts (cite 2).

Thin record. All three guides give c.1937 and 1955; the Forest Lookouts page credits its dates to Kresek and the other two appear to repeat them. Record access 'unknown' left as is: no source describes access, so no facts.access was added. No source names anyone who staffed it (Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history), so staffing is omitted from the story. Record height 12.2 m matches the 40-foot pole. No photo found; no source describes the site today.

Brief kind tower fits the 1939 L-4 tower, but the site first had a log cabin and a platform. All four sources are derivative of the same lookout databases, so independent confirmation is thin. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so the story omits staff. No source describes the site today; the story says so. Access is hike-in per Idaho Fire Lookouts, not verified on the ground.

Only three pages were read. The Clearwater Story PDF (foresthistory.org) and the NFSL history PDF were grepped for Junction Mountain: the NFSL file had no match, and the Clearwater Story matches are for the Junction Mountain landform and a 1907 survey, not the lookout. Staffing is undocumented in every source found, so a staffing history would need the Kelly Creek ranger district or Clearwater NF records. The 1955 date is the register's Built field; the 1931 date comes from the register's description and firelookout.com. Current status rests on 2014 register photos and a 2025 summary with no later visit. height_m 16.2 converts the register's 53 ft. No access level is set because no source says whether the cabin is open or closed.

Three short records agree that an L-4 tower stood in the 1930s and is now abandoned and gone. The decade is the only build date in the sources, so no year-stamped event is listed. No staffing record was found. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says it has no documented staffing and is not cited for that. A different Jungle Point (firelookout.com junglepoint.html: Nez Perce National Forest, 1930 camp, abandoned 1942, 5851 ft) is a separate site and must not be merged with this record. The record county 'Idaho' is the short form of Idaho County. No photos or present-day site evidence were found.

Location check needed. The record's point (46.20038, -115.68538) is about 10 km south of the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Idaho list entry for this tower (46.28971, -115.67174). The record's point was taken from the Idaho Fire Lookouts page, which has no coordinates of its own. Please check the pin. Dates are only given as the 1930s, so no year-level events are recorded. No source documents staffing, so the story has no staffing paragraph. The record currently links the Nez Perce camp page as if it were this tower; see corrections.

Four pages and one climbing guide were read. The register's Built 1935 and the 60-ft figure agree across three sources, and the 70-ft figure is a single quotation of a 1982 book, so treat it as disputed. The staffing record is built from newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts site, not from the newspapers themselves; the 1932 item predates the 1935 steel tower and is the earliest staffing shown here. Abandonment has no date in any source, so no event is recorded for it. Access is set to public from drive-up wording and the absence of any closure notice, not from a Forest Service statement. height_m 18.3 converts the register's 60 ft. The brief's record had no errors to correct. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Boise National Forest label appears to be an error. The Salmon-Challis Facebook post surfaced in search but its text was not read, so the naming of Jules Renaud is not used.

Brief status gone is not supported: the state list says Crowsnest Abandoned and Idaho Fire Lookouts says Abandoned, so the story says abandoned. Elevation conflicts (6,814 vs 5,814 feet). The 1927 staffing and photo predate the 1929 build date, which the story flags. Brief coordinates 48.993, -116.91826 come from the state list, but the University of Idaho photo is geotagged 48.702786, -116.920667 and firelookout.com places the site 13 miles north of Upper Priest Lake; the coordinates need checking before publication. No photo was added because no image URL was captured. No source describes what remains today.

Two guides agree on the 1932 build and 1962 destruction, and a 1962 Sandpoint News Bulletin story reprinted by Forest Lookouts describes the demolition of six lookouts, Katka Peak among them. The 1962 story says the six were built in the 1930s by the CCC; that matches 1932 but does not name Katka Peak's year. Record gave no design or height; design added from the guides, height not added because '10-foot pole' is ambiguous (the sources do not say whether it is the total height). Staffing names are the only ones listed in the sources. No photo found; no source describes the site today.

Record events list 1934 built; that matches the original tower, and the standing structure is the 1997 replica on the same footings, so a 1997 rebuilt event was added rather than changing the built year. Record height 6.1 m matches the original 20-foot pole; no source gives the replica's height, so height_m was not added to facts. Sources conflict on the original year (1934 vs 1935) and on staffing (Idaho Fire Lookouts says not staffed in recent years; willhiteweb says volunteers have staffed it). Trail length: 1.85 miles one way (Silver Mountain) vs 2 miles one-way (willhiteweb). Record access is not in the record; facts.access is public via the paid gondola. No photo added. Not visited.

Built 1934 and destroyed 1950 agree across four sources, and the visitor's page is independent of the databases. The 1943 Jardine staffing conflicts in place with the Forest Lookouts quote about Coeur d'Alene mountain, so the story reports both. The firelookout.com Initial Peak entry uses identical wording (1934 30' pole L-4 tower, destroyed 1950), so one of the two may be a copy; check before publication. The visitor's site page is undated, so the footings and view description may not reflect current conditions. No source gives a cause for the 1950 destruction.

This is the Idaho County Kelly Mountain (45.42264, -116.11289). Do not merge it with us-id-kelly-mountain, which is the Kootenai County site near Coeur d'Alene with its own 1934 pole tower story. Sources date the platform to 1930 and the tower to 1938, and agree on the 1958 destruction. No source names staff for this site, so the story has no staffing paragraph. No source describes the site today. The drive-up label is Idaho Fire Lookouts' own; no source states an access level, so access is omitted.

Four sources. The 1936 build year and the fire agree across all three history sites, and the Forest Service list (compiled June 2016) is the official-style record. Brief's status 'gone' is confirmed; brief's access 'unknown' is kept, so no access level is set. No staffing history found: Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history for this lookout, so staffing is left out. No source describes what remains at the site today. Height_m is converted from the 90-foot tower height (27.4 m). Brief coordinates match firelookout.org exactly (46.71996, -114.8751). No corrections to the brief's record. Visit.climbable was dropped: no source says whether the site can be climbed. The sources give 'Kelly Creek R.S.'; 'Ranger Station' is the usual expansion of that abbreviation and is not quoted.

Idaho Fire Lookouts (southern-idaho page) agrees on the 1937 cab, the 1975 new cab and the 2003 loss, but was not quoted because its page text has special characters. A 1940 Forest Lookouts item about Baldy Butte near Paul is a different site and was left out. The 1950 NGS description covers the house only and does not say what survives. Keeper names from firelookout.com's longer 1945-1970 list were not used beyond the three quoted from Forest Lookouts.

Brief's 1950 destroyed year is not in either source; both give the 1950s (see corrections). The destroyed event is left out of events until the schema accepts a decade-only event. Staffing names come from the Idaho list, which cites Wallace Press-Times items that were not checked. The antenna system is unidentified; a reader comment on the Idaho page links it to the 1980s and is not used. No image URL was captured; firelookout.com credits a photo to Abe Turley but gives no file.

No staffing history: Idaho Fire Lookouts says none is documented, so staffing is left out of the story. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1945 National Geodetic Survey station description that mentions a lookout house corner; its record is marked Removed and does not describe what survives, so it is not used. The Forest Service page is the public listing for the site; the spur road is rough.

Two web searches for the site today (Lake Mountain Salmon radio; Lake Mountain lookout site) returned no current description, so the today section is a gap. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 1918, 1928 and 1974 lines use en dashes and were not quoted. Record kind is two_story; the 1938 item describes an eight-foot log base with a walk-around platform, which does not settle the storey count, so the record was not changed.

The 1924, 1928, 1931 and 1956 dates agree across three pages, but the Forest Lookouts page credits them to one history (Kresek), so they are not independent checks. No source describes the site today, and no access, staffing or visit information was found. Height correction: the record's 6.1 m matches the 1928 platform, not the 40-foot pole of 1931. The record's coordinates match the FFLA list. The separate Wabaningo site is us-id-lakeview-wabaningo.

Dates are decades only: a 1930s platform and a 1950s abandonment. The record's event years (1930 and 1950) are the start of each decade, not sourced years. Coordinates conflict in the record: FFLA 48.60573, -116.93708 vs Idaho Fire Lookouts 48.60531, -116.94938, about 900 m apart. No source read settles which is right, so the record location is unchanged. Staffing, access and the current site are not documented in the sources read. Height 6.1 m is taken from the 20-foot platform. The Forest Lookouts page for this site is titled Lakeview, not Lakeview (Wabaningo).

Brief had no events; 1933 build added from three sources. No source dates the abandonment, so no abandoned event is recorded. Sources 1 and 3 both trace to Ray Kresek's book per the Forest Service list header, so they are not fully independent. Elevation: the three lookout sources give 5,539 ft; search snippets for the summit give 5,542 to 5,548 ft (not read in full), and the story uses the lookout figure. The brief coordinates (46.53931, -115.52759) look far east of Pierce for a 13-mile ENE distance by a rough check; verify the pin on a map before relying on it. Staffing: the Idaho page says none is documented, so nothing is written on staffing.

Only two detailed sources, both giving 1934 build and 1955 destruction. The burnt remark is the visiting writers' impression, so the story says the tower appeared to have burned. No staffing source exists; the Idaho page says none is documented. The brief coordinates (48.01733, -116.27380) should be checked against the firelookout.com location (10 miles SSW of Clark Fork) on a map; by a rough check they look closer to Clark Fork than that. No image URL captured. Neither page defines the term alidade, so the story no longer glosses it; add a sourced definition if the term needs one.

Built year is 1930 from the Forest Service list; the websites say 1930s. No source gives a reason for the 1960 removal. Access is marked public from National Forest land and the hike-in tag; no source says so directly. No staffing history in any source. No new photos found.

Thin record: one 1925 date and one 'Gone' entry for 1949, repeated across pages that share one history (the Forest Lookouts page credits Kresek). The sources do not say whether the 1949 loss was removal, fire or collapse, so that event is typed 'other'. No fire, staffing, access or current-site information was found. Elevation 7,882 ft appears on two pages. The record's coordinates match the FFLA list. The Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Hike-In' label is attributed in the story, not turned into a visit fact.

Three of the four listings agree on 1934 and 1963. The 1931 fire and the lookout it names come only from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes the Twin Falls Daily News; I did not check the newspaper itself. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so the story leaves staffing out. Today: no source describes the site now, and none gives access. The record's status gone, kind tower and agency match the sources. Facts height_m 12.2 is 40 feet converted; elevation 5,078 ft is in the story but is not a facts key. No new photos. The Forest Service list has a 'None' photo count for this lookout.

No year for the platform beyond the 1930s, so no built event is recorded. The 'Sheepeater LO' reference is taken as the Sheepeater lookout; the Sheepeater build dates conflict between the NHLR entry (1957 L-4 ground house) and Idaho Fire Lookouts (1934 L-4 cab), and that conflict is not used here. Access is marked public from wilderness land and the hike-in tag; no source says so directly. No photos found.

The 1934 and 1962 dates appear on three listings that cite each other's Kresek source. The 1967 staffer comes only from Idaho Fire Lookouts (citing the Kellogg Evening News); I did not check the newspaper. Forest name is in conflict (see resolved_conflicts). The Forest Service trail page is the only source that describes the site today: it reaches the old lookout site on foot, but it does not describe what remains. Ron Kemnow's page has a 'Removed' label with no date; it is not used. Access level 'public' rests on a Forest Service trail that accesses the site; the trail page gives no closure. No new photos. The record's height_m 3.0 is a correction, since it matches the base, not the tower.

Watchman spelling (Gwilliams on firelookout.com, Williams on idahofirelookouts.com) is unresolved. The newest source is the 2020 Register entry, so current staffing and condition are unconfirmed. The brief's height_m of 3.0 is dropped from facts pending editor sign-off. No photos added.

Both sources agree on the 1934 build and 1951 destruction. No staffing history in either source. Access is marked public from National Forest land and the drive-up tag; no source says so directly. Height 15.2 m is 50 feet converted, and the sources give no separate total height. No new photos; the existing record photo is from idahofirelookouts.com.

Thin record: three listings and no primary source. Ron Kemnow's page credits its dates to Ray Kresek; the other two do not say where theirs come from. I found no Kaniksu National Forest list for this lookout. Status is unresolved: the 'still there' remark on firelookout.com is undated. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says no documented staffing history, so the story leaves staffing out. Access beyond 'hike-in' is not established. No new photos. The corrections (kind platform to tower, 1940 to 1940s, status gone to unknown) need a check before they are applied.

Height: the record's 21.3 m (70 ft) conflicts with 80 ft in three sources; the 70-ft figure matches a 1933 tower at the Little Lightning creek station that the sources do not link to this peak. Record's 1953 'abandoned' is only 'Gone' in the sources, so it is recorded as other. Staffer name is spelled as the Idaho site prints it (Garreth Rouse); not checked against the 1949 Herald. One web search found no independent source for this tower. No site-today source found.

Destroyed year conflicts: 1960 (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) vs 1963 (Forest Lookouts, citing Kresek). Recorded 1960 with the variant in the note; a human should check Kresek's text. The archive caption places a lookout on the peak in 1957 but does not establish which cab it was. No staffing sources found. The record's existing photo is the same archive image; the archive rights statement reads In Copyright - Educational Use Permitted, so it is not free to reuse. Record had no events; design and events added.

Height disputed (25 vs 30 ft) and the 1955 fate is worded differently across sources; the story reports both. Staffing names come from Idaho Fire Lookouts' citations to Wallace Press-Times and Kellogg Evening News; the newspapers were not read directly. Idaho Fire Lookouts' header says Destroyed while its history says Removed; the story follows the history. The 1953 picnic-area plan is from the Weebly page's quotation of the Spokesman-Review; no source says whether a picnic area exists today. The existing 1938 photo in the record (idahofirelookouts.com) is kept; no new photos added. Correction (2026-10-10): Idaho Fire Lookouts lists George Adams for 1937 and George D Howard for 1946. An earlier draft put Howard in 1937; the record and story were corrected.

County: sources disagree. The record, the FFLA list and firelookout.com say Shoshone; the Forest Lookouts page says Benewah. The story now says the county is disputed. Correction proposed, not applied; check against county GIS. Dates 1935 and 1965 agree across pages. No staffing, no photo, and no site-today source found. One web search returned nothing about this tower.

Removal versus burning in 1950 is unresolved: the story reports the removal wording from firelookout.com and the either-or wording from Idaho Fire Lookouts. Elevation conflicts (4344 vs 5558 ft); 5558 ft also appears on the Little Baldy pages, so one of them may be a copy error. The story gives no elevation. The Thomas Hill platform is a separate site with its own record; only its footings and status are described here. Staffing is one name (John Gunn, 1944) from two sites; the Kellogg Evening News was not read directly. No access level is recorded because no source says whether the ground is open to the public. Correction (2026-10-10): the 1934 build year and the 1950 year on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page are now quoted with their years; the Thomas Hill 1934 build date comes from its own page (cite 4).

Timeline (camp 1920, cabin 1922, tower 1940, destroyed 1970) agrees across firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Weebly list. No source describes what remains on the site, so the story says so. The Witt names come from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; the Idaho page gives the name as Joe A Witt with no citation. Two other records named Little Baldy exist in data/towers/id (us-id-little-baldy-2 and -3, both gone); they may be duplicates to check. A different Little Baldy in Idaho County (firelookout.com/id/littlebaldy.html, Nez Perce National Forest) is a separate tower and was not used. Elevation 5558 ft appears on both pages, but the Linfor Hill page shows the same figure, so it was not used.

This is the Idaho County Little Baldy (45.93654, -115.68354). Do not merge it with us-id-little-baldy: Idaho Fire Lookouts' cda-region Little Baldy is a different site (1920 camp, 1940 20-foot pole L-4 tower on West point, destroyed 1970), and the Fire Lookout Association lists a Shoshone County Little Baldy as well. A Forest Lookouts (weebly) page for Little Baldy describes a 1930s tent camp; I did not confirm whether it is this site, so it is left out. The Nez Perce list's Status column reads 'abandoned' with 1950 on the row's second line (read from the PDF table layout); the 1940s entry is in its Photos column, so it is not the abandonment date. The 1950 date conflicts with the 1959 standing and 1963 gone in the other two sources. The story reports both and does not choose between them; the editor should check the PDF row. No source gives staffing for this site.

Dates disagree: built 1933 (Forest Lookouts, WillhiteWeb), 1934 (Idaho Fire Lookouts), 1935 (firelookout.com); destroyed 1961 (two 1961 newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts, WillhiteWeb) vs 1963 (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts). Forest name also disagrees (Kaniksu vs Coeur d'Alene); the record keeps Kaniksu. An undated WillhiteWeb photo caption says the summit has many towers, but no source names them or says whether the microwave station remains. Nothing says whether the summit is public. The HOA site is cited only for context on private homesites on the slope. No photos of the lookout found. Built event added to the record.

All three sites agree on 1934 and 1960. The Forest Lookouts entry cites Ray Kresek; the other two sites may draw on the same material, so treat them as one line of evidence. No staffing or access sources found. The Fire Lookout Museum photo credit on firelookout.com has no image URL captured. Record's 1960 destroyed event matches; 1934 built event added.

Forest Lookouts cites 'Potatch TPA combined Annual Report 1953-54'; Potatch is probably Potlatch but is unverified, so the story does not name it. The firelookout.com cabin observation is undated. The University of Idaho Keeping Watch record gives coordinates and a link only, so it is not cited. No Forest Service records or photos found.

Minor year conflict (1956 vs 1957) for the current cabin's construction, noted in the story and resolved_conflicts. Staff list on idahofirelookouts.com is extensive; only representative names used in the narrative to keep prose readable. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the 'nine miles north of Shoshone Camp' and '1 mile northwest' distance details were cited only to single sources in the draft though confirmed on additional sources (idahofirelookouts and recreation.gov both give the 9-mile figure; firelookout.com gives the 1-mile figure); the 1956/1957 build-year sentence was missing its NHLR (cite 1) footnote even though NHLR is the source of the 1956 date and dimensions. All three citation gaps fixed in the story.

The three sites agree on the 1924 camp, the 1930 cabin and the 1953 destruction, but none is a primary record and none gives a cause. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site Drive-Up; that may describe the historic approach, and no source says whether a road reaches the site now, so no access level is recorded. The brief's county field reads Shoshone/ Mineral (MT); the sources list both. The Weebly page has a staff name only on Idaho Fire Lookouts. Elevation 7,052 ft is recorded in the story only.

Core history agrees across sources: built about 1930 to 1933, decommissioned in the 1960s, restored by volunteers, burned 3 Sept 2016. Open points: (1) restoration start is 1987 in the register and the 1989 item but 1988 in the Spokesman-Review; (2) elevation is 6,590 ft (2,009 m) in the register, matching the record's 2008.6 m, but 6829 ft on firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com; (3) a 1983 Weebly item about a 'Little Snowy Lookout Tower' donated to Priest River may or may not concern this cabin; (4) the 'public' access level is inferred from the trail and the lack of any closure notice, not from a current access statement; (5) staff names come only from a fan site. The record's status and kind look correct; no correction proposed. The register calls the 2016 structure a tower in one line, which we treat as a register wording issue.

Elevation and forest name differ between sources (see resolved_conflicts). The 1957, 1958 and 1988 items are newspaper excerpts transcribed on a fan site, not checked against the original papers. Staffing is only partly known. No source describes what remains at the site today, and the 2011 salvage does not say whether any structure stands. No photo with a usable URL was found.

Tower fate conflicts and is not resolved: Idaho Fire Lookouts says removed (date unknown), the Forest Service list says in ruins, and firelookout.com and the FFLA list say gone. The 1929 cabin is described as standing by both Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com. The 30-foot height is left out of facts because no source says it is the height to the cab floor. No staff names in any source; only the 1950s emergency use is recorded. Drive-up is taken from the Idaho site's tag only. Two commercial camping listings date the cabin to the 1930s and say lookout guards used it; not used. Record elevation 1858.7 m matches the 6098 ft given by Idaho Fire Lookouts.

Gone; location, cab design and 1931 cab date agree across four sources. Date conflicts are reported in the story: the cab is 1931 in three sources but the Facebook copy says the lookout was built in 1930; burning is early 1950s in the Forest Lookouts copy of Hartig and 1953 in the Facebook copy. The brief's height_m 19.8 equals 65 feet, the tree-top crow's nest, so it is proposed for removal. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to the public, so access is omitted. The Facebook post repeats Hartig's 1981 history and is the only source for 1953 and the 1930 build date. The 1940s abandonment date is consistent with the 1941 last season. About 7 page reads and 1 WebSearch, slightly over the per-tower read budget, because the PDF and Facebook copies were needed to settle the dates.

Gone per the FFLA list, but the fate conflicts across three sources (standing 1983, disposed of by burning 1966, burned 1999) and the story reports the disagreement without choosing. Build year is 1933 in two sources and 1932 in Forest Lookouts. A Payette National Forest Facebook post seen only in a search snippet dates construction to 1931 and says the lookout was about 13 miles south of Riggins; the fetch returned a login wall, so it is not cited and needs a look by a reviewer with access. No source describes the site now or public access, so access is omitted. Reads: three lookout pages and the FFLA list, plus one WebSearch; the Payette post was not readable.

All four Idaho and Forest Service sources agree on the 1933 tower and the 1950 abandonment; firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the FFLA list all say gone. Nothing describes what, if anything, remains on the site or whether it is reachable. The drive-up tag ('Drive-Up Abandoned') is from Idaho Fire Lookouts only; it is recorded in facts as visit.drive_up and does not say whether the public may visit. Elevation is 4761 ft (about 1451 m) per two sources; the record's elevation_m is null, so a human may add it. The record's agency is null; the facts take Nez Perce National Forest from firelookout.com. No staffing in any source.

Thin record: no dated events, only the 1930s cabin and the word abandoned on two pages. The FFLA list says gone, which is the basis for the brief's status; the detail pages do not say it was removed, so the story says so. Forest Lookouts quotes a 1930s date attributed to 'Kresek', which the story leaves unidentified. Forest Lookouts also includes a 1959 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description (Yellow Pine horse pack route) for a marker on the same peak; it is not used because it describes a survey station, not the lookout site. No source describes the site now or public access, so access is omitted. Staffing is unknown; Idaho Fire Lookouts reports no documented history. Reads: three lookout pages plus the FFLA list, and two WebSearches.

Two conflicts are not resolved. (1) Design and date: firelookout.com and the Forest Service list give a 1935 L-4 cab on a log crib; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a 1935 camp. Both are reported. (2) Status and kind: the FFLA list says two-story cab and gone, firelookout.com and the Forest Service list say ruins; the status correction (gone to ruins) is for human review. (3) Location: the record (FFLA) has 46.38274, -115.69049, while another Idaho list in our cache has 46.35784, -115.70049. The township, range and section (35N, 6E, sec 10) and firelookout.com's 'nine miles southeast of Pierce' should be checked against the map point before trusting it. Elevation is given as unknown ('?') by firelookout.com, so none is recorded. No staffing in any source.

Built year disputed: 1934 (Nez Perce list, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, Kresek via Forest Lookouts) versus an undated 1932 inventory that gives an L-4 cab. Story uses 1934 and reports both. No staffing or fire sources found. No source found describing the site today or public access. Record county and agency corrected above.

Two coordinate points conflict: the record uses the FFLA point 48.07989, -116.71415; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 48.07657, -116.70825. Not resolved here. Staffing: a firelookout.com line that the tower 'had not been staffed for several years' was left out as ambiguous against the 1967 hire. A 1960 Weebly item calls the station the area's one surviving manned lookout and mentions a 'forest service lookout', which conflicts with the state agency; not used. The present-day tower is covered by us-wa-long-mountain-at-dave-kresek, which already exists. No source describes the Long Mountain site today.

Fact-check pass 2026-10-04: the original research under-cited idahofirelookouts.com's known-staff list, crediting Alexia Cochrane only as unspecified 'relief' staffing and omitting Chester "Chip" Beaty, Jeanne Kellar Beaty (1949-1950, and the 1953 book "The Lookout Wife" about Jeanne's time there), and Margie Cook (1974). The full list is now in events/evidence and the story names them. The 1920 Frank Hall newspaper accounts are strong evidence for an early lookout presence predating the first built structure by three years, worth flagging if the record's earliest date needs revision.

Staffing history is undocumented across all consulted sources; story omits a staffing section rather than guessing. Minor height discrepancy (55 ft vs 53 ft) noted but not resolved — no source explains it.

Two sources agree on the 1934 build, the 1970 abandonment and the gone status. The 1925 staff entry predates the 1934 build and is flagged in the story. Access is not stated in either source, so access is omitted rather than set. A search for this name also returned sah-archipedia.org (ID-01-021-0030; fetch returned 403) and a Southern Idaho Lookout Mountain Lookout; both are different lookouts and were not used. No new photos found.

Move year conflicts: 1975 on the Lookout Mountain pages versus 1976 on the Sheepeater pages and in the register. Elevation is 8680 ft on firelookout.com and 8669 ft on Idaho Fire Lookouts; not used in facts. A Payette NF Facebook post seen only in search results gives 1957 for the steel replacement; not read in full, so not used. No staffing or fire sources were found for the original site. Original site access and remains not described by any source read.

Current status is unclear. Idaho Fire Lookouts says a restoration was planned for 2026 and an L-4 cab is set for replacement in 2025/26, which conflicts with its own 2019 dismantling entry. The SAH Archipedia and Library of Congress pages returned 403 and were not used. SummitPost is out of date (says a 1977 tower is still used). The register's visit report dates to 2006. The record's L-4 design and 15.2 m height describe the 1939 pole tower, not the standing cupola.

The 1933 build year and the 1985-89 save-and-restore story agree across NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Elevation and forest name conflict across sources (see resolved_conflicts). Wikipedia's CCC claim is unconfirmed by the register or the other lists; check Wikipedia's refs before adding it. Do not confuse with other Lookout Mountain towers: Idaho Fire Lookouts' west-central 'Lookout Mountain Lookout' (1933 14x14 log cabin, moved 1975) and its northern-Idaho Lookout Mountain are different sites. The trail is a difficult hike and the summit is a lightning hazard; the cab itself is on emergency status. No notable fires were found in the sources read. NHLR photos (courtesy Luke Channer) have no licence shown, so none are listed. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1961 staffing event no longer implies this tower was staffed that year; the story no longer says the trail went 'up' the forest road.

Three sources agree on the 1934 build, the 1962 destruction and the 75-foot L-6 design; the Forest Service list (2016, compiled by Margaret Sand, Walde Lookout and Cindy Schacher) also gives 6876 ft and 9 miles SSE of Kelly Creek RS. Staffing rests on one name with no date. No source describes the site today, and the brief's access 'unknown' is kept, not set. Photo: the Forest Service list shows none. Also note the Idaho page's Armstrong Peak entry (1934, 60-ft L-6, destroyed 1962) is a different lookout and was not used.

Elevation is 7813 ft on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts, and 7820 ft in the 2023 IdahoAlpineZone trip report; not used. The only dated history is 1907 and the 2022 fire. No staffing source found. Access and drive/trail details come from one hiking trip report; the site itself has not been checked on the ground, and no source describes lookout remains.

Brief access 'unknown' left unset: no source says whether the site is open. All three detail pages give the same 1932 and 1950s dates, but Forest Lookouts attributes its dates to Kresek, so they may share one origin. No photo, staffing or site-condition source found. WebSearch returned no lookout-specific history beyond these pages.

Coordinates disagree in the brief: the firelookout.org record gives 47.78145, -116.39107 and the Idaho Fire Lookouts-derived record gives 47.77519, -116.38213, about 1 km apart. firelookout.com gives only '13 miles east of Hayden Lake' and no coordinates, so neither set is confirmed here; no correction proposed. Destruction date differs in wording (about 1950 vs 1950s), both kept. The brief's 'ground' kind matches the cabin description. Both lookout pages credit the Fire Lookout Museum for a photo, but no photo URL was recorded as a new find. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 'Hike-in' label is kept as a note only.

The 1938 build year and the 2007 destruction agree across four sources. The Red Bluff Fire name comes from one source only (Forest Lookouts); the Zena-Loon fire map page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The access level public is inferred from the wilderness location and the hike-in tag; no closure is described, and the story does not state an access level. The record's coordinates match the firelookout.org index. Nothing describes the site today.

The brief's kind is still unknown. Idaho Fire Lookouts says ground-mounted; firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page say log crib, so the editor may set kind to ground once mounting is settled. firelookout.com says early 1970s and Idaho Fire Lookouts says 1970s, with no exact year, so no staffed_last event was entered. No source describes remains or current conditions. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page has a 'Hike-In' label that the story reports, and the wilderness access level is inferred from the wilderness designation, not from a source that addresses visitor access.

Brief height 6.1 m looks like the 20-foot Forest Lookouts figure; three sources say 15 feet. Agency: brief says National Forest, which only Forest Lookouts says; the Priest Lake TPA name is in two sources. Brief access 'unknown' left unset; WillhiteWeb describes a hike but does not state a closure or permission rule. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists no staffing history. The WillhiteWeb page is a personal site, so its footing captions are the only evidence of what remains.

Minor conflict on pole-tower height of the 1937 structure (45 vs 50 ft); both figures are now attributed to their sources in the narrative rather than stated as a single number. Elevation conflicts slightly between brief (1907.4m) and rec.gov (6,414 ft = 1955m) but not asserted as a specific figure in the story. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): draft had stated the pole height as a flat '45-foot' figure sourced to both NHLR and firelookout.com, but NHLR actually gives 50 feet, contradicting its own citation -- fixed to attribute each figure correctly. Draft also said staffer Diane Young served 'around 1970'; idahofirelookouts.com's staff list actually dates her 1975-1978 -- fixed.

Built year: brief 1930 kept; Forest Service list and Firelookout.com say 1931 for the L-4 cab. Idaho Fire Lookouts' sentence that the L-4 style was built from 1929 to 1953 describes the design, not this lookout, so it is not used. Elevation and forest-name conflicts are noted above. Staffing is one name for 1960 from Idaho Fire Lookouts' Known Staff section; not corroborated. No photo URLs were added; the 1931 Louis Hartig photo is credited to the Nez Perce-Clearwater archives in two sources but no image URL was read.

Three sources agree on the 1933 camp, 1940 cabin and 1950 destruction. The 1936 staffer rests on one secondary quote (Forest Lookouts quoting the Ravalli Republic); we could not find the original item in web search. The Forest Lookouts page cites Kresek, which we did not read. Elevation 7,428 ft appears in two sources; the record has no elevation field filled. The access level stays unknown: no source gives one, so no access fact is recorded.
No source after the 2011 registration describes the current condition or any visit. No staffing history found. The 2000 abandonment date rests on one site. No photos added.

1956 vs 1957 last-staffed/abandonment discrepancy left unresolved in the story per guide instructions. NRHP nomination PDF (84001178) not pulled this pass; could firm up build details and exact staffing dates if more budget is available.

Thin record: the build year, form and D-6 label agree across the three sources, but no source gives a removal date, cause, staffing or site description. Elevation 7,554 ft appears in two sources; the record has no elevation field filled. The photo credited to Idaho Fire Lookouts is already in the record, so no new photo is listed.

Brief's 1950 'built' is the move year; corrected to 1938 build. Sunset Peak: the L-4 cab went there in 1950, but no source says what became of it; Sunset Peak got a concrete two-story cab in 1957, and both Idaho Fire Lookouts ('Destroyed/Repurposed', 1975) and firetower.org ('long gone') describe the later lookout only. Access 'public' is an inference from a hiker's route account plus the 'Drive-Up' tag; no closure or permit notice was found, and road condition is unconfirmed. Maple Peak is in the Coeur d'Alene NF per both register and firelookout.com; the brief's agency (USFS) is consistent. Sunset Peak is listed as administered by the Idaho Department of Natural Resources on the firetower.org Sunset page (not used for this record). Not checked: the USFS Clearwater/CDA lookout list at fs.usda.gov/media/259184. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 5,750 ft figure is now cited only to the three sites that give it; willhiteweb says 5,760 ft and is not cited for elevation.

Coordinates differ: the record uses the FFLA point 47.15075, -116.03253; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 47.15195, -116.02346, about 0.7 km away. No source here says which point is the tower. Elevation is 6,300 ft (about 1,920 m) in two sources; the record has none. Not to be confused with the Washington lookout also named Marble Mountain (Ferry County, FFLOS US 548). The account rests on one August 2025 trip report. Story stays brief because the sources are thin.

Sources agree on the about-1924 cabin and the 1950 destruction. The Sawyer Ridge replacement link is only a 'may have' in two sources, and Sawyer's 1949 date falls before 1950; do not treat it as established, and check it against any Sawyer Ridge record. Elevation 5,983 ft appears in two sources; the record's elevation_m is empty. The drive-up label describes the cabin as it stood, not a visit fact.

Only short listings and one newspaper-quoting page; no source describes the site today, so the access level is omitted. The forest name and the distance from Challis differ between sources. Record agency 'Challis National Forest' is one of two names in use. The 1953 rescue is an incident, not a fire; it is listed as 'other'. Elevation is in the story but has no facts key in the schema.

Two sources disagree on the tower's height (67 vs 90 feet), its build year (1933 vs 1934) and the replacement year (1962 vs 1963); the story reports both. Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site 'Drive-Up Removed', which is not explained, so no visit facts are recorded. No source describes what remains at the site or its public access, so no access key is included. Staff names come from a 1950 and a 1980 listing and a 1952 newspaper item.

Removal date unresolved: 1978 (Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com) against 'destroyed' in the 1980s (Shoshone County list). Spelling: the record and the lookout sites say Mastadon; the trail guide and map sites say Mastodon. Elevation 5,905 ft (about 1,800 m) in two sources; the record has none. The account rests on one hiking guide dated June 13, 2021, so a recent visit report would help. Access level 'public' is inferred from the guide's trail loop, not from a land manager.

Only the 1934 versus 1935 cupola date is disputed; the 1951 abandonment and the 2013 fire agree across sources. Elevation differs: the register gives 2,247 m (7,372 ft), and firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 7,424 ft. The record's elevation was left as it is. No source read describes the summit today. The 1951 Havre item is quoted on Kemnow's site and was not checked against the original newspaper.

The brief record's 1961 destruction date is contested by a June 1962 newspaper item that describes the tower as still being toppled and burned; no correction is proposed, so the editor should decide between 1961 and 1962. The 'L-4' design and 1933 build are consistent across both lookout sites. The 1950 'unstaffed' date comes from the newspaper item and names no staff. Height 6.1 m is converted from 20 feet. No source describes the site today.

Gone tower: the site today is undocumented in every source read; the story says so. The 1931 vs 1934 build date and the 1943 vs 1944 cab move are unresolved. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history for this lookout, so staffing is left out. No fires found. Access to the McDonald Peak site is unknown and left out of facts. The brief's design L-4 and agency Coeur d'Alene National Forest are confirmed. The Spyglass cab is the moved structure; the story covers both sites as the brief's moved-tower rule requires. Recreation.gov's 1930s date for the ground house conflicts with the 1943/1944 move; flagged, not resolved.

Dates 1935, 1960 and 1970 agree across sources, but only one page (Forest Lookouts) has detail, and it leans on Kresek and a reprinted newspaper item. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says no documented staffing history; left out of story. The 1939 item names John Frei as leading the bridge crew, not the lookout staff, so no staff name is given. A 1973 Latah County oral history (lib.uidaho.edu, Clay Gustin interview, 1973-07-25) mentions a McGary fire that burned over a mountain, which the speaker dated to 1931 or 1932 from memory; it is not clearly tied to this lookout, so it is left out. Site access and what remains today are not described by any source read. Elevation 4,457 feet per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; not a facts key. Brief's height 15.2 m matches the 50-foot figure.

The record's name collides with a different lookout: Meadow Creek Lookout in Valley County (NHLR US 944, ID 98) is standing and built in 1933. Keep the two apart. The record's coordinates (45.82788, -115.0239) differ from the firelookout.org index (45.81844, -115.14929) by roughly 10 km; neither was checked against a map. The forest is disputed (Nez Perce in two sources, Payette in one). The record's kind 'unknown' should probably read camp. No staffing record, photo or site description was found.

Current condition rests on a 2018 visit report and an undated climbing guide. The Idaho Statesman item is dated January 28, 1945 and describes a summer and fall before that date, so the season year is not certain. Access is recorded as restricted (emergency use); the story does not encourage visits. No new photo URLs captured.

Status is the open question. The record's 'gone' matches the FFLA list and Peakbagging, but Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com say the cabin now houses communication equipment, which may mean it still stands; Willhite says demolition date is unknown. A human should decide the status note before publishing. Ownership is 'unknown' in the record, but the summit land is state-retained per Willhite. Access is private: the story advises against going up without permission. Do not confuse with the Washington Mica Peak (FFLOS US 1509, WA 409, Spokane County), cached under data/raw/fflos/firetower.org/lookouts/us/wa/mica-peak-lookout-site/. No new photos added.

Only four sources, all short. Nothing confirms whether the cabin still stands, so the record's 'standing' is not supported. The access level 'public' is inferred from the wilderness hike-in note. Source 4 covers a different Cottonwood Point in Bonner County and is used only to prevent confusion. Staffing is recorded as not staffed since 1946, based on the abandonment notes. Build history (1914, 1930, 1934) is consistent across three sites. The 1962 end is disputed (removed vs destroyed). Three lookout listings agree on the 1939 camp, 1942 L-4 tower and 1954 destruction, and the state list agrees on the status. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the elevation as 6250 feet (used in the story). Height figures for both the 1938 and 1961 structures differ slightly between NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts; recorded as a range in the story rather than resolved, since no source explains the discrepancy. Four pages agree on a tower with an L-4 cab and its 1955 destruction; the Forest Service list dates the build to 1934 +/- and Forest Lookouts to c.1934. Three sources only. Forest Lookouts quotes the 1959 NGS datasheet description (PID QB1284) and the 1924, 1936, 1938 and 1941 newspaper items, which were not read at source. Thin record: the only date is the 1930s, and no source describes the abandonment, staffing, or any remains. History is consistent across sources. Nothing describes the site today; the story says so. The record's height of 23.2 m matches the 76-ft 1934 tower, not the 1925 cabin. The 1930 and 1938 dates and the design agree across the three pages that give them. Built 1930 and destroyed 1952 agree across sources. The 1966 survey description is the last source found about the site, and no current description was found. Height and first-structure descriptions conflict; the register's 74-foot figure is an outlier. Both sites agree on the 1934 L-4 tower and the 1952 destruction. Neither says how the tower was lost, and no source describes the site now. The three sources agree on the 1934 build and 1948 destruction. Location conflict not resolved: the record's ffla point (46.0566, -114.7576) matches the FFLA list (46.05660, -114.75760), but the idaho_fl point (46.07873, -114.7404) appears in no source read. Access is marked public by inference: the 2025 visit was a short walk from the road and no source describes a closure; confirm before relying on it. The history (1914 camp, 1922 cab, 1939 L-4 cab on a 10-ft tower) agrees across four sources. Used 1 websearch.py call and 6 page reads.

Brief's record matches the sources on design, agency, registration and staffing. The first-cabin date is disputed (1915 newspaper vs 1922 elsewhere). Two-story claim: the brief's kind 'two_story' is not supported by any page read for the Boise tower; corrections proposes a change for a human to decide. Recommend a targeted read of the weebly pilot-peak pages to settle the two-story question and any fire history. Access level left unset: no source states public access rules. Known-staff names are not included in the story. Converted-to-radio date is not given by any source, so no event is listed for it. Staffing as_of is the access date because the Idaho Fire Lookouts list is undated. The Payette tower's Idaho Fire Lookouts page (west-central/pilot-peak-lookout) appeared in search only and was not read.

Brief height_m 3.0 matches only the 10-foot base in the sources, not a confirmed total height, so it is left out of facts. Elevation: NHLR says 8,075 ft (2,461 m), firelookout.com says 8057 ft; the brief's 2461.3 m follows NHLR. Access level is not stated by any source, so access is omitted; visit.drive_up comes from the Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Drive-Up Staffed' label. Keeping Watch says L-4 cabs were built until 1952, which is earlier than the 1954 L-4 here; the design label may be loose. The Weebly list page has a '1932 log lookout house' entry that is not clearly this tower (the page lists many Pilot Peaks), so it is not used. A 2020 Idaho County Free Press article on restoration appeared in search results but returned HTTP 429 on fetch, so restoration is not in the story; worth a retry.

Unresolved: the 1944 John McKay entry predates the 1947 cabin date given by two sources, and no source explains it. Cab type disputed: L-4 per the register, R-4 per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts, Region 5 model 4A per the Forest Lookouts site. The story says so. Location conflict unresolved: brief lists ffla 48.77094,-116.91133 and idaho_fl 48.77131,-116.94912. The cached Idaho Fire Lookouts page did not show coordinates, so no correction made. The brief's height_m of 4.3 is not in any source read; recommend removing it. Conflict unresolved: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists George Howard in 1971 (citing a Kellogg Evening News item of 06/10/1971, which was not read directly), three years after the 1968 destruction date both sites give. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give the 1955 loss; the Forest Lookouts entry gives only the 1921 log cabin and the 1930 cupola cabin, and the register confirms the site is a gone ground site. Name conflict unresolved: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives J.B. Jenkins, Forest Lookouts quotes the 7/8/1915 Idaho County Free Press as Jinkins. The newspaper itself was not read. Agency conflict, unresolved: firelookout.com says Challis National Forest; Forest Lookouts and Idaho Fire Lookouts say Sawtooth. The record keeps Sawtooth and the story reports both. Staffing is undocumented in every source, so the story leaves it out. Read firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts (2022 post), Rex's page and the firelookout.org Idaho list (row: Quartz Mountain, Bonner, 48.32181 -116.94819, Crowsnest Abandoned; brief coordinates match it). Read firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, Rex's page, the NGS datasheet QZ0745, and the Forest Service Nez Perce list (fs.usda.gov/media/259204). Thin record. The 1930 build and abandonment in the 1940s agree across sources, but the cab type and staffing dates conflict or are unclear. The 1940 year on the abandoned event is a placeholder for the decade, not a sourced date. No access or remains information was found.

Read firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, Rex's page and Peakbagging.com (photo dated August 12, 2020). The 1928 build date appears on three pages; the abandonment year is the main conflict. Thin record. Removal versus destruction around 1950 conflicts across sources. The 1930s camp comes from a decade-only listing. No staffing is documented by any source. No source describes what remains on the ridge; the site is a wilderness-adjacent hike-in.

Thin record. No source gives a staffing history, a fire, or a description of the site today. Built dates (1923, 1939) and the 1967 destruction agree across all four sources. No source names the 1967 fire. The brief has kind 'ground'. Most sources describe an L-4 cab, which fits a cab on the ground, but WillhiteWeb's 1956 note mentions a tower, so the kind is left as is. Brief's height_m 14.0 belongs to a tower that is no longer standing. See corrections. Brief record says gone; the four sources say abandoned and still there in the 1980s, and none says it was removed, so status is corrected to unknown. Brief's elevation 1139 m is not in any source read and is not used. Kresek is named beside the crow's nest on Forest Lookouts with no explanation. Do not confuse with the separate Rocky Point records for Clearwater NF and Payette NF, which are different lookouts.

Brief elevation 1914.1 m matches NHLR (6,280 ft, 1,914 m); firelookout.com says 6280'. Brief height_m 3.0 corresponds to the 10-foot base only; no total height in sources, so it is left out of facts. Access level is not stated by any source (NHLR says relatively easy access from Powell, not visitor rules), so access is omitted. Keeping Watch's Rocky Point page gives coordinates 46.58222, -114.66587, which match this tower, but has no history. No fire, closure or move found in the sources read. Do not confuse with a separate West Central Idaho 'Rocky Point Lookout' (log cabin, 1936 per the Idaho Fire Lookouts search snippet, reported burned in 2015); that page was seen only in search results and was not read.

The 2015 fire and the wilderness location agree across all three sources. Build year (1936 or 1937) and abandonment (1952 or 1960s) conflict. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history. No source describes the site after the fire in text; the register and firelookout.com carry photos with captions only, so none was added as a new find. The brief's access 'unknown' was left unset, because no source states an access rule.

Build year conflicts (1914 on the Forest Service list, 1917 on the other two sources). The record's 1940 abandonment is a decade, not a year. Staffing: no names in any source read, so none given. Access is not stated beyond drive-up, so access is omitted. Forest Service list photo credited USFS but no image URL was captured.

Brief height 80.5 m is wrong (29-30 ft). The 1967 newspaper accounts (quoted by Forest Lookouts) say the Sundance fire destroyed the tower, but staff lists and firelookout.com's late-1970s staffing run past 1967; the story reports both and does not settle it. Current-site information rests on one personal trip report (sonnybou.ca) and a photo caption. The 1930 and 1970 event years are decade starts. Access is marked public because the lakes and summit climb are described; no closure found, so check with the Forest Service before any visit. Forest Lookouts also quotes a 1921 item about a telephone line to the Roman Nose lookout, so the story limits 'earliest' to named lookout people. Brief's status gone is corrected to ruins.

Gone status is on two lookout listings (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts); the Forest Lookouts listing gives only the 1930s cabin and does not say gone. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so no staffing is stated. The Gaia GPS page is a user-built trail listing: it shows a trail passes the point, not what is there. No source read describes remains, so the story says so.

Name spelled Roots Knob in the record and on two lookout sites; the UI archive calls it Root Knob. Record height_m 3.0 not written as a fact: sources give only a 10-foot pole (about 3.05 m), not a cab-floor height. The UI photo (archivalidaho193) is In Copyright, Educational Use Permitted, so it is not listed under photos. The Living New Deal page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Nothing says what remains at the site today; access left unset.

The three sources agree on 1935 build, the 50-foot L-4 design and destruction around 1961. The Forest Lookouts page credits its 1961 date to a source it names Kresek; the sources may not be independent of one another. Record height_m 15.2 is consistent with 50 ft (15.24 m), but the sources give pole height, not cab-floor height, so no height fact was written. The FFLOS entry 'Round Top Mountain Lookout Site' in search results is the Clearwater NF Round Top (us-id-round-top-mountain-2), not this one; it was not used. Nothing says what remains at the site today.

Identity: the Clearwater NF site (46.5338, -114.5916; 6,555 ft per register; 6560 ft per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts) matches the brief. A search snippet pointed to a different Round Top Mountain lookout in the north Idaho panhandle (1935 pole tower, destroyed 1961) and to a separate 'Roundtop Mtn' page on firelookout.com; neither was used. Date and height disagree across sources; no ground photo or recent source found. No photos added: the credited Montana Memory Project and Bud Moore images have no stated license in the pages read. Brief record 'status gone' is consistent with the sources; no corrections proposed.

Tower history agrees across sources 1-3, except the 1927 windmill date: firelookout.com gives 1927 and Forest Lookouts gives c.1927, so the story says around 1927. Source 4 lists the tower as gone with no year.Not to be confused with the Round Top lookouts in Clearwater National Forest (Idaho County, 1934 to 1972) or the Round Top Mountain in Bonner County; those are different sites and were not used. height_m is converted from the final 53-foot tower. No source gives a cause for the 1979 destruction, and no source describes the site today.

Two short sources agree on the 1933 L-4 cab, 1940 abandonment, Nez Perce NF and the location 28 miles east of Kooskia at 6,807 ft. The brief's source list includes the Idaho Fire Lookouts St. Joe-Clearwater page (/st-joe-clearwater-region/round-top-lookout/). That page is a different site: Clearwater NF, elevation 6560 ft, 1934 40-foot pole L-4, destroyed 1972, with cement footings found. It matches us-id-round-top-mountain-2, so it is not used for this lookout's history; the story cites it only to tell readers the two apart. The record's source_pages list should drop it. The other name 'Round Top Mtn Lookout' is also used by that Clearwater site, so the name alone does not identify this lookout. Record coordinates (46.1288, -115.38187) were not checked against any source. Nothing says what remains at the site today; access level left unset.

The Ruby Cabin post (bchistoricplaces.org, April 11, 2025) probably describes the frame cabin firelookout.com mentions, but the post never names Ruby Mountain. Confirm before saying so on a public page. Hollice Aldridge's dates: 1933 on firelookout.com, 1933-1934 on Idaho Fire Lookouts. The 1950s abandonment has no exact year; the event uses 1950 with a note. firelookout.com credits its photos to Kyle Cossairt and Luke Channer; no licence is known, so none are added. No source gives a current access status.

Two live disagreements. (1) Current use: Keeping Watch (an undated video page) and Wikipedia say staffed seasonally; firelookout.com and the Idaho Fire Lookouts July 2025 post say emergency status. The fact is recorded as emergency use dated 2025, and the story says the sources differ. (2) Last staffed decade: 1980s (register, Idaho Fire Lookouts) vs 1990s (firelookout.com). Idaho Fire Lookouts lists staff for 1984 and 1985 despite its own 1980s end date. Elevation: the register gives 9,291 ft (2,832 m), matching the record's 2831.9 m; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 9,407 ft, and Wikipedia gives 9,407 ft (2,867 m) for the peak. The record may be using the register's lookout figure, so a human should decide. Not read: Forest Service pages and any 2001 return-to-service record.

Build date and design conflict. The register, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Intermountain Histories give 1937 and an R-4 plan 80 cab similar to an L-4. firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts give a 1935 L-4 cab, attributed to Kresek; the story reports both and follows the register. Elevation: the register gives 7,139 ft (2,176 m), matching the record's 2176.0 m; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 7223 ft (about 2,202 m). Current condition: no visit report newer than the register's 2009 photo was found; the cab's present state is unknown. Staff names appear only in the events notes. No Forest Service wilderness or closure page was read.

Record's '1930 built' and '1930 abandoned' are not supported; see corrections. Cabin survival conflicts: register says the cabin was left (no current date), Firelookout.com says still there, Idaho Fire Lookouts says rumored; no recent visit report or photo dated after 2006 found, so today's condition is unknown. Forest name differs: register says Idaho Panhandle National Forests; Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say Kaniksu National Forest (not resolved). Access is not established; 'hike-in' is the only access label. A NaughtyHiker page on a Russell Peak (6,830 ft, Trout Creek, Selkirk Mountains; tower gone, cabin remains) appears to be a different summit (elevation differs from 6,618 ft), so not used. The 1933 Bonners Ferry Herald item was not read directly.

County corrected from 'Idaho' to 'Idaho County' per firelookout.com. Elevation 6,084 ft appears on two pages but is not a schema key, so it is only in the story. Height is the stated 50-foot tower converted to metres; the sources do not say whether that is measured to the cab floor. The 2010 Forest Service list has a '+/-' mark on the Sable Hill row that the text extraction does not explain. Only one staffer is named. No source describes the site today; the hike-in label is the only access detail.

Medium confidence. Unresolved: (1) the Packsaddle Mountain page says a 76-foot Aermotor tower from 1934 was intended for Saddle Mountain, while the register and firelookout.com describe a 40-foot tower; the record's design is left as the register's 40-foot tower. (2) Staff dated 1932-1933 predate the 1935 build, so an earlier structure may have stood on the site; no source found describes one. (3) No source describes the cab's present condition or public access. The record's 'standing' status is not confirmed by a source on the cab itself; the only current-use statement is the communication-site note on Idaho Fire Lookouts. Nothing here supports climbing or entering the site.

Build date conflicts: register 1926 (4A cab) vs Idaho Fire Lookouts 1923 two-story log cabin plus a 1930s R-4 cab, and firelookout.com 1930s. Cab type also conflicts (4A vs R-4). Forest name conflicts (Salmon-Challis vs Salmon). Distance from Salmon: a 1959 newspaper item places it about 20 miles west; firelookout.com says 27 miles WNW (not used in story). Latest condition evidence is the 2009 register visit report; no 2020s status was found. The record kind two_story appears to come from a firelookout.org '2-Story cab' label and was not independently checked. No photos added: the visible photos are credited to Luke Channer with no licence stated.

Medium confidence. Disagreements left open: ground cabin (register) vs two-story log cab (Idaho Fire Lookouts); wood frame vs log; elevation 9,604 ft / 2,927 m (register) vs 9592 ft (firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts). The record keeps kind 'ground' per the register. The 1934-36 staffing rests on a history site quoting 1930s newspapers; the 1935-36 items say 'LaSal mountain' and the page files them under Sal Mountain, but no source confirms that link directly. No source describes the current condition or public access. The record's conflict value 'gone' (idaho_fl) appears to be a misreading of 'Abandoned'.

NHLR's 1938 date for the first cupola tower conflicts with two other independent sources giving 1928; flagged in the story rather than silently resolved. Did not independently verify the NHLR-registered year of 2009 beyond the brief's own record.

The 1924 windmill tower (two sources) and the 1927 steel tower (one source) disagree on the tower's form; the record has no event that settles it. Sand Creek Lookout Site on willhiteweb.com is a Pend Oreille County, Washington site near Sullivan Lake, a different lookout, and was not used. No source read describes the site today or whether it is reachable; the Potlatch TPA is not described as public or private land in any source read. Staffing is not in any source read and is left out of the story.

The 1929 and 1931 newspaper items call the station Bald mountain or Mt. Baldy. The story takes them to mean this lookout because Forest Lookouts files them under Sandpoint Baldy; no newspaper names Sandpoint Baldy itself. The removal date is not given in any source; firelookout.com's R.I.P. 1922-? is blank at the end. No source read describes the site today or whether it is reachable. Staffing is partial: only these three named lookouts appear in the sources read.

Do not confuse with the other Savage Ridge in Valley County (45.08165, -115.58329; platform, abandoned in the FFLA list). The University of Idaho Keeping Watch page links to that Valley County lookout. The present-day description rests on one 2018 amateur radio summit report, not an official survey; recheck the trail and debris details before publishing. The 2018 report also mentions a SNOTEL station near the trailhead, which the story leaves out. No staffing source was found, so staffing is omitted.

The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with all the Valley County sources: Idaho Fire Lookouts and the state list say abandoned, and firelookout.com says the platforms are still there. The story keeps 'abandoned' and reports the still-there note as unconfirmed; a recent visit or source would settle it. The built event has no year because the sources give only the 1930s. The other cabin page calls it a Nez Perce cabin in its text but names the Clearwater National Forest on its forest line, and the story follows the forest line. Do not merge with the other Savage Ridge (Clearwater National Forest cabin, Idaho County, destroyed 1972, coordinates 46.45719, -114.58843 in the state list). Idaho Fire Lookouts has no documented staffing for this site, so staffing is left out.

The 1935 and 1951 dates appear on three listings that look like one shared inventory (Forest Lookouts marks its entries '(Kresek)'), so they are not three independent confirmations. The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with the FFLA 'Abandoned' status (see corrections). Elevation 6,904 ft from Idaho Fire Lookouts has no facts key, so it appears only in the story. The forest question is open and could be settled by Sawtooth or Challis National Forest records. No photo, NHLR or FFLOS number was found; the FFLA row has no registry entry. Brief coordinates 44.02978, -114.82511 match the FFLA list.

Coordinates: the original Sawyer Ridge record (45.68417, -115.95504) and the NHLR coordinates for the relocated Eyeful Tower (45.684020, -115.955446) are about 35 m apart. The sources do not say the original tower stood where the Dreher home is now, so check before reusing the original coordinates. No recent photo or status check was found for the relocated tower. The Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Drive-Up' label is not used because the tower is on private property.

NHLR gives elevation 7,273 ft at the Dreher property; idahofirelookouts.com gives 7,303 ft for the original Sawyer Ridge site — left unreconciled since they describe two slightly different points and neither source is clearly authoritative for the other's site. No source gives who built the original tower (a crew, not a named builder) or the exact reason the Forest Service decided it was surplus beyond space/staffing needs implied by the 1987 date. No current rental status or public visiting hours beyond 'by pre-arrangement' were found.

Removal: 1976 in three sources (Forest Lookouts, firelookout.com, and the 2025 account). Buyer conflict: firelookout.com says a Clark Fork farmer; the 2025 account says a family, which the story does not name. Mace's 'after 18 years of service' is hearsay; counting from 1954 gives about 1972, so it is reported as a disagreement. Record height 9.1 m is the 1938 tower; the 1954 tower was 41 ft (see corrections, not applied here). Agency conflict: Mace's 1953 diary places the lookout in the Kaniksu National Forest (Clark Fork District); Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com say Coeur d'Alene National Forest; the record uses Coeur d'Alene. Spelling: the Forest Lookouts page uses 'Shaffer'. Footings: the 2025 account reports six cement footings at the site, four attributed to the 1950s tower and no more than two of the original; an earlier draft wrongly said no source described footings. Staff named only on the 2025 account, not in events or the story: 1949 Bob Kurth and Arnold Krause; 1970 William Phillips. A geocaching listing repeats the 1976 date but was not read or cited. Record events and staffing were empty; staffing lines come from the sources above.

Removal year conflict: 1955 (association's 1955-56 report, via Forest Lookouts) against 1957 (Idaho Fire Lookouts, page dated October 21, 2022); both are shown in events and the story. The visit date itself is not stated; 2022 is the page's date. firelookout.com's 'R.I.P. 1923-1931' does not match the 1934 steel tower; those years match the first platform and pole tower, but no source explains the label. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says no documented staffing history, so none is given. No source read says who owns the summit today or what access rules apply. Record elevation_m is null; the 2022 page gives 4265 ft (about 1,300 m), which the editor may add to the record. Record design is null; no source gives a design letter for the 1934 steel tower.

Abandonment: 1950s in the Forest Lookouts page and the magazine article, but firelookout.com's header runs to 1970s; the record's 1950 abandonment event is not supported by the sources read (they say 1950s), so it was left out of events. The magazine article gives no publication date in the text read; it is the only source for the lightning deaths and the remains, so treat both as single-source. The magazine's 'rag camp' wording replaces an earlier 'bare camp' that no source used. Access: the article reports the trail closed in September 2015 and reopened in 2016; it gives no current rules, and the story says none was found. Staffing: only the 1924 Dr. Broady caption is documented; the record's staffing is unknown. The Scotchman Peak Wilderness reference comes from a photo caption, not a rules page. Record kind is 'ground' and material 'wood', consistent with the D-6 cupola cabin described.

Build dates agree (1920 cabin, 1934 L-4 cab), so the brief's warning about conflicting build years does not apply to this cab. Open questions: the foundation material (stone vs concrete) and current staffing, since every staffing source is undated. Brief access 'unknown' is now described as drive-up. No fire history and no rental listing appeared in the six pages read or the two searches run, so the story does not mention either. Budget used: 6 page reads, 2 searches.

Elevation 8,700 ft is from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; it is not a facts key, so it appears only in the story. The brief's status gone comes from the FFLA list; the two site histories say abandoned, which is why the status is recorded as abandoned. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so staffing is left out. The Drive-Up label is the only access-related detail; no source says whether the site is public, so access is not set. Camp Taylor's Scout Mountain Forest Recreation Area history covers a campground near 6,500 ft and does not mention this lookout, so it is not used.
Build/cabin sequence between 1917 and 1952 is not fully consistent across sources; treated as an open conflict rather than resolved. No new photos found during this pass.

The brief's county Idaho is corrected to Idaho County. Heights: 60 feet is 18.3 m. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists a 1927 staffer only as Ted Oliver's brother, so no name is given. The Forest Service PDF has only a general description of early tree crow's nests and an undated Seaburg photo caption; it has no Seaburg-specific history or image URL, so it is not added as a new photo. The brief's existing photo is an Idaho Fire Lookouts image.

Medium confidence. Elevation: the register gives 9,170 ft; firelookout.com gives 9167 ft, and the record keeps the register figure. The 2011 register date on Idaho Fire Lookouts contradicts the register's 2020 date. The 1981 'Emergency Status' entry is unexplained and is used only as a timeline line. No source describes public access beyond the drive-up label; the building is in radio use. No staffing history was found after completion, so no staffing fact is recorded.

County 'Shoshone' matches. Elevation 4,851 ft appears on both pages but is not a schema key, so it is only in the story. Height is the stated 20-foot tower converted to metres; the sources do not say whether that is to the cab floor. 'Drive-Up' is the Idaho Fire Lookouts label; no source describes the site today or public access. The 1945 Yahr staffing is flagged because Yahr's own page does not mention this site and lists Bear Butte for 1945 to 1948. The Smokechaser catalog record is cited only for the book's date and subject.

Read the NHLR page, the Forest Lookouts page (including its 1926-1959 newspaper extracts and its 1959 NGS survey description), Idaho Fire Lookouts, the climbing guide (updated Feb 2021) and firelookout.com. One WebSearch-equivalent search was run; the Idaho Statesman article it surfaced timed out twice and is not used. Access is recorded as restricted because the sources describe ski patrol occupancy and emergency use with no public visiting, but no source states the access rule outright, so a human should confirm before publishing. The 1980 change to the upper floors is disputed. The brief's height_m of 3.0 has no support in any source read and is proposed for removal. The brief's elevation_m (2286.6) matches NHLR's 7,502 ft, but three other sources give 7,582 ft. Fact-check 2026-10-08: every dated item in the story was confirmed on the cached Forest Lookouts page and the NHLR register text; the story's floor wording now follows the register, and the 'Please do not climb the tower' line is safety advice, not a sourced fact.

The brief's L-4 design is kept. Its height of 12.2 m matches the 1927 40-foot steel tower, so the correction proposes 15.2 m for the 1933 L-4 tower; the final 1959 tower at 44 feet would be about 13.4 m if the page should describe that one instead. The annual reports for 1957-58 and 1959-60 repeat the same tower completion text, so the date is left unclear. Clearwater Timber Protective Association merged with the Potlatch association in 1966 to form Clearwater-Potlatch TPA (cptpa.com), so the record name fits the lookout's operating years. No staffing history is documented (Idaho Fire Lookouts), so staffing is left out. The site today is not described by any source read.

Height is the 53-foot tower figure converted to metres (16.2 m). Elevation 6,226 ft comes from idahofirelookouts.com and has no schema key. The brief's county 'Idaho' is the name firelookout.org uses; left unchanged. A search returned a Shearer Guard Station in the Selway-Bitterroot, which is a different structure and is not used. No source read gives the cause of the 1973 destruction.

The gone status agrees across firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, the Clearwater National Forest list and the Forest Fire Lookout Association index. No source gives staffing, a removal date or the site's condition today, so the story omits staffing and says nothing is described. Do not confuse this with the standing, staffed Sheep Hill in the Nez Perce National Forest. The record's county 'Idaho' matches the index. The Clearwater list gives a location as Sec23 T33N R8E, which was not used.

Brief record was wrong in four places (see corrections): the 1928 build date belongs to the earlier cabin, height_m 3.0 is a base height, kind two_story is unsupported, and the sheep-hill-lookout-2 Idaho page is about a different Sheep Hill (Clearwater NF, Gone). The Idaho page used here is the Nez Perce one without the -2 suffix. Staffing dates are undated. The 1960s Babcock entries are decades, not exact years. No fire history found in the pages read. Budget used: 6 distinct page reads, 2 searches.

Dates agree across three sources (Idaho Fire Lookouts, firelookout.com, the Forest Service list). Staffing rests on one source, Idaho Fire Lookouts, which cites the book Fire Lookouts of the Northwest and gives no dates. That page spells the staffer's first name 'Everetee' in its header and 'Everete' in its body; the story follows the body. Elevation is 5,708 ft per the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts; the record's elevation_m is null. The access level is omitted: no source states an access rule, and the story says it is unknown whether the site is open; the drive-up label stays under visit. The 1950 date is in the Forest Service list's Sheep Mtn. row (its quote is the bare year, since the row's text is split across PDF lines).
