A rental listing for a different 'Sheep Mountain Fire Lookout' (built 1950) turned up in search and was not used. No recent photo or visit report was found.

The brief's coordinates (44.59928, -115.00904) match the firelookout.org Idaho list. The 39-mile distance from Challis is as firelookout.com states it; it roughly fits the coordinates on a rough check, not a measured one. No staffing source. The 1946 abandonment date rests on three sites, one of which credits a source named Kresek. Searches found nothing on the site today.

The climbing guide's peak is matched to the lookout by elevation (10,865 ft) and the Gilmore location; no source names the lookout on that summit. The 1930s build is undated, so no build event is recorded. The 1983 date comes from one source. Searches found nothing on what remains at the site today.

Build dates conflict across sources: NHLR places an L-4 ground house in 1957 while firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Keeping Watch give 1934; the first log structure is dated 1925 or the late 1920s. Design conflicts (NHLR CL-100 14x14 vs Keeping Watch R-6 15x15) and elevation conflicts (8,421 ft vs 8,486 ft) are reported, not resolved. The access level 'restricted' is an inference from hike-in, active staffed use; no source states a visitor policy for the cab. Staffing as_of 2025 is the Idaho Fire Lookouts article date (July 12, 2025); its named staff list ends in 2024. No source read records a fire this lookout spotted or one that damaged it; the Keeping Watch interview describes burned forest in view and early fires in the wider area. The 1954 yellow-paint episode is in the UIdaho file and is not a fire. The Try Ranger trail page was not read, so no trail length is given. The record's kind 'ground' was not checked against the cab-on-stone-base description.

Brief height_m 2.7 does not appear in any source read, so it is omitted. Brief elevation 2488.4 m matches NHLR (8,164 ft, 2,488 m); firelookout.com gives 8159 ft. Brief 'Sources give different build years' is resolved as 1933 first cab vs 1965 current cab. Rental status is unverified: firelookout.com says the tower is on the Recreation Rental program, but the Forest Service page does not mention rentals and no current recreation.gov listing appeared in search. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 'Emergency Status' tag is not explained anywhere read. The Keeping Watch page (coordinates 44.8825167, -114.0912) matches the brief but was not read for history. The weebly page's 1952 plane-crash item near Sheephorn is not in the story (not about the tower). A search result for Sheep Mountain Lookout in Bighorn NF is a different tower and was not used.

Sources disagree on the distance to Turkey Point (1.25 vs 1 1/2 miles); the story reports both. The 1927 staffing is single-sourced and the source says 'may have staffed'. Staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1961 follows from the destruction date; no source gives a staffing end date. The Idaho Fire Lookouts remnants and carvings note comes from its article dated October 25, 2023, so it is a 2023 description. The Idaho page header spells the destruction note 'Destoryed'; the evidence quote copies the typo as printed. The access level is omitted: no source states an access rule, and the story says it is unknown whether the site is open; the drive-up label stays under visit. The record's kind 'ground' matches the FFLA list; the sources do not say whether the L-4 cab stood on a tower. Elevation is 6,300 ft per both sources; the record's elevation_m is null. No photo beyond the one already in the record was found.

Only two detailed pages plus the FFLA list. Idaho Fire Lookouts states it has no documented staffing history, so staffing is left out of the facts and the story. The access level is omitted because no source gives an access rule; the only access statement is the hike-in label. Elevation is 8,565 ft per both pages; the record's elevation_m is null. Do not confuse this with Shellrock Peak, a different tower (FFLA list: 44.95651, -114.93658; NHLR US 1454, ID 147; listed as standing). Several search results blended the two names. No photos added: the register's 1980 photo (credit Don Patterson) and the firelookout.com photos have no image URLs in the text fetched. Thin record. The 1956 trailer date and type come from the Forest Lookouts page (citing Kresek); firelookout.com repeats the same date and gives no independent source. Two web searches found no other record or photo. No source describes the site today or its access. The PTPA quote is an abbreviation on the IFL page, used only as a check.

Staffing record is thin (only two named years found) and both Idaho Fire Lookouts notes it is incomplete; story mentions this limitation rather than implying a full record. Corrected a mismatched name/year: the 1967 staffer was Penny Kummrow, not Laura Grace Simon (who staffed in 2010).

No photos added: NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts credit photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Luke Channer, but the text fetched has no image URLs. The first-cabin date rests on sources that cite the same Kresek list. The 1932 item is quoted second-hand from Forest Lookouts (The Recorder Herald) and was not checked in the newspaper. Forest Service staff or history pages were not read for the staffing dates.

Good staffing list (names 1932-1980) came from firelookout.com's own page text, which also resolves the build-year 'conflict' already flagged on the tower record -- see the correction proposed above. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found the story had wrongly attributed that staffing list to the National Historic Lookout Register; NHLR's own page carries no staffing names at all, only firelookout.com does. Fixed in the story. Also removed an invented height_m value (2.4 m) that matched no source -- it appears to have been derived from the 8-foot concrete base rather than any stated structure height -- and dropped footnote [^6] (the climbing-guide page) from the recreation.gov rental sentence, since that page never mentions recreation.gov and states the rental runs first-come-first-served. Separately: recreation.gov's own page gives the cabin as 15'x15' on a 5-foot foundation, which doesn't match NHLR/firelookout.com's 14'x14' on an 8-foot base; the story's dimension sentence cites only NHLR/firelookout.com and is internally consistent, but a human may want to reconcile the two descriptions. No information found on staffing after 1980 or on when year-round staffing ended; left as unknown. The idahomagazine.com article 'Back to Shorty Peak' returned HTTP 403 and could not be read; it may be worth a human revisit if full text is reachable another way. idahofirelookouts.com's detail page for this lookout was not cached locally and was not fetched live (only its listing thumbnail is cached), so it is not cited here.

The two pages disagree on elevation (5,425 ft on firelookout.com, 5,238 ft on Idaho Fire Lookouts); the story says so and the record's elevation is left alone. The 40-foot figure is the pole height as stated; the sources do not say whether it is the cab-floor height, so no height_m is given. No source states whether the site is open to the public; the story says so. Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented; firelookout.com does not mention staffing, so staffing is omitted. The McPherson fire is cited from one photo caption only as regional context. No FFLOS or NHLR register page for this site was in the local cache, and the record lists none.

Brief status gone corrected to abandoned per the sources. The 1915 and 1927 dates come from Kresek through the Forest Lookouts page; firelookout.com repeats them, and no independent record was found in one web search. The Forest Service Clearwater National Forest lookout list does not name Silver Butte, so it is not cited. No source describes the site today.

Build year 1936 and the 2017 NHLR registration agree across all four sources. Access is not stated on any page read; Idaho Fire Lookouts says drive-up, and the story asks readers to check with the Forest Service. Staffing is dated (NHLR description at 2017, staff list 1965 and approximate 2019). The brief's height_m 7.3 matches the 24-foot base and is proposed for removal. Not read: the Idaho climbing guide page for Silver Creek (idahoaclimbingguide.com), which may describe access and location; it was not read because this tower hit its page budget.

Only two secondary pages describe this lookout, and they agree. Both give 1930s and a 10-foot pole, which is short for an L-4 tower; I did not check that against any register or photo. No event is recorded because the sources give only a decade and no removal date. Searches for Silver Mountain in Idaho return the Silver Mountain resort near Kellogg, which is unrelated and was not used. Idaho Fire Lookouts has a second post under the north-idaho-panhandle-region path with the same title; it added no facts. No FFLOS or NHLR register page for this site was in the local cache, and the record lists none.

Structure is described three ways across sources (see resolved_conflicts); kind two_story in the record rests on the FFLA list. Elevation 6,762 ft from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts (no facts key for elevation). Only current-site evidence is the route guide's description of the road to the site; no remains described. drive_up true is inferred from the route guide. Staffing status is free text, following the acorn-butte example.

Possible mix-up to check: the Middle Sister lookout also lost a tower in 1953 (firelookout.com/id/middlesister.html; Spokane Historical item 588 says the Middle Sisters tower was a cupola built in 1923, replaced in 1951, and burned in 1953). The firelookout.com Middle Sister page gives the same 1923, 1951 and 1953 sequence; the Spokane item was not checked in this pass. The Sisters Basin 1932 date and 1953 'Gone' come only from the two Sisters Basin pages, and neither explains the loss. Worth checking against St. Joe National Forest records before publication. The 1953 event is recorded as 'other' with the note 'Listed as gone; the cause is not stated', because the source wording is only 'Gone'. Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented; firelookout.com does not mention staffing, so staffing is omitted. The Donally history (npshistory) does not name this lookout, so it does not explain the 1932 date. No photos were found and no FFLOS or NHLR register page for this site was in the cache.

Cab and tower destruction is dated 1961 by both firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; no other date. The 2025 remains are described in one source only (Idaho Fire Lookouts), so the site-today text rests on it. Access level public is inferred from National Forest land plus the hike-in label; no trail or closure source found. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so no staffing fact is recorded. Record kind ground and coordinates match the FFLA list. No record corrections proposed.

The 1924 and 1932 items reach us only as summaries and quotes on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not found. Elevation 7,229 ft comes from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. A LiDAR listing (listsofjohn.com) gives 7,236 ft and was not cited. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open.

Kind platform is correct: structure_kinds says crow's nests count as platforms when a source calls them crow's nests, and FFLA's Crowsnest label agrees. Location conflict left open: record uses FFLA 47.50642, -116.7729; idaho_fl has 47.49963, -116.7896, about 1.46 km apart. I could not check either pair against the text (firelookout.com gives 3 miles north of Harrison). Elevation 3650 ft per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; no elevation key in the schema, so not stored. The access level restricted is my reading of WillhiteWeb's access note; please confirm before publishing. The same WillhiteWeb page also says a motorcycle trail runs straight up the ridge from the pass, which sits oddly with the non-motorized agreement; the story therefore gives no access advice. Harrison is sourced to firelookout.com only; the Idaho Fire Lookouts and weebly pages do not name it. WillhiteWeb is undated, so the search date is unknown and the research summary avoids a year for it. Dates rest on four sources that agree.

Build-year conflict noted in brief resolves cleanly: 1931 pole tower, 1948 L-4, 1979 current R-6 flattop, all per NHLR. Height field in brief (2.1m) likely refers to cab dimension, not tower height (41 feet); not corrected here since no source gives a clean meters figure for overall height.

No photos added: the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts credit photos, but the fetched text has no image URLs. The Forest Lookouts page for Sleeping Deer returned 404 and was not used. The Forest Service trail page's title says #4212 while its text says #212; the story does not cite the number. The climbing guide's trail and the Forest Service trail are both reported, not reconciled. Access is restricted because the lookout is on emergency status and in poor shape; no source describes a closure.

Standing rests on a single list entry; no photo or condition report was found. The brief's 'standing' is kept in facts with a status_note. Access is recorded as public on the strength of 'Hike-In' alone; no closure or permit page was checked. Only four sources were read. Elevation of 9121 ft (idahofirelookouts.com) was not used in the story. Idahofirelookouts 'Abandoned' appears to describe use, not the structure.

Staffing end date and the museum display differ across sources; both are reported in the story. Elevation conflicts: the Register gives 5,021 ft (1,530 m), Idaho Fire Lookouts and the marker give 6,280 ft; not used. The record's coordinates are roughly 20 km southeast of McCall, which fits the original site (firelookout.com says 14 miles southeast), not the museum; no correction proposed. The record's events text ('None relocated...') is a note rather than an event, so it was not used. The brief's source_pages point to a separate museum-site record (us-id-sloans-creek-point-at-cent-id-hist-museum); it may be a duplicate and should be checked. No source read describes the original site today. Used 6 page reads and 1 search.

Sources agree on the 1933 build, the 1994 cabin removal and the 2000 move to the museum. They disagree on staffing: NHLR says staffed into the 1970s; the marker says staffed 1934-1970; Idaho Fire Lookouts says no longer staffed in the 1970s. The story reports all three. Elevation: NHLR gives 5,021 ft for the museum coordinates; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6,280 ft, which may be the original site. Name variants: 'Sloans Creek Point' (record and FFLA index), 'Sloans Point' (NHLR), 'Sloan's Point' (marker). A separate record us-id-sloans-creek-point exists (FFLA 'Standing' at 44.74488, -115.92730); it may be the original site, so the two may need linking or review. Not used: search snippets (not fetchable) from a Waymarking/HMdb marker text say Ed Allen and his son dismantled the tower in 2000 and Richard Holm Jr. and volunteers restored it in 2006. The Waymarking body is not cached (JS-rendered) and the HMdb inscription is truncated, so these lines cannot be quoted; a human should check them. The 2006 date conflicts with NHLR's 2000 reconstruction account. Access and hours come from AllTrips, a travel site; the museum's own site was not checked and hours may have changed. No photos added; the NHLR photo of the interpretive panel is credited to waymarking.com with unknown licence.

Demolition in 2008 is supported by all three sources. No source describes what remains on the site today. The Drive-Up and Demolished tags describe the lookout as it was, so the story does not treat them as a current access statement, and no visit facts or access level are recorded. The brief's design field '2-story ground cabin' comes from the 2008 report and conflicts with the other two sources.

This is the Bonner County Smith Mountain. The Adams County Smith Mountain on the Payette National Forest (us-id-smith-mountain-2) is a different lookout with a different history, and search results mixed the two. Only the 1966 item names a staffer, and it describes a plan, not a record of service. No source supports an access level. The onX user reports conflict (Open, Sep 20, 2026; Obstructed, May 17, 2025) and are not official, so no access level is recorded. The remains claim comes from one trail-app listing and needs confirmation before publication.

Build-year conflict in brief (1963 per NHLR vs. longer history) resolves cleanly: 1908 camp, 1920 cupola cabin, 1932 L-4, 1963 current structure, per FireLookout.com detail not captured by the brief's single NHLR 'Built' field.

Kaniksu National Forest appears on all three pages; Boundary County appears on FireLookout.com and Rex's page. The Smith Peak in Plumas County, California is a different lookout and was excluded. A search result gave a 1929 L-2 design date from a blog; it was not used because it is unverified. The 1925 Kauffman staffing comes from a Fire Lookout Museum credit cited on Idaho Fire Lookouts. The 'Hike-In Ruins' tag is not treated as a current access statement, so no visit facts are recorded.

Open conflicts, not resolved and not stored as facts: (1) agency: firelookout.com says Clearwater-Potlatch TPA, the county list says Clearwater Timber Protective Association, Idaho Fire Lookouts says Clearwater National Forest; the story says the sources disagree and no agency fact is set. (2) Elevation: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 5577 ft; the Forest Service list gives 4550 ft. The schema has no elevation key, so neither is stored. Record coordinates 46.89895, -115.73933 match the FFLA list. Height 30.5 m is 100 feet converted. Drive_up false comes only from the hike-in label. No source says whether the land is open to visitors, and no access level is set. Staffing: none found. Confidence is medium because of the agency and elevation conflicts and because the site-today statement is a plain absence in every source.

Thin record: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts agree on the 1918 build and the 1930s abandonment, and FFLA files the site as abandoned. The 2016 Clearwater National Forest lookout list (fs.usda.gov/media/259185) has no Smith Ridge entry. Its nearby Smith Point (9 miles WNW of Canyon RS, 100-foot L-6 tower, fell in the 1950s, 4550 ft) is a different site and was not used. The FFLOS photo captioned Smith Ridge Lookout 1942 (firetower.org media 2774) is an Oregon lookout in Douglas County and must not be attached to this Idaho record. Height 4.6 m is converted from the 15-foot figure. Visit fact is the Drive-Up tag only; no route or access level is in the sources. No new photos added. Our record's location (46.89819, -115.79393) is the FFLA value. The Idaho record value (46.8984, -115.7942) is a few tens of metres away, and the Idaho page text itself has no coordinates; no conflict is flagged.

No independent source found by search; Idaho Fire Lookouts staffing repeats the firelookout.com page. A 1933 Bonners Ferry Herald item (UIdaho CCC collection, cccidaho1816) mentions Smith Creek district lookouts but does not name this lookout, so it was not used. Record kind 'ground' follows the FFLA list; firelookout.com says tower. Editor may want to decide the kind and the build year.

Location conflict is unresolved. The FFLA list gives 46.80395, -115.47140 (the value in our record). The Idaho Fire Lookouts record value, 46.80541, -115.49874, is about 2.1 km away, and the Idaho page text we read has no coordinates to check it against. Map check needed before any pin is published. Dates agree across firelookout.com, the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The Forest Service list places it at Sec18 T40N R8E and gives elevation 4550 ft. No source describes the site today, and no removal date is given for the tower. No new photos added.

Record height_m 3.0 matches the 10-foot concrete base, not the total tower height; no source gives total height, so height_m is omitted. Both pages name William Lassiter for 1960, so there is no conflict; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Kjell Peterson for 1968, not 1960 (corrected in fact-check 2026-10-08). No notable fires were found in the sources checked, so no fire events are recorded. Access 'restricted' rests on the August 2024 Idaho Fire Lookouts visit and the undated Forest Service page; no 2025-26 check. Elevation in the record (2057.1 m) matches the NHLR figure.

Location conflict is unresolved. The FFLA list gives 46.44208, -115.59187 (the value in our record). The Idaho Fire Lookouts record value, 46.42231, -115.59164, is about 2.2 km south, and the Idaho page text we read has no coordinates to check it against. Map check needed before any pin is published. Dates and elevation agree across firelookout.com, the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Forest Service list places it at Sec33 T36N R7E. FFLA Tower Gone gives no removal date. No source describes the site today. Record county is Idaho; sources say Idaho County. No new photos added.

Destroyed 1958 (two sources) versus removed with no date (Forest Lookouts) is unresolved. The Boundary County Museum holds Bonners Ferry Herald runs that might date the loss; not read. No photos found. The only current description is the drive-up label.

The only current-condition source is the Idaho Fire Lookouts post dated September 29, 2023. No 2024-2026 status found. Brief elevation (2058.9 m) matches NHLR's 6,755 ft. Brief label 'abandoned 1969' is contested, so the story reports both labels. Access is public on the sources read; no closure notice was found. No fire history and no rental listing appeared in the pages read. Budget used: 6 page reads, 2 searches.

Design is described two ways: two-story concrete base with a frame cabin (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus a concrete building with an observation room (Forest Lookouts Idaho). Both are noted in the story; not resolved. Access evidence is from a climbing guide dated as of July 2017; no current road status found. Staffing is undated. No notable fires found in the sources read, so no fire events are recorded. A BLM Owyhee Field Office closure notice dated 2026-09-19 appeared in search results (blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-09/20260919_OwyheeFieldOfficeClosure.pdf); it was not read and may not concern South Mountain, so check before adding any fire event. The record's height_m is absent because no source gives a total height.

Brief events for 2008 (decision to remove) and 2014 (removal postponed) are not in the NHLR page, the FFLOS page, the Forest Lookouts list, firelookout.com or the 2015 chapter report, so they are omitted and need a source before they go back in. Access is set to public from land ownership and the 2022 description; no current access rule was found. The ground house is from NHLR only. Photo credits (Gary Weber, CDC Photography, Doug Miles) are not recorded because licences were not stated.

Build year, 1955 loss and the forest are agreed across all four sources. The record's coordinates come from FFLA, while idaho_fl gives a pair about 2 km away; neither page says which is right, so check the map before publishing. The 9.1 m height is the 30-foot pole figure converted; no source gives a separate height. No staffing is documented in any source read, so the story leaves staffing out. The brief's events were empty; built 1934 and destroyed 1955 are added here. Access is not established beyond the hike-in label, so no access level is set.

Four sources agree on the 1931 build and the 1934 loss to the Pete King Fire. The brief's record is missing a built event and recorded the loss as destroyed, so both are fixed here. Records us-id-split-creek-point-2 and the Cent. ID Hist. Museum cab entry describe the Payette NF lookout, which is a different tower; the museum cab should not be attached to this record. The 9.1 m height is the 30-foot figure converted. No source describes the site today and no access level is supported. The 1981 Hartig history is a local secondary source and gives no staffing names, so staffing is left out.

The museum move of the cab is supported by the Register and Idaho Fire Lookouts, but no museum source names a Split Creek cab; the story flags this. Idaho Fire Lookouts says the tower went to Lewiston, which no other source read confirms. Elevation conflict: the Register gives 5,017 ft (1,529 m), Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6628 ft; not used. The brief's events field ('None relocated...') is a note, not an event, so it was not used. A separate Selway-region 'Split Creek Point' lookout exists on the Idaho Fire Lookouts site (seen in a search snippet only, not read); keep the two records apart. The brief's source_pages point to a separate museum-site record, which may be a duplicate. No source read describes the original site today or whether it is open to the public. Used 6 page reads and 2 searches.

The date the cab was moved is not given by the register, and a search did not find it. The register (2020) says the residence cabin stayed at the original site. The 2016 climbing guide describes a 1930s cabin still on the summit; it may mean the residence cabin, or the lookout cab before it moved. The sources do not settle this. Height: the register says 72 feet and the guide says 75 feet. The record's coordinates and elevation (1,529 m) are the museum's in McCall, not the original summit; the guide gives the summit at about 45.108 N, -115.775 W and 6,628 ft, which belongs to the record for the original site. A search result named a different McCall museum lookout (Sloan's Point); not verified and not used. The 2008 chapter report calls the damaged building 'the Split Creek Point cabin' and does not say whether it was the lookout cab or the residence cabin. The record status standing is kept, with a status_note added because the tower is gone. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story previously said the report did not name a cabin; it does, so the story now quotes that wording.

Sources disagree on whether a structure existed. Three sources give a 1915 crow's nest; the 1981 Hartig history says the point was used as an observation station from 1939 and that no structure was ever built there. The record's kind 'platform' and status 'gone' are not contradicted outright, but the 1981 account suggests a camp rather than a built platform; the editor may want to revisit the kind. The Gold Meadows entry on the A-L page is the source of the 1939 observer line. The trail source is a commercial trail app, used only for the fact that the trail passes the mountain. No access level is supported, so none is set.

Main open question: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 2010 as the year it was abandoned, yet the same page is tagged Actively Staffed, and the Keeping Watch interview and firelookout.com describe current summer or funded staffing. No dated source resolves it; the story reports both. The Keeping Watch item metadata gives Date Created 2021-09-25. The Forest Service Selway-Bitterroot lookout table (fs.usda.gov/media/259187) lists Spot Mtn. at 9 miles northwest of Magruder R.S. with a two-story log cabin (1922) and a 10 ft pole L-4 (1934), but its status column is ambiguous, so it was not cited. The Lynx Fire call-in is described on Keeping Watch but is not recorded as an event. The 2017 Eagle Creek evacuation is tied to the tower by the interview and a photo caption, so it is recorded as a 2017 fire event (corrected in fact-check 2026-10-08). Record height_m 3.0 matches the 10-foot concrete base, not the total tower height; no source gives total height, so height_m is omitted. Record elevation 2445.7 m matches the NHLR 2,446 m figure. Reader comments on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page were not used as sources. Trail length is not given anywhere in the sources.

Four sources, all short. Dating (1930s) and never-finished/abandoned status agree across sources 1-3. Nothing found on staffing, fires or access. Firelookout.com credits a photo to the U.S. Forest Service but gives no image URL, so no photos entry. Not NHLR-registered per the FFLA listing. Record county 'Idaho' corrected to 'Idaho County'.

The brief holds two coordinate points for this site. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives 47.98506, -116.34007; the other point, 47.9684, -116.28799, is not in any page read, so it is unverified. The November 2024 visit post is the only account of the site today. The build year rests on one-line entries.

Brief lists kind=tower/status=standing, but the historic 53-ft L-4 tower cab collapsed and was removed in 2014 (see correction). What's rentable today is the separate restored ground house. Design field left as L-4 since both the (removed) tower cab and the (standing) ground house were L-4 type; editor may want a status field update to reflect the tower/groundhouse distinction. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): draft named 'Robert and Wayne McCormick's families' as 1951 staff, but neither firelookout.com nor idahofirelookouts.com lists a Robert McCormick -- only Wayne McCormick (1951) is documented -- fixed to remove the fabricated name. Also rewrote the 1950-tower sentence, which closely echoed NHLR's own wording ('53' CT-2 treated timber tower with standard 1936-model L-4 cab'), into the story's own phrasing.
Brief's status field 'standing' is consistent with sources (structure exists, under restoration, not destroyed); added status_note to flag it is not a routinely staffed or open lookout.

Thin record: no staffing, no fire history, no photos, and no description of the site after 1960. The 1934 approval is known only through Forest Lookouts' quote of a Ravalli Republic item; the paper itself was not read. Forest and tower-versus-cabin wording differs between the 1934 item and later pages.

Early history conflicts across three sources (1933 vs 1940 first cab; 1938 replacement vs 1938 lightning loss). The 1981 present cab, BLM ownership and fire-season staffing agree. The 2.4 m height in the brief has no source; the 24-ft figure comes from a 1959 NGS station description on the Idaho Lookouts page and describes a structure older than the 1981 cab. The 2022 rename is reported only by a climbing guide and should be checked against a federal name record before publishing. Staffing after 2015 is not documented. Visitor access rules were not found.

Thin record: three sites repeat the same few lines and none describes the site now. The brief's status 'gone' is not in any source; they say abandoned. The only disagreement is 1930 versus the 1930s. No photo, staffing or abandonment date found. Elevation 2,850 ft is in the story but the record has no elevation field used here.

Name clash: Wahoo (Squaw) Peak (Nez Perce NF, built 1934, destroyed 1940s, 46.16470 -114.64692 in the FFLA listing) is a different lookout from Squaw Peak (Bitterroot NF, 45.52967 -114.60491). The 1941/1967 dates rest on Kresek as cited by Rex's page and Firelookout.com. Kresek's book (Fire Lookouts of the Northwest) is named in the Forest Service list as its source. No source describes the site today. The Spokane Historical photo has no image URL in our cache, so no photos entry. Brief record is consistent with sources.

Status is the open question: FFLA says gone, two visitor reports describe footings. The 20-foot observation house from the 1964 NGS description supports the brief's 6.1 m height. Idaho Fire Lookouts says The Wigwams - as Squawman is now named, which can be read as a rename; the USGS quad uses The Wigwams (1996), so the story treats the two as alternate names and does not claim a rename. The Squawman name may need an editor decision. The Idaho Fire Lookouts trip report is dated September 16, 2025 but says the visit was in 2026, so its date is unreliable. Footing evidence rests on visitor reports, not a survey. Gate status is not confirmed. The brief's material 'wood' was not checked against any page read here.

Build-year chronology (1920s camp -> 1935 L-4 -> 1954 current cab) is consistent across sources. Fact-check (2026-10-04) found the original 'Hollenbeck in 1932 vs 1960' conflict was an error: the 1932 entry on idahofirelookouts.com belongs to a different person (Herb Uttley), and both Idaho Fire Lookouts and Firelookout.com actually date the Hollenbecks to 1960. The story and this file were corrected to drop the false conflict. No source gives current public-access status beyond 'used as a communications vault', so access is inferred as restricted rather than confirmed closed/open.

Brief record said destroyed 1960; sources say the 1960s. Built date is 1930s only. Firelookout.com credits a photo to Alvin Friedland but gives no image URL, so no photos entry. Shoshone County Forest Lookouts page on idaholookouts.weebly.com has a State Line entry, but the cached text gives no dates, so it is not cited. Nothing found on staffing, fires or current site condition.

Record is the Coeur d'Alene NF site (47.72346, -116.20595), Shoshone County. Other Steamboat Peak lookouts exist in Idaho and were not used: a Payette NF site in Idaho County (1931 12-foot tower, removed; idaholookouts.weebly.com Idaho County M-W page and Idaho Fire Lookouts West Central page, elevation 8,530 ft, destroyed 1966) and an Idaho County site at 45.21270 listed as Tower Gone on firelookout.org. The record's 1950 is only the decade in the sources (1950s), so the story says the 1950s. The 1950 destroyed event was dropped from events because no source gives a year; status_note carries the decade. Sources are thin: no staffing history, no description of the site today, no photo found. Record access 'unknown' could be set to the Idaho site's hike-in label, though that label sits on a destroyed site. Search budget: 2 searches.

Do not mix with the other Steamboat Peak lookout in Shoshone County (FFLA list coordinates 47.72346, -116.20595, Tower Gone), which is a different structure. A search snippet for that other lookout (idahofirelookouts.com/cda-region/steamboat-peak-lookout/) gives a 1930 camp and a 1934 40-foot pole L-4 tower destroyed in the 1950s; that page was not read in full and is not used here. The 1925 station may or may not be the site of the 1931 tower; the sources do not say, so the story only reports the item. The record's 3.7 m height matches 12 feet. No photo found, no staffing history beyond the 1925 item, and nothing on the site today.

Brief height_m 3.0 is the 10-ft concrete base, not a height; removed. Brief design R-6 is supported. Summer staffing is undated. The 2001-2002 Mullikin entry is the only named staff. Forest name: register says Salmon-Challis, the other two say Salmon National Forest. Current condition and access are not confirmed by a recent source. No fire or rental record found. No photo URLs captured.

Sources conflict and this is not resolved. Three sources (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, the April 2010 USFS Nez Perce list) give a 30-foot pole L-4 tower built 1933 and destroyed about 1954. The 1981 Hartig history, quoted on idaholookouts.weebly.com, describes a 100-foot steel tower built 1939 with a glass observatory and a cabin in 1941, cabin burned 1979, steel tower still standing in 1981, and does not mention the 1933 pole tower. These may be one point with a later replacement, or the accounts may simply conflict. The record's 'gone' rests on the firelookout.org list and the 1954 date. The weebly Stillman entry also carries a photo caption 'LQ - August 15, 2011 - Ron Kemnow photo'; I did not open the image, so I cannot say what it shows, and it could bear on whether the steel tower stands. The text extract of the 2010 USFS list lost its highlighting, so I cannot tell whether Stillman is marked as still existing. The list's destruction date carries a +/- marker, which the story now gives as a margin of error. Before publishing the 'today' line, check the Nez Perce NF records or the photo. Search budget: 2 searches.

Brief's access 'unknown' kept: no source gives an access level, so the access key is omitted. Brief's height 13.7 m matches the 1920 platform; the tower is 50 ft. Fate disagrees: 1972 destroyed (two sites) vs Removed (Forest Lookouts, undated). The 1913 TPA report predates the 1914 crow's nest date. Staff entry is first name only. No source describes the site today; the Drive-Up tag is a label, not a condition.

Brief height_m 3.0 has no source; removed. Brief status standing is changed to abandoned, the status all three sources give; no source describes its condition after the 2015 photo, so standing is not asserted. Build year conflict (1934 vs about 1945) is unresolved. The climbing guide quotes a 1982 Bing Young history; the primary text was not read. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists no staff. A rental or current-condition check would need a fresher source.

Brief's status (gone) and 1969 destruction are confirmed by all sources. Added design, 1930 firefinder, 1935 build date, and 1967 staffer. The 25-ft height converts to 7.6 m. Access is not given: the Drive-Up tag is a label, so no access level is recorded. No source describes the site today. The 1935 construction report comes through the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes the Newport Miner; the Newport Miner text was not read directly. Idaho Fire Lookouts' National Archives photo was not added because no image URL was captured.

Both pages agree on 1915, 1928 and the 1940s abandonment. Idaho Fire Lookouts records no documented staffing history, so no staffing fact is given. Elevation is unknown on both pages. Two web searches and a grep of a Potlatch annual report (pot_tpa1931-1932) found nothing about this lookout. A second tower record, data/towers/id/us-id-stony-creek-2.json, exists alongside us-id-stony-creek.json; it was not checked or changed. Agency PTPA is not expanded in either source.

Design conflict is unresolved. The register says a modified L-4 cab on a one-story log base, which matches the record's design L-4. The record's kind two_story matches the Forest Lookouts page, Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com, which say two-story, but the register says one-story. Not proposed as a correction; a human should check the 1928 build against a Forest Service or a photo. Forest name: the register says Salmon-Challis National Forest; firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page say Salmon National Forest (the older name). Staff items come from newspaper quotes on a fan site and from Idaho Fire Lookouts, not checked against the original papers. Access level 'public' is inferred from national forest land and the hike-in label; no closure notice was found. Not read: a Forest Service Moose Fire update on Facebook and a groups.io post, both in search results. The 2022 chapter report includes a personal 2009 visit by its author; not used.

Lineage is consistent: NHLR says the 1959 cab was replaced in 1983, and the Airbnb listing and Small Home Tours say a 1959 lookout left Stranger Peak in 1983 (Idaho Fire Lookouts says 1982). The Washington record (us-wa-stranger-mountain) says the 1983 cab went to Colville in 2008; the two records should be checked against each other so the Stranger Mountain facts match. The Washington record's 1994 staffing refers to the mountain, not this cab, so it is not used here. Unverified: a June 2026 BoiseDev headline (seen only in search results; the page returned 403) says the owner has listed this property for sale. It is not in the story; check before publishing any status change. Elevation of 4,729 ft from Idaho Fire Lookouts is not a facts key, so it is left out. Idaho Crystal Peak (gone) is about 1.5 km from the Crystal Ridge coordinates. No new photos with usable URLs were found.

Name is shared with other Strawberry Mountain lookouts in search results (Washington state; a working tower near McCall, Idaho). This record covers only the Bonner County site. Brief's height 12.2 m matches the 40-ft pole tower. Fate rests on a 1962 newspaper report that towers were being toppled and burned; no later source confirms the outcome, and Forest Lookouts gives status Removed. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history, so staffing is omitted from the story. No site condition found today. Hike-In tag read as drive_up false.

Build date unresolved: register says 1919/20 (built field circa 1919); Firelookout.com says 1924; register photo captioned circa 1924. Staffing entries for 1920 (Bryan, cited to a 1968 North Idaho Press item) and 1928 (Richardson, cited to a 1928 Wallace Press-Times item) come from Idaho Fire Lookouts; the newspapers were not read directly and the 1920 citation date needs a look. Elevation differs across sources: 6,300 ft (register), 6316 ft (Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts), 6,329 ft (1919 Wallace Miner). Forest name: register says Panhandle National Forests with Coeur d'Alene National Forest as cooperator; Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say Coeur d'Alene National Forest. Access comes from a 2021 climbing guide and Idaho Fire Lookouts' hike-in label; no closure or permit notice found. Facts omit a precise access level. The record's kind 'ground' and 1936 burned event are not contradicted. Register photo captions (1924 Forest Service photo, alidade photo) are not added as photos because no image URLs were read.

Dates agree across firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts (1918 crow's nest, 1928 cabin with pole tower, 1955 destroyed). Staff names come from a book by Bert Russell (Hardship & Happy Times) that I did not see; only Dennis has a year (1919), and the other two are shown with unknown years. The Shoshone County Forest Lookouts page has an empty Stubtoe entry, so it is not cited. No description of the site today was found. Record county Shoshone matches the firelookout.org list; the Idaho site names the St. Joe National Forest. Record access 'unknown' could be updated to the Idaho site's 'Drive-Up' label, which is in visit. Search budget: 2 searches.
Consistent, well-documented staffing history and an active-use status make this one of the more straightforward entries. Only wrinkle is the 1932 vs 1933 build-year discrepancy, noted in the story.

Brief's 1950 abandoned is not supported: every source says gone in 1952. All sources are secondary lookout-history sites; no Forest Service record was found for this tower. Idaho Fire Lookouts has no staffing history. No source describes remains or public access; the only access fact is the hike-in tag.

Brief design L-4 is the 1935 cab; corrected to R-6 for the current cab. Brief height_m 6.1 kept; sources disagree (20 ft vs 15 ft). Brief agency Idaho Department of Lands is confirmed. Staffing is volunteer-based; the Idaho Fire Lookouts page is dated 2021. Access and rental status are not stated. Keeping Watch (University of Idaho) and an IDL page were seen in search results but not read. Brief elevation_m 1919.6 agrees with the register's 6,298 ft (1,920 m).

Staffing is disputed: firelookout.com and Daytrip Northwest say staffed every summer, Trails Off Road says unmanned, and none is dated. The brief's height_m 3.0 has no source among the pages read, so it is omitted. The 1994 SITPA history names a Sunset Mtn. lookout but gives no location; the story flags the uncertainty rather than linking it. No rental listing turned up; no Boise NF or recreation.gov page was read. The event dated 1940 is a SITPA-era event that may belong to another mountain.

Record height_m 129.2 has no support in any source read. The lookout was a cab on a concrete base and no height is given, so the value should probably be cleared; it is not written as a correction because no replacement value exists. The Idaho list names Howard Crist in the early 1980s, after the 1975 destruction; left out of events and flagged in the story. Access is not stated by any source; the 2020 hike guide describes a gate signed restricted access on the approach, so the access level is left unset. Record elevation 1958 m matches the register (6,424 ft).

No source gives a specific year staffing ended; firelookout.com's 'emergency status for several years' phrasing was used as-is. Sources conflict on tower height (20ft vs 30ft) -- flagged in resolved_conflicts and in the story rather than resolved. Removed an unsupported 'network'/'Upper St. Joe country' characterization and an unsupported 1930s-1960s service-span claim from the story; neither was backed by a source quote.

The record mixes two towers. The brief's county (Lemhi), elevation (2,566 m) and registration (FFLOS US 831, registered January 24, 2011) describe the Lemhi County site, whose FFLOS coordinates are 45.014283, -114.192100. The 1934 L-4 design, 1955 destruction and Harrison-area location describe the Kootenai County tower. Recommend splitting into two records. The record's coordinates 47.50666, -116.6405 do not appear on any page I read; they are consistent with seven miles northeast of Harrison but are unverified. Idaho Fire Lookouts also lists a third Swan Peak on the St. Joe National Forest (4,838 ft, 1930s camp, abandoned); it is not in the story. The Kootenai dates come from secondary sites that credit a source named Kresek; I did not check a primary record. No source describes the site today.

Build year of current cab disputed (1954 vs 1958). Date staffing ended not found in sources. Brief's kind 'ground' fits the 1922 cabin; the current cab sits on a concrete base and the Forest Lookouts page calls it two-story, so consider kind two_story. No fire at this lookout was found. No rental found. The 1958 'Swan Home' clipping on the Forest Lookouts page is a different place and was not used. The FS page says 'Last updated September 21, 2026' and carries a header notice 'UPDATED Sept. 19 - Crooked Fire Area, Road, and Trail Closure'; the notice does not name this site, so the reason for the site closure is not confirmed. The Forest Lookouts page is the only source with clippings for the 1920s to 1940s staffing.

Brief had no events; added the 1931 build and the destruction. Destruction year conflicts (1953 Forest Service list vs 1954 in two Idaho-area sources). Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site drive-up. No source describes remains or public access.

The 1931 staffing item is quoted secondhand on the Forest Lookouts page; the Idaho Evening Times original was not read, and the story does not name the person. No source gives a cause for the 1952 destruction. A web search turned up a Roamze hiking page for a Tailholt in Payette NF; it is marked as an AI-suggested draft, names no lookout, and was not used. The Payette display text does not name this site. Record fields: built year and staffing were blank and are now in events; status gone is consistent with the sources.

Thin record. Every source here is a lookout list or site page; firelookout.com and the Forest Service list both draw on the same Kamstra and Forest Service records, so they are not independent confirmation of the 1933 date. No staffing history (the Idaho site says none is documented, left out of the story), no photo, and no access rules were found. The 12.2 m height is the 40-foot pole height as given, not checked against a measurement. Elevation 4,697 ft is from the Forest Service list and the Idaho site, not entered as a fact field.

The NHLR coordinates (N 43.306, W 111.921) fall outside Lemhi County and do not match the brief's lat/lon (44.885, -114.216). The Rex's page location (24 miles southwest of Salmon) fits the brief's coordinates, so the brief's coordinates were left alone; the NHLR coordinates look wrong. The elevation conflict (7,414 vs 9,960 ft) is not settled; check USGS before relying on either. Access and permission are not stated on any page read. Read budget used: the Trailforks trail page returned HTTP 403.

The 1936 call-in is quoted secondhand from a Spokane Chronicle item on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not read. The 1931 'camp' entry is given without a cab, so it is kept as an 'other' event. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists known staff for 1934–1935 and for 1937; the story does not use them. A search for Taylor Peak surfaced Taylor Mountain in the Big Creek area of central Idaho, which has a lookout ruin; that is a different peak and was not used. No source gives a cause for the 1959 destruction or describes the site today.

The splattski.com trip report linked from the Forest Lookouts page (2018 Teapot trip) returns HTTP 404 on both http and https and was not used, so no source describes the Teapot Dome site today. Web searches on Teapot Dome mostly return the Wyoming oil reserve. The record status gone is proposed as moved for human review. Miners Peak dates disagree (1983 per Idaho Fire Lookouts, 1986 per the register and Firelookout.com); the Miners Peak story covers that dispute. The 1950s Guard School use comes from Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The register calls the 1986 two-story cab wood frame, while Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts both describe the two-story cab as log; the story treats the 1983 and 1986 entries as one cab.

Dates agree across four pages, but all are secondary lookout-history sites. The 1950 date is confirmed; the brief's abandoned is replaced by removed. The site notes (undated visit) describe footings and wire at the summit, which is the only physical-remains evidence found. No source says whether the site is open to the public.

Three of four listings give the 1924 camp, the 1935 L-4 cab and the 1958 destruction; the weebly page gives only the 1935 and 1958 dates and attributes them to Kresek. No staffing, cause of loss or present-day description was found, so the story leaves those out. The 6,924 ft elevation comes from idahofirelookouts.com and is not a brief field. No photos added; firelookout.com credits its photos to the Forest Service.

Brief status gone and the 1958 destruction are confirmed by four sources. Thompson Point does not appear in the 2016 Clearwater National Forest lookout list (fs.usda.gov/media/259184), which was searched. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history, so staffing is omitted. No source says whether the site is open to the public, so facts.access is omitted. No source gives the cause of the 1958 destruction. The 'Clearwater Timber Protective Association' agency comes from the county list only; firelookout.com uses the abbreviation CTPA.

Gone status rests on the FFLA list alone; both detail pages say only abandoned. The patrol point is one mile southwest atop Pinnacle Ridge in both sources, but neither says whether the cabin stood there or on the mountain, so the story does not say. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history and no fire history was found, so those are omitted. The Shoshone County Forest Lookouts list (idaholookouts.weebly.com/shoshone-county.html) has a Thor Mountain entry with no history lines, so it is not cited. Confidence is medium because only two short pages and one list describe the site.

Current status is not confirmed. A search result titled 'Thorn Creek Butte Lookout Tower [CLOSED]' on AllTrails could not be opened (HTTP 403), so it is not relied on; verify before any visit. No Forest Service page for this lookout was found. Not on the FFLA rentals list as far as the grep showed. The 1974-1982 staffing dates are the only dated staffing. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'restricted' on the basis of the sources' emergency-only language, which is a judgement call. A 2026 Crooked Fire closure near Idaho City appeared in search results but was not checked against this site.

Thin record: two lookout listings, one weebly page and a state index. None describes the site after the 1980s. The weebly photos come from the Bitterroot archive with permission required, so none were added. The brief's gone status is not supported by any source read; the correction proposes abandoned for editor review.

Dates are decades only (1930s, 1940s). The 2022 visit is the only physical evidence, and it is one party's search. Elevation: idahofirelookouts.com says 3600 ft (about 1,097 m), while the brief says 1111.3 m (about 3,646 ft); not corrected. The weebly page's 1930s camp credit was not used because its text was not confirmed. No free-licence photos found.

Build dates conflict: 1962 (NHLR field, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus 1962 or 1965 (NHLR description) and 1965 (Forest Lookouts). Cupola date 1933 versus 1922. Elevation 8,656 ft (NHLR) versus 8652 ft (firelookout.com). Staffing is seasonal and undated. No notable fire was recorded in the pages read. The brief's events for 1962 and the 2020 registration are supported. One search snippet, not read, described a jeep trail to within about 5 miles of the summit; it is unverified and not used. Current 2026 access was not confirmed.

Thin record: sources give decade-only dates and no current site description. Staffing is left out because Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented. The brief's status 'gone' is not supported by any source; the proposed correction is 'abandoned'. No photos added: firelookout.com has a 'Click for larger image' link but no image URL was extracted. Story is short on purpose.

The brief's status 'gone' is corrected to 'ruins' because the Idaho Fire Lookouts post describes footings and debris on the site. That 2023 post is the only source for the current state of the site and for the road being passable only on foot, so it may be out of date. The 1934 L-6 tower is disputed and is reported as disputed. Section numbers differ: the Clearwater County list gives 38N-12E-05 and the 2016 Forest Service list gives Sec38N R12E 12; the story does not use section numbers. height_m is a conversion of the 35-foot platform figure. No staffing or fire history was found, so those are omitted. No source says whether the site is open to the public, so facts.access is omitted.

Three sources agree on the 1934 build, L-4 design and 1950s abandonment. The 2022 Idaho Fire Lookouts post is the only physical description of the site. Staffing: no staff list found; the 1945 self-portrait is the only person-at-site detail and comes from a blog post describing a photo, not from a staffing record. No photos added: the image source and license were not confirmed. Crow's-nest platform's fate is not described by any source.

Agency is the main correction: the brief has Bitterroot NF, but current sources say Nez Perce NF, with the 1957 transfer. Section number disagrees between Rex's page (33) and the FS list (23); the story avoids it. Staffing: no source found. The 1934 L-4 entry comes from an undated inventory, so it is shown as a listing, not a dated build. No photos added. The FS PDF is a text extraction: the cite 4 quotes are single-line fragments of the Tony Point row, which also carries the 1933 and abandoned-1950 columns.

All three pages give the same 1930, 1934 and 1972 dates, and the weebly page cites Kresek for them, so they are probably not independent. The 'Known Staff' entry on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page reads '??? Leon Green (White Pines & Fire Book)' with no dates; the story names him as an undated listing and he is kept out of facts. No source describes the site today or its access. Searches for current site access returned only nearby Lookout Butte pages, which were not used.

Thin record: four sources, one of them a list. Core facts agree (1930s cabin and crow's nest, abandoned, Clearwater National Forest). The 1941 abandonment date and the Long Creek Ridge identity are disputed; the story reports both and the correction proposes removing the merged other_names entry for human review. The brief's kind 'platform' is kept as is. Staffing is left out of the story because the only source says none is documented. The FS list's columns are cut off, so the trailing 'None' value in its rows is not used. Used 1 search and 5 page reads.

Thin record: three short lookout listings, all with the 1930s date and none with a build year, and no staffing names. The 1967 Sundance-Trapper Peak fires in search results are a Boundary County story (oral histories on the Boundary County Museum site); they are probably a different peak and were not used. A geocache listing from search, which was not read, places a cache at the cabin site on a peak it calls Trapper Flat Peak; not cited. The lookout's elevation is 7892 ft on Idaho Fire Lookouts, not stored in facts because the story does not need it.

Elevation differs (6032 ft on firelookout.com, 6320 ft on Idaho Fire Lookouts); not stored in facts. A Facebook post from search says the lookout was built in 1921; not read, not cited. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page dates its 2026 visit and says a fire has since changed the site, with no date for the fire. No new photos recorded; the page images had no URLs in the cached text.

Staffing is dated: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a page date of September 3, 2021 and a staff list running to approximate 2008 to 2023, so current staffing may differ. Access level is not stated on any page read; the story asks visitors to get permission first. The brief's height_m 3.0 is the 10-foot base only and is proposed for removal. The 1922 vs 1956 build-year conflict is recorded in resolved_conflicts.

The brief's height_m 1.8 has no source among the pages read, so it is omitted. Concrete base 1950 (NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus 1956 (firelookout.com). Elevation 8,082 ft (NHLR) versus 8086 ft (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts). The association's name is spelled Protection on the NHLR and Protective elsewhere; the story uses Protective. Current staffing is unconfirmed: the association's undated employment page names only Brundage and Lookout mountains. No closure or rental notice was found. The brief's events for 1921, 1977 and 2020 are supported.

Only the 1931 fire finder listing is sourced directly; the 1947 tower date is an inference from benchmarks that the Idaho Fire Lookouts writers themselves call a guess. No source gives a year for abandonment, so no abandoned event was added. Do not confuse with us-id-trout-peak-2 (Idaho County camp, a different site). The record had no events; the events above come from the sources. The site's current access rules are not stated in any source read.

Very thin sourcing. The only dated item is 1937 with an unknown type. The Bethlehem Mountain entry (firelookout.com/id/bethlehem.html) places a 1937 20-foot pole L-4 tower on the southwest point of Tungston Mountain; a human should decide whether that is the same structure, and whether the Bethlehem Mountain site needs its own record. No staffing history is documented (Idaho Fire Lookouts says so). Access is not stated in any source read, so no access key was written.

Two detailed sources agree on the 1934 build, the 1969 destruction and the L-4 pole design. Staffing names come only from Idaho Fire Lookouts, which cites a book and the Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry; not checked against those. The drive-up tag is Idaho Fire Lookouts' label; no source states an access level, so none is set. The 2023 footings are from one visitor's post. The record's status 'gone' matches the sources and is not changed. Used 1 search and 3 page reads; no further sources found.

Two conflicts left open: (1) 1954 fate, destroyed (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus Removed (Forest Lookouts); (2) the 1933 lookout entry predates the 1939 tower, and no source explains that. The record did not list the 1939 build; it is added here from the sources. The record's 1954 destroyed event stands.

Brief's agency (Bitterroot NF) is the pre-1957 agency; see corrections. First build date conflicts (1925 vs 1928 for the platform). Idaho Fire Lookouts' Known Staff block shows ??? above the Dunlop name, so treat the staff entry as unverified. The USFS list cites photos from 1927-1929 but gives no image URL, so no photos added. No source states access level; access left out of facts.

The record's status 'ruins' is kept. The brief's conflict note says firelookout.com reads 'standing', but that page says 'Superstructure remains still there.' No source gives an access level, so none is set; the story says so. The 1946 windstorm year comes from peakbagging.com only, and Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give no year for the storm. Staffing names are from two lookout-history sites, not checked against the cited photo collection or newspaper. Used 1 search and 5 page reads.

Three conflicts need an editor's call: the 1932 structure (L-4 vs R-1), the 1964 base (concrete vs cinder-block), and elevation (10,337 vs 10,394 ft). Current staffing is contested. Access is set to public on the Chamber's visitor listing; the cab's interior is not described, so confirm with Salmon-Challis NF before treating the cab as open. The brief's height_m of 3.0 is the base height, not total height. No rental found. The FS page names three staffed lookouts and does not name Twin Peaks, but it does not say which unstaffed lookouts remain.

Thinnest of the three: every source gives a one-line history (1930s crow's nest, abandoned), with no staff, fire or construction detail. Coordinates conflict (see corrections); the FFLA listing is the only source we read with coordinates. Story length is short because the evidence is short. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page marks it Hike-In Abandoned and gives 4,032 ft.

Destruction year conflict (1957 vs removed before 1956) is the main open question. The Forest Lookouts directions come from a Geodetic Survey block and may be out of date, so the story presents them as what the page says. No photos found. The 1956 survey tablet is described in 1956 terms; no source says whether it is still there.

Four pages agree on the 1934 date, the 55-foot L-4 pole tower and the gone status. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page lists drive-up ruins, but no source confirms current road access, gate status or what the ruins look like, so access.level is left unset. No staffing, fire or removal date was found; the Idaho page says it has no documented staffing history. The Forest Lookouts page cites Kresek as its source for the 1934 entry, and that book was not read. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page also exists at a second URL (north-idaho-panhandle-region) with the same text. The brief's access field was 'unknown'; nothing here settles it.

Record's built year 1828 is a typo in NHLR's data field; 1928 is used. Sources disagree on end of use: Idaho Fire Lookouts says abandoned 1968, Forest Fire Lookout says not used since the 1970s. The cabin burning in 2012 rests on Forest Fire Lookout alone; the Idaho writer's 2012 photos show the cabin still standing. Access is unknown. The tower has broken ladder rungs and missing platforms; the story does not encourage climbing. Forest name differs between sources (Salmon vs Salmon-Challis). Idaho Fire Lookouts post dated January 16, 2023. Staffing history rests on that one site.

Build and destruction years agree across three sources; the CCC photo independently places a tower on Uranus Peak around 1938. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists two known staff under year headings, Lorenzo Lanter (1935) and Ernest Milot (1937); both are stored as staffed events. No source gives access or the site's condition today, so access level is unset. Record elevation_m is null; the sources give 4,977 ft (about 1,517 m), which has no facts key and was not stored. The CCC photo image URL was not captured, so no photos entry was added. The Coeur d'Alene NF attribution rests on the association and Forest Lookouts pages; the one web search found no other history.

Record kind is 'ground' from the association list. The 2016 Forest Service list describes a 50-foot spar pole platform with an L-4 cab, which could support 'tower', while the association's wording ('accompanying L-4 cab') could support 'ground'. Left unchanged for the editor to decide. The Forest Service list notes one USFS photo, which was not fetched; the existing idahofirelookouts photo stays. A cached Clearwater Story appendix (Appendix B) has a Van Camp entry, but its URL is not in the cache index, so it is not cited. Facts design is written to cover both platform heights, so no height_m is stored. Access level is not stated by any source and is left unset.

The record's county (Shoshone) and ground kind match the association's list and need no correction. The Forest Lookouts Shoshone County page lists Vanderbilt Hill with a township only and no history, so it is not cited. The one web search found no further history. No source gives access or the site's condition today, so access level is unset. No photos were found; the Forest Service list records none for this site.

Three sources agree on a 1924 log cabin with cupola, about 16 miles northeast of Elk City. Abandonment is dated only to the 1930s (Idaho listing) or by the late 1930s (firelookout.com), so the abandoned event uses 1930 as a placeholder year for the decade. Both Vermillion pages say Disgrace Butte may have replaced it, two miles southwest; the Disgrace Butte page says the same tower may have replaced Vermillion Peak, two miles northeast. These two directions describe the same pair, so they are not a conflict. No staffing or fire history was found. Do not confuse with the Montana Vermillion Peak (Kootenai NF, 23N-29W-9, built 1936 per montanalookouts.weebly.com/vermillion-peak.html), which is a different lookout and was not used. The brief's kind 'ground' matches the FFLA list's 'Ground' type. No current access information was found.

Four sources agree on a 30-foot pole observation tower and cabin in 1934 (cites 2 to 5, including the Selway-Bitterroot list, whose Wahoo (Squaw) row gives the same 1934 date and 1940s destruction), and all five that give a status date the destruction to the 1940s. The Nez Perce NF list says it draws on Ray Kresek's book and other sources, so these agreements are not fully independent. The 1925 log cabin appears only on the Forest Lookouts site, citing an undated inventory. A Spokane Historical photo from 1960 is captioned 'Squaw Peak Lookout' and places it in the Bitterroot NF, which fits poorly with the 1957 transfer to Nez Perce NF and the 1940s destruction; it may show a different Squaw Peak, so the story does not count it as evidence the tower survived. The FFLA list also has a separate 'Squaw Peak' (Idaho/Lemhi, 45.52967 -114.60491, Ground Gone) that is a different record and was not used. The Idaho page lists a hike-in and wilderness context, but no current access, remains or staffing information. The Forest Service Selway-Bitterroot list is a list of lookouts, not a statement of the site's legal status, so the story says only that it includes the site.
Brief's location conflict (NHLR vs RIDB coordinates, a few hundred meters apart) not addressed here since it concerns map data, not the narrative. No new photos found.

Brief record checks out: gone, destroyed 1958, Kaniksu NF, Boundary County. Two sources agree on a 30-foot L-4 tower built in 1937, but the Forest Lookouts page says only Removed, with no date. The 1933 staff name (Frank Heath) predates the 1937 build on the same page, and the story reports this without resolving it. Staffing comes only from three names, with no dates of service. No source describes the site today and no access status was found, so access is left out. Searched twice; no photo with a license was found.

Fate is disputed: Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Willhite Web page both tie the end to 1947, but the firelookout.com listing says the tower was offered for sale in 1953 and removed. The record's '1947 destroyed' is kept as the Idaho date. Access level is left unstated because no source says whether the site is open. The Willhite captions also call the summit 'Wall Mountain' in places, so searches may need that name. The record's county and coordinates are not contradicted by these sources.

Elevation conflict: NHLR says 5,890 ft; three other sources say 5,981 ft. Correction proposed, editor to confirm. The 1968 date is the current structure; earlier lookouts from the 1920s, 1932 and 1934 are noted but the 1920s date is only a decade. Only two staff names are on record (1974, 1977). Rental status is disputed (Forest Service list vs two web sources). The Hike-In Emergency tag is read from the Idaho Fire Lookouts header. No height_m in the record; sources give a 10-ft tower. Post dated October 2, 2025.

The two web listings give the same years and may share a source. Staffing rests on one Known Staff entry (Boyd Hanna, 1930) that cites a book; the book itself was not read. No route, remains or access rule was found, so the story is short. The record's coordinates are not contradicted by these sources.

Build year conflicts (1931 first tower vs NHLR 1961) and the staffing schedule differ across sources. A WebSearch snippet mentions a 2000 Burgdorf Junction Fire spotting role and fire-wrapping; not verified on a fetched page, so left out. Current record height_m 3.0 is the ten-foot block base, not total height. Access left restricted; no source documents public climbing or rental.

Dates agree across three sources except the brief's '1950', which all three replace with 'the 1950s'. Elevation 7,312 ft from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. 'Public' access is inferred from the hike-in description on national forest land; no source states it. Great Burn Lakes is a hiking site, so the summit-remnant claim rests on one source.

Brief record checks out: gone, Caribou-Targhee NF, Fremont County, 30-foot (9.1 m) height. Lists give 25 feet for the 1940s cab, and only the 1948 newspaper quotes give 30. Elevation differs: 6615 ft (Idaho listing) vs 6054 ft (firelookout.com); not used. The 1976 burn date comes only from the Idaho listing. A Facebook post by the FFLA group, seen only as a search snippet, says possibly burned in the 1960s; not read, so not used. A 2023 Pastmaps map blurb in search results still refers to a Warm River Lookout as a vantage point; not read, and it looks generated, so not used. Access 'public' is inferred from the 2011 road account and the lack of any closure notice; verify before relying on it. The only visit account is the July 2011 blog post; no later description was found.

Brief status 'gone' is contradicted: the index and both lookout pages say abandoned, and none says the structure was removed; corrected. Thin record: four short listings, no staffing names, no visit or access report, and no photo. Elevation 3,978 ft agrees across firelookout.com and the Idaho listing. The Forest Lookouts page credits the crow's nest to a name in parentheses; left out. Brief kind 'platform' is a reasonable fit for a crow's nest, so not corrected. Access not stated; left out.

Fixes to the record: height_m 9.1 is the 1931 pole tower; the current 53-ft tower is about 16.2 m. Access moved from unknown to closed per the Forest Service page (updated 2025-02-19); the search snippet of a camping listing and a trail guide were not read and are left out. The 1931 pole-tower height appears as 30 ft in NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts. No documented staffing history exists. The earlier fs.fed.us URL in the queue record does not resolve; the fs.usda.gov page was used instead. The 16 vs 38 mile discrepancy from Pierce is unresolved and reported as such.

Record has two coordinate sets: Forest Lookouts 46.55082, -114.8172 and Idaho Fire Lookouts 46.5366, -114.82506.
