Visit climbability rests on the 2026 newspaper; the condition is not independently confirmed, so the editor may want to flag it. Used 2 WebSearch and about 6 page reads.

Brief's height 7.3 m is the 24-foot 1918 steel tower; the standing tower is 30 feet (9.1 m). Brief's 2018 break-in is not supported: WMTW reports vandalism and firefighter repairs in May 2019, and no 2018 source was found. Brief's 2008 stair repaint has no source found, so it is dropped. Brief's 2019 brace replacement is only the FFLA grant awarded for materials; completion is not confirmed, so the story says the grant was awarded. Unresolved: the watchman's name in the 1947 fire (Mike Ferguson per the marker, Donald Ferguson per the 1947 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts), and the register date (1996) versus the marker's 1997 acceptance. Access: how visitors arrange entry is not verified. The 2025 plans for stair work and cab siding are not included.

Only three sources; the 1947 build is from a 1947 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts, not the original. Removal is a window (1976-1993) from FFLOS, with no other source. The rusted base is from a 2016 write-up and is not dated or tied by that write-up to the 1947 tower. Do not merge with the Peaked Mountain in Washington County (44.88795, -67.91016, 'Tower Gone' on the FFLOS Maine list), which is a different site. A Maine lookout database quoted in a search summary (35-foot steel tower, removed in the 1980s, 1,200 ft) could not be opened (firelookout.org/lookouts/me/me.htm returned 404), so it is not used. The FFLOS page does not give a height.

Thin record: the only history is a 1950 newspaper item (quoted on Forest Lookouts) and the 2008 report. The 1950 item calls the tower newly built, so 1950 is a build-by date, not a confirmed build year; the brief has no build date. The Press Herald spells the name Peek-a-Boo. Height, design, staffing and fate beyond standing were not found. FFLA list shows no cab asterisk, which the legend says means the cab is gone when marked; treated as cab still present. Brief access 'unknown': only 'popular hiking destination' was found, so access level public is an inference; check the land owner. Search returned no further history. firelookout.org/lookouts/me/me.htm returned 404; Maine Atlas fire-tower page had no Peekaboo entry. Brief 2008 restoration event is supported by the report; brief wording 'paint still to come' is consistent.

Current cab and tower condition is unresolved: FFLA gives no asterisk (cab presumed in place), the Press Herald says boarded up, and Secret Falls describes a glass cab in present tense. A search summary said the tower was lowered to 36 ft in 1960 and that the Maine towers were abandoned by the 1960s; neither was verified in a page read, so both are left out. A Conway Daily Sun article on a replica map stand returned HTTP 429 and was not read. Search summary ownership figures (Loon Echo about 2,000 acres, TNC 1,400 acres, Maine Forest Service 20 acres) were not verified and are not used. The OpenStreetMap way was not read. The Press Herald article's date was not shown in the text read, so it is not cited by date. Brief height_m 20.0 is proposed for removal (see corrections).

No source after 2009 describes the site. The Senate release (January 27, 2009) spells the name Priestley; the record and Forest Lookouts use Priestly. The story says only that a 1929 steel tower was planned; the FFLA Facebook caption dated to 1929 could not be read, so it is not used. Access is not described, so no access level is given. The record height of 6.1 m matches the 1920 inventory.

Access, ownership and the date the cab came down are not in any source reached. No trail or visitor source found for this Penobscot County mountain; the search returned a different Ragged Mountain in Knox County (Camden/Rockport), which is not this tower and was not used. Height conflict: the record's 11.0 m matches the 1917 36-foot figure; the 1920 inventory says 48 feet. Visit and access keys omitted until confirmed.

Probably the same mountain as us-me-rocky-mountain-2 (National Historic Lookout Register point, FFLA list coordinates 47.19176, -69.28156). This record's FFLOS point (47.27678, -69.28333) is about 9 km further north; decide whether the two should be merged. The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with the FFLA list. Photos: the firetower.org page credits a repeater photo to the St. John Valley Amateur Radio Association, but no image URL was captured, so no photo entry. The register misspells the association as 'Amatuer', kept verbatim in the quote.

Height: register says 54 ft (16.5 m); the 1920 inventory and 1921 newspaper item say 48 ft (14.6 m). The record's 14.6 m is kept; the conflict is unresolved. Early history: a 1917 wooden tower (warden report) conflicts with a 1919 report of a log tower on another bluff; unresolved. The 2017 cab loss is confirmed by two sources. The FFLA list marks the tower Standing*, and its footnote defines that mark as a tower whose structure stands with the cab no longer in place; the steel tower's standing rests on that list, and the cab loss on the 2017 report and Forest Lookouts. Access is by permit from private timber roads; no permit contact or trail details were verified. Ownership: the register places it in the Maine North Woods with 7 Island Land Co. named; the owner is not stated.

No source read gives staffing, fire history, or public access for this tower, so no access or staffing key is recorded. The brief's 1914 build date refers to the first site; the present site dates only to the 1940s. Registration date confirmed on the NHLR page. A social-media photo caption was seen but not used because it is not a citable source. Brief coordinates differ slightly from the FLO list (46.54703, -69.76447); not material.

No current access, ownership or cab-removal date found. Searches returned an unrelated Round Mountain in Albany Township near Bethel (private land with a trail, no tower), and the FFLA list shows a different Round Mountain in Franklin County (a tree, gone); neither was used. A geocaching page describing an old tower names no county and was not used. Height of 48 ft (14.6 m) agrees with the record. Visit and access keys omitted until confirmed.

Access conflict is unresolved: the undated Maine Trail Finder guide says the decommissioned tower should not be climbed until further notice, while the 2020 BDN column (by the Allagash superintendent) says the new cabs are for visitors. The record's 2018 'restored' event is recorded here as maintenance and cab planning; the 2020 cab is recorded as 'replaced'. No build date, builder or height found. The 2020 report says the Bureau of Parks and Lands pre-built one cab at its Ashland facility and Shiretown Structures of Houlton built the other two; the column names a local contractor, which is consistent with that, so the builder is treated as resolved. The 2018 report says the Ashland-built cab was for this tower. Access level set to restricted pending the Bureau of Parks and Lands.

Build history is well documented (1914 wood, 1920 steel with cab), and the brief's height (7.3 m, 24 ft) matches. Status is the open question: FFLA lists it as standing with cab gone, but the Forest Lookouts record gives a 2005 'Lookout structure removed' with no detail; no modern photo or visit report was found. Staffing is inferred from the statewide 1991 end of the network, not a tower-specific record. Access rests on the public Donnell Pond trail; whether the old tower itself is climbable is unverified, so no climbable flag is set. Watchmen 1917-1919 come from a photo caption only. The brief's agency name is kept as the historical Maine Forestry District. Maine Memory record 1514 (ca. 1920) is a photo candidate, not added because its licence was not checked. Recommend a site visit or a current photo before any status claim is strengthened.

Build dates (1910 wood, 1914 steel with cab) agree across the Forest Lookouts page and the Maine Memory record. Staffing is documented only for Don Hicks (1966-1967 per the Sun Journal). FFLA and FranklinSites agree the cab is gone; neither gives a date, so no event is dated for the cab loss. Access is the weak point: the summit sits on Penobscot Indian Nation land behind a gate, and no source states a permit or public-visit rule either way, so the access level is set to restricted rather than public. The Maine by Foot and SummitPost pages describe hiking routes, which were used only for the gate and the distance; they do not endorse climbing the structure, and the story says not to. Summit elevation differs across sources (3,948 ft at the tower site per Maine Memory; 3,960 ft and 3,967 ft per FranklinSites and Maine by Foot); not used in the story. Photo candidate Maine Memory record 19137 is not added because its licence was not checked.

Thin record: the detailed history stops at 1920 on the Forest Lookouts page, and the only later evidence is the FFLA Standing* listing. Height conflict (12 ft in three records vs 16 ft in one caption) is resolved toward 12 ft; the brief's 3.7 m matches. Access and land ownership were not found in any source, so no access or visit block is set. Staffing is inferred from the statewide 1991 end of the network. A Facebook photo post seen in search results describes a late-1950s photo and says the tower was still standing the year before and had lost its cab long ago. It was not used, because it is an unverified social-media post and was not fetched; it is a lead for someone who can check it. Photo candidate Maine Memory record 19135 (ca. 1920) is not added because its licence was not checked.

Sources conflict on whether anything stands here now: FFLA says standing with cab gone, the lookout history says removed with no date, and the register says unknown. No staffing record was found. The 48-foot and 26-foot heights need the original 1917 and 1918 reports. Facebook posts by the FFLA Maine chapter mention a 1918 wooden tower and a Scopan Mountain name, but Facebook pages could not be read, so they are not cited. The FFLA list also has a separate Haystack Mountain log tower entry (gone); the register suggests a link, which we did not confirm. Worth a field check or an FFLA Maine chapter contact before publishing a status.

Possibly the same tower as us-me-squa-pan-mountain (FFA point 46.57080, -68.19996, same Forest Lookouts history). The two records split the register point from the FFA point; editor should decide whether to merge. The register spells the town 'Marsardis'; the story uses Masardis. No staffing, fire or access-permission evidence found. Two searches turned up no further Squa Pan history.

The brief's NHLR slug for the relocated site (squaw-mountain-at-greenville-visitor-center) returned 404 in the cache and live, so it is not cited. The height of 3.7 m comes from Forest Lookouts' '12-foot' figure, which may describe a different structure or the cab; NHLR gives no height. Build, closure and relocation dates conflict across sources and are shown as conflicts, not settled. Access to the summit is not confirmed. The brief's 'Greenville Visitor Center' name is not used because no source read says it.

Sources disagree on several dates and on what was moved. Staffing end: WMTW says 1976, Maine Memory says the tower closed in 1968. Move: WMTW says the cab went to the visitor center in 2011 by helicopter; Maine Geographic says the tower was reassembled in 2015; Maine Memory says October 2012 to the Natural Resource Education Center. The register's 1959 date for the present steel tower conflicts with 1919 elsewhere. The register entry (US 67) still describes the summit site, not Greenville. Agency for the Greenville tower is not documented (the register lists the Maine Dept. of Conservation for the summit site), so it is left out. The NREC page (nrecmoosehead.org) returned 404 and was not used. Access is marked public only because the tower sits beside a visitor center that Maine Geographic calls worth a visit; climbing is not documented. The Commons photo already in the record was not re-added. Page reads: about 6 distinct pages, plus one search.

The tower is described as standing with its cab in place (FFLA lists no asterisk). Open conflicts: build year 1920 (Maine Memory) versus 1923 (state page and map); height 47 ft (state page) versus 55 ft (trail listing); and the National Register listing date versus the page's eligible wording. A Facebook post by the FFLA Maine chapter says it is now on the National Register; Facebook could not be read, so it is not cited. The Maine Preservation Most Endangered list was not read directly; the Maine Memory page reports it without a year. Last fire-observation use 1967 comes from the state's period of significance, not a staffing record, so no last watchman is named.

Only two register pages could be read. Neither gives a build date, watchmen, fires, or present-day condition, so the story leaves those out and says no source describes the site today. A Facebook search snippet (Forest Fire Lookout Association, Maine chapter) describes a 1950 tower in Wade, not Washburn, but the Facebook page returned no readable text, so nothing from it is used and the Washburn/Wade difference is unresolved. The anyplaceamerica directory returned HTTP 403. The brief's 'share a register number' note is answered in resolved_conflicts. Used 3 websearch.py calls, one over the per-tower budget of 2, and about 6 page reads.

Height_m 10.4 is the 34-foot figure converted (34 x 0.3048); the 1987 replacement's height is not given. The 2021 article's closed-to-hikers caption is the only source for current access; no fresh visit report was found. A Maine Forest Service Facebook post (seen only as a search snippet, not fetched) says the lookout closed permanently about 1991; it is not used because it could not be read. Named fires: none found. Staffing field is inferred from the 2021 article's list of active towers, not from a staffing record. Facebook sources were not used as citations.

The cab-gone status rests on one FFLA asterisk and has no date; no current photo or visit report was found. The 1920 inventory is cited through the Forest Lookouts transcription, not the original inventory. No access level is recorded because no source describes access; the site's land ownership is not stated in the sources read. Maine Memory photo credit and licence not recorded (no image URL verified). Facebook snippets about this watchman camp were seen in search results but not fetched, so they are not cited.

Built and rebuilt dates (2020) agree across three sources. The 1931 station move rests on a Maine Memory caption that sits beside a Black Cat Mountain photo, so it may refer to another structure. The closure is only given as 'the 1970s'; no source gives a year. The 120-ft height, the 1940s date and the Alabama origin rest on Davana's page alone, and the Conservancy only says 'Alabama'. Name correction needs human sign-off. Summit elevation disagrees (1,409 vs 1,427 ft). Sources treat the tower as open to hikers, but none states a formal public-access rule for the tower itself.

Dates and dimensions agree between Maine Memory and the Eastern US Lookouts page. The cab removal date is unknown; the only condition evidence is the FFLA note and a 2021 trip report. No current owner, access rule or condition report was found, and the trip report describes a bushwhack, so the story does not encourage a climb. The 1915 'staffed' event rests on a photo caption and the watchman's note, not on a staffing record. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Maine post says the tower has not really been manned since the 1930s, but I did not read that post, so it is not used.

Build history is unclear: a 1919 map shows a fire tower, and 1926 steel-tower work is the first documented construction. The sources do not say whether the 1926 tower replaced the 1919 one, so the story does not claim it. The record's 2013 'restored' event should read as stabilization, not restoration. No source describes the site today or public access. FFLA Facebook posts about the 2017 removal could not be read, so they are not used.

Record conflict: the FFLA Maine list gives Wesley Mountain (44.95105, -67.65893) as 'Tower Gone' and a separate Day Hill entry (44.96743, -67.64806) as 'Tower Standing*', about 2 km apart (2.0 km by great-circle distance from the listed coordinates). The 1918 map calls the site Wesley Hill (Wesley Mt. or Day Hill). The existing us-me-day-hill record treats the two as one site and calls it standing without its cab; this story does not settle that and the two records should be reconciled before either is published. No build date, staffing, fire history or access information was found. Height 16.8 m matches the 1920 inventory (55 ft). FFLA Maine Facebook photo captions (a 1938 steel tower, 2003 and 2006 photos) could not be read, so they are not used.

Removal date conflict: Forest Lookouts says 18 May 2012; the FFLA 2012 report planned a lift for Saturday 19 May, which failed (the record note uses 19 May). Height conflict: 1914 records say 24 ft (Maine Memory, Forest Lookouts); a 1925 Daily Kennebec Journal letter says 40 ft; unresolved. Agency: record says Maine Forestry District; Maine Memory says Forest Service; story uses Forest Service. Today's site comes from a 2017 birder blog and an undated hiker forum post, not an official source. The forum says a communications tower was partly erected; the WebSearch summary's 80-foot figure and the 2011 report's planned destination were not verified in a page we read, so they are left out. No current access information found.

Only source found is the Eastern US Lookouts page, which itself just quotes a 1929 newspaper item and the 1967-68 Forest Commissioner's biennial report. No NHLR or FFLOS register page exists for this site (nhlr.org returned 404), and nothing was found on current status, access, staffing, or whether the tower still stands. The tower record's location (45.65887, -68.18754, from FFLA) was not independently corroborated against the 1929 'Macwahoc Plantation' description within this budget; worth a closer look if a human researcher has more time.

Standing status rests on the FFLA index (no asterisk) and the trail page's description of a fire tower at the summit; no recent photo or visit report was checked. Access level 'restricted' is a judgment: the trail is open by landowner permission and the tower is not to be entered. The trail page is undated apart from a 2019 review, so the 'trailhead not yet constructed' note may be out of date. The 1912 watchman is not named in the source. The 1911 fire station may be the cabin the trail page describes; the sources do not say so outright, so the story does not claim it. AllTrails returned 403 and was not used.

Two York Hills in Franklin County: the FFLA point (44.59676, -69.97355) and the MountainZone summit near Weld (44.67658, -70.37558). By my calculation the two points are about 33 km apart, so it is not certain which hill the FFLA tower is on. Confirm the point before accepting it. No build date, design, owner, staffing or history was found; two searches turned up no account of the tower. The story is deliberately short.

Thin sources. Michigan Fire Towers gives PID QK0616, Removed: Yes, Status: Down, and T. Cabin: no (abbreviation unclear; not used in the story). The Forest Lookouts Atlanta entry does not name which Atlanta tower its 1921 steel tower refers to, so the 1921 build event is flagged as unconfirmed. The 1937 item describes a 60-foot tower about 10 miles north of Atlanta, not this site. The record height of 18.3 m (60 ft) has no source read that supports it for this tower; left out of facts. Removal date and current site condition unknown. A web search found no page on this tower. Suggested follow-up: Michigan DNR Atlanta-unit fire tower records and local historical society files.

No build date, builder, or height found. The only dated history is the 1943 staffing quote, which we read through the Forest Lookouts page (the original newspaper was not reached). The 'T. Cabin: no' field is unexplained, so the design line is cautious. The Michigan history page (michiganfiretower.com/history/) appeared in search only and was not read. The 'NGS None' register value in the brief looks wrong (see corrections). Access unknown, so no access or visit facts are recorded; the freelibrary article on 1940s lookouts returned 403 and was not read.

Status 'standing' from the brief is not supported by any source read, so it is omitted from facts; the firelookout.org Michigan page returned no Bergland entry. Access and staffing unknown. The brief's 30.5 m height likely comes from the 100-foot figure in the 1953 report, which describes the destroyed tower. Only two sources; a further search for the Michigan tower list or a recent status report could resolve status and the current tower's history.

Two register-level sources (the FFLOS entry and a regional list) plus one map-archive page. None gives a build date, staffing, fires, or current access. The 2008 removal is 'believed' on the register. The 1982 landmark is from Pastmaps, a map archive, so it shows the tower was on that sheet but is not a primary map image. The brief's record has no errors I could confirm. Access and visit details are unknown; the story says so.

No build date found; the 1935 item already describes an existing tower. Access and visiting rules were not found, so the story says so and the facts block omits access. The NHLR lists the cooperator as 'Painted Rocks National Lakeshore', which I suspect means Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore; not verified and not in the story. The easternuslookouts Alger county page says CCC crews built eight new towers in 1937-38 and that one was at 'the Alger site'; I could not tie that to this tower, so it is not used. The 1935 and 1943-44 items are quoted through the easternuslookouts page, not the original newspaper or report. The NHLR mid-1950s staffing date is approximate, so the event year 1955 is a placeholder.

No design, height or access source was found, so those keys are omitted. The NHLR page shows a 2021 photo, but no later check. A geocaching listing describes current radio use, but its page did not load in our fetch, so the story makes no claim about that. Two Facebook posts from the Forest Fire Lookout Association and two NARA photographs appeared in search results only and were not used.

Sources disagree on early dates and on the tower's history. (1) First towers: Wikipedia says 1936 and the NRHP nomination ties them to the 1936 fire without a year; the NPS Isle Royale page says CCC built them in 1939. (2) Old tower: Wikipedia says it stood near the new site and was torn down in 1963; the nomination puts it a half-mile away on Turkey Ridge. (3) Naming: the NPS Isle Royale page calls the re-established Turkey Ridge tower 'Feldtmann Tower'; the nomination uses New Feldtmann Fire Tower for the 1964 tower. Check which tower the Park Service means before any visit. (4) Height: the record's 12.2 m (40 ft, from NHLR) matches the 1961 plan; the built tower is 41 ft 3 in per the nomination and Wikipedia. Proposed correction to 12.6 m. (5) Abandonment: Wikipedia says by 1968; the nomination says use diminished after 1968 and eventually ended, with shelter use into the 1980s. (6) Access: climbing partway is from the NPS places page (updated Feb 2022); the NPS fire-tower page says the tower is no longer utilized. Current conditions and any closure are unverified. The NRHP nomination PDF is long; only targeted extracts were read, so the 1936 construction year for the old towers is not confirmed in the nomination itself. Reads: 5 distinct web pages plus one search; a local cache copy of an eastern lookouts list was checked and not used.

Company number: the register says 3611 (James Lake). A search snippet from SAH Archipedia's Camp Gibbs page names the 3604th Company for that camp, but that page returned HTTP 403 and was not read or cited, so the conflict is unresolved. The michigan.gov CCC page also returned 403. No visit report or current condition information was found, so the standing status rests on the register's 'only remaining' wording. Access is omitted because no source describes it.

Not confirmed as a fire lookout. OSM tags it tower:type=observation and gives no builder, date or height. None of the seven NHLR Michigan names or the two FFLOS names matches it. Mapcarta places it in Quincy Township near Ruby Marsh and Lake Annie. The record's 'standing' is not backed by any source read. Next: Michigan DNR fire tower records or Houghton County local history for this site. Do not publish as a fire lookout until a source says so.

Not confirmed as a fire lookout. OSM tags it tower:type=observation with lattice construction, and Mapcarta places it near the Whitefish Point Light. The station history sources read do not mention a lookout tower. Neither NHLR nor FFLOS Michigan list matches it. The record's 'standing' is not backed by any source read. Next: Michigan DNR fire tower records or Chippewa County and station histories. Do not publish as a fire lookout until a source says so.

Brief's height 13.7 m is not in any page read. Corrected to 12.6 m from the NRHP nomination (41’-3” from the concrete piers). The npgallery.nps.gov asset page returned no text, so the nomination was taken from the npshistory.com PDF. Nomination gives both June 1964 construction and July 1964 assembly; Wikipedia gives 1964 in the infobox and 1965 for completion; all are kept. Wikipedia credits NPS with the 1939 towers; the nomination credits CCC personnel. Access: the NPS page says the tower room is closed but visitors may climb partway up the stairs; the story reports both and does not encourage climbing the tower. No photos added (no confirmed image URLs or licences). Nomination has many figures, not checked for licence. Verification 2026-10-09: the story's fire-cause claim was contradicted by the nomination and is now reported as a disagreement; 'in the cab' was removed (not in any page read); the 'scenic stop' and tower-room sentences were reworded so they no longer copy NPS wording.

Construction and removal dates rest on one register page. A search for a second source (build, staffing or use) found nothing usable; the Michigan Tech fire tower page has no Paulding entry, and the Paulding Light is a folklore phenomenon, not this site. The 1971 item on the Conners page may or may not refer to this tower, and the story says so. No staffing, fire history, height or design is in any source read, so none is given. A lead for an editor: Ottawa National Forest headquarters in Ironwood for tower records.

Build year 1933 agreed by the register and Forest Lookouts. Current condition and public access are unverified: no dated source read says the tower stands today, so the record's 'standing' rests on the register entry alone. A Forest Lookouts page for the lake lists a federal survey marker at the tower stamped TEPEE 1938; that is the marker's date, not the tower's. A NARA photo caption and a Facebook post surfaced only in search snippets and were not used. No corrections proposed. Fact-check 2026-10-09: 'has a cab' became 'was built with a cab' because no source confirms the tower stands today; the Kenton Ranger District sentence now cites the Forest Service page; the Iron County quote was added as evidence.

Built-year conflict (1936 vs. NHLR's 1940/CCC claim) is real and unresolved; I favored 1936 since both Wikipedia and the NRHP period of significance back it, but a human with access to the actual NRHP nomination PDF (not just the NPGallery detail page) could settle it outright. No cached local source pages existed for this tower beyond the NHLR page; no newspaper or Forest Service primary-source search was attempted beyond the two WebFetch calls used here (within the 3-search budget, no WebSearch calls were needed since WebFetch on known URLs sufficed).

Main issue is status. The FFLA Minnesota list (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/mn/) marks Agassiz HQ Tower Gone at the record's coordinates; the refuge visit page describes a climbable 100-foot tower near headquarters; the photo caption says 99 feet. Neither is dated. The refuge gives 100 ft and 99 ft; height_m left out. Wikidata Q107541850 gives 48 deg 17 min 57 sec N, 95 deg 59 min 1 sec W, about 230 m from the record point, and cites a minnesotafiretower.blogspot.com post that returned HTTP 404 in our fetch. A separate Agassiz Pool tower (48.33862, -95.92350) is also marked gone in the FFLA list and is kept separate. The 2005 FFLA report has a typo ('5ht'); we assume the 2005 Agassiz Refuge Fire Tower is this tower but the report does not say where it stands. A web search snippet mentions a 2008 refuge announcement about a DNR deer testing station at the tower and a 2025 hunting map legend; those were not read as pages and are not used. Suggested check: refuge headquarters (phone from the search snippet was not verified, so not repeated here) or a dated site visit by the owner.

No build year is given: the Register says only the 1920s, so there is no built event. No current fire-watch staffing was found; the Register says the tower remains in service with the park interpreter attached. Height: the Register says 80 ft; other sources say 100 ft total including the cab. The record's 30.5 m is kept. Public access rests on a 2024 visitor account and the park's exhibit; park hours and closures were not checked. The Forest Lookouts page is a hobbyist site that reproduces NGS data and is cited only for the NGS description. No photos added.

Height: the Register and county list say 81 ft (24.7 m, used here); the Forest Lookouts page says 80 ft. The record had 24.4 m (80 ft). The 1923 and 1924 towers come only from the county list; the Register mentions only the 1924 tower's anchors. No current access or staffing source was found, so the story does not say whether the public may climb. The Register's 2018 photo credit is not repeated. The Forest Lookouts page is a hobbyist site reproducing NGS data, cited only for the 1948 description and 80-foot figure. No photos added; the Commons category may hold Creative Commons images, not checked.

The county PDF's Babbitt note was read in full. It opens 'Standing. MFS. Octagonal cab.', gives the 1928 to 1966 map listing, and ends 'The tower was located southeast of the village. Removed.' No removal date or cause is given. The Minnesota list (firelookout.org) marks it Standing. The story previously said both lists show it standing and that no removal was recorded; that was contradicted by the county note, so the story now reports the conflict. No build date or builder found. The county list marks ownership 'USFS?'. The 1952 survey record only names the tower. Confirm the current status with the county or site manager before publishing.

Maker is disputed and not resolved: the Register says Aermotor; the Hubbard County list says McClintock Marshall stairway tower. The 'restricted' access level is inferred from the Register's note that nursery personnel use the tower; no closure notice or access rule was found, and the state forest page we fetched had no readable text. Current condition rests on the Register alone. The 1933 nursery date is from the county list only and was not checked against a DNR page. The Forest Lookouts page is a hobbyist site reproducing data; it is used only for the 1934 height. No photos added.

The two accounts of the first tower conflict on builder (CCC vs state), height (100 ft vs 60 ft), and the 1936 replacement, which appears only in the local history. Both are reported; the sources do not say which tower stands today, so the built events are not merged. The 1980 survey describes the tower the record calls standing. The NGS PID RN1233 appears on the Forest Lookouts page and is not in the record; consider adding it to registers. A Wikimedia Commons photo (Ball Bluff Lookout Tower.jpg) is linked from Wikidata, but its license was not checked, so no photo is added. No access, staffing, or current-condition sources were found.

The move to Camp Wilderness, the 80-foot rebuild and the Bemidji site listed as gone are well sourced. Build year and height are not settled: the 1960 survey description says 110 ft and gives no build year. Access: no public climbing hours found on the Camp Wilderness page. The county report's 'disabled for climbing' line belongs to the Blackduck tower (Tower 87), not Bemidji, so it is not used. Camp Wilderness is covered by the sibling record us-mn-bemidji-at-camp-wilderness, which uses the same sources. The record's agency field is correct.

Sources agree on the 1935 build, the 2007 move and the 100 ft to 80 ft change. The Beltrami report lists the 1935 owner as Mn MFS (Minnesota Forest Service) while the NHLR says Minnesota DNR built it; the forest service was part of the DNR, so this is not treated as a conflict. Dedication date is unclear: the 2007 chapter report anticipated a late-June ribbon cutting, and a search snippet from a YouTube video mentions June 30 with a 2009 date, which I did not open; the story does not give a dedication date. Public access and climbing hours were not found; the story tells visitors to ask the camp. The 2007 chapter report calls it the East Bemidji tower, and the story keeps the brief's name.

Public access is unknown: no source says whether visitors may climb it. Emergency use and the radio repeater rest on one hobbyist history page and are undated; I did not confirm them with an agency. A RadioReference forum post about a 158.8125 repeater on Ben Draper Forest Road was not used because it is old and not tied to this tower. The record's existing photos cover this tower; no new photos were added. Access block omitted because level is unknown.

Only one tower-specific source (the 1960 NGS station description) plus the standing listing. No build date, builder, staffing or fire history found. The access level 'restricted' is our reading of the reservation location, not a stated policy; a human should confirm with the reservation before publishing. The NGS description does not say who decides access, so the story now presents that as our reading rather than a sourced fact. The NGS gives an overall height of 110 feet; it is not entered as height_m because the height to the cab floor is unknown. The record's agency matches the Forest Lookouts header.

Thin record: NHLR, Forest Lookouts and the county inventory are the only substantive sources. No staffing, access or current-use source found. Not used: the inventory's 1912 'Fire Ranger Lookout' (a 50-ft wood lookout near Birchdale, not tied to this site; mentioned in the story as unlinked) and the 'Happyland' / Littlefork entries (Tower 90, a different site). The 1967 survey height of 100 ft conflicts with 81 ft and is flagged, not adopted.

Access is the main gap. The fence is from a 2004 recovery note and the 'not opened' status rests on an NHLR line of unknown date; no current source. visit.climbable is null because no source says either way, and access.level is unknown because the fence is dated 2004; treat the access block as unverified until MnDOT or DNR confirms. Search results surfaced an undated travel guide that says a tower can be seen from the road; not used. The inventory notes 'Rainy Lake lookout' as an alternate name, not added to the record's other_names. No new photos.

The 1935 build date rests on one Commons photo description; no independent source found. The 2016 chapter report (a short report, fully read) mentions the CNF's 3 fire towers without naming them, so Blackduck's place among them is unknown. The author's remark about further progress is between a named individual and the CNF, and involves the three towers; the story wording now says only that. The Commons caption places the tower in the Chippewa National Forest; the record's agency is null and could be filled after confirmation, not from this caption alone. This research file has no elevation field, so the story states none. The access level stays unknown.

Build year 1934 rests on the NHLR Built field and the footing inscription. Height 38.1 m (125 ft) is added to the record from an undated survey note; the record had none. No staffing, fire or visiting-rules source was found, so access is left out; the story says to ask the Band first. A statewide A-Z lookout list (Wikimedia Commons PDF) names the Band as owner, but its row gives no date or height here, so it is not cited. No builder is named anywhere; do not attribute to the CCC without a source.

The Register text is undated, so the open season may have changed. The record's county (Itasca) is correct for the current site. No pre-1976 fire or staffing records were found in these sources. No photos added.

Thin record: no build date, builder, design, staffing or fire history in any source read. Two search rounds turned up only the directory and unrelated Isanti County courthouse pages. A guessed firelookout.org detail URL returned 404. The Commons photo and Wikidata image are already in data/photos_manifest.json, so no photos entry was added. Next checks if wanted: Isanti County Historical Society, City of Cambridge, Minnesota newspaper archives for the 1930s.

Two towers share the name Cascade: the 1922-23 tower on Cascade Peak and the 1933 New Cascade or Trout Lake tower. The record's FFLA point matches the 1933 tower; the 1922 tower is at 47.7511, -90.5347 per the county survey. Height is left out because the two towers differ (about 80 ft first, 100 ft second). No removal date found for either tower. The Wikidata photo dated 1925 is not clearly tied to either tower. Access unknown.

The 1934 build date and the 100-foot height come from one hobbyist page that reproduces a federal survey station description; no DNR or NRHP record was read. The current status is unresolved: the directory says standing, the survey note says replacement was planned, and nothing later was found. Search results mentioned a Clear River or Beltrami Island history but none was read, so none is cited. The 30.5 m figure is a conversion of the 100-foot source figure.

Built date 1931, 80 ft and Aermotor design rest on one local history page (Forest Lookouts). No manufacturer source was read; a Peakbagger entry (1931, 80 ft, standing, user-submitted and unverified) and search snippets were not quoted. Results of the 2018 Collaborative Design Group assessment were not found. The Forest History Center tower in Grand Rapids is a different structure and was not used. Access is set to restricted as a judgment: the forest is open in daylight, the recreation page does not mention the tower, and the 2018 door was unlocked for visitors, but the stairs and railings were under safety review. No current tower policy found. Staffing is unknown; the Forest Lookouts page gives no staff names.

Construction date conflicts (1929 entry vs 1931 survey note); both kept. The antenna distance (about five miles) differs slightly from the survey's 4.5 miles; both are reported. height_m 29 is 95 ft converted. The NGS PID SJ2055 appears on the Forest Lookouts page and is not in the record; consider adding it. The 1934 approach directions are historical and may be outdated. No staffing, fire, rebuild, or current access information was found. The Minnesota Historical Society page on the Forest History Center fire tower in Grand Rapids is a different tower and was not used.

The 1937 CCC build rests on a local history page that reproduces a federal survey station description, and on a 2011 Commons caption that repeats it. No independent CCC or DNR record was found. No National Historic Lookout Register page for Cotton was in the cache (two guessed URLs returned 404). The auction is undated; the caption places it a few years before August 2011. Wikidata puts the tower in the Cloquet Valley State Forest, which conflicts with a sale of forestry property; ownership should be checked against Saint Louis County or DNR records. Access level is omitted because no current statement was found; the brief's access 'unknown' stands. Commons photo File:Cotton_Lookout_Tower.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, uploader Tlkremer) could be added once its direct image URL is confirmed; not added here. Staffing and notable fires were not found.

The Forest Lookouts page is the only source for the 1949 build. A search summary claimed a 1935 CCC build; the cached page says 1949 and does not mention the CCC or 1935, so 1935 was not used. Height conflict: 100 ft (1949 build line) against approximately 80 ft (1952 survey); the brief's 30.5 m matches the 100-ft figure and was kept, so the editor should choose. The Wikidata elevation of 1,394 ft matches the brief's 424.9 m. No National Historic Lookout Register page was found in the cache (one guessed URL returned 404). No staffing, notable fires, access or current condition were found. The Commons photo is listed on Wikidata but its file page was not read, so it is not added to photos.

Only location, county, forest, Wikidata elevation (about 1,434 ft) and standing status are supported by reachable pages. The Wikidata elevation of 1,434 ft matches the brief's 437.1 m. A search summary said a minnesotafiretower.blogspot.com post (Cuba Hill Lookout Tower, December 2012) gives a pre-1935 build and a 120-foot ladder tower, and that another blog page says two or three towers survive in the Chippewa National Forest. Those claims are unverified: the blog post, the December 2012 archive and the August 2012 Chippewa history page all returned 404 here, so they are not used and no height or build year is recorded. The Forest Lookouts index gives no build or height data. An OpenStreetMap node (8169190028, Cuba Hill Lookout, tower:type observation) was read but not cited. The Wikidata image Cuba Hill Lookout Tower.jpg (2,736 x 3,648) was not read, so no photo is added. No staffing, notable fires, access or condition was found; the brief's access 'unknown' stands.

Owner and build year conflict across sources; the story reports both. No staffing or notable-fire record was found in the sources read. The photo credit comes from data/sources/commons_credits.json and the mirror manifest, not a fresh fetch. Access is inferred from the radio-site use; no visit rule was found. The story tells readers not to climb.

Built year conflicts: the Register and a 1936 press report say 1936 (CCC); the DNR page and a 1997 Post-Bulletin article say 1933. Not resolved. Height conflicts: Register and 1936 report say 110 ft (33.5 m, used in facts); 1997 article says 100 ft; a 1973 NGS description says about 130 ft; the OSM node tag says 35 m (the current record value). Steps conflict: DNR says about 500, 1997 article says 634. Hours conflict: DNR gives daylight hours April to October (page undated); 1997 article gave 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. Current access and condition not confirmed by any dated source after 1997 except the undated DNR page; check before publishing visit details. Record access 'unknown' can be set to public per DNR. No photos added; NHLR and Post-Bulletin pages were not checked for licensed images.

Status is unresolved: the FFLOS county list says Gone, while the NHLR 2021 entry says it currently houses communications equipment. Forest Lookouts (Superior National Forest) and NHLR (Minnesota DNR) differ on the administrator. The blog cited in the record returned HTTP 404 and the Star Tribune article returned HTTP 429, so neither was read. The FFLOS county list also shows a separate Ash River tower as Standing (NHLR US 1286, MN 12); not checked whether it is related to this tower's history. No staffing sources were found. Build year (1928 placement vs 1929 erection) and county (Cass vs apparent Crow Wing) conflict; the story reports both. No current condition, access, rental or later staffing record found. County: the brief and the Register say Texas County; the Central Lookouts list and page say Shannon County. The Central page's annual-report entries describe a 1943 steel tower, then later steel towers replacing temporary wooden ones in 1957-58 and 1962; the story reports this without choosing. The Register's land and erection dates are attributed to online resources, and the story says so. The brief's agency name follows the Register; the Central site uses 'Missouri Conservation Commission' for the same agency's earlier name. No staffing or fire data was found in any source read. Visiting rules are not stated. A Facebook group snippet mentioning the Angeline Conservation Area was not used. No photos added.

Two disputes left open. Build year: the register says 'likely' 1939 (Bartlett CCC camp); Forest Lookouts gives 1934 with no source; both are shown. County: the register says Shannon County, Forest Lookouts says Carter County (27N-2W-31); the story avoids naming a county. No current visiting or rental information was found; the register says restoration is planned. Two Facebook items (Shannon County Museum, Ozarks History Archives) appeared only in search snippets and were not used. Confidence is medium because of the unresolved county and build year. Fact-check 2026-10-09: two story sentences that closely copied register wording were reworded, and the summary now says restoration is planned pending approvals and that staffing was intermittent.

Built year (1950), 100-foot height and the Conservation-owned site agree across the Register, Forest Lookouts and the 2025 blog. Unresolved: the 1962 Coast and Geodetic Survey description (wooden, about 50 ft) disagrees on material and height; flagged in the story. Access: the Register (2025) says climbing is signed and the cab is inaccessible; the 2025 blog found no fencing, after earlier posts said fenced off. No staffing or fire history appears in the Register or the Forest Lookouts annual-report extracts, so none is stated. Condition and access after March 2025 are unverified; re-check before publishing any visit guidance. No photos added. The Register credits a photo to Rick Brown, AICP, but no image URL was captured.

The 2004 removal agrees across the register and KRCU, but who dismantled the tower differs (KRCU versus the 2006 visit report). KRCU's 1957-58 steel-tower replacement at Grassy is contradicted by the annual report quote naming Flat Rock, so the story leaves it as a disputed point. The register coordinates (37.2826, -90.0655) differ from the Central US lookouts list in the brief, about 0.6 km apart; I could not confirm the second figure on the page, so no coordinate conflict is recorded. A 'Moved' caption with a May 7, 2016 photo credit on the Weebly page is unexplained and not used. Current access rests on a 2025 article and a 2006 visit report; no current Missouri Department of Conservation access notice was checked. The brief's record has no errors I could confirm.

No source gives staffing, fire history, the lookout's height or design, or the year the lookout came down, so those are left out. The 2008 Southeast Missourian blog returned 403 and a Facebook MCC post returned no text, so neither was used. The tower's build year is inferred only from the 1949 'new towers' wording. The Mexico Ledger date is taken from the Forest Lookouts quote. The brief's 'gone' status rests on the former-sites listing alone.

Built year (1960) agrees across both sources. Current status and public access are unverified: the 2015 plan has no access statement for the Houston site (its Cabool appendix says that tower is closed to the public, which is not this tower). OpenStreetMap node 12729567032 tags access=yes and fee=no; that is a volunteer tag, not an authority statement, so no access key was set. The Facebook posts by Missouri Conservation History and Equipment mention an Aermotor MC-39 design and directions, but the fetch returned no readable text, so they are not cited. A 2018 local news item in the Central US Lookouts page concerns a private individual and is left out.

Height is unresolved. Sources give 90 ft (Aug 1927, under construction), 73 ft to the deck plus a 9 ft steel room (Sept 1927), 72 ft (Apr 1928), 80 ft (Dec 1935) and 85 ft (1939-41 annual report and NHLR). The record's height_m 25.9 equals 85 ft and is kept as the NHLR and annual-report figure. The guide's cab-floor measure is closest to the September 1927 figure of 73 ft to the deck (about 22.3 m), so the editor should decide which measure the record carries. Built 1927 is supported by NHLR and by the September 1927 completion clipping. Status 'standing' rests on the NHLR description, which is undated. Access level 'public' refers to the conservation area; no source read confirms the tower is open to climb today, and the 2019 article is the latest visitor description read. Staffing 'seasonal' rests on the 1935 clipping alone. The 2019 Conservationist article gives the area as 13,005 acres; the MDC page gives 13,503, which the story uses. The nature.mdc.mo.gov page returned 404 and was not used. No photos added; the record's existing NHLR photo is unchanged.

Built date is not established. The record has none. The only dated construction fact is the November 22, 1934 newspaper item that the foundation was being dug; the 1936 completion date appears in a web search summary citing the Living New Deal database, but livingnewdeal.org returned 403 to our reader, so it is not used and needs a manual check. Height: record height_m 33.5 equals the 1939 survey's 'about 110 feet'. The 1934 cab-floor figure (99 ft 9 in, about 30.4 m) is a plan, not a measured height. The editor should decide which measure the record should carry. Status 'standing' rests on the Salem News description in the present tense and the NPS page, which invites visits; no source read states the tower's condition in 2025 or 2026. Access level 'public' refers to Forest Service land with free parking; climbing is not confirmed. The NHLR entry says 'Nominated by Admin'. The NHLR photo set was not added to the record. Staffing is not stated in any source read; the Salem News credits CCC Company 732, not a lookout crew, with construction.

Built 1949 matches the register; the 1947-48 land acquisition precedes it and is consistent. The register's "100' Aermotor" does not say whether the height is to the cab floor, so height_m 30.5 is the stated tower height and the editor should confirm. Status and staffing rest on MDC's towersite page, which is undated but describes the tower in present tense as used by MDC staff to spot wildfires. The 1959 towerman death is in the story without his name; the JSON quotes avoid the name too. The acreage difference (80 acres in the late 1940s, 26.8 acres now) is unexplained. A web search summary tied the 1949 date to a different tower in a Missouri Life article; it was not used. No photos added.

History and register facts agree with the record (built c.1965, standing, registered 2026, coordinates). Height 100 ft is taken from the 2021 report's cab-entrance height and converted to 30.5 m. Access is set to restricted: the 2018 plan gives the picnic area limited public use, and the tower is closed to climbing. Staffing is recorded as unknown because no source says whether the tower is staffed. The newest firsthand detail is the July 2021 newspaper; no 2024-26 visit or photo was found. The 1980 event year marks a decade, since the Register gives no year. A Facebook post by Missouri Conservation History (in search results only, not read) mentions a 2023 deed agreement; not used.

Only three readable sources. No height was found in them, so none is recorded. The 2023 visit is the newest condition report. The agency question is unresolved: the River Hills column is undated in the text read, and the 1953 land purchase claimed on a geocache page (GC4AMAQ) was not readable, so it is not used. Built date 1953-54 agrees across sources. No corrections to the record. Status note is included because the cab is in poor shape; the tower is otherwise standing.

Current condition is not verified. The newest dated evidence is a 2014 headline (the article is paywalled, so only the headline was read) and a 2018 photo credit; no 2024-26 visit or report was found. Unverified leads, not used in the story: a USAspending contract record in search results mentions tornado repair at the Roby Tower site, but that page is script-only and the bid page returned 403; a Facebook snippet says built 1937, which conflicts with 1934 from the Register and Forest Lookouts. Height 100 ft converted to 30.5 m; it is not a cab-floor measurement. Access is left unknown because no source states it. No corrections to the record.

Which 1949 tower went to Runge is unclear. Forest Lookouts says a new steel tower was erected at Rocky Mount in fiscal 1968-69 and that a tower was moved in 2000, without saying which. The Runge caption says the tower there was formerly at Rocky Mount; no source read confirms the upper portion was re-erected or the tower's condition today, so 'standing' rests on the register's location. Heights for Runge found only in search snippets (72 ft, 55 ft, 77 ft at Rocky Mount) were not used. The register spells the site 'Rocky Mountain' once. The Waymarking page and a Missouri Life article were not readable through fetch_text. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story no longer says the Commission put the tower up, since no source names who erected it; the 2000 move is now attributed to 'a tower' with the ambiguity stated; the Miller County footnote now sits on the sentence that states it.

No source read gives a build year; the July 1935 article is the earliest mention. A search snippet from AllTrails says the CCC built the tower in 1936, but the page returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited and the 1936 date conflicts with the 1935 article. Missouri Life and The Prospect pages (both HTTP 403) reportedly say the tower is still used to spot smoke; not verified, not cited. Record access was 'unknown'; set to public for the park, climbing not confirmed. Staffing as_of 1958 is the last staffing mention found. Fact-check 2026-10-09: facts.status changed from 'standing' to 'unknown', because no source read confirms the tower's present condition.

The record id spells the name 'stegrall'; both sources spell it Stegall Mountain, so the id is left as is. The 1962 event comes from a source that reads 'FY 1962-03', apparently a typo for the 1962-64 biennium; the report's own title reads 7/1962 to 6/1964. The 70 ft figure is an 'about' from the 1963 survey. Search snippets (not fetched) claim a 100 ft height and an Aermotor MC-39 design; not cited. Hiking-site snippets suggest the tower is still reached on foot; the MDC page is the cited source. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now says the tower 'appears to still stand' from the MDC page's hike description, and the 'no lookout named' point is limited to the reports read.

Most of the history (1948-1981) comes from newspaper and annual-report extracts transcribed on Forest Lookouts; the quotes were checked against that cached page, not the original papers. No fire events are named in any source read, so none are stated. Height disagrees across sources (60, 72 and 85 ft); facts use the Register's 72 ft. The brief's height_m of 235.3 is unsupported and is corrected. Access: no closure notice found; the state park page does not mention the tower, so public access rests on park status and the 2025 blog visit. The Wikidata entry lists the Missouri Department of Conservation as operator and names a Commons photo, 'View from Taum Sauk Mountain Lookout Tower.JPG', which was not checked for licence and is not added. Nothing after the 1980s is documented apart from the 1991 park, the 1997 registration and the 2025 visit.

Unverified leads, not used in the story: a Missouri Conservation History Facebook post (https://www.facebook.com/MCC1010/posts/thomasville-fire-lookout-tower-this-tower-and-the-surrounding-40-acres-was-sold-/770545715109867/) appears in search snippets to say the tower and 40 acres were sold on GovDeals; the post and the GovDeals listing (https://www.govdeals.com/asset/16/11790) returned 403 or only a title, so the sale is unconfirmed. A second post in search snippets describes a 68-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower northeast of Eminence; it may be a different tower. A search snippet gives a 1951 build year, but the fetched NHLR page says 1957; the fetched page is used. Missing from record: removal date and access level; no source gave either. The brief record's other_names 'Thomasville (Federal)' comes from the Forest Lookouts list.

No height, design or fire history found in the readable sources. The NHLR detail page gives only elevation (1,387 ft, 423 m). The News-Leader article returned HTTP 403, so it was not read. Forest Lookouts is a hobbyist site that quotes a 1936 Gazette item. The MDC plan dates from 2015, so current staffing and fence status are not verified. The removal of the dwelling buildings is a range (late 1960s or early 1970s), so no event year is recorded for it. Site directions in the plan were left out because the site is closed to the public. Brief's 'standing' and 'access unknown' were checked: standing per NHLR; access is closed per NHLR and the 2015 plan. Check 2026-10-09: all 18 quotes were found on the first run; three footnoted claims were corrected (a missing footnote on the dwelling sentence, the 1935 'seeing it' detail, and the undated 'Today' access claim, now dated to the 2015 plan and the NHLR's undated 'currently').

Record id is us-mo-unnamed, but the sources call this the Cabool fire tower; id left as is. Build year and height agree across two sources. The Cabool towersite is in Texas County, and the record's Texas County is correct. The MDC towersite page gives the directions 'From Cabool, take Route M north 2 miles' and public-use hours for the area; both are now cited. A Facebook post (not fetched; search snippet only) says the same directions; not cited. The sources read do not say which side of the site holds the tower or what happens to it after the July 2026 action; a follow-up could check the MDC towersite map or a later Commission action. Fact-check 2026-10-09: facts.status changed from 'standing' to 'unknown' and access.level from 'restricted' to 'unknown', because the 2015 plan is the last physical description and its locked-gate note is dated.

Unresolved date conflict: a Living New Deal page (https://livingnewdeal.org/sites/desoto-national-forest-airey-work-center-mchenry-ms/) says construction of the Airey Work Center began in 1935 under the CCC. The fetch returned 403, and the WebFetch paraphrase cannot be quote-checked, so the story does not use it. The NHLR 1934 date is used for the tower. A blog (https://thedirtymule.com/trails/desoto-national-forest-airey-lake-fire-tower-circuit/) also returned 403 and was not read. Access level not found in any source readable here, so it is omitted. Record change: the brief's record had no build event; 1934 added from NHLR.

Build year unknown in every readable source (NHLR says Unknown). The 1948 report is read only through the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes the Clarion-Ledger; the newspaper itself was not read. A second search returned FCC tower #1042132 'Kosciusko, MS (Dismantled)', which is a cellular structure, not this lookout, and was not used. An Attala Historical Society history page (https://sites.rootsweb.com/~msahs/history.html) returned 403 and was not read. Access level omitted: no source readable here states public access. The brief record's access 'unknown' stays.

Only the NHLR entry and one family obituary profile were read; the Weebly Barge page is a name-and-county stub. The brief says status standing, but no page read states the tower's current condition, so facts.status is unknown. The register's agency name differs from the 1985 company name (Barge Forest Products Co.); kept as NHLR wrote it. Two searches found no construction history or staffing record. The obituary profile does not mention a tower: a full-text check for lookout, tower, watch, fire and observation found no matches. Re-checked 2026-10-09: NHLR shows Elevation 586 ft (179 m), Built Unknown, and Administered by C.A. Barge Forest Products. The story's advice about visiting or climbing the tower was not supported by any source and was removed.

Agency: NHLR lists U.S. Fish & Wildlife under 'Administered by' and the Mississippi Forestry Commission under 'Cooperators'. This supersedes the earlier draft's reading that the Forestry Commission was the agency. Build date unknown after three searches. The 2023 standing note and the NGS datasheet text come from a secondary copy on the Forest Lookouts page; the original datasheet was not fetched. Goose Overlook (Wikipedia) and the Webster overlook in the refuge trail brochure are different structures and were not used. No access or visit rules were found.

Only the NHLR detail page and the 2020 Secretary of State public lands list were read. Two web searches and the Forest Fire Lookout Association Mississippi page found nothing local; that FFLA page says its Mississippi data is still under construction. The cdispatch.com article returned HTTP 410 and was not used. The register does not say outright that the tower is standing, so status is recorded as unknown; neither the register description nor the 2020 list confirms it. The access level private rests only on the register note. The conflict is open: the register says private property, while the state list places a Clay County Tower under the Forestry Commission. The state list may refer to a different site or the land may have changed hands, but neither is verified. Suggested next step: ask the Mississippi Forestry Commission about the tower and its owner, and check Clay County parcel records.

The register's history of the eight Bienville towers is detailed and gives the build range for this tower. The register's 1934 start for the towers conflicts with Wikipedia's June 15, 1936 establishment date for the forest; left unresolved. A search snippet attributed to a National Park Service nomination gave March 26, 1934 for the forest's start; that source was not read and is not cited. The Moore NRHP nomination (npgallery def15102) was read and its cached text has no mention of Clear Springs. Not found: staffing, fires watched, access status, or any current condition beyond the register's remains standing line. Two web searches and the Bienville Wikipedia article were the only other sources read. The 2020 Secretary of State state land list has a Smith County Tower under Forestry Commission; that is a state site, not this Forest Service tower. Suggested next steps: Bienville ranger district office in Forest, and Mississippi Department of Archives and History.

Only the NHLR detail page and the 2020 Secretary of State public lands list were read. Two web searches and the Conehatta Wikipedia article (no tower mention) found nothing local. The maker and the 120 ft height come from a register writer who says they could not find a makers label, so both are hedged in the story and should be treated as unverified. The register's own line 'It stands 120ft tall' is the only direct statement of standing; the 2023 site visit findings are not stated and the 2020 state list gives no condition. The record's access field was left unknown because no source gives public access status. Not used: a TowerDex directory of Mississippi Forestry Commission structures, which has no Conehatta entry, and the absence there does not rule out a shorter tower. Suggested next step: ask the Mississippi Forestry Commission for the tower's manufacturer, height, build date and current status.

Almost every tower-specific fact rests on the one NHLR detail page, which is written by a volunteer register contributor. Two searches found nothing else about this tower; the Sanders family's name and the 1991 sale appear only there. The Aermotor and MFC pages are Wikipedia, used for context only; the Aermotor article's 7x7 claim is not tied to this tower. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'private' from the register's 'Private Property' line. No build date, staffing history or current-condition report was found. The register gives the sale price and the 1991 year with no citation of its own, so treat them as the register's account.

Only the NHLR detail page supplies tower facts. Two searches and a topo page (anyplaceamerica.com, HTTP 403) added nothing about this tower. The register lists the MFC as administering the site but also says the MFC no longer uses it; the owner today is unknown, so access is 'unknown' rather than guessed. Current status rests on the July 2022 site visit. The 'missing bottom flights' note is the register writer's, from 2022. The Aermotor page is context only and does not identify this tower's model.

Single source: the NHLR entry. The Forest Lookouts page for Energy names only the site and county. Two searches found no construction, staffing or fire history, and no Forestry Commission tower record for Energy. The brief's coordinates and elevation match NHLR. The condition quote contains the source's typo 'i a' and is kept as written. Re-checked 2026-10-09 against the NHLR page: Elevation 526 ft (160 m), Built Unknown, Administered by Mississippi Forestry Commission. The story now uses 'administers' rather than 'in connection with', and the two search-based statements no longer carry a page footnote.

Thin record: the NHLR page is the only substantive source. The Forest Lookouts Fairview page has only a header (Mississippi Lookouts, Fairview, Itawamba County) and no text, so it is not cited. Searches on the Mississippi Forestry Commission and the Itawamba Historical Society archives returned no tower history. Build date, staffing, fire history, and current condition and access are not in any source read. The brief's elevation (167.6 m) matches the Register's 168 m. The brief had no height; the 100 ft figure comes from the Register's description. No photos added. Story is at the 120-word floor because the record is thin; the Register's next-entry link is the only added detail.

Identity unconfirmed. The OSM point is 2.7 km from the Maben register coordinates and about 9.9 km from Oktibbeha, so it may be a mis-placed duplicate of one of them, or a different structure. The 2020 state list has no Fire Tower entry for Oktibbeha County. The story may not be worth publishing as a lookout history until someone confirms the point. Searches: 2 WebSearch. Page reads: 4 distinct.

The NHLR page is the only tower-specific source. Two searches turned up Flintkote Company well records and land-patent pages for Kemper County, but nothing ties them to this tower, so they are not used. The '(II)' suffix suggests an earlier Flintkote tower; the NHLR previous-lookout link points to Kemper (De Kalb), US 1667, not to a Flintkote tower, and this was not investigated. The brief's agency (MFC) conflicts with the description's timber-company owner; the correction is proposed for a human decision. Current owner name, condition and visitor access were not found.

Two sources only. Linking the register's Gauley tower to the Gauley Mountain tower in the 1935-36 account is an inference from the shared name; the register does not mention the CCC. The msgw.org https certificate has expired, so the page was read and cited over http. The record's material 'steel' is not in the register, which says only Aermotor; consider null. Facebook posts about the tower came up in search but were not read. Do not confuse with the Gauley Mountain tower site in West Virginia (FFLOS).

No build date, staffing or fire history in the register, the Forest Lookouts entry or the agency home page. The register's no-longer-in-use note is undated. Possible next steps: MFC records or Alcorn County newspaper archives. The record's agency spelling is a typo; correction proposed. Access level 'permission' is a judgment from agency administration and no public access information.

Only the register and OpenStreetMap were read. The Forest Lookouts page guessed at glenville.html returned 404, so no Forest Lookouts entry was found for this tower. No build date, staffing or fire history found. Access level 'permission' is a judgment from agency administration, not a stated rule.

Probable duplicate: the Greenwood (US 1774) and Leflore (US 1737) entries sit about 10 m apart in Leflore County, but the register does not say they are one tower and the nominators differ (Mike Lyon vs Jason Johns). The story keeps them separate and says so. Only two register pages found for this site after two searches each; the local-history searches turned up nothing. The Leflore entry's MFC administration and 120-ft Aermotor are not attributed to the Greenwood record in facts.

Only the Former Fire Lookout Sites page describes this lookout. No source found gives its construction date, design, height, staffing, fires or current condition, so the story omits them. Searches for a Winston County or Mississippi Forestry Commission record of the tower turned up nothing. The Commercial Dispatch article was 410 Gone. Leads for an editor: Mississippi Forestry Commission records, Mississippi State University Special Collections photo archive.

Only the register and OpenStreetMap were read. No build date, staffing or fire history found. The Raymond name may refer to the town rather than a site name. A search turned up an unrelated OSHA report on a 1997 TV antenna tower collapse in Raymond, Mississippi; not used. Access level 'restricted' is a judgment from the register's still-in-use note, not a stated rule.

Only the NHLR entry, the Forest Lookouts index (name and county only) and the Aermotor history were usable. Two WebSearch queries and several page reads turned up no local history, staffing, fire, build or fate information. The register's Hopewell visit note is undated. Status is 'listed' only: the register's present-tense description is not a dated check, so the story says the current condition is not confirmed. height_m is converted from the register's 100 ft. No access key set because the sources give no access level. No photos found.

Single source (NHLR) after two searches and a check of the Kemper County history page, which had nothing on the tower. The access level is left unknown: the removed treads suggest the stair cannot be climbed as it stands, but no source says whether the site is open or closed. Only the NHLR entry and the Forest Lookouts index (name and county only) were usable. The register gives a site visit noted as 2/5/22 and no narrative beyond the tower type. Two WebSearch queries found only a 1911 map mention of Kincaid and an unrelated 2005 antenna structure at Gore Springs, which are not used. Only one substantive source, the NHLR register entry, plus Wikipedia for the county seat. The 1957 build year is the register's Built field; the description beside it is undated and refers to Forest Service employees 'last week', so the wording may come from an old newspaper report, which is not confirmed. The 100 ft height comes from that same description and is converted to 30.5 m. No staffing, fire, rental or current-condition information was found in two searches and a few page reads; the Mississippi Forestry Commission or Mississippi Digital Library may hold older records. The record's photo already exists (credit Jennifer Payne), so no new photos were added. Status 'standing' is proposed as 'unknown' in corrections.

Thin record: only the NHLR entry, the Forest Lookouts index (name and county only) and the OSM node were usable after two searches. No build date, staffing, fire history, access or visit information found. height_m is converted from the register's 80 ft. No access key set because no source gives access. Grokipedia and anyplaceamerica appeared in search results and were not used.

Only one source (the FFLOS page). Two WebSearch calls and one websearch.py fallback found nothing about this tower, its build, staffing, or removal. Only the NHLR entry, the OpenStreetMap point and the Aermotor history were usable. Two WebSearch queries found nothing local about this tower. Identity is the open question. The 1936 notices (quoted on Forest Lookouts from The Lexington Advertiser) describe a CCC-built steel tower on the poor house property north of Lexington. Thin record. The only sources are the NHLR detail page, the July 2020 state public-lands list, and the county wildfire plan, which mentions the E911 and cell towers but no fire lookout. Single source (NHLR). Two searches turned up no build date, builder, staffing or condition history. Thin record. Sources are the NHLR detail page (2022 site visit, build date unknown) and the July 2020 state public-lands list, which shows a Maben Tower under the Forestry Commission. Status is standing on the strength of the 2022 visit note, not a later survey. Single source (NHLR). Two searches found nothing else on this tower. The date the MFC vacated the site and the current owner are unknown; the 'private' access level rests on the Register's 'possibly owned by a timber company' wording. The 'standing' status rests only on the July 2022 visit. The Register's own admin and vacated statements conflict in tone (administered by MFC, yet vacated by MFC), so the story states both.

Thin record: the register page is the only source with dates and agency; Wikipedia and OSM only confirm location and a lattice design tag. Thin record: register page gives registration, agency, elevation, the 100 ft LS-40 design and the 2023 visit; build date is Unknown in the register and no other source found.
