Elevation (7,700 ft) is in the story but not set as a fact, since no field for it is in the facts list; the record's elevation_m is null and can take 2347 m if the editor wants it. No photo found.

Stair status after rehabilitation is unconfirmed; NHLR says the lower stairs were removed in 2005 and no source I read says they were replaced. Completion year is unclear: NHLR says fall 2013 and also lists volunteer staffing from 2012. Search summaries (not cited, not verified) said the tower returned to service in 2012 and was staffed by volunteers 2012-2017 and by a Forest Service employee from 2018. The Forest Service PDF named in the brief (stelprd3792970.pdf) returned 404 and was not used. The NHLR page links a Bob Marshall Wilderness Complex newsletter on the renovations; it is a lead for the stair and completion question. The height correction (3.7 m to 9.1 m) rests on firelookout.com alone. Coordinates match NHLR. The Flathead Beacon source spells the lookout 'Baptise' (typo kept in the quote).

height_m 9.1 in the record is the 30-foot height from the May 1934 plan (the record's source is the Ron Kemnow site); no as-built height was found, so the story says 'planned'. The 1934 and 1936 items are newspaper quotes on the Forest Lookouts page, not checked in the original papers. The 1940 survey text calls the forest the Cabinet National Forest. Two web searches and one page on the Flathead National Forest history (which names the Cabinet National Forest as a separate forest but does not give the change) gave no further detail. No register listing (NHLR or FFLOS) and no photo found. The FFLA list's 'Flathead' column is the county, not the forest, so the forest name rests on firelookout.com alone. The Oct 1940 Pine Mountain item (Sanders County Independent-Ledger, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) says the earlier Barzee site had only a tent; it does not say whether the 1934 tower was finished, so the story keeps 'planned'. The Ron Kemnow source named for height_m is not in the sources list and was not checked.

Two sources agree on the 1922 cabin, the 1934 or 1930s L-4 tower, and the 1962 cab. Staffing and the active-service status are undated, so the current status is medium confidence. The access level was changed from 'restricted' to 'unknown': that was inferred from the active lookout service, and the sources give no visiting rules. The visiting-advice sentence had no source and was removed from the story. The brief's height of 3.0 m is the concrete base, not the overall height. Photos are credited to the Fire Lookout Museum, USFS and Gary Weber, but no image URLs were found, so none are listed. The brief's 'two_story' kind describes the 1922 cabin, not the present structure.

Built 1940 and NHLR registration (2011) match the record. The record's height_m 3.0 is not confirmed: the sources give only "10' wooden tower", with no clear unit, so the height is left out of facts. Abandonment is given only as 'since the 1970s', so the 1970 event year is a decade marker, not a dated event. The 1966 map is described on Pastmaps (a generated description of the map); the map itself was not read. A 1956 Daily Inter Lake item quoted on montanalookouts.weebly.com places a William Justis 'on Barren Peak' but does not say he was at a lookout, so it is omitted. No photos were added; NHLR photos already in the record. Access 'public' is inferred from the hiking route and absence of any closure in the sources read; the record had access 'unknown'.

The brief's 1983 built event is right for the current cab per CSKT, but the 1934 and 1938 towers were missing; they are added. The height_m of 3.7 m equals the 12-foot base, not total height. The access level was changed from permission to unknown on 2026-10-09: no source states a permission rule, and the ask-the-tribes wording is advice. No fire, rental or closure information was found. The fate of the 1934 and 1938 towers is not recorded. The 'late 1950s or early 1960s' first posting has no exact year, so it is not in events. Read budget ran slightly over (7 cached fetches, 1 WebSearch).

Thin record: the 1932 build year and 1957 loss come from one page (firelookout.com). No staffing, fire history or present-day site description was found in two searches and the pages read, so none is in the story; the story is near the 120-word floor. Access left unset because no source describes the site today. No photos with a usable image address were found.

The brief's kind 'platform' is consistent with the index type 'Crowsnest', so it was not changed. The 1935 article places the station 'five miles southeast of Superior'; check the brief's coordinates against that direction on a map before publishing. The second coordinate pair was not checked. No present-day site description, photos, or access information were found.

Build year and location agree across sources; the end date does not. Sources also call the site Bare Mountain and Crossley Ridge Lookout. The Montana History Portal has two Glacier National Park Archives photos (node 5165, HPF 5790, and node 5166) marked copyright undetermined; no image addresses were captured, so no photo entries. The hike guide is a third-party source, not NPS, and it does not link the overlook to the lookout site. Glacier trail status was not checked.

Build history conflicts: NHLR says a camp in 1928 then the L-4 in 1933, while a 1931 clipping says a smoke chaser occupied the Bear Top lookout before the 1932 house. Name variants: Beartop, Bear Top, Bare Top, Bare mountain. No source found for current staffing, rental or visiting status; the register's 'usually staffed' line is undated. The FFLA Facebook post did not load. The Hiking Project trail is not confirmed as the route to the lookout. Pages read: 5 (firelookout, montanalookouts, NHLR, FS cabin page, Hiking Project). Search: 2 queries.

Thin: two listing pages and one 1937 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. No description of the site today was found. Firelookout.com credits 'Lolo National Forest/Montana DNRC'; the record names only the Forest Service. The 1937 injury is reported as White's own account, in the story's words.

Thin: listing pages only. Elevation of 7,099 feet comes from the firelookout.com page and is not in the record; it is not a key in facts, so it appears only in the story. The record's 'ground' kind matches the association list. No photos with direct image URLs were found. No description of the site today was found.

Build year disagrees: firelookout.com says 1953; the newspaper items say work began in September 1952 and was complete by January 1953. The newspaper items are read through the Forest Lookouts transcription page, not from the original papers. The 1964 replacement and 1976 date appear only on firelookout.com. The record's 9.1 m height is the 1953 tower. No description of the site today or of current access was found. The firelookout.com page credits photos to Mike Barr, but no image URLs were found.

Built dates 1931, 1940 and 1965 agree across NHLR, firelookout.com and the Weebly history. The 2017 PDF's roof and assessment lines are not quotable: pdftotext duplicates every line, so check_quotes cannot match them, and the story leaves them out. Current tower condition rests on one Forest Service sentence about restoration. The brief's 2017 'restored' event is overstated (see corrections). Elevation disagrees by about 114 ft between sources. Trail access is public; nothing supports climbing the tower and the story says so.

Two independent web sources agree the tower is gone (firelookout.com: Gone 1969; FFLA list: Tower Gone) and that it was manned in 1960. Build date conflicts: firelookout.com says 1935, the 1936 newspaper items (cited through Forest Lookouts; originals from the Missoulian, Flathead Courier, Char-Koosta and Daily Inter Lake not checked) describe construction in 1936. Height conflicts: 50 ft (firelookout.com) versus about 40 ft (1936 plans). The 1956 NGS survey note reads like a station description, not a tower inspection, so it is not evidence of the tower's condition. Elevation 5,176 ft per firelookout.com; the record has no elevation field. Agency suggestion: the record's agency is null; the Forest Lookouts header and the 1936 items point to the Indian Service, Flathead Indian Agency. Searched once; the CSKT Fire Lookouts page is an interactive list and did not yield Jette text. No NRHP or site visit information found; the site's current condition and access are unknown.

Thin record. Only firelookout.com gives a build year (1933), tower size and end date (1957). Forest Lookouts and the FFLA list give status only, and they describe the ending differently from firelookout.com. One web search and a grep of the Flathead National Forest history (Trails of the Past, npshistory chapters) found nothing specific to this lookout; those hits concern the Big Creek Ranger Station on the North Fork. Elevation 6,430 ft from firelookout.com; the record has no elevation field. Do not confuse with Big Creek Baldy (us-mt-big-creek-baldy), a standing Kootenai NF tower in Lincoln County. No staffing, fire or site-today information found; the story omits those topics.

Reasonably well documented for a rental-program lookout: two independent narrative sources (National Forest Foundation, Western News) corroborate the NHLR/firelookout.com build history. The 1980s retirement from fire duty comes from the National Forest Foundation piece; the 1984 rental start and the builder's name (Stef Ludvikson, for both the 1928 cabin and the 1934 tower) come only from the Western News article — NHLR and firelookout.com do not name a builder, so that attribution rests on a single source. Two small, unresolved conflicts flagged above: the cabin's build year (1928 vs 1929) and the summit elevation (three different figures across sources). A third, odder wrinkle: the National Forest Foundation piece implies the log cabin standing near the tower today was moved to the site in the 1950s to replace a deteriorated building, which sits awkwardly against the 1928/1929 'first structure, still there' framing from NHLR and firelookout.com — the story notes this rather than resolving it. The Purcell Mountains location also comes only from the National Forest Foundation piece. No NRHP nomination form or newspaper archive hit was found in the search budget; a Chronicling America or Montana Memory Project search might turn up more on the 1934 or 1966 construction if someone wants to dig further.

No newspaper or NRHP nomination form located; the 1984 date is NRHP-eligibility, not a formal National Register listing, and the story is careful to say so. Two official-ish sources (Recreation.gov listing vs. the Forest Service's own Lolo NF page) disagree slightly on the lookout's water source: non-potable spring 3/4 mile downhill vs. a filterable spring 0.5 mile away. Wikipedia's 'Big Hole Lookout' article was used only to find the underlying USFS citation (fs.usda.gov/r01/lolo/recreation/big-hole-lookout), not cited directly, per the guide. Record's existing 'design' field was null; proposed a correction above. One WebSearch call used, plus WebFetch on two known URLs. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): firelookout.com actually lists the elevation as 6919 ft, not 6,922 ft, so that figure is now cited to NHLR alone; the 'Cabinet National Forest' detail and the precise staffed-to-1972 date are not on firelookout.com or NHLR's visible text respectively and were re-cited to the sources that actually state them (Recreation.gov and the USFS Lolo NF page); a missing footnote on the cabin's furnishings/vault-toilet sentence was added.

Gone status is consistent across firelookout.com (Abandoned 1942. Gone.) and the FFLA list (Tower Gone); the Forest Lookouts entry has no status line. Build date conflict: a July 1930 newspaper item (via Forest Lookouts) describes construction and an 85-ft tower; firelookout.com dates the L-4 cab to 1934. Height 25.9 m comes from the 1930 newspaper figure, not a later source. Staffing evidence: a July 1930 item says Jack Halfstead was to be stationed there, and a single 1938 item mentions a Hoodoo lookout without naming an observer. Elevation 5,236 ft from firelookout.com; the record has no elevation field. Record fields agree (county Lincoln, agency Kootenai NF). Did not check the 1930 Western News or the 1938 Montana Standard originals, or NHLR and Forest Service records; one web search found nothing more specific. Site today and access are unknown.

Three conflicts for a human. (1) County: the Register says Flathead; the other sources say Lincoln. A correction is proposed, not applied. (2) Elevation: the Register gives 6,841 ft (2,085 m), firelookout.com gives 4,064 ft, and the 2022 visitor account gives 1,237 m. The record keeps the Register figure; this is unresolved. (3) Design and height: the brief's L-4 label and 2.4 m height describe the 1939 tower or match no source, so corrections are proposed. Access, the locked gate and the sign's hours come from one 2022 visitor account; recheck with the Kootenai National Forest before any visit guidance. Staffing as_of is 'undated' because the Register page has no date. The 1948 to 1957 entries come from a fan site quoting newspapers; the originals were not read. No rental was found for this lookout; the Recreation.gov Webb Mtn. rental is a different lookout.

Two WebSearch queries found nothing on Black Peak beyond these three pages. The 1966 USGS recovery note on the Forest Lookouts page reads STATION DESTROYED, but it describes a survey station, not the cabin, so it is not used for the fate. No source describes the site today or public access.

Thin record. The Register description is 'No information at this time', and two web searches found nothing about Black Spring itself. Facts come from four pages: the Register, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts (quoting a 1957 USGS-described survey station) and the FFLA Montana list (undated). Unknown: build date, design, height, staffing, current condition. Open conflicts: distance and bearing from Lame Deer (firelookout 5 mi NW vs survey 2 mi N and 6 mi W); elevation (Register 3,685 ft vs firelookout 3,692 ft). Record's elevation (1123.2 m) is the Register figure, kept. Access level 'restricted' is our reading of tribal land; the record's 'permission' is not stated by any source read, so please pick the level. No photos: firelookout.com credits a photo by Luke Channer but gives no image URL. Not verified: whether the tower stands today.

The brief's events line reads 'None relocated', but the record has a relocated event with no year; corrections propose 1978. The sibling record us-mt-blackpine-mountain-at-missoula-smokejumper-visitor-center says kind ground and status standing, while the Forest Service page only says the visitor center is closed for renovations, so display of the cab is unconfirmed. The first source_pages entry is an internal relative link, so the Forest Service page was used instead. One web search for the original site today found nothing usable. Newspaper dates and quotes come from the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers themselves were not read.

The build date is disputed (1933 against 1938-39), and so is the elevation (7937 ft against 7,500 ft). The 1977 move was planned; firelookout.com dates the move to 1978. The visitor center page says it is closed for renovations; that may have changed by the time anyone visits. We did not confirm that the cab is still on display. Searches: 2 WebSearch calls; about 4 distinct pages read.

Brief status 'gone' confirmed. Brief agency differs from firelookout.com (Montana DNRC); recorded as Flathead National Forest, which both sources name. height_m omitted because the lookout had two towers (40 ft, 53 ft). Access and visit left out: no source describes access. Staffing as_of 1952 is the last named lookout, not a closing date. Trails of the Past (foresthistory.org) mentions a Blacktail mining prospect, not this lookout; not used. The Blacktail Mountain Ski Area near Lakeside is a different business as far as the sources show; not used. Photo credit on firelookout.com (Barbara Boorman, Fire Lookout Museum) has no image URL in the fetched text; none added. Staffing and fire history is thin: no fires are named in either source.

The register and firelookout.com disagree on the tower's form (flat top versus two-story cab). Neither gives a removal date; the Montana page's bare 'Removed' label is ambiguous, so the story gives no date for removal. Firelookout.com's photo credit names Larry Smith, while the register spells the name Lawrence. Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook posts give different 1960 and 1961 wording, but their text was not readable from the cache, so they are not used. The brief's access 'unknown' was left unset.

Location, forest and elevation conflict. The register (US 2058, MT 9) places the site in the Kootenai National Forest, Sanders County, Montana, at 5,863 ft, matching the record's elevation_m 1787 and coordinates. Firelookout.com gives the same 5,863 ft but says Shoshone County, Idaho/Sanders County, Montana, on the Coeur d'Alene/Kootenai forests. The Idaho Fire Lookouts site gives 4,932 ft and the Coeur d'Alene National Forest, and it lists a 30-foot L-4 tower. The record's kind 'ground' follows the register's wording ('may have been an L-4 cab'). The register hedges the design, so no correction is proposed. Staffing is unknown. The Idaho site has no staffing history, and no other staffing source was found. The 'removed after 1943' wording is vague; the year 1943 in the event list is the register's bound, not a confirmed removal date. No access statement from the Forest Service was found; the Idaho site's 'Drive-Up' label is the only access evidence. The Idaho site's photo ('Photo circa 2011') has no licence given, so no photo is proposed. The Montana state listing (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/mt/) was checked for the Bloom Peak line and lists it with 'Sanders/Shoshone (ID)'.

Blue Mountain (Kootenai NF, Libby) is a different site from other Blue Mountain lookouts in Montana, so keep the Libby identity and the NHLR number US 342, MT 24. Height conflicts (72 vs 80 ft). Current staffing and access are unconfirmed: firelookout.com is undated and describes summer staffing, and a travel blog with no visible date describes a host trailer and a rough road. The Kootenai camping-and-cabins page excerpt I read does not list Blue Mountain, but the list was partial, so rental status is left unstated. No notable fire at the site appears in these sources. The 2020 PDF could not be quote-checked because its extracted text is duplicated, so the 2020 assessment is in events without a quote.

Access level omitted: the register gives no access rule, and the 2013 KGVO report is the only road description. No staffing key: the register calls it active, undated. Elevation not used: the register gives 1,940 m, and a search summary gave a different figure I could not confirm on a fetched page. A search summary mentioned a 37-year lookout staffer; it was not on any fetched page, so it is left out. Film-date conflict is unresolved and flagged in the story.

Brief status 'gone' and design 'L-4' confirmed; design now reads 40' pole L-4. height_m 12.2 is 40 ft converted to metres. Access left out: no source describes access or the site today. Build year conflict (1934 vs c.1936) is the main open question. Forest Lookouts has 'Frenchtown district' and township 17N-23W-31; firelookout.com gives 14 miles east of Superior. No image URLs were in the fetched text (firelookout.com credits the Fire Lookout Museum); none added.

Brief status 'gone' and height 15.2 m (50 ft) both confirmed; design added from sources. Only firelookout.com gives the 1957 destruction date. Staffing: no source names a lookout. Access and visit left out: no source describes access or the site today. Forest Lookouts' 1938 newspaper items carry the construction story (Independent Record and Missoulian). No image URLs in the fetched text; none added.

Brief record is consistent with sources: coordinates, Ground type and Lolo National Forest agency all match. Build year 1931 is supported by two sources. Fate conflicts (destroyed 1962 vs removed, undated). Nothing found on staffing, fires or current condition. Sanders County Ledger column (cite 4) is general on L-4 design and does not list Border Peak.

The 1920 build year rests on one source (Fire Lookout). The 2003 loss is supported by three sources. Two WebSearch queries returned only unrelated 2022 fire coverage. No source describes the site today or access.

Built year (1937) and L-4 design agree across sources, so confidence on those is high. Current condition is the weak point: no source found is dated after the 2003 restoration, and firelookout.com's 'presently abandoned' note is undated. The nomination's condition description has no date in the text I read. Location: the record uses the NHLR point (45.83737, -114.28933); the RIDB point (45.82449, -114.29445) in the record is about 1.5 km away. Not resolved; a human should check which point is right. Elevation: 7,688 ft (NHLR) vs 7,753 ft (firelookout.com); the record's 2343.3 m follows NHLR. NRHP listing date not confirmed: I did not read the NPGallery listing record for a date; search snippets suggest 2018 but are unverified, so no listing-date event was written. Staffing ended 'mid-1980s' (approximate year 1985). The 1958 start of the staff list is the first name listed on firelookout.com; staff names are deliberately not reproduced.

Brief record matches sources: coordinates 48.18180, -109.68475 and Ground type. Brief has no agency; none found in cited sources. No build date, fate date or present-day description found; two web searches returned only location and reservation context. Quoted NGS datasheet (cite 2) is reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page. Distance from Havre differs between sources (26 vs 30 miles).

Brief record matches sources: coordinates 47.33482, -115.22456, Tower type and L-4 design. Agency Lolo National Forest added from both pages (brief had none). Fate conflicts (abandoned vs removed, both undated). The Forest Lookouts page credits '(Kresek)' without naming a work; a WebSearch linked Ray Kresek's book on Northwest lookouts but could not confirm it covers Boyd Mountain, so it is not cited. Nothing found on staffing, fires or current condition.

Build dates conflict: a 1922 camp and 1939 L-4 cab on firelookout.com versus a 1930 Superior Building Company pre-cut house on the Forest Lookouts page. The 1930 entry is unverified. Two searches found nothing specific to Bruce Ridge, and no staffing or fire records were found. The removal date is unknown. No source describes the site today or its access.

Thin record: the register has no description, firelookout.com has one line, and the Montana list confirms standing status and register numbers. Searches for fires, staffing, design and height found nothing for this tower. The brief's access value 'permission' has no supporting source, so it is proposed as unknown and omitted from facts. Coordinates, county, 1930 build, 2022 registration and elevation (1,433 m) match the register. Story length is set by this evidence.

Brief height_m 4.6 does not appear in any page read, so it is omitted from facts; the editor should check its source. The 1930 build year comes only from firelookout.com. Staffing and the 1948 fire come from newspaper clippings reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page; they are checked against that reprint, not the original papers. Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1971 and the Forest Lookouts page says removed in 1971. Access level public is inferred. No source describes the site today.

Thinnest record of the three: two short pages and one list row. No staffing, fire, builder or removal date was found. Two searches found no Bunker Point lookout source in Montana. Search results also returned Bunker Hill (a Washington lookout) and Bunker Park (a landform in Flathead County); do not mix these up.

Fate: blog and Kamstra give 1950 destroyed/gone; Kemnow says removed with no date. Kemnow page gives Lolo NF and Missoula County. Staffing: no source found. Remains at the summit: not described by any source read; the Kamstra and Kemnow pages are brief. The 2011 blog is a personal blog; its 1932 and 1950 dates are the main sources beyond Kamstra.

Built year conflicts: Kamstra 1934 vs 1937 press (story follows press). Fate conflicts: destroyed 1978 (Kamstra) vs removed, undated (Kemnow). Location conflict in the record remains open: FFLA 46.21766,-113.2213 vs west_us_lookouts 46.2527,-113.19339, about 4.4 km apart; the 1937 papers only say northeast of Georgetown Lake. Last known staffing is 1943; no later date found. Not checked: the forest's current name, and whether anything remains on the peak.

Brief's 1921 'built' and L-4 design/12.2 m height describe earlier structures, not the present steel tower, so corrections are proposed. Build date and design of the 1984 steel tower are not given by any source read. No access or visitor information found; a WebSearch for rental or visiting returned nothing for Calx (Big Creek Baldy and Yaak Mountain results were for other towers and were not used). Staffing has no year.

Dates disagree and are not settled. Present tower: Register 1960, lookout site 1961. Earlier structure: 1956 inspection gives 'Year Built - 1933' for a 50-foot catwalk tower with a 14 by 14 foot cab; Register and lookout site give 1935 for a 20-foot pole first lookout; a 1928 newspaper lists Camel's Hump among new structures, which would precede 1935. Height correction (record 6.1 m to 12.5 m) assumes the 41-foot figure is to the cab floor; the sources only say '41' tower', so please check. 'Staffed every summer' is in the 2022 Register text and in an older lookout site; no current staffing or access source found. Two web searches returned no rental or visit listing for this lookout (hits were other Camel's Hump peaks). Access left out of facts. No photos added; firelookout.com credits photos but gives no image URLs. Medium confidence because the three historical pages agree on the 1956 replacement need but not on dates.

Thin record: brief one-line entries only. Kamstra's 1940 may or may not be the build year. The O'Neil description names Canyon among neighbouring stations, some unmanned, but does not say Canyon was unmanned. No remains or access description found. The NRHP Hornet Lookout form cites Flathead NF improvement plan records, which may hold Canyon's construction details; not searched.

Dates and design come only from firelookout.com (one page). The Forest Lookouts page gives the county, forest, township and section. Two web searches found no other account of the cab, its staffing, fires or present state. The record label credits Ron Kemnow for the Forest Lookouts site; the page read does not show that name, so the story does not use it.

Dates (1936 cab, 1955 abandonment) come only from firelookout.com. The Forest Lookouts page marks the site 'Removed' with no date. Two web searches found nothing on Cardinal Peak in the Seeley Lake area and no account of staffing, fires or the present site. The 8,551-foot elevation is recorded only in the story, not in facts, because the facts schema has no elevation key.

firelookout.com gives only decades (1940s build, 1950s abandonment), so no year-level built or abandoned events are recorded. The 1939 Augusta News plan may not match the 1940s date; the story reports both and says neither source reconciles them. Height 6.1 m is 20 feet converted; check before publishing. Two web searches found no other account of the tower or site; the Helena/Lewis & Clark National Forest office may hold records.

Brief height_m 6.1 matches the 20-foot tower planned in the 1937 item, not a documented built height, so it is left out of facts for you to decide. Brief kind two_story matches the firelookout.org label '2-Story cab'. Access moves from unknown to public on trail evidence only; no agency closure statement read. The 1937 item names High peak; only the Forest Lookouts page ties it to Casey Peak. The blog links a Helena Independent Record article on the lookout that I did not open. No staffing, fire or rental information found for this site.

Brief record (gone, Lolo NF, 12.2 m) matches the sources, so no corrections. A 2016 Forest Service list of Clearwater lookouts (fs.usda.gov/media/259185) has no Cayuse entry in the text I searched, so the 1933 'Clearwater forest' wording looks like an error or may refer to a different tower; a Lolo NF or Montana SHPO record would settle it. The 1932 build date and the private-land note rest on firelookout.com alone. The web search turned up only an unrelated Cayuse Hills range in Sweet Grass County. No staffing or fire records found.

Brief height_m was null; the 30-foot pole height from firelookout.com gives 9.1 m and is added to facts. The NGS station position (47 40 04.93 N, 113 56 13.87 W, NAD 83) is about 50 m from the record coordinates, which supports the location. The Forest Lookouts page gives 22N-18W-17 as its location; not checked against other records. Removal date and cause are not given in any source read, and no source describes the site today or public access. The 1951 item shows only that the lookout was still used as a landmark, not that it was staffed. Two web searches found no other Cedar Point lookout in Montana.

Dates (1933, 1947, about 2000) rest on one site, firelookout.com, which also says the tower was a 30-foot pole L-4 tower with a crow's nest. Forest Lookouts and the FFLA list only give Removed and Gone. The Pastmaps map label (1968, published 1970) is the only later reference and does not say whether a structure stood. Brief record was right on status, kind and coordinates; added design and height. Elevation 7,017 ft per firelookout.com has no facts key, so it is left out of the JSON. No staffing, access or photo data found. Web searches used: 2.

Thin record. All construction and abandonment dates come from one page (firelookout.com) and are decades only, so the 1940 and 1950 event years stand in for the decades; read them as decade markers. Forest Lookouts gives location only, no status. The FFLA list gives Gone and Ground, which match the brief record, so no corrections. No staffing, access, fire or photo data found. Web searches used: 3, one over the budget of 2.

Status corrected from gone to abandoned: both sources say Abandoned, with no removal noted. No source gives a year for abandonment, so no abandoned event is recorded. The 1930s camp on firelookout.com and the 1935 placement report are both kept, and the 1935 date is a newspaper report quoted secondhand by Forest Lookouts; the Missoulian itself was not read. The summit figure 7231 on firelookout.com is unclear and is not used. Coordinates 46.5574, -113.7669 from the FFLA list match the record. No access or photo data found. Web searches used: 2.

Build year 1958 is in all three pages (Register, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts). The 1930s tent camp has no exact year, so it is not an event. Elevation disagrees: Register 9,097 ft (record 2,772.8 m) vs firelookout.com 9,235 ft; the Register figure is kept, unresolved. Wood vs treated timber left open (Register says wood; the other two say treated). Height 3.05 m is 10 feet from the sources; the record's 3.0 m was not changed. 'Last used for emergencies in the late 1960s' is the only use source; the staffing status 'no longer staffed' is our reading of it, not a source phrase. Two web searches gave a 1957 build date and a Big Sky location; neither was cited because those pages were not read. No source read says whether the cab is open to visitors. No photos found with image URLs. Not verified: current condition.

Two independent write-ups (firelookout.com and the 2021 Ledger column) agree on the 1934 build, the 20-foot L-4 design and staffing to 1969. The forest is disputed (Lolo vs Kootenai) and the story says so; check which one the brief should carry. The Ledger spells the town Thomson Falls; the quote is kept as printed. A search surfaced Cougar Peak Lookout and other Sanders County lookouts; none is this site and none was used. No source describes the site today, and no source gives access.

Record says status gone, design L-4, height 6.1 m, access unknown. NHLR says the 1928 cabin is still there, so status and design were corrected; kind 'tower' fits the 1935 tower rather than the cabin, editor to decide. Not verified: the 2012-2014 rehabilitation and the 2016 paint and 2017 gable and wall work from the existing record. The NWMT 2014 and 2017 project pages were not readable (the 2017 page is a PDF wrapper), so those events are left out. The 2014 date rests on the North Fork post's link to the 2014 projects page. The 1930s platform tower has no year in the sources, so it is not an event. Access 'public' is inferred from the national forest trail route; trail details are from an older hike report, so check current road and trail status. The NHLR coordinate sits at 7,268 ft, between the cabin (7,285 ft) and the 1935 tower (7,105 ft). No new photos added.

Both lookout write-ups agree on the 1934 build, the 30-foot L-4 design, the Lolo National Forest and the Mineral County location. Nothing in the sources read says how or when the tower came down beyond gone by 1967. A WebSearch surfaced an onXmaps trail listing (Cobden Point Lookout, FSR 9907) that says the tower was dismantled in 1967 and describes a route up Deep Creek Road (FSR 285). Fetching that page returned HTTP 404, so it is not cited anywhere. If it can be recovered, it would be the only source on the site today and would need a fresh quote check. The 'Removed' label on the Forest Lookouts page is not used as evidence.

Weakest of the three. Build date (1936 or 1937) and end date (1971 destruction vs 1972 removal plan) disagree and the story reports both. The only description of the site today is an undated-in-body hiker's forum post started Aug 30, 2016; it is anecdotal and not an official source. The forum post places Rimini near Red Mountain, while the 1935 article says Colorado mountain is near Rimini; flag this for the editor. The forest name is Helena National Forest as printed in both lookout write-ups. A second search found no Forest Service record for the lookout. Access is not stated in any source; no access level is set.

Tower-specific detail is thin: firelookout.com gives the build year, height and gone-by-1975; the other lookout pages only say Removed or Tower Gone. Station and rental facts come from the Forest Service page and a rental blog. Height 27.4 m is converted from 90 ft. The Bigfork Eagle 1956 caption is the only evidence the tower stood after 1949 apart from the 1975 cutoff. The Montana Ranger Stations correction names the truck shed date but gives no tower date. No source describes the tower footings today.

Very thin record. Firelookout.com is the only source with a build year, a destruction year and the elevation. Forest Lookouts and the FFLA list say only Removed or Tower Gone. Two searches found no newspaper, Forest Service or survey source for this tower. Height 9.1 m is converted from 30 ft. No source describes the site today or its access, so no access key is set.

No access level: nothing fetched says whether the tower can be entered. Staffing conflict is unresolved; the 2016 report is the only dated staffing source (its 2014 sister report was not read). Brief's R-6 design belongs to the 1968 tower; the 1933 first tower was L-4. Trail facts come from a Seeley Lake visitor page on the Rumble Creek Lakes hike, not a Forest Service source. A 1956 Forest Service photo caption mentions a Condon lookout tower but cannot be tied to Cooney, so it is omitted. Height 30 ft converted to 9.1 m.

NPGallery asset page metadata was readable but the full nomination narrative PDF text did not come through in the grep; architect name (Clyde Fickes) and significance period are confirmed from the metadata fields themselves. No new photos found.

Thin record. Firelookout.com gives 1936, abandoned in the 1930s, still there in 2014, and the 2016 burn of the tree. Forest Lookouts gives only the tent-camp description and the 22N-27W-14 location code. The FFLA list says Abandoned, so the status choice is a judgement call for the editor. The brief lists kind platform, which matches the crow's nest. No source describes the site today, and two searches found no fire report for 2016.

The 1926 build date and 1972 destruction rest on firelookout.com; the Weebly page corroborates the 1972 vandalism and planned burning but does not name the building, and calls it an outlook. The 1956 Coast and Geodetic Survey text describes a small white house at the survey mark, which suggests a building was still there in 1956. Brief's status 'gone' and county match both lists. No corrections proposed. Nothing found on what remains at the site or on public access; the access field is left out.

Only two lookout listings and a USGS name entry. The build decade, the 1956 abandonment and the 1959 burn rest on the firelookout.com listing alone. Nothing found on staffing, on what remains at the site, or on public access; the access field is left out.

Build year 1937 and destruction in the 1950s rest on firelookout.com; the 1940 survey text independently shows a lookout house in place. Only the destruction decade is given, so the 1950 event year is a placeholder for the decade. Brief's status 'gone' and county match. No corrections proposed. Nothing found on staffing, on what remains at the site, or on public access; the access field is left out.

Thinnest of the three: three short pages, no dates for building or removal, no staffing, no photos. The firelookout.com line '1930s: history unknown. Abandoned.' does not say whether the decade is the build or the abandonment, so the story says so. The FFLA list coordinates are 48.00000 -113.14046; the latitude is a round number and may be approximate, so check the location before relying on it. The story is about 123 words after this check's wording fixes, so it meets the 120-word guide floor; the sources give no more, and it was not padded. Not checked: 1930s newspapers and Flathead NF history reports, which could date the lookout.

Only one dated source: a June 1938 Sanders County Independent-Ledger item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. The original newspaper was not opened, and the item reports the start of construction, not completion. Removal date and site condition are unknown. Two current lists agree on Lolo NF, Mineral County and gone. Consider adding Cruzana Mountain to other_names, since firelookout.com uses that spelling. The story is about 117 words, just under the 120-word guide level; the sources give no more, and it was not padded. Next step if budget allows: 1938-1970s Sanders or Mineral County newspapers for completion and removal.

The 1935 and 1936 items are newspaper quotes printed on the Forest Lookouts page; the original Sanders County Independent-Ledger was not opened. The destroyed-versus-removed conflict is unresolved. The access and trail details come from an undated hiking guide and are used for access only; no source describes the lookout site itself today. The guide gives the summit as 7,110 ft; the record elevation_m is still null, so it could be filled with a note on the source. Possible next step: 1959 Sanders County newspapers for the end of the tower.

Structure and dates are well corroborated (NHLR and firelookout.com agree). Staffing evidence is dated (2014 guide) or undated (NHLR); the Trekking Wild visit is undated. No fire history, NRHP nomination or rental listing found. Elevation not used: NHLR gives 6,028 ft, firelookout gives 6031 ft. Verify current season and cab access with the Flathead National Forest before publishing.

Build year conflict: listings say 1931, a July 1930 newspaper item (quoted on montanalookouts) describes the station being established. Collapse year: 1971 vs winter 1971-72. No source found on what remains at the site, or on access; the story says so and nothing more. One websearch.py lookup done; no NRHP or Forest Service page found. The firetower.org page mentions a Gary Weber photo with no usable URL, so no photo was added.

The 1971 destruction date rests on firelookout.com alone; two web searches found no second source. Only the two lookout pages and the 1933-34 newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page were read; the NHLR and FFLOS registers hold no entry for this site. Firelookout.com gives elevation 6767 ft; the record has none. Record coordinates were not checked against the 7-mile description. The 1933 items mention an existing lookout before the 1934 tower; the sources do not say whether the new tower replaced it. Story is about 150 words.

Brief's height_m 2.1 is wrong; sources describe a 60 ft steel tower. Two WebSearch queries and four page reads found no staffing, fire history or abandonment date. Searches for Davis Mountain returned other lookouts and a 2018 Davis Fire near Yaak, none used. The 2017 Northwest Montana FFLA newsletter PDF mentions only volunteers named Davis. No access level given: abandoned status alone does not establish closed, so access is omitted.

Distance conflicts: the 1944 item says 20 miles south of Missoula by road; firelookout.com says 11 miles south. Both are reported in the story. Chronology gap: the January 1946 item says the model was being completed, and the 1957 entries say a new 41-foot tower was erected; no source read says how the two relate. Height: the record's height_m 12.2 (40 ft) matches the 1946 design, while the 1957 structure is 41 ft per both lookout pages; not changed. Elevation: firelookout.com gives 5699 ft for Davis Point. Blue Mountain figures differ between sources (firelookout.com 6460 ft; NHLR 6,366 ft; cab 14x14 in the 1946 plan, 15x15 in the NHLR entry); the Blue Mountain record (us-mt-blue-mountain-lolo-nf) should carry its own story. The filming claim in the NHLR entry was not checked elsewhere. A web search found no description of the Davis Point site today.

Two Montana pages only. The 1941 and 1950 dates come from firelookout.com alone; the Forest Lookouts page gives a location code and the word Removed, with no date. Two web searches found no second source. Not used: an Idaho Deer Creek Point page on idaholookouts.weebly.com (not read; a different site) and a 1931 Deer Creek Fire incident on the Kootenai NF, which involved a different lookout. Record kind 'ground' fits the cabin entry. Record has no elevation; firelookout.com gives 8,367 ft. Record coordinates not checked against the distance description.

Record check: height_m 3.0 is not carried. It matches the 10-foot concrete base, not a sourced overall tower height. Conflicts left open: the first cabin is dated 1926 by NHLR and firelookout.com, but a September 1924 newspaper item already has a man stationed there, so the station may be older. Present cab: NHLR 1960 vs newspaper 1961 (see corrections). No notable fire was found in the sources read. No access or visiting information was found, so the access key is omitted. Staffing evidence is an undated firelookout.com page; no 2020s staffing source was found. Reads: 5 pages (NHLR, firelookout.com, montanalookouts, two Bitterroot pages; the Darby district page and the fire management page did not mention the lookout) and 2 searches. The Forest Fire Lookout Association 2025 social post in search results (about the 1926 cabin) was not read.

Built and destroyed dates come from one page (firelookout.com). Two web searches found no second source; they returned only other lookouts, and Mineral Peak, a different lookout, was not used. The 1935 item is known only as quoted by montanalookouts.weebly.com; the Missoulian was not read. The source gives 30' without saying it is tower height, so height_m is omitted. No access or visit facts: no source describes them, so the brief's access 'unknown' stands. No photos added: firelookout.com credits a photo to the Fire Lookout Museum but gives no image URL.

Brief record checks out: county, status, and coordinates match the FFLOS list. Open conflicts: the 1919 cabin is only on two sources; destroyed (firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb) versus removed (Weebly); and the visit note's hang-gliding site versus the half-mile-south location. Access 'public' is inferred from the visitor's road description, not an official statement. Summit elevation differs between sources (WillhiteWeb 6,440 ft; Weebly calls it almost 7,000 ft), so it is left out. No photo records added.

No source gives an original construction/first-staffed date before the 1958 relocation, or details on specific notable fires fought from this lookout. 'Yager' vs 'Yeager' Butte spelling differs between NHLR and Recreation.gov; story uses both forms once. firelookout.com (source 3) duplicates NHLR's text nearly verbatim, so it was used only to corroborate, not as an independent source.

Brief says NPS-administered with 1931 build and 2022 registration; both confirmed. Build and replacement dates conflict (1931 house; 1932 vs 1934 octagon; 1938 header). The NPS article (cached copy, last updated August 12, 2025) calls Divide Lookout one of the few left from Moe's era, which conflicts with firetower.org and firelookout.com; the story flags the conflict and does not resolve it, so check the NPS page before relying on any 'today' description. No source gives current public access; the story omits it. Foundation is the only remains described (firetower.org, as of 2022). Firetower.org mentions a 2022 photo by Michael Wharton and firelookout.com credits photos to Mark Hufstetler and Luke Channer, but neither page gives a usable image URL, so no photos were added. Page-read budget used up; no WebSearch beyond one websearch.py query. The 1932 observer and the 1934 lookout station were planned in the reports, not confirmed, so the staffing fact was dropped and the 1932 event is marked as planned.

Coordinates conflict: the record uses the FFLA point 47.96641, -116.02442; firelookout.com gives 47.97274, -116.03039. Not resolved; treat the point as approximate. Staffing left out: Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history. Idaho Fire Lookouts has Weber family photos (1937, 1939, 1971) of the site, not added here because the page gives no image URLs in the cache. No source describes remains or public access today.

Brief kind 'ground' kept: FFLOS's 'Ground' fits a cab on piers with no tower. The Sanders County Ledger text reads 'rick piers', most likely a typo for 'rock', so it is not quoted in the story. No staffing, fire or current-site information in the sources read. No access source. Photo credit on firelookout.com (Fire Lookout Museum) has no image URL in the cache, so no photo record was added.

Height 13.7 m in the brief matches the 1959 survey's 45 ft overall for the cab on pole framework; it does not match the 1925 steel tower (35 ft) or the 1935 pole tower (20 ft). Destruction year unresolved: firelookout.com says 1961; the 1967 survey note says about three years before 1967. Cusick gives no date for the tower or for the worker's lookout job. No access or current-site source. Brief had no agency; Montana DNRC added from firelookout.com.

Three sources only. The 1930 staffing report and the 1931 build date conflict and the story says so. No photos found. No public-access information found, so the story points readers to the Flathead National Forest. Brief record had no conflicts to correct.

Brief's existing record (built 1933, L-4, 6.1m height) is consistent with Recreation.gov/firelookout.com; only NHLR's page gives 1932 instead, so the story reports the one-year discrepancy rather than silently picking a side. NRHP reference number 100002041 taken from the brief's register field, which matches NHLR's own cross-reference. No newspaper coverage or NRHP nomination PDF was consulted; confidence is high because three independent, consistent descriptive sources exist even though they disagree on the exact year.

Brief listed agency as Kootenai NF; corrected to Lolo NF. Fate of the tower and building is contested (1969 removal vs 1978 destruction) and the story says so. The 2020 Priscilla Peak move is a proposal; no completion record found. The Forest Service project page for it (project 58117) showed no status in the copy read. Verify with Lolo NF before publishing any claim that the move happened. No photos gathered.

Brief record matches the sources (tower, Bitterroot NF, gone); no corrections. No staffing names for Dutch Hill itself in any source read. The Kress Point newspaper item may describe a different station; the story does not assume it does. Fate of the original L-4 cab after its 1968 replacement is not described in the sources, so the story omits it. The Antrim Point index entry (Gone) was not used. No photos gathered.

No source gives access, so the access key is left out and the brief's 'unknown' stands. No source describes what remains on the site today. NGS listing ST0579 'EAST SPREAD LOOKOUT TOWER' is at 47 09 36 / 113 03 16, which matches the brief's coordinates, but its status codes are unclear, so it is not cited. The 2024 Seeley Swan Pathfinder item is an opinion column by a former seasonal worker. The 1967 list is a planned-use list, not a staffing record. Height correction (15.2 to 6.1 m) rests on firelookout.com's 20-foot wording; please confirm.

Distance conflict left open: firelookout.com says 8 miles southeast of Thompson Falls, the 2020 Ledger says about 21 miles southeast. The visiting hours and gate description come from a commercial operator's page and are not verified with the Forest Service; the access level is my judgment. The lookout was confirmed staffed in 2020 only; NHLR's still-staffed statement is undated. Record's height_m 3.0 is not carried (no sourced overall height). Reads: 6 pages and 2 searches. Brief's build year 1982 is the present cab, which the sources support.

Built year conflicts: 1935 (firelookout.com) against 1928 and 1934 newspaper mentions; the 1928 item is ambiguous. The 20-foot height comes only from firelookout.com's '20' pole' wording. The photo url is the Montana History Portal item page, not the image file, so the editor will need the image file if it is used. The 1967 list is planned use, not confirmed staffing. No source describes the site today, and access is not documented.

History is well covered by two independent sources (firelookout.com and the 2026 Pathfinder column). No source describes what remains today, so the story says so. Brief access 'unknown' is omitted because no access level is supported. The OpenStreetMap point is a map entry, not evidence of a structure. The firelookout.com photo (credited to the Fire Lookout Museum) was not added because no image URL was found. Page reads ran over the six-read budget because of repeat reads of cached pages.

Thin record: the 1938 and 1963 dates come only from firelookout.com. The montanalookouts page says 'Removed' with no date, so no removal event is dated. A Reddit thread (r/firelookouts) for this site could not be read. Access is not documented, so the brief's 'unknown' stands. No source describes what remains at the site today.

Location: the record's NHLR point and the FFLA 'Elk Patrol' point (48.46258, -114.89668) are about 1.56 km apart, and no source here explains why. The FFLA Montana list also has a separate 'Elk Mountain' entry (Lincoln, 48.45553, -114.91496, marked 'Tower Gone') at the NHLR point's coordinates, so it may duplicate this record or us-mt-elk-mountain; a human should check. Kind: the record says 'ground', but the 1940 structure is a 10 ft pole tower with an L-4 cab; the 1923 cab is described only as a frame cab with roof platform. Photos: the NHLR photos are already on the record; firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum, Gary Weber and Luke Channer, but no image URL was found, so none added.

Do not confuse with the NHLR Elk Mountain Lookout (US 1504, MT 82, Lincoln County, Kootenai NF), a different tower. The 1930 vs 1932 build date and 1963 vs 1965 destruction date are unresolved; the NPS 1930 report was read only as quoted by Forest Lookouts. The photo record says copyright not specified; check before reuse.

Thin record: three sources, no description of the site today, and no staffing history. The 1948 date comes only from firelookout.com and the reason for removal is not given. The Hungry Horse News 1948 archive (loc.gov) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A Flathead NF history (npshistory.com, chapter 6) does not mention Emery Hill. Firelookout.com spells the name Emery; the 1933 item spells it Emory. Worth checking Hungry Horse News 1948 and Flathead NF lookout records before publication.

The firelookout.org index also lists a different Falls Point (Ravalli County, camp abandoned); do not mix it with this site. The CDT article on cdtcoalition.org is about Patrol Mountain, not Falls Point, and is not used. Access 'public' is inferred from the trail descriptions in PNW-SOTA; no closure is described.

Only three thin pages (two one-line firelookout.com and montanalookouts entries, plus the FFLA list row). Build date and fate disagree across sources, and the 1931 staffing notice predates the 1934 build date. No NRHP, Forest Service or newspaper-archive record was reached. The records place the site at 48.10209, -115.98305; access is unknown.

Gone status is consistent across three sources. The build year (1929) conflicts with a 1928 newspaper item, and the elevation differs slightly (8241 vs 8,200). Only three thin pages were available; no Lolo National Forest record or newspaper archive was reached. Records place the site at 47.21725, -113.12463.

Built year: the register's 1970 and the sources' 1935 cabin are both correct for different structures, so the story gives both. Staffing: 'staffed every summer' appears on the register and the tribal page, but neither page is dated, so the 2022 as_of was removed (it was the register's registration year).
