Build year 1953 is well corroborated across NHLR, firelookout.com and 1952-1953 newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. Staffing is only described as summer and is undated. The Moss Mountain Inn guide is a lodging site's hiking article and its road-access and gate details are undated. No fire history or rental listing found. Verify current access and staffing with the Flathead National Forest. Brief record fields (design L-4, 1953 build, 2011 registration) are supported, so no corrections proposed.

The 1937 date, design and the 1958 date come only from firelookout.com; the other two sources confirm the site is gone without dates. The 8,525-foot elevation and the 21-mile location appear only on firelookout.com. This is the Montana Fish Lake, not us-wa-fish-lake (Washington). No Bitterroot National Forest record or newspaper was reached.

Dates (1928 built, 1942 abandoned) come from one firelookout.com line; the Association list supplies the Gone status. Rex's page has only the land location code and no history. Two searches turned up nothing on staffing, fires or the site today. Fisher Point (Granite County, a camp on the same list) is a different site and was not used. The story is short because the sources are.

The record's L-4 design and 15.2 m height describe the 1934 pole tower, not the platform (see corrections). Staffing rests on a 1930 Western News item as quoted by Rex's page; the original newspaper was not checked. The trip report is dated October 2020, so the current condition may have changed since. The L-4 loss is only dated 'late 1940s', so it has no event entry. firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Rex Kamstra, but no image URL was in the cache, so none were added.

Thin record: the build and abandonment dates and the elevation come from one firelookout.com page; the Association list and Rex's page add the status and land location. Nothing on staffing, fires or the site today was found in the search. A Watch Duty listing (search snippet only, page not opened) shows a 3-acre 'Foolhen Fire' on Foolhen Mountain dated 27 Sep 2025; no source ties it to the platform, so it is left out of the story.

The 1933 build year and 1977 destruction rest on firelookout.com alone; two searches found no second source. The agency conflict (Glacier National Park vs Flathead National Forest) is unresolved. The creek name is spelled Hallowat in the title and Hollowat in the text. Height of 9.1 m is converted from the listed 30' pole. Elevation on firelookout.com is 6497' but has no facts key. Hungry Horse News and Daily Inter Lake archives could confirm the 1977 removal.

Every date (1940 build, 1948 abandonment) comes from firelookout.com alone. Forest Lookouts gives only the legal location and agency. Two searches found nothing more on this site. The brief's coordinates and agency match the Association's list. The Flathead National Forest records or Hungry Horse News archives could confirm the dates.

Only firelookout.com dates the lookout (1930s) and describes its remains (ruins). Forest Lookouts gives the legal location and agency. Two searches found no history of this lookout. The 1930 event year is only the start of the decade, not a source date. Missoula ranger district or Lolo NF heritage files may hold site records.

No source gives an end date for staffed fire-watch duty, or names any specific fire spotted from Garnet Mountain. The brief's record flags a build-year conflict across sources, but all three sources checked here agree on the same build sequence (1930 camp / 1950 cab / 1962 cab), so no conflict was found in what we read; it's possible the flagged conflict is against a source not checked in this pass (e.g. an NRHP nomination). Fact-check 2026-10-04: the draft misstated Garnet Mountain as sitting 'in the Gallatin Range' -- source 2 lists the Gallatin Range only as a feature visible to the south, not the mountain's own range, so the story was corrected to list it alongside the other viewed features. Two footnote citations were also wrong: the 1950 secondhand-cab/Lincoln Mountain sentence had cited source 2 (Recreation.gov), which says nothing about that history, instead of source 3 (firelookout.com); and the 'one of the more popular lookouts' claim, which comes only from source 3's wording, had been attached to sources 1 and 2.

Dates rest on one page (firelookout.com): 1936 L-4 cab and 1956 abandonment. The 1940 Geodetic Survey description (Forest Lookouts page) is the only independent sighting of the structure. The two sources use different reference points (Spotted Bear vs Big Prairie); not reconciled. The record's elevation is null; firelookout.com gives 8121 ft, which has no slot in facts. The Forest Lookouts page also carries a 'Removed' tag without a date, not used. No staffing, fire or access information found in the three pages read. Forest Service records were not checked.

Staffing and fire history: none found in one search and the pages read. A search summary mentioned a 1934 claim near Garry above Nyack citing npshistory.com Trails of the Past ch. 9, but the cached chapter has no Garry match, so it is unused; the Trails of the Past PDF at foresthistory.org is the next place to check. The Glacier archive photo (HPF 2605, dated 1971-02-28, David S. Shea) is the same image already on the record, so no new photo entry. Elevation 4,499 ft (register) vs 4500' (firelookout.com) is immaterial.

Brief's 'height_m: 1.8' field looks like an error or placeholder (1.8m is under 6 feet, implausible for any lookout tower; rec.gov says the current tower is 40 feet tall). Flagging as a possible data issue for the editor rather than a sourced correction, since no source gives a tower height in meters directly. Built-year conflict (1963 vs 1964 for the current tower) handled as the brief's note anticipated.

Two independent, detailed sources agree closely on the build history (1921 rag outfit -> 1939 L-4 on 20-ft pole tower -> 1964 R-6 flattop on 30-ft timber tower) and on staffing into the 1970s. Flagged a likely height_m error in the tower record (20 ft vs. the current 30-ft tower). Minor elevation discrepancy not flagged: NHLR gives 6,029 ft (1,838 m, matches record); firelookout.com gives 6,092 ft -- not material enough for a correction. Did not need to use the web-search budget; both cached pages were sufficient. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed an uncited 'Clark Fork River country' detail from the opening sentence (not in either source) and rewrote two sentences that too closely copied source wording ('rag outfit' tent description; 'without permanent living quarters' line). Spot-checked the NHLR registry-number/date quote and both firelookout.com quotes (location and named personnel) directly against fetch_text.py output; all three matched the source exactly.

Construction, design and CCC attribution rest on the NRHP nomination (stated as belief). The brief lists NRHP 100002297 as a register; the nomination file calls the lookout eligible for listing. I did not confirm a listing date or final status, so the story says eligible. The last staffing year is not exact (firelookout.com says into the 1980s; NHLR calls it inactive in 1984). The rental is current per the Forest Service page (undated). Brief record fields (1939 build, L-4 design, 2003 registration) are supported, so no corrections proposed.

Unresolved: a September 1921 Missoulian notice (quoted by Forest Lookouts) calls the point's lookout 'in use for years' and being remodeled, while firelookout.com dates an L-4 cab to 1933. The sources do not say whether these describe the same structure, so the story gives both without choosing. The 1953 destruction date and the 1933 cab rest on a single page. The record's elevation is null; firelookout.com gives 7207 ft, which has no slot in facts. No staffing, access or photo found in the three pages read. The Forest Lookouts page quotes no other staffing or fire events for this site.

Height: the record's 18.3 m (60 ft) matches only the Missoulian's August 1922 description; firelookout.com gives a 38-ft pole tower (1914) and a 30-ft pole with 8x8 cab (1920), so the height of the structure that stood at the 1955 end is not known. The 1924 observatory item and firelookout.com's 1928 D-6 cabin date conflict; both are given. Staffing 'seasonal' is from 1922 only. The photo entry uses the Montana History Portal record page as its URL because the direct image URL was not captured; fetch the image file from that record before publishing it. The record's elevation is null; firelookout.com gives 7088 ft. The Forest Lookouts page quotes more Missoulian items (1922-1934) than the story uses. No access information found.

Build year disputed. The June 1930 newspaper item (cite 2) says the cabin and tower were completed; firelookout.com (cite 1) dates the tower to 1931 and the cabin to 1930. The built event uses 1930 from the newspaper; change it to 1931 if an editor prefers the page. Location conflict is still open. The record point (48.04148, -115.78897) matches the FFLA list; the other coordinates in the brief (west_us_lookouts, 48.0313, -115.7261) come from a source not read here, and no source read gives coordinates for the lookout itself. height_m 15.2 treats the 50 ft as tower height; firelookout.com does not say whether that is tower or cab height. Staffing names come from newspaper items as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers themselves were not checked. The 1950 abandonment rests on firelookout.com alone. Nothing read covers fires, access or present-day condition. No photos added.

Thinnest record of the three. The only history is firelookout.com's '1930s: history unknown', so no events are listed because no year is given. The Forest Lookouts page gives only the county, forest and survey location. The FFLA coordinates match the record's point. Nothing read gives the builder, design, staffing, fires or present-day condition. Two web searches turned up only the same pages and unrelated Seeley Lake material. The Seeley Lake Pathfinder article on lookouts that I checked does not mention this site. An editor could check Flathead National Forest records before publishing. No photos added.

Elevation differs notably between NHLR (6,887 ft / 2,099 m, matching the brief's elevation_m field) and Recreation.gov (7,587 ft) -- flagged in the story rather than silently picking one, since neither page explains the gap and it's larger than a rounding difference. Build-year conflict between firelookout.com (1934/1954) and NHLR+Recreation.gov (1932/1962) also flagged; went with the two-source majority for the main narrative. No staffing-end date is corroborated outside firelookout.com, so that claim is attributed to it alone. No NRHP nomination PDF or newspaper source found in two web searches; confidence is medium given the unresolved elevation and date conflicts.

Thin record. Both firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page say the land is private cooperator land, Toole County, 1930s cabin, abandoned. The FFLA list gives type Ground and status Gone, and its coordinates match the record's point. No year is given beyond the decade, so no events are listed. The record's agency field reads Private; it is an ownership label, so facts.agency says Private cooperator. A search result for Gold Butte, about 32 miles northeast of Shelby in the Sweet Grass Hills, is a different site and was not used. Nothing read gives present-day condition or public access. No photos added.

Build date is disputed: 1930s (firelookout.com) against 1940 (memoir and 1940 tent-lookout reports); the story says so and the brief's 1930 is proposed for correction. Agency is disputed (AFPA vs Deer Lodge NF). Ruins status is confirmed by three sources. No source read describes the remains in detail or says whether the site is open to the public. Road guide starts at Dry Creek Road while the memoir names Mill Creek Road. The NGS name is Grassy Hill Lookout Tower. Two WebSearch calls were used.

Two independent history pages agree on c.1936 and 1975, though both draw on the same local researcher (Kresek) for those dates. The 10 ft figure is unexplained (cab or tower height?), so no height_m. No source found describes the remains or public access today; two WebSearch calls turned up nothing about the site now. No staffing names in any source read.

Build year 1936 and destruction year 1966 come from firelookout.com alone; Rex's page says only Removed. Staffing is from 1956-1959 newspaper items quoted on Rex's page plus one firelookout.com personnel line. No source read describes what remains on the mountain or public access. The 50 ft height is the record's tower height as stated, converted to metres. Two WebSearch calls used; neither found a current description of the site.

Three short sources and one 1941 newspaper item; no fire history and no photos found. The 1955 date appears only on firelookout.com. Two searches found nothing else. Do not confuse with the Grouse Mountain lookouts in Idaho (Kaniksu NF) or California (Six Rivers NF) that appear on sibling weebly sites. The brief lists the agency as Cabinet National Forest; firelookout.com says Kootenai, so the editor may want the current name in the record.

Thin record: two short pages and the state index agree on forest, date, abandonment and gone status. Two searches found no staffing, fire or photo sources, so the story leaves those out. The brief record is consistent with these sources.

Coordinate conflict left open: the state index gives 47.67105, -115.59675 (matches the brief), while west_us_lookouts gives 47.66521, -115.57655 and cites the weebly page. The story gives no coordinates. The 'WNW of Thompson Falls' bearing was not checked against a map; the editor should choose the point. Two searches found no other source. Height 6.1 m is the 20-foot pole height converted.

Brief height_m 6.1 has no support in any page read; it equals 20 feet, the height of the Harvey Point tower, so it may be a copy error. Left out of facts; please check before keeping it. Elevation: firelookout.com gives 8,091 ft; Hiking Project's trail high point is 8,079 ft (a trail value, not the summit). Dates disagree across sources (1924 / 1928 / 1932 / 1933). Hiking Project is user-maintained; its trail entry is the only current-access evidence. No photos found in the pages read.

Thin record: one dedicated page, the Granite County list, and the statewide index. Two searches found no staffing, fire, or site-description sources. Brief coordinates (46.61505, -113.39605) were not checked against the township data beyond the Weebly entry. The moved cab's current status is unknown. Staffing omitted for lack of any source. No photos found.

Name: the newspapers and the Weebly page spell it Haskell; firelookout.com uses Haskill. The record keeps Haskill; consider Haskell if the editor agrees. Haskell Pass (Wikipedia, 48.163 N, 114.747 W) is about 19 km from the record's coordinates and was not used; the Courier 'Haskell Pass lookout' may or may not be this site. No height in any source; the brief has none. No photos found. Site today: no source found in two searches.

Dates conflict: Rex gives 1916, 1937 and 1955, while the July 1924 newspapers quoted on Forest Lookouts report a fire that destroyed the station. A newspaper archive search for 1924 and 1955 could settle it. Rex's page also gives an elevation of 4793 ft; the record has no field for it. No source found on staffing, access or what remains.

Thin record: two lookout pages and the FFLA list. The only build date is the 1930s, with no removal date and no staffing. The agency conflict is unresolved; the record says Deerlodge. The FFLA list gives the type as Ground. Nothing found on what remains or on access.

Record height_m 4.3 (14 ft) matches the 14-foot cabin in the 1936 report and the 14 x 14-foot cab in the county write-up. Those are cab sizes, not a tower height, so the field may need review. Record kind 'ground' matches the FFLA list, but the county write-up calls it a tower and the photo page calls the remains a footing. Rex's page says 19 miles northeast of Butte; the trail listing says 12 miles north. Elevations vary: 8,000 ft in the 1936 report, 8,819 to 8,821 ft in later pages. Five sources agree on the 1936 and 1977 dates.

Access key omitted: no source describes access to this spot. Wikipedia describes the range's visitor center and scenic roads, not this site. No staffing, fire or removal-date sources found. The Wild Horse page on the same range carries the same 1934 quote (search snippet), so the Forest Lookouts page's link of that quote to this site is weak. Two web searches used.

Construction history is well documented (NRHP nomination and NPS planning file). Current condition and access rest on 2012-era sources; no 2026 source was found. Elevation conflict: NHLR gives 6,810 ft (2,076 m), which matches the brief's 2075.7 m; firelookout.com gives 7244 ft. Not used in the story. The NPS planning file's date is not shown in the fetched text. The Wikipedia Built 1945 infobox matches the nomination. Pages read: 6 (NHLR, Wikipedia, firelookout, NRHP PDF, Whitefish Pilot, NPS planning PDF). Search: 1 query.

Build year is the main conflict: 1869 (firelookout.com), 1874 (Montana Free Press), 1876 (register and Visit Helena listing). The brief's record of 1876 is kept. Restoration cost and start month conflict as noted. The year 2025 for the restoration is inferred: the Free Press story is dated April 7, 2025 and says the work was expected to finish by the end of May, and KTVH does not print a year. The city's restoration project page (helenamt.gov) returned no text. Whether the public may climb the tower is unknown. Pages read: 6 (NHLR, Visit Helena listing, firelookout.com, Montana Free Press, mthistory.org, KTVH). Search: 1 query.

Only one descriptive page (firelookout.com) gives dates and design; the Forest Lookouts page has no site text beyond agency and township. Height not converted: the 10' may be the tower height but the source does not say so. No staffing, fire, elevation or NHLR/FFLOS record found. Access key omitted. Brief coordinates were not checked against the 19-miles-from-Essex description. A Facebook group post in search results mentions an L-4 at another Flathead site; it was not opened and is not used.

Only firelookout.com gives the dates and elevation; the Forest Lookouts page adds only the Lolo National Forest and a township-section reference. The L-4 design comes from a Sanders County article about a different county, used only as general background. No access, staffing or fire information found. Access key omitted. Search found no Hemlock Point-specific article.

Brief access 'permission' is not supported by any source read, so it is omitted. Brief agency (CSKT) is corrected to USFWS on two sources; the CSKT list is still cited for the reservation context. Height conflict (60 vs 65 ft) is resolved in favour of the 65 ft sources. Staffing not found in the sources read. No source describes the site today. The 1968 survey description is quoted via the Montana page, not the NGS datasheet.

No fire at this site appears in the sources read. The brief's kind two_story is not verified: NHLR describes an L-4 cab on a one-story concrete base, and a search snippet quoting a firelookout.org directory (not read) called it a two-story cab. Left unchanged. Consider whether the 1954 event should be replaced rather than built. Staffing and current access are unconfirmed; no Forest Service page was read. One WebSearch was used.

Thin record. firelookout.com gives a 1941 crow's nest and camp, abandonment in the 1940s and 'Still there' with no detail; the FFLA index says Abandoned; the Montana Lookouts entry gives only agency and type. The brief's 'gone' is not supported by any page I read. The Rex's Fire Lookout Page linked from the Montana Lookouts entry was not read because of the page budget; it may hold the history and the current condition. Story is about 120 words.

Two web inventories (firelookout.com and the Montana Lookouts page) agree on a 1935 build, the 1946 cabin fire and removal about 1969. The Montana Lookouts timeline cites Kresek's inventory; I read it only through that page. Height conflict: 60 ft vs about 70 ft in the 1940 survey description; the record keeps 18.3 m. The FFLA list names the site Hog Heaven Lake. No photos added and no official record read. Story is about 150 words.

Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer says Indian Flats Cabin is rentable; its Recreation.gov page says it does not offer reservations there. Status is unsettled. The 2018 disposal notice says the lookout was excess; the recreation.gov listing (undated) says it is manned mid-June through September; the 2024 chapter report says it seems to be the primary lookout threatened. Not read, due to budget: a May 2021 Hogback Lookout Restoration NEPA document and a 2023 FFLA chapter report, both seen only in search snippets. The 2021 document may show whether the 2018 disposal went ahead or was replaced by restoration; it should be checked before publishing a status. Budget note: this tower used 3 WebSearch calls (one over the 2-call budget) and 6 page reads. Record's elevation 2380.2 m matches the NHLR figure. No corrections proposed.

Record says status gone, design L-4, kind ground. The register and Firelookout.com both say the 1931 stone and shake cabin is still there, so status and design were corrected. Kind 'ground' was left as is. The 1953 abandonment conflict is real: the two lookout sites tie it to the gone L-4 cab, and a single 2014 personal blog ties it to the standing cabin. Access and the 6.3-mile route rest on that one blog, so check current trail and trailhead status. The early-1930s L-4 date has no exact year, so it is not an event. The record's note that Holland Ridge shares a register number is not borne out here: the register lists US 1494, MT 72, and Coal Ridge is US 1498. No photos added.

Good agreement across NHLR, Wikipedia (citing the NRHP nomination), and Recreation.gov. No source gives an exact date for when staffing ended besides 'approximately 1946' or exactly when restoration occurred, only that it was 'abandoned for a number of years' before restoration.

Staffing conflicts: the register's October 2012 visit report says staffed sometimes and used in emergencies; the undated Chronicle feature says regularly manned; the smokejumper article (undated, refers to 2012 as past) says staffed in high fire danger. Story reports all three; facts.staffing uses the 2012 register statement. Height: 41 ft (register, firelookout.com) vs 40 ft (Chronicle, Montana Lookouts); height_m 12.5 is 41 ft converted. Elevation: record 2094.6 m matches the register's 6,872 ft; firelookout.com and the Chronicle give 7,077 ft. Record left unchanged. The register's description calls it Horse Mountain Lookout in one sentence, a name slip. Current access and climbability not verified on site. No photos added.

Only firelookout.com gives the history (camp 1914, cabin and platform 1915, cab 1921, pole L-4 tower 1941, destroyed 1975). The Montana Lookouts entry gives only the agency and a township-range; the FFLA index says Tower Gone. Height 15.2 m is converted from the 50-ft pole tower of 1941; no height is given for the 1915 platform. No cause for the 1975 loss appears in any page I read. No photos added. Story is about 130 words.

Dates and agency rest on one listing (firelookout.com). The West Valley Naturalists article lists a Hubbart Lookout among the Northern Montana Fire Association's three lookouts but gives no date, so it is not known to be the same structure as the 1956 cabin. The Forest Lookouts (montanalookouts.weebly.com) page gives legal location 25N-24W-9 and spells the agency 'Montana DRNC'; it was read but not cited. No source describes present condition or access. No photos with a clear licence were found.

The brief's 'built: 1924' field is likely referring to the original pole-platform predecessor, not the structure now standing (built 1933); flagged as a correction. The current staffing claim comes only from firelookout.com, a hobbyist site with no visible date on that claim, so it is not strongly corroborated -- an NPS source confirming present-day staffing would strengthen this. Did not attempt to retrieve the NRHP nomination PDF itself (npgallery asset page returned only a metadata summary, not the full nomination text) or the NHLR newspaper-article PDF due to the per-tower read budget. Editorial pass 2026-10-04 fixed two footnote misattributions in the story: the 1924 pole-platform/log-cabin sentence was cited to Wikipedia ([^2]) but that detail is only in firelookout.com ([^3]); the 'chain of staffed fire lookouts' sentence was cited to NHLR ([^1]) but the quote is on Wikipedia ([^2]). The NRHP+NHLR registration sentence was missing a [^2] cite for the NRHP facts.

Brief height 3.7 m matches no source; corrected to 60 ft. Build date (1913 vs 1915) and tower end date (1974 vs 1976) conflict between firelookout.com and the Montana page. The summit-remains and trail details come from a climbers' guide (SummitPost), not an agency record, so no agency source was found for the site today. Access level 'public' rests on that guide alone.

The 1978 tower is described on the Whitefish Mountain page as moved from Ingalls. The 2022 yard tower is a probable match only: the article is unnamed and says 40 feet. SummitPost has typos ('there is anything hardly left'); quotes are verbatim. No staffing records for Ingalls Mountain were found. No photos with a clear licence were found.

Height correction proposed: the brief's 15.2 m matches the May 1930 plan, not the built tower. A photo may exist: Montana History Portal item 20368, 'Iris fire lookout, Bonita District' (University of Montana Mansfield Library, USFS Region One collection), rights statement 'NO COPYRIGHT - UNITED STATES', dated 1930 on the page, showing the lookout before the new one was built. The image URL was not confirmed, so no photo entry was added. The survey datasheet's route description is dated 1957 and may be out of date.

Elevation: the record's 459.6 m matches CSKT's 1508 ft; firelookout.com gives 5500 ft. Not resolved, so no elevation field was added. Height: the record's 15.2 m matches the 1939 50-foot plan; firelookout.com says 80 ft. height_m omitted because the sources conflict. The record's access 'permission' has no source among the pages read; see corrections. The 1935 and 1939 start dates are both sourced and the story reports both. The 1960 USGS survey station description is on the montanalookouts page, which is the only source for the Elmo location and the east-west ridge. Edits 2026-10-10: 'after seven years' corrected to 'who had spent seven years in the towers' (the 1979 item says she had been working in the towers for seven years as of July 1979); the 1960 USGS description, the 1979 Courier item and the May 3, 1939 date were added to the evidence; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's 'Irvine Lake' name is now stated; the 14-vs-15-mile distance conflict is recorded.

Brief build year 1964 (FFLOS) conflicts with three sources saying 1965; the story gives 1965 and notes the register figure. The removal reason is thin: the only read source is a picture-tour page that says safety reasons; a Montana Standard article returned HTTP 429 and a search snippet mentions technology overtaking the site, so verify the reason before publishing. Remains (foundation posts, 1986 benchmark) come from peakbagging.com, undated. Access: no source gives a road or trail route or a public-access status, so none is stated; the picture-tour page only advises a hike. Page reads and searches are used up. Photos: firelookout.com credits Dale Osborne and peakbagging.com has photos, but no image URLs were captured, so none added. Fact-check note: the same picture-tour page also says many Montana lookouts are being razed to reduce liability costs and that this one was no exception; the story gives only the safety reason, so check that reason before publishing.

Two short sources only; no staffing, fire or height record found. WebSearch returned only Wyoming's Jackson Lake Ranger Station (NRHP) and an unrelated Beaverhead NF catalog entry, so neither is used. The montanalookouts page lists the site under a Beaverhead NF section (3S-13W-18) while the NHLR says private property; the station may have been on Forest land historically, but this is unverified. Record agency 'Private Property' is the NHLR administered-by field, not an agency, so facts.agency is omitted; the editor may want the field changed. firelookout.org's Montana list tags it 'Rooftop Abandoned'.

Core dates come from FireLookout.com, with newspaper notes and a Forest Service history for staffing and the 1923 photo. The FireLookout.com page title and search snippet call this a 'Fire Lookout Cabin' offering accommodations, but the page text I read (R.I.P. 1916-1934, no rental mention) does not say that; check for a rental before setting any rental or access field. The 1923 photo is a Forest Service figure with no direct image URL, so no photo entry was added.

Only the register and firelookout.com describe this site. One search returned a CSKT page for a different Jocko lookout 12 miles east of Arlee in Lake County (elevation 7769 ft, standing); not used, and not the same tower. No staffing or fire records found. The record's name Jocko #2 follows the register; firelookout.org and firelookout.com call it Jocko #1, which is already in other_names. The register's photo (Erik Youngquist, footing) is already on the record, so no new photo entry. Access is unknown: firelookout.com places the site on the Flathead Indian Reservation, which may need permission, but no source says so directly.

Two registrations share the name Jocko #2. This record (NHLR US 1543) is the standing 1969 CSKT R-6 timber tower. FFLOS US 2089 is a different 1934 Forest Service steel tower, removed, with footings only; keep them apart. Access level 'permission' in the record is not supported by any page read; it is left out of facts and should be treated as unverified. County (Missoula vs Lake) and elevation (7,636 vs 7,769 ft) conflict across sources. Staffing comes from an undated CSKT page. Leads not read: nwmt-ffla.org (Northwest Montana Lookout Association, lists historic, staffed and rental lookouts) and the CSKT preservation page. Page-read budget was used up, so no physical-state check was done.

Nearly all Johnson Peak history comes from one page (FireLookout.com). The 1966 Forest Service list names only 'Johnson', so that staffing entry is likely but not confirmed to be this peak. Idaho's Johnson Peak Lookout (CDA region, idahofirelookouts.com) is a different lookout and was not used. The Forest Lookouts page for Johnson Peak has only a header with agency and township, so it was cited for the agency alone.

Staffing: the register says semi-regularly staffed since 2001; firelookout.com says only that it was staffed in 2001. Access and rental not verified. Elevation: register 8,214 ft (2,504 m), firelookout.com 8284 ft; record 2503.6 m follows the register. The Powell County blog gives its newspaper quote as September 17, 1957 and then cites the same paper as September 17, 1954; the story says so. The Flathead NF Facebook lookout profile could not be read (page returned only its title), so it is not cited. A Forest Service Wikimedia Commons photo is geotagged about 60 m from the lookout, but the page does not say what the image shows, so no photo was added. Wikipedia says the 1957 lookout replaced a cabin of 1937, consistent with the register; it was used as a lead only.

The loss date is unresolved: a 1968 destruction is not confirmed by the June 1968 report. A Spokesman-Review archive search for later 1968 coverage could settle it. The 1919 entry in the Forest Service list gives 2,500 with no unit, so the story gives the bare figure. Two YouTube videos titled as a 1968 Montana lookout that vanished came up in search; they are unsourced and were not used, but they may be worth checking against this record.

The brief says the NHLR record shares a register number with another entry (US 1114, MT 62). Check for a duplicate record. Elevation conflicts (3,783 ft in NHLR vs 4943 ft on firelookout.com), and the record keeps the NHLR figure. Height correction: 15.2 m is 50 ft, the 1934 tower's height; the present 53-ft tower is about 16.2 m. The firelookout.com page is undated and says the tower is available for emergencies; the 2026 assessment says current access is closed for grizzly habitat. Do not encourage visiting. The 2026 condition assessment PDF linked from the NWMT page was not opened.

Status is undated: the decommissioning and window removal appear in two undated pages; only the 2017 collapse risk has a year. The trail sources disagree: Visit Montana gives Road 761 and 2.5 miles, easy; The Outbound gives Road 763 and about 3 miles, moderate. No staffing or fire record was found. The Forest Lookouts Montana page for Kenelty carries a 1956 newspaper item placing a man on the mountain without describing a job, and an item about a lookout on another mountain; neither is used. The record's 3.0 m height is close to the 10-foot (about 3.05 m) tower given by the source. A Forest Service Museum catalog record was mentioned in search but not read.

Brief checked: status gone, kind tower and Lolo National Forest agree with the sources; no corrections. The 1934 build date rests on firelookout.com and is consistent with the Montana History Portal's 1934 start. The fate is disputed (destroyed in 1980 vs removed, undated) and the story says so. No staffing, fire, access or site-condition source was found. Not tried: Lolo NF records, Montana SHPO files, a photo search for the summit.

Brief checked: kind ground (an L-4 cab), status gone and Flathead NF agree with the sources; no corrections. Only firelookout.com dates the cabin (1930) and its 1956 presence; no source gives a removal date. Montanalookouts and the FFLA list say removed or ground gone with no date. The Flathead Beacon piece is about the forest generally and does not name Kid Mountain, so the story says so. A 2025 FFLA social-media post (seen only as a search snippet, not read) shows the cabin in a flyby photo and spells the name 'Kid (Kidd?)'; the Facebook page did not return text, so it is not cited. firelookout.com credits a Fire Lookout Museum photo with no URL, so no photo entry was added. Worth checking: Flathead NF archives, and the FFLA post for its photo credit and date.

Brief checked: status gone, kind ground (log cupola cabin) and Helena NF agree with the Montanalookouts page; firelookout.com also names Lolo NF, recorded as a resolved conflict. No corrections. The 1960 National Geodetic Survey station description is quoted on the Montanalookouts page; no NGS datasheet URL was fetched, so it is cited to that page. No builder, staffing or fire record was found. Worth checking: the NGS datasheet for PID ST0528 for a newer description, and Helena NF records.

Thin sources. The 1937 build year comes from one Forest Lookouts page; the Fire Lookout Tower site says construction is unknown and presumes the purpose was wildlife observation, which the story reports only as that site's presumption. Public climbing and current condition are unconfirmed; no staffing, fire or closure record was found. Refuge visitor-center hours were not captured from the visit page, and a third-party listing's phone number was not used. The record's 30.5 m height matches the 100-foot figure, and 2,042 m matches the 6,700-foot elevation.

Build date (1934) and fire (2000) agree across sources; the 1930 cabin date comes only from firelookout.com. The Missoulian article body is not readable in our cache, so only its headline and subhead are quoted; its date and fire details are not verified beyond those. The 1939 Ravalli Republican item is cited only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. No access or present-day site information was found, so the record's access 'unknown' stands. Photos credited to Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber on firelookout.com were not added because no licence is stated. The record's status, kind, design, agency and coordinates match the sources; no corrections proposed.

Thin record: three short listings, with no staffing, no fire history and no present-day description. firelookout.com lists an L-4 cab for 1930, yet the association list classes the site as ground; the sources do not say whether the 1930 cab stood on a tower. A text search of the Flathead National Forest history (Trails of the Past) found no mention of Lena Peak. Record matches the sources on status, agency, county and coordinates; no corrections proposed.

Two open problems. (1) Forest and location: firelookout.com, the association list and the record put the butte in Stillwater County on the Custer NF. The Forest Lookouts page carries a 1940 NGS station description of a Limestone lookout in the Flathead NF near Spotted Bear and Bear River, which may be a different structure. Not resolved; the story follows the Stillwater sources. (2) Status: the record says gone, but the association list says Abandoned; the correction above is for editor review. Kind: the record says platform, and the sources say crow's nest (association type Crowsnest); left unchanged. No staffing, fire history or present-day description was found.

Thin record. firelookout.com (one page) is the only history source: a cabin in the 1930s, half a mile below the summit on the north spur, listed as abandoned, with no year given for abandonment. The Association list gives the county, coordinates and Ground/Gone status, and the Forest Lookouts page gives only the legal location 25N-13W-35. No events are logged because the only date is the decade 1930s, and a year field would invent precision. No staffing, fires, access or current-condition sources were found in two websearch.py queries and about five page reads. The brief's record (gone, ground, Flathead County, coordinates) holds, so no corrections. The story is about 110 words, which is the thin-source length in the guide.

The destruction date (1950) rests on one page, firelookout.com; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list agrees only on 'Gone' and gives no date. The brief's record (tower, gone, Flathead County) holds, so no corrections. Staffing and fires are left out because no source covers them. Kemnow's Forest Lookouts page gives only a legal location (30N-19W-15) and no history. The 2023 Hungry Horse News item is about a proposed fuel break and does not describe the lookout site. Access level is omitted because no source gives it. Search budget: two websearch.py queries and about six page reads for this tower.

The brief's record (ground, 2009 removed, access unknown) holds except access. The USFS trail carries the lookout's name, so access is set to public for the trail; confirm the summit's status on the ground before any visit is suggested. The 1939 camp and 1958 cab come only from firelookout.com. The Arizona chapter report is a chapter newsletter, not a site survey. It does not define 'the area'. Its preceding paragraph describes the removal of Scenery Mountain Lookout (Kootenai NF, MT), which may be the other lookout lost in 2009, but the report does not say so. Edits 2026-10-10: 'managed the land' changed to 'listed under Custer National Forest' because the sources name the forest and do not say who managed the site; the Powder River County and Custer National Forest quotes were added to the evidence, as was the trail-data source line.

Record status 'gone' is proposed as 'relocated': the tower and cab moved to Williams Peak in 1977 and the May 2026 report describes a lookout there. The Little Joe summit itself has no source describing what, if anything, remains, and no source gives visiting or access rules for either site; access is omitted from facts. Staffing 'unstaffed' comes from the Williams Peak page, not from Little Joe; the Little Joe personnel list ends in 1967. Not used in the story: firelookout.com gives Little Joe elevation 5398 ft, while mineralcounty.info (Little Joe Lookout Station) gives 5174 ft. The Scout jamboree is spelled Farragut (NHLR) and Farrugut (firelookout.com). The NHLR registration (March 20, 2016, US 1119, MT 63) belongs to the Williams Peak lookout, so it is left out of Little Joe's events. Search budget: one websearch.py query and six page reads for this tower.

The 1977 build date is well supported and corrects the brief's 1969 build event. Staffing conflicts between NHLR (not regularly staffed) and the 2017 chapter report (DNRC part time); the as-of date is 2017. Current access is unconfirmed; no visiting or rental program found. height_m 6.1 converts the reported 20 feet of cab height, which is an inference from two sources. The 2016 Whitefish article calls Little Napa an L-4 design lookout in passing; design was not recorded because no source states it directly. One WebSearch was used. Five page reads.

Build and destruction years rest on one detailed listing (firelookout.com); the Forest Fire Lookout Association index confirms only that the tower is gone. Two searches and the Flathead history turned up no staffing, fire or photo record for this site. The site is in designated wilderness, so access is marked public as national forest land, but no source states visiting rules or describes what remains. The brief's record (Flathead NF, tower, gone, access unknown) matches the sources; no corrections proposed.

Platform (1922), L-4 tower (about 1934) and destruction (1963) agree between firelookout.com and the Montana History Portal library note. The 1928 staffing rests on two newspaper items that name no staff beyond the one notice; later staffing is not in the sources. The 1957 photo (Montana History Portal node 114482, UM Mansfield Library, photo FS99.05579, public domain per the record) is a good find, but the image URL was not captured, so no photos entry is included; add one if the image address is confirmed. Its catalogue title says Lolo Peak lookout. The FFLA Instagram post repeats the Lolo Springs identification but was not cited. Nothing in the sources describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to the public.

Thin record. Built (1917) and abandoned (by 1930) dates come from one detailed listing (firelookout.com); the FFLA index only confirms it is gone. The roughly 1,100-foot comparison in the story is our arithmetic from the lookout's listed 6,360 feet and the Wikipedia pass elevation of 5,233 feet. The firelookout.com record shows R.I.P. 1917-? so the end date is unknown. Two searches and a Montana History Portal check found no staffing, fire, structure or photo record for this site. Nothing in the sources describes what remains or whether the public may visit.

All dates, the 1998 collapse and the 1956-58 personnel come from one firelookout.com page. The oral history gives no years. The original site and the first build date are unknown in every source read. The record's access level 'permission' is not confirmed: the tribal page and NHLR say nothing about visitors, and a Facebook group post that mentions a tribal permit could not be opened, so it is not cited. Access is set to unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story had said both sources describe summer staffing, which the tribal page does not; the 1970 build is recorded as about 1970 to match both sources; and the earlier permission-only access note was dropped from the story as unsupported. Height 16.2 m is the 53-foot figure converted, which matches the record.

The original lookout's date is not settled (1935, 1936 or 1937 across sources), so the story gives the range. The NRHP nomination is the strongest source for the current structure and the 2008 work. An Independent Press article (which a search snippet says gives 1939) returned HTTP 429 twice and was not used. The 1937 and 1966 facts come from newspaper quotes reproduced on a hobbyist site, not the original papers. The access level is unknown: the picnic ground and road are public, but no source says whether the cab itself is open to visitors. Height correction (6.1 m to 9.1 m) is the main fix to the record. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the forest name is now sourced to the NRHP form; the 1937 last spring wording and the 1966 Ashland and Fort Howes blazes have exact evidence quotes; the story's causal link between the 1966 blazes and the evacuation was removed; and the sentence saying the cab had stood in its 1955 form since the 2008 repairs was dropped as unsupported.

The NPS nomination PDF is OCR text, and the 'last of eleven' sentence is garbled, so the quote is a clean fragment. Staffing 'unstaffed' since 1972 is inferred from 'not used for fire detection much after 1972'. Current public access is unconfirmed. The visit detail rests on one SummitPost trip report. No notable fires found in sources read. No new photos: the NHLR photos are all rights reserved. The NPS PDF also has a passage saying the lookout is eligible 'under the Multiple Resource Submission', which sits uneasily with the letter's 'not included with the submission'. The build history is disputed. The 1933 items and the 1937 article are quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; I did not check them against the original newspapers. The 1931 and 1968 cabs are both real per the register and firelookout.com, so the record's build-year conflict is two cabs, not an error. No new photos. 2026-10-08 check: the 9 July 1931, 15 August 1940 and 16 August 1984 dates and the forest name were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page and added to the evidence record; the story text is unchanged.

Core build and registry facts are solid (NHLR). Very thin. The Register has no description beyond 'No information known at this time.' and gives only the 1930s as the build period, so no build year is recorded. Standing status rests on the FFLA Montana list and NHLR's description; the only account of the site today is one July 2026 trip report, which does not say whether the tower was climbed or what condition it is in. Built date conflicts: firelookout.com says 1928, while 1921 and 1923 newspaper items (as transcribed on Rex's page, not checked against the originals) mention a lookout earlier. Thin record: four sources, and the Firelookout.com page has one line of detail. The 1921 forest lookout job and the 1923 platform date may describe different structures; the story says so. Distance: firelookout.com gives about 11 miles north of Lincoln; the 1956 survey datasheet, quoted on the weebly page, gives about 12 miles north-northwest. The story attributes each figure. The repo already has us-mt-red-mountain-2.json for it. The 1925 item's Lander's Fork location cannot be matched to either site from the text alone; check a map before publishing. Dates disagree: firelookout.com gives 1929; the 1925 item says construction was about to begin and a lookout had been kept for two years; a 1923 photo caption calls it a proposed lookout. Elevation is 9,411 ft on firelookout.com and 9,390 ft in the 1925 item. The only source on the summit today is the 1956 survey description, quoted on the weebly page; the NGS datasheet itself was not fetched. Staffing is known only for 1936, and there are no fire records.

Replacement completion: 1955 (Montana Lookouts page) against 1957 (firelookout.com). Three one-line listings only. No build date, builder, staffing or removal date found. Two web searches returned nothing specific to this lookout. The 1972 entry is ambiguous. Dates conflict (1931 build vs 1932 opening; 1962 burning vs 1963 destruction) and both are reported. The 1931 erection is quoted secondhand through Forest Lookouts from an annual forestry report. Early history is disputed. No web search used for this tower.

Two short site pages and one list; no staffing, fire record or photo beyond the FFLOS image already on the record. One search found nothing about this site. Thin record. NHLR is the only substantive source; firelookout.com and the Montana Forest Lookouts page repeat its agency and build year, and the firelookout.com page confirms the 29-mile location. Thin record: three short pages, two of them one-line entries. The only date is 'the 1940s', so no built event was added, following the convention for decade-only dates. Three short listings only: firelookout.com (observation tower, decade-only dates, '1 mile west of Victor', elevation), Forest Lookouts (private co-operator, 8N-21W-36), and the firelookout.org list (coordinates, Tower Gone). Two history sites and one listing; no NHLR or FFLOS registration. The newspaper items are read only as quoted on the montanalookouts page, not from the original papers. The 1936 L-4 date from firelookout.com conflicts with the 1921 and 1927 accounts quoted on montanalookouts; neither source explains it, and a replacement tower is not documented in what was read. Brief's 1930 build, L-4 design, ground kind and NHLR registration (September 28, 2010) are supported. No source read gives public access rules or climbability, so no access or visit keys are set. Brief lists design as L-4 and status 'standing', consistent with sources, but the 1920/1934/1984 structure history (tree platform -> pole/L-4 -> concrete) is richer than the brief's single '1920 built' event; consider adding the 1934 and 1984 events to the record. No NHLR/NRHP source was checked for this tower in this pass; firelookout.org listing only confirmed location/name match.

Only two enthusiast pages and one association list. Both give 1961 for the end, but the build date is decade-only. No staffing, fire or present-day site sources were found, and access is unknown. Do not confuse this with the Threemile Wildlife Management Area near Stevensville, which appears in Forest Service burn news and is a different place.

The two firelookout.com pages for this tower disagree on the end date (1973 abandoned versus 1975 destroyed) and on the wooden or pole design. Built 1937 by the Thunderbolt CCC camp with 1938 staffing, but sources give no fire record and nothing on the site today. Elevation conflicts across sources (8,597 vs 8,000, 8,400 and 9,400 ft). Only two short lookout pages and the FFLA list say anything about this site. firelookout.com names the lookout Tillson Peak but puts the crow's nest on Packrat Mtn; the Forest Lookouts index lists both peaks under Powell County. The record's coordinates are for Tillson Peak, so the location is unverified. No staffing, fire or present-day source found; two web searches returned nothing on this lookout.

The 2014 burn rests on one source, FireLookout.com. Only the firelookout.com entry, a 1956 NGS station description reproduced on Forest Lookouts, and the FFLA list say anything about this site. Two web searches found no other history for a Montana Tower Mountain lookout; results were for Oregon and Washington sites. No staffing or fire information found.

Agency, height, registration and standing status agree across sources. Not verified: whether the cabin still exists and the tower's current condition.

Two web searches on Tuchuck found no other lookout history.

Brief record checks out: status gone, kind tower (for the 1934 structure), agency Kootenai NF, and coordinates match the association list. Brief record checks out: status gone, kind ground, agency Kootenai NF. No source describes the peak today or access, so the access key is omitted. The photo has no date on the page. One WebSearch and about four page reads used.

Brief record checks out on status (gone) and kind (ground). Core facts agree across sources: Granite County location, DNRC Forestry Division administration since 1973, NHLR registration March 31, 2003, standing status. Flagged the 1930s vs 1966 build-year discrepancy between recreation.gov and NHLR/firelookout.com in both the story and resolved_conflicts; did not find a source that explicitly reconciles it.

Three sources only: the firelookout.com page (1939 L-4 cab), the Forest Lookouts page (1940 survey description, Flathead NF, legal location 22N-16W-6) and the Montana list (Ground, Gone). Key open question: Recreation.gov's listing for Mt. Wam now says 'No longer a rental' with no date or reason.
