Only the register entry, the Ohio list and an encyclopedia lead were usable. Two searches found no build date, staffing, fire history or present-site description. A Meigs County Historical Society photo post from July 21, 2019 (facebook.com/meigshistory/posts/2943446459213231/) may hold height detail and a dismantling question; the page is login-walled and was not readable, so nothing from it is used or cited. Staffing and the 60-foot height rest on an October 27, 1934 Chillicothe Gazette item as transcribed on the Eastern U.S. Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not checked. The register gives only location, elevation, registration date and gone status. Two searches found no build date, height, staffing, fire history or present-site description. Thin record: after two searches no source gave a build date, staff, fires or current condition. The ODNR agency line comes from an undated Forest Lookouts listing. The Ohio marker is general context and does not name this site. Check Athens County or ODNR records before expanding.

Thinnest of the three. Story body is about 127 words, just above the floor, and the editor may want to hold it until a better source turns up.

Build year 1929 is inferred: the February 20, 1930 Plymouth Daily Times item quoted by the Forest Lookouts site says 'erected last October'. The 1930 report names the suspect 'Mr. Bradford' and says the fire was put out by Fire Warden F.J. Etterling and Robert Bradbury; the story names none of them. The FFLOS 'Standing' row has no asterisk, which the list's own note links to towers with the cab gone; this is an inference from the list's convention, not a stated condition. Not verified: any post-2014 restoration or closure.

Only the register gives tower details, and it gives no exact build year, so no built event is recorded. Record status 'standing' is not confirmed: the register's NHLR page we read has no status field and no source says the tower stands today. Height 80 ft converted to 24.4 m. The OFS history gives context on 1930s CCC fire towers but does not name Bear Mountain. The Forest Lookouts page has only a county line. Access and condition left out. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 3 page reads (NHLR, Forest Lookouts, OFS history) plus one FFLA Oklahoma list that returned no Bear Mountain row.

The tower's location after the city's purchase is unconfirmed. The Sandite Pride item does not name the tower but its details match Beaver's (100 feet, from Cookson, on the register); a human should check this with Sand Springs Parks or the Oklahoma Forestry Services. The News On 6 story is dated October 8, 2019 on the cached page. The register does not place the stump near the summit, so the story omits that detail. The Sandite Pride item's date is not printed; its URL suggests March 2020. Because the date and move are uncertain, no event was recorded for either. The record's status 'standing' may be out of date. The 1960 staffing comes from one newspaper quote. Height 30.5 m is the NHLR's 100 feet. The SummitPost access note is undated.

Two independent, consistent sources cover the build/rebuild history well (1926 original, 1937 rebuild, 1974 storm loss and Aermotor replacement with the footings-error deck), but neither says anything about staffing history, specific fires spotted, or current public access — those fields stay unknown. Flagged a height correction: the record's 30.5 m (100 ft) reflects the tower's planned height, not the 75 ft (22.9 m) it was actually built to after the footings error; worth a human call on which figure the map should show. Did not refetch nhlr.org or firetower.org per the guide; no additional web search was needed given the two cached sources agreed.

Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the draft had the tower 'watching over the surrounding Ouachita National Forest' and being in active service 'as of' its 1997 register listing, both attributed to NHLR. Neither is in the NHLR text — the page only says the tower 'is still in active service' as of its last update (Nov 2016), with no statement about what it watches over or forest-boundary claims. Softened both in the story and removed the unsupported forest-duty claim. Also split the 1974 storm-destruction citation to NHLR only, since the Forestry Service page never mentions a storm. Rewrote the Aermotor-rebuild paragraph, which had tracked the NHLR sentence structure too closely (same clause order and several repeated phrases like 'measuring error at the footings').

No access level or visit rules were found, so access is left out of facts. The NHLR's 'remains in service' has no date and is the only current-status source. The 2018 press release is the latest visit evidence. LASR (403) and a Facebook post (login wall) could not be read. The height correction (16.8 m to 30.5 m) is the main change to the record; check the 100-ft figure against the tower if measured data exists. Staffing today was not found.

Corrections are proposed, not applied: built year, longitude (the registry's W 091.55 is outside Oklahoma; the agency's DMS value is inside McCurtain County), elevation (agency ground elevation 520 ft versus the record's 167 ft figure), and status (standing not confirmed). The agency data sheet's coordinates carry a '(2017)' label, so they may predate recent changes. The Instagram post is dated March 13, 2025 but shows a circa 1985 photo, so it is unclear whether the 'Status: Closed' line is current. The observer is named in the source; the story leaves the name out. The registry spells the maker 'Aermotor' and the agency sheet 'Aeromotor'; we use 'Aermotor' only in quotes. No new photo was added: the one found has no clear license.

No source describes what remains on the site today. The register has a 2002 photo captioned 'Site on June 3, 2002' whose content is not described. Access is omitted because no source gives it. The brief's 2010 FFLOS registration date (August 16, 2010) does not appear in the register text read, so it is not repeated. The 1933 completion date comes from a history page and firelookout.com gives 1932, so the editor may want to choose one for the infobox.

The 1938 vs 1939 date for the L-4 tower is unresolved: Forest Lookouts relies on an undated report, firelookout.com says 1939. A Library of Congress record for the Abbott Butte Fire Lookout Complex (loc.gov/item/or0644/) looked likely to settle the date and the D-6 design, but the fetch returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. The tower fate and burning are reported by two sources and are high confidence. The 2022 date is the report date; the collapse itself happened over winter 2021-22, exact time unclear. The 2022 event was changed from destroyed to other because no cause is given. No photos added: the firelookout.com photos are credited to other collections and no image URLs or license were read. Access rests on the wilderness designation and a 2023 hike report; no current site description was found. Fact-check 2026-10-10: wording of the 1927 packing, 1940 Poole visit (Mr. and Mrs.), winter collapse timing and the current-state claims was corrected to match the sources.

Brief's 'Aermotor' design is supported by Forest Lookouts and the Lake County blog; the register does not name a make. Main unresolved conflicts: build year (1932 vs 1934) and height (60 vs 72 ft). Removed vs destroyed in 1976 is also reported as a conflict. The brief's access 'unknown' is kept out of facts because no source states access. The NGS survey mark is recorded close to the lookout's living quarters; whether it still exists is not verified. One search used.
Brief's 1964 built date and R-6 design matched all three sources exactly; no corrections needed.

Built-year conflict (1942 vs 1943) unresolved; story notes both. The story itself states no year for the NRHP listing, so no story edit was needed there. All four footnoted citations and their quoted evidence were spot-checked against the live sources and confirmed verbatim.

Brief record matches the register (US 749, OR 158, registered 17 Nov 2010, elevation 1,510 m). Removal year disputed: removed (register) vs destroyed (firelookout.com). Height of 5.8 m is converted from the 19-ft figure. No current access or condition source found, so no access level is recorded. The register credits a 1940 photo to the Howard Verschoor collection, but no image URL was captured, so no photo is added. Staffing as_of is the removal year, since the tower could not be staffed after it was gone.

Brief height 33.5 m (110 ft) is corrected to 32.6 m (107 ft); the register's 110 ft and 1932 date conflict with most other sources and both are in resolved_conflicts. Brief's Aermotor design is confirmed (LS-40). Brief's access 'permission' has no source support: sources name the reservation as administrator and WillhiteWeb lists drive-up, but none states a permit rule, so no access level is recorded. WillhiteWeb photo captions (tower footings, ground house foundation) have no image URLs captured, so no photo entries are added. Staffing as_of is the 1979 dismantling year.

Brief record checked: built 1933 and FFLOS registration 15 Nov 2019 match the register. Height disputed (38 ft in register and July 1933 field report; 40 ft in April 1933 plan and October 1933 report); the brief's 12.2 m rests on the 40-ft figure, so this record uses 11.6 m. The register credits 1930s and 2010 photos (Howard Verschoor collection) and a 1938 panorama (National Archives Pacific Northwest Region), but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are added.

Brief height_m 23.2 (76 ft) matches only the 1944 history-page tower; the register and firelookout.com say 85 ft (about 25.9 m). The brief's 1940 build date matches the register, not the history page's 1944. The brief's L-4 design code appears only on the 1944 cab, so design is recorded as the register's steel cab. A Recreation.gov listing for a separate Green Ridge Lookout (built in the 1960s) is not tied to this site by any source read, and visitors could confuse them. A mapcarta listing called the site a ruin and a Facebook group post mentioned a 1965 last season; neither was read in full, so neither is used. Access is omitted because no source describes it.

Brief record: design L-4 describes the 1934 cab, not the standing 1960 cab; correction proposed. Staffing is disputed across three sources (NHLR: ODF; firelookout.com undated: Ochoco NF; Aug 2023 Malheur NF notice: BLM). Search results also included a different Aldrich Butte in Washington, near North Bonneville; it was not used. No photos were added: the NHLR and firelookout.com photo credits have no licence or URL in what was read.

Brief coordinates conflict (FFLOS 44.46235, -123.50021 vs West US lookouts 44.46679, -123.50371); not used in the story. Height 3.0 m comes from the 1940 newspaper's 10-foot tower; the register gives no height, so treat it as approximate. The FFLOS registration date in the brief (Sept 22, 2010) did not appear in the fetched text, so there is no fflos_registered event. The 1946 item is a plan ('will occupy and maintain'), not a confirmed occupation. No source describes the site today; the Alsea Historical Society Facebook post was not readable.

The 60 ft vs 40 ft height conflict is unresolved; the story reports both. The Forest Lookouts page is a compilation of Coos Bay Times and Myrtle Point Herald clippings. Its April 1929 item says the Forest Service would erect a lookout that summer; its July 1929 item says the primary station was completed that spring. Neither says whether a tower stood in 1929, so the story no longer says the tower came later. One search returned no current description of the site; no photos captured (the register page shows collection photos from 1933-1956 but no image URLs were captured).

Build year conflicts (1933 newspaper vs 1935 register and firelookout.com); the story gives both. The only account of the site today is the April 2015 visit reported on the Forest Lookouts page; no later description was found. A search snippet cited 5,177 ft (Oregon Field Register); not checked and not used. The register page shows collection photos (1935-1965, 1959, 2015) without image URLs, so no photo entries.

Gone. The 2018 hike report is the only source that describes the site now; it is a single blog visit, so treat the footings detail as 2018 only. Build year conflicts: 1933 (2018 report and the Sept 1933 plan) vs 1934 (Forest Lookouts, firelookout.com); left as a conflict. Abandonment: 1958 (2018 report, firelookout.com) vs mid-1950s (Forest Lookouts). Height: 30 ft (9.1 m, matching the record) per the 2018 report and Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says '10' pole L-5 tower', which we did not use. Not verified: whether the record's coordinates (42.97805, -122.47775) mark the lookout on Anderson Mountain or the Anderson Camp meadow; the FFLA entry uses the Anderson Camp name. Access level 'public' is inferred from the 2018 hike on Forest Service trails, and no closure, permit or closed wording on the full 2018 page; no official site access statement was read. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 5 page reads (within budget). No photos used: the 2018 blog photos have no stated licence, and firelookout.com credits a private collection.

Built year and height disagree across the three sources (1935 or 1933; 24, 16 or 20 feet); the story says so. The 2024 burn of a later 10-foot platform tower appears only on firelookout.com, which calls that tower's history in question; a follow-up search for the fire found nothing, so treat it as unconfirmed. A search surfaced an Idaho Ant Hill lookout (Clearwater NF, destroyed 1946) that is a different site and was excluded. Rex's page quotes the 1941 survey note that the lookout tower was a house on a 16-foot tower; that supports the record's 4.9 m. No correction proposed.

The build year is disputed (1928/1929/1930) and the register's 1963 is unsupported; the story says so. The 1974 move is well documented by a contract quoted on Forest Lookouts. The record's coordinates match the register; another source in the brief's record gives a point about 470 m away, which was not read. Whether the cab is open to visitors inside is not stated in any source read. The 2022 Cheryl Hill visit is the newest source. The register's 1963 may be a data-entry error; a Malheur NF or NHLR contact could confirm.

Built year conflicts: register and firelookout.com say 1937 for a 30-foot tower; Rex's page quotes two September 1933 papers describing a 14x14 house on a 30- or 35-foot tower. A reviewer should confirm the height convention used for the record. No source describes what remains on the summit today, and none gives access, so those keys are omitted. Two web searches found no independent history for this lookout beyond the listing and location. An Umatilla NF Desolation Butte result was off-topic and excluded.

Build year is unresolved: register and FFLOS give 1936, while the Klamath agency entry on the Forest Lookouts (Oregon) page describes a 1935 build. Height and completion date conflict: 67 feet and 1946 (register, firelookout.com) against 83 feet in a January 1948 Ukiah report quoted by Rex's page. The record uses 20.4 m (67 ft), as the register and firelookout.com give; a reviewer should confirm which structure it describes. Two web searches returned a summary saying that concrete pillars remain on the site and that a spur road runs north from Forest Road 53 (about 1.9 miles from pavement, with a roughly 0.8-mile walk, seasonal). I could not read any page that states this: a geocaching listing (GC1YFBX) returned only its title through fetch_text, and the summary was not checkable. For that reason the story says no source describes the site today, and access keys are omitted. Before adding either detail, check with the Umatilla National Forest, Heppner Ranger District.

Brief record checked: status gone, FFLOS registration June 12, 2011 and Crook County/Ochoco NF all confirmed. The brief's access 'unknown' is omitted because no source gives access. The 1981 tDAR record 161708 (Bedortha, 'Commercial Thinning and Cultural Resource Property Management of the Arrow Wood, Double Cabin, Friday, Parrish, West Maury or Big Daddy') may describe the site in the field but its abstract did not load, so it is not cited. Cross-check the 1934 Central Oregonian notices if a newspaper search is possible; they are quoted only on the Oregon Lookouts page.

Height conflict (110 ft FFLOS vs 82 ft firelookout.com) is unresolved; no newspaper or Forest Service record was consulted. The brief's elevation 1159.2 m matches firelookout.com's 3803 ft. The FFLOS page carries a photo captioned 'Aschoff Butte Lookout 1925 - 1935 - courtesy of Howard Verschoor collection', but no image URL was extracted, so it is not in photos. The firelookout.com page is headed 'McCartie Ranch Fire Lookout Tower' above the Aspen Butte entry, and gives 18 miles WNW of Klamath Falls where the 1933 survey note says 18 miles W; the title mismatch suggests a copied header, so it is cited only for the 1910 camp, the 1920s cupola and the 1928 date. Township differs: weebly gives 37S-6E-35, the blog gives Sec 26 T37S R6E; not used in the story. The 1933 Coast and Geodetic Survey directions are omitted as too old to be useful for access. No newspaper archive or Forest Service document was consulted.

The timeline rests mostly on one compiled page (oregonlookouts.weebly.com) that quotes 1930s-1960s Lincoln County fire annual reports and Corvallis newspapers. The register and firelookout.com repeat the 1940 and 1942 details and the removal year, so they are not independent confirmation. Two WebSearch calls and four distinct page reads used. The 'Baker' and 'Babor' spellings in the old records were not used in the story text.

The early history and the replacement cab rest on a 2008 personal inventory blog and a compiled newspaper page; the register and firelookout.com agree on the 1939 abandonment and removal but not on the cab type or the date. firelookout.com's 4,273 ft elevation is contradicted by the register and the 1932 newspaper and is treated as an error. Brief record checked: elevation_m 2763.0 matches the register; kind 'ground' is supported for the 1931 cab but the 1922 cupola cabin's placement is not stated; no corrections proposed. Access left out of facts because no source describes access today; Wikipedia's 'ski lifts' route line is the only current-use source. Used one WebSearch and five distinct page reads.

Built year, design and 1967 removal are agreed across the register, firelookout.com and the Oregon lookouts page. Brief record checked: kind 'ground' and design 'L-4' are supported by the 1934 'ground cabin' note; coordinates and elevation match the register; no corrections. Brief access 'unknown' is now 'public' on the strength of the Forest Service trail page, which lists a trail to the former site with directions and no closure for that trail (the page carries a general Willamette wildfire-closure alert, which is not specific to this trail). The Oregon lookouts page's remark about remains being thrown into a toilet pit was left out as not needed. No staffing record found in any source read, so staffing is omitted. Used one WebSearch and four distinct page reads.

Thin record: one directory entry (firelookout.com) gives the location, elevation and 1930s era; the FFLA list and Forest Lookouts confirm the name, county and status only. No builder, design, height, staffing, fire or demolition details were found in any source read, so none are stated. Name clash: the FFLOS 'Badger Butte Lookout Site' (US 563, Hood River County, 44.87, -121.70, built around 1933) is a different lookout; its panoramas and history must not be attached to this record. The Forest Service archive record (forestservicemuseum.pastperfectonline.com) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Record kind 'unknown' is left as is; no correction proposed. Budget: 2 WebSearch, 3 page reads, 1 failed archive fetch.

Location is an open conflict, not resolved. The register (US 563) gives N 44.872618 W 121.697292, well south of the FFA list point 45.29428 -121.55224 that this record uses. Firelookout.com's 'nine miles southeast of Mt. Hood' fits the FFA point, which suggests the register coordinates are the wrong ones, but I did not check a map or Forest Service data. Settle the pin before publishing a location. The story says the register and the list disagree and does not choose. Not the same lookout as us-or-badger-butte (Grant County, OR). Suggested kind for the editor: tree (the sources describe a fir tree with a crow's nest); the brief still says unknown, and I did not write a correction for it. The 12.2 m height is the tree's height as Forest Lookouts gives it (about 40 ft). No source read gives access, staffing or fire history, so those keys are left out. The register's 2011 photo and the 1933 panoramas are already in the record and were not re-added.

Build year and height conflict across the three sources; the 1938 construction start and 1939 completion may be the same job, but no source says so. Forest Lookouts is the only source with construction detail and cites a 1938 annual report and investment record that we could not check against originals. Record elevation 449.9 m matches the register's 1,476 ft; firelookout.com gives 1835 ft, which we did not use. Main history agrees across all three sources. Cab size conflicts: Forest Lookouts gives 8x8 in its 1941 entry and 7x7 in the May 1942 inspection report; the story reports both and does not choose. Staff names come from 1942-43 entries on Forest Lookouts (quoting period newspapers and reports); the 1954 observer is deliberately not named. No source describes what remains today or public access; the one web search surfaced storm coverage only, not site status. The 'Activated ... Portland Filter Center' note on Forest Lookouts is quoted as written and not explained further.

Build date is unresolved: the register says 1948; firelookout.com says the 1930s; Forest Lookouts has panorama photographs from October 20, 1935. The story reports the disagreement without choosing. Thin source base: three pages, none with an account of the site today, ownership change or public access. No source we read describes what remains on the site today, so the story says so. Build and removal dates disagree: 1941 build and 1944 cut (register, firelookout.com) against a 1933 plan and a 1952 40-foot replacement (Rex). Height kept at 12.2 m from the record, which matches the 40-foot figure in Rex and Oregon Hikers; the register and firelookout.com say 41 feet after 1944. The editor may want to confirm before using it.
No staffing dates or named lookouts found; built year (1931) is consistent across NHLR and firelookout.com. No contradictory info encountered for this tower.

Status is disputed and needs a human decision before the record changes. The FFLA Oregon 2007 report lists Bald Butte as lost in 2007 and burnt to the ground; the May 2018 visit describes the tower as still standing, abandoned and in bad shape; firelookout.com (undated) says condemned and severely vandalized. The record's Bald (Dooley) entry (US 1104) and the register's second Dooley Mountain entry (US 1116) disagree on the build year (1934 against 1936), the abandonment (1947 on US 1116 only), and the elevation (6,683 ft against 6,151 ft). Their coordinates are about 5 km apart: US 1104 at 44.57412, -117.89368 and US 1116 at 44.58244, -117.83097. firelookout.com's Dooley page gives 6151 ft and points to the Bald Mtn. account, so the editor should decide whether these are one site recorded twice before the record's elevation and location are trusted. The record's 2037 m is the US 1104 figure and is not necessarily wrong for that entry. Rex's page treats Bald Mountain as the same station through 1975, while the 1947 abandonment date is not reconciled with it. John Badon (Rex, 1933) and John Bacon (firelookout.com, 1932) may be the same man. No source describes what remains on the site, and no source gives access. The Rex 'Removed' heading carries no date. The brief lists the agency as 'U.S.Forest Service' with no space; the story uses 'U.S. Forest Service'.

Agency conflict: the register and the record say Oregon Department of Forestry, while Rex's page (1933 and 1934 newspaper items, and a 1936 Forest Service station description) places the lookout in the Siuslaw National Forest with a Forest Service disk. The story reports both and does not resolve it. Build year conflict: the register and firelookout.com date a crow's nest to 1923, which Rex's page does not mention. The register says the cabin was built in 1934, and firelookout.com says 1936. Name: the sources call the site Hell Canyon or Bald Mtn. (Hells Canyon); the 1936 survey note says it is the same mountain as Sheridan Peak. County: the record says Yamhill, and Rex's 1933 item says the lookout is on the line between Tillamook and Yamhill counties; the 1941 note places it just east of the county line. The removal date rests on the register and firelookout.com; Rex's page has a Removed heading with no date. No source gives the current state of the site or its access. Oregon Digital images titled Bald Mountain from Lane County concern a different site and were excluded.

Brief's location conflict (NHLR vs RIDB coordinates) was not resolved here since it doesn't affect the narrative; recreation.gov currently lists amenities as unavailable due to vandalism/storm damage, worth double-checking closer to the 2026 rental season for accuracy.

Access was 'unknown' in the brief; filled as public because the summit path is open to hikers. No source gives a removal date or reason. Brief's conflict note ('They share a register number') could not be checked against the sources read. The firelookout.org list gives coordinates 45.39725, -121.74509, which differ from the register coordinates the record uses. Two other pages named Bald Mountain (Josephine County, NHLR US 480 in Klamath County) were not used. No staffing or fire history found.

Record height 18.3 m appears to come from the 60-foot tower announced in 1928, not the present 29.5-foot tower; correction proposed. The 1928 tower's height and the first-lookout date are disputed in the sources. Staffing is contested (firelookout.com says staffed; a Cheryl Hill index says unmanned) and undated; check with Walker FPA or Fremont-Winema NF. Cheryl Hill's index also gives 1947 in the same row; that is not used. The register's 'Fremont National Forest' is now the Fremont-Winema NF. Access (whether the cab is open to visitors) is not stated in any source read. The 2003 registration date is from the register. A May 1941 newspaper item names a builder for the new tower; the register says the Forest Service constructed it, and the story follows the register.

Elevation conflict: firelookout.com gives 3,730 ft; Oregon Hikers and SummitPost give 3,975 ft for the summit. Treated as the same peak on the Illinois River Trail; the story gives both figures. The 1914 trail item, the 1931 fire, the 1932 death, the 1941 staffing and the 1943 filter-center note all come from Forest Lookouts' transcriptions of old newspaper items; no second source was read for them. Removal date not found. No source describes the site today. Not the Bald Mountain lookouts in Clackamas County (US 565) or Klamath County. Record elevation_m is null; leave for editor given the conflict. Distance conflict: the Grants Pass Daily Courier item of September 4, 1929 (quoted by Forest Lookouts) puts the lookout 58 miles from Grants Pass, while firelookout.com gives 29 miles west of Grants Pass; no source explains the difference, and the story reports both.

Thin record: no construction year, staffing, fire or removal history found in four pages, and two web searches returned nothing usable. Location conflict: firelookout.com says about 27 miles southeast of Mount Hood in Mount Hood NF; the Rex's page gives Warm Springs Indian Agency, 6S-11E-12. The register and firelookout.com agree on elevation (3,725 ft). The brief's access 'unknown' is left unfilled because no source states access. Peakvisor lists 1,138 m, not used.

Brief access 'permission' is not stated by any source read, so access is left out of facts. Brief height_m 13.7 matches the 45-foot tower in the 1935 report, not the 40-foot pole tower in the register; it was removed from facts because no source read states a height in metres. Brief elevation 2003.8 m matches the register (2,004 m). The 1925 letter's author is not named in the text read. A 2001 'Bald Peter Fire' on the reservation appeared only in search snippets and was not read, so it is not used. No staffing names are used beyond what the sources state.

Build year conflicts: 1912 (Osbornes Project; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1912 Morning Oregonian item) vs 1937 (firetower.org, firelookout.com). Photos dated August 1, 1933 show a lookout before the 1937 date; the story reports both dates and does not pick one. Do not merge with the Jefferson County Bald Peter Mountain site (Warm Springs reservation, 1933 pole tower, destroyed in a 1943 fire; firetower.org and firelookout.com baldpeter33b): that is a different lookout with a different registry entry. No source gives current site condition, visibility or public access. Removal date is not given anywhere. Staffing evidence is one sentence (Green Peter fire patrolman).

Brief record is consistent with the sources (status gone, agency USFS, elevation 2318 m). Build year and removal/destruction are disputed and reported as such. Staffing 'as_of' 1945 is the last staffing mention found, not a documented end date. No source describes the site today, its access, or any remains; a survey station description from 1946 is the only physical detail, and it predates the 1968 removal. Photos on firetower.org (1930s, Al Opdahl) have no image URLs in our cache, so none were added.

Build date is only the decade (1930s); no source gives a year, so no built event is recorded. Height conflict (70 ft vs 65 ft tower height) is left unresolved. No source describes current condition or access, so access is unset. The 1935 panorama is on firetower.org and iamwho.com; no image URLs were captured, so no photo records were added.

Brief record matches sources (status gone, tower type, Union County, elevation 4,716 ft). The 1933 and 1960 tower dates agree across Register and firelookout.com; the 1981 gone date too. Only the Forest Lookouts page gives a 1935 panorama entry and the 1958 and 1962 newspaper items. A 1978 NADB citation (Kesselman, Preliminary Cultural Resources Report, Bally Mountain Salvage Sale, tDAR 158488) lists 'Lookout' as a keyword, but tDAR holds only the citation, so it was not used. No source describes the site today, its access, or any remains. Photo credit on firelookout.com (courtesy Umatilla National Forest) has no image URL in our cache, so no photos were added.

The 1933 cab and the 1962 end are consistent across three sources, but the design (L-5 vs L-4) and the forest name disagree. The 1980 NGS-style survey description calls the house now abandoned, which does not fit a 1962 removal; the page does not say whether a building still stood then. Two correction proposals (design L-4 to L-5, access unknown to public) are for the editor to accept or reject. No photos added: no image URLs were available from the pages read. Staffing is only the 1941 season; later staffing is not in the sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now says the 1928 packer was going to drag logs (the source says he was to), and drops the unsupported 'short walk' wording.

Height 3.0 m in the record matches the 1942 survey's about-10-feet description, which may be of an earlier building than the 1957 steel house. Design is sourced from the 1933 L-5 entry; no design is in the brief. Replacement year (1955 vs 1957) and move year (1973 vs 1974) disagree and are both reported. The 1967 and 1972 staffing items come from newspaper clippings reprinted on Oregon Lookouts and were not checked against the papers. No photos added: the Register's panorama photo credits had no image URLs in the pages read. The Forest Service trail page was last updated August 12, 2025. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the helicopter move is attributed only to Oregon Hikers and Oregon Lookouts, not the Register or Firelookout.com.

Core facts agree across the Register and Firelookout.com: the 1933 USFS pole tower, never manned or used, gone by 1949. The record has no access or visit facts, and no source read describes the site today or whether the summit is open, so those keys are left out. The Register page credits a 2012 photo of the site (courtesy Howard Verschoor); its image URL was not available, so it is not added. The story is short because the sources are thin.

Brief shows only the 2010 registration; the build and removal events are added from Forest Lookouts and Firelookout. Build year (1933 vs 1934) and fate wording conflict across sources. The brief's access 'unknown' is kept; no source describes the site now. Brief distance and elevation match the register. The August 1934 document is a memo from the Umpqua forest supervisor to the regional forester, not a work report.

Brief has only the 2010 registration; build, staffing, replacement and removal events come from Forest Lookouts, Firelookout and the register. Build and replacement dates disagree across sources. The only source on the site's condition is a 2014 hiker forum thread, a user report and not a survey; no source describes the site today. Staffing is recorded only to 1944, the last documented staffing; the earlier 'unstaffed as of 1969' had no source. Access is 'unknown' because no source states whether the site is open. Web search snippets were not used as facts; only fetched pages are cited.

The brief record shows 1933 built and 1965 removed from the register's fields. The register's description and the other two sources disagree on the tower dates and fate. Staffing is recorded as last documented in the 1963 season; the earlier 'unstaffed as of 1967' was the destruction date and had no staffing source, so it was replaced. A 1970 placeholder event was dropped; the 1970s comes from Firelookout's status note only. The NGS data sheet linked from Forest Lookouts was read: a 1943 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description that calls the lookout a Forest Service lookout and says the station was not marked and not visited by that party. It describes 1943, not today, so the 'no source describes the site today' note stands. One WebSearch was used and yielded only unrelated 2024 fire results, so it was not cited.

Four sources, all read. The 1930s L-4 cab has no exact year in any source, so it is in the story but not as a dated event. The record's material 'wood' (material_from design) is not stated by any source we read; left unchanged. Oregon Hikers also lists a 'Baty Butte via Thunder Mountain' route tagged 'Closed'; unclear what that refers to, so not used. No new photos found; the existing FFLOS panorama is the only image in the record.

Sources conflict on the 1933/1934 tower (10 vs 20 ft), the present tower height (50 vs 54 ft 6 in), and current status (register says active service; firelookout.com says emergencies only). Staffing as_of is undated. Elevation: record 793.1 m matches the register's 2,602 ft; Cheryl Hill lists 2,866 ft. Access is set to restricted from the Cheryl Hill column; confirm with the Douglas FPA before any visit advice.

Three sources, all read; none describes the site today. Spelling varies (Bear Bones, Bearbones). The record's material 'wood' is not stated by any source we read; left unchanged. A Willamette National Forest lookout history (a scholarsbank thesis) appeared in search results but was not read; it may give a removal date and the design. Staffing evidence is a single 1935 item.

Access 'permission' is inferred from Weyerhaeuser land ownership and the 1965 permit; no current access rule was found, and the story gives no visiting directions. The 2025 visit report calls the cabin abandoned and barely standing and describes a bushwhack, so the record's status keeps 'standing' with a status note. The 2025 report lists a 20-ft steel tower, which conflicts with the cabin in other sources; check the type before using 'design'. A 1935 US Forest Service recovery note places the station at the center of the lookout house but gives no size. The 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey note may describe an earlier house rather than the 1949 cabin. The record's elevation (1677.3 m) follows the NHLR figure.

Three sources read; the Forest Lookouts page is a compilation of dated newspaper and Forest Service items, and only items about the lookout are used. Not used: firelookout.com heading 'R.I.P. 1924-1932' conflicts with its own text (L-4 cab 1932 to 1965). Lead for a future pass: a Siskiyou National Forest lookout inventory PDF (digital.sou.edu, collection p16085coll18, id 41128) lists Bear Camp with 1932 and 1965 dates in its appendix table; the table layout did not extract cleanly, so it is not cited. The 1915 cabin's relation to the 1924 shake cabin is unresolved. No new photos found.

Access is left out: no source says whether the land is open to the public, so the brief's unknown stands. No source describes remains or a view at the site now; the story says so. The brief's 26.2 m height matches only the Forest Lookouts 86-ft figure. firelookout.org lists a different Castle Rock (FFLOS US 944, Lane County, 44.15131, -122.21206); that is a separate site and was not merged. Lookout names Charles Kingsley and Bob Wagner come from 1935 and 1940 press items quoted on Forest Lookouts; they were not checked against the newspapers.

The brief's firelookout.com link for this site (https://www.firelookout.com/or/bearpoint.html) returns a page for the Eagle Rock Fire Lookout Cabin (Willamette NF, Marion County, 1934 L-5 cab, gone 1953), not Bear Point. It was not used, and the record's source list should drop that URL or point it at the correct page. A Forest Service page and an AllTrails listing for a Bear Point summit trail (Trail #3342, one labelled closed) came up in search; neither was read in full and neither is used, so visit and access facts are omitted. The brief's design (L-4), county, agency and elevation (1,841.9 m) are confirmed; no corrections proposed.

Removal is only dated to the 1960s, and the sources disagree on removed versus destroyed; the event uses year 1960 as a placeholder for the decade. The 2000 site photo is captioned on the register page, but no image URL was taken, so no photos entry. Access and visit facts are omitted: no source gives access rules and the brief's access is unknown. The record's coordinates (42.10127, -124.01822) match the register, and elevation 726.9 m matches 2,385 ft. No corrections proposed.

Brief record checked: status gone, elevation (1,544 m), agency and 2010 registration all match the register. No corrections. The 1928 fire, 1928 letter and 1950 lookout come from one weebly page each, so they carry the medium rating. Height 4.9 m is converted from the 16-foot figure, assuming it is tower height, as firelookout.com's wording suggests. Access level 'permission' is carried from the existing record; the register names the reservation as administrator but no source read states visiting rules, so it needs a check before publication. Do not confuse with the Beaver Butte on the Idaho Forest Lookouts page (idaholookouts.weebly.com), a different tower. The Forest Lookouts page's 'Removed' entry gives no date. No photo URLs recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the January 1928 letter is now described as material on hand for a line, not a line that would be built. Evidence quotes added for the Wasco County location, the May 24 and July 17 dates, the Bend Bulletin item and the January 10, 1928 letter date.

Brief record checked: gone, Coos FPA, 2010-era registration and 607 ft all match. Brief height 15.2 m (50 ft) is the 1934 tower only; the 1958 replacement was 40 ft (about 12.2 m) per the register and firelookout.com, but the 1958 district report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 50 ft, so the record should say which tower the height describes. Brief design 'L-4' is supported only for the 1934 tower. Access 'unknown' is kept from the record: no source read says whether the site is public. The Forest Lookouts page now reads in full, so its 1936 fire entry (a lookout beat back flames threatening his tower) is complete; it is not used in the story. Do not use Wikipedia's 'Beaver Hill, Oregon' for the lookout: that article is a coal-mining ghost town whose coordinates are a few kilometres from the lookout's, and it says only that nothing is left of the town. The register's photo (courtesy Howard Verschoor) has no image URL in our data, so no photo is recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story states the 40 ft versus 50 ft disagreement about the 1958 replacement without choosing one; the sources read do not settle it.

Thin record: only the register and firelookout.com give dates, and the Forest Lookouts page has only the site name, forest and 'Removed'. No staffing or fire history appears in any source read, so none is recorded. Brief record checked: gone, U.S. Forest Service, 1920 and 2019 dates match; the 1940 removal year is approximate (see corrections). Height 9.1 m is 30 ft and refers to the 1936 tower. The register's photo caption reads 'Beaver Mountain Lookout 1920 - 1936', which may describe a photo span only; it is not used as evidence of removal. A Wallowa-Whitman lookouts ArcGIS app appeared in search results but was not read. The lat/long differs slightly between the register (45.13715, -118.16262) and firelookout.org (45.13737, -118.16270); the register figure is kept. No photo URLs recorded.

Four sources, all hobbyist or database compilations; no Forest Service record was found. The 1932 station and 1939 tower conflict is unresolved. The 2020 account is the only description of the site today and is a personal hike. Firelookout.com credits photos to the USFS and Jim Doerter, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed. The brief's agency and elevation match the sources.

Brief height_m 36.6 (120 ft) matches no height in the pages read: the register gives 128 ft for the 1943 steel tower, the history page gives 130 ft for the 1942 tower, and 105 ft after the 1963 rebuild. The record's source for 36.6 should be checked. The brief's 2010 FFLOS registration date (November 22, 2010) does not appear in the register text read, so it is not repeated. The Tillamook County Bell Mountain (FFLOS US 669) is a different site and was excluded. A Douglas Forest Protective Association Facebook post seen in search says the 1962 storm destroyed the tower; it was not read, and the register and history page say damaged, which the story follows. Current access and land ownership are not described in any source read, so access is omitted.

The register and Oregon Lookouts disagree on the tower sequence (1925 and 1934 newspapers vs 1935 and 1936 register and Rex's page); the story gives both and does not choose. The brief's source_pages includes the Douglas County Bell Mountain page, a different site, and it should be removed from this record. A firelookout.org directory row seen in search (not fetched) pairs this site with FFLOS US 761, which is the Douglas County number. One search found no current description of the site; access is not stated in any source read. No photos added.

Three sources. The brief's agency string reads U.S.Forest Service; corrected here to standard spacing. No height is recorded in any source. No source describes the site today, and access is not recorded. A web-search summary attributed the 1948 abandonment to an Idaho Bennett Mountain; the register and firelookout.com both state it for this site, so the search summary was not used.

Three sources, two of them compilations. Builder of the 1942 tower is disputed (association with AWS/FFE funds vs CCC). The register's 30-foot height and the 1942 survey's 35 feet conflict. No source gives current public access. The 2002 recovery note is the most recent description found. The c.1935 35-foot tower entry was left out of the story because it conflicts with the cabin history and is undated.

Brief had access unknown; no access level is set because no source describes public access. The Clatskanie Mountain tower is a separate replacement structure (US 679), not the Benson tower. Source [4] is a personal blog, used only for the replacement's history and location. The 1942 inspection (45 ft) and the register (40 ft) disagree on height; the brief's 13.7 m follows the 45 ft figure. No photos added.

Brief height_m 25.9 looks like the 85-foot ladder, so it was removed from the story in the 2026-10-09 fact-check. Brief kind 'ground' may not fit: sources describe an enclosed base with a cab reached by ladder on a rock; left unchanged for a human to decide. A search result for a Forest Service photo record (picryl.com, not opened, returned 403) gives the build date as ca. 1934, which conflicts with the 1931 date; unverified and not used in the story. Source [4] is a user review on a trip-listing site and is hedged in the story. No access level set: no source describes public access today. No photos added. Checker (height_m): our record's 25.9 m may be wrong: 25.9 m matches the 85-foot ladder the 1932 article describes, not the height of the structure. No source read gives an overall height.

Only three sources, none describing the site today. Brief lists access as unknown, so no access level is set. The 1958 heliport item is a Forest Lookouts quotation of a Zigzag District report; the report itself was not opened. A Nature Conservancy page on 1930s Forest Service panoramas (maps.tnc.org) may hold a photo lead; not opened, so no photo added.

The three sources agree on the 1973 build, the October 1973 blowdown, the 1974 rebuild and the 1990 removal. The only real disagreement is which agency ran the tower, and the story says so. Nothing in our sources describes the original site or the Wallowa tower today, so the 'today' paragraph says that plainly. A quick check with the Wallowa Fire Department or the Wallowa History Center would settle whether the hose tower still stands, but I did not chase that.

Thin record. Elevation 4,686 ft (firelookout.com); a peakbagging.com table row reads 'Big Hill Bald (LO site)' at 4680 ft (only the row was read). County: Wallowa (firelookout.com, FFLA list) vs Union (Forest Lookouts Union County page). Location code: section 29 (Big Hill page) vs section 20 (Union County page). The 1936 entry on firelookout.com is ambiguous ('1936: unknown') and is not recorded as a build event. The 1940 abandonment rests on firelookout.com alone; a web search found no second source. Web search hits for Red Hill and Bald Knob are different lookouts and were not used. No photos found. Forest Lookouts' Union County page is the only source placing it in Union County, and its section code conflicts with the Big Hill page; an editor should check the Wallowa-Whitman records before the county is changed.

The register says the tower was removed in 1958; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story reports both and does not choose. The register's only photo is the 2001 foundation-block image; no current description was found. One search found nothing newer about the site. Brief elevation 1561.2 m matches the register's 5,122 ft. No fire events appear in the sources read. The register's map image was not read.

Access 'restricted' is inferred from firelookout.com's 'available for emergencies' (undated); no 2020s source confirms current use. The 2010 peakbagging photo caption (dated July 16, 2010) says the lookout was staffed by two people; the names are left out of the story. Elevation was not reconciled: NHLR gives 2,172 m (matches the record), firelookout.com gives 7120 ft, peakbagging gives 7126 ft. The record's height_m of 3.0 m is only the 10-ft base; check it before publishing a height. The 1975 and 1962 items come from newspaper excerpts on the Forest Lookouts page, not the newspapers themselves.

Sources disagree on the builder (register: Santiam Lumber Company; the August 1950 item quoted by Forest Lookouts: Fire Patrol crew) and on distance from Sweet Home (32 miles in the August 1950 item, 16 miles on firelookout.com); the story reports both without choosing. The record's '2007 restored' looks wrong and is proposed as a correction; the 2007 report describes a survey and winter sealing only. Design labels differ (BC-301, L-4, 14x14 type). The original cab burned to the ground on June 21, 1951 (Albany Democrat-Herald, quoted by Forest Lookouts); Every Lookout in Oregon says it was reconstructed in 1951. The sources do not say how much of the standing cab is the 1951 rebuild, so the 1950 build date may not describe the structure visitors see today. An earlier note that no notable fire appears in the sources was wrong. The 2020 Holiday Farm Fire came close; the lookout survived. Access: private timber land behind a closed locked gate; a gate sign allows non-motorized recreation at fire precaution level 1 or lower. The 2026 description is a single blog visit.

Abandonment in 1958 is backed by two sources (register and Fire Lookout), but the tower height and build year differ across sources and the story says so. The Forest Lookouts page is a summary of Umpqua National Forest files and Roseburg News-Review clippings, so the 1933 cab date has less independent support. Nothing we read describes the site today. Name clash: searches for Big Squaw Mountain return other peaks with the same name, so a reader may need the county to confirm they have the Oregon site.

The 1938 to 1962 history is well sourced from newspapers and district reports. The register's removal date (1967) conflicts with state inventory entries from 1974 and 1977, and the 1962 replacement type is disputed. The story flags both. The 1942 survey description was written about the summit building and is quoted through the Forest Lookouts page; I did not open the federal datasheet itself. Nothing we read describes the summit today. The site is called Bill's Butte in the newspapers and Bill Peak in the register and on USGS maps.

Brief record errors: height_m 3.0 and design D-6 describe the cupola and the wrong structure; corrections proposed. The 1934 tower dimensions, collapse date and cupola date conflict across sources. Current staffing is only confirmed to 2019 (Nugget) and July 2016 (Cheryl Hill). No current access source was read beyond the 2016 blog, so the public-access level is provisional. Oregon.com, Oregon Hiking and Hikespeak showed up in search results and were not read; one gives 62 ft for the replacement, which is not used. The NHLR photos (1972 DNF archive; 2006 Ron Kemnow) have no URLs or licences, so none were added.

Only three sources. The NHLR and firelookout.com pages are both undated, so current status and staffing are unverified. Build year conflicts (1936 NHLR, 1933 firelookout.com). Brief design L-4 and height 6.1 m match the NHLR's 20-ft pole tower; the 20-ft figure is read as the tower height. Searches mostly returned the Black Butte near Sisters (Deschutes NF, Jefferson County, 1934/1995 towers) and a 2021 Black Butte Fire 8 miles NE of Antelope Lookout; neither is this tower and neither was used. Access is provisional. Editor should check with the Prairie City Ranger District on current status before publishing. No photos added.

Design is not in the current record (design null); the register and firelookout.com both support the 1925 frame cabin and the 1930s L-4 cab, so it is proposed as a fact, not a correction. The 1930s replacement has no exact year. Elevation differs (7,251 ft register vs 7,260 ft 1936 USFS station description) and is reported both ways. Current site condition is unknown: no source describes remains or public access to the old site. Search results included a 2026 real-estate blog and an AllTrails listing that describe the summit as burned in the 2003 B&B Fire; not used because they are not reliable sources about the lookout, but worth checking against Forest Service fire history. A Forest Service trail page sentence about a former lookout did not appear in the cached fetch, so it is not cited. Verification 2026-10-09: the story no longer calls the 1925 house the first house. A Bend Bulletin item quoted on Forest Lookouts, dated August 20, 1925, already refers to 'the Black Crater lookout house' (ice on its west side, reported by Blanchard), so the sources do not show when the summit house was first occupied; the September 1925 item describes a standard lookout house under construction.

Sources conflict on design, date and status. Firelookout.com says the platform is still there, but gives no date for that; the FFLA index says Abandoned. The photographer's page (about 2001) reports 1931 photos of a tree lookout, a 1940 Kresek listing, and doubts the cabin came from this peak; Kresek's book was not read. Not used: a 1913 Crook County Journal item on Forest Lookouts' page that mentions a telephone at a lookout station on 'Black Butte', which may not be this peak. Record elevation_m 1617.3 was not checked against a source in this run. The cabin's current location rests on one 2023 article. A recent site visit or an Ochoco NF contact would settle the status. The 2023 article gives the site 25 miles south of Prineville in its lead and 25 miles east in another passage (the camp near the old ranger station); the story reports both.

Location conflict is unresolved and the story gives no coordinates: the current record uses the FFLA point 43.16, -122.464, while the FFLOS register gives 43.19564, -122.2922, about 14 km apart. Both name Umpqua NF and Douglas County. Check against the forest map before using either point. Forest Lookouts gives the forest location as 28S-3E-4 (not checked against a map). Build date and fate conflicts are reported, not resolved. The 2024 account is a personal blog, so access today is unconfirmed and the story says so. No access level is recorded because no agency source describes current access. Staffing as_of 1965 is inferred from the building being described as discontinued.

Current status conflicts: the register describes the Douglas association staffing it, while firelookout.com says emergency status and the 2015 visit found it not regularly staffed and boarded up. The 1996 vs 1997 remount date is unresolved. Elevation: record 784.6 m matches the register's 2,574 ft; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 2,696 ft. Record height 6.1 m vs present 20 ft 4 in (6.2 m) is a small difference, so no correction is proposed. Staffing as_of is undated. Visit route comes from a 2015 blog visit; recheck before publishing any visit advice.

Thin sourcing: three web sources, two of them the same register and firelookout.com pair. The newspaper quotes are all reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page. The identity of Cummins Lookout is unresolved. The Lane County Cummins Peak entry (US 1796, in the record at data/towers/or/us-or-cummins-peak-lane-county.json) gives a 1954 tower and 1975 removal, which does not line up exactly with the 1953 move, so the link is unproven and the story says so. The height correction (6.1 m to 12.2 m) is proposed; the 20-foot figure is the February 1943 plan. A PDF copy of the Forest Lookouts page (orww.org) matches the weebly page. An NRHP nomination for the Blodgett tract turned up in search but was not read; it may help with the tract but is unlikely to describe the lookout.

Basic facts (built 1955, abandoned and gone 1970) agree across three sources. Staffing rests on one 1957 newspaper item quoted by the Oregon Lookouts page; the original newspaper was not read. No source describes the site today. Brief coordinates match the register. Brief's agency spelling corrected. Elevation disagreement left unresolved.

Built 1933, abandoned 1966 and dismantled 1974 are supported by several sources. Height and build year conflict and are left out of facts. Coordinates conflict between the register detail page and the list; the list values from the brief were kept but not checked on a map. The 1942 survey marker is the only description of the site; whether it survives is not stated. Staffing names come from 1935-1945 newspaper items quoted on the Oregon page; originals not read. Photos on the register page are credited to a private collection and were not added.

Original site: no source describes it today. Move of the 1963 tower to Robinson Butte is well sourced, but the Oregon list's standing tower at Robinson Butte was not checked on the ground to confirm it is the same structure. Build year and height conflict; height_m left out. Staffing evidence is thin (1940-1952 newspaper items via the Oregon page). Photos on the sources were not added (licence not stated).

The 1934 platform and the 2007 move of the cab are well supported. The tower date is disputed: 1950 in the register's Built field, 1958 in its own description and in Weebly, mid-1950s in FFLOS. No source names a lookout who staffed it. The park name The Perch and the June 2022 visit come from a single personal travel blog. The brief's source list points to a sister record, us-or-bly-ranger-at-bly-city-park, which I did not read. Reads used: 6 (register, FFLOS, firelookout.com, Weebly, the 2022 blog, and Wikipedia's Bly Ranger Station page, which has no lookout content and is not cited). Searches: 1.

The record's 'standing' status and 'ground' kind refer to the relocated cab, not a tower. Access is unverified beyond the park location; no source describes entry. The condition of the cab in 2026 rests on the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and could not be checked further. The 2007 chapter report says the cab was moved, not the tower. The 1950 vs 1958 build year is a source conflict; the story reports both.

Built year conflicts: 1941 (register, firelookout.com) vs 1940 (Siskiyou NF history quoted on Oregon Lookouts). Design wording differs: pole L-4 vs round timber. No source describes what remains on the site today, and none gives public access, so access is omitted. No source describes what remains on the site today or whether the site is open to the public, so access is omitted. No source describes what remains at the site today, and no access information was found, so access is omitted. Build year conflict (1934 vs 1937) unresolved. Newspaper items are quoted second-hand from the Oregon lookouts page; the original News-Review and Oregon Statesman issues were not checked.
