Brief record lists the Winema NF; the 1934 sources say Deschutes NF. The Weebly page marks the tower 'Removed' with no date, so only the by-1965 bound is used. WillhiteWeb's 2022 photo is captioned only, so no current remains are described. Access level is left out because no source states public status; drive-up is recorded under visit. Revision 2026-10-09: the 15 Feb 1933 letter is addressed to a fire-protection association ('your protective area'), so the story says it was sent to the association, not written by it; the detection wording is 'excellent'.

The 1961 replacement, the 67-foot timber tower and the 2022 register date agree across sources; the brief's 15.2 m height is the earlier 50-foot steel tower, so a correction is proposed. Staffing comes from undated firelookout.com and trail-guide text, so the as_of date is the research date; a current staffing check would strengthen it. Access is restricted to the road and staffed-lookout permission; the sources do not say whether the tower itself is open to visitors, so climbable is omitted. Confidence is high on the build history and medium on current staffing.

Thin record. Sources are one dated entry (1934 crow's nest and camp), an abandonment date in the 1940s, a directory listing and a one-line Forest Lookouts entry. Two WebSearch calls found nothing about this lookout. A Jonsrud Viewpoint result in Sandy mentions a ridge also called Devil's Backbone; it is a different place and was not used. The brief's status gone is not supported; sources say abandoned. The story is at the short end of the length range because the evidence is thin. Verification 2026-10-10: the story's 'location code' label was changed to 'code', since the page does not label 2S-5E-11, and a Clackamas County heading quote was added to the directory evidence.

Weebly and the register agree on 1912, 1936 and 1962. The 1936 structure is called a cab on six-foot pillars, not a tower. No source describes the site today or public status. TopoQuest gives a locale at 4,740 ft against the register's 4,820 ft; not used. A 2024 Forest closure near Highway 46 was found in search but nothing ties it to this lookout, so it is not used. Revision 2026-10-09: no source calls Devils Knob a summit, so the story calls it a former lookout site; the register gives the 1962 removal without a method and the story attributes burning only to the history page.

Brief record matches the NHLR's 1952 cab date, but firelookout.com calls the 1933 cab the present one. The NHLR and firelookout.com pages are both undated, and the 2014 NHLR visit report is the newest staffing data. Current access is the main open question: the Cool Creek trail page (undated copy) says closed for storm damage, and the Austin and Narrows fire closure (Sept 16 to Dec 31, 2026) boundary text does not name the trail or Still Creek Road; whether it covers this peak was not confirmed. Search snippets said the trail page was updated Jan 5, 2026, and that the Cool Creek trailhead sits in the Zigzag district; neither was read on the page, so neither is used. Search results also included a 1952 date from a photo aggregator, which was not used. No photos added.

Not the Devils Peak near Mount Hood (us-or-devils-peak). The Mountaineers page found in search describes that Hood-area peak and was not used. Agency naming differs: Rogue River/Winema (register), Crater then Rogue River (history page). The 2017 trip report is a hiker's account, not an agency record. No source states current public access. The 1917 cabin claim is contested. Revision 2026-10-09: the 1930 building is described as on its way (will arrive July 24), the 1968 removal is of the L-4 cab, and the 1963 snowbound item now has an evidence entry.

Brief height_m 36.6 (120 ft) matches Rex's '120-foot high Diamond Rock', which describes the rock, not a tower; the register says a 100-foot rock pillar. Tower height omitted from facts. Removal year conflicts (1968 vs 1969). The 1959 restaffing year is derived from 'restaffed 18 years later'. No source describes the site or its access today; the 2008 register photo's content is not described and was not viewed. Brief access 'unknown' left as is. No photos added.

Brief height_m 9.1 (30 ft) agrees with the annual report quoted on Rex's page; the register says 35 ft, so the height is contested. Brief agency 'Eastern Lane FPA' matches the register; Rex's page header reads 'Eastern Lane District, Oregon Department of Forestry'. The brief's removal status is consistent with both dates. No source describes site condition or access today; the web search for current status found nothing. No photos added (the register's photos are unlabelled by content and were not viewed).

Source 4 is a first-person personal website; only site facts and the author's staffed seasons are used, the author is not named, and no personal details are carried into the story. The account dates its return visit to 1972 ('I had visited Divide in 1972'). The site's navigation menu lists a page titled 'Return to Divide Lookout on a Forest Service trail crew', but the account text does not say the 1972 visit was made with a trail crew, so the story does not say so. Removal year is not in any source; the status note says so. Brief agency 'U.S. Forest' is a truncated register value; correction proposed. Brief height_m 12.5 (41 ft) matches. Brief elevation_m 571.5 matches the register but firelookout.com gives 1,785 ft. Current access not found. Three photos are credited to the register and firelookout.com collections without URLs, so none were added.

Brief's height_m 3.7 has no source in the pages read and is proposed for removal. The 1968 present-cab date is consistent across NHLR, Rex's page and Trails Offroad. Elevation conflict left open: NHLR 7,511 ft vs 7,592 ft on Rex's page and Cheryl Hill. Staffing is from Rex's page (undated, every summer) and a July 2024 visit; current season not confirmed. Name spellings differ across accounts for the 1916 observer (Noey vs Noah Blaine), so no name is used. Forest Lookouts' newspaper items were read as quoted on that site, not from the originals. Trails Offroad is a paid trail-guide site; only its free text was used. Dixie Butte is not on the Malheur NF rental list, which names Fall Mountain Lookout. No new photos recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the L-4 house replaced a cupola cabin of the early 1920s (NHLR), not several early cabins; the 1916 observer phoned the fire's point location, which the story now says.

FFLOS and Forest Lookouts describe a tree crow's nest. firelookout.com does not say tree and titles its page 'Fire Lookout Tower', so the brief's tower question is only partly settled by the sources; the story avoids saying it was not a tower. A separate Forest Lookouts Wasco County entry (June 1934, 100-foot crow's nest; 1935 telephone ring) is a different entry and was not used. The brief's kind 'platform' is close to firelookout.org's 'Crowsnest'; no correction proposed. No access or present-day remains found; access omitted.

Brief's design L-4 describes the 1947 cabin, not the cab standing now (two-story, 1997); corrected. Staffing is contested: Rex's page says staffed every summer (undated), while the June 2022 visit found it locked for the season and no one present. Cab size (15 by 15 vs 15 feet 4 inches) and elevation (6,890 vs 6,936 feet) conflict across sources and are both reported. The 1947 structure type conflicts too (L-4 vs Aladdin-style 14 by 14). The 1995 proposal and 1997 build details come from Forest Lookouts quoting Forest Service archive text; not read in the original. Lookout history of Bertha Covert (1918) is from the register; the 1919 and 1920 newspaper item was not used. No photos added; the register and Rex's page carry photo credits that were not checked for license. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1956 and 1960 Malin items are cited to Forest Lookouts' Herald and News quotes; 'locked up' is now the 2022 visitor's own report that it seemed locked; 6,890 and 6,936 feet are elevations, not summit claims.

Build year 1932 agrees across the register, firelookout.com and Rex's page. Removal year conflicts: register 1965 (matches its photo caption span 1932-1965) vs firelookout.com 'Gone 1969'; Rex's page says only 'Removed'. Structure type conflicts: register calls it a wooden L-4 tower; Rex's page and the 1932 item say L-4 ground house (14x14); the record's kind 'tower' follows the register, so it is a source disagreement rather than a clear record error. The '15' in the register and firelookout.com is not explained (cab or tower height), so no height_m was recorded. No source describes the site today; the record's access 'unknown' is left as is. Two web searches turned up nothing further on Dog Prairie. The Dog Prairie Mount Bailey location is 'five miles west of Mt. Bailey'; the register coordinates are not checked against that.

Three thin sources and no build date, design detail, staffing or fire history found. The 1928 entry lists a crow's nest and tent cabin, so it is recorded as an 'other' event rather than a build. The brief's 'gone' status matches the FFLA mapping of 'Abandoned'; the sources say abandoned, and the undated note says an 8-foot crow's nest remained, so a visit could find remains. Two WebSearch runs returned only the same pages plus unrelated Clatsop items; the Clatsop State Forest Wikipedia page was read and does not mention the lookout. No access, visit or rental information found; the story says so and points to ODF.

Build date conflict left open: register says 1948 (L-4 cab); firelookout.com says L-4 cab 1936; Rex's page says a lookout house c.1936 and a 14x14 L-4 ground house in 1948. Register photos captioned 1942 suggest a lookout stood before 1948, but that is an inference, and the story says so. Forest conflict: register and firelookout.com say Umpqua National Forest; Rex's page heading says Willamette National Forest. Destruction date: Rex's page quotes a 9-17-68 note; firelookout.com says 1968; register says gone by 1969. Do not confuse with Dome Rock Lookout Site - WNF near Detroit (Marion County, US 588 in the FFLA list), which is a different site. Record coordinates (43.45151, -122.4045) differ from the FFLA list (43.45173, -122.40248) by roughly 160 m; no correction proposed. No source describes what remains on the summit today; the 1953 route description is historical and no current access level is recorded, so the access field was left out.

The brief has no height and the site is a ground-level lookout house, so no height is given. Current condition rests on an undated Oregon Hikers guide and 2000 register photos; no current photo was found. The removal date conflicts (1951 vs 1965) and is reported as a conflict. Newspaper items spell the 1944 lookout Jim or Jimmy Poole; the story uses Jimmy as quoted. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-09: all dates checked against the Forest Lookouts page (1928, July 5 and July 30 1929, July 7 1932, Oct 3 1935, Sept 1944, 1947 survey, c.1965); 'Forest Lookouts register' corrected to 'Former Fire Lookout Sites register'; the Oregon Hikers guide is undated, so its remains claim is stated without 'still'.

Build year 1949 agrees across the register and firelookout.com; the 1950 Bend Bulletin item and 1952 inspection are consistent with a tower standing then. Two open conflicts: (1) forest: Ochoco National Forest per the register and Rex's Donnelly page, Malheur National Forest per Rex's Harney County listing (both Rex's sources give township 20S-26E-01); (2) ending: register says removed in 1972, firelookout.com says destroyed 1972, Rex's page gives no date. height_m 21.6 is converted from the register's 71 ft; the register does not say whether 71 ft runs to the cab floor, so check before publishing a height. The record's design field is null; the register and firelookout.com support L-4, so facts.design was added. The record's agency reads 'U.S.Forest Service' (spacing typo); facts.agency is written as U.S. Forest Service. The 1950 honeymoon item names private individuals; the story does not name them. No source describes the butte today; the 1952 road reference is historical and no current access level is recorded.

Record conflicts: 1947 abandonment (register, firelookout.com) vs the July 1958 staffing item (Forest Lookouts). Second entry to check: firelookout.com also lists 'Bald (Dooley) Mountain', ground, gone, FFLOS US 1104, OR 460, at 44.57412, -117.89368; our record is 44.58244, -117.83097 (about 5 km apart). Could be a duplicate or a separate site; not resolved. The Baker Air Force Station radar site (Beaver Mountain, 1959-1968) came up in a search snippet but was not read, so it is not in the story. Access: no source read; left out.

Source [3] reproduces a 1941 USC&GS / 1960 DMA survey description for the Dorn Peak station (designation DORN PEAK LOT, PID QE2307). The survey mark and bronze disks may still exist; that was not checked on the NGS datasheet, so the story says no source describes the peak today. Access: sources give no current access information; the 1941 survey route through a gate is old and was left out. Record height_m 24.4 is supported by the 80-foot NGS figure. Register elevation 868 m matches the record. Dorn vs Doran spelling appears in the 1929 item.

No removal date or reason found in any source. Two web searches turned up no removal record and no link between this site and 'Roba Swift' other than the Roba name in the Forest Lookouts items. If the tower record holds a built year of 1929, a human may want to change it to 1930 (the tower) with a note that the cabin came in 1929; the brief did not show a built field, so no correction is proposed here. Access and present condition: no source read. The 40-foot figure gives height_m 12.2 (about 40 ft). Elevation 6,266 ft matches the record.

Brief's conflict note ('they share a register number') appears to be a brief-generation artifact, not addressed here since no evidence was found that Drake Peak and Bald Butte actually share an NHLR number; NHLR page for Drake Peak gives its own distinct register entry. Flagging for editor to check the queue tool's register-number field if this matters.

Six page reads and one search. The Register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill and The Roaming Civic agree on the 1932 build date and the 70-foot height. Forest Lookouts quotes 1929-1934 newspaper items, which are the only source for the 1929 tree platform and the 1931 delivery. Elevation differs: the Register gives 6,241 ft (1,902 m), firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 6,281 ft, and the brief's 1902.3 m is the Register figure; not in facts. The Forest Lookouts history gives no fire names. The Facebook post from the Forest Fire Lookout Association could not be read (login wall), so nothing is cited from it. Access level is restricted because the sources describe emergency use and a decommission listing without an open-to-public statement. Current status: the Cheryl Hill directory (July 2026) lists it as unmanned and warns its information may be out of date; the Roaming Civic trip report is undated but post-2017. No photos added. The firelookout.com page credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were extracted.

Height is disputed: the register says a 60-ft CT-2 tower, firelookout.com says 50 ft. No height_m is set and the record has none. The 1941 date agrees across both lookout pages. Staffing comes from a 2023 local news report and a May 2022 register visit, so current status is unconfirmed. History searches turned up nothing beyond these pages. No photos gathered. Visit details are from a single visitor report.

Agency conflict: FFLOS credits the Oregon Department of Forestry; firelookout.com and Rex's page put the tower at the Forest Service compound, and Wikipedia calls the station a Forest Service facility in the Mount Hood National Forest. Build year: 1933 (Rex's page, firelookout.com) vs 1934 (FFLOS). The FFLOS point (45.45706, -121.12616) and the firelookout.com index point (45.45742, -121.12364) are about 200 m apart. Access level 'restricted' is inferred from the working compound; no source states it. No removal date appears in any source. The brief's ODF agency is left unchanged.

Brief height_m 3.0 is not supported; corrected to 4.5 m (14'8"). The first-tower dates conflict (1925/1934/1936) and the register's 1936 height conflicts with the Forest Lookouts page. Only firelookout.com dates the structure to winter 2026; no source describes what, if anything, stands on the site now or whether it is accessible. Access fields left out for that reason. Second search found nothing new on the removal. Photos not added. Fact-check 2026-10-09: all dated claims checked against the Forest Lookouts, NHLR and firelookout.com pages (May 26, 1925; Aug 1, 1934; 1936; 1939; 1958; 1970; March 1, 2000); no factual errors found. Story wording changed only where it copied quote text closely.

Built date and CCC garage, 1942 AWS conversion and 1999 repair come from the NRHP nomination, the strongest source. Current staffing is unverified: firelookout.com is undated and says staffed in summer; IJPR (2017) uses present tense. No 2025-26 schedule found. Summit elevation differs across sources (7,364, 7,417, 7,418 ft); the record's 2244.5 m matches the register's 7,364 ft. The record's access 'unknown' can be set to public per the sources, but whether the cabin interior is open to visitors is not confirmed. A trail-guide claim that the lookout is still used for emergency fire detection was seen only in a search snippet and not used.

Five page reads and two searches. The build date is the main open question: NHLR and firelookout.com say about 1935, while the agency letters transcribed by Forest Lookouts describe a 1939-1940 purchase and erection, which suggests the 1935 date may be wrong. Reported as a conflict, not resolved. Height 107 ft (32.6 m) agrees across NHLR and firelookout.com. Elevation: NHLR gives 3,168 ft (966 m), firelookout.com and the directory 3,175 ft; the brief's 965.6 m is the NHLR figure and is not in facts. Current status is taken from the Cheryl Hill directory (listed as of July 2026, which warns it may be out of date) and firelookout.com (undated staffing claim). The Madras Pioneer retrospective quotes a line saying the forest service still provided lookouts for three towers in the McQuinn Strip, which does not clearly apply to Eagle Butte, so it is not cited. A 1992 Spilyay Tymoo OCR page mentions a lookout at Eagle Butte, but the OCR is too garbled to quote. No photos added. The 2026 Bench Fire news on the reservation does not mention Eagle Butte in the pages read, so no damage claim is made.

Unresolved: a 1934 panorama caption predates the 1937 build date, and the 1953 destruction note differs from the 1957 'gone by' date on FFLOS and firelookout.com. Staffing is inferred from the 1954 note that the loss left one full-time lookout in the district; the story no longer states that Eagle Creek itself was a full-time post, because the note does not say so. No access, present-day or photo-of-site information found; access omitted. The firelookout.org county list (type Ground, status Gone) agrees but was not cited.

Build year conflict: the August and October 1933 items on Rex's page vs 1934 on FFLOS and firelookout.com; firelookout.com repeats the FFLOS facts. Coordinates: the FFLOS point (44.77281, -122.0306) and the west_us_lookouts point in the brief (44.7772, -122.0445) are about 1.2 km apart and were not resolved here. No staffing or fire information appears in these sources. Access is unknown; the brief's status and kind stay as recorded.

Build year: 1933 (FFLOS, Rex's page) vs 1932 (firelookout.com, which may be following the August 1932 plan). Removal in 1971 is consistent across all five sources. The 1953 survey station description is quoted through Rex's page; we did not fetch the NGS datasheet itself, so the station's current condition is unknown. Oregon Hikers is a community-edited wiki; the trail details are current as of its cached copy and should be checked before publishing. Access 'public' comes from the trail guide; no closure appears in these sources, but no land manager statement was checked. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the FFLOS registration credit was corrected (the register names a private nominator, not the Forest Service, so the nominator is omitted here).

Original 1932 tower and 1995-96 replacement are well documented across sources; the NHLR says 1995 and the Weebly history says 1996 for the finished tower. Elevation (6,371 vs 6,400 ft) and county (Deschutes vs Lake) conflict and are not resolved. The brief height_m 9.1 is the original 30-ft tower, corrected to 6.1 for the current 20-ft tower. The 1959 fire item is from a Bend Bulletin article quoted by the Weebly site. The 2023 'not invited up' remark is one visitor's account and is not an official access rule. The Roaming Civic 2023 title and date come from a search result; the quoted lines were fetched from its page. firelookout.com says the 1995 structure is a replica of the original 30-foot tower, while the NHLR and Cheryl Hill say 20 feet. The record uses 20 feet (6.1 m) and the story attributes the 20-foot figure to the NHLR. This conflict is not in the story.

Three pages, all agree the towers were built in 1938 and are gone; staffing and fires are not described. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 'gone' statement now cites the Former Fire Lookout Sites page alone; the 1946 observation-tower mention no longer implies it was one of the 1938 towers; Baker County and the 1946 survey year now have quotes. The NGS survey text on the Forest Lookouts page carries a status line reading 'Removed' whose meaning is unclear (it may refer to the survey mark), so it is not used as evidence for the lookout's status. Direction from Baker City differs by source (12 miles south vs 13 miles air-line southeast). The 1946 tower reference does not say which structure it was. Access and remains today not described in any source read. Only a few pages read; a second web search was not used.

Register and firelookout.com agree on about 1932 and gone by 1969. The Forest Lookouts page (survey text) adds a 1964 deactivation and a 1970 note that the house was destroyed with the foundation remaining; it is the last physical description found. No source describes the site today. The Forest Lookouts page does describe the route in (a 1.5-hour pack, with a well-marked trail from where truck travel ends) but does not say whether the area is open to visitors. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1970 date and the east-end location now have quotes. The Forest Lookouts listing also carries a 'Removed' status line, not used as evidence because its meaning is unclear. Survey mark stamped 'ZIGZAG 1953' is not a lookout date and is not used. Three pages read; no web search used.

Thin record: one register entry and one index row describe the structure. No build date, builder or staffing found in the register, the index, the ODFW visitor guide, the Wenaha Wildlife Area management plan PDF, the Oregon Lookouts Wallowa County page, or the Cheryl Hill standing-lookouts list (which excludes crow's nests). The Oregon Lookouts Wallowa page lists an Eden Ridge Tree in Wenaha State Wildlife Area at 5N-43E-18; not checked against this site. The 'still stands' status rests on a 2021 photo; it needs a current check before publication. Story does not encourage climbing the structure.

Built history is clear for 1940 and 1960. The current status (camera since 2010, unstaffed) comes from firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts. Access is the Cheryl Hill column, which covers legal access to the site and says nothing about climbing. The 1995 profile's 50-foot height conflicts with the 40-foot figure. The FFLA Oregon list confirms the site as a standing tower but was not cited.

Tower history conflicts across all four sources: first build year, 1974 and 1975 tower heights, the present tower's date (1999 vs 2008), and the county (Curry vs Coos). The record's height (1.8 m) and material (wood) look wrong for the present steel tower. Access is the Cheryl Hill column, which gives no reason for 'No'. No visiting information was found. The site was not checked against NHLR or FFLOS registers.

Built 1940 is consistent across all three pages. Removal year conflicts: register says 1956 'removed', firelookout.com says 'Destroyed 1956', Forest Lookouts page says '1960: Removed'; story reports all three without choosing. Location conflicts: firelookout.com says nine miles southeast of Tillamook; the 1940 Forest Log quote on the Forest Lookouts page says nine miles west of Camp Trask. Construction material differs (pole vs timber). The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1936 newspaper (Daily Capital Journal) and a 1937 annual report, both cited through that page, not read directly. The register page carries a 2010 photo credited to Howard Verschoor; image URL and licence were not captured, so no photo entry. No source describes the site today or public access. One web search run; nothing new found. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1936 newspaper sentence in the story is now paraphrased rather than quoted; the October 1940 date and the crew cabin have quotes; the 14x14 cab is given without a unit because the page gives none.

The only source for 'no longer standing' and for the fir setting is a 2022 visit account on a blog; confirm with the Mt. Hood National Forest before relying on the access note. The 1930 date comes from Rex's page; 'built in the 1930s' comes from the blog. The blog's 1940s abandonment is a stated presumption and is reported that way. The brief's conflict (firelookout_com status Standing) is a crawl value not shown on the detail page. Forest Lookouts gives staffing only through the tent line, so staffing is 'early years, undated'. Two WebSearch runs found no official history. No rental information found.

Sources disagree on build year (c.1928, 1932, 1933) and removal (1962 or 1963; removed vs destroyed). The brief's point 43.28116, -122.22768 matches the register's coordinates (N 43.281160, W 122.227680). The brief's other point, 43.30123, -122.23643 (west_us_lookouts), is not from any source we read and was not checked. No source describes the site today; the register's 2007 site photo was not viewed. Access status unknown; no source found.

County conflict: the register says Union County, firelookout.com says Wallowa County; the story keeps the firelookout.com wording and says the register places it in Union County. The 1966 object was identified as a balloon in the same clipping, and the story now says so. Early history unsettled: the 1928 patrolman item and firelookout.com's 1928 staff entry predate the 1933 build year, and the 1932 plan for a 25 ft tower with a 14x14 house may or may not be the 1933 tower. Record height is not used because the sources give 10 to 40 ft. Ownership conflict: the register lists USFS as administrator while firelookout.com and the directory describe private land; the agency field keeps the register wording with a note. Elevation: 5,127 ft (register) vs 5,122 ft (firelookout); the record's 1562.7 m matches the register. Register photo credit (Ray Kresek, 1993) noted but no image URL was found, so no photo added. Record status 'standing' kept; the cab is abandoned.

Build year 1965 is consistent across four sources. Removal wording differs (removed, destroyed, dismantled); years agree at 1989 or the 1980s. The brief's coordinates match the register (N 43.133360, W 123.925130). The Dora event report names lookouts only at Brewster Rock, not this site, so no staff names were used. The earlier Brewster Rock tower is not this record. Current site condition and access are not described in any source read. Do not confuse with Elk Mountain (Hood River County, US 592) or the Elk Mountain in Wallowa County (US 1614).

Thin record: one register entry, one one-line cabin note, and a 1933 panorama credit. The 1920s build and 1940s loss are decade-only; the 1920 and 1940 years in events are placeholders, not dates from a source. The brief's coordinates (N 45.335951, W 121.611463) match the register; firelookout.com's index lists 45.33579, -121.61127, a small difference. The brief lists the site as kind ground and status gone; the register's wording supports that. Do not confuse with Elk Mountain in Coos County (US 793) or the Wallowa County Elk Mountain (US 1614). No photo of current condition found; no access information found.

Register and firelookout.com both date the tower to about 1941, but Rex's page quotes 1916 and 1925 newspapers that name an Elk's Peak station. A station probably predates the 1941 tower, but no source says so directly. The two 1916 notices disagree on whether a station already stood. Access is unknown and no site description was found. A Coos FPA website appeared in search results but was not read, so it is not cited. Verified 2026-10-09: the full register text and firelookout.com text were read and neither mentions a replacement.

Read: the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register page, FireLookout.com, and Forest Lookouts' Oregon page with dated newspaper and Forest Service items from 1921 to 1939. Thin on the tower: no build contract, and the height and removal come from the register and FireLookout.com only, which may share a basis. No removal record found; the story gives only gone by the 1940s. The 1922 house is kept as written. Worth trying: Central Oregonian and Ochoconian issues 1933-1945, Ochoco National Forest records, and the Harney County Historical Society. The 2008 photo credit (Ron Kemnow) is the nominator's for the register and was not followed up.

No source describes what remains at the site today, and no source states access. One WebSearch found nothing current for this site; its results pointed to Bald Butte, a different Ochoco lookout in Harney County, which is not used here. The register's 2008 photo is listed but not examined. The register says the 1933 tower replaced the house; Rex's 1933 item says a tower and a house were being built. Do not confuse with us-or-emigrant-butte-lane-county (a separate Lane County site). The register also has a photo captioned 1940 (Ron Kemnow collection), which is not used to date the removal.

The register says a 30-foot tower and Rex's page says 20 feet (c.1940). The record's height_m of 6.1 matches Rex, not the register; the two heights appear in the design field only because the sources disagree. The record's elevation of 1970.2 m matches the register's 6,464 ft. Both sources give only 'the 1930s' for the build, so the built event and the abandoned event use the decade start as their year and say so in the notes. No source describes what remains; the remains heading on Rex's page has no text in our copy. The 1938 item, as quoted on Rex's page, spells the butte 'Immigrant Butte'. The story treats it as this lookout because Rex's page files it under Emigrant Butte; the spelling is worth a check.

Most detail comes from association annual reports and newspapers as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. The 1965 tower is called a 34-foot live-in tower built from the bottom half of the Norton Hill lookout by Rex's page. The Norton Hill record says its tower moved to Euchre in 1965 according to one source and was dismantled and salvaged in 1967 according to another, so the two stories should be read together. The 1938 association entry (steel ladder, 6 x 6 cage, '100 foot tree lookout') is unclear about what it describes and is not used. The 30.5 m height matches the 100-foot tower. No current condition, access, visit or rental information found; the story says so. Only one WebSearch run was used for this tower; an orww.org PDF copy of the same article appeared in search results but was not read.

Build year conflict left open: the register says 1942 (with a 1942 photo caption) and firelookout.com says the 1930s, with a 1936 name. The 1952 cab move agrees across Rex, the NHLR and firelookout.com. Today's condition rests on one 2023 visit report (Cheryl Hill) and was not checked against a Forest Service source. The site has three names (Buckhorn Point, Buckhorn Mountain, Buckhorn Overlook); the identification with the cab rests on Cheryl Hill's statement that the Fairchild cabin was moved there. The 1954 history is cited only through Rex's page, which quotes it; it was not read directly. The register's 2010 site photo is captioned but not described, so it does not establish what remains. Record elevation of 1631.0 m matches the register.

The record's status 'gone' is not supported by any source read; sources say abandoned, last described as standing in 1994. Do not confuse with Fairview Peak, a different lookout (Umpqua NF; cherylhill.net lists it as standing). An Oregon Digital photo record titled 'Fire lookout platform on Fairview Peak. Structure collapsed about 1990' appeared in search but could not be fetched (SSL certificate error) and names a different peak, so it is not used. No staffing, access, or current-condition source found.

Sources conflict on the cupola date (1921 register and 1921 newspaper vs 1924 in two others), the 1936 tower height (20, 29 or 30 ft), and whether the tower is in the rental program (2015 removal per a 2026 blog vs rental until pulled for 2022 per a 2022 trip report vs an FS page offering overnight rental). Current access is unresolved: FS marks the site open with a rental, Travel Oregon says temporarily closed, and a 2026 visitor found the road gated. Staffing after 2024 is hearsay from a TikTok account, which also describes a few days of staffing in July 2025. Elevation differs across sources (NHLR 5,857 ft; Roaming Civic 5,933 ft; firelookout 5,933 ft); the brief's 1785.2 m matches NHLR. No source found on any fire spotted from the tower. The brief's built 1972 refers to the present tower; the first structure dates to 1912.

The tower record's build-year conflict (1930 vs 1933) resolves fairly well once the NHLR page is read in full: it describes an emergency post dating to around 1930/1933 with the cab original but the tower rebuilt in 1953 — a detail not yet in the tower JSON's events. No newspaper or Forest Service administrative-history source was found in the cache or a quick web check; everything here comes from the three register/rental pages already linked on the record. Did not propose a correction since the conflict is explainable rather than contradictory, but an editor may want to add the 1953 tower-rebuild event to the main tower record.

Brief record height 30.5 m only fits the 100-ft towers; the final tower was 40 ft (corrected). FFLOS/Fire Lookout early-tower account conflicts with the Forest Lookouts newspaper and annual-report account; story reports the contemporary account and says so. The NGS data sheet (marks stamped FANNO 1972) describes reference marks cemented in concrete posts that were legs of the old tower foundation; whether any of it survives today is unverified, and no source says what remains today. The 1964 transfer to Willamette Valley Lumber Co. is the lead for current ownership and access; not verified. No photos added: the FFLOS 1941 photo has no licence we could confirm.

Three sources agree on the 1930 build and 1970 end but disagree on removed (register, Oregon history) vs destroyed (firelookout.com); the story says so. No source describes the site today or public access, so no access or visit facet was written. Staffing: the only staff-related item is the emergency-lookout use, kept as an 'other' event. Brief record (gone, 2011 registration, USFS, 928 m) is consistent with the sources; no corrections. Two WebSearch queries turned up no page on the site today. No photos added.

Build date unresolved: the September 1927 letter says erected, the register and firelookout.com say 1932; a May 1925 newspaper item predates both and is now the story's earliest documentation (the draft had wrongly called the 1927 letter the earliest). The story reports these and does not choose. The brief records no build date, so no correction is proposed. Height 12.8 m matches the 42-foot figure in the 1927 letter. No source describes the site today or public access; access and visit are omitted. The 1936 survey-disk line is a description, not evidence that the disk survives. Used 2 WebSearch queries (nothing on the current site) and 3 page reads. No photos added; the register's 1944 photo is already on its page.

Not cited: dangerousroads.org says a tower was built in 1933 and taken down in 1967, leaving only the access track. It conflicts with the 1922 reports and the hiking guide's foundation account, so it was not used. Access level 'public' is inferred from the hiking guide's trailhead hike; no closure notice was read. The 'today' claim (foundation and detritus on the summit) rests on one hiking guide; its date is not stated beyond a 2023 trailhead note. Staffing as_of 1942 is the latest dated staff mention found. Used 1 WebSearch and 5 page reads. Brief record (gone, 2011 registration, USFS, 2,244 m) checks out; no corrections.

Removal year not found in the four sources read. The access description rests on one 2022 visit report (WillhiteWeb), not a Forest Service statement, so the story gives no access level. A 1991 Deschutes NF eligibility study of its lookouts (State Library of Oregon record, https://digitalcollections.library.oregon.gov/nodes/view/275303) was found, but its text was not readable here; worth checking for the removal date. Record fields look correct.

Height is disputed (12 ft in the register and Firelookout.com, about 30 ft in the 1947 survey). The closure notice is taken from the Oregon Hikers page and was not checked against the Forest Service closure order, which was not read. The newspaper quotes come from a transcription on the Forest Lookouts page, not the original papers. The Trail Advocates Fish Creek page and the Oregon Hikers post-fire report were not read.

Build year disputed (1938, 1939, 1940). Removal year disputed (1984, 1988, and 1977 per Firelookout.com, unsupported by the 1979 profile). Firelookout.com alone lists a 1934 119-foot L-6 tower, not mentioned in the Forest Lookouts page; left out of the story body except as a disputed sentence. No source describes the summit today. The 1979 profile gives Alvord on the forest since 1951 and at Fishhole since 1964; both are stated. The 1973 closure plan is in the story but no closure event is recorded, because the 1979 profile shows the lookout still staffed. Height record corrected from 21.0 m to 16.5 m (54 ft).

Ground site on public forest land. No source gives a structure height, so height_m is left out. The brief's height_m was never set here. Nothing is known about the site beyond the trail guide's undated report of timbers on the summit (onX, which is commercial and third-party). The 1960s burn date is the guide's 'supposedly', not confirmed. A Southern Oregon University Siskiyou inventory lists Fish Hook Peak, Curry County, built 1934, L-5, with no removal date; it agrees on the build year and was not quoted because its table spacing does not allow a clean quote.

No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to visitors, so access and visit are left out. Coleman Point has its own register record; the editor may want to check that its build and move dates match this story. The brief's elevation (1952.9 m) agrees with the register's 1,953 m. The 1960 staffing item is from a Herald and News quote on the Oregon list and is not confirmed elsewhere.
No current staffing status found in sources, so staffing left as unknown rather than guessed; the brief's 1957 built-year is confirmed by all three sources.

Rental: the brief's rental.available false is consistent with the fire, but recreation.gov still lists the lookout as a place to stay, so the listing needs fixing. The brief's 2004 'restored' event (repainted, steps repaired by the chapter) could not be verified: the NHLR visit reports show only a 2007 visit, and the FFLA 2004 PDF returned no readable text. It is left out; please check the PDF or drop the event. OregonLive (the story said 'century-old') returned 403 and is not used. Brief elevation 1717.9 m is consistent with NHLR's 1,718 m.

No source describes what remains at the site, and the register's 2017 site photo is not described in the text, so it is not cited. The 1972 sale is listed under this site on the Oregon list, but its 4,680-foot mountain does not match the 6,511-foot register elevation, so the editor should decide whether to keep the sale in the record. The brief's height_m of 207.3 looks like an error; the correction proposes 7.3 for the 1931 platform tower only. Staffing evidence is thin (a 1936 substitute and a 1945 summer job near the lookout). The Bulletin item describes the community of Medical Springs, not the lookout. The August 1972 notice names the site the former Medical Springs Lookout Site. The story no longer says the land is private, and the access level is set to unknown for that reason.

Present-cab year conflicts: register and Wikipedia say 1960, firelookout.com says 1966. Record height_m 2.4 is wrong; proposed 16.2 m from firelookout.com's 53 ft, which may be overall height. firelookout.com also describes a 30-foot Snowshoe lookout a mile east; the story omits it because the sources give little detail. The 2025 staffing is from the register; the 2023 notice is from a local news report. No drive-up or trail information found. No photos gathered.

Brief had no height; 25.0 m is the 82-ft tower per the FFLOS register. The late-1920s tree platform has no exact year, so it is not an event. The register says removed and the Fire Lookout page says destroyed (both 1975). The only site-level detail is a 1936 Forest Service survey station description; whether the mark or any footing survives is unverified. No photos added; the FFLOS 2001 marker photo has no confirmed licence.

The record's status 'gone' conflicts with the Forest Service page, which says the original platform, grown into the tree, can still be seen; firelookout.org's list also shows it as 'Platform Abandoned'. The elevation 5310' appears only in a search snippet from firelookout.com, not in the fetched page, so it is not used. No staffing source found. The Forest Service page is undated, so its condition statement may lag. The trail is public; the tree is retired, and no source encourages climbing it.

Brief height 22.9 m equals the 75-ft 1941 tree lookout and was corrected to the 40-ft tower. The 1948 53-ft tower (Forest Lookouts) and the 1951 40-ft tower (FFLOS, Fire Lookout) conflict; both are reported. The brief note that sources disagree on a tower versus a tree is answered: tree platforms, then towers. The 1934 entry is a secondary lookout point, not the first lookout. No source describes the site today and no current access information was found; the 1968 road reference is historical. No photos added.

Height of the 1953 tower is disputed: register says 40 ft laminated wood, firelookout.com says 50 ft wooden. The record's height_m 15.2 matches firelookout.com only; left as is, not changed. Access (private, no public access) and staffing (into the 2010s) come only from firelookout.com; the register says in active service without a date. Few sources were available, and the searches found no ODF or Wikipedia history. No photos gathered. Treat the access claim as needing confirmation before publishing.

The record's status 'gone' is not supported; firelookout.com says 'Abandoned. Ruins.' The brief's note that firelookout.com says 'standing' does not match the fetched page. Agency conflict: Northwest Oregon FPA (firelookout.com) vs Oregon Department of Forestry (Oregon lookouts history). firelookout.com also says '8 miles southeast of Newhalem', which does not fit Tillamook County (Newhalem is in Washington State), so it is not used. A Facebook group post mentions a 'cabin in ruins' but is social media and is not used. No access, current-condition, or staffing source beyond the 1943 activation date.

Brief height_m 12.2 is kept: it matches the 40-foot tower on the Rex's page; the register and FFLOS say 41 ft (about 12.5 m). Access is not stated by any source, so no access key. Status gone is confirmed by sources 1, 3 and 4. The Rex's page ends with a bare 'Removed' and no date, so no removed event. The Rex's header files the site under Mount Hood National Forest; the register does not. No photos added: no image URLs were captured from the cached pages. The brief's coordinates match the register.

Brief status gone refers to the Fort Klamath site; the tower itself is at Sugarpine Mountain (us-or-sugarpine-mountain may need its own record). height_m 6.1 is 20 ft converted to metres. The register gives 4,200 ft elevation, matching the brief. No access information in any source, so no access key. No photos added: no image URLs were captured. The 1949 Grange Hall reference may describe the same building as the community center platform; the sources do not say so.

Sources conflict on the timeline: the 1936 build and 1938 removal (Forest Lookouts) against a 1940 live-in tower abandoned in the 1940s (firelookout.com). No source describes what remains at the site. The Look-Out building (ARG) is a separate 1937 coffee shop and gift shop beside the Otter Crest viewpoint; no source links it to the fire lookout site. The ARG page is undated, so the 'next spring' reopening cannot be dated. The brief's elevation is not in the facts schema and was left out (firelookout.com gives 420 ft; a Lincoln County index snippet gives 1,200 but was not read on a page). Corrections: none proposed.

Disputed 1926 damage: the register says the cupola burned, Bend newspapers of August 1926 say the lookout tower was destroyed, and a January 1927 report says the tower was not burned but two supports were. The story says the sources disagree. Elevation: the register gives 6,065 ft (the record's 1848.6 m); firelookout.com and the 2021 directory give 6,025 ft. Record matches the register; not changed. Current status: the 2021 visitor wrote that the Forest Service proposed removal; the FS project page (last updated Feb 2025) lists it cancelled, so the removal threat may be over but no current agency statement was found. Access: gated road, not a public visit; the story recommends not climbing. Newspaper transcriptions are on the weebly page and were not checked against original newspaper scans.

Only three pages describe this site, and they agree on the 1953 cab but not on its fate. No construction, staffing or fire history in any source. The 1970s emergency use is in the story but not an event, since the register gives only the decade. Access is not stated; no access key. Do not confuse with Frazier Mountain in Ventura County, California. Coordinates differ: register 45.07619, -117.69498; FFLOS list 45.07974, -117.69300. The brief's record matches the register. No photos added: no image URLs captured.

Six page reads and one search. The brief's height_m of 2.1 is a clear error (100 ft, about 30.5 m) and is proposed as a correction. The brief's 1940 build date comes from the NHLR's ground house sentence and is contradicted by the tower dates of 1936-37 elsewhere. The Roaming Civic history also says a 4-year-old boy fell from a landing and died, attributed to the Fire Lookouts of the Northwest book; it gives no date and no second source, so it is left out of the story. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a Glendale Log item from January 1937 and a Burns Times-Herald item from 1943. Story says the 1930s first site was a point about half a mile away; the sources differ on direction (firelookout says southeast, Cheryl Hill says south). Status: NHLR (2019 survey) and Cheryl Hill (2021) describe the tower as condemned and slated for removal; the July 2026 directory calls the site abandoned but legally accessible and warns its information may be out of date. The tower's current condition after 2022 is unverified. The FFLA Facebook post in the search results was not fetched. No photos added; firelookout.com credits photos to the U.S. Forest Service, National Archives and Records Administration, and Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were extracted.

Brief record confirmed: gone, 30 ft (9.1 m), FFLOS registration December 18, 2010. Build year (1935 vs 1937) and height (30 vs 40 ft) disagree across sources and the story reports both. No source describes the site today or its public access, so access is omitted. Photo credits (Howard Verschoor, Ron Kemnow) appear on the register and firelookout pages but no image URLs were read, so no photos are recorded. Forest Lookouts page cites Medford Mail Tribune and Southwest Oregon District annual reports; those original clippings were not read.

Brief record confirmed: Aermotor design (Forest Lookouts 1931 entry), 72 ft, status gone, FFLOS registration May 20, 2011. Build year (1931 vs 1936) and height (72, 75 or 80 ft) disagree and the story reports both. Access is public through Recreation.gov for the rebuilt cabin, not the tower. Photo credit to Howard Verschoor appears on firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts pages, but no image URLs were read, so no photos are recorded. The Herald and News article on the rebuild was not read because the site returned HTTP 429.

Thin record: two sources give the 1954 trailer and the 1957 removal; Forest Lookouts gives only the location. Brief record confirmed (Grant County, Malheur NF, gone, registered June 23, 2011). Story is short because the evidence is short. No photos recorded. Brief lists kind as mobile; the trailer fits that. No access, height or staffing facts are supported, so none are recorded.

Newspaper items are read from the Rex's Fire Lookout Page transcriptions, not the original papers, which were not checked. Spellings vary (Frissell, Frissel, Frisell, Frizelle). Both registers say the site is gone. Access level is not set: no source says whether the site is open. The last manned year is not stated; the 1967 memo implies the station had been empty for a couple of years. No photo URLs with credits were found. The Frissell Point Facebook video result was not used as a source.

Brief's registration date (Aug 24, 2010) is not in the cached FFLOS text (the date field is blank in extraction), so it is not used here. The FFLOS photo caption 'Building currently on site 10/27/2002' does not say what building it is, so it is not used. Goat Mtn. is not located in any source; WebSearch returned only Goat Mountain pages in other states, none tied to this tower. height_m is 75 ft converted to metres. The 'public' access level rests on a single 2012 visit. Two WebSearch calls used.

Bend Bulletin item is read from the Rex's Fire Lookout Page transcription; the original paper was not checked. The Removed entry on the lookout history has no date, so no removal event is recorded. A 1991 Forest Service eligibility study of Deschutes National Forest lookouts is listed in Oregon's digital collections (https://digitalcollections.library.oregon.gov/nodes/view/275303); it was not read and may describe the site. Access level not set: no source says whether the site is open. Staffing: only the 1932 plan is recorded. No photo URLs with credits were found.

Only two detailed sources, both thin on post-1941 history. No source describes what remains on the ground or whether the site is accessible. Forest Lookouts gives the 1941 staffing and 'Removed' with no date. The Peakbagging table lists 'Game Lake Peak (LO site)' with a 4,401 ft elevation and a 1989 date of unclear meaning; it was not used. The sources do not name a builder. The record's 'ground' kind is supported by the Oregon list's 'Ground' label, but firelookout.com's L-4 cab and cabin wording may suggest a small building rather than a tower; the editor may want to check the kind field. Corrections: none proposed.

The renaming year (1946 on two sites), the end of staffing (1973 in the register, 1960s on firelookout.com) and restoration status all conflict and are reported as such. The brief's L-4 design is kept; the register adds that the cab is an updated BC-301 version. A search snippet from cherylhill.net gives 1944 for the renaming; that page was not read in full, so it is not used. Restoration status is the most likely to be stale and should be rechecked before publishing. Access is marked public for the trail only; the sources do not say whether the cabin can be entered, and the Forest Service warns about its condition, so the story does not encourage entry.

A Living New Deal page on the Camp Reehers fire towers in Tillamook State Forest returned HTTP 403 and was not read; it may mention this site. No staffing or fire information found for Gauldy Mountain, so none is given. The register's panorama and 2009 site photo have no image URLs in the cached text, so no photos are added. Access level not set: no source says whether the site is open.

Status conflict: FFLOS and firelookout.com say the tower is gone, but a July 2020 blog describes an abandoned, closed, decaying lookout about a third of a mile up an old road from the Palisade Rocks trailhead (NF-012). Whether it is the same structure is unknown from these sources; worth checking before changing status. Brief access 'unknown' is set to closed on the blog's word only. Brief height 3.7 m does not match the 10-foot tower. The 1926 summit lookout may or may not be the 1930 lookout.

Unresolved: 1934 tower height (66 ft in a 1934 newspaper vs 50 ft on firelookout.com). Rebuild year 1968 (NHLR, 1968 report) vs 1969 (firelookout.com, 1969 report); the 1968 and 1969 reports both describe the same winter, so the year depends on how the reports count. Staffing 'every summer' comes from an undated page; the latest dated staffing in the pages read is 1965. No rental information found. Record access 'unknown' can be set to private (NHLR and firelookout.com agree).

Thin evidence: three sources, two of which are short directory entries, and no source describes the site today. The brief's access 'permission' is not stated by any source we read, so access is not changed; the editor should decide whether to keep it. The brief's built year 1930 is stated by no source; the correction proposes the decade. Two searches turned up no further history.

Brief access 'unknown' is set to private per FFLOS and firelookout.com. Brief built year 1931 and agency Private are confirmed. Tower year and height conflict across sources; the story says so. Most history comes from newspaper and Forest Service material quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not from the originals. The register's 1935 National Archives panoramas and other photos were not added because no image URLs were extracted.

Main open question is status. firelookout.org (FFLA list) marks the tower Standing* (cab gone); Rex's page says it fell over in 2003; CherylHill lists Unknown, not standing as the brief said. The FFLOS detail page is a former-sites register and does not say the tower is gone. Height is 100 ft in two sources and 90 and 82 ft in 1936 records. The sale year conflicts (1977 via Rex's quote of an ODF report vs 1984 auction). The 1970 replacement plan has no record of happening. The cab removal date is not recorded. Staffing as_of is the last dated personnel record, 1954. A 1937 warden item on Rex's page concerns the Glass Mountain lookout, not Glass Hill, so it was dropped. No photos or recent visit reports were checked; no new photos added.

Heights disagree across six sources; height_m is proposed as 25.0 (82 ft from the 1951 rebuild) against the record's 21.3 m, which is the 1949 70-ft figure. Firelookout.com also gives a 1952 '20 ft L-4 tower' that no other source confirms; it was left out. Whether the 1967 steel tower and the 1985 timber tower are the same structure is not stated, so the story does not link them beyond the Frog Lake record. The Oregon list's 'gone' status conflicts with the July 16, 1985 entry; the editor may want to re-check the status field. No source describes staffing or fires at this site. Two online forum threads were seen in search results but not read, so the story makes no claim from them about current towers or access. Ownership is from a 1953 survey note and may be out of date. The 'today' section is limited to 1985 as the latest description.

Thin record: both lookout sources restate one short description (1950s platform and trailer quarters, gone by 1959). No staffing, access, visit or remains information was found, so those keys are omitted. Brief elevation 342.9 m matches the register's 343 m and firelookout's 1,125 ft. Coordinates match the register. Wikipedia is used only for the firefinder definition. An anyplaceamerica summit listing for 'Gobblers Knob' in Lincoln County returned HTTP 403 and was not used, so it is unconfirmed whether that summit is this site.

Sources disagree on tower height (40 ft register vs 34 ft firelookout.com), on the build year (1953 newspaper item announces construction two years after the register's 1951), and on the end year (1962 removal vs 1965 abandonment). Hiking guide elevation 3,054 ft differs from the register's 3,052 ft. The guide's user reports are undated. No staffing information was found. The register page credits photos to the Howard Verschoor collection, but image URLs were not returned by fetch_text, so none are listed. Brief record dates (1951 built, 1962 removed, 2019 registered) match the register.

Main issue: the register and firelookout.com date the lookout to 1935, but 1924 and 1925 newspaper items quoted on the Oregon lookouts site describe a Gold Mountain fire lookout earlier. Not resolved. Record coordinates (42.85302, -123.79253) match the register; the brief notes a conflicting West US lookouts position (42.8461, -123.7911), which was not checked here. The weebly page calls the agency 'Coos County Fire Patrol' and has a 'Removed' field with no date, so no removal cause is given. No design, access or remains information found, so those keys are omitted. No photos found.

Elevation conflict: brief/NHLR give 4,477 ft (1,365 m), Recreation.gov gives 4,618 ft. Left out of story text since it's a minor figure; see corrections entry. Fact-check 2026-10-04: all three citations re-fetched and verified verbatim against the live sources, including the Recreation.gov Directions section ('last 2 miles of road access are rough gravel and dirt at a 10 percent uphill grade'), which backs the story's 'rough gravel roads' detail though it falls outside the short evidence quote on file. No unsupported claims or citation errors found; no edits needed to the story text.

Access left unset: no source gives an access level, and the brief's 'unknown' is not a valid enum value. A Forest Service Gold Hill trailhead listing turned up in search, but the cached page is a generic recreation index and a WebFetch redirect went to the same index, so no current access or site condition was found. The register page (firetower.org, source 2) does list 'Date Registered May 7, 2011', so the fflos_registered event is included (an earlier note said the date was not found). The summit's current condition is undescribed in every source read.

The access level 'restricted' is a judgment from the Forest Service trail page, which lists a seasonal closure to all users (January 1 to July 31) and a Bedrock Fire impact. The trail page was last updated August 12, 2025. The height correction from 27.4 m to 8.5 m is proposed; the record's 27.4 m matches only the 1924 tree. Distance from Oakridge is 14 to 15 miles across the sources (see resolved_conflicts).

Height disagrees across sources (60, 66, 100 ft); the brief's 2.1 m was wrong and is corrected to 18.3 m. Brief's cherylhill=standing claim is wrong: the 2012 post and table both say Abandoned. Cab-loss year differs (2007-08 vs 2008). The brief's alternate coordinate (west_us_lookouts) was not checked. Status rests on the undated firelookout.org list and a 2012 visit; no later check found. Staffing 'abandoned' as_of 2012 is from the CherylHill table. No new photos added. Access 'public' is the CherylHill table's accessibility column; the tower itself is abandoned and the story advises against climbing.

No source gives an access level or describes the site today, so facts.access is omitted. The brief's height_m of 15.2 m (50 ft) is proposed for correction to 12.5 m (41 ft, the 1954 tower). A peakery.com search snippet gave 1,621 ft for the summit; it is not used because it conflicts with the register's 1,826 ft and is not a lookout source.

Only two sources, which disagree on build decade and elevation. The firelookout.org index lists this site at 42.44456, -123.30929, a different point several kilometres from the register's coordinates (42.499609, -123.369304) that the record uses; the index lists only FFLOS US 1816, OR 539 for it, so the brief's shared-register note is not confirmed. No source says what remains or whether the ODF office grounds are open. Staffing is not stated anywhere we read. firelookout.com's 'wooden' is not in the register. One WebSearch found nothing specific to this tower; its hits were other southern Oregon lookouts, not used. The corrections block proposes a current built year of 1930, but the tower record's built field is null, so that correction is left for human review.

Built year (1934 vs 1935), the 1950/1951 tower and its height (40 ft FFLOS vs 42 ft Forest Lookouts), and the removal year (1968 vs 1969) are unresolved source disagreements; the story reports them. Current access and ownership of the site are not described by any official source; the Summit Post report is user-written. Brief elevation 1100.9 m matches FFLOS 1,101 m, so no correction. Brief has no design or height, which are now filled from sources.

The 1986 move is disputed: FFLOS and firelookout.com say the tower moved; Forest Lookouts says the move failed and salvaged parts built the Warner Ridge tower. Not resolved; both are reported. Brief height_m 15.2 is corrected to 12.5. No source describes the original summit today. The Warner Ridge lookout is a replica on a 40-ft tower (Recreation.gov); its name differs between sources (Warner Ridge Lookout vs Warner Mountain Lookout). Warner Ridge availability and rental status were not checked live. Firelookout.com's Warner page is an enthusiast site; Recreation.gov is the official rental listing.

Oregon Hikers is a volunteer field guide (contributor bobcat), not an official record. Its 1958 build and 1970s decommission conflict with the register and Forest Lookouts (gone by 1968); the 1958 structure may be a later cabin, which we could not confirm. Forest disagreement (Willamette vs Umpqua) unresolved. Brief elevation 1719.7 m (5642 ft) and design L-5 match the register; no correction. No official source describes the summit today. Trail data is from the hiking listing only and was not checked on the ground; the story does not give directions.

Brief design D-6 covers only the 1925 cupola; corrected in corrections. Height 3.0 m is the 10 ft tower. The FFLOS register lists the date registered as December 19, 2010, so a 2010 registration event is included. A second Forest Lookouts page (grasshopper-mountain.html, 1938 and 1941 staffing) appeared only in search snippets and was not read, so it is not used. Access is public per the Forest Service trail page, which notes wilderness rules. No photos with stable image URLs were found.

Height and end date conflict across sources; the story gives both. Access 'public' is inferred from Mount Hood National Forest land and the hiking guide's route, not from a closure statement. The hiking guide shows no date in the fetched text. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced. Brief's 21.9 m height is the 72 ft figure only.

Brief kind 'ground' fits the 1941 cabin, but the earliest structure was a 1931 tree tower or crow's nest, so the brief's kind may need a 'tree' note. No height, access or current-condition source was found, so those keys are left out. The Forest Lookouts 'Removed' line has no date, so no removal event. The panorama is credited to National Archives Pacific Northwest Region in the register text, but no image URL was fetched, so no photos entry. Two WebSearch-style searches returned no description of the site today.

The brief's 3.7 m height matches the 12-foot tower in the Oregon Lookouts note, while the FFLOS and firelookout.com pages describe a 10x10 ft cab; I kept 3.7 m as the height. Build year (1934 vs 1935) and incident year (1942 vs the June 1943 newspaper date) are unresolved. The Oregon Lookouts page is a compiled history with dated extracts, so its year labels may be off. The access note rests on the Oregon Hikers description; no official access source was checked. The brief's events list is otherwise accurate.

Thin record: two short site pages and one index line. The 1916 cabin and the 1940s abandonment rest on firelookout.com alone; the 1912 alidade and the removal rest on the Rex page. Not used, because they belong to other records: the Douglas County Green Butte (Umpqua NF, 31S-3W-25; the 1932-1945 items on oregonlookouts.weebly.com/green-butte2.html) and the Lake County Green Butte (a 2022-23 visit reported on theroamingcivic.com; FFLOS US 2057, OR 570). Thinnest of the three. The only history is one firelookout.com line and the FFLA entry (Crowsnest, Abandoned). The Forest Lookouts page gives only the name and 3S-7E-15, so it is not cited. Core dates (1931 first lookout, 1998 current structure, 2003 register) agree across all three pages. Open: staffing and whether the cab is open to visitors are not established by any page read. A search snippet suggested a 1913 telephone line and an earlier cabin; the full page was not read, so it is not used. The brief's record of a 1998 build is correct for the present tower but omits the 1931 original.

The brief's height_m 30.5 m matches the 1939 100-ft tower; kept. No source describes the summit today, so access is unknown. The Forest Lookouts site quotes district annual reports and newspapers secondhand. One web search turned up no further Lenhart Butte sources.

The brief has no height, and no source gives one, so none is recorded. No staffing source was found. Thin record: three short pages, all agreeing on 1936 and the 1940s. Two web searches found no other Limber Jim sources; a 1936 Kirkland guard station that came up is unrelated and not used. Access is unknown; no source describes the site today.

Site today: no source read describes remains or public status. A Forest Service trail page (fs.usda.gov recarea, recid 63838, actid 50) appeared in search with a snippet saying the lookout is gone and the trail leads to the former site, but the cached page did not contain that text, so it is not quoted. An editor who can read that page could add a site-today sentence. The ORWW Osbornes Project page for Little Black Rock (orww.org/Osbornes_Project/Douglas/Little_Black_Rock/index.html) mentions 2010 documentary photos of current conditions but no text on remains. A 1933 item on the Oregon Lookouts page plans a 10 x 10 CCC lookout; it is not clearly this site, so it is left out. The panorama date differs (August 5, 1936 on the Oregon Lookouts page, August 7 on the ORWW index), so it is not used. No photos added: no image URLs were read.

No source describes the site today, so the story says so; access is left out. The register's scanned Dean Norman PDF (firetower.org/media/4205/dean-norman-book.pdf, 29 pages) has no text layer and no OCR tool is installed, so it was not read or quoted; it may cover the 1953 period. Brief's elevation (1618.8 m) matches the register's 1,619 m and is not changed. Two WebSearch calls used.

Current access and staffing rest on the Forest Service page (undated in our copy; treated as 2026). The 2004 restoration rests only on Oregon Hikers, a volunteer-edited wiki; the 2004 scanned report cited in the brief (firelookout.org cr-or-2004.pdf) has no text layer and could not be machine-checked, so it is not used. The brief's 2004 rental-program claim comes from that same PDF and is omitted; no source read mentions a rental program. Firelookout.com also gives elevation 4255 ft; search snippets (not read as pages) also show 4,236 ft (Oregon Hikers) and 4243 ft (Outerspatial). The story reports only the register and Forest Service figures. The Bedrock Fire is named with no date (none found in sources read), so the story gives no year. The brief record's elevation_m 1215.5 matches the register. The brief record had only the 1960 build; the 1923 cupola and 1967 standby events are added from the register.

Brief's kind 'two_story' is not supported by the sources read: the register calls it a flattop 14x14 lookout and Cheryl Hill calls it a ground cabin; firelookout.org's list says '2-Story cab' but was not cited. Brief's height_m 4.3 has no supporting source in the pages read, so it is not in facts. Elevation in the brief matches the register. Forest Lookouts' 'Waldo Mountain' versus 'Waldo Hill' is unresolved beyond the register and Rex's agreeing on Waldo Hill. Two ODF or Forest Service pages were not checked.

No source read describes what remains at Little Hebo or Table Mountain today, or whether either is open to visitors. No staffing history was found for Little Hebo, so none is written. The FFLOS page calls the destination 'Table Lookout'; the Table Mountain sources name Table Mountain in Lincoln County, and the story uses that name. An ORWW Osbornes Project PDF on Table Mountain (Kemnow, 2020) confirms 'The lookout was removed' in 1973; it was not cited because the Oregon Lookouts page carries the same line. Oregon Digital (Siuslaw National Forest Collection, item pc289j289) has a Little Hebo Lookout image that was not opened, so no photo is added. The Table Mountain page quotes a 1958 Lincoln FPA annual report that calls the tower reassembled there 'a wooden tower' ('It is a wooden tower'); no story claim relies on it, but it bears on the steel-or-wooden conflict and is not cited here.

Height conflict: register and firelookout.com say 20 feet; the 1937 item says 10 feet; the brief's 15.2 m (50 ft) traces to the 1934 proposal and is corrected above. No source read describes the site today or public access. Two web searches found nothing about the current site. The ORWW Osbornes Project page for Live Oak Mountain (orww.org/Osbornes_Project/Douglas/Live_Oak_Mountain/index.html) returned 404. Staffing comes from one history site that quotes local newspapers; the 1957 and 1962 items are the latest named staff. 'Douglas FPA' is not expanded in the story because no source read spells it out.

Sources disagree on 1969: FFLOS and firelookout.com say removed, Forest Lookouts and onX say it burned after arson. The 1926 build year is consistent across all sources. The 1919 lookout's structure is undescribed. The Warner Ridge tower (about 2 miles SW) has its own record (us-or-warner-mountain); its Grass Mountain framework claim rests on firelookout.com, and the Grass Mountain record notes that sources differ on whether the frame moved. Access comes from onX, a trail app, not an agency page; no Forest Service closure notice was checked. The record's design field is null; 'D-6 cupola cabin' (FFLOS) is recorded under facts.design. No record corrections proposed.

The register's '20' pole' is read as the tower height (6.1 m); the register does not say whether 20 ft is the cab or the pole height. The fate follows the 1963 Oregonian report as quoted by Forest Lookouts; the register (removed 1964) and firelookout.com (destroyed 1964) disagree. Today's remains rest on one hiking guide's photos (WillhiteWeb); no official source describes the site now. Coordinates and elevation match the record (register: N 45.340720, W 121.712480; 2,012 m). The WillhiteWeb page gives walking access (Magic Mile lift and hike down the road, or the access road from Timberline Lodge). The story now mentions this in one sentence and states that no source found says whether the public may visit; the step-by-step route is not in the story.

Thin sources. The 1933 build year and L-4 design agree across the register and Forest Lookouts; removal date is unknown in all sources read. The 1948 entry calls the site 'Long Creek Mountain' and may or may not be this lookout; it is included with that caveat. The 1936 survey description is historical; no current survey recovery note was found (the NGS datasheet fetch returned only a listing). No staffing or fire history was found, so none is written. The site today is undescribed in every source read.

The link between the Tiptop tower's 2016 buyer (a Fire Lookout Association member planning a family ranch on the Imnaha River) and the Long Ridge site is inferred. No source states it outright, so the story says so; the buyer is not named in the story. The 2016 Lookout Network item is only known second-hand through cherylhill.net; the original was not read. The facebook post from Oregon Department of Forestry about Long Ridge was not read (not cached). Height is not in any source read, so height_m is omitted. Access: a fire lookout listing says private, no public access; the NHLR has no access note. Photo candidates not added: NHLR and firelookout.com both credit a 2016 photo to Rex Kamstra, licence unknown, no image URL retrieved. Record's agency 'Land Owner' is kept as 'Private landowner' in facts.

Demolition is in the Forest inventory and the Forest Lookouts newspaper item; firelookout.com gives only Columbus Day 1962, so no exact day is recorded. The 1963 transfer year is inferred from Quail Prairie's construction date; the Forest Lookouts page does not date the transfer, so treat the 1963 'replaced' event as approximate. The FFLA entry for Quail Prairie carries an asterisk that the list does not explain; the story reports 'standing' without the asterisk. A Facebook history post surfaced in search but was not read or cited.

Thinnest of the three. Only three pages and one quoted report; two WebSearches gave no new source. The 1936 start date rests on the Forest Lookouts quote; the original report was not located. The 'permission' access level follows from reservation land, not from a published visitor policy. The Lookout Butte on the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest (fs.usda.gov, Idaho) is a different tower and was not used. The record's 13.7 m height matches the 45-foot figure. A removal date and a site description may sit in reservation or tribal records; not searched.

Build year (1932 vs 1942) and height (40 vs about 60 ft) conflict across sources; the brief height of 18.3 m is proposed as a correction to 12.2 m. No source describes the site today. Search results for Lookout Butte mostly return an unrelated rentable tower in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest, Idaho, which is not this site. No new photos taken from the fetched text: the register photo caption (2007, Ron Kemnow) has no image URL in our fetched text.

Height correction is the main fix to the brief (18.3 m is the 1935 tower). Heights for the present tower differ across sources (82, 87, 90 ft). Location and elevation differ between the brief and the register; not changed. The 1947 newspaper plan gave 83 ft and was not confirmed as built at that height. Walla Walla ranger district office or Umatilla NF recreation page not read; they may confirm current staffing and access.

Three sources disagree on the 1938 tower's material, height and whether any tower stands now. The Removed tag on the Forest Lookouts page sits under the 1965 entry and may refer to the portable cab rather than the whole site. No access or current-condition source was found, and no ODF page was read. The 1938 Forest Log item was used only for the lookout's name; its medical detail was left out. The firelookout.com entry itself is short (R.I.P. 1938-?, 34 ft steel, 1965 crank-up replacement).

Thin record: three listings, no structure details, no height, no photos, no staffing or access information. The 1930s date is given without a year, so no built year is recorded. Lane County, Willamette NF and the 3 mi north of McKenzie Bridge location agree across firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page; the index coordinates match the brief. The 2023 Lookout Fire appears in the story only as a hedged sentence: the McKenzie Bridge community center says lightning hit a Lookout Mountain about 4 mi NE of town, and the Andrews timeline dates the start to Saturday, August 5, 2023, but neither source ties it to this lookout site, so no fire event is recorded. A different, standing Lookout Mountain (82 ft tower, elevation 5,229 ft, reached via Road 370) appeared in search results on cherylhill.net and was not used because it is not this gone site.
