Brief design D-6 is only the 1924 cupola cabin; the proposed correction gives the 1949 L-4 tower. The 1966 abandonment date conflicts with the 1972 letter describing use; the story reports both. No source describes the site today. The register photo captions (1948, 1956) have no image URLs in the fetched text, so no photos are added.

The 10-foot dimension in the sources is ambiguous (platform, live-in tower, or tower height), so no height_m is given. The register gives no removal date. No source describes the site today. Brief elevation 1988.8 m agrees with the register's 1,989 m. No photos added; register photo captions have no image URLs in the fetched text.

Thin record. The register, firelookout.com and the Rex page are the only pages with detail; the statewide list adds the gone status only. Two web searches found nothing on what remains today, so the story says no source describes the site now. The brief's access 'unknown' is left unfilled. A Deschutes NF historic-lookout eligibility study (digitalcollections.library.oregon.gov, node 275303) came up in search, but its PDF was not read; it may cover this site.

Two strong sources (the register and firelookout.com) agree on the 1931 pole L-4 tower; the Rex page only confirms removal and gives the survey location. No source describes what remains on the summit today. The access level 'public' is inferred from the Oregon Hikers hike listing, not stated by any source, so treat it as medium confidence. The Oregon Hikers page is for this summit by title and location; the Umatilla NF Lookout Mountain (oregonlookouts lookout-mountain4) is a different site and was not used. The brief's height is not in any source as metres, so no height_m was set.

The richest of the three. Newspaper items come from the Oregon Lookouts page, which reproduces them from several local papers; the story cites that page, not the original papers. The 1912 build instruction is a 1930 retrospective quote, so it is marked 'other' rather than 'built'. The brief's height_m 3.4 is unsupported and is proposed for removal. The register's photo captions (1912, 1925, 1942) have no image URLs in the cache, so no photos were added. Today's remains come from the Oregon Hikers field guide only; no official source describes the foundations.

Thin record: two register and index entries, with no staffing, fire, access or present-condition source. A web search on Wallowa-Whitman lookouts found nothing on this site. The 1930 event year is a decade placeholder. firelookout.com's 'may not have been used, possible proposed site' note sits against the register's 'now gone', which does not conflict but leaves the original cab's existence uncertain. The brief's 'ground' kind and the 2011 FFLOS registration match the register.

Three sources describe the site. The register and firelookout.com agree on the 1933 cabin, 1934 pole tower, 1964 tower and 1967 fire loss. The Weebly 1932 build date, the 1963 annual report and the 1954 personnel history do not match them and are flagged. The brief's height_m of 15.2 is the 1934 pole tower; the 82-foot tower is 25.0 m. No photo or access source was read; the Fire Lookout Museum photo credit on firelookout.com was not checked.

Current condition rests on one July 2024 visitor blog. No 2025-26 source was read. Forest Service pages were not fetched; a Fremont-Winema trailhead page appeared in search and was not read. The 1931, 1932 and 1947 newspaper items are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. Unresolved: the 1932 Bend Bulletin item says the legs were sixteen feet high, while later sources say the tower was 20 ft; the story says the sources differ. Photos not added: no image URL with a confirmed license.

Four sources agree on the 1920s tower, the 1962 storm loss and the burned cabin. FFLOS and firelookout.com agree on 1915, the 1932 L-4 cab and gone by 1966. Oregon Hikers gives 1916 and the 1914 newspaper item points earlier; both flagged. The Oregon Hikers route tags say 'Closed' with no explanation; check Mt. Hood NF notices before publishing the access line. Not verified on the ground. No licensed photo found.

Sources agree the tower is gone and the cabin ended up at Tower Mountain, a separate summit with its own 1935 tower. No source read describes the Lucky Strike site itself today; firelookout.com's list only covers 1936-37 staff. A geocache page for the site and a Roaming Civic Tower Mountain post were seen only as search snippets and are not cited.

No staffing names found for Lutsey Point, so staffing is omitted. The only description of the site today is one visitor's May 2026 blog post; it is cited as such. The access note is an inference from the blog's walk up a road it calls closed, so check Ochoco NF status before publishing the access line.

Three sources agree on the 1934 build (or the 1933 plan) and the removal around 1960, but they disagree on the word removed or destroyed. No staffing record was found in these sources, so staffing is omitted. No source describes the site today, so access is omitted. The register photo caption 'Mace Mountain Lookout 1933 - 1965' is left as an unresolved conflict with the 1960 date; the editor may want to check the photo's source. The brief's 2011 FFLOS registration date was not visible in the register text read, so it is not repeated. The 1950s abandonment is given only as a decade, so the year 1950 in events is a placeholder. The record's height_m 1.8 is not supported by any page read. NHLR photo credits (1940 and 1955 Forest Service) are not added as new finds.

Brief's NHLR registration date (July 4, 2022) was not in the NHLR text I read, so no nhlr_registered event is recorded; the NHLR page was read only for location, elevation, build and design. Registry numbers US 1632 / OR 150 and the Standing status appear on the Forest Fire Lookout Association standing list (read during the McGraw task; not cited as evidence here). Search snippets mentioned a 2024 trailhead closure and a 2023 staffed trip report; neither was read, so neither is in the story. A 1981 helicopter accident at the lookout site (quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) is omitted for length. Reads: 5 pages plus one re-read of the Forest Lookouts page; 2 web searches.

Elevation in the brief (2,382.9 m) matches the register's 2,383 m; FFLOS registration date May 11, 2011 matches the register. The removal date conflict (1955 burning vs 1958 removal) is unresolved in the sources and is reported in the story. The summit condition relies on a single undated photo caption ('Metal parts of lookout remain') from a hiking guide. The 1908 observation use and the 1920 first camp are both reported as the sources give them.

The only support for the relocation is the FFLA Oregon table row 'Boardman Airport (Relocated Malheur NWR) Morrow 45.81523 -119.80168 Beacon Tower Standing'. Ownership, access and current condition unknown. Suggest contacting the Port of Morrow and Malheur NWR staff.

Thin record: the only dates (1930 crow's nest and cabin, abandoned 1935) come from firelookout.com; the Forest Lookouts page has no dates. County conflict is real: firelookout.com and the Oregon index say Polk; the Forest Lookouts page lists it under Columbia County with the Columbia County FPA and Oregon Department of Forestry. The brief's coordinates (45.8121, -123.12287) match the Oregon index; the west_us_lookouts point (45.8195, -123.117) was not in any source read, so that location conflict is not resolved here. The 1930 entry is read as the built date, which is an inference from the listing. Vernonia Eagle newspaper hits from 1930 and 1941 gave nothing on this site. The brief's built year (1961) and removal year (2010) match the register and firelookout.com. The annual-report sequence (materials 1959, construction 1960) suggests the build may be 1960, so the editor may want to choose between 1960 and 1961 for the infobox. The staffing end is 2006 in two sources and 2007 in one. No source describes what remains at the site today, and no access information was found, so access is omitted. Search results for the 2010 burning were unrelated (a California fire of the same name) and were not used.

Name conflict: the register calls this Marion Peak; the hiking guide calls the viewpoint Marion Mountain and says it is not Marion Peak to the south. The register coordinates in the record (44.54775, -121.8804) are within about 10 m of the guide's point (44.54774, -121.88047), so the editor should confirm whether the register site is the Marion Mountain viewpoint. Removal date conflicts: c.1964 (Kemnow) versus 1965 (register, Kamstra). The register's FFLOS registration date (May 11, 2011, from the record) was not checked on the page. No staffing or fire sources found. Access is inferred from the hiking guide only.

Three sources agree on county, forest and the 'gone' or 'abandoned' fate. The date is the weak point: firelookout.com gives only '1930s: unknown', so no built year is recorded. The 1940 Record-Courier item (quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) says Neal Taylor would be placed at the site once a house was built, but the page does not say whether that happened, so the story states only the plan and no later staffing. Elevation 6,535 ft comes from firelookout.com only. The brief's coordinates (45.09072, -118.2183) match the Oregon index row (-118.21830). No photos, height or access information found. Budget: 1 WebSearch round plus the second round; about 4 page reads.

Dates for the first structure conflict across sources: 1933 (register, Kamstra), a July 1937 station opening (Gazette-Times via Kemnow), and 1942 CCC construction (BPA). The register says the 1959 tower was destroyed in 1962; the BPA says the log structure was demolished and replaced by 1959; Kamstra's span is 1933 to 1959. The record's kind 'tower' fits the 1959 structure, but the earliest structure was a log cabin. The Benton County museum page (hbd.bentoncountymuseums.org) timed out and was not read. Trail, road and parking details come from a visitor blog and may be out of date. The BPA summit description may also be dated.

Removal conflict: the register and Kemnow say removed in 1965, Kamstra says destroyed in 1965. The 1962 vandalism report is the only account of damage; no source describes the 1965 event itself. Staffing evidence is a single 1939 newspaper item. The Oregon Hikers and Forest Service pages were read for access and do not describe the summit today. The guide's 6,229 ft elevation and the 1939 item's 6,225 ft differ by a few feet; the record's 1898.6 m is consistent with either.

Rodeo Butte (other name in the record) is not confirmed as this site. The oregonlookouts item places the 1943 tower in the Klamath FPA area near Bly; the register puts McCartie Ranch in Lake County 9 miles north of Bly. Build year is decade-only. No access level found in any source read; visit fields left out. Search returned only a Montana McCart lookout, which was not used. The three cited sources do not link Rodeo Butte to McCartie Ranch; the register page does not mention Rodeo.

Record agency reads 'U.S.Forest Service' on the register page; normalised to 'U.S. Forest Service'. firelookout.com spells the town 'Chemault' (Chemult is the usual spelling); the story does not use it. The 1939 date is approximate per Forest Lookouts. Staffing after the 1943 appointment is unknown. The register lists a 1948 Curtis family photo (courtesy Ron Kemnow collection); no image URL was found, so no photo entry. No source describes the site now, and one web search was run and it added no usable page beyond the register and firelookout.com.

Brief's registration date (July 4, 2022) and registry numbers US 1633 / OR 151 are confirmed on the NHLR page. Brief's height_m of 3.0 is wrong; corrected to 25.0. No access level is recorded: no source read says whether the public can visit or climb the tower, so the access key is omitted. A search snippet mentioned a Hells Canyon MVUM legend with a Cabin Rental entry near Imnaha; it was not tied to McGraw and was not read, so it is not used. Reads: 4 pages (NHLR, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, FFLA standing list); 2 web searches.

Build date conflict: 1941 (register and Firelookout.com) vs first built and manned about 1926 (Oregon history page); the story says the sources do not explain the gap. End date conflict: removed or destroyed 1964 vs a July 1966 closing item. The record's kind 'ground' fits a cabin on the ground. Access not found in any source read, so no access or visit facts. One web search returned a Wolf Mountain Lookout Site snippet with 1941 and 1964 dates; it names a different site and was not used.

Only two pages describe this lookout, and the Forest Lookouts entry is a one-line listing with a 1938 panorama date. Elevation 5,253 ft (about 1,601 m) is not in facts; the record's elevation_m is null and could take it. The 'Ron Kemnow photo' caption (July 2007) appeared only in a search snippet, not on the fetched page, so it is not used. Most dated facts come from one compiled page (Forest Lookouts), which quotes a 1948 Coos Bay Times item, an August 1948 Forest Log item, a 1948 Oregon Department of Forestry report and a 1949 Coos Bay Times item. Thin record. Three short listings agree the tower is gone (or removed) and give the 1937 build; no source gives a removal year, cause, staffing, fires, or any description of the site today, so the story says only what the register says. Status and dating rest on undated or old notes: firelookout.com's 'Still there' has no date, and the most recent dated report is 2001 in a local list. The 1936 cab date rests on the register alone. Brief elevation_m 460.9 (about 1,512 ft) disagrees with TopoQuest's 1368 ft MSL (about 417 m); the source of the brief value was not checked, so the brief is unchanged. No source read describes the site today or public access. Register gives 4,913 ft (1,497 m), matching the brief's 1497.5 m. Thin record: the register and firelookout.com give only 'the 1930s' for the build, and no source read gives staffing, access or the site today. The brief's height (24.4 m) is the original 80-ft tower; corrected to 120 ft. The construction date is disputed: 1933 in the register and firelookout.com, 1935-1937 in the Forest Service reports quoted by Forest Lookouts. Access level is left out: a 2022 visit lists drive-up access, but no source read says who controls the land now. A Herald and News column (heraldandnews.com, 'What's the point at Modoc Point?') reportedly says its writers found no evidence of an old lookout; the fetch returned HTTP 429, so it is not cited. The brief's agency and access fields are not corrected; the agency conflict is recorded above. No new photos found.

Identity of the Forest Lookouts 'Bald Mountain' with the register's Monmouth Bald is inferred from the Polk County location and the shared 1947 40-foot tower, not stated in any source. Removal (1969, Forest Lookouts) and abandonment (1971, Register and firelookout.com) dates conflict and are unresolved. The 1942 inspection and 1941 pole tower do not line up cleanly; the 1942 inspection's post is not named on the page, though it sits in the Bald Mountain history. The 1943 memo on that page mentions a 'Monmouth cabin' and Fanno posts, which may be the same station and was not used. Access level is unknown; no source describes the site now or public access. Access to the site was not confirmed. No photos found. Brief's height_m 27.4 corrected to 12.2.

Brief's height_m 15.2 (50 ft) is the 1945 plan, not the built tower; corrected to 55 ft, with 52 ft from the 1947 district report noted as a conflict. Build year: Forest Lookouts shows construction in 1946, Register says 1947. Staffing: Forest Lookouts history stops at 1966 and does not confirm the 1978 last-staffed date, which comes from the Register and firelookout.com only. Access is recorded as closed based on 'There is no public access' (Register and firelookout.com); the brief's 'unknown' should be updated to match. The brief's elevation (1181.4 m) matches the Register's 1,181 m. No source describes what remains at the site. No new photos with URLs found.

Start date conflicts: Forest Lookouts shows an alidade about 1914; the Register and firelookout.com start with a camp in 1916; both are recorded and not resolved. Kind 'ground' kept: the sources describe a lookout house or cabin with an L-4 cab on the summit, not a tower. Access level unknown: no source says whether the site is open. No source we read describes what remains at the site. The 1964 storage facility and the 1946 concrete base are the only physical details and their current status is not described. Location distance: firelookout.com gives 8 miles WSW of Detroit and a 1942 newspaper says 10 miles east of Gates; not reconciled. No height in the brief and none found, so no height_m. Staffing as_of 1973 is inferred from removal; last documented staffing is 1956 (Simons). No photos with URLs found.

Brief record checks out: BLM, Malheur County, status gone. Two other Oregon Monument Peaks exist (Linn County, 44.69848 -122.32734, FFLOS US 978; and the Rex page's Linn County entry); do not merge. Access is unknown and no current access source was found. Staffing dates come from newspapers and one personnel list. The 1965 survey mark is on the southern, highest of the Jones Buttes about 30 ft northeast of the lookout, not at the peak's highest point, so the story says so. The 2015 Ron Kemnow photo credit on the Rex page has no image URL, so no photo was added. The one web search returned only a Montana Monument Peak, which was not used.

Built year 1930 comes from the register alone; Firelookout.com only says 'the 1930s'. Abandonment in 1969 is in two sources. No design, height, staffing or fire record found in the sources read. What, if anything, remains at the site is unknown. Access is by the Forest Service trail; the record's access 'unknown' can be updated to public.

Elevation conflict, not resolved: the register gives 7,180 ft (2,188 m), which matches the record's elevation_m; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 7,234 ft (about 2,205 m). Origin site is disputed: the Round Pass record (US 1040) gives 7,462 ft at the pass, while Cheryl Hill places the earlier cabin on Round Mountain, also 7,462 ft. The 2020 Brattain Fire is mentioned only by the 2024 staffer; the fire itself was not checked, and a search turned up Paisley news reports that were not read. Staffing and access rest on a July 2024 visit and an undated firelookout.com page; nothing newer was found. Weebly page read only in targeted lines.

Sources disagree on abandonment: the register says 1959; Firelookout.com says 'Abandoned 1960s' and lists named lookouts through 1967. Not resolved by the sources read. Forest Lookouts gives 'Removed' with no date. Record kind 'platform' matches the cabin-on-platform description. Access and current remains are unknown; no source read describes them. Web search budget ran out before a Forest Service or history source on removal was found.

Dates for build (1922) and removal (1959) agree across register and chronology. Firelookout.com's 'abandoned 1942' matches the chronology's end of use in 1942. The chronology's staffing entries come from newspaper reports it quotes; the name is spelled Ali in 1938 and Al in 1939. The Oregon Lookouts page also lists 1908-1913 references to an 'Ashland Butte' lookout; that is a different summit and is left out. The page's 1952 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description is for a station about a mile south of Ashland city centre, not the mountain, so it is left out. Access and current remains are unknown; the Wikipedia ski-area line is a lead only. Record's access 'unknown' stays until a Forest Service source is found.

Brief access 'unknown' changed to public because a Forest Service trail to the summit is listed; the trail page does not describe the lookout site. No source read describes what remains on the summit today, so the story says so. The 1917 'established' date (ORWW) is treated as the first staffing, not the cabin date. Newspaper quotes are as reproduced on the Oregon lookouts site, not the original papers. No corrections proposed; the brief's status 'gone' and D-6 design fit the sources. Checked 2026-10-09: the 1921 temporary station was only planned (the July 1921 report says it 'will be provided'), so the story and event now say planned; the telephone line date rests on a January 28, 1922 report that says 'Last year'.

The brief's design D-6 (height 3.0 m) matches the 1928 cab on a 10-foot tower; the final 1955 structure was a 10-foot L-4 tower, so the correction adds it rather than replacing the 1928 entry. The 1955 vs 1957 date for the final house is unresolved and the story says so. The FS trail page and a 1984 plaque are the only present-day features described; no source describes lookout remains. The Oregon lookouts page quotes 1914-1942 Siskiyou Bulletin and newspaper items; quotes were checked against that page. Confidence is high for the 1914, 1928 and 1958 dates, which agree across sources. Checked 2026-10-09: wording now matches the cited pages (bids were being readied, not requested; the 1934 appointment is a position received; the 1928 materials and the summit plaque are paraphrased); the steep-slope detail is backed by a December 1914 quote.

Brief record checks out: Siskiyou NF, status gone, ground. Build year is unresolved (1929 per firelookout.com, 1930 per newspapers); the story follows the newspapers. The 2939 ft elevation on firelookout.com is ground elevation, not tower height, so it is not used. Access is unknown and no current source was found. Two web searches found only unrelated sites (a Port Orford lifeboat tower, Snow Camp, Bolan Mountain and Butler Butte in Umpqua NF); none was used. Butler Butte is a different lookout and must not be merged.

Today's summit description rests on one hiking blog (The Roaming Civic); no Forest Service or recent photo source was found, so treat the communication buildings as unconfirmed. The brief's design L-4 and height 12.2 m describe the 1934 40-foot tower; the final 1962 tower was a 41-foot R-6 flat-cab, about 12.5 m, which the record does not list, so the design field notes it rather than replacing the earlier design. The brief's elevation (1511.8 m for the site) was not checked; Wikipedia gives the peak as 5,010 ft (1,527 m). Access marked public because the hiking route is a listed trail; the 2017 Eagle Creek Fire closure has since reopened per the blog. Checked 2026-10-09: the 1960 'letter' is a dated entry (February 4, 1960) in the Oregon lookouts history; the 1962 claim no longer cites the hiking blog, which has no 1962 quote.

Brief coordinates (42.10237, -124.1528) match the NGS-based coordinates in Wikipedia's Mount Emily article; the west_us_lookouts point (42.0698, -124.1059) is the outlier. The 1922 cabin date and the 1973 end are both disputed. No read source describes the summit today; the Clio entry describes the bombing site, not the lookout footprint. An AllTrails page returned 403. A YouTube description seen only as a search snippet says wildfire destroyed the tower; it was not read and is not used. The 1966 recruiting notice on the weebly page is left out as a plan, not a staffing record. Wikipedia tags its 'not dropped from the correct height' and 'two men' sentences [citation needed]; the story keeps both under footnote 4, so they should be checked against a better source before the story is final.

The brief height (12.2 m) is corrected above. The weebly history mentions a Blumenstein cabin at the lookout headquarters in 1914, before the 1916 cupola, so 1916 is not the first building on the site. The firelookout.com 1958 name is the last known lookout. No source read says what remains on the summit or whether the old lookout site is open; MERA's page gives no location detail. The WWNF record could not be checked against the FFLOS detail page beyond the registration date.

The brief record (R-6, 1959 cabin, 1968 end, 2011 registration) is supported. The brief lists the agency as 'U.S.Forest Service'; the register's page spells it that way too, so no correction is proposed. The 360cities summit panorama, which describes the 1968 removal, returned 403 and was not read. Oregon Hikers is the only read source on the summit today; it does not describe any remains. Dates for the first cabin disagree across three sources and the story does not pick one.

Thin record: three pages, no staffing, fires or current-site description in any source read. Height conflict (24 vs 25 ft) and name spelling (Hagen vs Hagan) are unresolved. The Eugene Guard items are read only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. The Forest Lookouts heading names Eastern Lane District, Oregon Department of Forestry, where the register says U.S. Forest Service; not used. One web search found nothing specific to this lookout, so none is cited. Budget: 1 search, 6 page reads.

Brief had no height; height_m 12.2 is 40 feet converted to metres. Access level omitted: no source states whether the site is public or closed; the 2012 account describes a rough road and a hike of about 1.8 miles. Second-tower date (late 1930s vs 1942) and 1957 construction material are unresolved. No staffing record after 1954 found. A 2012 account is the newest status evidence.

Correction proposed: the record's height_m 9.1 (30 ft) matches the 1924 structure, not the 67-ft tower removed in 1978. Coordinates in the record match the register's point (45.21987, -123.72479); the west_us_lookouts point listed in the brief's conflicts (45.2145, -123.755) was not checked. Elevation 961.3 m matches firelookout.com's 3154 ft. Pew's 3,175 ft is a rise, not an elevation. No source read describes the summit today; the editor may want a Siuslaw NF or on-site check. Budget: 1 search, 6 page reads.

Record height_m 68.6 (225 ft) is not supported by any source read; the sources describe a summit cupola cabin and give no height, so facts omit it and no correction is proposed. The record's kind 'ground' is not contradicted, but no source says ground-mounted; check. Elevation 3427.5 m matches firelookout.com's 11,245 ft. Sources read agree on 1935 abandonment and 1941 collapse. A web search summary mentioned other abandonment years and remains on the summit; those pages were not opened, so they are not cited or used. Budget: 1 search, 6 page reads.

Brief's record checks: registration July 5, 2022 and US 1338 / OR 153 are confirmed on the NHLR page; the 1916 build date is confirmed. The brief's 'ground' kind matches NHLR, but a 2023 visit page calls it a steel tower. No access level is firmly established: the sources say the lookout is staffed and reachable on a 3.5-mile trail, but not whether the cab is open to visitors, so access is marked restricted. The 2021 article's staffing outcome is not confirmed beyond the June 9 statement. Search snippets mention a Whitman Ranger District phone number, a Wikipedia elevation of 8,325 ft and a 2021 Blue Mountain Eagle version; none were read, so none are used. Reads: 6 pages (NHLR, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, 2023 visit page, 2021 La Grande Observer article); 2 web searches.

Brief had access unknown; the sources describe a hiking route to the summit in the Sky Lakes Wilderness, so access is recorded as public. The remaining foundation rests on one undated hiking guide and on 1973 and 1987 photo captions; no source describes the summit today in more detail. The 1930 storms and the wind account conflict and are both reported.

The 1964 build year and the 1923/1929/1933 sequence agree across sources. Staffing is from undated firelookout.com text and an undated register line; the only access report is a 2011 blog visit, so current road and cab-access status is unverified. Design wording differs slightly (NHLR says wooden; firelookout.com says treated timber), and both were kept as timber. Elevation is 6,800 ft per NHLR and 6816 ft per firelookout.com. The 2008 burn was a patrol point, not the lookout. Not read: the Ochoco National Forest pages and the Facebook FFLA post.

Records agree on a 30-foot tower and on removal or destruction in 1967, but disagree on the 1931 and 1932 build dates and on the 1950 and 1951 replacement. No source describes remains or public access today, so no access key is recorded.

Current status is consistent across the register (emergency use), firelookout.com (available for emergencies) and the 2024 blog (not staffed, USGS equipment). The founding date is disputed (1923, 1924, or 1924/25 with the house built 1929). Elevation differs: NHLR 8,806 ft; firelookout.com 8926 ft; Wikipedia 8,934 ft (not used in the story). The NHLR 1977 visit report lists staffing as Sometimes; not used because it is dated. The brief's agency 'U.S. Dept. of the Interior' matches the register; the NPS is named as cooperator. Willhite Web is a personal history site that reproduces park files; treat its dates as secondary. Not read: any Crater Lake NPS page on visitor access to the cab.

The record's 'built 1947' is the replacement date; the first tower is 1932 per NHLR text, firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts. Access is not stated by any source read, so no access level is given. Elevation differs across sources (NHLR 4,665 ft, firelookout.com 4715 ft, Wikidata 4,695 ft) and the record's 1421.9 m was left alone. Staffing as_of is the NHLR 'mid 1980s' wording because the pages are undated. Cherylhill.net also gives 1946 for the replacement but was not fetched.

Only four pages were read and none describes staffing, fires, the removal date or the site today. The link between the 1934 panorama and the 1933 to 1935 Forest Service survey is inferred from the dates, not stated by any source. Access is not recorded.

The 1922 pole platform (register) and the 1923 steel tower (newspapers) are unreconciled. The 1911 entry is an establishment, not a tower build. The access level 'permission' is the brief's value; the sources only say the summit lies inside the reservation. No photo or current-condition source found. Brief's coordinates, elevation and 2010 registration match the register.

Elevation conflict: register 2,855 ft (870 m, matches brief's 870.2 m) vs firelookout.com 5149 ft; not resolved, and elevation is not in the facts schema. Brief's access 'unknown' is left out because no source states access. Only three short sources; no current-condition source or photo found. Weebly page's 'only a few scattered boards remain' is undated.

Built year is approximate (NHLR says as early as 1924; firelookout.com has a question mark). The 1916 heliograph placement conflicts: NHLR ties it to Mule Peak, the 1916 newspaper item quoted by Oregon Lookouts places it on Granite Butte; both kept, unresolved. Staffing and today's status rest on one 2025 blog trip report and a 1980s name from firelookout.com; no Forest Service document found. Access 'restricted' is an inference from the locked cab and staffing; no official visitor policy found. Judy Wing is named only as a historical lookout attendant. One websearch used. Cheryl Hill's standing-lookouts list marks Mule Peak unmanned, which conflicts with the 2025 trip report; both are reported. Record access 'unknown' and staffing 'unknown' could be updated from the sources above.

Brief had Klamath/Douglas, USFS, gone, access unknown; the register and firelookout.com agree on a 1930s cab that is gone. No staffing, fire or access source was found for this Mule Peak. The two searches returned only Union County (Wallowa-Whitman, elev. 8,679 ft) and California Mule Peak pages, which were not used for this record; the Union County lookout appears in one disambiguation sentence in the story. The brief's kind 'ground' is not stated in any source read, so it is left out of facts. Not read: cedarcountrylumber.net 2021 re-roof post and cherylhill.net 2023 Mule Peak page, both probably the Union County site.

Brief's coordinates (43.81102, -122.20839) and 5,470 ft elevation match the register. Sources disagree on the relocation year (1952 vs 1953) and height (40, 41 or 52 ft). The Oregon Lookouts page also has a separate 'Mule Mountain #1' entry, which was not checked. No source describes current condition or access; the brief's access 'unknown' is left out. No photo found beyond the register's 1961 caption.

Only the register and firelookout.com record a 1933 lookout on Mutton Mountain, and neither names a builder or design beyond unknown type. The only Mutton-specific history is the 1925 letter debate: Wilkes and Heritage recommended Mutton Mountain, the April 24 letter objected and favored Bald Peter, and a May 13 Bend Bulletin item reported a tower to be erected on Bald Peter that season. The sources do not connect that to the 1933 structure. Brief access 'permission' is not stated by any source read, so access is left out of facts. Not used: a 2,424-acre fire 15 miles northeast of Warm Springs, east of the Mutton Mountains, reported Friday August 28 (1981 newspaper page at oregonnews.uoregon.edu, PDF seq-11). It names the area but no lookout, so it is left out of the story. A Washington lookout called Mutton Mountain (washingtonlookouts.weebly.com) appeared in search; it is a different site and was not used.

Build year and height disagree across all three sources. The story follows the 1936 district records, the only dated primary-style evidence, but the 1936 correction is a judgment call for the editor. No source describes the site today, its ownership after the 1968 sale, or public access; the 1970 NGS note is the latest physical record. No staffing history is in these sources, so staffing is omitted.

Brief record has two errors: status should be abandoned (not gone) and kind should be crowsnest (not platform); see corrections. Both are now reflected in facts and the story. Only the 1924 season is documented for staffing. The 1968 article gives the builder's name as Glover Blake; a web search surfaced a Grover C. Blake tied to Big Butte on the Umatilla, which is unrelated and was not used. West Myrtle Butte (NHLR, standing 60-foot tower, 1929) is a different lookout and must not be merged. Access is unknown; no visit or access fact was found.

The brief says this record shares a register number with another site. The firelookout.com list shows Mount Nebo as US 980 and Nebo Peak in Wallowa County as US 1128, so the shared-number note needs checking. The register photo caption reads 1934 to 1955, which does not match the 1970 and 1971 removal dates, so it is not used. No source describes the summit today or public access, so access is omitted.

Brief said USFS, gone, access unknown, tower; the register and firelookout.com agree on the 1933 build and the 1970s loss but disagree on tower type and height, and on removed versus destroyed. Staffing names come only from firelookout.com. The 1955 modification and the 1923 cabin note come from the register and the Forest Lookouts page respectively. The 'retired sheepman' description is the Forest Lookouts page's own narrative, not the text of the 1923 note. No source read gives access or the site's condition today. The Forest Lookouts page calls the forest the Wallowa National Forest, which is an older name; the story uses the current Wallowa-Whitman name from the register.

No source describes what stands on the summit now or whether the public can reach it. The 2008 site photo is in the register gallery, but its caption does not say whether any structure is visible; an editor could check the image itself. The names in the staffing list come only from firelookout.com. Edward Dmytryk is named only as the sources give him: the Wikipedia article on the film director of that name does not mention a lookout, and nothing in these sources ties the two together, so the story does not link them.

Brief access was unknown; filled from Wikipedia and the Friends hike guide. Brief height 3.7 m matches the 12-foot tower in the October 1934 notice. Elevation differs by source: 3,880 ft (register), 3,872 ft (firelookout.com), 3,848 ft (Wikipedia peak); not used in the story. No staffing roster or fire events found; staffing left as unknown with the 1937 line-change note only. The register's 1963 and the Oregon history's c.1959 are both kept. The hike guide's old fire lookout is the main open question; a dated photo or a Forest Service check would settle it. No new photos captured (firetower.org captions present but image URLs were not in the cached text).

Build year disputed: 1936 (Oregon Lookouts, from contemporary photographs and a 1936 newsletter item) vs 1937 (both register pages). The story gives both. No source describes the site today, its condition, or public access; access was left out of facts because no source supports a level. The brief's access 'unknown' is unchanged. The 2010 FFLOS registration date from the brief was not visible in fetched text, so no registration event was written. firetower.org shows a 1936 panorama credited to the National Archives Pacific Northwest Region; its licence was not checked, so no photo entry was added. One WebSearch was run; its results were not used as sources.

Major disagreements: the 1939 build year and the 1951 replacement appear only in the registers; the Oregon Lookouts page documents a 1947 cabin on a tower and a 1961 40-foot replacement. Abandonment (1963 vs 1965) and removal (1994 vs undated) also differ. The story gives both accounts. Height 12.2 m is the 40-ft figure from the 1961 replacement, a conversion from the source's feet. No source describes the site today, the 1969 radio building included, or its access. The Oregon Lookouts page does not explain its 'Portland Filter Center' or 'AWS' wording, so the story does not expand either term. The brief's agency and county are consistent with the sources. One web search was run for this site; its results were not used.

The history is consistent across all three pages: 40-foot wooden tower built 1952, removed or destroyed 1970. Height 12.2 m is the 40-ft figure converted. No source describes the site today or its access, so no access or visit facts were written. Ochoco National Forest and Harney County are both listed on the register page. A human should confirm the forest's extent, since our sources do not settle which county the forest lies in. One web search was run for this site; its results were not used as sources. The site photos on firetower.org (a 1963 view credited to Howard Verschoor's collection and a 2002 site view) have no licence stated, so no photo entries were added. The brief's agency spelling 'U.S.Forest Service' is a spacing typo in the source and is written 'U.S. Forest Service' here.

Three sources only; two searches found nothing else about an Oregon Ninemile lookout (results were Montana sites and other Douglas County towers). The Oregon lookouts page quotes newspapers and a 1939 forest history second-hand; originals not checked. Dates conflict (1933 vs 1934), removal date and method unknown, and no source describes the site today or public access, so access is omitted rather than set. The 1928 shake cabin appears only on firelookout.com. The brief's coordinates, 'gone' status and 40 ft height agree with the sources; no corrections proposed. The Oregon lookouts page's 'Removed' line is a single word with no date.

Dates conflict: register and firelookout.com say a 100-foot crow's nest in 1937 and a steel tower in 1940; the Forest Lookouts page's district annual reports say a 140-foot steel tower was erected in 1957. The brief's height_m 42.7 (140 ft) matches the 1957 tower, not the register's 1937 crow's nest (100 ft); the design field says so. The 145-foot Molalla tower in the 1959 and 1961 items may or may not be this one; the story does not link it. Staffing: no named lookout found. Access: no source found, so no access fact is recorded. Removal date: not found. Oregon Department of Forestry records (CCC-era lookout blueprints and inventories, mentioned in an Oregon State Archives guide surfaced by search) might settle the dates; not read.

Two thin sources that agree. No source gives the removal date, staffing, or what remains at the site. The brief coordinates (45.386522, -121.940748) match the register page's own coordinates (N 45 23.191, W 121 56.445). The weebly Oregon lookouts list also shows the site as removed, but its text was not quoted here.

No source describes what remains on the site today, and none gives access. The cabin date is only 'the 1920s' in both sources; the 1920 event year is a decade placeholder. The 1928 letter describes a plan to occupy the points, not a record of anyone staying there. Source 3 is a transcription on a hobby site; the original Forest Service letter was not checked. The brief's record (gone, USFS, FFLOS 2010) is consistent with the sources, so no corrections.

Two thin pages from the same register family. The 1936 photo caption predates the 1939 build date and is unexplained. The 1939 structure is a cupola on a warehouse roof, not clearly a platform, so the brief's kind of platform fits the 1942 addition better. A ranger roll call (ppolinks.com PDF) surfaced in search lists district rangers, not lookout staffing, so it was not used. No source describes the site today.

Two register-family pages plus Wikipedia for the park. The firelookout.com header says R.I.P. 1920-1953 while its body says destroyed in 1966; the body was used. The 1913 camp was not a lookout cab, so it is coded other. Wikipedia is a lead, not a primary source; the trail and park facts should be checked against an Oregon Parks page before publishing. The Wikipedia coordinates are about 300 m from the brief's coordinates, consistent with the same peak. Access level 'public' rests on the park's listed type, not on a rule for the lookout site itself.

Sources disagree on the build year (register 1942 vs Rex's 1954 entry) and on the fate (moved to Euchre in 1965 vs dismantled in 1967). Nothing ties the Euchre 1965 tower to Norton Hill. Brief height 6.1 m is the 1939 pole lookout. Registration date checked on the FFLOS page. No new photos added; the register already carries the 1942-1965 and 1997 photos.

Register says removed 1964; Fire Lookout website says destroyed 1964. Brief agency 'U.S.Forest Service' is consistent with the Umpqua National Forest pages, but the exact agency wording was not printed in the cached FFLOS text. Brief height 3.0 m matches the 10-ft pole. Registration date checked on the FFLOS page. No photos added.

Brief's 2010 registration date confirmed (September 19, 2010). Register says removed 1967; Fire Lookout website says destroyed 1967. Brief's county (Clackamas) is not stated on any page read, so the story omits it. The brief's 'ground' kind fits the register and Fire Lookout pages; the 1959 'tower' wording is the only conflict. No height or photos were found.

Thin record: three short listings, no staffing, no fire history, no present-day description. The story is about 90 words, under the 120-word floor, because the sources give nothing more; editor to decide whether to keep it short. The geocache and Oregon Historic Sites pages returned only a title or a redirect from the cache, so they are not cited. Brief's build year (1930), status (gone) and coordinates agree with the sources. The brief's elevation_m of 609.6 matches the register figure only.

Thin record: one line of history on firelookout.com, no staffing, fire or visit data, and no present-day account. Coordinates differ by about 0.7 km: the record's point (44.46002, -120.29167, matching the Association list) against west_us_lookouts (44.4593, -120.30029). Not resolved here. A search snippet of the Forest Lookouts page mentioned a 1918 photo credited to the Bowman Museum in Prineville, but that caption is not in the cached page text, so it is left out and should be checked before use. A Wheeler County Fire & Rescue post about lookout history could not be read. No photo with a licence was found.

Staffing and the current tower date rest on visitor blogs and an undated firelookout.com page. The 1915, 1927, 1942 and 1962 newspaper items are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. No Forest Service or Deschutes National Forest page was read. Photos not added: firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber, but no image URLs or licenses were confirmed.

Two accounts of the first structure conflict (1913 lumber cabin vs 1915 steel windmill tower) and both are kept. Access corrected from permission to restricted because no source found requires a permit. The brief's kind 'ground' is disputed; height_m 9.1 comes from the register's 30-foot tower figure only. The story is about 320 words. Oregon Hikers and Outdoor Pilgrim are trip guides, not records, so their statements about access and remains are attributed to them.

Build year is disputed across four sources (1930, 1931, 1932; a 1933 date appears in a Facebook group post seen only as a search snippet, not read, not used). The Statesman Journal 2020 article returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Rex's page is a hobby site quoting old newspapers; quotes were checked against its page text, not the original papers. Brief access was unknown; facts.access is public from the FS trail page, which gives no closure information for the summit. No source describes what remains on the summit, and the story says so. No new photos added.

Do not use https://www.oregonhikers.org/field_guide/Old_Baldy_Hike for this record. It describes a different Old Baldy in the Mt. Hood National Forest (Salmon-Huckleberry Wilderness, near Githens Mountain) and was excluded. Access and present-day status are not described by any source, so no access fact is recorded. Brief's design D-6 is treated as a misreading of a column name. The story is about 215 words. The lookout's name is spelled three ways in the quoted papers; the story reports this rather than choosing one.

WebSearch was unavailable for this run (the shared search budget was spent before this tower), so nothing about the site today was checked beyond the four pages read. The brief's height_m of 4.3 looks wrong; a 50 ft tower is about 15.2 m. The brief's FFLOS registration date (March 26, 2011) did not appear in the page text read here, so no fflos_registered event is recorded. The 1938 and 1955 details are quoted second-hand from Douglas FPA and ODF annual reports on the Weebly page; those reports were not opened. The camera-system replacement is recorded as a plan only.

No source describes the site today, and the story says so. The 1956-1976 history comes from a Weebly transcription of Douglas FPA annual reports, not the reports themselves. Brief record is correct (gone, FFLOS registration 2011-03-26, 50 ft = 15.2 m); no corrections. Access is left unset because no source gives it.

Two sources, both naming the Oregon Dept. of Forestry, with no staffing record and no access information. No source gives a date for the ruins or describes the site today. A Grokipedia.com page on the mountain says BLM administers the land; it is an encyclopedia mirror, not a primary source, so it was not used. Editor may want to confirm the administering agency with ODF or BLM before publishing. The brief's agency entry is correct.

Current rental is closed to reservations (confirmed live on Recreation.gov as of 2026-10-04), consistent with Firelookout.com's note that the site is presently abandoned; treated access as 'restricted' rather than fully 'public' to flag that. Minor year discrepancy on the first platform tower (1915 vs 1916).

No source describes the site today. The 1921 item names Outerson Park, which may not be the summit; the story now says the 1921 item does not state whether Outerson Park is the summit. The 1929 and 1921 entries come from newspaper clippings as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page. The 1962 fate is disputed (removed vs destroyed). Brief record (gone, ground, registered 2010-09-19) checks out; no corrections.

Build year (1933), tower height (72 ft) and CCC origin agree across the register, firelookout.com and the 2024 blog. Purpose is unresolved: firelookout.com says it was primarily for wildlife observation; Cheryl Hill doubts it was used for fire detection. Current status and access rest on an April 2024 blog visit and the register's undated text; nothing newer was found. The 2024 blog's tower-height conflict (80/90/99 ft) concerns a different refuge tower (the headquarters tower, US 429), not this one. Wikipedia's P Ranch article (NRHP 1979) describes the ranch and was read but not used for the lookout. The fws.gov Malheur cultural heritage page appeared in search and was not read.

No source describes the site today. The register's coordinates (42.02758, -124.02256) differ from the second database in the brief (42.03067, -124.00786); that database was not checked, so the coordinates are unresolved. The brief's D-6 design looks wrong (see corrections). The 1913 vs 1914-1915 start and the 1930 vs 1933 cab date are both disputed and both are reported. The 1939 history and Siskiyou Bulletin quotes come through the Forest Lookouts transcription, not the originals.

The build year (1930 on two sites, 1932 newspaper plan) and the end (gone by 1960 vs burned in 1968) disagree; the story gives both. No source describes what remains today or whether the site is open. Two search snippets (AllTrails 'Mcbee Trail to Packsaddle Mountain' route and PeakVisor, 1,873 m, which matches the record's 1,872.7 m) suggest a summit trail exists, but I could not read those pages (AllTrails returned 403), so they are not used. The brief's first source_pages URL (packsaddle-mountain-lane-county) returns 404; the registered URL is packsaddle-mountain-lookout-site-lane-county. Excluded namesake: Packsaddle Mountain in Idaho (Kaniksu NF), which has its own lookout history.

Three sources agree the 1913 platform is gone, but none gives a removal date or says what remains today; access is unknown. Oregon has a second Palmer Peak (Crater/Rogue River NF, Jackson County, 1914 lookout per Medford Mail Tribune items on oregonlookouts.weebly.com/palmer-peak1.html); it is a different site and was excluded. The 1930 and 1933 panorama dates are for two photos, not a conflict. The USGS page search hit was Joel Palmer's journal, not used. The brief's FFLOS registration date (September 19, 2010) matches firetower.org.

The history is from 1913-1916 newspaper and report quotes reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not read. The brief's 36.6 m height is the hypothetical 120-foot tower, not a built height. The brief's kind 'platform' differs from the Association's Crowsnest. Do not mix this record with the Multnomah County Palmer Peak (US 634, OR 68; Mt. Hood National Forest). The July 11, 1933 panorama entry on the Jackson page also appears in the firetower.org Multnomah record, so it is left out of the story until someone checks which tower it belongs to. No photo with a licence was found. No source describes the site today.

Thin record: the register and firelookout.com give only a 1941 (possibly 1935) cabin, abandonment and loss. No staffing, fire or removal-year sources were found. Two searches and a handful of reads turned up nothing more. The FFLOS list page gives coordinates 45.99474, -117.95819, while the detail page the record uses gives 46.009306, -117.961881; the detail-page point matches the record, so no correction is proposed, but the list point differs by about 1.7 km. The Washington index text is a short listing, not a site history. The Paradise Fire of July 2026 near Walla Walla is a different event and is not linked to this site.

The Mount Wilson origin of the cab appears only on firetower.org; firelookout.com does not mention it, and the Mount Wilson page read does not mention Parkdale. The 1923 six-foot house on Mount Wilson conflicts with the 7x7 cab, and the story says so. No source describes the tower remains or whether the grounds are open to visitors; the NRHP listing covers the station building only. The brief's conflict note ('They share a register number') could not be confirmed: firetower.org lists Parkdale as US 635 and Palmer Peak as US 634. A Living New Deal page (403) and a search snippet calling the station the Parkdale Work Station were not read, so the current use of the station is not stated in the story.

The 3.0 m height in the record is wrong (see corrections). Heights (40 vs 50 ft), cab size and cause and year of loss (arson 1995 vs vandals or arson 1996) conflict across sources, so the story reports the disagreement. A 1937 newspaper line describes the old tower as 50 feet above the rocky top, which does not square with the 30 ft 1934 tower named by the Register and firelookout.com; not reconciled. Current staffing rests on undated firelookout.com plus the June 2022 visit. Access is recorded as permission because the gate sign on Green Diamond land grants revocable recreational use; no public-entry rule for the tower was found.

Build, height, removal and abandonment years agree across the register, firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts. The only account of the site today is one 2013 forum post, so the current condition is unverified; the site's public access is not described in any source read. Brief's design 'Aermotor' and height 22.9 m are confirmed (75 ft). No fires found in the sources read. A 1957 child injury at the station is in the Forest Lookouts quotes but was left out as not about the lookout's history.

The brief's height_m of 121.9 m (400 ft) is not supported by any source read and is recorded as a correction. The brief's 'L-4' design and 'ground' kind hold, with the caveat that Forest Lookouts describes a 1964 cab on a short tower. The Oregon Hikers guide is the only source for the site today; it describes a parking area and overlook, but does not say whether any lookout remains are visible. Predecessor, build and removal dates disagree across sources and are shown as conflicts. Cora Leland's 1918 claim appears in two 1918 items on Forest Lookouts with slightly different wording; the story uses the July 18 version. No fires found in the sources read.

The 1991-2012 repair chronology rests mainly on the Sand Mountain Society page, written by the group that did the work; the register corroborates the 1954 replacement and the 1994 completion, and firelookout.com corroborates the 1920 start. The record's access 'public' is not stated outright in the sources read: the society opens the lookout each spring and says visitors have made changes, but it posts no visitor rules. Confirm before treating public visiting as established. Staffing is set to unknown; no source read describes fire staffing. The record's 2008 'modified' and 2011/2012 restorations come from the society page, so they are supported by one source. Firelookout.com places the lookout '13 miles northwest of Cave Junction' and the society places it '10 miles WNW of Selma'; the story uses the society's location. The society names the agency 'Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest'; the register says 'Siskiyou National Forest' and the story does not name the forest.

Brief's county and height (93 ft = 28.3 m) are confirmed; the brief had no design, so the 93-foot wooden tower with 7x7 cab is added. Built year (1934 or 1935) and height (93 or 104 ft in the 1953 letter) disagree across sources and are shown as conflicts. No source read describes the site today; the only later note is the 2011 register's 'still there' about the guard station. No access information found. Recruitment and stairway items are the only staffing notes; no fires found in the sources read.

WebSearch was unavailable for this run (the shared search budget was spent before this tower), so nothing about the site today was checked beyond the pages read. The brief's second coordinate pair (42.60178, -123.6421, from west_us_lookouts) comes from a source not opened here. The firelookout.org index places an NHLR US 498 entry on a line next to a Clackamas County Peavine Mountain entry, while the NHLR page puts US 498 in Josephine County; worth a data check. The 1961 cab size is in the NHLR text but its quotes use curly apostrophes, so it is not recorded. The 1915-1941 details come from Weebly's quoted Forest Service station history, which was not opened directly. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the Weebly page's 2005 entry says the lookout was deemed unsafe and no longer staffed; that is compatible with 'staffed into the 2000s' and is not recorded as an event.

Brief's record is accurate: register page gives US 638, OR 70, N 45.013400 W 121.835420, 4,732 ft, U.S. Forest Service, removed by 1957. Brief says this site and another Peavine share a register number; the register page lists only US 638, OR 70 for this site, and the firelookout.org Oregon index lists the Josephine County Peavine as FFLOS US 889, OR 256. The index also lists a 'NHLR US 498, OR 91' line beside this entry, but that NHLR number belongs to the Josephine County tower per the existing us-or-peavine-mountain research record; not re-verified here. The index gives this site as 45.01834, -121.83240, roughly 600 m from the register coordinates the brief uses; the register value was kept. No source read describes the site today, and no source states access, so access is omitted. The register page has a 1933 panorama (National Archives, Pacific Northwest Region) and the 2011 photo; no image URLs were captured, so no photos were added.

Minor unresolved discrepancy on exactly which restoration campaign (1991 SMS/Jim Borders re-roofing, a Pete Bond-led Oregon State Parks restoration per NHLR, or a 1995 date per firelookout.com) is the 'main' one; these may all be real, sequential volunteer efforts. Current brief listed access as 'public' which matches what we found; staffing/status fields can be added since the brief omitted them. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the story described John Oblack as a 'Czech stonemason's helper,' which isn't in any source (source 1/BLM calls him 'a Czechoslovakian from Molalla with help from an unknown stone mason from Portland,' i.e. Oblack built it himself with an unnamed mason's help, not the other way around); corrected to match the source wording. Spot-checked the 1918 rangefinder-only origin and the 'four sides / 360-degree view' claim directly against the BLM page, and the 1991 'autumn rains' re-roofing detail directly against the Sand Mountain Society page; all three confirmed. The 'only stone lookout remaining in Oregon' claim was also confirmed on the BLM page (not previously quoted in the evidence list, but present in the source).

Current status (standby, used only in emergencies, unmanned) rests on NHLR, firelookout.com and an undated standing-lookouts list; no Forest Service document was found and the present road and visitor status is unverified. The first-structure date conflicts: 1934 newspapers (tower erected, station under construction) versus firelookout.com's 1935. The 1980 newspaper item and the 1986 date for the present cab do not line up cleanly; the 1980 item describes a 39-foot tower and a lookout to be stationed the next summer. Elevation: register 7,994 ft (2,437 m) matches the record; firelookout.com and the standing-lookouts list give 8,035 ft. Staffing 'unstaffed' as_of 'undated' is from the standing-lookouts list and standby status. Access 'restricted' is an inference, not an official policy. One websearch (unproductive) and five page reads were used for this tower.

Brief's core record holds up: built 1937, abandoned 1955, ODF, Multnomah County and coordinates match the register. Left open in the story: the 1936 newspaper item predates the 1937 build year, and Weebly's Forest Service retention after 1943 conflicts with the ODF attribution. Access is set to restricted because Oregon Hikers warns the route borders private land; an AllTrails listing labelled 'PRIVATE PROPERTY' appeared only in a search snippet and was not opened. The 1957 Sunday Oregonian field-day item quoted on Weebly was left out of the story as it is not about the lookout's condition or use. The staffing as_of 1936 rests on one newspaper item about a watch assignment. No photos with usable image URLs were found.

The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with the 2005 and 2020 remnant reports; 'ruins' is proposed as a correction for a human to check. The brief's 'conflict' line says firelookout.com=standing, but the page read gives no status word; the Association list says Abandoned. The 1930 built year is the decade only. The Oregon Hikers page is undated. The 2020 tree identification is the blogger's tentative guess. Fivemile Butte is a separate lookout and is not covered here. No photo with a licence was found.

Brief's record had no build, staffing or removal events; those come from the register, firelookout.com and Weebly, which agree on the 1930 crow's nest and the 1941 tower. Only the removal wording differs (removed vs destroyed). Weebly's 1929 tower is a plan in a newspaper item; no source read says it was built. The 1941 tower's date is consistent across the register and firelookout.com. Two-source identity is solid: coordinates N 44.464170 W 120.084540 and elevation 6,194 ft match the brief. No source read describes the site today, and none states access, so access is omitted. The register has a 1934 panorama and a 1942 photo caption (Howard Verschoor collection); no image URLs were captured, so no photos were added. Search returned no further Peterson Point pages.

Build-year conflict between NHLR (1958) and recreation.gov/firelookout.com (1934 original, 1948 current tower) is unresolved; flagged in both the story and resolved_conflicts. height_m corrected to ~12.5 (41-ft tower) in facts; the original brief's 7.6 figure appears to have been cab-only or an error and has been applied/fixed. Fact-check 2026-10-04 also found and fixed a footnote misattribution (the homesteader sentence cited firelookout.com, which never mentions 1898/Pickett, instead of recreation.gov) and a cab-dimension conflict between NHLR (14'x14') and recreation.gov (12x12) that the brief had not flagged; both are now noted in the story and resolved_conflicts.

Coordinates disagree: the Register gives N 43.264680, W 122.264680, while the record's longitude of -122.37989 (and 43.2642 latitude) differs by about 0.11 degrees, roughly 9 km. Not resolved in the record; the editor should check the coordinates against the Register and a map before any change. Current status rests on a 2023 visitor report and the undated Roaming Civic post; no 2025-26 source read. Forest Service trail page and an FFLA Facebook post were seen in search but not read. The 1950 and 1951 staffing items and the 1962 News-Review item are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. Photos not added: no image URLs or licenses confirmed.

The 1921 cabin and 1932 tower agree across the register and firelookout.com. The replacement tower differs: 1951 and 41 ft (register) against 1952 and 28 ft (Oregon history). The record's height_m of 8.5 m matches only the 28-foot tower. firelookout.com's span of 1921-1951 conflicts with removal by 1968 in the other two sources; the story reports both. The record point is roughly 3 km from the summit coordinates on Wikipedia (43.8031, -120.9134), so the sources do not place the lookout on the observatory summit and the story does not. One web search found no source on the site's current condition. No access level is given for the lookout site itself, so none is recorded. Photos were not fetched or added. Verification 2026-10-09: the 1929 lightning account conflicts between two newspapers, so the story now reports both; the 1932 fire is described as in the 1930 Big Springs burn, as the source says; the campground is now quoted with its Forest Service label.

The height in the record (4.3 m) matches no cited source; a correction is proposed for human review. Build year (1940 construction vs 1941 register) and agency (Oregon Dept. of Forestry in the register vs the Siuslaw National Forest in the 1940 announcement) conflict, and the story reports both. One web search for the butte's current condition returned nothing relevant. The register has a 1944 photo and a 2008 site photo, both courtesy of Howard Verschoor; these were not fetched or added. Verification 2026-10-09: the story now credits both the register and firelookout.com for the 41-foot tower; the Mary's Peak location and the 1940 and 1941 dates are now carried in dated quotes from the Corvallis Gazette-Times reprints on the Oregon history page.

The record's two location points (FFLOS 45.79771, -123.04986; West US Lookouts 45.81284, -123.05064) are about 1.7 km apart; the story does not choose between them. The record's height_m is null; the 20-foot figure is listed under design and not as a height. A map-database label 'Pisgah Lookout' in Columbia County turned up in search, but it has no history, so it is not cited. Two web searches found no source on the current site condition. Verification 2026-10-09: the story said the site was activated 'as an aircraft observation post'; the Oregon history gives the Portland Filter Center listing and the volunteers' aircraft observation work, but not that label, so the story now says only that. The register's 'Administered by' field is now quoted as the administering agency.

No source describes the site today. Access is omitted because no source describes it. A search snippet from AllTrails (the page returned HTTP 403 and was not read) describes a lookout at the summit; if that is accurate the gone status is wrong, so check before publishing. The State Library of Oregon record for the 1991 Forest Service eligibility study of Deschutes lookouts was read only as metadata; the study itself may cover this site. No photos added because no image URLs were captured.

Three sources agree on the 1949 tower and the emergency use, but they disagree on the early dates. Forest Lookouts (1937 note) argues against the 1934 tower that the register and firelookout.com give, so the 1934 event is flagged for review. Forest Lookouts spells the point 'Poque Point' in one 1937 item; the record uses the standard name. The Unity Ranger Station (Wikipedia, not cited) has a separate fire lookout tower built 1936-38; it is not this site and should not be confused with it. No source describes the site today, and access is omitted because no source describes it. No photos added because no image URLs were captured.

Staffing (seasonal, as_of 2012) rests on firelookout.com's undated 'staffed every summer', a 2012 visit report and an undated standing-lookouts list; no Forest Service source found. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the staffed cab and a 2012 visitor not being invited up; the road's current condition is unverified. Two record corrections: height_m 9.1 is the 1931 pole tower, and design 'L-4' omits the 82-ft tower. Omitted on purpose: a 1961 fatal fall from this tower, reported in a Bend Bulletin item quoted by Oregon Lookouts; it is not part of the lookout's fire-watch history, so the editor may want to decide whether to add it. Elevation: register 6,710 ft and the record's 2045.2 m agree; firelookout.com and the standing-lookouts list give 6,745 ft.

No source describes what remains at the site today, and no access level is supported, so access is omitted. The sources agree the tower was gone by 1948 but disagree on the build year (1934 vs 1935), the agency (ODF vs Rogue River NF) and whether the 1948 end was removal or destruction. No staffing information was found beyond the 1950 house salvage. No photos added because no image URLs were captured. Stories are short because the evidence is thin.

Three sources. The 1941 build date and the 1935 panorama conflict and no source explains it; the story reports both. Other lookouts named Porcupine Ridge (Glacier National Park, Montana; Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm, Washington) were excluded. A Facebook post from Memories of Morrow County that the search snippet connects to this lookout returned only its title on fetch, so it was not used. Photo image URLs were not captured; the register's 1935 panorama (credit: National Archives-Pacific Northwest Region) and 2009 site photo (credit: Rex Kamstra) are mentioned in text only. No source describes the site today or gives access.

Brief record checked: coordinates, elevation and FFLOS registration match. No access source found, so no access key. No source describes the site today. Staffing evidence is limited to a 1936 telephone ring and a 1964 deactivation; no staff are named. The 1920s camp, 1932 ladder and 1937 pole tower cannot all be reconciled from these sources. The brief's access 'unknown' is left as is.

Tower design and dates conflict across three sources. No source describes what remains at the site beyond the Oregon Hikers note of little remaining and an antenna. No source states public access; the hiking guide describes a loop that reaches the site, so access is left out of facts. Fate: removed after the 1965 entry, undated.

No source gives a removal date. The Forest Service interpretive page does not mention the lookout, so nothing describes the tower footprint today. Access is taken from the Forest Service listing and a tourism page. Staffing names come from firelookout.com and 1937 newspaper notices quoted by Forest Lookouts. Brief record matched on height (60 ft) and elevation.

Only two detailed sources, and they describe the structure differently (guard station at the base versus a cab). No staffing, fires or build date beyond the 1930s were found. No source describes the site today or its public access. Brief record checked: coordinates and elevation match FFLOS; kind 'ground' matches the FFLA type label only, and whether the cab stood on the summit is unclear, so the editor may want to check. A cached Oregon Fire Lookouts SW table lists 'Pothole Butte (LO site)', which the table defines as a site where the building has been removed or its status is unknown; its URL was not identified, so it is not cited. Do not use the table's 1931 date: it is the benchmark placement year, not the lookout's build year.

Not a tower: the record's point kind is right, and the NHLR page describes an Osborne fire-finder in an enclosure. Build date is approximate (circa 1930s). The 1935 panorama note does not say who Osborne was, so the story does not link him to the finder's name. No fires, named staff or closure history were found in the sources read. Access: the finder is locked and used only in emergencies, and the pull-out is on a public road, so access is rated restricted. Photos on the NHLR and firelookout.com pages are credited to Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were captured, so none are added. One search returned a Forest Fire Lookout Association history page of the Osborne finder (firelookout.org/resources/plans/hist-osborne/) that was not read; it could add build and staffing detail. Cheryl Hill's table header was read on 2026-10-08: Unmanned is the STATUS column, and the last column is Accessible to Public (legal access only, per the directory's own note).

Build year conflicts (1933 vs 1934). No source describes the site today or its access. An unverified Facebook group comment surfaced in search results about the structure and the 1970s; not used because the page could not be read and the claim is unsourced. Record's ground kind and L-4 design match the sources.

Build date is unresolved; the story gives both the register's 1913 account and the collection's 1920-21 account. Last staffing record found is 1931 (a planned summer posting); a 1935 entry on the collection page is garbled and was not used. The warden entry is dated 1914 on the collection page (its report is cited as 1915), so the story uses 1914. Mayo's 160-fire report is dated September 13, 1917, and the story now places it in 1917. Backman's initials differ across 1924 items (F.G. in June, V.G. in August); the story uses V. G. as in the August report. The 2012 camera claim rests on one collection page (c.2012); no ODF or FPA listing names this site. The register lists 1958, 1982 and 2001 photos but gives no image URLs, so none were added. Access and what remains today: no source found. The undated 'Removed' label on the collection page was not used.

Two independent pages agree on the 1942 AWS ground post, but the 1930s crow's nest rests on one listing. Brief's location conflict is unresolved: FFLA directory 44.65623,-123.36243 (matches our record) vs west_us_lookouts 44.62817,-123.38739. The Oregon Lookouts page header says 10S-5W-29 while its 1942 letter places the post in Section 36, T10S R6W. The 1942 post is also called Price Observation Post (Albany 95) and Arboretum in planning letters. The Oregon Lookouts 1942 letters themselves document the AWS role. No staffing, access or current-site source found; access left unset. Status Removed on the weebly page is unexplained.

Build date is unresolved: the register and firelookout.com say 1933, but a July 1931 item and a 1932 lightning-protection entry point to an earlier lookout. The story sets the 1942 memo's 61 ft 11 in (measured from ground to the cab floor) against the register's 60-foot figure and does not use it as height_m. Forest name differs between sources (Winema vs Fremont). The brief's second coordinate pair is not verified. The undated 'Removed' label on the collection page was not used. Last staffing record found is 1940. The register lists 1945 and 1948 photos but gives no image URLs. No access information found.

The Wildfire Today article spells the photographer's name as Stenkap in its body and Stenkamp in its first sentence; the story uses Stenkamp. The article's '81 feet' is drone data for the platform, while firelookout.com says '80' tree'; both are reported. Access: no source says whether the site is open, so no access key. The Roaming Civic post is a trip report by a visitor, not a survey; it is cited only for the failed search. The FFLOS page's 'Nominated by Steve Stenkamp' and the May 2020 photo credit are not used because no photo URL or license was found. Brief coordinates are about 40 m from the FFLA list's coordinates.

The brief lists this as kind 'ground' with design L-4; no tower is recorded, so the story calls it a lookout house. Removal year conflicts (1952 vs 1953) and the wording differs (removed vs destroyed); both are reported. The firelookout.com header puts the site in the Mt. Hood National Forest; the register says U.S. Forest Service, not contradicted. The 1934 traveler's passage is dated August 19, 1934 (Sunday Oregonian); the story now quotes the writer's steep-and-crooked wording rather than paraphrasing it as a cause. No staffing records found. Elevation per register is 6,095 ft (1,858 m). No photos with usable URLs were found. No access or current-condition information found.

No source gives the year the lookout was removed; Oregon Lookouts lists it as 'Removed' after its 1964 entries, undated. The register says 'used for emergency in 1971' while firelookout.com says 'Emergency 1971'; read here as emergency use. The 1953 lease and 1954 build are from the Central Oregon District annual report quoted on Oregon Lookouts. Register photos (1954, 1959, courtesy Howard Verschoor collection) not used because licence was not verified. Staffing as_of 1964 is the last dated record, not a current status.

Agency conflict: the register says Coos FPA administered the site; Oregon Lookouts files its 1934-1941 record under the Siskiyou National Forest. Neither source gives a change date. Removal: the register says 'removed in 1951' while firelookout.com says 'Destroyed 1951'; not reconciled. No source describes the site today. The 1935 and 1939-1941 staffing entries come from newspaper and planning quotes on Oregon Lookouts. The register and firelookout.com give no access information. Brief record kind 'ground' and elevation 767 m are consistent with the register.

Current rental status needs a check closer to publication — recreation.gov shows it closed to reservations 'until further notice' and firelookout.com attributes this to storm damage, but neither gives a date for the storm or an expected reopening. Brief's rental.available=true is likely stale. Fact-check 2026-10-04 found the story had wrongly dated NHLR registration to 'the mid-1990s' (actually March 2003, per NHLR) and had overstated current staffing: NHLR's own 2007/2015 volunteer visit reports say the tower was unstaffed and, by 2015, badly deteriorated. Both fixed in the story and logged above.

Two built dates: 1934 (register, with panorama photos May 1934) and 1931 (KFPA annual report quoted on Oregon Lookouts). Not reconciled; a human could check the KFPA annual report or a Forest Service history. Agency: register says U.S. Forest Service and Fremont NF; Oregon Lookouts files the 1931-1941 record under Klamath FPA. Removal: 'Removed' on Oregon Lookouts is undated. The 2005 photo caption on the register is not described. The NGS survey datasheet (designation QUARTZ, 1948 description of the summit) was seen embedded on Oregon Lookouts but not cited because it describes 1948 conditions; that embedded note also gives road directions from Bly, so the story's no-access claim is limited to the register. No current site description found.

Brief said status gone and agency U.S. Forest Service; both kept. Access is unknown in every source read, so no access fact is written. The 1972 removal versus destruction is unresolved, and the story says so. No source describes the site now. The 1937 staffing date is the last staffing mention found, not an end date. Three sources only, all from the same small set of pages; a newspaper search was not run beyond the brief's pages.

Brief record kept: status gone, agency Oregon Dept. of Forestry, with the forest-attribution conflict recorded. Access is unknown in every source read, so no access fact is written. A Kemnow PDF copy of the Forest Lookouts page at orww.org carries the same entries (the 1941 quote is split across lines there), so the weebly page is cited. Two web searches found nothing describing the site today.

Brief record checked: L-4 design and 4.6 m height (15 ft) agree with the sources. Today's status rests on a 2018 hiking blog; the concrete foundation belongs to a later shelter cabin, not the lookout. Access is inferred from that blog's trail description, so the access note is dated 2018. Staffing as_of 1941 is the fire-season reference; the 1942 Redifer item is in the story.

Sources disagree on several points and the story says so where it matters. (1) Purchase year: the register says 1980, CLUI says 1981. (2) Departure: the register says the followers left in the 1990s; CLUI says the property was vacated after the Bhagwan's 1985 deportation and sold at auction in 1988. (3) Design and height: the register describes a two-story ground house; firelookout.com gives a six-foot wooden tower with a 14-by-14-foot cab. The record's height_m 4.3 m equals 14 ft, which matches the cab dimension rather than a height. No reliable height was found, so height_m is not repeated in facts and a human should review the record's value. (4) Elevation: the record and register give 2,654 ft (809 m); firelookout.com and the directory give 4,040 ft. Not resolved. (5) Coordinates: the register gives 44.91068, -120.7228; firelookout.org's Oregon list gives 44.83310, -120.62426, roughly 11 km apart by my arithmetic. Not resolved, and the record keeps the register's point. (6) Staffing: the register says the lookout stands empty; the directory says Unknown. Story uses unstaffed, undated.
