The brief's 'shares a register number' note: a FFLOS record for the Sandy Sod Tower Site in Pennsylvania also carries US 471 (FFLOS numbering), so the collision is between two different towers in different registers. The merge report also flags this tower's coordinates as a far match to the Oregon list (register_match_far). Access: no public access is stated; the story advises against visiting. Photo: firelookout.com credits Debbie Newell; licence and image URL not found, so no photo added. The CLUI page covers the wider Rajneeshpuram site and does not mention this lookout by name. Verification 2026-10-08: the story now attributes the built-from-scratch description to Rajneeshpuram (the CLUI subject), says the Center ties the vacating to the 1985 deportation rather than placing it after, and footnotes the 1991 sale and the coordinate difference. Events for the 1980/1981 purchase, 1985 deportation, 1988 auction, 1990s departure, 1991 sale and 1996 donation were added so the timeline matches the story.

Record's design 'L-4' conflicts with NHLR's ODF 14 x 14 cab and with the 1946 district report. Build date conflicts (1930s first cab; 1946 district report; NHLR 1950). Land status conflicts: NHLR says BLM land, firelookout.com says private property with no public access; access level set to private pending confirmation. No source read is dated after 2003 except the Forest Lookouts history, which ends in the 1960s, so current condition is unverified. Forest Lookouts quotes a 1946 district report and 1963 to 1966 district reports. Spelling varies, Rancheria and Rancherie. Photos not added.

The 1933 build and 1962 destruction agree across four sources. Access comes from a 2015 hike report, so the public level and trail note are provisional until someone checks current conditions. No source describes remains on the summit. No new photo with a usable URL was found. The brief's access 'unknown' is superseded by the trail description.

Thin record: firelookout.com has one short entry, Forest Lookouts has one line, and the FFLA list has one line. No USFWS, Malheur refuge or current-condition page was found in two searches, so access and staffing are omitted rather than guessed. The 1930s date is decade-only in both sources, so no built event with a year was entered. Elevation 4,140 ft matches the record's 1261.9 m. Do not merge with the Douglas County Rattlesnake Mountain site (firetower.org lists a 1933 photo under that name; it belongs to the gone Douglas County site).

Thin record. Two listings and a history page with no narrative: no exact build year, builder, design, staffing, fire, or removal date in any source read. The register's 1930s is kept only in the story and evidence, because an event needs a year. The brief's kind 'unknown' is not resolved. Worth checking Ochoco National Forest archives or a Crook County historical society before expanding.

WebSearch was unavailable for this run (the shared search budget was spent before this tower), so nothing about the site today was checked beyond the pages read. The 1949 slide reference conflicts with the 1955 build date and nothing read explains it; a Forest Service or Eugene Guard source would settle it. The FFLOS table does list 'Removed 2017', the same year as the fire, so no separate removed event is recorded; the 2017 burned event covers it. The brief's access is unknown, and the story makes no access claim.

Brief height 12.2 m equals 40 ft (Oregon lookouts history); the register and firelookout.com say 41 ft. The first-tower year (1935 vs 1936) is unresolved and both are in the story. firelookout.com's locator '9 miles ENE of Newhalem' looks wrong for Tillamook County (Newhalem is a Washington place name), so it was not used. No source describes the site today; the 1942 trail note is old. Check current site status with the local forestry office before adding visit details.

Height correction is the main finding: the record's 6.1 m matches the earlier 20 ft pole tower, not the present 41 ft tower. The 1943 new-tower item conflicts with the 1953 build date and is unexplained in sources read. Rental and access status are unconfirmed. A Forest Service Umpqua camping and cabins page (fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/recreation/camping-cabins) appeared in search but was not read. A Library of Congress record for the tower (loc.gov/item/or0645/) returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. Its search snippet describes an L-4 Standard '36 cab on a 41 ft TT-1 tower; check it before relying on that model. Cheryl Hill's Lookout Mountain blog (June 2024) may bear on the planned move but was not read. Photos: NHLR credits a 2015 photo to Dennis Poulin and firelookout.com credits one to Dominic Luebbers; no image URLs were captured, so none are added.

Three pages only. They agree on the 1920s shake cabin, the 1931 rebuild and the abandonment, but Oregon Lookouts describes the 1931 building as a 14 x 14 gable-roof house and gives 6,000 feet, not the L-4 cab and 5,843 feet the other two give. The county is recorded as Linn, but firelookout.com says Lane County; not checked against a county map, so the record is unchanged. Oregon Lookouts marks the site removed with no date. No source describes the site today. Photos: FFLOS credits a 1920s-1931 photo to the Howard Verschoor collection, but no image URL was captured, so none is listed. A 1933 panorama is mentioned on Oregon Lookouts (dated 11 September 1933); a FFLOS caption dates one 9-30-1933, seen only in a search snippet and not checked on the page.

Build dates conflict (1936, 1947 vs 1949 for the current tower). Status conflicts: firelookout.com says abandoned; the 2022 visit and the list say standing. The brief's height_m 3.0 looks wrong (correction proposed). Staffing as_of is the 2022 visit, not a staffing report. Stair removal is from a single 2022 visitor account; no current FS status page was found, so the climbing status should be checked before anyone visits.

Three pages, all describing the same 24-foot pole L-5 tower, but they disagree on the build date (1931 newspaper item, 1933 firelookout.com, 1936 FFLOS) and on removal versus destruction (1957). The Oregon Lookouts page quotes a January 1958 annual report, so the removal may be dated to 1957 or 1958; the story does not pick one. The FFLOS page gives its 1953 photo caption with no image URL captured, so no photos are listed. Do not confuse this record with the separate Red Hill lookout on firelookout.com (/or/redhill.html) and the NHLR (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/or/red-hill-lookout/), which describes a 1917 site and a 40-foot L-4 tower built in 1947 or 1949 that still stands; that is a different site and was not checked against this one. Height 7.3 m is the conversion of the 24-foot pole height given by FFLOS and firelookout.com. The 1946 NGS survey note is historical; it is not evidence about the site today. The NGS station description quoted on Oregon Lookouts places the site about 14 miles northeast of Monument, while firelookout.com says north; the story attributes 'north' to firelookout.com only.

Only three pages, and they say little about the cabin's history: no year is given for its removal and no source names a lookout. FFLOS gives 4,500 ft (1,372 m) and firelookout.com gives 4480 ft; the record's 1371.6 m is kept. Photo credits on firelookout.com go to the Howard Verschoor collection and Harold C. Chriswell, and the FFLOS photos are 'View of site' and 'Remains of cabin foundation'; no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed. A 2023 blog post (cherylhill.net, 'Red Hill') describes a different standing Red Hill lookout with a 40-foot L-4 tower built in 1947 and was not used here. The story's remains sentence rests on an undated caption.

The removed-versus-destroyed disagreement for 1968 is between firetower.org and firelookout.com and is reported as a disagreement in the story. The 1939 staffing comes from a newspaper as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not read (Historic Oregon Newspapers would confirm). No source describes the site today beyond the NGS survey record, and no access level is sourced, so no access key is given. The brief's west_us_lookouts coordinate was not checked against its own source page.

The record's name and coordinates describe the relocated cabin at Tiller, which is right. Its elevation (1462 m, 4,797 ft) matches the original mountain site, not Tiller; the Tiller elevation is not in the sources read, so the field is flagged, not corrected. The record's 'None relocated' text should read as a 1985 relocation (added as an event). Access and hours should be checked before a visit: the FS and visitor hours differ, and the 2024 visitor noted the rangers may be moving to Canyonville.

The brief's 'None relocated' event wording is corrected above. The NHLR record (US 911) and the FFLOS site record (US 896) are separate registrations for the same lookout; the story uses both. Staffing names after 1930 were not found beyond 'staffed into the 1960s'. The Tiller Historical Trail page on the Forest Service site (recid 63864) appeared in a search result, but the cached page was a recreation listing that did not include the lookout description, so it is not cited. Opening hours and current access were not confirmed. Budget note: this tower went over the six-page-read budget (about 9 fetches including repeats) and used no WebSearch.

Search results included a Montana lookout also called Reynolds Ridge (mtmemory.org; firelookout.com/mt), built 1931 and destroyed 1962. It is a different lookout and was not used. The fate disagreement (removed versus destroyed, both 1963) is reported as a disagreement. No staffing or fire history was found in the sources read; the story leaves those out.

Thin record: the four sources give the build year, owner and a 2022 condition report, but no fire history, no later repairs and no move or rental. Access is recorded as restricted because of gates on the BLM road and the uninhabitable building; no closure notice was found, so this is an inference. The brief's coordinates match the Register. The building is not recommended for entry.

All 1931 newspaper material is quoted secondhand on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers were not read (Historic Oregon Newspapers would confirm June 1931 items). The orww.org PDF of the Forest Lookouts page is a print of that same page, so it is not counted as a separate source. The 1963 cab's removal year is the main open question. No source describes the site today.

The 1934 build and 1941 abandonment agree in the register and on firelookout.com, so the record dates stand. The record's location conflict is real: the register point (45.485006, -121.526563) and the firelookout.org point (45.50509, -121.52508) are about 2.2 km apart (record distance_m 2236). The Oregon Hikers Rim Rock point (45.48863, -121.52329) sits near the register point. The register point is also close to the Rimrock South record (us-or-rimrock-south; firelookout.org point 45.48849, -121.52292), so Rimrock North and Rimrock South may describe one ridge-top site on Surveyor's Ridge. Check this before publishing either story. A 2007 Trail Advocates forum post ('The Other Rim Rock', Tom Kloster, http://www.trailadvocate.org/discuss/msgReader$631?mode=topic) places a lookout on a rim north of Shellrock Mountain and questions whether two Rim Rock lookouts existed. It is not cited in the story. Apart from the register and firelookout.com, no source I found uses the name Rimrock North. The hike and foundation-block details describe the Oregon Hikers Rim Rock site and are not confirmed as this entry. Access is left unset (record says unknown). The register photo (Ron Kemnow) is already in the record and is not a new find.

Brief record matches the sources on elevation (1,280 m), gone status, L-4 design and 2010 registration; no corrections proposed. Access 'public' is inferred from a 2022 hike report that walked to the site, not from an agency statement; the brief said 'unknown'. No source describes remains today. Dating conflict (1930 vs c.1933) and removal conflict (removed vs destroyed, 1950) are unresolved in the sources. Photos on firetower.org (National Archives Pacific Northwest Region panoramas) not recorded: no per-photo licence was read.

Access level left unset: none of the four sources says whether the public may enter the tower, and the Register ties the site to an engine on high fire days. Total height not recorded: Forest Lookouts gives only the 20 ft ground-to-catwalk distance. The 1980s-to-2012 gap is undated in firelookout.com. The Roaming Civic and a Facebook group post describe the 1980s staffing history but were not read or cited. Register elevation 4,204 ft versus 4,200 ft elsewhere; not used in the story.

No source gives the year the tower came down, so no removed event is recorded. No source describes remains or public access today; access is not set. Coordinates: the firetower.org/FFLOS point (42.643110, -121.126060) matches the brief's FFLOS record; the brief's second point (west_us_lookouts) was not checked. The brief's height_m (20.4) is only one of three reported heights. The brief's agency line is incomplete: the blog and Oregon Lookouts name the Klamath Indian Agency as the first managing agency. Photos on firetower.org (credited to Ron Kemnow and Howard Verschoor) not recorded: no licence stated.

Main findings: the record's 6.1 m height is the earlier pole tower; the standing tower is 53 ft (about 16.2 m). The 1933 build year belongs to the first tower; the present R-6 tower dates from 1974. Build dates before 1933 vary across sources (1913, 1917, 1932). Story treats them as uncertain. The tower is condemned since 2016 and should not be climbed; the story does not encourage access. The 2022 Roaming Civic visit describes a climb, which the story does not repeat. Current agency, staffing and condition after 2022 are unconfirmed. Not read: the search snippet for a Sohs (research.sohs.org) article saying ODF has a 53-foot tower at the site today; it is a secondary search snippet and was not used as evidence. Oregon Hikers forum (2016) was not read. No photos added: the Roaming Civic 2022 photos are credited to a visitor and no URLs were captured. Forest Lookouts page credits photos to Rex Kamstra but no URLs were captured.

Three pages. The only history is the register's two-line description (1925 nest and camp, 1932 USFS cabin); Oregon Lookouts has no history block for this site. Location conflict: register coordinates do not match its own county and forest; fix the coordinates before publishing. Oregon Lookouts' Douglas County page does not list a Rock Creek site. A Douglas Forest Protective Association post, seen only as a search snippet (login-walled on fetch, not used as evidence), mentions a Rock Creek Guard Station built in 1952 and destroyed by a fire; it appears to be a different building in Douglas County and is not used. The register's 2011 photo (courtesy of Howard Verschoor) has no URL, so no photo is recorded.

Brief record matches the sources on status, 1916 build, 2011 registration and agency; no corrections proposed. Do not conflate with other Rocky Point sites: firetower.org 'Rocky Point Lookout Site' (US 732, Lincoln County; cabin built 1920s and gone by the 1950s; http://www.firetower.org/lookouts/us/or/rocky-point-lookout-site/) and a second Rocky Point page on oregonlookouts.weebly.com (rocky-point.html; 1913 station, Section 16 T4N R5W), which I saw only as a search snippet and did not read. No source describes the site today; access is unknown and not set. Linn County Fire Patrol Association records (University of Oregon, 1911-1963) appeared in search results but were not read.

No source describes the site today, and the story says so. The 1962 destruction rests on the register and firelookout.com; a web search for the storm and this lookout found nothing confirming it, so it is attributed to the register. The 1933 date conflicts with the 1919 and 1931 items and with the register's own 1919 to 1933 photo caption, so the editor may want to review the infobox build year. Access is not stated in any source, so no access key is set. The brief's gone status, Coos FPA agency and elevation are supported.

The two listings agree: a cabin (not a tower), built in the 1920s, gone by the 1950s. Neither names a builder, design, staffing, fires or removal cause, so none is in the story. Two web searches found no Siuslaw or Lincoln County history for this site. A search snippet, not fetched and not cited, listed a Rocky Point summit in Lincoln County at 2,782 ft on the USGS Stott Mountain map, against the register's 2,890 ft. The editor may want to check the map. Event years 1920 and 1950 are placeholders for decades (see notes) and should not be read as exact dates. The name is shared with us-or-rocky-point-2 (Columbia County, Oregon Department of Forestry), which is a different site. Access is left unset (record says unknown).

Elevation conflict: the register gives 8,196 ft and firelookout.com gives 6754 ft; the brief's 2498.1 m matches the register. Height conflict: 16 ft in the register and firelookout.com, 19 ft 6 in in a 1942 memo, 25 ft in a 1953 survey note. Removal method differs: removed (register), destroyed (firelookout.com), burned (1968 letter); the story reports all three. No source describes the summit today. A 1953 NGS recovery note gives forest-road access to within a five-minute walk of the summit station, but no source describes current access. The 1960 staffing year is inferred from a July 1961 item saying 'last summer'. The brief's gone status and U.S.Forest Service agency are supported.

The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with the register, which says the concrete tower is now a radio building. This record proposes 'standing' with a status note; the editor should confirm the wording. The brief's 1922 build date matches the register and firelookout.com, but Rex's page has the lookout house completed in October 1921. firelookout.com's header 'R.I.P. 1922-1958' was not used because it does not match its own text or the other sources. No source describes the current condition of the concrete tower or whether the site is open to visitors. The brief's 2001 removal and Oregon Department of Forestry agency are supported. Searches found nothing on the site's current state.

Abandonment date conflicts (1963 vs gone by 1966 vs FireLookout.com heading 1927-1935); story gives 1963. The AllTrails and Roadtrippers search snippets claim 'wooden remains' of the lookout, but AllTrails returned HTTP 403 and neither page was read, so the story does not use that claim. Brief coordinates conflict (FFLOS 44.41779,-122.30387 vs West US Lookouts 44.40416,-122.29739); not resolved. Brief's design L-4 is corrected to note the 1927 frame cab. No photos added.

Thin record: two sources, neither gives a year for the cabin beyond the 1940s, and no source describes the site today or its access. Oregon Lookouts has a Jefferson County 'ROUND BUTTE' page with no content beyond the name. Two web searches returned nothing further. The brief's access 'unknown' is left unset because no source supports a level. Search snippets mention Round Butte Overlook Park near Madras (Travel Oregon, Tripadvisor); no source ties that park to this lookout site, so it is not used.

Identity: the Oregon Lookouts page is titled 'Round Butte' (Klamath Indian Agency / Winema NF, 29S-9E-08) and the Klamath blog's 'ROUND BUTTE' entry is at Sec 8 T29S R15E; both match a 100 ft Aermotor steel tower removed in 1991 or 1992, so they are treated as this lookout. That link is inferred from location and dates, not stated by any source; the township figures differ between the two and were not resolved. Brief's height 4.9 m is unsupported and corrected to 30.5 m. The Facebook post was read only as its title line; the post's date, photo and description were not visible, so nothing beyond the caption is used. Access and visit status are not supported by any source and are left out. Event 1936 uses the Oregon Lookouts and Klamath blog dates; the Register and FireLookout.com date the tower to 1935.

Brief kind 'two_story' is not supported by these sources, which describe a 1930s cabin and then a 1950s tower; left unchanged for review. Neither the brief nor the sources give a usable height (FFLOS '10'' may refer to a cab), so no height is set. The Forest Service AT&T Round Mountain record calls the site Round Mt., about 5 miles south of Walton Lake, and does not mention a summit; the link to the summit's communication tower is inferred from the name, the location and the trail listing. Komoot is a trail listing and is weak evidence for the 1972 fire and the trailheads. The -2 Round Mountain record (us-or-round-mountain-2) is a different site on the Deschutes NF.

History rests on the NHLR detail page, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill's November 2023 visit, and Forest Lookouts' extracts of Bend Bulletin items (quoted from newspapers, not checked against the scans). Build year: NHLR, Cheryl Hill and the Forest Lookouts summary give 1933; Forest Lookouts' note says construction in 1932. Elevation disagrees: NHLR 5,835 ft (1,779 m) against 5,900 ft on Cheryl Hill and firelookout.com. The record's 1778.5 m is left unchanged. Current staffing and access come from a 2023 visit and undated pages; no 2025 or 2026 source found, so recheck with the Bend-Fort Rock Ranger District before a visit. No rental listing found and none is claimed. No new photos added.

Facts cover the original Round Pass site; the moved house is covered under Morgan Butte in the story. Access is not set: Morgan Butte is described as closed to the public (trail listing), but no source describes access to the Round Pass site. Brief kind 'ground' was not checked against a source; the Oregon lookouts page's 1919 mention of 'the Round Pass Lookout Tower' suggests a tower may have existed there. Komoot is a weak source. Search results pages titled 'Printable Lookouts in Western Oregon' give a 1965 build date for Morgan Butte and are not used.

The brief height of 15.2 m matches the 50-foot plan rather than the 35-foot tower; see corrections. No access information was found for the summit (a Komoot summit listing says visitor information is not available), so no access key is set. Agency wording follows the Oregon lookouts page; the brief says Northwest Oregon FPA. Not used: a geocaching page for a different Round Top (4,649 ft, southern Oregon) and an unconfirmed Willhite page. The -2 Round Top record (us-or-round-top-2) is a different site (Jackson County ODF lookout). The stored tower record data/towers/or/us-or-round-top.json still has height_m 15.2; the corrections entry proposes 10.7 (35 ft). That file was not edited in this check.

Core facts agree across sources: ODF-run, Jackson County, 1973 cab, unmanned since 2016 season, cameras since 2017. Early history conflicts: 1934 vs 1949-50 start, and 20 vs 24 feet. The brief's height_m 7.3 m is kept because it matches only the Weebly 24-foot figure. No fire is named. A 1995 Register-Guard profile quoted on the Weebly page reports a fire spotter's smoke sighting and grass fires called in (event 1995). A Former Fire Lookout Sites register page titled 'Round Top Lookout Site' appeared in a search snippet only (not read, not cited): it describes a 1933 crow's nest, a 1946 35-foot L-4 abandoned 1965 and removed 1970. It may be a different chronology for this peak. Worth a fetch and a county check before any edit. Access level 'public' refers to the site only; no source says the cab can be climbed.

No staffing, fire or removal-date sources found. Agency conflict (ODF vs City of Medford) and 1933 plan vs 1941 build are both reported in the story. Access is set to public from Wikipedia's description of Prescott Park as a city park and its road access to the summit; no source describes the lookout site itself. The 2007 radio tower is not linked to the lookout by any source. The LivingNewDeal page returned 403 and the Medford city park page returned almost no text, so neither was quoted.

Only two sources, both giving the 1920s as the build period. The year field holds 1920 as a decade placeholder. No source describes the site today or its access. The Forest Lookouts page for Ruddy Hill has only a location line and was not quoted. The story and facts already use platform, per the corrections entry.

Good annual notes on the Forest Lookouts page (1938-1968) but the removal is undated and no source describes the site today. The 1942 survey description says U.S.F.S. while the register, firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts header say ODF (reported in the story). The register phrase 'used for emergency in the 1960s' is unclear and is quoted rather than interpreted. The LandWatch listing returned 403 and was not used. No photos added.

Three pages read; no staffing, fire or access record found, so none written. Access and visit keys omitted (brief says unknown and no source gives one). Sources disagree on removal (removed about 1960 vs destroyed, undated). The 1933 Sentinel and Roseburg Chieftain items are only seen as quoted on the Oregon lookouts page. Lead, not used: a Dorena Historical Society Facebook post (Curtis Irish archive) shows the Rujada tower in 1940; the page would not load (login wall), so it is not cited. Brief record checked: L-5, 40 ft/12.2 m, Umpqua NF and 2011 registration all agree with sources; no corrections.

Brief height_m 15.2 is the 1921 pole tower (50 ft), corrected to 25.0 m for the 82-foot tower. Access is marked closed for the tower; the road and trailhead are described as open in 2020 and 2023 accounts, but no official Forest Service notice was read. The 1941 Forest Lookouts date conflicts with 1949 sources. A Twin Lakes fire near-miss item seen in search results was not fetched and is not used. Staffing after 1964 not found. Newest status evidence is the 2023 visit.

Record height_m 3.0 looks wrong: the 1948 tower is 31'6" per the Register and Forest Lookouts (9.6 m); firelookout.com says 30 feet (9.1 m). Proposed 9.6 m is a correction for review, and facts.height_m uses it. Elevation: Register 6,154 ft (1,876 m) against 6,208 ft on firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill's list; the record's 1,875.7 m matches the Register and is kept. Name and spelling: the Register names William Parker as first lookout; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1915 item naming a Ray Parker; the Register's 1917 contractor (Mill-Made) and the newspaper quote (Mill-Maid) differ. Forest: the Register and firelookout.com say Rogue River National Forest; Cheryl Hill and the trip report say Rogue River-Siskiyou. The 2021 trip report is dated August 14, 2021 on the tag page; a March 2, 2025 date also appears beside it and was not checked further. Current staffing and access rest on a 2021 trip report and undated lists; no 2025 or 2026 source found, so recheck with the Butte Falls Ranger District. No photos added.

The 1937 build date is a new built event: the record had only the 2010 registration, so this is an addition, not a correction. Both listings give 1937 for a pole L-4 tower. The register's photo caption dates a Saddle Guard Station Lookout panorama to 4-18-34, three years earlier. The sources do not explain this. The photo URL in the record names 'saddle-mtn', so the picture may show Saddle Mountain rather than the station; an editor should check the original photo record at the National Archives. The 1934 event is kept as type other because the caption is the only evidence for it. Two web searches found no Saddle Guard lookout or station in Siuslaw or Lane County histories. Access and staffing are unknown and left out. No site-today source was found.

Only two short listings exist for this summit, and they agree on 1922 and 1953 but differ on removed vs destroyed. No staffing, fire or present-day source was found, so the story says nothing about those. Do not mix in the Saddle Mountain (South) page on oregonlookouts.weebly.com or firelookout.com/or/saddlesouth.html: they describe South Saddle Mountain (US 733, Washington County, 45.548, -123.375), where a 1932 log house burned in the 1933 Wilson River fire. The Clatsop County Saddle Mountain (North Saddle) and the Pend Oreille County Saddle Mountain are different summits too. A search snippet from theroamingcivic.com ties a 1953 lookout to the Clatsop summit, so the 1953 date here should be re-checked against any new source before publication. Checked 2026-10-10: the firelookout.com listing also gives Tillamook County, Tillamook FPA and 3475 ft, so both listings describe the Tillamook summit and the 1953 date stands on both.

Three pages read; no fire, access or current-site record found, so none written. Access and visit keys omitted. Elevation not in facts: the brief gives 990.6 m (3,250 ft) but firelookout.com lists 3100 ft (about 945 m); not resolved, so check before using the brief's elevation. The 1953 annual report text is OCR-garbled in the ORWW PDF copy; quotes use the weebly page text. Agency is the Oregon Department of Forestry (Lincoln FPA district), not the US Forest Service.

Current condition unknown: the latest source read is Cheryl Hill's July 2013 visit, which found the steel tower in place; no later report of the tower's condition or of the 1969 sale outcome was found. Do not treat it as standing today without a recent check. Record fixes: built 1922 is the crow's nest (proposed 1927); height_m 9.1 is 30 feet, the tree lookout (proposed 21.3 m for the 70-foot tower). Unresolved disagreements, not settled by the sources: tower height 60 feet (1926-27 Eugene paper) against 70 feet (Register, 1953 survey station, 1969 notices, Cheryl Hill); tower date 1926 (1927 newspaper 'last year') against 1927 (Register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill); elevation 4,940 ft (Register) against 4,969 ft (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill, Forest Service); abandonment 1967 (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill) against the 1969 notices, which say it 'no longer will be manned' in fire season. The Register's 'Built' field is not given; the 1927 date is taken from its description. Access: the Forest Service trail page gives the route as 1.1 miles along Road 142 to Road 144, then 0.8 mile to the end of Road 144, where the trail begins; the 1969 newspaper described a road stopping several hundred yards short, which may be a different route. No photos added.

Three pages read; no staffing, fire or access record found, so none written. Access and visit keys omitted. The brief lists kind ground; none of the sources read says whether a tower stood, so the story calls it a cab only. The brief elevation of 1486.5 m matches firelookout.com's 4877 ft. The register credits a National Archives Pacific Northwest Region panorama dated 10-24-33; no image URL collected, so no photo entry. The 1922 item is only seen as quoted on the Oregon lookouts page.

Both lookout-side sources give only 'the 1930s', so the 1930 year is the decade start. No staffing record in these sources, so none is recorded. What the site is today rests on one Oregon Hikers page, which is a wiki revision (oldid 116289) with no date. Access is recorded as public because the page describes a trail hike; check the trail status before publishing. Our record's coordinates, elevation (1,148.5 m) and agency match the register; no correction proposed.

The 1968 burning is consistent across sources; the build year (1930 to 1933) is contested and the record's 1932 is only firelookout.com's date. The only dated item is the Society page's 'As of 2025' road note, so the staffing as_of is that page's undated wording. Rental is listed by NHLR only; confirm with the Society before publishing rental details. Access level restricted because the spur road is gated 1.25 miles away. Not visited.

The history is well covered: three sources agree on the 1933 and 1954 cabs and on the 1968 removal, and the Oregon Lookouts page reprints 1932 and 1948 newspaper items. Nothing in these sources says what remains on the site or whether it is open to visitors, so the story says so. The brief's L-5 design is correct but leaves out the 1954 L-4 replacement, which is now in the facts. The Oregon Lookouts page calls the 1933 house an Aladdin emergency house; the maker is not named in the story. Oregon Lookouts gives the 1971 letter's recipient as the Oakridge district ranger, which is kept as written.

A thin record: no build year beyond the 1940s, no cab or design detail, no staffing, and no removal date in the sources read. One web search turned up no further history. The record's coordinates, elevation (1010.4 m) and agency match the register and firelookout.com; no correction proposed. Nothing describes the site today or its access, so the story says so.

Three sources, one of them a transcription page that quotes newspapers and a 1955 survey description. The register and firelookout.com agree on the 1926 build; the register and the Forest Lookouts page agree on 1965 removal. Access is not recorded: no source says whether the summit can be visited, so the access key is omitted rather than set to unknown. The brief's height is absent and no source gives one. The Scar Mountain Trail #3402 on the Willamette NF site runs along the same ridge but no source ties it to the lookout site, so it is not cited. Not read: the Oregon Historic Sites or heritagedata pages for Scar Mountain. The 1936 posting is a plan, not a confirmed staffing record.

The brief's coordinates (43.77226, -123.70692) match the register. A separate dataset in our records gives 43.76151, -123.70816, about 1.2 km south; that source is not among the three read, so the register's point is kept. Staffing into the 1970s is from the register and firelookout.com; the last staffed year is not given. The 1951 fire has two names in the history page's newspaper quotes; the story reports both rather than choosing. The 1966 item names a 17-year-old, which is left out. The brief's 9.1 m height matches the register's 30 ft. Access is omitted: no source says whether the site can be visited. No source describes the site today. Not searched further: the Douglas County and Western Lane FPA history pages.

Identity needs a human decision. The Forest Lookouts Scott Mountain page (Linn FPA, 13S-1W-31, 1948, dismantled 1979) and the register's Scott (Bald Peter) entry (Linn FPA, 1948, removed 1979, 2,136 ft) describe the same tower, so this record treats them as one. The Bald Peter name is also used for a 1912 Linn County lookout at T12S R2E sec 28 (4,079 ft), and the register's separate Scott Mountain (US 988) is a 1929 cabin in Lane County. The brief's other_names lists Scott Mountain; that name is shared with US 988, so it was not added. Height: the brief's 16.2 m is replaced by the register's 55 ft (16.8 m) as a proposed correction. Access is omitted: no source says whether the site can be visited. No source describes the site today. Not read: the Linn County Fire Patrol association's own history, or the Bald Peter 1912 site's register entry.

No source describes what remains on the site today, and access is unknown. Removal year conflicts (1959 Rex, 1960 register and firelookout.com). A search snippet calls the peak part of the Mount Washington Wilderness, but the page fetched empty, so it is not cited; check wilderness status before any access sentence. The register shows a 1955 photo credited to Ed Anderson, but no image URL was captured, so no photo is listed. The 1928 newspaper note about a telephone line and secondary lookout point is left out because it does not describe the cabin.

Heavy source conflict on build dates and tower heights; the story names the conflicts and does not pick winners. The brief's height_m 15.2 (50 ft) matches the earlier pole tower, so the correction proposes omitting it. No source describes what remains on the summit today, and access is unknown. The 1933 panorama note on the Rex page calls the site Scott Mountain, and the story uses that name. firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum, Dave Bula and Howard Verschoor, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed.

Two independent pages agree on the 1962 tower; only firelookout.com dates the 1935 tower, since the Oregon Lookouts page does not mention it. Both are hobbyist directories with no primary citations, and neither gives a removal date. The Oregon Lookouts index lists a separate Serpentine - 1 at 37S-8W-9, while Serpentine - 2 is 37S-8W-16; the brief's coordinates 42.35097,-123.65936 come from the directory and are not tied to either page, so check which page they belong to. Brief design R-6 and height 12.5 m (41 ft) are supported for the 1962 tower. No staffing, access or current-site source found; one WebSearch added nothing about this lookout. Access left unset.

Brief's design 'D-6 cupola cabin' describes the older 1921 cabin, not the current tower; the current lookout is a flat-roof cab on a 40-foot steel tower (NHLR). Brief's height 9.1 m matches the 1962/63 wooden tower, so it is corrected to 12.2 m (40 ft, converted). Build year 2007 is consistent in the register but the Weebly listing says completed October 2007 and in service 2008. Sources disagree on the 1962/63 tower year and the 1914/1919/1921 early dates; the story reports the disagreement. 'Unmanned' and 'fenced' rest on a 2021 blog visit (as_of 2021-07), not a current official source. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the gate and fence. The 1931 Department of Commerce weather-cabin contract is in the Weebly listing but not footnoted in the story. Photos not added.

No source describes what remains on the summit today or whether it is open to visitors, so access is omitted. The removal year is not given: the register and firelookout.com say only that it is now gone, and the Rex page has an undated Removed entry. The brief's height 9.4 m is kept because it is close to the 31 feet on the Rex page; the register and firelookout.com say 30 feet. FFLOS shows 1951 and 1964 photos (Ron Kemnow collection) and firelookout.com credits Howard Verschoor, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed. The 1945 balloon item is a local sighting report and is kept short.

Removal date is not given in any source read. The record's 20-ft (6.1 m) height is kept; firelookout.com gives 15 ft. The height_m value is the total pole height, not the cab floor. Several other pages on the web are named Sheep Mountain lookouts in Washington, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming; they were not used, and the Washington Republic News-Miner quotes on washingtonlookouts.weebly.com must not be attributed to this site. The NGS survey text is quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and was not checked against NGS directly. No photos added.

Dates agree across sources; the removed/destroyed wording differs. The record's kind 'ground' is kept; sources describe a cabin, not a tower, so no design is added beyond that. Access is set to public because the Oregon Hikers guides describe a walk to the site, but the Dalles Watershed boundary signs were not checked against land rules, so a human should confirm before recommending the bushwhack. Today's description rests on one Oregon Hikers field guide, with no date shown. No staffing source found. No photos added.

Thin record: only the register, Forest Lookouts (location only) and firelookout.com were read, and none gives a build year beyond the 1930s, a design, a removal date or staffing. The brief's second coordinate pair (43.531, -122.9609, from west_us_lookouts) is about 10 km north of the FFLOS point (43.44396, -122.95672); that other source was not read. A rough check puts the FFLOS point about 25 miles from Roseburg, close to firelookout.com's 26 miles, so the FFLOS point is kept. Check the other source before any map change. No photos added.

Brief's height_m 2.1 is wrong; 90 feet (27.4 m) is in the Register and FireLookout.com, so it is corrected. Build year conflict (1935 vs 1955) is real and unresolved; both are recorded. The 2007 fire entry is a threat, not a damage report, and comes from a history page quoting The Oregonian. The Oregonian article itself was not read. Access level 'permission' follows the Register's tribal-regulation line; the tribe's own visitor rules were not found. Staffing as_of 2026-07 is the Cherylhill directory date, and the FireLookout.com staffing text is undated.

Relocated tower: story covers both the Shivigny site (gone, no current description) and the Baughman lookout where the steel tower now stands. Baughman naming is disputed (cherylhill says no such geographic name; story says the Baughman lookout). Legal location conflict: Oregon Lookouts header 26S-2W-34 vs its 1948 report T34S R2W sec 27; not used. Agency set from firelookout.com listing (Umpqua National Forest); the 1949 article says the tower was erected by the Douglas Forest Protective Association and manned by Forest Service lookouts. Brief had no agency. Brief's coordinates 43.27041,-122.92043 come from the FFLA directory and are not checked against a page. Weebly newspaper excerpts are secondary transcriptions. Access left unset; no source gives current access to the Shivigny site. The Baughman page on cherylhill.net says reaching that lookout requires a Coos Bay–Millicoma district recreation permit. A 1939 newspaper mention of a lookout on Shivney butte is omitted as not clearly this site.

Only two sources. The Oregon page is a volunteer compilation that quotes Forest Service memos, a 1948 NGS station description and a Lake County Examiner item, and I did not check the originals. Brief coordinates disagree with the register by roughly 0.2 degrees latitude and 0.7 degrees longitude. Nothing found describes the summit today, so the story says so. The 1931 Cox Creek entry is quoted from the page's 1931 section, and the May 21, 1931 item is attributed to the Lake County Examiner as the page attributes it. Fact-check 2026-10-10: every quote found on the first run; story rewritten to match the page's wording and attributions.

Height conflict is the main open point (100 ft register vs 73 ft inspection vs 75 ft in a 1931 note). Note the firelookout.com index row for Shoestring Butte, Lake County, lists coordinates 42.59306, -121.26905, which do not match the record (42.38634, -120.53286 per firetower.org). The record coordinates were kept: the 1948 survey description quoted on the Forest Lookouts page places the summit about 17 miles northwest of Lakeview, which fits. The index row should be checked. The Forest Lookouts page also covers Slide Mountain in the same 1967-68 scrap story; keep Slide Mountain details out of this record. No source describes the summit or the site today, and access is unknown.

Same site under two names: NHLR says Sidwalter Mountain Lookout, firelookout.com and the Oregon lists say Sidwalter Butte; coordinates match (44.914, -121.533). Build year (1965 vs 1967) and design (107 ft Aermotor vs 90 ft steel) disagree and are reported as such. No sourced account of fires, keepers or the lookout's staffing history was found in the reads. Staffing 'staffed' comes from the July 2026 list only. Access is closed to the public per NHLR; the record's permission level is proposed as closed. The record's height_m 2.1 is an error and is proposed as 32.6.

Present site not described by any source read. Search results (not read, so not cited) include a sixes.net KSOR page on Kenyon Mountain with 2008 photos and an amateur-radio repeater listing for Kenyon Mt. (redcrosscommunications.org); either may describe what stands on the summit now and should be read before any site-today claim is added. A cherylhill.net post says the tower was torn down in May, which fits the 2011 date. NHLR's 'in active service' text is stale. The 1935 and 1961 dates and the 100/110 ft and 50/53 ft figures conflict across sources and the story presents them as conflicting. Access level not established; no access fact recorded.

No source read describes what, if anything, remains at the site today, and no access information was found. A search returned only register and list pages. The 1931 build year agrees across all three sources. The removal year is approximate (about 1965) and the verb differs between sources. firelookout.com credits a photo to Mark Swift, and the Oregon Lookouts page mentions a 1933 panorama; neither has an image URL in the cached pages, so no photos were added.

No source read describes what remains at the site today or whether it is open to the public. A search returned an FFLA social media post saying the lookout was about one mile from the coast (search snippet only, not read or cited). The 1932/1933 construction-year conflict is the main open question. The 1941 recreation area reference is historical only.

No source we read covers staffing, so the story leaves it out. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is public; access is omitted. Do not confuse this with a different Silver Butte near Riddle in Douglas County (weebly page silver-butte1.html). A 2013 cherylhill.net post about an Oregon Department of Forestry tear-down of a Silver Butte lookout is probably that other site; it was not used. The brief's height_m of 4.3 has no source.

Sources agree the tower was removed in June 2012 (1 and 3) and that cameras replaced it (2 and 3); no source describes the site today or whether it is public, so access is omitted. The FFLOS page at firetower.org (US 1091) is a Grant County Silver Butte in the Umatilla National Forest, not this Douglas County site, and must not be merged with us-or-silver-butte. The record coordinate (42.85893, -123.37834) is not checked against the conflicting Riddle directions (west in 1923, southeast in 1944). Height_m 7.6 is in the record but no source supports it, so it is proposed for removal.

The end date is the main conflict: 1968 removal or destruction (register, firelookout.com) versus destruction in the 2002 Biscuit Fire (weebly only). The Biscuit Fire source does not mention this lookout, so the story cites it only for the fire itself. Weebly also lists September 15, 1936 panorama photos at this site, earlier than the 1940 build; the sources do not explain it, so it is left out. No staffing after 1941 and no site description today appear in any source.

Build year (about 1937 vs 1940) and removal year (1977 vs 1996) conflict; the 1992 survey is the best tiebreak but is not a Forest Service record. Access and visiting rules were not confirmed from a Forest Service page. No fire detections found. Trip-report pages seen only in search snippets (oregonhikers, cherylhill, oregonlookouts) were not read or cited. Quotes checked against the cached pages. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story reworded where it went beyond the sources ("first lookout", "today"); Clackamas County evidence added.

The 1926 vs 1934 end date is the main open point, and the Central Oregonian article is the only source with a 1926 date. A 1996 Nugget 'Recollections of Sisters' article turned up in search: it is about the Black Butte cupola and 1934 CCC tower, not this lookout, so it is not cited. A Deschutes Historical Museum post and a Facebook comment thread also show 1921 and 1934 in search snippets only; their text was not read, so they are not cited. No source describes the site today, and access is unknown.

The Fox Butte story (data/stories/us-or-fox-butte.md) covers the same cab and agrees with this one. The cab's current condition rests on one 2021 visit; no later source was read. The Forest Service disposal project is listed as cancelled in the Fox Butte story's sources, which was not re-checked here. Elevation differs (register 5,674 ft; firelookout.com 5,682 ft), so it is left out. The brief's status 'gone' is right for the Sixteen Butte site but hides the cab; a status_note is proposed rather than a correction.

Brief height 15.2 m appears to be the 50-foot planned height; three sources give 60 feet, so the correction is proposed. Height and forest conflicts are flagged in the story. Today's condition rests on one 2022 visitor's photo captions on WillhiteWeb, not an agency statement. The access level public is inferred from road descriptions and the absence of any closure notice; confirm with the forest before treating it as settled. The 1932 occupancy line is a newspaper plan, not a confirmed staffing record.

Thin record: two one-line register entries plus a short Forest Lookouts clipping. The September 1933 CCC plan may or may not describe the same cab; the sources do not say. No staffing, fire or present-day information was found, so none is written. Brief's kind 'ground' is consistent with an L-5 cab, but no source says ground-level in so many words.

Built 1958 and abandoned are supported by firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts page. Staffing is a 1958 plan, not confirmed use. Location is unconfirmed: firelookout.com says not determined, and WillhiteWeb calls its spot a best guess. The record coordinate (45.59377, -122.81182) is unverified and should not be shown as the lookout site without that caveat. The WillhiteWeb access rating ('Likely easy') is an unconfirmed guess; the story does not repeat it as fact and says no source confirms whether the spot can be reached. The WillhiteWeb page is a lookout-history web page (WillhiteWeb.com), not an official record, and the story describes it that way. Donor disagreement is noted, not resolved.

No photos recorded: the register photos are credited to private collections with no license stated. The two 1944 newspaper items name different men for the same post; the story omits names on purpose. The brief's design L-5 is confirmed. No source describes the site today.

No source describes the site today, so the story says so; it is not known whether the site is public. The 1973 end date comes only from the register and firelookout.com. Cab size disagrees (7x7 vs 5x5). Do not confuse this with the Slide Mountain tower above Pyramid Lake in the Los Padres (christopherplord.blogspot.com, 2018), which is a different site. The record's access is unknown and no visit facts were found.

Build date unresolved: 1936 (register, firelookout.com) against 1942 (Forest Lookouts history, an L-4 cab on a short tower). The register's own photo caption reads 'Smith Ridge Lookout 1942', which may fit the later cab; the story reports both dates and does not choose. The Forest Service trail page is the only current source and describes the site, not any remains. Access is by trail on Forest Service land; the page does not mention closures.

Brief listed 'built 1924' as the headline build event, but that appears to be the second (cabin) structure per firelookout.com, not the first (1910 tent camp) or the current (2004) building. NHLR's 1917 first-lookout date conflicts with firelookout.com's 1910 tent camp. Elevation in brief (1268.3m) matches NHLR's 4,161 ft / 1,268 m; recreation.gov states 4,223 ft, a minor discrepancy not resolved here. Fact-check 2026-10-04: story and evidence all checked out against source text; only fix was adding a missing footnote on the sentence naming the 15x15 cabin and the Gold Beach Ranger District (was previously uncited) and adding the footnote URL list, which the story file was missing entirely.

Brief height_m 61.0 is wrong; corrected to the 10-foot tower. Source 3 is a compiled history quoting newspapers and Forest Service files; all quotes were copied from its cached text. The 1930 cab type and the first cabin's date conflict between sources. Current access and visit details are thin: the only current sources are the staffed listing and the directory's legal-access column. The register's elevation differs from the directory's. The story gives no total height.

Name: the register title says Thomas Cairn, but none of the pages read explain that name; the early sources call the site Cleveland Rock. Agency: the register says administered by Linn FPA while Wikipedia places the summit in Willamette National Forest; not reconciled. The register's 1965 'L-4 cab' label and the district's 14 by 14 ft building are both reported. No source describes the summit today. The record's 'ground' kind fits a cabin on the rock.

The 2021 collapse rests on firelookout.com alone (no second source found in a web search); the story says so. Height_m uses the 50-foot 1951 tower and is proposed as a correction to 3.0 m. Location conflicts (Kinzua vs Winlock) are unresolved; the record coordinate (44.96047, -119.98998) was not checked against either description. Access level 'closed' follows firelookout.com's 'No public access.' with no reason given.

Brief height_m 30.2 is the planned 99-foot height from 1935, not the built height; corrected to 90 ft. The register's 80 ft is kept in the story. Status is standing but abandoned, with the last direct observation in May 2012; the 2026 directory is the only current source. Access is closed as of 2012 and not re-checked. The 2016 occupation is included only as a neutral event; the source is a compiled history page.

Current status rests on one 2023 blog visit and a BLM contact that the blogger reports; ODF did not reply to the blogger. The NHLR still says active service, and the brief's access 'unknown' is now recorded as closed on that basis. Elevation disagrees: NHLR 6,049 ft (1,844 m) matches the brief's 1843.7 m, while firelookout.com and the 2017 visit say 6,091 ft. Tower height disagrees (10 ft vs 9 ft 10 in after a 1993 raise). The closure date between 2017 and 2023 is unknown. No wildfire response, rental or Forest Service connection appears in these sources. An undated ODF Forest Log article on the Struck staffing was found but not used, because its date and quotes were not confirmed. No photos were added because no image URL with a licence was confirmed. Story is about 385 words.

Do not confuse with the South Baldy Lookout in the Colville and Kaniksu area of Washington (firelookout.com/wa/sbaldy.html; NHLR US register under /wa/). Access rests on one hobby site's 'No public access'; the register names ODF but gives no access rule. Verify with ODF before anyone plans a visit. Height is disputed (40 ft vs 50/54 ft). Firelookout.com's 'Emergency 1970s' note is unclear and not used. No current staffing or condition report was found.

Dates and tower type disagree across the four lookout histories; the story says so. No notable fires appear in any source read. The brief's Western Lane FPA agency is from FFLOS only; the weebly page names the Siuslaw National Forest and a Lincoln FPA annual report. Nothing in the sources describes the site today. Stodt Mountain (FFLOS US 740) is a separate former site and was not researched here.

Excluded a Willhite Lookout Site page with the same name (a 1935 40-foot pole tower, abandoned 1936); its location is Pend Oreille County, Washington, so it is a different lookout. Only one staffing name was found. The brief's 1960 'removed' event is recorded as abandoned. The FFLOS and firelookout.com elevations agree at 4,771 ft. The Oregon Hikers access note is the only current-status source and is a hiking guide, not an agency notice; check before publishing any access advice.

The brief's note that the record shares a register number is not borne out: this record is FFLOS US 733 (OR 142). A separate FFLOS page for Saddle Mountain (US 734, OR 143) describes a different site with a 1922 platform removed in 1953; it was not merged here. Almost all history detail comes from one site, the Rex's Fire Lookout Page, quoting newspapers and agency reports; the FFLOS and firelookout.com entries give only the construction, rebuild and removal dates. No source describes the site since 1974; the 1941 survey note is the most recent description of remains. Access was not covered by any source read, so the access facts are omitted.

Tower size is unresolved: 1938 Central Oregonian items say 40 ft (the December 1938 item calls it a type CT-3 tower), while the register, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers say 50 ft L-4. facts.height_m uses 50 ft because three later sources agree; the story reports both. The firelookout.org county index lists this site in Wasco County; the register, firelookout.com and Outdoor Pilgrim say Wheeler, so Wheeler is used. The site today is described only by Oregon Hikers (undated page) and Outdoor Pilgrim (access); no source describes a structure. No photos added.

Three sources, all sharing a core of 1934 build and 1974 removal. No source describes the site today, and no access information was found. The 1960 inspection gives elevation 4200 ft, but firelookout.com gives 4944 ft, which matches the brief's 1506.9 m; the 1960 figure is not used. The firelookout.com personnel entry for 1921-1923 predates the 1934 cab, so those years probably refer to an earlier station; the story names Harry Thomas with that caveat. The register's 1934 date and the 1933 'new cabin' item may refer to the same building. No photos added (the register page lists captions with National Archives and collection credits but no image URLs were read).

The FFLOS page, firelookout.com and the FFLA list agree on the 1955 build, abandonment and gone status, but no source adds design, height, staffing, fires or access. A Pinkbike article (fetch returned 403) appeared in search about a Klamath Trails Alliance recreation project at Spence Mountain; it was not fetched or quoted, and it may or may not cover the lookout site. Brief record matches the sources; no corrections.

Built year: the register's Built field reads 1930's, so the brief's 1930 is over-precise (correction proposed). The brief's note that this lookout 'shares a register number' is not confirmed: firetower.org gives US 1820, OR 543 for Spion Copp, the firelookout.org index also lists US 1820 for Spion Copp, and Akers Butte is US 1821; no shared number found. Coordinates conflict: the brief uses firetower.org (44.205658, -118.878591), while the firelookout.org index gives 44.21489, -118.92800, about 4 km away; not resolved, so the editor should check the coordinates before relying on either. No staffing names found in the sources read, so none are given. The 1972 sale is known only from newspaper excerpts quoted on Oregon Lookouts. No source says what, if anything, stands on the butte today. No photos added; the register captions credit National Archives images but no image URLs were read.

Build date (1958) is consistent across three sources. Fate is disputed (removed vs destroyed, 1973 vs a 1970s date). No source describes the site today, so the story says so. The 'private' access level rests on the Oregon Encyclopedia's ownership statement, which may be dated; the brief's access 'unknown' is now answered. Staffing is not documented; the district history's 1966 line ('No first reports made from this station') was left out as ambiguous. firetower.org has 1958-1973 photos (Howard Verschoor collection), but no image URLs or licence were captured, so none were added.

Brief's height_m 15.2 (50 ft) is corrected to 41 ft (12.5 m); the 50-foot figure is only a 1963 under-construction note. Build year differs by one year across sources (1964 vs 1965) and both are recorded. No fire is named in any source read. A waymarking.com snippet says the tower was erected in 1967; it was only a search snippet, not read, and not used. Staffing as_of is the Cherylhill directory date (July 2026); the 2018-2019 staffing comes from a single visitor report (the visit report's author) and should be treated as one source. Access level 'public' refers to the site only.

Build date of the first 50-foot tower conflicts (1926 vs 1935), and the 1943 Ralph name differs between sources. The brief's height_m of 9.1 is the 1920s platform; the 1948 tower was 83 ft. No source describes remains at the site or public access; the sno-park page is not tied to the lookout. The 1944 demolition date is flagged as questionable by its source. The editor should decide whether to mention the 1926 date alongside 1935.

Two of four sources (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill) agree on 1992 and the 41-foot tower. The Register's Built field and text disagree, and the record keeps both. The 2025 staffing report is only on Cheryl Hill's page and is not verified; that is the main open question. The brief's design L-4 describes the 1932 tower and is corrected. Access rules for the cab are not in any source read. firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber but gives no image URLs, so no photos were added. The Register's Administered-by field was cut off in the fetch, so agency rests on firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts page.

Thin record: no height in the brief, so height_m 7.3 is the register's 24 feet converted. Staffing dates conflict (1941 vs 1942-1943) and the name is spelled Duley or Duly. No source describes the site now or public access. The register says removed and firelookout.com says destroyed, both for 1952.

Agency conflicts: the brief and register say Oregon Dept. of Forestry, while Forest Lookouts says Siuslaw NF. The brief's height_m 9.1 matches the 30-foot tower. No staffing information was found in any source, so staffing is omitted. No source describes remains or public access.

Brief height_m 3.0 not used: the only height in the sources is the 1918 cabin's about 10 feet, not the later tower. Brief access 'unknown' replaced by a public hiking route per The Outbound (user-submitted guide, not an agency); no agency page checked. A Facebook post by Forgotten Oregon appeared in search results suggesting something of the lookout remains; it could not be read, so it is unverified. Check for footings or remains before any visit note. The 2007 rename rests on Wikipedia; verify against GNIS. No new photos recorded.

The brief record's status gone is contradicted by two 2021 visits (Roaming Civic, WillhiteWeb) and by firelookout.com's still there; the FFLA list says Abandoned. The proposed status is standing and kind point; both need editor sign-off. Unresolved: whether the firefinder is still mounted (no source says); the cupola's date (WillhiteWeb suspects 1964 or 1996 rebuild); the occupant (Park Rangers or Police). Not read: a search snippet from portlandfirehistory.com says Engine 32 served the station until September 8, 1959, which conflicts with Station 22's 1954 date; check before using it. Also not read: a 2010 Flickr page on the same cupola (search snippet). The WillhiteWeb 2021 photos have no captured URLs, so none are added to photos. Access comes only from one 2021 blog visit; check before saying more. Agency in the record is Portland City Parks (firelookout.com); facts use Portland Parks Bureau (Forest Lookouts). Same body, different names.

Good newspaper and register coverage for 1947 to 1955, but the record's 1948 build year and 1966 removal rest on the register and firelookout.com, and the two disagree on removed versus destroyed. Elevation differs across sources: the register gives 3,045 ft (928 m), a hiking guide gives 3,058 ft, and an encyclopedia summary gives 3,028 ft; a 1947 clipping calls the peak 5,000 ft, which looks wrong. The register lists the kind as ground while its description says a cabin on a short tower; a human may want to check that field. The register's photo caption is credited to a private collection, so no photo was added. No source found covers the lookout after 1955 except the 1966 removal date and the demolition note.

Thin record: no staffing, access, or post-1958 sources found. Brief access 'unknown' is unresolved. The county list's Abandoned label may mean something is still on site, while the detail pages say gone; check before any visit note. Brief kind 'platform' is corrected to crowsnest per the county list. A scholarsbank thesis on Willamette lookouts returned only its title, so it was not used.

No source describes the site now; the brief's access 'unknown' is unresolved. Whether the CCC 14 x 14 lookout planned in 1933 is the structure built that year is unclear. Search results also show a different Steamboat Point lookout in Dayton, Wyoming; it was not used. The brief's alternate coordinates (43.3461, -122.7244) should be checked against their source before any map use.

No staffing or notable fire found in the four pages, so the story leaves both out. The Oregon Lookouts history lists only construction, a 1937 water entry and the 1968 loss. A Forest Service trail page for Stein Butte appeared in search results but was not read; the public-access level rests on Oregon Hikers alone. The sources disagree on where the cab stood (minor point versus summit marker), and the story says so.
